And with you in abundance are workers: stonecutters and craftsmen of stone and wood, and every skilled man in every kind of work.
Of the gold, the silver, the bronze and the iron there is no number. Arise and act, and may YHWH be with you.
And David commanded all the officials of Israel to help Solomon his son:
Is not YHWH your God with you, and has he not given you rest round about? For he has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before YHWH and before his people.

Now set your heart and your being to seek YHWH your God; and arise and build the sanctuary of YHWH God, to bring the ark of the covenant of YHWH and the holy articles of God to the house that will be built for the name of YHWH.

1 chronicles_23.t: And David was old and satisfied with days, and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
And he gathered all the officials of Israel and the priests and the Levites.
And the Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward, and their number, by their skulls, by men, was thirty-eight thousand.
Of these, to act as overseers over the work of the house of YHWH, twenty-four thousand; and officers and judges, six thousand;
and four thousand gatekeepers; and four thousand praising YHWH with the instruments that I made for praising.
And David divided them into divisions, for the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham and Joel — three.
The sons of Shimei: Shelomith and Haziel and Haran — three. These were the heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan.
And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei — four.
And Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; and Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they became one father's house, one muster.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel — four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart, to be set apart as holy — a holy thing of holy things, he and his sons for ever — to burn as smoke before YHWH, to serve him and to bless in his name for ever.
And Moses the man of God — his sons were named with the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
And the sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief. And Eliezer did not have other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah were exceedingly numerous.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
And Eleazar died, and he did not have sons but only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their kinsmen, took them.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jeremoth — three.

These were the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, the heads of the fathers' houses as they were enrolled, in the number of names, by their skulls, doing the work of the service of the house of YHWH, from twenty years old and upward.
For David had said: YHWH the God of Israel has given rest to his people, and he has settled in Jerusalem for ever.
And also for the Levites, there is no more carrying of the tabernacle and of all its articles for its service.
For by the last words of David, these were the number of the sons of Levi from twenty years old and upward.

For their function was at the side of the sons of Aaron, for the service of the house of YHWH, over the courts and over the store-rooms and over the cleansing of every holy thing, and the work of the service of the house of God;

and for the bread of the row, and for the fine flour for a grain offering, and for the wafers of unleavened bread, and for the griddle, and for the well-mixed dough, and for every measure of volume and length.
And to stand morning by morning to give thanks and to praise YHWH, and likewise at evening;
and for every offering up of burnt offerings to YHWH on the sabbaths, on the new moons and at the appointed times, by number, according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before YHWH.
And they kept the charge of the tent of meeting and the charge of the holy place and the charge of the sons of Aaron their kinsmen, for the service of the house of YHWH.

1 chronicles_24.t: And for the sons of Aaron, their divisions. The sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
And David divided them, with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, according to their muster in their service.

And the sons of Eleazar were found more numerous, by the chiefs of the men, than the sons of Ithamar, and they divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, heads of fathers' houses, sixteen; and for the sons of Ithamar, by their fathers' houses, eight.
And they divided them by lots, these with those; for there were officials of the holy place and officials of God among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.

And Shemaiah son of Nethanel the scribe, of the Levites, recorded them before the king and the officials and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech son of Abiathar and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites — one father's house drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn, drawn for Ithamar.
And the first lot went out to Jehoiarib, to Jedaiah the second,
to Harim the third, to Seorim the fourth,
to Malkijah the fifth, to Mijamin the sixth,
to Hakkoz the seventh, to Abijah the eighth,
to Jeshua the ninth, to Shecaniah the tenth,
to Eliashib the eleventh, to Jakim the twelfth,
to Huppah the thirteenth, to Jeshebeab the fourteenth,
to Bilgah the fifteenth, to Immer the sixteenth,
to Hezir the seventeenth, to Happizzez the eighteenth,
to Pethahiah the nineteenth, to Jehezkel the twentieth,
to Jakin the twenty-first, to Gamul the twenty-second,
to Delaiah the twenty-third, to Maaziah the twenty-fourth.
These were their musters for their service, to come into the house of YHWH according to their ordinance, by the hand of Aaron their father, as YHWH the God of Israel had commanded him.
And for the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites: Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
And the sons of Jeriah: Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno; and Shoham and Zaccur and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, and he had no sons.
Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
And the sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites by their fathers' houses.

And they too cast lots, corresponding to their kinsmen the sons of Aaron, before David the king and Zadok and Ahimelech and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and of the Levites — the fathers of the chief corresponding to his youngest brother.

1 chronicles_25.t: And David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, with harps and with cymbals. And their number, the men of the work for their service, was:
Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur and Joseph and Nethaniah and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied under the hands of the king.

Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun — Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six — under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, over giving thanks and praising YHWH.
Of Heman: the sons of Heman — Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman the seer of the king, in the words of God, to lift up a horn. And God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the hands of their father in the song of the house of YHWH, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for the service of the house of God — under the hands of the king: Asaph and Jeduthun and Heman.
And their number, with their kinsmen trained in song to YHWH, all who had understanding, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
And they cast lots for their charge, one alongside another, the small as the great, the one who understands with the pupil.
And the first lot went out for Asaph, to Joseph; Gedaliah the second, he and his brothers and sons, twelve;
The third, Zaccur: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The fourth, to Izri: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The fifth, Nethaniah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The sixth, Bukkiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The seventh, Jesharelah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The eighth, Jeshaiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The ninth, Mattaniah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The tenth, Shimei: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The eleventh, Azarel: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The twelfth, to Hashabiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the thirteenth, Shubael: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the fourteenth, Mattithiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the fifteenth, to Jeremoth: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the sixteenth, to Hananiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the seventeenth, to Joshbekashah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the eighteenth, to Hanani: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the nineteenth, to Mallothi: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twentieth, to Eliathah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-first, to Hothir: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-second, to Giddalti: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-third, to Mahazioth: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-fourth, to Romamti-ezer: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.

1 chronicles_26.t: For the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third and Sakar the fourth, and Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth — for God had blessed him.
And to Shemaiah his son were born sons who ruled over their father's house, for they were mighty men of ability.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni and Rephael and Obed, Elzabad; his kinsmen were men of ability, Elihu and Semakiah.
All these were of the sons of Obed-edom — they and their sons and their kinsmen, men of ability with strength for the service — sixty-two belonging to Obed-edom.
And Meshelemiah had sons and kinsmen, men of ability — eighteen.
And Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief — for he was not the firstborn, but his father appointed him chief —
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and kinsmen of Hosah were thirteen.
To these belonged the divisions of the gatekeepers, to the chiefs of the men, charges corresponding to their kinsmen, to serve in the house of YHWH.
And they cast lots, the small as the great, by their fathers' houses, for gate after gate.
And the lot for the east fell to Shelemiah; and for Zechariah his son, a counsellor with insight, they cast lots, and his lot came out for the north.
To Obed-edom, the south; and to his sons, the house of the stores.
To Shuppim and to Hosah, the west, beside the gate of Shalleketh on the highway that goes up — guard alongside guard.
On the east, six Levites; on the north, four a day; on the south, four a day; and at the stores, two and two.
At the Parbar on the west: four at the highway, two at the Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers, of the sons of the Korahites and of the sons of Merari.
And of the Levites: Ahijah was over the storehouses of the house of God and over the storehouses of the holy things.
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and Joel his brother, who were over the storehouses of the house of YHWH.
Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
And Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was leader over the storehouses.
And his kinsmen, of Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zikri his son, and Shelomith his son.

That Shelomoth and his kinsmen were over all the storehouses of the holy things that David the king had set apart as holy, and the heads of the fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the army.
From the wars and from the plunder they had set apart as holy, to strengthen the house of YHWH.

And all that Samuel the seer had set apart as holy, and Saul son of Kish, and Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah — everything that anyone set apart as holy was under the hand of Shelomith and his kinsmen.
Of the Izharites: Kenaniah and his sons were for the outside work over Israel, as officers and as judges.

Of the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his kinsmen, men of ability, one thousand seven hundred, were over the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the work of YHWH and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites: Jeriah was the chief of the Hebronites, by his generations, by fathers' houses. In the fortieth year of David's reign they were sought out, and mighty men of ability were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.

And his kinsmen, men of ability, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers' houses; and David the king appointed them over the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter of God and matter of the king.

1 chronicles_27.t: And the people of Israel by their number: the heads of the fathers' houses and the commanders of thousands and hundreds and their officers who served the king, for every matter of the divisions that came in and went out month by month, for all the months of the year — each division, twenty-four thousand.
Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
Of the sons of Perez, the chief of all the commanders of the armies for the first month.
And over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and his division; and Mikloth was the leader; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The commander of the third army, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, chief; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
That Benaiah was the mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty; and in his division was Ammizabad his son.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the leader Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
And over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer son of Zikri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
for Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
for the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
for the half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the commanders of the tribes of Israel.
And David did not take their number, from twenty years old and downward, because YHWH had said he would multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count and did not finish, and because of this wrath came upon Israel; and the number did not go up into the number in the account of the days of King David.
And over the storehouses of the king was Azmaveth son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the open country, in the cities and in the villages and in the towers, was Jonathan son of Uzziah.
And over those doing the work of the field, for the labour of the ground, was Ezri son of Kelub.
And over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over what was in the vineyards for the storehouses of wine was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
And over the olive trees and the sycamore figs that were in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the storehouses of oil was Joash.
And over the cattle grazing in Sharon was Shirtai the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the valleys was Shaphat son of Adlai.
And over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the she-asses was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials of the property that belonged to King David.
And Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counsellor; he was a man of understanding and a scribe. And Jehiel son of Hacmoni was with the king's sons.
And Ahithophel was a counsellor of the king; and Hushai the Arkite was the friend of the king.
And after Ahithophel were Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. And the commander of the king's army was Joab.

1 chronicles_28.t: And David assembled all the officials of Israel at Jerusalem: the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions who served the king, and the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the officials over all the property and livestock of the king and of his sons, together with the court officials and the mighty men and every mighty man of ability.

And David the king rose to his feet and said: Hear me, my brothers and my people. As for me, it was with my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of YHWH, and for the footstool of the feet of our God, and I prepared to build.
But God said to me: You shall not build a house for my name, for you are a man of wars and you have shed blood.

And YHWH the God of Israel chose me out of all my father's house to be king over Israel for ever; for he chose Judah as leader, and in the house of Judah, my father's house; and among my father's sons he took pleasure in me, to make me king over all Israel.
And out of all my sons — for YHWH has given me many sons — he chose Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of YHWH over Israel.
And he said to me: Solomon your son, he shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be a son to me, and I will be a father to him.
And I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he is strong to do my commandments and my judgements, as at this day.

And now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of YHWH, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek all the commandments of YHWH your God, so that you may possess the good land and give it as an inheritance to your sons after you for ever.

And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing being; for YHWH searches all hearts and understands every inclination of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; and if you forsake him, he will reject you for ever.
See now that YHWH has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and act.
And David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch and of its houses and its treasuries and its upper rooms and its inner rooms, and the house of the mercy seat;

and the pattern of all that was with him in the spirit, for the courts of the house of YHWH and for all the rooms round about, for the storehouses of the house of God and for the storehouses of the holy things;
and for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of YHWH, and for all the articles of the service of the house of YHWH;
for the gold, by weight for the gold, for all the articles of service and service; for all the articles of silver, by weight, for all the articles of service and service;

and the weight for the lampstands of gold and their lamps of gold, by the weight of a lampstand and a lampstand and its lamps; and for the lampstands of silver, by weight for a lampstand and its lamps, according to the service of a lampstand and a lampstand;
and the gold by weight for the tables of the row, for a table and a table; and silver for the tables of silver;
and the forks and the basins and the jugs, pure gold; and for the bowls of gold, by weight for a bowl and a bowl; and for the bowls of silver, by weight for a bowl and a bowl;
and for the altar of incense, purged gold by weight; and for the pattern of the chariot, the cherubim of gold, spreading out and covering over the ark of the covenant of YHWH.
All this in writing from the hand of YHWH upon me, he made me understand — all the works of the pattern.

And David said to Solomon his son: Be strong and be courageous and act. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for YHWH God, my God, is with you. He will not abandon you and he will not forsake you, until all the work of the service of the house of YHWH is finished.

And here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and with you in every work is every willing man with skill for every service; and the officials and all the people are at all your words.

1 chronicles_29.t: And David the king said to all the assembly: Solomon my son, the one whom God has chosen, is a youth and tender, and the work is great; for the citadel is not for a man but for YHWH God.

And with all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God: the gold for the gold, the silver for the silver, the bronze for the bronze, the iron for the iron and the wood for the wood; onyx stones and stones for setting, stones of antimony and of variegated work, and every precious stone, and alabaster stones in abundance.

And further, because I take pleasure in the house of my God, I have a treasure of gold and silver; I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the house of the holy place:
three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of purged silver, to overlay the walls of the houses;
gold for the gold and silver for the silver, and for all the work by the hand of craftsmen. And who is willing to fill his hand today for YHWH?
And the leaders of the fathers' houses and the leaders of the tribes of Israel and the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials over the king's work, made willing gifts;

and they gave for the service of the house of God five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand darics, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
And whoever had stones with him gave them to the treasury of the house of YHWH, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
And the people rejoiced over their willing giving, for with a whole heart they had given willingly to YHWH; and David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
And David blessed YHWH in the sight of all the assembly, and David said: Blessed are you, YHWH, God of Israel our father, from everlasting and to everlasting.

Yours, YHWH, is the greatness and the might and the splendour and the endurance and the majesty; for all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours, YHWH, is the kingdom, and you are the one who lifts himself as head over all.
And the wealth and the honour are from before you, and you rule over all; and in your hand are strength and might, and in your hand it is to make great and to make strong, to all.
And now, our God, we are giving thanks to you and praising the name of your splendour.
And who am I, and who are my people, that we should retain strength to give willingly like this? For all is from you, and from your hand we have given to you.
For we are sojourners before you, and resident aliens, like all our fathers; our days on the earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope.
YHWH our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build you a house for the name of your holiness — it is from your hand, and all of it is yours.

And I know, my God, that you test the heart and take pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have given all these willingly; and now your people who are found here — I have seen with joy that they give willingly to you.
YHWH, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our fathers, keep this for ever as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart of your people, and direct their heart to yourself.
And to Solomon my son give a whole heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies and your statutes, and to do all of it, and to build the citadel for which I have made preparation.
And David said to all the assembly: Bless YHWH your God. And all the assembly blessed YHWH the God of their fathers; and they bowed low and bowed down to YHWH and to the king.

And they sacrificed sacrifices to YHWH, and they offered up burnt offerings to YHWH on the next day after that day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
And they ate and drank before YHWH on that day with great joy. And they made Solomon son of David king a second time, and anointed him to YHWH as leader, and Zadok as priest.
And Solomon sat on the throne of YHWH as king in place of David his father, and he succeeded; and all Israel listened to him.
And all the officials and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, gave the hand under Solomon the king.
And YHWH made Solomon exceedingly great in the sight of all Israel, and put upon him the majesty of kingship, such as had not been on any king before him over Israel.
And David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
And the days that he reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three.
And he died in a good old age, satisfied with days, wealth and honour; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
And the matters of David the king, the former and the latter, here they are, written in the words of Samuel the seer and in the words of Nathan the prophet and in the words of Gad the seer,
with all his kingship and his might, and the times that passed over him and over Israel and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

1 kings_1.t: And King David was old, come into the days; and they covered him with clothes, but it was not warm for him.

And his servants said to him: Let them seek for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and let her stand before the king and be a nurse for him; and let her lie in your bosom, and it will be warm for my lord the king.
And they sought a beautiful young woman in all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite, and they brought her to the king.
And the young woman was exceedingly beautiful, and she became a nurse to the king and served him; but the king did not know her.
And Adonijah son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying: I will be king. And he acquired for himself a chariot and horsemen, and fifty men running before him.
And his father had not rebuked him from his days, saying: Why have you done thus? And he too was very good of form; and she bore him after Absalom.
And his words were with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped after Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei and Rei, and the mighty men who belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.

And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and cattle and fatlings near the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel; and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.
But Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he did not invite.
And Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon: Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know?
And now, come, let me counsel you counsel, and save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

Come and go in to King David, and you will say to him: Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne? And why has Adonijah become king?
Behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I myself will come in after you and confirm your words.
And Bathsheba went in to the king, to the room; and the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
And Bathsheba bowed low and bowed down to the king. And the king said: What is it to you?
And she said to him: My lord, you yourself swore by YHWH your God to your maidservant: Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.
And now, behold, Adonijah has become king — and now, my lord the king, you do not know.

And he has sacrificed oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and he has invited all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army; but Solomon your servant he has not invited.
And you, my lord the king — the eyes of all Israel are on you, to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
And it will be, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be counted sinners.
And behold, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
And they told the king, saying: Here is Nathan the prophet. And he came before the king and bowed down to the king on his face, to the ground.
And Nathan said: My lord the king, have you said, Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne?

For he has gone down today and sacrificed oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and he has invited all the sons of the king and the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest; and there they are, eating and drinking before him, and they have said: Long live King Adonijah!
But me — me, your servant — and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant, he has not invited.
If this thing has come about from my lord the king, then you have not made known to your servant who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
And King David answered and said: Summon Bathsheba for me. And she came before the king and stood before the king.
And the king swore and said: By the life of YHWH, who has ransomed my life from every trouble —
that just as I swore to you by YHWH the God of Israel, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me and he will sit on my throne in my place — so I will do this day.
And Bathsheba bowed low, face to the ground, and bowed down to the king, and said: May my lord King David live for ever!
And King David said: Summon for me Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.
And the king said to them: Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on the mule that is mine, and bring him down to Gihon.
And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet will anoint him there as king over Israel; and you will blow the ram's horn and say: Long live King Solomon!
And you will come up after him, and he will come in and sit on my throne; and he will reign in my place, and I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king and said: Amen! So may YHWH, the God of my lord the king, say.
Just as YHWH has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon; and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.

And Zadok the priest went down, and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and they caused Solomon to ride on King David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.
And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon; and they blew the ram's horn, and all the people said: Long live King Solomon!
And all the people came up after him, and the people were playing on flutes and rejoicing with great joy; and the ground was split open by their noise.
And Adonijah heard, and all those invited who were with him, and they had finished eating. And Joab heard the sound of the ram's horn and said: Why is the sound of the town in an uproar?
While he was still speaking, behold, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came in. And Adonijah said: Come, for you are a man of worth, and you bear good news.
And Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah: Indeed, our lord King David has made Solomon king.
And the king has sent with him Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride on the king's mule.
And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him as king at Gihon, and they have come up from there rejoicing, and the town was in an uproar. That is the noise that you have heard.
And Solomon has also sat on the throne of the kingship.

And the king's servants have also come to bless our lord King David, saying: May God make Solomon's name better than your name, and may he make his throne greater than your throne. And the king bowed down on the bed.
And the king also said thus: Blessed be YHWH the God of Israel, who has given this day one sitting on my throne, and my own eyes seeing it.
And all those invited who belonged to Adonijah trembled, and they rose and went, each on his way.
And Adonijah was afraid before Solomon; and he rose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

And it was told to Solomon, saying: Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon; and behold, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying: Let King Solomon swear to me this day that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.
And Solomon said: If he becomes a son of worth, not one of his hairs will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, then he will die.
And King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar; and he came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him: Go to your house.

1 kings_2.t: And the days of David drew near to die, and he commanded Solomon his son, saying:
I am going in the way of all the earth. And you will be strong and become a man.

And you will keep the charge of YHWH your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments and his judgements and his testimonies, according to what is written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn;

so that YHWH may establish his word that he spoke concerning me, saying: If your sons keep their way, to walk before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul, then there will not be cut off to you a man from the throne of Israel.

And you also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me — what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether: he killed them and put the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war on his belt that was on his loins and on his sandals that were on his feet.
And you will act according to your wisdom, and you will not bring his grey head down in peace to Sheol.
And to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite you will do loyalty, and they will be among those who eat at your table; for so they drew near to me when I fled from before Absalom your brother.

And behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera the Benjaminite from Bahurim; and he cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim. And he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by YHWH, saying: I will not put you to death by the sword.
And now, do not leave him unpunished, for you are a wise man; and you will know what you are to do to him, and you will bring his grey head down in blood to Sheol.
And David lay down with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David.
And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.
And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his reign was firmly established.
And Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she said: Is your coming peace? And he said: Peace.
And he said: I have a word for you. And she said: Speak.
And he said: You know that the kingship was mine, and all Israel set their faces on me to be king; but the kingship turned round and became my brother's, for it was his from YHWH.
And now, one petition I am asking from you; do not turn away my face. And she said to him: Speak.
And he said: Say, please, to Solomon the king — for he will not turn away your face — that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.
And Bathsheba said: Good. I myself will speak to the king concerning you.

And Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonijah. And the king rose to meet her and bowed down to her, and he sat on his throne; and he placed a throne for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
And she said: One small petition I am asking from you; do not turn away my face. And the king said to her: Ask, my mother, for I will not turn away your face.
And she said: Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as a wife.

And King Solomon answered and said to his mother: And why are you asking Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingship too, for he is my brother, older than I — for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!
And King Solomon swore by YHWH, saying: So may God do to me and so may he add, if it is not at the cost of his own life that Adonijah has spoken this word.
And now, by the life of YHWH, who established me and set me on the throne of David my father and who made me a house just as he spoke — this day Adonijah will be put to death.
And King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he fell on him, and he died.

And to Abiathar the priest the king said: Go to Anathoth, to your own fields, for you are a man of death; but on this day I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of Lord YHWH before David my father, and because you were afflicted in all that my father was afflicted.
And Solomon drove out Abiathar from being a priest to YHWH, to fulfil the word of YHWH that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
And the report came to Joab — for Joab had turned aside after Adonijah, though after Absalom he had not turned aside — and Joab fled to the tent of YHWH and took hold of the horns of the altar.
And it was told to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of YHWH, and behold, he was beside the altar. And Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying: Go, fall on him.

And Benaiah came to the tent of YHWH and said to him: Thus says the king — come out. And he said: No, for here I will die. And Benaiah brought the king back word, saying: Thus Joab spoke, and thus he answered me.
And the king said to him: Do just as he has spoken; fall on him and bury him, and you will remove from me and from my father's house the blood without cause that Joab shed.

And YHWH will return his blood on his own head, because he fell on two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword — and my father David did not know: Abner son of Ner the commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether the commander of the army of Judah.
And their blood will return on the head of Joab and on the head of his offspring for ever; but to David and to his offspring and to his house and to his throne there will be peace for ever from YHWH.
And Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and fell on him and put him to death; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
And the king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the army; and Zadok the priest the king put in the place of Abiathar.
And the king sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him: Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere at all.
And it will be, on the day you go out and cross the wadi of Kidron, you will surely know that you will surely die; your blood will be on your own head.
And Shimei said to the king: The word is good. Just as my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do. And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.
And it happened at the end of three years that two of Shimei's servants fled to Achish son of Maacah king of Gath; and they told Shimei, saying: Behold, your servants are in Gath.
And Shimei rose and saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his servants; and Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
And it was told to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.

And the king sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him: Did I not make you swear by YHWH and warn you, saying: On the day you go out and go anywhere at all, you will surely know that you will surely die? And you said to me: The word is good; I have heard.
And why have you not kept the oath of YHWH and the command that I commanded you?
And the king said to Shimei: You know all the evil that your heart knows, which you did to David my father; and YHWH will return your evil on your own head.
And King Solomon will be blessed, and the throne of David will be established before YHWH for ever.
And the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and fell on him, and he died. And the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.

1 kings_3.t: And Solomon made himself son-in-law to Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her to the city of David, until he had finished building his own house and the house of YHWH and the wall of Jerusalem all around.
Only, the people were sacrificing at the high places, because a house had not been built for the name of YHWH until those days.
And Solomon loved YHWH, to walk in the statutes of David his father — only, at the high places he was sacrificing and making smoke.
And the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place; a thousand burnt offerings Solomon offered up on that altar.
At Gibeon YHWH appeared to Solomon in a dream of the night, and God said: Ask what I shall give you.

And Solomon said: You have done with your servant David my father great steadfast love, just as he walked before you in faithfulness and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart with you; and you have kept for him this great steadfast love, and you have given him a son sitting on his throne, as at this day.
And now, YHWH my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father; and I am a young lad — I do not know going out and coming in.
And your servant is in the midst of your people whom you have chosen, a numerous people that cannot be numbered or counted for multitude.
And you will give your servant a listening heart, to judge your people, to distinguish between good and evil; for who is able to judge this massive people of yours?
And the thing was good in the eyes of the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

And God said to him: Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked for yourself many days, and have not asked for yourself wealth, and have not asked the life of your enemies — but you have asked for yourself understanding, to hear judgement —
behold, I do according to your words. Behold, I give you a wise and understanding heart, so that there has been none like you before you, and after you none will arise like you.
And also what you did not ask I give you — both wealth and honour — so that there has not been anyone like you among the kings all your days.
And if you will walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, just as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.

And Solomon awoke, and behold — a dream. And he came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and he offered up burnt offerings and made peace offerings, and he made a feast for all his servants.
Then two women, prostitutes, came to the king and stood before him.
And the one woman said: Pardon me, my lord — I and this woman are dwelling in one house, and I gave birth with her in the house.
And it happened on the third day after I gave birth that this woman also gave birth; and we were together — there was no stranger with us in the house, only the two of us in the house.
And this woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.
And she rose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant was sleeping, and she laid him in her bosom; and her dead son she laid in my bosom.
And I rose in the morning to suckle my son, and behold — he was dead. And I looked at him carefully in the morning, and behold — it was not my son whom I had borne.

And the other woman said: No — my son is the living one and your son is the dead one. And this one was saying: No — your son is the dead one and my son is the living one. And they spoke before the king.
And the king said: This one is saying, This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one; and this one is saying, No — your son is the dead one and my son is the living one.
And the king said: Take a sword for me. And they brought the sword before the king.
And the king said: Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to one.

And the woman whose son was the living one said to the king — for her compassion grew warm over her son — and she said: Pardon me, my lord, give her the living child, and do not kill, do not kill him. And this one was saying: It will belong neither to me nor to you — cut!
And the king answered and said: Give her the living child, and do not kill, do not kill him — she is his mother.
And all Israel heard the judgement that the king had judged, and they were afraid before the king; for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to do justice.

1 kings_4.t: And King Solomon was king over all Israel.
And these were the officials who were his: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, the recorder;
and Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army; and Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
and Azariah son of Nathan over the overseers; and Zabud son of Nathan, a priest, the king's friend;
and Ahishar over the house; and Adoniram son of Abda over the forced labour.
And Solomon had twelve overseers over all Israel, and they supplied the king and his household; one month in the year it fell on each one to supply.
And these are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker, in Makaz and in Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;
Ben-hesed, in Arubboth — to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher;
Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor — Taphath the daughter of Solomon became his wife;
Baana son of Ahilud: Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead — to him belonged the villages of Jair son of Manasseh which are in Gilead; to him belonged the region of Argob which is in Bashan, sixty large cities with wall and bar of bronze;
Ahinadab son of Iddo, at Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he too took Basemath the daughter of Solomon as a wife;
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and one overseer who was in the land.
Judah and Israel were numerous, like the sand that is by the sea for multitude — eating and drinking and rejoicing.
And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River, the land of the Philistines, and as far as the border of Egypt; they were bringing tribute and serving Solomon all the days of his life.
And Solomon's food for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of flour,
ten fat cattle and twenty pasture cattle and a hundred sheep, apart from deer and gazelle and roe-deer and fattened birds.
For he was ruling over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah as far as Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River; and he had peace on all his sides round about.
And Judah and Israel dwelt in security, each under his own vine and under his own fig tree, from Dan as far as Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariotry, and twelve thousand horsemen.
And those overseers supplied King Solomon and everyone who came near to the table of King Solomon, each in his month; they left nothing lacking.
And the barley and the straw for the horses and for the steeds they brought to the place where it was, each according to his measure.
And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding, very great, and breadth of heart, like the sand that is on the seashore.
And Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the people of the east and than all the wisdom of Egypt.
And he was wiser than all humankind — than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman and Kalkol and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his name was among all the nations round about.
And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five.

And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that comes out of the wall; and he spoke about the animals and about the birds and about the creeping things and about the fish.
And they came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

1 kings_5.t: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had been a friend to David all the days.
And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying:
You know David my father, that he was not able to build a house for the name of YHWH his God because of the war that surrounded him, until YHWH put them under the soles of my feet.
And now YHWH my God has given me rest on every side; there is no opponent and no evil occurrence.

And here I am, saying that I will build a house for the name of YHWH my God, just as YHWH spoke to David my father, saying: Your son, whom I will put in your place on your throne — he will build the house for my name.

And now, command that they cut cedars for me from Lebanon; and my servants will be with your servants, and the wages of your servants I will give to you, according to all that you say. For you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.
And it happened, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced exceedingly and said: Blessed be YHWH this day, who has given David a wise son over this great people.
And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying: I have heard what you sent to me; I myself will do all your desire in cedar timber and in cypress timber.

My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts on the sea to the place that you send me word of, and I will break them up there, and you will carry them away. And you will do my desire by giving food for my household.
And Hiram was giving Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber, all his desire.
And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of pressed oil. Thus Solomon gave to Hiram year by year.
And YHWH gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had spoken to him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.
And King Solomon raised forced labour out of all Israel; and the forced labour was thirty thousand men.
And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in relays: a month they would be in Lebanon, two months at home. And Adoniram was over the forced labour.
And Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stone-cutters in the hill country,
apart from the chiefs of Solomon's overseers who were over the work: three thousand three hundred, who ruled over the people doing the work.
And the king commanded, and they quarried large stones, costly stones, to found the house with dressed stones.
And Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites cut them to shape; and they prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

1 kings_6.t: And it happened in the four hundred and eightieth year after the coming out of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv — that is the second month — of Solomon's reigning over Israel, that he built the house for YHWH.
And the house that King Solomon built for YHWH — sixty cubits was its length, and twenty its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.
And the porch, in front of the temple of the house — twenty cubits was its length, across the breadth of the house; ten by the cubit was its breadth, in front of the house.
And he made for the house windows of narrowing frames.
And he built against the wall of the house an extension all around — against the walls of the house all around, for the temple and for the innermost room; and he made side-chambers all around.

The lower extension was five by the cubit in its breadth, and the middle six by the cubit in its breadth, and the third seven by the cubit in its breadth; for he made ledges for the house all around, on the outside, so as not to take hold in the walls of the house.
And the house, when it was built, was built of whole stone from the quarry; and hammers and the axe, any article of iron, was not heard in the house when it was built.
The entrance of the middle side-chamber was at the south side of the house; and by stairs they went up to the middle, and from the middle to the third.
And he built the house and finished it; and he covered the house with beams and planks of cedar.
And he built the extension against all the house — five cubits was its height — and he fastened it to the house with cedar timber.
And the word of YHWH came to Solomon, saying:

This house that you are building — if you will walk in my statutes and observe my judgements and keep all my commandments, to walk in them, then I will establish my word with you that I spoke to David your father;
and I will dwell among the sons of Israel, and I will not abandon my people Israel.
And Solomon built the house and finished it.

And he built the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling he overlaid with wood on the inside; and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
And he built twenty cubits from the rear parts of the house with boards of cedar, from the floor to the walls; and he built it on the inside as an innermost room, as the holy of holies.
And forty by the cubit was the house — that is, the temple in front.
And cedar was on the house within — carving of gourds and spread-out flowers; the whole was cedar, no stone was visible.
And an innermost room in the middle of the house, on the inside, he prepared, to put there the ark of the covenant of YHWH.
And in front of the innermost room — twenty cubits length, and twenty cubits breadth, and twenty cubits its height; and he overlaid it with refined gold, and he overlaid the altar with cedar.
And Solomon overlaid the house on the inside with refined gold; and he drew chains of gold across in front of the innermost room, and he overlaid it with gold.
And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until all the house was finished; and the whole altar that belonged to the innermost room he overlaid with gold.
And he made in the innermost room two cherubim of olive wood, ten cubits its height.
And five cubits was the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the second wing of the cherub — ten cubits from the ends of its wings to the ends of its wings.
And ten by the cubit was the second cherub; one measurement and one shape belonged to the two cherubim.
The height of the one cherub was ten by the cubit, and thus the second cherub.

And he put the cherubim in the middle of the inner house, and they spread out the wings of the cherubim; and the wing of the one touched the wall, and the wing of the second cherub was touching the second wall; and their wings, towards the middle of the house, were touching wing to wing.
And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
And all the walls of the house round about he carved with carved engravings of cherubim and palm trees and spread-out flowers, within and without.
And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, within and without.
And for the entrance of the innermost room he made doors of olive wood; the pillar, the doorposts, a fifth.

And two doors of olive wood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim and palm trees and spread-out flowers, and overlaid them with gold; and he hammered out the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.
And thus he made for the entrance of the temple doorposts of olive wood, a fourth.
And two doors of cypress wood: two sides of the one door revolving, and two hangings of the second door revolving.
And he carved cherubim and palm trees and spread-out flowers, and overlaid with gold, made smooth over the carved work.
And he built the inner court, three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams.
In the fourth year the house of YHWH was founded, in the month of Ziv.
And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — that is the eighth month — the house was complete in all its parts and according to all its specifications; and he built it seven years.

1 kings_7.t: And his own house Solomon built thirteen years, and he completed all his house.

And he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon — a hundred cubits its length, and fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height — upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.
And it was panelled with cedar above, over the side-chambers that were on the pillars — forty-five, fifteen the row.
And window frames, three rows; and window opposite window, three times.
And all the openings and the doorposts were square of framework; and the front, window opposite window, three times.
And the Porch of the Pillars he made — fifty cubits its length and thirty cubits its breadth — and a porch in front of them, and pillars and a threshold in front of them.
And the Porch of the Throne, where he would judge — the Porch of Judgement — he made; and it was panelled with cedar from the floor to the floor.
And his own house where he would dwell, in the other court, inward from the porch, was of this same workmanship. And he made a house like this porch for Pharaoh's daughter, whom Solomon had taken.
All these were costly stones, according to the measurements of dressed stone, sawn with the saw within and without — and from the foundation to the coping, and from the outside to the great court.
And it was founded with costly stones, large stones — stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
And above were costly stones, according to the measurements of dressed stone, and cedar.
And the great court all around had three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams — and so for the inner court of the house of YHWH, and for the porch of the house.
And King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

He was the son of a widow woman from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a Tyrian man, a worker in bronze. And he was filled with the wisdom and the skill and the knowledge to do any work in bronze; and he came to King Solomon and did all his work.
And he fashioned the two pillars of bronze: eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and a line of twelve cubits went round the second pillar.
And two capitals he made, to set on the tops of the pillars, cast of bronze: five cubits was the height of the one capital, and five cubits the height of the second capital.
Networks, the work of a network; festoons, the work of chains, for the capitals that were on the top of the pillars: seven for the one capital and seven for the second capital.
And he made the pillars; and two rows all around on the one network, to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates; and so he did for the second capital.
And the capitals that were on the top of the pillars were a work of lilies, in the porch — four cubits.
And the capitals were on the two pillars, also above, close to the bulge that was beside the network; and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows all around, on the second capital.
And he set up the pillars for the porch of the temple; and he set up the right-hand pillar and called its name Jakin, and he set up the left-hand pillar and called its name Boaz.
And on the top of the pillars was a work of lilies. And the work of the pillars was complete.
And he made the sea, cast metal: ten by the cubit from its lip to its lip, round all about; and five by the cubit its height; and a measuring line of thirty by the cubit went round it all about.
And gourds were beneath its lip all around, encircling it, ten by the cubit, surrounding the sea all around; the gourds were two rows, cast in its casting.
It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, and three facing west, and three facing south, and three facing east; and the sea was upon them, above, and all their hindquarters were inward.
And its thickness was a handbreadth, and its lip was like the work of the lip of a cup, a lily blossom; it held two thousand baths.
And he made the ten stands of bronze: four by the cubit was the length of the one stand, and four by the cubit its breadth, and three by the cubit its height.
And this was the work of the stand: they had rims, and rims between the crossbars.
And on the rims that were between the crossbars were lions, oxen and cherubim; and on the crossbars was a base above; and beneath the lions and the oxen were garlands, hanging work.
And four bronze wheels belonged to the one stand, and bronze axles; and its four feet had supports; beneath the washbasin were the supports, cast, beside each one, garlands.

And its opening, from inside the capital and upward, was a cubit; and its opening was round, the work of a base, a cubit and a half of the cubit; and also on its opening were carvings; and their rims were square, not round.
And the four wheels were beneath the rims, and the axle-supports of the wheels were in the stand; and the height of the one wheel was a cubit and a half of the cubit.
And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axle-supports and their rims and their spokes and their hubs — the whole was cast.
And four supports were at the four corners of the one stand; from the stand were its supports.
And at the top of the stand was half of the cubit in height, round all about; and on the top of the stand its axle-supports and its rims were of one piece with it.
And he engraved on the plates of its axle-supports and on its rims cherubim, lions and palm trees, according to the clear space of each, with garlands all around.
Like this he made the ten stands: one casting, one measurement, one shape for all of them.
And he made ten washbasins of bronze: the one washbasin held forty baths; the one washbasin was four by the cubit; one washbasin was on the one stand, for the ten stands.
And he put the stands, five on the side of the house from the right and five on the side of the house from its left; and the sea he put from the right side of the house, eastward, opposite the south.
And Hiram made the washbasins and the shovels and the basins. And Hiram finished doing all the work that he did for King Solomon, the house of YHWH:
two pillars; and the bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars, two; and the networks, two, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
and the pomegranates, four hundred, for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for the one network — to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the face of the pillars;
and the stands, ten; and the washbasins, ten, on the stands;
and the one sea; and the oxen, twelve, under the sea;
and the pots and the shovels and the basins. And all these articles that Hiram made for King Solomon, the house of YHWH, were of polished bronze.
In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the thickness of the ground, between Succoth and Zarethan.
And Solomon left all the articles unweighed, from very very great abundance; the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
And Solomon made all the articles that were in the house of YHWH: the altar of gold; and the table on which was the bread of the presence, of gold;
and the lampstands, five from the right and five from the left, before the innermost room, of refined gold; and the blossom and the lamps and the tongs, of gold;

and the bowls and the snuffers and the basins and the pans and the firepans, of refined gold; and the sockets for the doors of the inner house, for the holy of holies, and for the doors of the house of the temple, of gold.

And all the work that King Solomon did, the house of YHWH, was complete. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father — the silver and the gold and the articles — and he put them in the treasuries of the house of YHWH.

1 kings_8.t: Then Solomon called together the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of YHWH from the city of David — that is Zion.
And every man of Israel assembled to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the festival — that is the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests lifted the ark.
And they brought up the ark of YHWH and the tent of meeting and all the holy articles that were in the tent; and the priests and the Levites brought them up.
And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered to him were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.
And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of YHWH to its place, to the innermost room of the house, to the holy of holies, to beneath the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim were spreading out wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered over the ark and over its poles from above.
And the poles were long, and the heads of the poles were visible from the holy place in front of the innermost room, but they were not visible outside; and they have been there until this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone that Moses placed there at Horeb, where YHWH made a covenant with the sons of Israel when they came out from the land of Egypt.
And it happened, when the priests came out from the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of YHWH.
And the priests were not able to stand to serve because of the cloud, for the glory of YHWH filled the house of YHWH.
Then Solomon said: YHWH has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
Building, I have built a house of loftiness for you, a place for your dwelling for ever.
And the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.
And he said: Blessed be YHWH the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and with his hand has fulfilled it, saying:

Since the day I brought out my people Israel from Egypt, I did not choose a city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name to be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.
And it was with the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of YHWH the God of Israel.
And YHWH said to David my father: Because it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.
Only, you yourself will not build the house; but your son who comes out from your loins — he will build the house for my name.

And YHWH has established his word that he spoke; and I have arisen in place of David my father and have sat on the throne of Israel, just as YHWH spoke, and I have built the house for the name of YHWH the God of Israel.
And I have set there a place for the ark, where the covenant of YHWH is, which he made with our fathers when he brought them out from the land of Egypt.
And Solomon stood before the altar of YHWH, in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms to the heavens.

And he said: YHWH, God of Israel, there is no God like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath — keeping the covenant and the steadfast love for your servants who walk before you with all their heart;
you who have kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him — and you spoke with your mouth and with your hand you have fulfilled it, as at this day.

And now, YHWH, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying: There will not be cut off to you a man from before me sitting on the throne of Israel — only if your sons keep their way, to walk before me just as you have walked before me.
And now, God of Israel, let your word be established, please, which you spoke to your servant David my father.
For will God really dwell on the earth? Behold, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain you — how much less this house that I have built!
And you will turn to the prayer of your servant and to his supplication, YHWH my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer that your servant is praying before you today,
so that your eyes may be open towards this house night and day, towards the place of which you said, My name will be there — to listen to the prayer that your servant prays towards this place.

And you will listen to the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel, which they pray towards this place; and you yourself will listen in the place of your dwelling, in the heavens — and you will listen and forgive.
When a man sins against his neighbour and an oath is imposed on him to put him under oath, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house —

then you will listen in the heavens and act, and judge your servants: to condemn the guilty, to bring his conduct on his own head, and to declare righteous the righteous, to give to him according to his righteousness.
When your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they sin against you, and they turn back to you and give thanks to your name and pray and seek favour before you in this house —
then you will listen in the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the ground that you gave to their fathers.
When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they sin against you, and they pray towards this place and give thanks to your name and turn back from their sin because you afflict them —

then you will listen in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk; and you will give rain on your land that you gave to your people as an inheritance.
When there is famine in the land, when there is pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, grasshopper; when his enemy besieges him in the land of his gates — any plague, any sickness —
any prayer, any supplication that comes to any human, to all your people Israel, who each knows the plague of his own heart and spreads out his palms towards this house —

then you will listen in the heavens, the place of your dwelling, and forgive and act, and give to each according to all his ways, since you know his heart — for you alone know the heart of all the children of humankind —
so that they may fear you all the days that they are alive on the face of the ground that you gave to our fathers.
And also to the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, and comes from a distant land for the sake of your name —
for they will hear of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — and he comes and prays towards this house —

then you will listen in the heavens, the place of your dwelling, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for — so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name, to fear you as your people Israel do, and to know that your name has been called over this house that I have built.
When your people go out to battle against their enemy by the way that you send them, and they pray to YHWH towards the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name —
then you will listen in the heavens to their prayer and to their supplication, and do their justice.

When they sin against you — for there is no human who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them up before an enemy, and their captors take them captive to the land of the enemy, distant or near,

and they bring it back to their heart in the land where they have been taken captive, and they turn back and seek favour before you in the land of their captors, saying: We have sinned and done wrong, we have acted wickedly —

and they return to you with all their heart and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and they pray to you towards their land that you gave to their fathers, the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name —
then you will listen in the heavens, the place of your dwelling, to their prayer and to their supplication, and do their justice;

and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions by which they transgressed against you; and you will make them objects of compassion before their captors, and they will have compassion on them.
for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out from Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.
so that your eyes may be open to the supplication of your servant and to the supplication of your people Israel, to listen to them in all their calling to you.

For you yourself separated them for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, just as you spoke by the hand of Moses your servant when you brought out our fathers from Egypt, Lord YHWH.

And it happened, when Solomon had finished praying to YHWH all this prayer and supplication, that he rose from before the altar of YHWH, from kneeling on his knees with his palms spread out to the heavens.
And he stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying:
Blessed be YHWH, who has given a resting place to his people Israel according to all that he spoke; not one word has fallen from all his good word that he spoke by the hand of Moses his servant.
May YHWH our God be with us, just as he was with our fathers; may he not forsake us and not abandon us,
to incline our heart to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgements, which he commanded our fathers.

And may these words of mine, with which I have sought favour before YHWH, be near to YHWH our God day and night, to do the justice of his servant and the justice of his people Israel, the matter of a day in its day;
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that YHWH — he is God; there is no other.
And let your heart be complete with YHWH our God, to walk in his statutes and to keep his commandments, as at this day.
And the king and all Israel with him were sacrificing a sacrifice before YHWH.

And Solomon sacrificed the sacrifice of the peace offerings that he sacrificed to YHWH: cattle, twenty-two thousand, and sheep, a hundred and twenty thousand. And the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of YHWH.

On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of YHWH, because he offered there the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings; for the bronze altar that was before YHWH was too small to contain the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings.
And Solomon observed the festival at that time, and all Israel with him — a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the wadi of Egypt — before YHWH our God, seven days and seven days: fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king; and they went to their tents joyful and good of heart on account of all the good that YHWH had done for David his servant and for Israel his people.

1 kings_9.t: And it happened, when Solomon had finished building the house of YHWH and the house of the king and all Solomon's desire that he delighted to do,
that YHWH appeared to Solomon a second time, just as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

And YHWH said to him: I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you have made before me. I have consecrated this house that you have built, to put my name there for ever; and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.

And as for you, if you will walk before me just as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, doing according to all that I have commanded you, and you will keep my statutes and my judgements,
then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel for ever, just as I spoke concerning David your father, saying: There will not be cut off to you a man from the throne of Israel.
If you and your sons surely turn back from after me and do not keep my commandments and my statutes that I have set before you, and you go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

then I will cut off Israel from the face of the ground that I have given them; and the house that I have consecrated for my name I will cast out from before me, and Israel will become a byword and a taunt among all the peoples.
And this house will be most high; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say: On account of what has YHWH done thus to this land and to this house?

And they will say: Because they forsook YHWH their God, who brought out their fathers from the land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them — therefore YHWH has brought upon them all this calamity.
And it happened at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses — the house of YHWH and the house of the king —
Hiram king of Tyre having supported Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber and with gold, according to all his desire — then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they were not pleasing in his eyes.
