And he said: What are these cities that you have given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Cabul, until this day.
And Hiram had sent the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.
And this is the matter of the forced labour that King Solomon raised, to build the house of YHWH and his own house and the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed the Canaanites dwelling in the city; and he had given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
And Solomon built Gezer, and lower Beth-horon,
and Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,

and all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, and the cities of the chariotry and the cities of the horsemen — and Solomon's desire that he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who remained of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of the sons of Israel —
their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had not been able to devote to destruction — Solomon raised them for forced labour of labouring, until this day.
But of the sons of Israel Solomon did not make a slave; for they were the men of war and his servants and his officials and his officers, and the commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
These were the chiefs of the overseers who were over Solomon's work: five hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people doing the work.
Only, Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her own house that he had built for her; then he built the Millo.

And Solomon offered up three times in the year burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he had built for YHWH, and made offerings smoke with it, which was before YHWH. And he completed the house.
And King Solomon made a fleet at Ezion-geber, which is beside Elath on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Edom.
And Hiram sent in the fleet his servants, men of ships who knew the sea, with the servants of Solomon.
And they went to Ophir and took from there gold — four hundred and twenty talents — and brought it to King Solomon.

1 kings_10.t: And the queen of Sheba was hearing the report of Solomon in connection with the name of YHWH, and she came to test him with hard questions.
And she came to Jerusalem with a very numerous retinue, camels carrying spices and very much gold and precious stones; and she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was with her heart.
And Solomon told her all her words; there was nothing hidden from the king that he did not tell her.
And the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built,

and the food of his table, and the seating of his servants, and the standing of his attendants, and their clothing, and his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings that he offered up at the house of YHWH — and there was no more breath in her.
And she said to the king: The word that I heard in my own land about your words and about your wisdom was truth.
And I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes saw; and behold, the half was not told to me. You have added wisdom and good beyond the report that I heard.
How blessed are your people! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing your wisdom!
May YHWH your God be blessed, who delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel! Because YHWH loves Israel for ever, he has appointed you king, to do justice and righteousness.
And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and very much spice, and precious stones. There has never again come such abundance of spice as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
And also the fleet of Hiram, which carried gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir very much almug wood and precious stones.

And the king made the almug wood into supports for the house of YHWH and for the house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers. Such almug wood has never come, nor has it been seen, until this day.
And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire that she asked, besides what he gave her according to the hand of King Solomon. And she turned and went to her own land, she and her servants.
And the weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold.
apart from the men of the merchants and the merchandise of the traders, and all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land.
And King Solomon made two hundred body shields of beaten gold; six hundred of gold he put on the one body shield.
And three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold he put on the one shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
And the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with refined gold.
Six steps belonged to the throne, and a round top belonged to the throne behind it; and arms were on this side and on that beside the place of the seat, and two lions were standing beside the arms.
And twelve lions were standing there on the six steps, on this side and on that. Nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.

And all King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the articles of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were refined gold. There was no silver; it was not reckoned as anything in the days of Solomon.
For the king had a fleet of Tarshish on the sea with the fleet of Hiram; once in three years the fleet of Tarshish would come, carrying gold and silver, ivory and monkeys and apes.
And King Solomon became great, more than all the kings of the earth, in wealth and in wisdom.
And all the earth was seeking the face of Solomon, to hear his wisdom that God had put in his heart.
And they were bringing, each his gift — articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments and weaponry and spices, horses and mules — the matter of a year in its year.
And Solomon gathered chariotry and horsemen; and he had a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. And he led them in the cities of the chariotry and with the king in Jerusalem.
And the king made silver in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars he made like the sycamores that are in the Shephelah, for abundance.
And the export of the horses that Solomon had was from Egypt and from Que; the king's traders would take them from Que for a price.

And a chariot came up and went out from Egypt for six hundred of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty; and so, by their hand, they brought them out for all the kings of the Hittites and for the kings of Aram.

1 kings_11.t: And King Solomon loved many foreign women, and the daughter of Pharaoh — Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite women —

from the nations of which YHWH had said to the sons of Israel: You shall not go among them, and they shall not go among you; truly they will turn aside your heart after their gods. To these Solomon clung, to love them.
And he had seven hundred wives, noblewomen, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned aside his heart.
And it happened at the time of Solomon's old age that his wives turned aside his heart after other gods; and his heart was not complete with YHWH his God, like the heart of David his father.
And Solomon walked after Astarte the god of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the detestable thing of the Ammonites.
And Solomon did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and did not fully follow after YHWH like David his father.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable thing of Moab, on the mountain that is opposite Jerusalem; and for Molech, the detestable thing of the sons of Ammon.
And so he did for all his foreign wives, who were making offerings smoke and sacrificing to their gods.
And YHWH was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned aside from YHWH the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,
and had commanded him concerning this matter, not to walk after other gods; and he did not observe what YHWH commanded.

And YHWH said to Solomon: Because this has been with you, and you have not observed my covenant and my statutes that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
Only, in your days I will not do it, for the sake of David your father; from the hand of your son I will tear it away.
Only, I will not tear away the whole kingdom; one tribe I will give to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.
And YHWH raised up an opponent against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite; he was of the royal offspring in Edom.
And it happened, when David was with Edom, when Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, that he struck down every male in Edom —
for six months Joab remained there, and all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
And Hadad fled, he and Edomite men from among his father's servants with him, to go to Egypt; and Hadad was a young lad.
And they arose from Midian and came to Paran, and took men with them from Paran; and they came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he gave him a house and assigned him food, and gave him land.
And Hadad found great favour in the eyes of Pharaoh, and he gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, and Tahpenes weaned him within the house of Pharaoh; and Genubath was in the house of Pharaoh among the sons of Pharaoh.
And Hadad heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army had died; and Hadad said to Pharaoh: Let me go, and I will go to my own land.
And Pharaoh said to him: But what are you lacking with me, that here you are seeking to go to your own land? And he said: No — but you must surely let me go.
And God raised up against him an opponent: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from Hadadezer king of Zobah his master.
And he gathered men to himself and became the leader of a marauding band, when David killed them; and they went to Damascus and dwelt in it, and they reigned in Damascus.
And he was an opponent to Israel all the days of Solomon — besides the harm that Hadad did; and he loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
And Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephrathite from Zeredah — and the name of his mother was Zeruah, a widow woman — a servant of Solomon, also raised a hand against the king.
And this is the reason why he raised a hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo, he closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
And the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of strength; and Solomon saw the young man, that he was a doer of work, and he appointed him over all the forced labour of the house of Joseph.

And it happened at that time, when Jeroboam had gone out from Jerusalem, that Ahijah the Shilonite the prophet found him on the way; and he was covering himself with a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open country.
And Ahijah seized the new cloak that was on him, and tore it into twelve pieces.
And he said to Jeroboam: Take for yourself ten pieces; for thus says YHWH the God of Israel: Here I am, about to tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give you the ten tribes.
And the one tribe will be his, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

Because they have forsaken me and bowed down to Astarte the god of the Sidonians, to Chemosh the god of Moab and to Milcom the god of the sons of Ammon; and they have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my eyes, and my statutes and my judgements, like David his father.
But I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, for I will make him a ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, who observed my commandments and my statutes.
And I will take the kingship from the hand of his son and give it to you — the ten tribes.
And to his son I will give one tribe, so that there may be a lamp for David my servant all the days before me in Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen for myself, to put my name there.
And you I will take, and you will reign over all that your being desires, and you will be king over Israel.

And it will be, if you listen to all that I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right in my eyes, observing my statutes and my commandments, just as David my servant did — then I will be with you and will build for you an enduring house, just as I built for David; and I will give Israel to you.
And I will afflict the offspring of David on account of this — but not all the days.
And Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death; and Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
And the rest of the matters of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom — are they not written on the book of the matters of Solomon?
And the days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.
And Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

1 kings_12.t: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
And it happened, when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard — and he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from before King Solomon — that Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt.
And they sent and summoned him; and Jeroboam came, and all the assembly of Israel, and they spoke to Rehoboam, saying:
Your father made our yoke hard; and you now — lighten some of your father's hard service and some of his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you.
And he said to them: Go yet three days, and return to me. And the people went.
And King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had been standing before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying: How are you counselling to bring back a word to this people?
And they spoke to him, saying: If today you will be a servant to this people and serve them, and answer them and speak kind words to them, then they will be your servants all the days.
But he forsook the counsel of the elders that they had counselled him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
And he said to them: What are you counselling, that we may bring back a word to this people, who have spoken to me, saying: Lighten some of the yoke that your father put on us?

And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying: Thus you shall say to this people who have spoken to you, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy and you — lighten it from us; thus you shall speak to them: My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
And now, my father loaded a heavy yoke on you, and I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, and I will discipline you with scorpions.
And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had spoken, saying: Return to me on the third day.
And the king answered the people harshly, and he forsook the counsel of the elders that they had counselled him.

And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying: My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, and I will discipline you with scorpions.
And the king did not listen to the people; for it was a turn from YHWH, so as to establish his word that YHWH had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

And all Israel saw that the king had not listened to them; and the people brought the king back word, saying: What portion have we in David? And there is no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David! And Israel went to its tents.
And the sons of Israel who were dwelling in the cities of Judah — Rehoboam reigned over them.

And King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the forced labour; and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Rehoboam made a strong effort to get up into the chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
And Israel has rebelled against the house of David until this day.

And it happened, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent and called him to the congregation and made him king over all Israel. There was no one after the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.

And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and called together all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin — a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, makers of war — to do battle with the house of Israel, to restore the kingship to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
And the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying:
Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:

Thus says YHWH: You shall not go up and shall not do battle with your countrymen, the sons of Israel; return each to his own house, for this thing has come about from me. And they listened to the word of YHWH and turned back to go, according to the word of YHWH.
And Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and dwelt in it; and he went out from there and built Penuel.
And Jeroboam said in his heart: Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.

If this people go up to make sacrifices in the house of YHWH in Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will return to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah; and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.
And the king took counsel and made two calves of gold; and he said to them: It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
And he set the one in Bethel, and the one he put in Dan.
And this thing became a sin; and the people went before the one, as far as Dan.
And he made a house of high places, and made priests from the ends of the people, who were not of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam appointed a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the festival that was in Judah; and he offered up on the altar. So he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made; and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.

And he offered up on the altar that he had made in Bethel, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month — in the month that he had devised from his own heart; and he appointed a festival for the sons of Israel, and he went up on the altar to make offerings smoke.

1 kings_13.t: And behold, a man of God came from Judah by the word of YHWH to Bethel; and Jeroboam was standing at the altar to make offerings smoke.

And he called out against the altar by the word of YHWH and said: Altar, altar! Thus says YHWH: Behold, a son is to be born to the house of David — Josiah is his name — and he will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who make offerings smoke on you, and human bones will be burned on you.
And he gave a sign on that day, saying: This is the sign that YHWH has spoken — behold, the altar is about to be torn apart, and the fatty ash that is on it will be poured out.

And it happened, when the king heard the word of the man of God that he called out against the altar at Bethel, that Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying: Seize him! And his hand that he stretched out against him dried up, and he was not able to bring it back to himself.
And the altar was torn apart, and the fatty ash was poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of YHWH.

And the king answered and said to the man of God: Entreat, please, the face of YHWH your God, and pray for me, that my hand may come back to me. And the man of God entreated the face of YHWH, and the king's hand came back to him and was as at the first.
And the king spoke to the man of God: Come with me to the house and take refreshment, and let me give you a gift.
And the man of God said to the king: If you give me half your house, I will not go with you; and I will not eat bread and I will not drink water in this place.
For thus he commanded me by the word of YHWH, saying: You shall not eat bread and shall not drink water, and you shall not return by the way that you went.
And he went by another way, and did not return by the way that he had come to Bethel.

And one old prophet was dwelling in Bethel; and his son came and recounted to him every deed that the man of God had done that day in Bethel — the words that he had spoken to the king — and they recounted them to their father.
And their father spoke to them: Which way did he go? And his sons had seen the way that the man of God who came from Judah had gone.
And he said to his sons: Saddle the donkey for me. And they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it.
And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under the oak; and he said to him: Are you the man of God who came from Judah? And he said: I am.
And he said to him: Come with me to the house and eat bread.
And he said: I am not able to turn back with you and to go with you; and I will not eat bread and I will not drink water with you in this place.
For a word came to me by the word of YHWH: You shall not eat bread and shall not drink water there; you shall not return to go by the way that you went.
And he said to him: I too am a prophet like you, and a messenger spoke to me by the word of YHWH, saying: Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water. He lied to him.
And he went back with him and ate bread in his house and drank water.
And it happened, while they were sitting at the table, that the word of YHWH came to the prophet who had brought him back.

And he called out to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying: Thus says YHWH: Because you have been disobedient to the mouth of YHWH and have not kept the command that YHWH your God commanded you,
and you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place of which he said to you, Do not eat bread and do not drink water — your corpse will not come to the grave of your fathers.
And it happened, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him — for the prophet whom he had brought back.
And he went, and a lion met him on the way and killed him; and his corpse was thrown down in the road, and the donkey was standing beside it, and the lion was standing beside the corpse.
And behold, men were passing by and saw the corpse thrown down in the road, and the lion standing beside the corpse; and they came and spoke of it in the city where the old prophet was dwelling.

And the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard, and he said: It is the man of God who was disobedient to the mouth of YHWH; and YHWH has given him to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke to him.
And he spoke to his sons, saying: Saddle the donkey for me. And they saddled it.
And he went and found his corpse thrown down in the road, and the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse. The lion had not eaten the corpse and had not mauled the donkey.
And the prophet picked up the corpse of the man of God and placed him on the donkey and brought him back; and he came to the city of the old prophet, to mourn and to bury him.
And he placed his corpse in his own grave; and they mourned over him: Alas, my brother!
And it happened, after he had buried him, that he said to his sons, saying: At my death, bury me in the grave in which the man of God is buried; beside his bones place my bones.
For the word that he called out by the word of YHWH against the altar that is in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria, will surely come to pass.

After this thing Jeroboam did not turn back from his evil way; and he returned and made priests of high places from the ends of the people. Whoever desired it, he filled his hand, and he became one of the priests of the high places.
And by this thing it became the sin of the house of Jeroboam — to annihilate it and to destroy it from the face of the ground.

1 kings_14.t: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became sick.

And Jeroboam said to his wife: Arise, please, and disguise yourself, so that they will not know that you are the wife of Jeroboam; and go to Shiloh — behold, Ahijah the prophet is there, he who spoke concerning me that I would be king over this people.
And take in your hand ten loaves and cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him; he will tell you what will happen to the lad.
And the wife of Jeroboam did so; and she arose and went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. And Ahijah was not able to see, for his eyes were fixed from his old age.

And YHWH had said to Ahijah: Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to consult you for a word concerning her son, for he is sick; thus and thus you shall speak to her. And it will be, when she comes, that she will be pretending to be another.

And it happened, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet coming in at the entrance, that he said: Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why is it that you are pretending to be another? And I have been sent to you with a hard message.
Go, say to Jeroboam: Thus says YHWH the God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you a ruler over my people Israel,

and tore the kingdom from the house of David and gave it to you — and you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and who walked after me with all his heart, to do only what is right in my eyes;
and you have done evil, to act more than all who were before you, and you have gone and made for yourself other gods and cast images, to provoke me to anger; and me you have cast behind your back.

Therefore, behold, I am bringing calamity on the house of Jeroboam, and I will cut off from Jeroboam every one who urinates against a wall, the shut up and the freed in Israel; and I will sweep away after the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung, until it is gone.
The one of Jeroboam who dies in the city, the dogs will devour; and the one who dies in the open country, the birds of the heavens will devour — for YHWH has spoken.
And you — arise, go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.
And all Israel will mourn for him and bury him; for this one alone of Jeroboam's will come to a grave, because in him something good towards YHWH the God of Israel was found in the house of Jeroboam.
And YHWH will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam — this day; and what — even now.

And YHWH will strike Israel as a reed sways in the water, and he will pluck up Israel from this good ground that he gave to their fathers, and will scatter them beyond the River — because they have made their Asherim, provoking YHWH to anger.
And he will give up Israel on account of the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and by which he caused Israel to sin.
And the wife of Jeroboam arose and went and came to Tirzah; she was coming at the threshold of the house, and the lad died.
And all Israel buried him and mourned for him, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by the hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.
And the rest of the matters of Jeroboam, how he waged war and how he reigned — behold, they are written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
And the days that Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years; and he lay down with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

And Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was a son of forty-one years when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that YHWH had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there; and the name of his mother was Naamah the Ammonite.
And Judah did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; and they made him jealous more than all that their fathers had done, by their sins that they sinned.
And they too built for themselves high places and pillars and Asherim, on every high hill and under every luxuriant tree.
And there was also a cult prostitute in the land; they did according to all the abominations of the nations that YHWH had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
And it happened in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
And he took the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the house of the king; he took everything. And he took all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
And King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place, and entrusted them to the hand of the commanders of the runners who guarded the entrance of the king's house.
And it happened, as often as the king went to the house of YHWH, that the runners carried them and returned them to the guardroom of the runners.
And the rest of the matters of Rehoboam, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.
And Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and the name of his mother was Naamah the Ammonite. And Abijam his son reigned in his place.

1 kings_15.t: And in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.
Three years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
And he walked in all the sins of his father that he had done before him; and his heart was not complete with YHWH his God, like the heart of David his father.
For for the sake of David, YHWH his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, by raising up his son after him and by establishing Jerusalem —
because David had done what was right in the eyes of YHWH and had not turned aside from all that he commanded him all the days of his life — only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
And the rest of the matters of Abijam, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
And Abijam lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place.
And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah.
And forty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
And Asa did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, like David his father.
And he made the male cult prostitutes pass away from the land, and he removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

And also Maacah his mother — he removed her from being queen mother, because she had made an abominable image for the Asherah; and Asa cut down her abominable image and burned it in the wadi of Kidron.
But the high places were not removed; only, Asa's heart was complete with YHWH all his days.
And he brought the holy things of his father and his own holy things into the house of YHWH: silver and gold and articles.
And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, so as not to permit anyone going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

And Asa took all the silver and the gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of YHWH and the treasuries of the king's house, and gave them into the hand of his servants; and King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Aram, who dwelt in Damascus, saying:

There is a covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you a bribe of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will go up from me.

And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of the armies that were his against the cities of Israel; and he struck Ijon and Dan and Abel-beth-maacah, and all Kinnereth with all the land of Naphtali.
And it happened, when Baasha heard, that he ceased from building Ramah, and he remained in Tirzah.

And King Asa made proclamation to all Judah — there was no one exempt — and they carried off the stones of Ramah and its timber, which Baasha had built; and King Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

And the rest of all the matters of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities that he built — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah? Only, at the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
And Asa lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
And Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and walked in the way of his father and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin.

And Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were laying siege to Gibbethon.
And Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

And it happened, when he became king, that he struck down all the house of Jeroboam; he did not leave any breathing thing to Jeroboam, until he had destroyed it — according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by the hand of his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
because of the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned and by which he caused Israel to sin, by his provocation with which he provoked YHWH the God of Israel to anger.
And the rest of the matters of Nadab, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah — twenty-four years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin.

1 kings_16.t: And the word of YHWH came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:

Because I raised you up from the dust and made you a ruler over my people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger by their sins —
behold, I am sweeping away after Baasha and after his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
The one of Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will devour; and the one of his who dies in the open country, the birds of the heavens will devour.
And the rest of the matters of Baasha, and what he did, and his might — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Baasha lay down with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his place.

And also by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani the prophet the word of YHWH came against Baasha and against his house, both for all the evil that he did in the eyes of YHWH, provoking him to anger by the work of his hands, to be like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah — two years.
And his servant Zimri, commander of half the chariotry, conspired against him while he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.
And Zimri came in and struck him down and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigned in his place.

And it happened, when he became king, when he sat on his throne, that he struck down all the house of Baasha; he did not leave him one who urinates against a wall — neither his kinsmen-redeemers nor his friend.
And Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of YHWH that he had spoken against Baasha by the hand of Jehu the prophet,
because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and by which they caused Israel to sin, provoking YHWH the God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
And the rest of the matters of Elah, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri became king seven days in Tirzah; and the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
And the people who were encamping heard it said: Zimri has conspired, and he has also struck down the king. And all Israel made Omri, commander of the army, king over Israel on that day, in the camp.
And Omri went up, and all Israel with him, from Gibbethon; and they laid siege against Tirzah.
And it happened, when Zimri saw that the city was captured, that he went into the fortress of the king's house and burned the king's house over himself with fire, and he died —
because of his sins that he sinned, by doing what was evil in the eyes of YHWH, by walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin that he did, to cause Israel to sin.
And the rest of the matters of Zimri, and his conspiracy that he conspired — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
Then the people Israel was divided in half: half of the people was after Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half after Omri.
And the people who were after Omri prevailed over the people who were after Tibni son of Ginath; and Tibni died, and Omri became king.
In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel — twelve years. In Tirzah he reigned six years.

And he bought the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built on the hill, and he called the name of the city that he built after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill: Samaria.
And Omri did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and did evil more than all who were before him.
And he walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking YHWH the God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
And the rest of the matters of Omri that he did, and his might that he showed — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his place.
And Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah; and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
And Ahab son of Omri did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, more than all who were before him.

And it happened — was it a trifling thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat? — that he took as a wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served the Baal and bowed down to him.
And he set up an altar for the Baal in the house of the Baal that he built in Samaria.
And Ahab made the Asherah; and Ahab did more to provoke YHWH the God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

In his days Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates — according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.

1 kings_17.t: And Elijah the Tishbite, of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab: By the life of YHWH the God of Israel, before whom I stand — there will not be dew or rain these years except by the mouth of my word.
And the word of YHWH came to him, saying:
Go from here and turn eastward, and hide yourself at the wadi of Kerith, which is opposite the Jordan.
And it will be that you will drink from the wadi; and I have commanded the ravens to supply you there.
And he went and did according to the word of YHWH; and he went and dwelt at the wadi of Kerith, which is opposite the Jordan.
And the ravens were bringing him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the wadi.
And it happened at the end of days that the wadi dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of YHWH came to him, saying:
Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there; behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to supply you.

And he arose and went to Zarephath and came to the entrance of the city; and behold, a widow woman was there gathering wood. And he called to her and said: Get me, please, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And she went to get it; and he called to her and said: Get me, please, a piece of bread in your hand.

And she said: By the life of YHWH your God, I have nothing baked — only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug; and here I am gathering two sticks, and I will go in and prepare it for myself and for my son, and we will eat it and die.
And Elijah said to her: Do not fear. Go, do according to your word; only make me from it a small cake first and bring it out to me, and for yourself and for your son you will make afterwards.
For thus says YHWH the God of Israel: The jar of flour will not be at an end, and the jug of oil will not be lacking, until the day YHWH gives rain on the face of the ground.
And she went and did according to the word of Elijah; and she ate, she and he and her household, for days.
The jar of flour was not at an end, and the jug of oil was not lacking, according to the word of YHWH that he spoke by the hand of Elijah.
And it happened after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick; and his sickness was very severe, until no breath was left in him.
And she said to Elijah: What is between me and you, man of God? You have come to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance and to put my son to death.
And he said to her: Give me your son. And he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
And he called out to YHWH and said: YHWH my God, have you also brought harm on the widow with whom I am staying as a sojourner, by putting her son to death?
And he stretched himself out over the lad three times, and called out to YHWH and said: YHWH my God, let the life of this lad return to his inward parts.
And YHWH listened to the voice of Elijah; and the life of the lad returned to his inward parts, and he lived.
And Elijah took the lad and brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother; and Elijah said: See, your son is alive.
And the woman said to Elijah: Now this I know, that you are a man of God and that the word of YHWH in your mouth is truth.

1 kings_18.t: And it happened after many days that the word of YHWH came to Elijah in the third year, saying: Go, present yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain on the face of the ground.
And Elijah went to present himself to Ahab; and the famine was severe in Samaria.
And Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was over the household; and Obadiah feared YHWH exceedingly.
And it happened, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of YHWH, that Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men in a cave, and supplied them with bread and water.
And Ahab said to Obadiah: Go through the land, to all the springs of water and to all the wadis; perhaps we will find grass and keep horse and mule alive, and not lose any of the livestock.
And they divided the land between them to pass through it; Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
And Obadiah was on the way, and behold, Elijah was to meet him; and he recognised him and fell on his face and said: Is this you, my lord Elijah?
And he said to him: It is I. Go, say to your lord: Here is Elijah.
And he said: What have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Ahab, to put me to death?

By the life of YHWH your God, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you; and when they said, He is not here, he made the kingdom and the nation swear that they had not found you.
And now you are saying: Go, say to your lord, Here is Elijah.

And it will be that I will go from you, and the spirit of YHWH will carry you off to where I do not know; and I will come to tell Ahab, and he will not find you, and he will kill me. And your servant has feared YHWH from my youth.

Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of YHWH — that I hid a hundred men of the prophets of YHWH, fifty men, fifty men, in the cave, and supplied them with bread and water?
And now you are saying: Go, say to your lord, Here is Elijah — and he will kill me!
And Elijah said: By the life of YHWH of hosts, before whom I stand, today I will present myself to him.
And Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him; and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
And it happened, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said to him: Is this you, troubler of Israel?
And he said: I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father's house, in that you have forsaken the commandments of YHWH and you have gone after the Baals.
And now, send and gather to me all Israel to Mount Carmel, and the prophets of the Baal, four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the Asherah, four hundred, who eat at Jezebel's table.
And Ahab sent among all the sons of Israel and gathered the prophets to Mount Carmel.
And Elijah drew near to all the people and said: How long will you go limping on two crutches? If YHWH is God, go after him; and if the Baal, go after him. And the people did not answer him a word.
And Elijah said to the people: I alone am left a prophet of YHWH, and the prophets of the Baal are four hundred and fifty men.

Let them give us two young bulls; and let them choose for themselves the one bull and cut it in pieces and put it on the wood, but set no fire. And I will prepare the other bull and put it on the wood, but set no fire.
And you will call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of YHWH; and the god who answers by fire — he is God. And all the people answered and said: The word is good.
And Elijah said to the prophets of the Baal: Choose for yourselves the one bull and prepare it first, for you are the many; and call on the name of your god, but set no fire.

And they took the bull that was given them and prepared it; and they called on the name of the Baal from the morning until noon, saying: Baal, answer us! And there was no voice and no one answering. And they went limping around the altar that he had made.

And it happened at noon that Elijah mocked them and said: Call out with a loud voice, for he is a god! For he is musing, or he has stepped aside, or he is on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep and will wake up.
And they called out with a loud voice and cut themselves, according to their custom, with swords and with lances, until blood poured out over them.
And it happened, when noon had passed, that they prophesied until the going up of the offering; and there was no voice and no one answering and no attention.
And Elijah said to all the people: Draw near to me. And all the people drew near to him. And he repaired the altar of YHWH that had been torn down.
And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of YHWH had come, saying: Israel will be your name.
And he built the stones into an altar in the name of YHWH; and he made a trench, like a receptacle of two seahs of seed, around the altar.
And he arranged the wood and cut the bull in pieces and put it on the wood. And he said: Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood.
And he said: Do it again. And they did it again. And he said: Do it a third time. And they did it a third time.
And the water went around the altar; and he also filled the trench with water.

And it happened at the going up of the offering that Elijah the prophet drew near and said: YHWH, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, today let it be known that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant, and that at your word I have done all these things.
Answer me, YHWH, answer me, so that this people may know that you, YHWH, are God, and that you have turned their heart back.
And the fire of YHWH fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust; and the water that was in the trench it licked up.
And all the people saw and fell on their faces and said: YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!
And Elijah said to them: Seize the prophets of the Baal; let not one of them escape. And they seized them; and Elijah brought them down to the wadi of Kishon and slaughtered them there.
And Elijah said to Ahab: Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the roar of rain.
And Ahab went up to eat and to drink; and Elijah went up to the top of Carmel and crouched down to the ground and put his face between his knees.
And he said to his servant: Go up, please, and look towards the sea. And he went up and looked and said: There is nothing. And he said: Go back seven times.

And it happened at the seventh time that he said: Behold, a small cloud like a man's hand is coming up from the sea. And he said: Go up, say to Ahab: Harness and go down, so that the rain does not stop you.
And it happened, in the meantime, that the heavens grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain; and Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.
And the hand of YHWH was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab, until you come to Jezreel.

1 kings_19.t: And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and all how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
And Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying: So may the gods do and so may they add, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the life of one of them.
And he saw, and he arose and went for his life; and he came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and he left his servant there.

And he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness; and he came and sat under one broom bush, and he asked for his life to die, and said: Enough! Now, YHWH, take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.
And he lay down and slept under one broom bush; and behold, a messenger was touching him, and he said to him: Arise, eat.
And he looked, and behold, at his head was a cake baked on hot stones, and a jug of water; and he ate and drank, and turned back and lay down.
And the messenger of YHWH returned a second time and touched him, and said: Arise, eat, for the journey is too great for you.
And he arose and ate and drank; and he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights, to Horeb, the mountain of God.
And he came there, to the cave, and spent the night there. And behold, the word of YHWH came to him, and he said to him: What are you doing here, Elijah?

And he said: I have been exceedingly zealous for YHWH the God of hosts; for the sons of Israel have forsaken your covenant, they have torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword; and I alone am left, and they have sought my life, to take it away.

And he said: Go out and stand on the mountain before YHWH. And behold, YHWH was passing by, and a great and strong wind was tearing mountains and breaking rocks before YHWH — YHWH was not in the wind. And after the wind, an earthquake — YHWH was not in the earthquake.
And after the earthquake, a fire — YHWH was not in the fire. And after the fire, a sound of a thin silence.

And it happened, when Elijah heard, that he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And behold, a voice came to him and said: What are you doing here, Elijah?

And he said: I have been exceedingly zealous for YHWH the God of hosts; for the sons of Israel have forsaken your covenant, they have torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword; and I alone am left, and they have sought my life, to take it away.
And YHWH said to him: Go, return on your way, to the wilderness of Damascus; and you will come and anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
And Jehu son of Nimshi you will anoint as king over Israel; and Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel-meholah, you will anoint as prophet in your place.
And it will be that the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu will put to death; and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put to death.
And I will leave in Israel seven thousand — all the knees that have not bowed to the Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.
And he went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat; and he was ploughing, twelve pairs before him, and he was with the twelfth. And Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak on him.
And he left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said: Let me kiss my father and my mother, and I will go after you. And he said to him: Go, turn back — for what have I done to you?

And he turned back from after him and took the pair of oxen and sacrificed it; and with the equipment of the oxen he cooked the flesh and gave it to the people, and they ate. And he arose and went after Elijah and served him.

1 kings_20.t: And Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his army, and thirty-two kings were with him, and horses and chariotry; and he went up and laid siege against Samaria and fought against it.
And he sent messengers to Ahab king of Israel, to the city; and he said to him: Thus says Ben-hadad:
Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children, the best ones, are mine.
And the king of Israel answered and said: According to your word, my lord the king — I am yours, and all that is mine.
And the messengers returned and said: Thus says Ben-hadad, saying: For I sent to you, saying, Your silver and your gold and your wives and your children you will give to me —

— but about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants; and it will be that every desirable thing of your eyes they will put in their hand and take away.

And the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said: Know, please, and see, that this man is seeking harm; for he sent to me for my wives and for my children and for my silver and for my gold, and I did not withhold them from him.
And all the elders and all the people said to him: Do not listen and do not consent.

And he said to the messengers of Ben-hadad: Say to my lord the king: All that you sent for to your servant at the first I will do, but this thing I am not able to do. And the messengers went and brought him back word.
And Ben-hadad sent to him and said: So may the gods do to me and so may they add, if the dust of Samaria will suffice for handfuls for all the people who are at my feet.
And the king of Israel answered and said: Say — Let not the one who girds on boast like the one who loosens.
And it happened, when he heard this word — and he was drinking, he and the kings, in the booths — that he said to his servants: Take your positions. And they took their positions against the city.

And behold, a certain prophet drew near to Ahab king of Israel and said: Thus says YHWH: Have you seen all this great multitude? Here I am, giving it into your hand today; and you will know that I am YHWH.
And Ahab said: By whom? And he said: Thus says YHWH: By the young men of the officials of the provinces. And he said: Who will begin the battle? And he said: You.
And he mustered the young men of the officials of the provinces, and they were two hundred and thirty-two; and after them he mustered all the people, all the sons of Israel — seven thousand.
And they went out at noon; and Ben-hadad was drinking, drunk, in the booths — he and the kings, thirty-two kings who were helping him.
And the young men of the officials of the provinces went out first; and Ben-hadad sent, and they told him, saying: Men have come out from Samaria.
And he said: If they have come out for peace, seize them alive; and if for battle they have come out, seize them alive.
And these went out from the city — the young men of the officials of the provinces, and the army that was behind them.
And they struck down, each his man; and Aram fled, and Israel pursued them; and Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on a horse, with horsemen.
And the king of Israel went out and struck down the horses and the chariotry, and struck Aram with a great slaughter.
And the prophet drew near to the king of Israel and said to him: Go, strengthen yourself, and know and see what you will do; for at the turn of the year the king of Aram is coming up against you.

And the servants of the king of Aram said to him: Their God is a god of mountains; therefore they were stronger than we. But let us do battle with them on the level ground — surely we will be stronger than they.
And do this thing: remove the kings, each from his place, and appoint governors in their place.

And you — muster for yourself an army like the army that fell from you, and horse like the horse and chariotry like the chariotry; and let us fight them on the level ground — surely we will be stronger than they. And he listened to their voice and did so.
And it happened at the turn of the year that Ben-hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek for the battle with Israel.
And the sons of Israel were mustered and supplied, and they went to meet them; and the sons of Israel encamped before them like two little flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.

And the man of God drew near and spoke to the king of Israel and said: Thus says YHWH: Because Aram have said, YHWH is a god of mountains and he is not a god of valleys — I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am YHWH.
And these encamped opposite these seven days; and it happened on the seventh day that the battle drew near, and the sons of Israel struck down Aram — a hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day.
And the ones who remained fled to Aphek, into the city; and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand men who remained. And Ben-hadad fled and came into the city, room within room.

And his servants said to him: Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel — that they are kings of loyalty. Let us put, please, sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our head, and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will let your life live.

And they girded sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said: Your servant Ben-hadad says, Let my life live, please. And he said: Is he still alive? He is my brother.

And the men were watching for an omen, and they hurried and caught it from him, and said: Your brother Ben-hadad. And he said: Go, fetch him. And Ben-hadad came out to him, and he brought him up onto the chariot.

And he said to him: The cities that my father took from your father I will return; and you will make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. And I — with a covenant I will let you go. And he cut a covenant for him and let him go.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, by the word of YHWH: Strike me, please. And the man refused to strike him.

And he said to him: Because you did not listen to the voice of YHWH, behold, you are going from me, and the lion will strike you down. And he went from beside him, and the lion found him and struck him down.
And he found another man and said: Strike me, please. And the man struck him — striking and wounding.
And the prophet went and stood for the king beside the way, and disguised himself with ashes over his eyes.

And it happened, as the king was passing by, that he cried out to the king and said: Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and behold, a man turned aside and brought a man to me and said, Guard this man; if he is ever missing, then your life will be in place of his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.
And it happened, while your servant was busy here and there, that he was gone. And the king of Israel said to him: So is your judgement — you yourself have decided it.
And he hurried and removed the ashes from over his eyes; and the king of Israel recognised him, that he was one of the prophets.
And he said to him: Thus says YHWH: Because you have let go from your hand the man of my devotion to destruction, your life will be in place of his life, and your people in place of his people.
And the king of Israel went to his house, sullen and furious; and he came to Samaria.

1 kings_21.t: And it happened after these things: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard that was in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying: Give me your vineyard, and let it be mine for a garden of vegetables, for it is near, beside my house; and I will give you in its place a vineyard better than it. If it is good in your eyes, I will give you silver, the price of this one.
And Naboth said to Ahab: Far be it from me, from YHWH, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you.

And Ahab came to his house sullen and furious over the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, when he said: I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers. And he lay down on his bed and turned away his face, and did not eat bread.
And Jezebel his wife came to him and spoke to him: Why is this — your spirit sullen, and you are not eating bread?

And he spoke to her: Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, Give me your vineyard for silver; or if you desire, I will give you a vineyard in its place. And he said: I will not give you my vineyard.
And Jezebel his wife said to him: You — are you now exercising kingship over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and let your heart be good. I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And she wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and to the nobles who were in his city, who dwelt with Naboth.
And she wrote in the letters, saying: Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
And seat two men, sons of worthlessness, before him; and let them testify against him, saying: You have blessed God and the king. And take him out and stone him, and let him die.
And the men of his city, the elders and the nobles who dwelt in his city, did as Jezebel had sent to them, as it was written in the letters that she had sent to them.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

And the two men, sons of worthlessness, came and sat before him; and the men of worthlessness testified against Naboth before the people, saying: Naboth has blessed God and the king. And they took him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
And they sent to Jezebel, saying: Naboth has been stoned, and he has died.

And it happened, when Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and had died, that Jezebel said to Ahab: Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver; for Naboth is not alive, for he is dead.
And it happened, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab arose to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
And the word of YHWH came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria; behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

And you will speak to him, saying: Thus says YHWH: Have you murdered, and also taken possession? And you will speak to him, saying: Thus says YHWH: In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, the dogs will lick up your blood — yours too.
And Ahab said to Elijah: Have you found me, my enemy? And he said: I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH.
Behold, I am bringing harm on you, and I will sweep away after you; and I will cut off from Ahab every one who urinates against a wall, and the one shut up and the one left free in Israel.

And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked, and you have caused Israel to sin.
And also of Jezebel YHWH has spoken, saying: The dogs will devour Jezebel at the rampart of Jezreel.
The one belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will devour; and the one who dies in the open country, the birds of the heavens will devour.
Certainly there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH, whom Jezebel his wife incited.
And he acted exceedingly abominably by walking after the idols, according to all that the Amorites did, whom YHWH dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
And it happened, when Ahab heard these words, that he tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his body and fasted; and he lay in the sackcloth and went about dejectedly.
And the word of YHWH came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:

Have you seen that Ahab has humbled himself from before me? Because he has humbled himself from before me, I will not bring the harm in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the harm on his house.

1 kings_22.t: And they remained three years; there was no war between Aram and Israel.
And it happened in the third year that Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
And the king of Israel said to his servants: Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, and we are keeping still from taking it from the hand of the king of Aram?

And he said to Jehoshaphat: Will you go with me to the battle at Ramoth-gilead? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: As I am, so are you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: Consult, please, today the word of YHWH.

And the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them: Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to the battle, or shall I refrain? And they said: Go up, and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.
And Jehoshaphat said: Is there not still here a prophet of YHWH, that we may consult him?

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: There is still one man to consult YHWH through him, but I myself hate him, for he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil — Micaiah son of Imlah. And Jehoshaphat said: Let the king not say so.
And the king of Israel summoned a certain court official and said: Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, clothed in garments, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah son of Kenaanah made himself horns of iron and said: Thus says YHWH: With these you will gore Aram until you have finished them.
And all the prophets were prophesying so, saying: Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, and YHWH will give it into the hand of the king.

And the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah spoke to him, saying: Behold now, the words of the prophets are with one mouth good to the king; let your word, please, be like the word of one of them, and speak good.
And Micaiah said: By the life of YHWH, what YHWH says to me, that I will speak.

And he came to the king; and the king said to him: Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to the battle, or shall we refrain? And he said to him: Go up and succeed, and YHWH will give it into the hand of the king.
And the king said to him: How many times must I make you swear that you will speak to me nothing but truth in the name of YHWH?
And he said: I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like a flock that has no shepherd. And YHWH said: These have no masters; let them return, each to his house, in peace.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: Did I not say to you, He does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?
And he said: Therefore hear the word of YHWH. I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing beside him, on his right and on his left.
And YHWH said: Who will entice Ahab, so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And this one said one thing and this one said another.
And the spirit came forth and stood before YHWH and said: I will entice him.
And YHWH said to him: By what? And he said: I will go out and be a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said: You will entice, and you will also prevail. Go out and do so.
And now, behold, YHWH has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these your prophets; and YHWH has spoken evil concerning you.
And Zedekiah son of Kenaanah drew near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said: Which way did the spirit of YHWH pass from me to speak with you?
And Micaiah said: Behold, you will see on that day, when you go into a room within a room to hide yourself.
And the king of Israel said: Take Micaiah and turn him back to Amon the official of the city, and to Joash the son of the king.
And you will say: Thus says the king: Put this one in the house of imprisonment, and feed him bread of oppression and water of oppression, until I come in peace.
And Micaiah said: If you ever return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me. And he said: Listen, peoples, all of you.
And the king of Israel went up, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, to Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you — wear your own garments. And the king of Israel disguised himself and went into the battle.
And the king of Aram had commanded the commanders of the chariotry that were his, thirty-two, saying: You will not do battle with small or great, but with the king of Israel alone.

And it happened, when the commanders of the chariotry saw Jehoshaphat, that they themselves said: Surely he is the king of Israel. And they turned aside against him to do battle; and Jehoshaphat cried out.
And it happened, when the commanders of the chariotry saw that he was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from after him.

And a man drew the bow in his innocence and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the body armour. And he said to his charioteer: Turn your hand and take me out from the camp, for I am wounded.
And the battle went up on that day, and the king was propped up in the chariot facing Aram; and he died in the evening, and the blood of the wound flowed into the bottom of the chariot.
And the cry passed through the camp as the sun was going down, saying: Each to his city, and each to his land.
And the king died and came to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria.
And he washed off the chariot at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood; and the prostitutes washed — according to the word of YHWH that he had spoken.

And the rest of the matters of Ahab, and all that he did, and the house of ivory that he built, and all the cities that he built — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Ahab lay down with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
And Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was a son of thirty-five years when he became king, and twenty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

And he walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what is right in the eyes of YHWH. Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and making offerings smoke at the high places.
And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
And the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he showed, and how he waged war — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And the rest of the cult prostitute that remained in the days of Asa his father, he swept away from the land.
And there was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for the gold; but it did not go, for the ships were broken at Ezion-geber.
Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat: Let my servants go with your servants in the ships. But Jehoshaphat was not willing.
And Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; and he reigned over Israel two years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
And he served the Baal and bowed down to him, and provoked YHWH the God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done.

1 samuel_1.t: And there was one man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah son of Jeroham son of Elihu son of Tohu son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.
And he had two wives: the name of one was Hannah and the name of the second was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, and Hannah had no children.
And that man would go up from his city year by year to bow down and to sacrifice to YHWH of hosts at Shiloh. And there the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to YHWH.
And the day came, and Elkanah sacrificed; and he gave to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions.
And to Hannah he would give one portion, a double one — for he loved Hannah, and YHWH had closed her womb.
And her rival provoked her sorely, to disconcert her, because YHWH had closed her womb.
And so he did year by year: as often as she went up to the house of YHWH, so she would provoke her; and she wept and would not eat.
And Elkanah her husband said to her: Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?
And Hannah arose after they had eaten at Shiloh and after they had drunk; and Eli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the temple of YHWH.
And she was bitter of being, and she prayed to YHWH and wept bitterly.

And she vowed a vow and said: YHWH of hosts, if you will surely look on the affliction of your maidservant and remember me and not forget your maidservant, and will give your maidservant offspring of men, then I will give him to YHWH all the days of his life, and a razor shall not go up on his head.
And it happened, as she prayed long before YHWH, that Eli was watching her mouth.
And Hannah — she was speaking upon her heart; only her lips were moving and her voice was not heard. And Eli took her for a drunken woman.
And Eli said to her: How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from you.
And Hannah answered and said: No, my lord. I am a woman hard of spirit, and wine and strong drink I have not drunk; and I have poured out my being before YHWH.
Do not give your maidservant before a daughter of worthlessness; for out of the greatness of my complaint and my provocation I have spoken until now.
And Eli answered and said: Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition which you have asked of him.
And she said: May your maidservant find favour in your eyes. And the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer as it had been.
And they rose early in the morning and bowed down before YHWH, and they returned and came to their house at Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and YHWH remembered her.
And it happened at the turn of the days that Hannah conceived and bore a son; and she called his name Samuel, for she said: From YHWH I asked him.
And the man Elkanah went up, and all his household, to sacrifice to YHWH the yearly sacrifice and his vow.
And Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband: Until the boy is weaned, then I will bring him, and he will appear before the face of YHWH and dwell there for ever.
And Elkanah her husband said to her: Do what is good in your eyes. Stay until you have weaned him; only may YHWH carry out his word. And the woman stayed and suckled her son until she had weaned him.
And she brought him up with her when she had weaned him, with three bulls and one ephah of flour and a skin of wine; and she brought him to the house of YHWH at Shiloh. And the boy was a boy.
And they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to Eli.
And she said: Pardon me, my lord — as your being lives, my lord — I am the woman who stood with you in this place, praying to YHWH.
For this boy I prayed, and YHWH has granted me my petition which I asked of him.
And I also, I have lent him to YHWH: all the days that he lives, he is lent to YHWH. And he bowed down there to YHWH.

1 samuel_2.t: And Hannah prayed and said: My heart rejoices in YHWH; my horn is exalted in YHWH. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, for I rejoice in your deliverance.
There is none holy like YHWH, for there is none besides you; and there is no Rock like our God.
Do not multiply speaking so haughtily, so haughtily; let arrogance not go out from your mouth. For YHWH is a God of knowledge, and by him deeds are weighed.
The bow of warriors is shattered, and those who stumbled gird on strength.
Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, and those who were hungry cease. Even the barren has borne seven, and she who had many sons languishes.
YHWH kills and gives life, brings down to Sheol and brings up.
YHWH makes poor and makes rich, brings low, he also exalts.

He raises the poor from the dust, from the ash heap he lifts the needy, to seat them with nobles; and a throne of glory he gives them as an inheritance. For the pillars of the earth belong to YHWH, and he has set the world upon them.
The feet of his loyal ones he guards, and the wicked are silenced in the darkness; for not by strength does a man prevail.

YHWH — those who contend with him are shattered; against them he thunders in the heavens. YHWH will judge the ends of the earth, and he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.
And Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house; and the boy was serving YHWH before the face of Eli the priest.
And the sons of Eli were sons of worthlessness; they did not know YHWH.
And the custom of the priests with the people was this: every man who sacrificed a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with the three-pronged fork in his hand,
and thrust it into the pan or the kettle or the cauldron or the cooking pot; all that the fork brought up the priest would take for himself. Thus they did to all Israel who came there, at Shiloh.
Also, before they made the fat smoke, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing: Give meat to roast for the priest; he will not take boiled meat from you, but raw.

And the man would say to him: Let them surely make the fat smoke first, and then take for yourself as your being desires. And he would say: No, but you shall give it now; and if not, I will take it by force.
And the sin of the young men was very great before the face of YHWH, for the men treated the offering of YHWH with contempt.
And Samuel was serving before the face of YHWH — a boy, girded with an ephod of linen.
And his mother would make him a small robe and bring it up to him year by year, when she went up with her husband to sacrifice the yearly sacrifice.
And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say: May YHWH appoint you offspring from this woman in place of the petition that was asked for YHWH. And they would go to his place.
