For YHWH visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up with YHWH.
And Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and that they were lying with the women who served at the opening of the tent of meeting.
And he said to them: Why do you do such things as these? For I hear of your evil doings from all these people.
No, my sons; for the report that I hear is not good — you are making the people of YHWH transgress.

If a man sins against a man, God will mediate for him; but if a man sins against YHWH, who will intercede for him? And they did not listen to the voice of their father, for YHWH desired to put them to death.
And the boy Samuel went on growing and was good, both with YHWH and also with men.
And a man of God came to Eli and said to him: Thus said YHWH: Did I not reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, to the house of Pharaoh?

And I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel for myself as a priest, to go up on my altar, to make incense smoke, to bear an ephod before my face. And I gave to the house of your father all the food offerings of the sons of Israel.

Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I commanded — a dwelling place — and honour your sons above me, fattening yourselves from the choicest of every offering of Israel, of my people?

Therefore — the declaration of YHWH, the God of Israel — I said indeed that your house and the house of your father would walk before my face for ever; but now — the declaration of YHWH — far be it from me! For those who honour me I will honour, and those who despise me will be made light of.
Behold, days are coming, and I will cut off your arm and the arm of the house of your father, so that there will not be an old man in your house.
And you will look at the distress of a dwelling place, in all that he does good to Israel; and there will not be an old man in your house all the days.
And a man of yours I will not cut off from my altar, to cause your eyes to fail and to grieve your being; and all the increase of your house will die as men.
And this will be the sign for you, which will come upon your two sons, upon Hophni and Phinehas: on one day the two of them will die.

And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest; he will do according to what is in my heart and in my being, and I will build him a sure house, and he will walk before the face of my anointed all the days.

And it will be that everyone who remains in your house will come to bow down to him for a payment of silver and a round loaf of bread, and will say: Attach me, please, to one of the priesthoods, to eat a piece of bread.

1 samuel_3.t: And the boy Samuel was serving YHWH before Eli. And the word of YHWH was rare in those days; vision was not spread abroad.
And it happened on that day, when Eli was lying in his place — and his eyes had begun to be dim, he could not see —
and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying in the temple of YHWH, where the ark of God was —
that YHWH called to Samuel; and he said: Here I am.
And he ran to Eli and said: Here I am, for you called me. And he said: I did not call. Go back, lie down. And he went and lay down.
And YHWH called again: Samuel! And Samuel rose and went to Eli and said: Here I am, for you called me. And he said: I did not call, my son. Go back, lie down.
And Samuel did not yet know YHWH, and the word of YHWH had not yet been revealed to him.
And YHWH called Samuel again, a third time. And he rose and went to Eli and said: Here I am, for you called me. And Eli understood that YHWH was calling the boy.
And Eli said to Samuel: Go, lie down; and if he calls to you, you shall say: Speak, YHWH, for your servant is listening. And Samuel went and lay down in his place.
And YHWH came and stood, and called as at the other times: Samuel! Samuel! And Samuel said: Speak, for your servant is listening.
And YHWH said to Samuel: Behold, I am about to do a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.
On that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, beginning and ending.
And I have told him that I am about to judge his house for ever, for the iniquity that he knew: that his sons were bringing a curse upon themselves, and he did not rebuke them.
And therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or by offering, for ever.
And Samuel lay until the morning, and he opened the doors of the house of YHWH; and Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
And Eli called Samuel and said: Samuel, my son. And he said: Here I am.
And he said: What is the word that he spoke to you? Do not hide it from me, please. So may God do to you, and so may he add, if you hide from me a word of all the word that he spoke to you.
And Samuel told him all the words and did not hide from him; and he said: He is YHWH; let him do what is good in his eyes.
And Samuel grew up, and YHWH was with him, and he let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was established as a prophet to YHWH.
And YHWH appeared again at Shiloh, for YHWH revealed himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of YHWH.

1 samuel_4.t: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. And Israel went out to meet the Philistines for battle, and they encamped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines encamped at Aphek.
And the Philistines deployed to meet Israel, and the battle spread out, and Israel was defeated before the Philistines; and they struck down in the battle line, in the field, about four thousand men.

And the people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said: Why has YHWH defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us take to ourselves from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of YHWH, that it may come among us and deliver us from the hand of our enemies.

And the people sent to Shiloh, and they carried from there the ark of the covenant of YHWH of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim; and there the two sons of Eli were with the ark of the covenant of God, Hophni and Phinehas.
And it happened, when the ark of the covenant of YHWH came into the camp, that all Israel shouted a great shout, and the ground was stirred.
And the Philistines heard the sound of the shout and said: What is this sound of a great shout in the camp of the Hebrews? And they knew that the ark of YHWH had come into the camp.
And the Philistines were afraid, for they said: A god has come into the camp. And they said: Woe to us! For it has not been like this yesterday or the day before.
Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.
Show yourselves strong and be men, O Philistines, lest you serve the Hebrews as they have served you. And be men, and fight.
And the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each fled to his tents; and the slaughter was very great, and there fell of Israel thirty thousand foot soldiers.
And the ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.
And a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, and his garments were torn and earth was on his head.
And he came, and behold, Eli was sitting on the seat beside the road, watching, for his heart was trembling for the ark of God. And the man came to tell it in the city, and all the city cried out.
And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said: What is this sound of uproar? And the man hurried and came and told Eli.
And Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were set, and he could not see.
And the man said to Eli: I am the one who has come from the battle line; and I fled from the battle line today. And he said: What has happened, my son?

And the bearer of news answered and said: Israel has fled before the Philistines, and also there has been a great slaughter among the people; and also your two sons have died, Hophni and Phinehas; and the ark of God has been taken.

And it happened, when he mentioned the ark of God, that he fell backwards off the seat, beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died; for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

And his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant, about to give birth; and she heard the report about the taking of the ark of God and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, and she crouched down and gave birth, for her pangs had turned upon her.
And about the time of her dying, those standing over her spoke: Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son. And she did not answer, and she did not set her heart.
And she called the boy Ichabod, saying: Glory has gone into exile from Israel — because of the taking of the ark of God, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
And she said: Glory has gone into exile from Israel, for the ark of God has been taken.

1 samuel_5.t: And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it beside Dagon.
And the Ashdodites rose early the next day, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of YHWH. And they took Dagon and returned him to his place.

And they rose early in the morning the next day, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of YHWH; and the head of Dagon and the two palms of his hands were cut off, at the threshold — only Dagon was left upon him.
Therefore the priests of Dagon and all who come into the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.
And the hand of YHWH was heavy against the Ashdodites, and he devastated them; and he struck them with tumours — Ashdod and its territories.
And the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, and they said: The ark of the God of Israel shall not remain with us, for his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god.

And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines to them and said: What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel? And they said: Let the ark of the God of Israel be brought round to Gath. And they brought round the ark of the God of Israel.

And it happened, after they had brought it round, that the hand of YHWH was against the city — a very great panic; and he struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumours broke out on them.

And they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it happened, when the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying: They have brought round to me the ark of the God of Israel, to kill me and my people!

And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said: Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its own place, and let it not kill me and my people. For there was a panic of death in all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
And the men who did not die were struck with tumours; and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

1 samuel_6.t: And the ark of YHWH was in the region of the Philistines seven months.
And the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners, saying: What shall we do with the ark of YHWH? Make known to us how we shall send it to its place.

And they said: If you are sending away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty; but you shall surely send back to him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand does not turn aside from you.

And they said: What is the guilt offering that we shall send back to him? And they said: The number of the rulers of the Philistines — five tumours of gold and five mice of gold; for one plague was on all of them and on your rulers.

And you shall make images of your tumours and images of your mice that are ruining the land, and you shall give glory to the God of Israel; perhaps he will lighten his hand from upon you and from upon your gods and from upon your land.
And why will you harden your heart as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? Was it not when he had dealt wantonly with them that they sent them away, and they went?
And now, take and make one new cart, and two nursing cows on which no yoke has come up; and harness the cows to the cart, and take their calves back home, away from them.

And you shall take the ark of YHWH and put it on the cart; and the articles of gold that you are sending back to him as a guilt offering you shall put in a box beside it. And you shall send it away, and it shall go.

And you shall see: if it goes up by the way of its own territory, to Beth-shemesh, then he has done us this great harm; and if not, then we shall know that it was not his hand that touched us — it was chance that happened to us.
And the men did so. And they took two nursing cows and harnessed them to the cart, and their calves they shut up at home.
And they put the ark of YHWH on the cart, and the box, and the mice of gold, and the images of their tumours.

And the cows went straight on the road, on the road to Beth-shemesh; on one highway they went, going and lowing, and they did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the rulers of the Philistines were going after them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
And Beth-shemesh were harvesting the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

And the cart came to the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped there; and a large stone was there. And they split the wood of the cart, and the cows they offered up as a burnt offering to YHWH.

And the Levites brought down the ark of YHWH and the box that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and they put them on the large stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices on that day to YHWH.
And the five rulers of the Philistines saw it, and they returned to Ekron on that day.
And these are the tumours of gold that the Philistines sent back as a guilt offering to YHWH: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.

And the mice of gold were the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to the village of the open country — and as far as Abel the great, on which they set down the ark of YHWH, to this day, in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

And he struck down among the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of YHWH; and he struck down among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men. And the people mourned, because YHWH had struck the people with a great blow.
And the men of Beth-shemesh said: Who is able to stand before YHWH, this holy God? And to whom shall he go up from us?
And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying: The Philistines have brought back the ark of YHWH. Come down, take it up to yourselves.

1 samuel_7.t: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of YHWH and brought it to the house of Abinadab on the hill; and Eleazar his son they set apart as holy, to keep the ark of YHWH.
And it happened, from the day the ark dwelt at Kiriath-jearim, that the days grew many, and they were twenty years; and all the house of Israel mourned after YHWH.

And Samuel said to all the house of Israel: If with all your heart you are turning back to YHWH, remove the foreign gods from among you, and the Ashtaroth, and direct your heart to YHWH and serve him alone; and he will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.
And the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served YHWH alone.
And Samuel said: Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you to YHWH.
And they gathered to Mizpah and drew water and poured it out before YHWH, and they fasted on that day and said there: We have sinned against YHWH. And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.

And the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered to Mizpah, and the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel; and the sons of Israel heard, and they were afraid before the Philistines.
And the sons of Israel said to Samuel: Do not keep silent from us, from crying out to YHWH our God, that he may deliver us from the hand of the Philistines.
And Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering to YHWH; and Samuel cried out to YHWH for Israel, and YHWH answered him.

And Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, and the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel; and YHWH thundered with a great sound on that day against the Philistines and routed them, and they were defeated before Israel.
And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
And Samuel took one stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, and said: Until now YHWH has helped us.
And the Philistines were brought low, and they did not come again into the territory of Israel; and the hand of YHWH was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

And the cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel returned to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath; and their territory Israel delivered from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
And he would go year by year and go round Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.
And his return was to Ramah, for his house was there, and there he judged Israel; and he built there an altar to YHWH.

1 samuel_8.t: And it happened, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.
And the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
And his sons did not walk in his ways; and they turned aside after unjust gain, and took a bribe, and turned aside justice.
And all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
And they said to him: Behold, you have grown old, and your sons have not walked in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us, like all the nations.
And the matter was displeasing in the eyes of Samuel when they said: Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed to YHWH.
And YHWH said to Samuel: Listen to the voice of the people, to all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from reigning over them.
Like all the deeds that they have done from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day — they have forsaken me and served other gods — so they are doing also to you.
And now, listen to their voice. Only, you shall surely warn them and tell them the right of the king who will reign over them.
And Samuel spoke all the words of YHWH to the people who were asking a king from him.
And he said: This will be the right of the king who will reign over you. Your sons he will take and set for himself in his chariotry and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariot;
and to appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and to plough his ploughing and reap his reaping, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariotry.
And your daughters he will take for perfumers and for cooks and for bakers.
And your fields and your vineyards and your good olive groves he will take, and give them to his servants.
And of your seed and your vineyards he will take a tenth, and give it to his officials and to his servants.
And your male servants and your female servants and your best young men and your donkeys he will take, and use them for his work.
Your flocks he will take a tenth of; and you yourselves will become servants to him.
And you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves; and YHWH will not answer you on that day.
And the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel; and they said: No! But a king shall be over us,
and we also will be like all the nations; and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.
And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he spoke them in the ears of YHWH.
And YHWH said to Samuel: Listen to their voice, and make a king reign over them. And Samuel said to the men of Israel: Go, each to his own city.

1 samuel_9.t: And there was a man from Benjamin, and his name was Kish son of Abiel son of Zeror son of Becorath son of Aphiah, a son of a Jaminite man, a mighty man of substance.
And he had a son, and his name was Saul, a young man and good; and there was no man among the sons of Israel better than he. From his shoulder upwards he was taller than all the people.
And the she-asses of Kish, Saul's father, were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son: Take with you, please, one of the servants, and arise, go, seek the she-asses.

And he passed through the hill country of Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalishah, and they did not find them. And they passed through the land of Shaalim, and there was nothing; and he passed through the land of the Jaminite, and they did not find them.
They came into the land of Zuph, and Saul said to his servant who was with him: Come, let us turn back, lest my father cease from the she-asses and be anxious for us.

And he said to him: Behold, please, a man of God is in this city, and the man is honoured; all that he speaks certainly comes to pass. Now let us go there; perhaps he will tell us our way on which we have gone.
And Saul said to his servant: But see, if we go, what shall we bring to the man? For the bread is used up from our bags, and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What is with us?
And the servant answered Saul again and said: Behold, there is found in my hand a quarter of a shekel of silver; and I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.
Formerly in Israel, thus a man said when he went to consult God: Come, let us go to the seer — for the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.
And Saul said to his servant: Your word is good. Come, let us go. And they went to the city where the man of God was.
They were going up the ascent of the city, and they found young women coming out to draw water; and they said to them: Is the seer in this place?
And they answered them and said: He is; behold, he is ahead of you. Hurry now, for today he has come to the city, because there is a sacrifice today for the people at the high place.

As you come into the city, so you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice — after that those who are invited eat. And now go up, for at this very time you will find him.
And they went up to the city. They were coming into the midst of the city, and behold, Samuel was coming out to meet them, to go up to the high place.
And YHWH had uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came, saying:

About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as leader over my people Israel; and he will deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have seen my people, for their cry has come to me.
And Samuel saw Saul, and YHWH answered him: Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you — this one shall restrain my people.
And Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said: Tell me, please, where is the house of the seer?

And Samuel answered Saul and said: I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, and you shall eat with me today; and in the morning I will send you away, and all that is in your heart I will tell you.

And as for the she-asses lost to you three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And to whom does all the desire of Israel belong? Is it not to you and to all your father's house?

And Saul answered and said: Am I not a Jaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And is my clan not the least of all the clans of the tribes of Benjamin? And why have you spoken to me in this way?
And Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the room, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited; and they were about thirty men.
And Samuel said to the cook: Give the portion that I gave you, of which I said to you: Put it beside you.

And the cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it, and set it before Saul; and he said: Behold, what was left — set it before you, eat; for it has been kept for you for the appointed time, as I said: I have invited the people. And Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
And they went down from the high place to the city; and he spoke with Saul on the roof.

And they rose early; and it happened, as the dawn came up, that Samuel called to Saul on the roof, saying: Arise, and I will send you away. And Saul arose, and the two of them went outside, he and Samuel.

They were going down at the edge of the city, and Samuel said to Saul: Say to the servant that he should pass on before us — and he passed on — and you, stand still as at this time, and I will make you hear the word of God.

1 samuel_10.t: And Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him, and said: Has not YHWH anointed you over his inheritance as leader?

When you go today from me, you will find two men near the tomb of Rachel in the territory of Benjamin, at Zelzah; and they will say to you: The she-asses that you went to seek have been found. And behold, your father has abandoned the matter of the she-asses and is anxious for you, saying: What shall I do about my son?

And you will pass on from there and beyond, and come to the great tree of Tabor; and three men will find you there, going up to God at Bethel — one carrying three kids, and one carrying three round loaves of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.
And they will ask you about your welfare and give you two loaves of bread, and you will take them from their hand.

After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the garrisons of the Philistines are; and it will be, as you come there to the city, that you will meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place, and before them a harp and a tambourine and a flute and a lyre, and they will be prophesying.
And the spirit of YHWH will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.
And it will be, when these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds, for God is with you.

And you shall go down before me to Gilgal; and behold, I am coming down to you to offer up burnt offerings, to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do.
And it happened, when he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, that God turned another heart for him; and all these signs came on that day.
And they came there to Gibeah, and behold, a company of prophets to meet him; and the spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

And it happened, everyone who knew him from yesterday and before saw, and behold, he was prophesying with prophets; and the people said, each to his neighbour: What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?
And a man from there answered and said: And who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb: Is Saul also among the prophets?
And he finished prophesying and came to the high place.
And Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant: Where did you go? And he said: To seek the she-asses. And we saw that they were not there, and we went to Samuel.
And Saul's uncle said: Tell me, please, what Samuel said to you.
And Saul said to his uncle: He certainly told us that the she-asses had been found. But the matter of the kingship, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.
And Samuel called the people together to YHWH at Mizpah.

And he said to the sons of Israel: Thus said YHWH, the God of Israel: I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.

And you today have rejected your God, who is a deliverer for you from all your calamities and your troubles; and you have said to him: You shall set a king over us. And now, present yourselves before YHWH by your tribes and by your thousands.
And Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.
And he brought near the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the clan of the Matrite was taken; and Saul son of Kish was taken. And they sought him, and he was not found.
And they enquired again of YHWH: Has the man come here yet? And YHWH said: Behold, he is hiding himself among the baggage.
And they ran and took him from there, and he presented himself in the midst of the people; and he was taller than all the people from his shoulder upwards.
And Samuel said to all the people: Do you see the one whom YHWH has chosen? For there is none like him among all the people. And all the people shouted and said: Let the king live!
And Samuel spoke to the people the right of the kingship, and wrote it in the book and set it before YHWH. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his house.
And Saul also went to his house at Gibeah; and the force whose heart God had touched went with him.
And sons of worthlessness said: How will this one deliver us? And they despised him and brought him no gift. And he was like one who kept silent.

1 samuel_11.t: And Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash: Cut a covenant with us, and we will serve you.
And Nahash the Ammonite said to them: By this I will cut it with you, by gouging out every right eye of yours; and I will make it a reproach on all Israel.
And the elders of Jabesh said to him: Leave us seven days, and let us send messengers through all the territory of Israel; and if there is no one to deliver us, then we will come out to you.
And the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the ears of the people; and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
And behold, Saul was coming after the cattle from the field; and Saul said: What is with the people, that they are weeping? And they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
And the spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned exceedingly.

And he took a pair of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them through all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying: Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen. And the dread of YHWH fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
And he mustered them at Bezek; and the sons of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

And they said to the messengers who had come: Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: Tomorrow deliverance will be yours, when the sun is hot. And the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.
And the men of Jabesh said: Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you shall do to us according to all that is good in your eyes.

And it happened the next day that Saul set the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck down Ammon until the heat of the day. And those who were left were scattered, and no two of them were left together.
And the people said to Samuel: Who is the one who said, Shall Saul reign over us? Give up the men, and we will put them to death.
And Saul said: No one shall be put to death on this day, for today YHWH has done deliverance in Israel.
And Samuel said to the people: Come, and let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.

And all the people went to Gilgal, and they made Saul king there before YHWH at Gilgal; and they sacrificed there sacrifices of peace offerings before YHWH, and Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced there exceedingly.

1 samuel_12.t: And Samuel said to all Israel: Behold, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
And now, behold, the king is walking before you; and I am old and grey-haired, and behold, my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

Here I am. Testify against me before YHWH and before his anointed: Whose ox have I taken, and whose donkey have I taken? And whom have I oppressed, whom have I crushed? And from whose hand have I taken a ransom, that I might hide my eyes with it? And I will restore it to you.
And they said: You have not oppressed us and you have not crushed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of anyone.
And he said to them: YHWH is a witness against you, and his anointed is a witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand. And he said: He is a witness.
And Samuel said to the people: It is YHWH, who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your fathers up from the land of Egypt.
And now, present yourselves, and let me enter into judgement with you before YHWH concerning all the righteous acts of YHWH that he did with you and with your fathers.
When Jacob came to Egypt, your fathers cried out to YHWH; and YHWH sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

And they forgot YHWH their God, and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.
And they cried out to YHWH and said: We have sinned, for we have forsaken YHWH and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. And now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.
And YHWH sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and delivered you from the hand of your enemies round about; and you dwelt in security.
And you saw that Nahash king of the sons of Ammon was coming against you, and you said to me: No, but a king shall reign over us — while YHWH your God was your king.
And now, behold the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for; and behold, YHWH has set a king over you.
If you fear YHWH and serve him and listen to his voice, and do not rebel against the mouth of YHWH, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be after YHWH your God —
And if you do not listen to the voice of YHWH, and you rebel against the mouth of YHWH, then the hand of YHWH will be against you and against your fathers.
Also now, stand and see this great thing that YHWH is about to do before your eyes.

Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to YHWH, and he will give thunder and rain; and know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of YHWH by asking for yourselves a king.
And Samuel called to YHWH, and YHWH gave thunder and rain on that day; and all the people feared YHWH and Samuel exceedingly.
And all the people said to Samuel: Pray for your servants to YHWH your God, and let us not die; for we have added to all our sins an evil, by asking for ourselves a king.
And Samuel said to the people: Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil; nevertheless do not turn aside from after YHWH, and serve YHWH with all your heart.
And do not turn aside — for it would be after emptiness, which cannot benefit and cannot rescue, for they are emptiness.
For YHWH will not abandon his people, for the sake of his great name; for YHWH was pleased to make you a people for himself.
As for me also, far be it from me to sin against YHWH by ceasing to pray for you; and I will teach you the good and upright way.
Only fear YHWH and serve him in faithfulness with all your heart; for see what great things he has done with you.
And if you still do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.

1 samuel_13.t: Saul was a son of a year when he became king, and two years he reigned over Israel.

And Saul chose for himself three thousand from Israel; and two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people he sent away, each to his tents.
And Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard. And Saul blew the ram's horn throughout all the land, saying: Let the Hebrews hear!
And all Israel heard it said: Saul has struck the garrison of the Philistines, and also Israel has made itself odious among the Philistines. And the people were summoned after Saul to Gilgal.

And the Philistines gathered to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and a people like the sand that is on the seashore for multitude. And they came up and encamped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

And the men of Israel saw that they were in distress, for the people were hard pressed; and the people hid themselves in the caves and in the thickets and in the rocks and in the underground chambers and in the cisterns.
And Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; and Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people trembled after him.
And he waited seven days, to the appointed time that Samuel had set; and Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
And Saul said: Bring near to me the burnt offering and the peace offerings. And he offered up the burnt offering.
And it happened, as he finished offering up the burnt offering, that behold, Samuel was coming; and Saul went out to meet him, to bless him.

And Samuel said: What have you done? And Saul said: Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and you had not come at the appointed time of the days, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
and I said: Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not entreated the face of YHWH. And I forced myself, and I offered up the burnt offering.
And Samuel said to Saul: You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of YHWH your God, which he commanded you; for now YHWH would have established your kingdom over Israel for ever.

And now your kingdom will not stand. YHWH has sought for himself a man according to his own heart, and YHWH has appointed him as leader over his people, because you have not kept what YHWH commanded you.
And Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul mustered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were found with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin; and the Philistines encamped at Michmash.
And the destroyer went out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned toward the road of Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
and one company turned toward the road of Beth-horon; and one company turned toward the road of the border that looks down over the Valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
And a craftsman was not to be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said: Lest the Hebrews make a sword or a spear.
And all Israel would go down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his ploughshare and his mattock and his axe and his ploughshare.
And the charge was a pim for the ploughshares and for the mattocks and for the three-pronged fork and for the axes, and to set the goad straight.
And it happened, on the day of battle, that no sword or spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and with Jonathan; but it was found for Saul and for Jonathan his son.
And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

1 samuel_14.t: And the day came, and Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armour: Come, let us cross over to the garrison of the Philistines that is on the other side over there. And to his father he did not tell it.
And Saul was staying at the edge of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree that is in Migron; and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.
And Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli, the priest of YHWH at Shiloh, was bearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.

And between the passes by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the garrison of the Philistines, there was a tooth of crag on the one side and a tooth of crag on the other side; and the name of the one was Bozez and the name of the other Seneh.
The one tooth was a pillar on the north, opposite Michmash, and the other on the south, opposite Geba.

And Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armour: Come, let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps YHWH will act for us, for there is no restraint to YHWH, to deliver by many or by few.
And the bearer of his armour said to him: Do all that is in your heart. Turn where you will; here I am with you, according to your heart.
And Jonathan said: Behold, we are crossing over to the men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.
If they say this to us: Stand still until we reach you — then we will stand where we are, and we will not go up to them.
And if they say this: Come up to us — then we will go up, for YHWH has given them into our hand; and this will be the sign for us.
And the two of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines; and the Philistines said: Behold, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves.

And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and the bearer of his armour and said: Come up to us, and we will make something known to you. And Jonathan said to the bearer of his armour: Come up after me, for YHWH has given them into the hand of Israel.
And Jonathan went up on his hands and on his feet, and the bearer of his armour after him; and they fell before Jonathan, and the bearer of his armour was killing after him.
And the first slaughter that Jonathan and the bearer of his armour struck was about twenty men, within about half a furrow of an acre of field.
And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the destroyer trembled, they also. And the earth quaked, and it became a trembling of God.
And the watchmen of Saul at Gibeah of Benjamin saw, and behold, the multitude was melting away and going, and here.
And Saul said to the people who were with him: Muster, please, and see who has gone from us. And they mustered, and behold, Jonathan and the bearer of his armour were not there.
And Saul said to Ahijah: Bring near the ark of God — for the ark of God was on that day with the sons of Israel.
And it happened, while Saul was speaking to the priest, that the tumult in the camp of the Philistines went on growing and growing. And Saul said to the priest: Withdraw your hand.
And Saul and all the people who were with him were called together, and they came to the battle; and behold, each man's sword was against his neighbour — a very great panic.
And the Hebrews who had belonged to the Philistines as before, who had gone up with them into the camp round about — they too turned to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan.
And every man of Israel who had hidden himself in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, and they too pursued closely after them in the battle.
And YHWH delivered Israel on that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

And the men of Israel were hard pressed on that day; and Saul had put the people under an oath, saying: Cursed be the man who eats food until the evening, until I have avenged myself on my enemies. And none of the people tasted food.
And all the land came into the forest; and there was honey on the surface of the field.
And the people came into the forest, and behold, a flow of honey; and no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

And Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under the oath; and he stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb, and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
And a man from the people answered and said: Your father certainly put the people under an oath, saying: Cursed be the man who eats food today. And the people were weary.
And Jonathan said: My father has troubled the land. See, please, how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
How much more, if the people had eaten freely today of the plunder of their enemies that they found! For now the defeat among the Philistines has not been great.
And they struck down the Philistines on that day, from Michmash to Aijalon; and the people were very weary.
And the people rushed on the plunder and took sheep and cattle and calves and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate with the blood.
And they told Saul, saying: Behold, the people are sinning against YHWH by eating with the blood. And he said: You have acted treacherously. Roll a large stone to me today.

And Saul said: Scatter among the people and say to them: Bring near to me each his ox and each his sheep, and slaughter here and eat, and do not sin against YHWH by eating with the blood. And all the people brought near, each his ox in his hand, that night, and slaughtered there.
And Saul built an altar to YHWH; it was the first altar he began to build to YHWH.

And Saul said: Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder among them until the light of the morning, and let us not leave a man among them. And they said: Do all that is good in your eyes. And the priest said: Let us draw near here to God.
And Saul enquired of God: Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel? And he did not answer him on that day.
And Saul said: Draw near here, all you corners of the people, and know and see how this sin has come about today.
For as YHWH lives, who delivers Israel — even if it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. And no one from all the people answered him.
And he said to all Israel: You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on one side. And the people said to Saul: Do what is good in your eyes.
And Saul said to YHWH, the God of Israel: Give Thummim. And Jonathan and Saul were taken, and the people went out.
And Saul said: Cast between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.
And Saul said to Jonathan: Tell me what you have done. And Jonathan told him and said: I certainly tasted with the end of the staff that was in my hand a little honey. Here I am; I will die.
And Saul said: So may God do, and so may he add — for you shall surely die, Jonathan.

And the people said to Saul: Shall Jonathan die, who has done this great deliverance in Israel? Far be it! As YHWH lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has acted with God this day. And the people redeemed Jonathan, and he did not die.
And Saul went up from after the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.

And Saul took the kingship over Israel, and he waged war round about against all his enemies — against Moab and against the sons of Ammon and against Edom and against the kings of Zobah and against the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he acted wickedly.
And he did valiantly and struck Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of the one who plundered it.
And the sons of Saul were Jonathan and Ishvi and Malchi-shua; and the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merab and the name of the younger Michal.
And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
And Kish was Saul's father, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
And the war was severe against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and Saul saw every mighty man and every son of strength, and gathered him to himself.

1 samuel_15.t: And Samuel said to Saul: It was I whom YHWH sent to anoint you as king over his people, over Israel. And now, listen to the voice of the words of YHWH.
Thus said YHWH of hosts: I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how it set itself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.
Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to destruction all that it has; and do not spare it, but put to death from man to woman, from child to suckling, from ox to sheep, from camel to donkey.
And Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand of the men of Judah.
And Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the wadi.

And Saul said to the Kenite: Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I sweep you away with them; for you showed loyalty to all the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt. And the Kenite departed from among Amalek.
And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as you come to Shur, which is opposite Egypt.
And he seized Agag king of Amalek alive; and all the people he devoted to destruction with the mouth of the sword.

And Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and the cattle and the fatlings and the lambs, and all that was good; and they were not willing to devote them to destruction. But all the property that was despised and worthless — that they devoted to destruction.
And the word of YHWH came to Samuel, saying:
I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not carried out my words. And it burned within Samuel, and he cried out to YHWH all the night.

And Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and it was told to Samuel: Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he was setting up a monument for himself; and he turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal.
And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him: Blessed are you to YHWH! I have carried out the word of YHWH.
And Samuel said: And what is this sound of sheep in my ears, and the sound of cattle that I hear?
And Saul said: They brought them from the Amalekites, because the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle in order to sacrifice to YHWH your God; and the rest we devoted to destruction.
And Samuel said to Saul: Stop, and let me tell you what YHWH said to me last night. And he said to him: Speak.
And Samuel said: Was it not when you were small in your own eyes that you became the head of the tribes of Israel? And YHWH anointed you as king over Israel.
And YHWH sent you on a journey and said: Go and devote to destruction the sinners, Amalek, and wage war against it until they have finished them.
And why did you not listen to the voice of YHWH? And you rushed on the plunder and did the evil in the eyes of YHWH.
And Saul said to Samuel: I did listen to the voice of YHWH, and I went on the journey on which YHWH sent me; and I brought Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to destruction.
And the people took from the plunder sheep and cattle, the choicest of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to YHWH your God at Gilgal.
And Samuel said: Has YHWH delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of YHWH? Behold, to listen is better than sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is the sin of divination, and presumption is wickedness and teraphim. Because you have rejected the word of YHWH, he has rejected you from being king.
And Saul said to Samuel: I have sinned, for I transgressed the mouth of YHWH and your words; for I feared the people and listened to their voice.
And now, forgive my sin, please, and return with me, that I may bow down to YHWH.
And Samuel said to Saul: I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of YHWH; and YHWH has rejected you from being king over Israel.
And Samuel turned round to go, and he took hold of the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
And Samuel said to him: YHWH has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to your neighbour, who is better than you.
And also the Glory of Israel does not deal falsely and does not regret; for he is not a man, that he should regret.
And he said: I have sinned. Now honour me, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel; and return with me, and I will bow down to YHWH your God.
And Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul bowed down to YHWH.
And Samuel said: Bring near to me Agag king of Amalek. And Agag came to him cheerfully. And Agag said: Truly the bitterness of death has departed.
And Samuel said: As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women. And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before YHWH at Gilgal.
And Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul. And YHWH regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

1 samuel_16.t: And YHWH said to Samuel: How long will you mourn over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen among his sons a king for myself.
And Samuel said: How can I go? Saul will hear, and he will kill me. And YHWH said: Take a heifer of the herd in your hand, and say: I have come to sacrifice to YHWH.
And you shall invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do; and you shall anoint for me the one whom I tell you.
And Samuel did what YHWH had said, and he came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city trembled to meet him and said: Do you come in peace?

And he said: In peace. I have come to sacrifice to YHWH. Set yourselves apart as holy, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he set Jesse and his sons apart as holy and invited them to the sacrifice.
And it happened, when they came, that he saw Eliab and said: Surely before YHWH is his anointed.
And YHWH said to Samuel: Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For it is not what a human sees: a human sees by the eyes, but YHWH sees by the heart.
And Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel; and he said: Neither has YHWH chosen this one.
And Jesse made Shammah pass by; and he said: Neither has YHWH chosen this one.
And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel; and Samuel said to Jesse: YHWH has not chosen these.

And Samuel said to Jesse: Are the young men finished? And he said: The youngest still remains, and behold, he is shepherding the flock. And Samuel said to Jesse: Send and bring him, for we will not sit down until he comes here.
And he sent and brought him. And he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and good to look at. And YHWH said: Arise, anoint him, for this is he.
And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the spirit of YHWH rushed upon David from that day and onwards. And Samuel arose and went to Ramah.
And the spirit of YHWH departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from YHWH terrified him.
And Saul's servants said to him: Behold, please, an evil spirit of God is terrifying you.

Let our lord say, please — your servants are before you — let them seek a man who knows how to play on the lyre; and it will be, when an evil spirit of God is upon you, that he will play with his hand, and it will be good for you.
And Saul said to his servants: See, please, for me a man who plays well, and bring him to me.

And one of the young men answered and said: Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play — and a mighty man of valour, and a man of war, and discerning in speech, and a man of form; and YHWH is with him.
And Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said: Send to me David your son, who is with the flock.
And Jesse took a donkey, bread, and a skin of wine, and one kid of the goats, and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.
And David came to Saul and stood before him; and he loved him exceedingly, and he became his armour-bearer.
And Saul sent to Jesse, saying: Let David stand before me, please, for he has found favour in my eyes.
And it happened, when a spirit of God was upon Saul, that David took the lyre and played with his hand; and there was relief for Saul, and it was good for him, and the evil spirit departed from him.

1 samuel_17.t: And the Philistines gathered their armies for battle, and they were gathered at Socoh which belongs to Judah; and they encamped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes-dammim.
And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and they deployed for battle to meet the Philistines.
And the Philistines were standing on the mountain on one side, and Israel were standing on the mountain on the other side; and the valley was between them.
And a man of the space between came out from the camps of the Philistines; his name was Goliath, from Gath; his height was six cubits and a span.
And a helmet of bronze was on his head, and he was clothed in body armour of scales; and the weight of the body armour was five thousand shekels of bronze.
And leg armour of bronze was on his legs, and a javelin of bronze between his shoulders.
And the wood of his spear was like a weavers' beam, and the blade of his spear was six hundred shekels of iron; and the bearer of the body shield was walking before him.

And he stood and called out to the battle lines of Israel and said to them: Why do you come out to deploy for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and you servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
If he is able to fight with me and strike me down, then we will become slaves to you; and if I prevail over him and strike him down, then you will become slaves to us, and you will serve us.
And the Philistine said: I defy the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together.
And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
And David was the son of that Ephrathite man from Bethlehem of Judah, and his name was Jesse; and he had eight sons. And the man in the days of Saul was old, advanced among men.

And the three eldest sons of Jesse had gone; they had gone after Saul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who had gone into the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and his second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
And David — he was the youngest; and the three eldest had gone after Saul.
And David was going and returning from Saul to shepherd his father's flock at Bethlehem.
And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and took his stand for forty days.
And Jesse said to David his son: Take, please, to your brothers this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread, and bring them quickly to the camp, to your brothers.
And these ten portions of milk you shall bring to the commander of the thousand; and you shall attend to your brothers' welfare, and take their pledge.
And Saul and they and every man of Israel were in the Valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

And David rose early in the morning and left the flock with a keeper, and lifted up and went, just as Jesse had commanded him. And he came to the camp as the army was going out to the battle line, and they shouted the war cry in the battle.
And Israel and the Philistines deployed, battle line to meet battle line.
And David left the baggage from upon him in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the battle line; and he came and asked his brothers after their welfare.

And he was speaking with them, and behold, the man of the space between was coming up — Goliath the Philistine was his name, from Gath — from the battle lines of the Philistines; and he spoke according to these words, and David heard.
And every man of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from before him and were greatly afraid.

And the men of Israel said: Have you seen this man who comes up? For he comes up to defy Israel. And the man who strikes him down — the king will make him rich with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and will make his father's house free in Israel.

And David said to the men standing with him: What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has defied the battle lines of the living God?
And the people said to him according to this word, saying: So it will be done for the man who strikes him down.

And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David, and he said: Why is it that you have come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle.
And David said: What have I done now? Was it not a word?
And he turned away from beside him toward another, and spoke according to this word; and the people brought him back word, like the former word.
And the words that David spoke were heard, and they told them before Saul; and he sent for him.
And David said to Saul: Let no one's heart fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
And Saul said to David: You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth and he is a man of war from his youth.
And David said to Saul: Your servant was shepherding for his father among the flock, and the lion came, and the bear, and carried off a sheep from the flock.
And I went out after it and struck it and rescued it from its mouth; and it rose up against me, and I took hold of its beard and struck it and killed it.
Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear; and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the battle lines of the living God.
And David said: YHWH, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, he will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said to David: Go, and may YHWH be with you.
And Saul clothed David in his garments, and put a helmet of bronze on his head, and clothed him in body armour.

And David girded his sword over his garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. And David said to Saul: I am not able to walk in these, for I have not tested them. And David removed them from himself.

And he took his stick in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in the shepherds' bag that he had — in the pouch — and his sling was in his hand; and he drew near to the Philistine.
And the Philistine came, coming and drawing near to David; and the man who bore the body shield was before him.
And the Philistine looked and saw David, and despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy, with a handsome appearance.
And the Philistine said to David: Am I a dog, that you come against me with sticks? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
And the Philistine said to David: Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the field.

And David said to the Philistine: You come against me with sword and with spear and with javelin; and I come against you in the name of YHWH of hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have defied.

This day YHWH will deliver you up into my hand, and I will strike you down and remove your head from you; and I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that Israel has a God.
And all this assembly will know that YHWH does not save by sword and by spear, for the battle is YHWH's; and he will give you into our hand.
And it happened, when the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, that David hurried and ran to the battle line to meet the Philistine.
And David put his hand into the bag and took from there a stone, and slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
And David was stronger than the Philistine with the sling and with the stone, and he struck the Philistine down and killed him; and there was no sword in David's hand.

And David ran and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword and drew it from its sheath and killed him, and cut off his head with it. And the Philistines saw that their mighty man was dead, and they fled.

And the men of Israel and Judah arose and shouted the war cry, and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance to Gath and as far as the gates of Ekron. And the slain of the Philistines fell on the way of Shaaraim, and as far as Gath and as far as Ekron.
And the sons of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines, and plundered their camps.
And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem; and his weapons he put in his own tent.
And when Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army: Whose son is this youth, Abner? And Abner said: As your being lives, O king, I do not know.
And the king said: You ask whose son the young man is.
And when David returned from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
And Saul said to him: Whose son are you, young man? And David said: The son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

1 samuel_18.t: And it happened, when he had finished speaking to Saul, that the being of Jonathan was bound to the being of David; and Jonathan loved him as his own being.
And Saul took him on that day and did not let him return to his father's house.
And Jonathan and David cut a covenant, because he loved him as his own being.
And Jonathan stripped off the robe that was on him and gave it to David, and his garments, and even his sword and his bow and his belt.
And David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he prospered; and Saul set him over the men of war. And it was good in the eyes of all the people, and also in the eyes of Saul's servants.

And it happened, as they were coming, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, that the women came out from all the cities of Israel to sing, and the dancing, to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.
And the women who played sang and said: Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands.

And it burned within Saul exceedingly, and this matter was displeasing in his eyes; and he said: They have ascribed to David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed the thousands. And what more is there for him but the kingship?
And Saul was eyeing David from that day and onwards.
And it happened the next day that an evil spirit of God rushed upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house; and David was playing with his hand as day by day, and the spear was in Saul's hand.
And Saul hurled the spear, and said: I will strike David to the wall! And David turned aside from before him twice.
And Saul was afraid before David, for YHWH was with him and had turned aside from Saul.
And Saul removed him from himself and made him a commander of a thousand for himself; and he went out and came in before the people.
And David was prospering in all his ways, and YHWH was with him.
And Saul saw that he was prospering exceedingly, and he was in dread of him.
And all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.

And Saul said to David: Here is my elder daughter Merab; her I will give you as a wife. Only be for me a son of strength, and fight the battles of YHWH. And Saul said: Let my hand not be against him, but let the hand of the Philistines be against him.
And David said to Saul: Who am I, and who are my kinsfolk, my father's clan in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?
And it happened, at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, that she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.
And Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David; and they told Saul, and the matter was right in his eyes.

And Saul said: I will give her to him, and she will become a snare for him, and the hand of the Philistines will be against him. And Saul said to David: By the second one you shall be son-in-law to me today.
And Saul commanded his servants: Speak to David in secret, saying: Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you. And now, be son-in-law to the king.
And Saul's servants spoke these words in David's ears; and David said: Is it a trifling thing in your eyes to be son-in-law to the king, when I am a poor man and lightly esteemed?
And Saul's servants told him, saying: According to these words David spoke.

And Saul said: Thus you shall say to David: The king has no delight in a bride-price, but in a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to avenge himself on the king's enemies. And Saul planned to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
And his servants told David these words, and the matter was right in David's eyes, to be son-in-law to the king. And the days were not completed.

And David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down among the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full to the king, to be son-in-law to the king. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.
And Saul saw and knew that YHWH was with David; and Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.
And Saul was still more afraid before David; and Saul was David's enemy all the days.
And the commanders of the Philistines went out; and it happened, as often as they went out, that David was more successful than all Saul's servants; and his name was greatly esteemed.

1 samuel_19.t: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about killing David; but Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted in David exceedingly.
And Jonathan told David, saying: Saul my father is seeking to kill you. And now, take care, please, in the morning; and stay in a hiding place and hide yourself.
And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak about you to my father; and I will see what there is and tell you.

And Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father, and said to him: Let the king not sin against his servant, against David, for he has not sinned against you, and because his deeds have been very good for you.

And he put his life in his palm and struck down the Philistine, and YHWH made a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. And why will you sin against innocent blood, by killing David without cause?
And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore: As YHWH lives, he shall not be put to death.
And Jonathan called David and told him all these words; and Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was before him as yesterday and before.
And the war continued; and David went out and fought against the Philistines, and struck them with a great defeat, and they fled from before him.
And an evil spirit of YHWH was upon Saul, and he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand; and David was playing with his hand.
And Saul sought to strike David with the spear, and the wall; and he slipped away from before Saul, and he struck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.

And Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him and to kill him in the morning. And Michal his wife told David, saying: If you do not deliver your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death.
And Michal let David down through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.
And Michal took the teraphim and put it on the bed, and the quilt of goats' hair she put at its head, and covered it with the garment.
And Saul sent messengers to fetch David, and she said: He is sick.
And Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying: Bring him up to me on the bed, to kill him.
And the messengers came, and behold, the teraphim was on the bed, with the quilt of goats' hair at its head.
And Saul said to Michal: Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he escaped? And Michal said to Saul: He said to me: Let me go — why should I kill you?
And David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed at Naioth.
And it was told to Saul: Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.

And Saul sent messengers to fetch David; and he saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as chief over them. And the spirit of God was upon Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.
And they told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers again, a third time, and they also prophesied.
And he also went himself to Ramah, and came as far as the great cistern that is at Secu; and he asked and said: Where are Samuel and David? And someone said: Behold, at Naioth in Ramah.
And he went there, to Naioth in Ramah; and the spirit of God was upon him also, and he went on, going and prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel; and he fell down naked all that day and all the night. Therefore they say: Is Saul also among the prophets?

1 samuel_20.t: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and said before Jonathan: What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin before your father, that he is seeking my life?

And he said to him: Far be it! You will not die. Behold, my father does not do anything great or anything small without uncovering my ear; and why should my father hide this thing from me? It is not so.

And David swore again and said: Your father knows well that I have found favour in your eyes, and he has said: Let Jonathan not know this, lest he be grieved. But as YHWH lives and as your being lives, there is only about a step between me and death.
And Jonathan said to David: Whatever your being says, I will do for you.
And David said to Jonathan: Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I should certainly sit with the king to eat. But let me go, and I will hide myself in the field until the third evening.
If your father misses me at all, then say: David asked leave of me urgently to run to Bethlehem his city, for the yearly sacrifice is there for all the clan.
If he says this — Good — then there is safety for your servant. But if it burns hot within him, know that the harm has been determined by him.

And you shall do loyalty to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of YHWH with you. And if there is iniquity in me, kill me yourself; but why should you bring me to your father?
And Jonathan said: Far be it from you! For if I ever know that the harm has been determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you?
And David said to Jonathan: Who will tell me? Or what if your father answers you harshly?
And Jonathan said to David: Come, and let us go out to the field. And the two of them went out to the field.

And Jonathan said to David: YHWH, God of Israel — when I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and behold, there is good toward David, shall I not then send to you and uncover your ear?

So may YHWH do to Jonathan, and so may he add, if it seems good to my father to bring the harm upon you and I do not uncover your ear and send you away, and you go in peace. And may YHWH be with you, as he has been with my father.
And if I am still alive — and may you not fail to do the loyalty of YHWH with me — then I shall not die;
and may you not cut off your loyalty from my house for ever — not even when YHWH cuts off the enemies of David, every one, from the face of the ground.
And Jonathan cut a covenant with the house of David: And may YHWH require it at the hand of David's enemies.
And Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, for he loved him with the love of his own being.
And Jonathan said to him: Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will be empty.
And on the third day you shall go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself on the day of the deed, and stay beside the stone Ezel.
And I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, sending them for myself at a target.

And behold, I will send the lad: Go, find the arrows. If I say plainly to the lad: Behold, the arrows are on this side of you — fetch it and come, for it is safe for you, and there is nothing, as YHWH lives.
But if I say this to the young man: Behold, the arrows are beyond you — go, for YHWH has sent you away.
And as for the matter that we have spoken, I and you — behold, YHWH is between me and you for ever.
And David hid himself in the field. And the new moon came, and the king sat down to the food to eat.
And the king sat on his seat as at other times, on the seat by the wall; and Jonathan arose, and Abner sat at Saul's side; and David's place was empty.
And Saul said nothing on that day, for he said: It is an accident; he is not clean, surely he is not clean.
And it happened on the next day, the second of the new moon, that David's place was empty; and Saul said to Jonathan his son: Why has the son of Jesse not come to the food, either yesterday or today?
And Jonathan answered Saul: David asked leave of me urgently for Bethlehem,

and he said: Let me go, please, for we have a clan sacrifice in the city, and my brother himself has commanded me. And now, if I have found favour in your eyes, let me slip away, please, and see my brothers. Therefore he has not come to the king's table.

And Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him: Son of a perverse woman of rebelliousness! Do I not know that you are choosing the son of Jesse — to your own shame and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?
For all the days that the son of Jesse lives on the ground, you will not be established, you and your kingdom. And now, send and fetch him to me, for he is a son of death.
And Jonathan answered Saul his father and said to him: Why should he be put to death? What has he done?
And Saul hurled the spear at him to strike him; and Jonathan knew that it had been determined by his father to kill David.
And Jonathan arose from the table in the heat of anger, and he did not eat food on the second day of the new moon, for he was grieved concerning David, because his father had put him to shame.
And it happened in the morning that Jonathan went out to the field at the appointed time with David, and a small lad was with him.
And he said to his lad: Run, find, please, the arrows that I am shooting. The lad ran, and he shot the arrow to make it pass beyond him.
And the lad came to the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot; and Jonathan called after the lad and said: Is not the arrow beyond you?
And Jonathan called after the lad: Quickly, hurry, do not stand still! And Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows and came to his master.
And the lad knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
And Jonathan gave his weapons to the lad who was his, and said to him: Go, take them to the city.
The lad went; and David arose from beside the south, and fell on his face to the ground and bowed down three times. And they kissed one another and wept with one another, until David exceeded.

And Jonathan said to David: Go in peace, since we have both sworn, the two of us, by the name of YHWH, saying: YHWH will be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, for ever. And he arose and went; and Jonathan came to the city.

1 samuel_21.t: And David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest; and Ahimelech trembled at meeting David and said to him: Why are you alone, and no man with you?
