And Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the king's house — he took everything; and he took the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
And King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place, and entrusted them to the hand of the commanders of the runners who guarded the entrance of the king's house.
And as often as the king came to the house of YHWH, the runners came and carried them, and returned them to the guardroom of the runners.
And when he humbled himself, the anger of YHWH turned back from him, so as not to destroy him to complete destruction; and also in Judah there were good things.

And King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned; for Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that YHWH had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
And he did the evil, for he did not set his heart to seek YHWH.

And the matters of Rehoboam, the former and the latter — are they not written in the words of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, for genealogical enrolment? And the wars of Rehoboam and Jeroboam were all the days.
And Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David; and Abijah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_13.t: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
And Abijah joined battle with an army of mighty men of war, four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam drew up battle against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty in strength.
And Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
"Is it not for you to know that YHWH the God of Israel gave kingship to David over Israel for ever — to him and to his sons, a covenant of salt?
"But Jeroboam son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon son of David, arose and rebelled against his master.

"And empty men, worthless fellows, gathered to him and made themselves strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon; and Rehoboam was a young man and weak of heart, and did not show himself strong before them.

"And now you are saying you will show yourselves strong before the kingdom of YHWH in the hand of the sons of David; and you are a great multitude, and with you are the golden calves that Jeroboam made you as gods.

"Have you not driven out the priests of YHWH, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made yourselves priests like the peoples of the lands? Anyone who comes to fill his hand with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest to what are not gods.
"But as for us, YHWH is our God, and we have not forsaken him; and priests serving YHWH are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites are at the work.

"And they burn to YHWH burnt offerings morning by morning and evening by evening, and incense of spices, and the row of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand and its lamps to burn every evening; for we keep the duty of YHWH our God, and you have forsaken him.

"And look — God is with us at our head, and his priests, and the trumpets of alarm to sound the alarm against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight against YHWH the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed."
But Jeroboam had brought the ambush round to come from behind them; and they were in front of Judah, and the ambush behind them.
And Judah turned, and behold, the battle was before them and behind. And they cried out to YHWH, and the priests were blowing the trumpets.
And the men of Judah sounded the alarm; and it was, when the men of Judah sounded the alarm, that God defeated Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
And the sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.
And Abijah and his people struck them with a great striking; and there fell slain of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.
And the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah prevailed, because they leaned on YHWH the God of their fathers.
And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel and its daughters, and Jeshanah and its daughters, and Ephrain and its daughters.
And Jeroboam did not retain strength again in the days of Abijah; and YHWH struck him, and he died.
And Abijah strengthened himself, and took for himself fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
And the rest of the matters of Abijah, and his ways and his words, are written in the record of the prophet Iddo.

2 chronicles_14.t: And Abijah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son became king in his place. In his days the land was quiet ten years.
And Asa did the good and the right in the eyes of YHWH his God.
And he removed the foreign altars and the high places, and broke down the pillars and cut down the Asherim.
And he said to Judah to seek YHWH the God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.
And he removed from all the cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars; and the kingdom was quiet before him.
And he built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was quiet; and there was no war with him in those years, because YHWH had given him rest.

And he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with wall and towers, gates and bars. The land is still before us, because we have sought YHWH our God; we sought him, and he has given us rest all around." And they built and prospered.

And Asa had an army bearing large shield and spear, from Judah three hundred thousand; and from Benjamin, bearing shield and bending the bow, two hundred and eighty thousand. All these were mighty men of valour.
And Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a thousand thousands and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
And Asa went out before him, and they drew up battle in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa called out to YHWH his God and said, "YHWH, there is none like you to help, between the mighty and one with no strength. Help us, YHWH our God, for on you we lean, and in your name we have come against this multitude. YHWH, you are our God; let no man retain strength against you."
And YHWH defeated the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar; and there fell of the Cushites so that they had no preservation, for they were broken before YHWH and before his camp. And they carried off very much booty.
And they struck all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of YHWH was on them; and they plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.
And they also struck the tents of livestock, and took captive sheep in abundance and camels; and they returned to Jerusalem.

2 chronicles_15.t: And Azariah son of Oded — the spirit of God was upon him.

And he went out before Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin: YHWH is with you while you are with him; and if you seek him, he will let himself be found by you; and if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
"And for many days Israel was without a true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law;
"but it turned back in its distress to YHWH the God of Israel, and they sought him, and he let himself be found by them.
"And in those times there was no peace for the one going out or the one coming in, for great disturbances were on all the inhabitants of the lands.
"And they were crushed, nation by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every trouble.
"But you, be strong, and let not your hands drop, for there is reward for your work."

And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he strengthened himself and removed the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities that he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of YHWH that was before the porch of YHWH.

And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those sojourning with them from Ephraim and Manasseh and from Simeon; for they fell over to him from Israel in great numbers, when they saw that YHWH his God was with him.
And they gathered to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
And they sacrificed to YHWH on that day, from the booty they had brought: seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
And they entered into the covenant, to seek YHWH the God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
and everyone who would not seek YHWH the God of Israel would be put to death, from small to great, from man to woman.
And they swore to YHWH with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets and with ram's horns.
And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart, and with all their will they had sought him; and he let himself be found by them, and YHWH gave them rest all around.

And also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king — he removed her from being queen mother, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; and Asa cut down her abominable image, crushed it and burned it in the wadi Kidron.
But the high places were not removed from Israel; only the heart of Asa was complete all his days.
And he brought the holy things of his father and his own holy things into the house of God: silver and gold and articles.
And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

2 chronicles_16.t: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah, so as not to allow anyone to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
And Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of YHWH and the king's house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,
"A covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Here, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, that he may go up from me."
And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of the armies that were his against the cities of Israel; and they struck Ijon and Dan and Abel-maim and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And it was, when Baasha heard, he ceased from building Ramah and made his work stop.
And King Asa took all Judah, and they carried off the stones of Ramah and its timber that Baasha had built with; and he built Geba and Mizpah with them.

And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you leaned on the king of Aram and did not lean on YHWH your God, therefore the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
"Were not the Cushites and the Libyans an army in great numbers, with chariots and horsemen in exceedingly great abundance? Yet because you leaned on YHWH, he gave them into your hand.
"For YHWH — his eyes rove through all the earth, to show himself strong with those whose heart is complete toward him. You have acted foolishly in this; for from now on there will be wars with you."
And Asa was angry at the seer and put him in the house of the stocks, for he was in a rage with him over this. And Asa crushed some of the people at that time.
And behold, the matters of Asa, the former and the latter — behold, they are written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Asa became diseased in his feet in the thirty-ninth year of his reign; his disease was exceedingly severe. And even in his disease he did not seek YHWH, but the physicians.
And Asa lay down with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

And they buried him in his own graves that he had dug for himself in the city of David, and laid him on the bier that he had filled with spices and various kinds blended in a perfumer's mixture; and they made an exceedingly great burning for him.

2 chronicles_17.t: And Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
And he put an army in all the fortified cities of Judah, and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
And YHWH was with Jehoshaphat, for he walked in the former ways of David his father, and did not seek the Baals;
for he sought the God of his father, and walked in his commandments and not according to the deeds of Israel.
And YHWH established the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah gave tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had wealth and honour in abundance.
And his heart was high in the ways of YHWH; and again he removed the high places and the Asherim from Judah.
And in the third year of his reign he sent his officials — Ben-hail and Obadiah and Zechariah and Nethanel and Micaiah — to teach in the cities of Judah;

and with them the Levites — Shemaiah and Nethaniah and Zebadiah and Asahel and Shemiramoth and Jehonathan and Adonijah and Tobijah and Tob-adonijah, the Levites — and with them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests.
And they taught in Judah, and with them was the scroll of the law of YHWH; and they went round through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
And the dread of YHWH was on all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, and they did not make war with Jehoshaphat.

And some of the Philistines were bringing Jehoshaphat tribute, and silver as a load; also the Arabs were bringing him flocks — seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
And Jehoshaphat went on and became exceedingly great; and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah.
And he had much property in the cities of Judah; and men of war, mighty men of valour, were in Jerusalem.
And these were their musters by their fathers' houses: of Judah, commanders of thousands — Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
and at his hand, Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
and at his hand, Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered himself to YHWH, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
and of Benjamin, a mighty man of valour, Eliada, and with him two hundred thousand equipped with bow and shield;
and at his hand, Jehozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand equipped for the host.
These were those serving the king, besides those whom the king put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

2 chronicles_18.t: And Jehoshaphat had wealth and honour in abundance; and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.
And after some years he went down to Ahab, to Samaria; and Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and incited him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.
And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" And he said to him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; and with you in the battle."
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Seek the word of YHWH today, please."

And the king of Israel assembled the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or shall I desist?" And they said, "Go up, and God will give it into the hand of the king."
And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not a prophet of YHWH here still, that we may enquire of him?"

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man to consult YHWH through, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me but evil all his days — he is Micaiah son of Imlah." And Jehoshaphat said, "Let not the king say so."
And the king of Israel called one court official and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly."

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, clothed in garments, and sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says YHWH: 'With these you shall gore Aram until they are finished.'"
And all the prophets were prophesying so, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, and YHWH will give it into the hand of the king."

And the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Look, the words of the prophets are with one mouth good toward the king; let your word, please, be like one of theirs, and speak good."
And Micaiah said, "As YHWH lives, what my God says, that I will speak."
And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or shall I desist?" And he said, "Go up and succeed, and they will be given into your hand."
And the king said to him, "How many times shall I make you swear that you will speak to me nothing but truth in the name of YHWH?"
And he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And YHWH said, 'These have no masters; let them return, each to his own house, in peace.'"
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not say to you that he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"
And he said, "Therefore hear the word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on his right hand and on his left.
"And YHWH said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, so that he goes up and falls at Ramoth-gilead?' And this one was saying one thing and that one another.
"And the spirit came out and stood before YHWH and said, 'I will entice him.' And YHWH said to him, 'By what?'
"And it said, 'I will go out and become a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.' And he said, 'You will entice, and you will also prevail. Go out and do so.'
"And now, look — YHWH has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of these prophets of yours; and YHWH has spoken calamity concerning you."
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah drew near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the spirit of YHWH pass from me to speak with you?"
And Micaiah said, "Look, you will be seeing on that day when you go into an inner room to hide yourself."
And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the official of the city, and to Joash the son of the king,
"and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this one in the house of imprisonment, and feed him bread of oppression and water of oppression, until I return in peace.'"
And Micaiah said, "If you return, returning, in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me." And he said, "Hear, you peoples, all of you!"
And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up against Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your own garments." And the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
And the king of Aram had commanded the commanders of his chariotry, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, but with the king of Israel alone."

And it was, when the commanders of the chariotry saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "He is the king of Israel," and they surrounded him to fight. And Jehoshaphat cried out, and YHWH helped him, and God lured them away from him.
And it was, when the commanders of the chariotry saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from after him.

And a man drew the bow in his innocence and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the body armour; and he said to the charioteer, "Turn your hand and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded."
And the battle went up on that day; and the king of Israel was propping himself up in the chariot facing Aram until the evening, and he died at the time of the going down of the sun.

2 chronicles_19.t: And Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his house in peace, to Jerusalem.
And Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked, and love those who hate YHWH? And because of this, wrath is upon you from before YHWH.
"But good things have been found in you, for you have burned the Asherahs out of the land and have set your heart to seek God."
And Jehoshaphat dwelt in Jerusalem; and he went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and turned them back to YHWH the God of their fathers.
And he appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, for each city;
and he said to the judges, "See what you are doing, for you do not judge for humankind but for YHWH; and he is with you in a matter of judgement.
"And now, let the dread of YHWH be upon you. Take care and act, for with YHWH our God there is no injustice, or lifting of faces, or taking of a bribe."

And also in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and the priests and some of the heads of the fathers of Israel, for the judgement of YHWH and for disputes; and they returned to Jerusalem.
And he commanded them, saying, "Thus you shall do, in the fear of YHWH, in faithfulness and with a complete heart.

"And any dispute that comes to you from your brothers who dwell in their cities — between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgements — you shall warn them, so that they do not become guilty before YHWH and wrath come upon you and upon your brothers. Thus you shall do, and you will not become guilty.

"And look — Amariah the chief priest is over you for every matter of YHWH, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, for every matter of the king; and the Levites are officials before you. Be strong and act, and may YHWH be with the good."

2 chronicles_20.t: And it was after this that the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.
And they came and told Jehoshaphat, saying, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram; and here they are in Hazazon-tamar" — that is En-gedi.
And Jehoshaphat was afraid, and set his face to seek YHWH, and proclaimed a fast over all Judah.
And Judah gathered to seek from YHWH; also from all the cities of Judah they came to seek YHWH.
And Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of YHWH, before the new court,
and said, "YHWH, God of our fathers, are you not God in the heavens? And you rule over all the kingdoms of the nations; and in your hand are power and might, and there is no standing against you.
"Did not you, our God, dispossess the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham your friend for ever?
"And they dwelt in it and built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,

"'If calamity comes upon us — sword, judgement, or pestilence or famine — we will stand before this house and before you, for your name is in this house; and we will cry out to you from our distress, and you will hear and save.'

"And now, look — the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you did not allow Israel to enter when they came from the land of Egypt, so that they turned aside from them and did not destroy them —
"and here they are, repaying us — by coming to drive us out from your possession that you gave us to possess.
"Our God, will you not enter into judgement with them? For there is no strength in us before this great multitude that is coming against us, and we do not know what to do — but our eyes are on you."
And all Judah was standing before YHWH — their little ones too, their wives and their children.
And Jahaziel son of Zechariah son of Benaiah son of Jeiel son of Mattaniah the Levite, of the sons of Asaph — the spirit of YHWH was upon him in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, "Pay attention, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! Thus says YHWH to you: 'You — do not fear and do not be dismayed before this great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God's.
"'Tomorrow go down against them. Here they are, coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the wadi, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

"'It is not for you to fight in this. Take your stand, stand still and see the salvation of YHWH with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Tomorrow go out before them, and YHWH will be with you.'"
And Jehoshaphat bowed low, face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before YHWH, to prostrate themselves to YHWH.
And the Levites, of the sons of the Kohathites and of the sons of the Korahites, stood up to praise YHWH the God of Israel with an exceedingly loud voice.

And they rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. And as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Trust in YHWH your God and you will be established; trust in his prophets and you will succeed."

And he consulted with the people, and appointed singers to YHWH and those praising in holy adornment, as they went out before the armed men, saying: "Give thanks to YHWH, for his steadfast love is for ever."
And at the time they began with a shout and praise, YHWH set ambushers against the sons of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.

And the sons of Ammon and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, to devote them to destruction and to annihilate them; and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped each other to destruction.
And Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness and turned toward the multitude — and there they were, corpses fallen to the ground; and there was no one who escaped.

And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their booty, and found among them in abundance both property and corpses and precious articles; and they stripped off for themselves until there was no carrying. And they were three days plundering the booty, for it was much.
And on the fourth day they assembled in the valley of Berachah, for there they blessed YHWH; therefore they have called the name of that place the valley of Berachah, until this day.
And every man of Judah and Jerusalem turned back, with Jehoshaphat at their head, to return to Jerusalem with joy; for YHWH had made them rejoice over their enemies.
And they came to Jerusalem with harps and lyres and trumpets, to the house of YHWH.
And the dread of God was on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that YHWH had fought against the enemies of Israel.
And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, and his God gave him rest all around.
And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
And he walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing the right in the eyes of YHWH.
Only the high places were not removed, and still the people had not set their heart on the God of their fathers.
And the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, the former and the latter — there they are, written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which was taken up into the scroll of the kings of Israel.
And after this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel; he acted wickedly in what he did.
And he allied himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish; and they made ships at Ezion-geber.

And Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, YHWH has broken your works." And the ships were broken, and they were not able to go to Tarshish.

2 chronicles_21.t: And Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Jehoram his son became king in his place.
And he had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah and Jehiel and Zechariah and Azariahu and Michael and Shephatiah. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
And their father gave them many gifts — silver and gold and precious things — with fortified cities in Judah; and the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, for he was the firstborn.
And Jehoram rose over the kingdom of his father and strengthened himself, and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the leaders of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH.
But YHWH was not willing to destroy the house of David, on account of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he had said, to give him a lamp, and to his sons, all the days.
In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king king over themselves.
And Jehoram crossed over with his commanders, and all the chariotry with him; and he arose by night and struck Edom, which was surrounding him, and the commanders of the chariotry.
And Edom has rebelled from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time from under his hand, because he had forsaken YHWH the God of his fathers.
He too made high places in the mountains of Judah, and made the inhabitants of Jerusalem prostitute themselves, and thrust Judah aside.

And a writing came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying: "Thus says YHWH, the God of David your father: 'Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

"'but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem prostitute themselves as the house of Ahab made them prostitute themselves, and have also killed your brothers, your father's house, who were better than you —
"'here — YHWH is about to strike a great blow on your people, and on your sons and your wives and all your property;
"'and you will be in great sicknesses, in a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out from the disease, days upon days.'"
And YHWH stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who were beside the Cushites,

and they came up against Judah and broke into it, and took captive all the property that was found belonging to the king's house, and also his sons and his wives; and no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
And after all this, YHWH struck him in his bowels with a disease for which there was no healing.

And it was, in the course of days, and at the time of the going out of the end, at two days' time, his bowels came out with his disease; and he died in harmful diseases. And his people made no burning for him like the burning for his fathers.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he went with no desire; and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the graves of the kings.

2 chronicles_22.t: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the marauding band that had come with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the elder ones. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to act wickedly.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, like the house of Ahab; for they were his counsellors after the death of his father, to his destruction.
He also walked in their counsel, and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead; and the Arameans wounded Joram.

And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds with which they had wounded him at Ramah when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. And Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.
And Ahaziah's downfall was from God, by his going to Joram. And when he came, he went out with Jehoram to Jehu son of Nimshi, whom YHWH had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it was, when Jehu was entering into judgement with the house of Ahab, that he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.

And he sought Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria; and they brought him to Jehu and put him to death, and they buried him — for they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought YHWH with all his heart." And the house of Ahaziah had no one to retain strength for the kingship.
And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead; and she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath the king's daughter took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in the bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest — for she was Ahaziah's sister — hid him from Athaliah, and she did not kill him.
And he was with them, hiding in the house of God, six years; and Athaliah was reigning over the land.

2 chronicles_23.t: And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the commanders of hundreds — Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri — into a covenant with him.
And they went around in Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the fathers of Israel; and they came to Jerusalem.
And all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said to them, "Look — the king's son shall reign, as YHWH has spoken concerning the sons of David.
"This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you who come in on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be gatekeepers of the thresholds;
"and a third at the king's house, and a third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people in the courts of the house of YHWH.
"And let no one come into the house of YHWH except the priests and those of the Levites who serve — they may come in, for they are holy; and all the people shall keep the duty of YHWH.

"And the Levites shall surround the king all around, each with his weapons in his hand; and whoever comes into the house shall be put to death. And be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."

And the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded; and each took his men, those coming in on the sabbath together with those going out on the sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
And Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the shields and the bucklers that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of God.
And he stationed all the people, each with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king.
And they brought out the king's son and put on him the crown and the testimony, and made him king; and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they said, "May the king live!"
And Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people at the house of YHWH.

And she looked, and there was the king standing at his pillar at the entrance, and the officials and the trumpets beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with instruments of song, leading the praise. And Athaliah tore her clothes and said, "Treason! Treason!"

And Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks; and whoever goes after her shall be put to death with the sword" — for the priest had said, "You shall not put her to death in the house of YHWH."
And they laid hands on her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's house; and they put her to death there.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be a people belonging to YHWH.
And all the people came to the house of Baal and pulled it down, and they broke its altars and its images; and Mattan the priest of Baal they killed before the altars.

And Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of YHWH into the hand of the priests, the Levites, whom David had apportioned over the house of YHWH, to offer up the burnt offerings of YHWH as is written in the law of Moses, with joy and with song, by the hands of David.
And he stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of YHWH, so that no one unclean in any matter should enter.

And he took the commanders of hundreds and the nobles and the rulers among the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of YHWH; and they came through the Upper Gate to the king's house, and seated the king on the throne of the kingdom.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword.

2 chronicles_24.t: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
And Joash did the right in the eyes of YHWH all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
And Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And it was after this that it was with the heart of Joash to renew the house of YHWH.

And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and collect silver from all Israel to repair the house of your God, year by year; and you, act quickly in the matter." But the Levites did not act quickly.

And the king summoned Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not required of the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the levy of Moses the servant of YHWH, and of the assembly of Israel, for the tent of the testimony?"
For Athaliah — the wicked woman — her sons had broken into the house of God, and had also used all the holy things of the house of YHWH for the Baals.
And the king spoke, and they made one chest and put it at the gate of the house of YHWH, outside.
And they made a proclamation in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring to YHWH the levy of Moses the servant of God, laid on Israel in the wilderness.
And all the officials and all the people rejoiced, and brought in and threw into the chest until it was finished.

And it was, at the time the chest was brought to the king's oversight by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that the silver was much, the king's scribe and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, and take it and return it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and gathered silver in abundance.

And the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of YHWH, and they were hiring stonecutters and craftsmen to renew the house of YHWH, and also craftsmen in iron and bronze, to repair the house of YHWH.
And those who did the work worked, and the repair went up for the work by their hand; and they set the house of God on its measurement and made it strong.

And when they had finished, they brought the remainder of the silver before the king and Jehoiada, and it was made into articles for the house of YHWH — articles of service, and for offering up, and pans, and articles of gold and silver. And they were offering up burnt offerings in the house of YHWH continually, all the days of Jehoiada.
And Jehoiada grew old and was satisfied with days, and died; he was a hundred and thirty years old at his death.
And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, for he had done good in Israel, and with God and his house.
And after the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king; then the king listened to them.
And they abandoned the house of YHWH the God of their fathers, and served the Asherim and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
And he sent prophets among them to bring them back to YHWH; and they warned them, but they did not give ear.

And the spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "Thus says God: 'Why are you transgressing the commandments of YHWH, so that you will not prosper? Because you have forsaken YHWH, he has forsaken you.'"
And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the command of the king, in the court of the house of YHWH.
And Joash the king did not remember the loyalty that Jehoiada his father had shown him, and he killed his son. And as he died he said, "May YHWH see and require it."

And it was, at the turn of the year, that the army of Aram came up against him; and they came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people from among the people, and sent all their booty to the king of Damascus.

For the army of Aram came with a small number of men, and YHWH gave into their hand an army in exceedingly great numbers, because they had forsaken YHWH the God of their fathers; and on Joash they executed judgements.

And when they had gone from him — for they left him in great sicknesses — his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and killed him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the graves of the kings.
And these are those who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.

And as for his sons, and the many oracles against him, and the founding of the house of God — there they are, written in the record of the scroll of the kings. And Amaziah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_25.t: Amaziah became king at twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
And he did the right in the eyes of YHWH, only not with a complete heart.
And it was, when the kingdom was secure upon him, that he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But their children he did not put to death, for it is as written in the law, in the scroll of Moses, where YHWH commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for children, and children shall not die for fathers, but each shall die for his own sin."

And Amaziah assembled Judah and appointed them by ancestral houses, by commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin; and he mustered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand chosen men, going out to the host, holding spear and large shield.
And he hired from Israel a hundred thousand mighty men of valour for a hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God came to him, saying, "O king, let the army of Israel not go with you, for YHWH is not with Israel — all the sons of Ephraim.
"But if you go, act, be strong for the battle — God will make you stumble before the enemy; for there is strength in God to help and to make stumble."
And Amaziah said to the man of God, "And what is to be done about the hundred talents that I gave to the troop of Israel?" And the man of God said, "YHWH has more than this to give you."

And Amaziah separated them — the troop that had come to him from Ephraim — to go to their place; and their anger burned exceedingly against Judah, and they returned to their place in the heat of anger.
And Amaziah strengthened himself and led out his people, and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir.
And ten thousand alive the sons of Judah took captive, and brought them to the top of the rock, and threw them down from the top of the rock; and all of them were split open.

And the sons of the troop that Amaziah had turned back from going with him to the battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria as far as Beth-horon; and they struck down three thousand of them and plundered much plunder.
And it was, after Amaziah came from defeating the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Amaziah, and he sent to him a prophet, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of the people who did not deliver their own people from your hand?"

And it was, as he was speaking to him, that he said to him, "Have we made you a counsellor to the king? Stop! Why should they strike you down?" And the prophet stopped, and said, "I know that God has counselled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
And Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."

And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
"You have said, 'Look, I have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up to glory. Now stay in your house. Why should you provoke harm and fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah did not listen, for it was from God, so as to give them into a hand, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
And Joash king of Israel went up, and they looked one another in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
And Judah was defeated before Israel, and they fled, each to his tents.

And Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh; and he brought him to Jerusalem, and made a breach in the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
And all the gold and the silver, and all the articles found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, and the sons of the pledges — and he returned to Samaria.
And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
And the rest of the matters of Amaziah, the former and the latter — are they not written on the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel?

And from the time that Amaziah turned aside from following YHWH, they conspired a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they carried him on the horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.

2 chronicles_26.t: And all the people of Judah took Uzziah, and he was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his fathers.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
And he did the right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
And he was one who sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the seeing of God; and in the days when he sought YHWH, God made him prosper.
And he went out and fought against the Philistines, and made a breach in the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
And God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
And the Ammonites gave tribute to Uzziah, and his name went as far as the entrance of Egypt, for he grew exceedingly strong.
And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the Buttress, and he made them strong.

And he built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had much livestock — and in the Shephelah and on the plain — farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in the fertile land, for he was one who loved the ground.

And Uzziah had an army making war, going out to the host by troops, in the number of their muster by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
The whole number of the heads of the fathers, of mighty men of valour, was two thousand six hundred.
And under their hand was an army of the host, three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, making war with powerful strength, to help the king against the enemy.
And Uzziah prepared for them, for all the host, shields and spears and helmets and body armour and bows and sling stones.

And he made in Jerusalem engines, the invention of an inventor, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot with arrows and with large stones. And his name went out far, for he was wonderfully helped until he was strong.
And when he was strong, his heart was haughty to his own destruction; and he acted unfaithfully against YHWH his God, and went into the temple of YHWH to burn incense on the altar of incense.
And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of YHWH, sons of valour.

And they took their stand against Uzziah the king and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to YHWH, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are set apart as holy to burn incense. Go out from the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; and it will not be for your honour from YHWH God."

And Uzziah was enraged, and in his hand was a censer to burn incense; and while he was enraged with the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of YHWH, beside the altar of incense.

And Azariah the chief priest turned to him, and all the priests, and there he was, with leprosy on his forehead; and they hurried him out from there, and he himself also rushed to go out, because YHWH had struck him.

And Uzziah the king had leprosy until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house, having leprosy, for he was cut off from the house of YHWH; and Jotham his son was over the king's house, judging the people of the land.
And the rest of the matters of Uzziah, the former and the latter, Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet wrote.

And Uzziah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He has leprosy." And Jotham his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_27.t: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
And he did the right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Uzziah his father had done — only he did not go into the temple of YHWH. And still the people were acting corruptly.
He built the Upper Gate of the house of YHWH, and on the wall of the Ophel he built much.
And he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded areas he built fortresses and towers.

And he fought with the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed over them; and the sons of Ammon gave him in that year a hundred talents of silver and ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. This the sons of Ammon brought him, and in the second year and the third.
And Jotham strengthened himself, for he had directed his ways before YHWH his God.
And the rest of the matters of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways — there they are, written on the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
And Jotham lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Ahaz his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_28.t: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do the right in the eyes of YHWH, as David his father had.
And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; and he also made molten images for the Baals.
And he burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and burned his sons in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom YHWH had dispossessed before the sons of Israel.
And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places and on the hills and under every luxuriant tree.

And YHWH his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram, and they struck him and took a great body of captives from him and brought them to Damascus. And he was also given into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him a great blow.
And Pekah son of Remaliah killed in Judah a hundred and twenty thousand in one day, all of them sons of valour, because they had forsaken YHWH the God of their fathers.
And Zichri, a warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, and Azrikam the officer of the house, and Elkanah the second to the king.
And the sons of Israel took captive from their brothers two hundred thousand — women, sons and daughters — and they also plundered much booty from them, and brought the booty to Samaria.

And there was a prophet of YHWH there, Oded was his name; and he went out before the army that was coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look — in the wrath of YHWH the God of your fathers against Judah he gave them into your hand, and you have killed among them in a rage that has reached to the heavens.
"And now you are saying you will subdue the sons of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female slaves for yourselves. Are there not, even with you yourselves, guilty acts against YHWH your God?
"And now hear me, and return the captives whom you have taken captive from your brothers, for the burning of YHWH's anger is upon you."
And men from the heads of the sons of Ephraim rose up — Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai — against those coming from the war,

and said to them, "You shall not bring the captives here; for you are saying it will bring guilt before YHWH upon us, to add to our sins and to our guilt. For our guilt is great, and burning anger is upon Israel."
And the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the commanders and all the assembly.

And the men who were designated by name rose and took hold of the captives, and all their naked ones they clothed from the plunder; and they clothed them and gave them sandals and fed them and gave them drink and anointed them, and led all who stumbled on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palms, beside their brothers; and they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
And again the Edomites had come and struck Judah and taken captives.

And the Philistines had raided the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah, and had captured Beth-shemesh and Aijalon and Gederoth, and Socoh with its villages and Timnah with its villages and Gimzo with its villages; and they settled there.
For YHWH had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let Judah go unrestrained and had acted very unfaithfully against YHWH.
And Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and harassed him, and did not strengthen him.
For Ahaz had stripped the house of YHWH and the house of the king and the officials, and had given to the king of Assyria; but it was of no help to him.
And at the time of his being harassed, he increased in acting unfaithfully against YHWH — this was King Ahaz.

And he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had struck him, and said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram are helping them, I will sacrifice to them so that they may help me." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.
And Ahaz gathered the articles of the house of God and cut up the articles of the house of God, and shut the doors of the house of YHWH; and he made himself altars at every corner in Jerusalem.
And in every single city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked YHWH the God of his fathers.
And the rest of his matters and all his ways, the former and the latter — there they are, written on the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Ahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem — for they did not bring him to the graves of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_29.t: Hezekiah became king at twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
And he did the right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that David his father had done.
He, in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of YHWH and repaired them.
And he brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them into the eastern square,
and said to them, "Hear me, Levites! Now set yourselves apart as holy, and set apart as holy the house of YHWH the God of your fathers, and bring out the impurity from the holy place.
"For our fathers acted unfaithfully and did the evil in the eyes of YHWH our God, and forsook him; and they turned their faces away from the tabernacle of YHWH and gave it their back.
"They also shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps, and did not burn incense, and did not offer up burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
"And the wrath of YHWH was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them a terror, a horror and a hissing, as you are seeing with your own eyes.
"And look — our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
"Now it is with my heart to make a covenant with YHWH the God of Israel, that the burning of his anger may turn back from us.
"My sons, do not now be negligent, for YHWH has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and to be for him servants and those who burn incense."

And the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; and of the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; and of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
and of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
and of the sons of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
And they gathered their brothers and set themselves apart as holy, and came, according to the command of the king by the words of YHWH, to cleanse the house of YHWH.

And the priests went inside the house of YHWH to cleanse it, and brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of YHWH into the court of the house of YHWH; and the Levites received it, to carry it out to the wadi Kidron, outside.

And they began on the first of the first month to set apart as holy, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of YHWH; and they set apart as holy the house of YHWH for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
And they went inside to Hezekiah the king and said, "We have cleansed all the house of YHWH — the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, and the table of the row and all its articles.
"And all the articles that King Ahaz rejected in his reign, in his unfaithfulness, we have prepared and set apart as holy; and there they are, before the altar of YHWH."
And Hezekiah the king rose early and gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of YHWH.

And they brought seven bulls and seven rams and seven lambs and seven male goats for a sin offering, for the kingdom and for the sanctuary and for Judah; and he told the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer them up on the altar of YHWH.

And they slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and dashed it against the altar; and they slaughtered the rams and dashed the blood against the altar; and they slaughtered the lambs and dashed the blood against the altar.
And they brought near the goats of the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

And the priests slaughtered them and made a sin offering with their blood against the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king had said that the burnt offering and the sin offering were for all Israel.

And he stationed the Levites in the house of YHWH with cymbals, with harps and with lyres, by the commandment of David and of Gad the king's seer and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was by the hand of YHWH, by the hand of his prophets.
And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with trumpets.

And Hezekiah said to offer up the burnt offering on the altar; and at the time the burnt offering began, the song of YHWH began, and the trumpets, and by the hands of the instruments of David king of Israel.
And all the assembly was prostrating itself, and the song was singing and the trumpets were blowing — all of it until the burnt offering was finished.
And when they had finished offering up, the king and all who were present with him bowed and prostrated themselves.
And Hezekiah the king and the officials told the Levites to praise YHWH with the words of David and of Asaph the seer; and they praised to the point of joy, and bowed low and prostrated themselves.

And Hezekiah answered and said, "Now you have filled your hand to YHWH. Draw near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of YHWH." And the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were willing of heart brought burnt offerings.
And the number of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy cattle, a hundred rams, two hundred lambs — all these for a burnt offering to YHWH.
And the holy offerings were six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep.

Only the priests were too few, and they were not able to skin all the burnt offerings; so their brothers the Levites strengthened them until the work was finished and until the priests had set themselves apart as holy — for the Levites were more upright of heart to set themselves apart as holy than the priests.
And there were also burnt offerings in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings and with the drink offerings for the burnt offering. And the service of the house of YHWH was arranged.
And Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people, over what God had prepared for the people; for the thing had come about suddenly.

2 chronicles_30.t: And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to the house of YHWH in Jerusalem to keep a passover to YHWH the God of Israel.
And the king and his officials and all the assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel to keep the passover in the second month.
For they had not been able to keep it at that time, because the priests had not set themselves apart as holy in sufficient number, and the people had not gathered to Jerusalem.
And the thing was right in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of all the assembly.

And they established a decree to send a proclamation through all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, to come to keep a passover to YHWH the God of Israel in Jerusalem; for they had not kept it in great numbers as it is written.

And the couriers went with the letters from the hand of the king and his officials through all Israel and Judah, and according to the king's command, saying: "Sons of Israel, return to YHWH the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, that he may return to the escaped remnant that remains to you from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
"And do not be like your fathers and like your brothers, who acted unfaithfully against YHWH the God of their fathers, so that he made them a horror, as you are seeing.

"Now do not harden your neck like your fathers. Give a hand to YHWH, and come to his sanctuary that he has set apart as holy for ever, and serve YHWH your God, that the burning of his anger may turn back from you.

"For when you return to YHWH, your brothers and your children will find compassion before their captors, and will return to this land; for YHWH your God is gracious and compassionate, and will not turn his face away from you if you return to him."
And the couriers were passing from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh and as far as Zebulun; but they were laughing at them and mocking them.
Nevertheless, men from Asher and Manasseh and from Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
Also in Judah the hand of God was there, to give them one heart to do the command of the king and the officials by the word of YHWH.
And a numerous people gathered at Jerusalem to keep the festival of unleavened bread in the second month — an exceedingly great assembly.
And they arose and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the incense altars they removed and threw into the wadi Kidron.

And they slaughtered the passover on the fourteenth of the second month; and the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and set themselves apart as holy, and brought burnt offerings to the house of YHWH.
And they stood at their post, according to their ordinance, according to the law of Moses the man of God; the priests were dashing the blood from the hand of the Levites.

For there were many in the assembly who had not set themselves apart as holy; so the Levites were over the slaughter of the passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to set them apart as holy to YHWH.

For the greater part of the people — many from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun — had not cleansed themselves, but ate the passover otherwise than as it is written. For Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May YHWH, who is good, make atonement for
"everyone who has set his heart to seek God, YHWH the God of his fathers, even though not according to the cleansing of the holy place."
And YHWH listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.

And the sons of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the festival of unleavened bread seven days with great joy; and the Levites and the priests were praising YHWH day by day, with instruments of strength to YHWH.

And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites who showed good understanding toward YHWH. And they ate the appointed feast seven days, sacrificing sacrifices of peace offerings and giving thanks to YHWH the God of their fathers.
And all the assembly took counsel to keep another seven days; and they kept seven days with joy.

For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed to the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials contributed to the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and priests set themselves apart as holy in great numbers.
And all the assembly of Judah rejoiced, and the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, and the sojourners who came from the land of Israel and those living in Judah.
And there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had been nothing like this in Jerusalem.
And the priests, the Levites, arose and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy dwelling, to the heavens.

2 chronicles_31.t: And when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and broke the pillars and cut down the Asherim and pulled down the high places and the altars, out of all Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had finished. And all the sons of Israel returned, each to his holding, to their cities.

And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to his service, for the priests and for the Levites, for burnt offering and for peace offerings, to serve and to give thanks and to praise in the gates of the camps of YHWH.

And the king's portion from his own property was for the burnt offerings — for the burnt offerings of the morning and the evening, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed times — as is written in the law of YHWH.
And he told the people, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they might be strong in the law of YHWH.
And as the word spread, the sons of Israel multiplied the first of grain, new wine and fresh oil and honey, and all the produce of the field; and the tithe of everything they brought in abundance.

And the sons of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah — they too brought a tithe of herd and flock, and a tithe of the holy things that were set apart as holy to YHWH their God; and they made heaps upon heaps.
In the third month they began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.
And Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, and blessed YHWH and his people Israel.
And Hezekiah enquired of the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.

And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, said to him: "From the time the contribution began to be brought to the house of YHWH, there has been eating and being satisfied and having plenty over; for YHWH has blessed his people, and what is left is this abundance."
And Hezekiah said to prepare chambers in the house of YHWH; and they prepared them.
And they brought in the contribution and the tithe and the holy things in faithfulness; and over them as officer was Conaniah the Levite, and Shimei his brother was second.

And Jehiel and Azaziah and Nahath and Asahel and Jerimoth and Jozabad and Eliel and Ismachiah and Mahath and Benaiah were officers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the officer of the house of God.
And Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper toward the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the contribution of YHWH and the most holy things.

And under his hand were Eden and Miniamin and Jeshua and Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in faithfulness, to distribute to their brothers by divisions, to the great as to the small,

besides their enrolment by genealogy of males from three years old and upward — to everyone who entered the house of YHWH for the matter of each day on its day, for their service in their duties by their divisions;
and the enrolment by genealogy of the priests by their fathers' houses, and of the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their duties by their divisions;
and to enrol by genealogy all their little ones, their wives and their sons and their daughters, for the whole assembly; for in their faithfulness they set themselves apart as holy.

And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the fields of the pasture land of their cities, in every single city, there were men designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled by genealogy among the Levites.
And Hezekiah did thus in all Judah; and he did the good and the right and the faithful before YHWH his God.
And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God — with all his heart he did it, and he prospered.

2 chronicles_32.t: After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah, and encamped against the fortified cities, and said he would break into them for himself.
And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, and that his face was set for war against Jerusalem.
And he took counsel with his officials and his mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that were outside the city; and they helped him.
And a numerous people gathered and stopped up all the springs and the wadi that flowed through the midst of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?"

And he strengthened himself and rebuilt all the wall that was broken down, and raised towers on it, and outside it another wall; and he strengthened the Millo of the city of David, and made weapons in abundance, and shields.
And he appointed commanders of war over the people, and gathered them to himself in the square at the city gate, and spoke to their heart, saying,
"Be strong and be courageous. Do not fear and do not be dismayed before the king of Assyria and before all the multitude that is with him; for with us is one greater than with him.
"With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is YHWH our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people supported themselves on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem — and he was at Lachish, and all his imperial might with him — to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying:
"Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: 'On what are you relying, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
"'Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by hunger and by thirst, saying, "YHWH our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria"?
"'Is it not this same Hezekiah who removed his high places and his altars, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, "Before one altar you shall bow down, and on it you shall burn incense"?
"'Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands at all able to deliver their land from my hand?
"'Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?

"'And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers — how much less will your gods deliver you from my hand!'"
And his servants spoke still more against YHWH the God, and against Hezekiah his servant.

And he wrote letters to taunt YHWH the God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, "Like the gods of the nations of the lands who did not deliver their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver his people from my hand."
And they called out with a loud voice in Judean to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to make them afraid and to terrify them, so that they might capture the city.
And they spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
And Hezekiah the king and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about this, and cried out to the heavens.

And YHWH sent a messenger, who annihilated every mighty man of valour and officer and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. And he returned with shame of face to his own land; and he entered the house of his god, and some of those who came out of his own body felled him there with the sword.
And YHWH saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of everyone; and he led them on every side.
And many were bringing an offering to YHWH at Jerusalem, and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah; and he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations from then on.
In those days Hezekiah was sick to the point of death, and he prayed to YHWH; and he spoke to him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was haughty; and wrath came upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
And Hezekiah humbled himself for the haughtiness of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the wrath of YHWH did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.

And Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and honour; and he made himself treasuries for silver and for gold and for precious stone and for spices and for shields and for all kinds of desirable articles,
and storehouses for the yield of grain and new wine and fresh oil, and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and flocks for the stalls.
And he made himself cities, and livestock of flock and herd in abundance; for God had given him very much property.
And it was Hezekiah who stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them down to the west of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his work.
And so also with the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who were sent to him to enquire about the sign that had happened in the land — God left him, to test him, to know all that was in his heart.
And the rest of the matters of Hezekiah, and his acts of loyalty — there they are, written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet, on the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.

And Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him on the ascent to the graves of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honour at his death. And Manasseh his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_33.t: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to the abominations of the nations that YHWH had dispossessed before the sons of Israel.

And he turned back and rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had pulled down; and he set up altars to the Baals and made Asherahs, and bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
And he built altars in the house of YHWH, of which YHWH had said, "In Jerusalem my name shall be for ever."
And he built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of YHWH.

And he made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and practised soothsaying and divination and sorcery, and dealt with a medium and a spiritist. He did much evil in the eyes of YHWH, to provoke him.

And he set the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever.

"And I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the ground that I appointed for your fathers — only if they take care to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the law and the statutes and the judgements by the hand of Moses."
And Manasseh misled Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to do more evil than the nations that YHWH had annihilated before the sons of Israel.
And YHWH spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not pay attention.
And YHWH brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh with hooks and bound him with bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.
And when he was harassed, he entreated the face of YHWH his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
And he prayed to him, and he was entreated by him and heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that YHWH — he is God.

And after this he built an outer wall for the city of David, west of Gihon in the wadi, and to the entrance at the Fish Gate; and he carried it round the Ophel and raised it very high. And he put commanders of the army in all the fortified cities in Judah.
And he removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of YHWH, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of YHWH and in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the city.
And he rebuilt the altar of YHWH and sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and thanksgiving; and he told Judah to serve YHWH the God of Israel.
But the people were still sacrificing at the high places — only to YHWH their God.
