And the rest of the matters of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of YHWH the God of Israel — there they are, in the matters of the kings of Israel.

And his prayer, and how he was entreated, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places in which he built high places and set up the Asherim and the carved images before he humbled himself — there they are, written in the words of Hozai.
And Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house; and Amon his son became king in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, as Manasseh his father had done; and to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made Amon sacrificed, and he served them.
And he did not humble himself before YHWH as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; for he, Amon, increased guilt.
And his servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house.
And the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

2 chronicles_34.t: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
And he did the right in the eyes of YHWH, and walked in the ways of David his father, and did not turn aside right or left.

And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his father; and in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places and the Asherim and the carved images and the cast images.

And they pulled down before him the altars of the Baals, and the incense stands that were above them he cut down; and the Asherim and the carved images and the cast images he broke in pieces and ground to dust, and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
And the bones of priests he burned on their altars, and he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the cities of Manasseh and Ephraim and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around —
— and he pulled down the altars, and the Asherim and the carved images he crushed to dust, and all the incense stands he cut down in all the land of Israel; and he returned to Jerusalem.

And in the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah and Maaseiah the official of the city and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of YHWH his God.

And they went to Hilkiah the great priest and gave him the money that had been brought to the house of God, which the Levites who kept the threshold had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned to Jerusalem.

And they put it into the hand of those doing the work, who were appointed over the house of YHWH; and those doing the work, who were working in the house of YHWH, gave it out to mend and repair the house.
And they gave it to the craftsmen and to the builders, to buy hewn stone and timber for the couplings, and to make beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.

And the men did the work in faithfulness; and over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee; and the Levites — every one skilled with instruments of song.
And they were over the burden-bearers and directed all who did work, service by service; and some of the Levites were scribes and officials and gatekeepers.
And when they brought out the money that had been brought to the house of YHWH, Hilkiah the priest found the scroll of the law of YHWH by the hand of Moses.
And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the scroll of the law in the house of YHWH." And Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan.
And Shaphan brought the scroll to the king, and brought back word to the king further, saying, "All that was given into the hand of your servants — they are doing it.
"And they have poured out the money that was found in the house of YHWH and put it into the hand of those appointed, and into the hand of those doing the work."
And Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a scroll." And Shaphan read aloud from it before the king.
And when the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Abdon son of Micah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,

"Go, seek YHWH on my behalf and on behalf of what remains in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the scroll that has been found; for great is the wrath of YHWH that has been poured out on us, because our fathers did not keep the word of YHWH, to do according to all that is written in this scroll."

And Hilkiah, and those whom the king had appointed, went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments; and she was living in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter. And they spoke to her to that effect.
And she said to them, "Thus says YHWH the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
"Thus says YHWH: Here I am, bringing harm on this place and on its inhabitants — all the curses that are written in the scroll that they have read before the king of Judah.
"Because they have forsaken me and made offerings smoke to other gods, so as to provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands, my wrath will pour out on this place and will not be quenched."
"And to the king of Judah, who sent you to seek YHWH — thus you shall say to him: Thus says YHWH the God of Israel concerning the words that you have heard:

"Because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and against its inhabitants — and you humbled yourself before me and tore your clothes and wept before me — I also have heard, declaration of YHWH.

"Here I am, gathering you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your graves in peace; and your eyes shall not look on all the distress that I am bringing on this place and on its inhabitants." And they brought word back to the king.
And the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up to the house of YHWH, and every man of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests and the Levites, and all the people from great to small; and he read in their ears all the words of the scroll of the covenant that had been found in the house of YHWH.

And the king stood at his place and cut the covenant before YHWH — to walk after YHWH and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to do the words of the covenant written in this scroll.
And he made everyone who was found in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand to it; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.

And Josiah removed all the abominations from all the lands that belonged to the sons of Israel, and made everyone who was found in Israel serve — to serve YHWH their God. All his days they did not turn aside from after YHWH, the God of their fathers.

2 chronicles_35.t: And Josiah kept a Passover to YHWH in Jerusalem; and they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month.
And he appointed the priests to their duties and strengthened them for the service of the house of YHWH.

And he said to the Levites who instructed all Israel, who were holy to YHWH, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. There is no burden for you on the shoulder. Now serve YHWH your God and his people Israel,
"and prepare yourselves by your ancestral houses, according to your divisions, by the writing of David king of Israel and by the document of Solomon his son.
"And stand in the holy place by the groupings of the ancestral houses of your kinsmen, the sons of the people, and a division of an ancestral house for the Levites.
"And slaughter the Passover, and consecrate yourselves, and prepare for your kinsmen, to do according to the word of YHWH by the hand of Moses."

And Josiah contributed for the sons of the people flocks — lambs and young goats, all of them for the Passover offerings, for everyone present — to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand cattle. These were from the property of the king.

And his officials contributed as a freewill offering for the people, for the priests and for the Levites. Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, the officers of the house of God, gave the priests for the Passover offerings two thousand six hundred, and three hundred cattle.

And Conaniah and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, contributed for the Levites for the Passover offerings five thousand, and five hundred cattle.
And the service was arranged; and the priests took their stand at their place, and the Levites by their divisions, according to the command of the king.
And they slaughtered the Passover, and the priests sprinkled from their hand, and the Levites were skinning.

And they set aside the burnt offering, to give it to the groupings of the ancestral houses of the sons of the people, to bring near to YHWH as it is written in the scroll of Moses; and so for the cattle.
And they cooked the Passover in the fire, according to the rule; and the holy offerings they boiled in pots and in cauldrons and in pans, and brought them quickly to all the sons of the people.

And afterwards they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests the sons of Aaron were offering up the burnt offering and the fat pieces until night; so the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their post, according to the command of David and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun the seer of the king; and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to turn aside from their service, for their kinsmen the Levites prepared for them.
And all the service of YHWH was arranged on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer up burnt offerings on the altar of YHWH, according to the command of King Josiah.
And the sons of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days.

And no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; and none of the kings of Israel kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites and all Judah and Israel who were present and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover was kept.
After all this, when Josiah had put the house in order, Necho king of Egypt came up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates; and Josiah went out to meet him.

But he sent messengers to him, saying, "What is between me and you, king of Judah? Not against you are you today, but against the house of my war; and God has said to hurry me. Cease, for your own sake, from the God who is with me, that he not destroy you."
But Josiah did not turn his face from him, but disguised himself to fight with him; and he did not listen to the words of Necho, from the mouth of God, and he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
And the archers shot King Josiah; and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."

And his servants took him away from the chariot and made him ride in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he died, and was buried in the graves of his fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem were mourning over Josiah.

And Jeremiah lamented over Josiah; and all the male singers and female singers have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day. And they made them a fixed practice in Israel, and there they are, written in the Laments.
And the rest of the matters of Josiah, and his acts of loyalty, according to what is written in the law of YHWH,
and his matters, the former and the latter — there they are, written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.

2 chronicles_36.t: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
And the king of Egypt removed him in Jerusalem, and fined the land a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
And the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; and Necho took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH his God.
Against him Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and bound him with bronze fetters to take him to Babylon.
And some of the articles of the house of YHWH Nebuchadnezzar brought to Babylon, and put them in his palace in Babylon.

And the rest of the matters of Jehoiakim, and his abominations that he did, and what was found against him — there they are, written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH.
And at the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the precious articles of the house of YHWH; and he made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, from the mouth of YHWH.
And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning back to YHWH the God of Israel.

Also all the leaders of the priests and the people multiplied unfaithfulness, according to all the abominations of the nations; and they made unclean the house of YHWH that he had consecrated in Jerusalem.
And YHWH the God of their fathers sent to them by the hand of his messengers, rising early and sending — for he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
But they were deriding the messengers of God and despising his words and mocking his prophets, until the wrath of YHWH rose against his people, until there was no healing.

And he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, the old or the decrepit — he gave them all into his hand.
And all the articles of the house of God, the great and the small, and the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the king and his officials — everything he brought to Babylon.
And they burned the house of God and pulled down the wall of Jerusalem, and all its citadels they burned with fire, and all its precious articles were destroyed.
And he took into exile to Babylon those who remained from the sword, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfil the word of YHWH by the mouth of Jeremiah — until the land had accepted its sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, to fulfil seventy years.

And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, for the completing of the word of YHWH by the mouth of Jeremiah, YHWH stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation through all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:

"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: 'All the kingdoms of the earth YHWH the God of the heavens has given me, and he himself has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who among you is from all his people? YHWH his God be with him, and let him go up.'"

2 kings_1.t: And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

And Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room that was in Samaria, and he became ill. And he sent messengers and said to them, "Go, consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this sickness."

And the messenger of YHWH spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak to them: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?'
"And therefore, thus says YHWH: 'The bed on which you have gone up — you shall not come down from it, for dying you shall die.'" And Elijah went.
And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is this that you have returned?"

And they said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him: Thus says YHWH: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? Therefore the bed on which you have gone up — you shall not come down from it, for dying you shall die.'"
And he spoke to them, "What was the manner of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
And they said to him, "A man, an owner of hair, with a belt of hide girded on his loins." And he said, "That is Elijah the Tishbite."
And he sent to him a commander of fifty with his fifty; and he went up to him, and there — he was sitting on the top of the hill. And he spoke to him, "Man of God, the king has spoken: Come down!"

And Elijah answered and spoke to the commander of fifty, "And if I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.
And he returned and sent to him another commander of fifty with his fifty; and he answered and spoke to him, "Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly!"

And Elijah answered and spoke to them, "If I am the man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And the fire of God came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.

And he returned and sent a third commander of fifty with his fifty. And the third commander of fifty went up and came and bowed down on his knees before Elijah and sought his favour, and spoke to him: "Man of God, let my life and the life of these your servants, these fifty, be precious in your eyes.
"Behold, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the two former commanders of fifty and their fifties. And now let my life be precious in your eyes."
And the messenger of YHWH spoke to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." And he rose and went down with him to the king.

And he spoke to him, "Thus says YHWH: Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron — is it because there is no God in Israel to consult his word? — therefore the bed on which you have gone up, you shall not come down from it, for dying you shall die."
And he died, according to the word of YHWH that Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, for he had no son.
And the rest of the matters of Ahaziah that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

2 kings_2.t: And it was, when YHWH was about to take Elijah up to the heavens in the whirlwind, that Elijah went, and Elisha, from Gilgal.
And Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me as far as Beth-el." And Elisha said, "As YHWH lives and as your self lives, I will not leave you." And they went down to Beth-el.
And the sons of the prophets who were at Beth-el came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know. Be silent."
And Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Jericho." And he said, "As YHWH lives and as your self lives, I will not leave you." And they came to Jericho.
And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know. Be silent."
And Elijah said to him, "Stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to the Jordan." And he said, "As YHWH lives and as your self lives, I will not leave you." And the two of them went.
And fifty men from the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite, at a distance; and the two of them stood at the Jordan.
And Elijah took his cloak and rolled it up and struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that; and the two of them passed over on dry ground.
And it was, when they had passed over, that Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." And Elisha said, "Let a mouth of two be in your spirit toward me."
And he said, "You have made hard the asking. If you see me taken from you, it shall be so for you; and if not, it shall not be."
And it was, as they were going, going and speaking, that there — a chariot of fire and horses of fire! And they separated between the two of them; and Elijah went up in the whirlwind to the heavens.
And Elisha was seeing, and he was crying out, "My father, my father! The chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!" And he saw him no more. And he took hold of his clothes and tore them into two pieces.
And he took up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him, and he went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

And he took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters, and he said, "Where is YHWH, the God of Elijah — even he?" And he struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that; and Elisha passed over.
And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him opposite and said, "The spirit of Elijah has rested on Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.

And they said to him, "Behold now, there are with your servants fifty men, sons of ability. Let them go, please, and search for your master, lest the spirit of YHWH has carried him off and cast him on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys." And he said, "You shall not send."
And they urged him until he was ashamed, and he said, "Send." And they sent fifty men, and they searched three days and did not find him.
And they returned to him — and he was staying at Jericho — and he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"
And the men of the city said to Elisha, "Behold now, the site of the city is good, as my lord sees; but the waters are bad, and the land is bereaving."
And he said, "Fetch me a new jar, and put salt in it." And they brought it to him.
And he went out to the outlet of the waters and threw salt there, and he said, "Thus says YHWH: I have healed these waters. There shall not be from there any more death or bereaving."
And the waters have been healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
And he went up from there to Beth-el; and he was going up on the way, and small boys came out from the city and jeered at him, and they said to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"
And he turned behind him and saw them, and he cursed them in the name of YHWH. And two she-bears came out from the forest and tore in pieces forty-two of the boys.
And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

2 kings_3.t: And Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; and he reigned twelve years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH — only not like his father and like his mother; and he removed the pillar of the Baal that his father had made.
Only to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, he clung; he did not turn aside from it.
And Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-breeder, and he used to render to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams, with the wool.
And it was, when Ahab died, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
And King Jehoram went out on that day from Samaria and mustered all Israel.

And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?" And he said, "I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
And he said, "By which way shall we go up?" And he said, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."
And the king of Israel went, and the king of Judah and the king of Edom; and they went around a way of seven days, and there was no water for the camp or for the animals that were at their feet.
And the king of Israel said, "Alas! For YHWH has summoned these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."

And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not here a prophet of YHWH, that we may consult YHWH by him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Here is Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah."
And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of YHWH is with him." And the king of Israel went down to him, and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom.

And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What is between me and you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." And the king of Israel said to him, "No — for YHWH has summoned these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."
And Elisha said, "As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand — were it not that I am lifting up the face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you."
"And now, fetch me a musician." And it was, when the musician played, that the hand of YHWH came upon him.
And he said, "Thus says YHWH: Make this wadi ditches, ditches."
"For thus says YHWH: You shall not see wind and you shall not see rain, yet that wadi will be filled with water; and you shall drink, you and your livestock and your animals."
"And this is a trifling thing in the eyes of YHWH; and he will give Moab into your hand."

"And you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and you shall fell every good tree, and you shall stop up all the springs of water, and every good portion of land you shall spoil with stones."
And it was in the morning, at the going up of the grain offering, that there — water was coming from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with the water.
And all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, and they were called out, from everyone who girds on a belt and upward, and they took their stand at the border.
And they rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water; and Moab saw the water opposite, red like blood.
And they said, "This is blood! The kings have utterly fought one another and struck each his neighbour. And now, to the plunder, Moab!"
And they came to the camp of Israel, and Israel rose and struck Moab, and they fled from before them. And they went on into it, striking Moab.

And the cities they tore down; and every good portion of land they threw, each his stone, and filled it; and every spring of water they stopped up, and every good tree they felled — until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth. And the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
And the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, and he took with him seven hundred men drawing the sword, to break through to the king of Edom; but they were not able.

And he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel; and they departed from him and returned to the land.

2 kings_4.t: And a certain woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you yourself know that your servant was one who feared YHWH; and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
And Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a jar of oil."
And he said, "Go, ask for yourself vessels from outside, from all your neighbours — empty vessels; do not make them few.
"And you shall go in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and you shall pour into all these vessels; and the full one you shall set aside."
And she went from him and shut the door behind her and behind her sons; they were bringing to her, and she was pouring.
And it was, when the vessels were full, that she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is no other vessel." And the oil stopped.
And she came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt; and you and your sons shall live on what is left."
And it was the day that Elisha passed on to Shunem, and a great woman was there; and she urged him to eat bread. And it was, as often as he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat bread.
And she said to her husband, "Behold now, I know that he is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.
"Let us make, please, a small walled upper room, and let us put there for him a bed and a table and a chair and a lampstand; and it shall be, when he comes to us, he will turn aside there."
And it was the day that he came there, and he turned aside to the upper room and lay down there.
And he said to Gehazi his young man, "Summon this Shunammite." And he summoned her, and she stood before him.

And he said to him, "Say to her, please: Behold, you have shown us all this care. What is to be done for you? Is there a word to be spoken for you to the king or to the commander of the army?" And she said, "I am dwelling among my own people."
And he said, "And what is to be done for her?" And Gehazi said, "Indeed, she has no son, and her husband is old."
And he said, "Summon her." And he summoned her, and she stood at the entrance.
And he said, "At this appointed time, about the time of life, you will be embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, man of God — do not tell a lie to your maidservant."
And the woman conceived and bore a son at this appointed time, about the time of life, of which Elisha had spoken to her.
And the child grew, and it was the day that he went out to his father, to the harvesters.
And he said to his father, "My head! My head!" And he said to the young man, "Carry him to his mother."
And he carried him and brought him to his mother; and he sat on her knees until noon, and he died.
And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and she shut the door behind him and went out.
And she called to her husband and said, "Send me, please, one of the young men and one of the donkeys, and let me run to the man of God and return."
And he said, "Why are you going to him today? It is not new moon or sabbath." And she said, "Peace."
And she saddled the donkey and said to her young man, "Lead on and go. Do not hold back for me in riding unless I tell you."
And she went and came to the man of God, to Mount Carmel. And it was, when the man of God saw her opposite, that he said to Gehazi his young man, "Behold, that Shunammite!
"Now run, please, to meet her and say to her: Is it peace for you? Is it peace for your husband? Is it peace for the child?" And she said, "Peace."

And she came to the man of God, to the mountain, and took hold of his feet. And Gehazi drew near to push her away, and the man of God said, "Let her alone, for her self is bitter within her; and YHWH has hidden it from me and has not told me."
And she said, "Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"

And he said to Gehazi, "Gird your loins and take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not bless him; and if anyone blesses you, do not answer him. And you shall put my staff on the face of the boy."
And the mother of the boy said, "As YHWH lives and as your self lives, I will not leave you." And he rose and went after her.
And Gehazi passed on before them and put the staff on the face of the boy, and there was no voice and no attention. And he went back to meet him and told him, saying, "The boy has not awakened."
And Elisha came to the house, and there — the boy was dead, laid on his bed.
And he went in and shut the door behind the two of them, and he prayed to YHWH.
And he went up and lay on the child and put his mouth on his mouth and his eyes on his eyes and his palms on his palms; and he crouched over him, and the flesh of the child grew warm.
And he went back and walked in the house, once this way and once that; and he went up and crouched over him. And the boy sneezed as many as seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
And he called to Gehazi and said, "Summon this Shunammite." And he summoned her, and she came to him. And he said, "Take up your son."
And she came and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground; and she took up her son and went out.

And Elisha returned to Gilgal, and the famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And he said to his young man, "Put on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."

And one went out to the field to gather herbs, and he found a vine of the field and gathered from it wild gourds, the fullness of his garment; and he came and sliced them into the pot of stew, for they did not know.
And they poured out for the men to eat; and it was, when they ate of the stew, that they cried out and said, "Death is in the pot, man of God!" And they were not able to eat.
And he said, "Then fetch flour." And he threw it into the pot and said, "Pour out for the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing bad in the pot.
And a man came from Baal-shalisha and brought to the man of God bread of firstfruits — twenty loaves of barley — and fresh grain in his sack. And he said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat."
And his attendant said, "What? Shall I set this before a hundred men?" And he said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat, for thus says YHWH: They shall eat and have some left over."
And he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of YHWH.

2 kings_5.t: And Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his master and lifted up of face, for by him YHWH had given victory to Aram; and the man was a mighty man of valour — afflicted with leprosy.
And Aram had gone out in marauding bands, and they had taken captive from the land of Israel a young girl; and she was before the wife of Naaman.
And she said to her mistress, "Would that my lord were before the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would deliver him from his leprosy."
And he went and told his master, saying, "Thus and thus the girl who is from the land of Israel spoke."
And the king of Aram said, "Go, come, and let me send a letter to the king of Israel." And he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver and six thousand of gold and ten changes of clothes.
And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, "And now, when this letter comes to you — behold, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, and you shall deliver him from his leprosy."

And it was, when the king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man is sending to me to deliver a man from his leprosy? Only consider, please, and see, that he is seeking an occasion against me."

And it was, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, please, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel."
And Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and he stood at the entrance of the house of Elisha.
And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall return to you, and be clean."

And Naaman was angry and went, and he said, "Behold, I said to myself, 'Coming out he will come out to me and stand and call on the name of YHWH his God, and wave his hand toward the place, and deliver the one afflicted with leprosy.'
"Are not Amanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" And he turned and went in a rage.
And his servants drew near and spoke to him and said, "My father, had the prophet spoken to you a great thing, would you not do it? How much more when he has said to you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
And he went down and dipped in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh returned like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.

And he went back to the man of God, he and all his camp, and he came and stood before him and said, "Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now, accept, please, a blessing from your servant."
And he said, "As YHWH lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept." And he urged him to accept, but he refused.

And Naaman said, "If not — let there be given, please, to your servant the load of a pair of mules of earth; for your servant will no longer offer a burnt offering or a sacrifice to other gods, but to YHWH.

"For this matter may YHWH forgive your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he is leaning on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon — when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may YHWH forgive your servant in this matter."
And he said to him, "Go in peace." And he went from him a stretch of land.

And Gehazi, the young man of Elisha the man of God, said, "Behold, my master has restrained this Naaman the Aramean from accepting from his hand what he brought. As YHWH lives, I will run after him and accept something from him."
And Gehazi pursued after Naaman; and Naaman saw one running after him, and he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is it peace?"

And he said, "It is peace. My master has sent me, saying, 'Behold, just now two young men have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets. Give them, please, a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'"

And Naaman said, "Be willing — accept two talents." And he urged him, and he bound up two talents of silver in two bags, and two changes of clothes, and he gave them to two of his young men, and they carried them before him.
And he came to the Ophel and took them from their hand and deposited them in the house; and he sent the men away, and they went.
And he came and stood before his master; and Elisha said to him, "From where, Gehazi?" And he said, "Your servant has not gone anywhere at all."

And he said to him, "Did not my heart go with you when a man turned from upon his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to accept silver and to accept clothes and olive groves and vineyards and sheep and cattle and male servants and maidservants?
"And the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your offspring for ever." And he went out from before him, afflicted with leprosy, like snow.

2 kings_6.t: And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Behold now, the place where we are dwelling before you is too cramped for us.
"Let us go, please, as far as the Jordan, and let us take from there each one beam, and let us make ourselves a place there to dwell in." And he said, "Go."
And one said, "Be willing, please, and go with your servants." And he said, "I will go."
And he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and cut down the trees.
And it was, as one was felling the beam, that the iron fell into the water; and he cried out and said, "Alas, my lord! And it was borrowed."
And the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place; and he cut off a piece of wood and threw it there, and he made the iron float.
And he said, "Lift it up for yourself." And he stretched out his hand and took it.
And the king of Aram was fighting against Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "At such and such a place shall be my encampment."
And the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Take care not to pass by this place, for there Aram is coming down."
And the king of Israel sent to the place of which the man of God had spoken to him and warned him; and he took care there, not once and not twice.
And the heart of the king of Aram was enraged over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me who among us is for the king of Israel?"
And one of his servants said, "No, my lord the king; for Elisha the prophet who is in Israel tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedchamber."
And he said, "Go and see where he is, that I may send and take him." And it was told to him, saying, "Behold, he is in Dothan."
And he sent there horses and chariotry and a massive force; and they came by night and surrounded the city.

And the attendant of the man of God rose early to get up and went out; and there — a force surrounding the city, and horses and chariotry! And his young man said to him, "Alas, my lord! What shall we do?"
And he said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

And Elisha prayed and said, "YHWH, open his eyes, please, that he may see." And YHWH opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw; and there — the hill was full of horses and chariotry of fire around Elisha!
And they came down to him, and Elisha prayed to YHWH and said, "Strike this nation, please, with dazzlement." And he struck them with dazzlement, according to the word of Elisha.
And Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city. Come after me, and let me lead you to the man whom you seek." And he led them to Samaria.

And it was, when they came to Samaria, that Elisha said, "YHWH, open the eyes of these men, that they may see." And YHWH opened their eyes, and they saw; and there — they were in the midst of Samaria!
And the king of Israel said to Elisha, when he saw them, "Shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down, my father?"

And he said, "You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their master."
And he prepared for them a great feast, and they ate and drank; and he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the marauding bands of Aram did not come again into the land of Israel.
And it was after this that Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his camp and went up and laid siege to Samaria.
And there was a great famine in Samaria; and behold, they were besieging it, until a donkey's head was worth eighty of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung five of silver.
And it was, as the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, that a woman cried out to him, saying, "Deliver, my lord the king!"
And he said, "If YHWH does not deliver you, from where shall I deliver you? From the threshing floor or from the wine-press?"
And the king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" And she said, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, and let us eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.'
"And we boiled my son and ate him. And I said to her on the next day, 'Give your son, and let us eat him' — and she had hidden her son."
And it was, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he tore his clothes — and he was passing by on the wall — and the people saw, and behold, sackcloth was on his flesh underneath.
And he said, "Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today!"

And Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And he sent a man from before him; before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, "Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent to remove my head? Look — when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him back with the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
He was still speaking with them, and behold, the messenger was coming down to him. And he said, "Behold, this calamity is from YHWH. Why should I wait for YHWH any longer?"

2 kings_7.t: And Elisha said, "Hear the word of YHWH. Thus says YHWH: About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria."

And the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God and said, "Behold, if YHWH were making windows in the heavens, could this thing be?" And he said, "Behold, you are about to see it with your own eyes, and from there you shall not eat."
And there were four men, afflicted with leprosy, at the entrance of the gate; and they said each to his neighbour, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

"If we say, 'We will enter the city,' the famine is in the city and we will die there; and if we sit here, we will die. And now, come, let us fall to the camp of Aram. If they let us live, we shall live; and if they put us to death, we shall die."
And they rose at twilight to go to the camp of Aram; and they came to the edge of the camp of Aram, and there — no one was there!

And the Lord had made the camp of Aram hear a sound of chariotry, a sound of horses, a sound of a great army; and they said each to his brother, "Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us!"
And they rose and fled at twilight and abandoned their tents and their horses and their donkeys — the camp as it was — and they fled for their lives.

And these men afflicted with leprosy came to the edge of the camp, and they went into one tent and ate and drank and carried off from there silver and gold and clothes, and they went and hid them. And they returned and went into another tent and carried off from there, and they went and hid them.

And they said each to his neighbour, "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the light of morning, punishment will find us. And now, come, let us go and tell the household of the king."

And they came and called to the gatekeeper of the city and told them, saying, "We went into the camp of Aram, and there — no one was there, and no sound of anyone! Only the horses tied up and the donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."
And he called the gatekeepers, and they told the household of the king within.

And the king rose by night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what Aram has done to us. They know that we are hungry, and they have gone out from the camp to hide themselves in the open country, saying, 'When they come out from the city we will seize them alive, and we will enter the city.'"

And one of his servants answered and said, "Let them take, please, five of the remaining horses that are left in it — behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that are left in it; behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that have perished — and let us send and see."
And they took two chariots of horses, and the king sent them after the camp of Aram, saying, "Go and see."
And they went after them as far as the Jordan; and behold, all the road was full of clothes and equipment that Aram had thrown away in their hurrying. And the messengers returned and told the king.
And the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram; and a seah of fine flour was for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of YHWH.

And the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned over the gate; and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken, who spoke when the king came down to him.
And it was as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, "Two seahs of barley for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, shall be about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria" —

and the officer answered the man of God and said, "And behold, if YHWH were making windows in the heavens, could it be according to this word?" And he said, "Behold, you are about to see it with your own eyes, and from there you shall not eat."
And so it happened to him: the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

2 kings_8.t: And Elisha had spoken to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, "Arise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you may sojourn; for YHWH has called for a famine, and it is also coming upon the land for seven years."
And the woman rose and did according to the word of the man of God; and she went, she and her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.
And it was at the end of seven years that the woman returned from the land of the Philistines; and she went out to cry out to the king for her house and for her field.
And the king was speaking to Gehazi, the young man of the man of God, saying, "Recount to me, please, all the great things that Elisha has done."

And it was, as he was recounting to the king how he had restored the dead to life, that behold — the woman whose son he had restored to life was crying out to the king for her house and for her field! And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life."

And the king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. And the king assigned her a court official, saying, "Restore all that is hers, and all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now."
And Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick; and it was told to him, saying, "The man of God has come as far as here."
And the king said to Hazael, "Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God, and consult YHWH by him, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"

And Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand, and every good thing of Damascus, the load of forty camels. And he came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"
And Elisha said to him, "Go, say to him, 'Living you shall live.' But YHWH has shown me that dying he shall die."
And he set his face and fixed it until he was ashamed; and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, "Why is my lord weeping?" And he said, "Because I know the harm you will do to the sons of Israel: their fortresses you will send into fire, and their young men you will kill with the sword, and their children you will dash in pieces, and their pregnant women you will rip open."
And Hazael said, "But what is your servant, the dog, that he should do this great thing?" And Elisha said, "YHWH has shown me you as king over Aram."
And he went from Elisha and came to his master, and he said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he said, "He said to me, 'Living you shall live.'"
And it was on the next day that he took the coverlet and dipped it in water and spread it over his face, and he died; and Hazael reigned in his place.
And in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel — and Jehoshaphat was king of Judah — Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.
A son of thirty-two years was he when he became king, and eight years he reigned in Jerusalem.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH.
But YHWH was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, as he had said to him — to give him a lamp for his sons all the days.
In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king king over themselves.

And Joram passed over to Zair, and all the chariotry was with him; and he rose by night and struck Edom, which was surrounding him, and the commanders of the chariotry — and the people fled to their tents.
And Edom has rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time.
And the rest of the matters of Joram, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Joram lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
A son of twenty-two years was Ahaziah when he became king, and one year he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
And he went with Joram son of Ahab to battle with Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead; and the Arameans wounded Joram.

And Joram the king returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds with which the Arameans had wounded him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, for he was sick.

2 kings_9.t: And Elisha the prophet summoned one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird your loins and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
"And you shall come there and look there for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi; and you shall go in and raise him up from among his brothers and bring him into an inner room.
"And you shall take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, 'Thus says YHWH: I have anointed you as king over Israel.' And you shall open the door and flee, and you shall not wait."
And the young man went — the young man, the prophet — to Ramoth-gilead.
And he came, and behold, the commanders of the army were sitting; and he said, "I have a word for you, commander." And Jehu said, "For which of us all?" And he said, "For you, commander."
And he rose and went into the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, "Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: I have anointed you as king over the people of YHWH, over Israel.
"And you shall strike down the house of Ahab your master; and I will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of YHWH, from the hand of Jezebel.
"And the whole house of Ahab shall perish; and I will cut off from Ahab every one who urinates against a wall, and the shut up and the freed in Israel.
"And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah."
"And Jezebel the dogs shall devour in the territory of Jezreel, and there shall be no one to bury her." And he opened the door and fled.
And Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and one said to him, "Is it peace? Why did this madman come to you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and his talk."
And they said, "Falsehood! Tell us, please." And he said, "Thus and thus he said to me, saying, 'Thus says YHWH: I have anointed you as king over Israel.'"
And they hurried and took each his garment and put them under him on the bare steps; and they blew the ram's horn and said, "Jehu is king!"
And Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been keeping watch at Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Aram;

but Jehoram the king had returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds with which the Arameans had wounded him when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. And Jehu said, "If this is your mind, let no fugitive go out from the city to go and tell it in Jezreel."
And Jehu rode and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.

And the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the throng of Jehu as he came, and he said, "I see a throng." And Jehoram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"

And the rider of the horse went to meet him and said, "Thus says the king: Is it peace?" And Jehu said, "What is it to you and to peace? Turn round behind me." And the watchman reported, saying, "The messenger came as far as them and has not turned back."
And he sent a second rider of a horse, and he came to them and said, "Thus says the king: Peace?" And Jehu said, "What is it to you and to peace? Turn round behind me."
And the watchman reported, saying, "He came as far as them and has not turned back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives with madness."

And Jehoram said, "Harness!" And they harnessed his chariot. And Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot; and they went out to meet Jehu and found him in the portion of land of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And it was, when Jehoram saw Jehu, that he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And he said, "What peace, while the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries continue?"
And Jehoram turned his hands and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
And Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Jehoram between his arms, and the arrow came out from his heart; and he sank down in his chariot.

And he said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him into the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember, I and you were riding in pairs behind Ahab his father, and YHWH lifted up this oracle against him:

"'Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons — the declaration of YHWH — and I will repay you on this portion of land — the declaration of YHWH.' And now, pick him up and throw him onto the portion of land, according to the word of YHWH."

And Ahaziah king of Judah saw and fled by the way of Beth-haggan; and Jehu pursued after him and said, "Strike him down too, into the chariot!" — at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
And his servants caused him to ride to Jerusalem, and they buried him in his grave with his fathers in the city of David.
And in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king over Judah.
And Jehu came to Jezreel; and Jezebel heard, and she set her eyes with eye-paint and made her head good, and she looked down through the window.
And Jehu came into the gate, and she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
And he lifted up his face to the window and said, "Who is with me? Who?" And two or three court officials looked down at him.
And he said, "Let her fall!" And they let her fall; and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
And he went in and ate and drank, and he said, "Attend to this accursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
And they went to bury her, and they found nothing of her except the skull and the feet and the palms of the hands.

And they returned and told him; and he said, "This is the word of YHWH that he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, 'In the territory of Jezreel the dogs shall devour the flesh of Jezebel;
"'and the corpse of Jezebel shall be like dung on the surface of the field, in the territory of Jezreel, so that they shall not say, "This is Jezebel."'"

2 kings_10.t: And Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
"And now, when this letter comes to you — and with you are the sons of your master, and with you are the chariotry and the horses, and a fortified city and the weaponry —
"you shall see the best and the most upright of the sons of your master, and set him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your master."
And they were exceedingly afraid, and they said, "Behold, the two kings did not stand before him — and how shall we stand?"

And the one who was over the house, and the one who was over the city, and the elders and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and all that you say to us we will do. We will not make anyone king. Do what is good in your eyes."

And he wrote them a second letter, saying, "If you are for me, and you are listening to my voice, take the heads of the men, the sons of your master, and come to me about this time tomorrow, to Jezreel." Now the sons of the king, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, who were bringing them up.
And it was, when the letter came to them, that they took the sons of the king and slaughtered seventy men; and they put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
And the messenger came and told him, saying, "They have brought the heads of the sons of the king." And he said, "Make them two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
And it was in the morning that he went out and stood and said to all the people, "You are righteous. Behold, I conspired against my master and killed him — but who struck down all these?"
"Know then that nothing shall fall to the ground of the word of YHWH that YHWH spoke concerning the house of Ahab; and YHWH has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah."
And Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men and his acquaintances and his priests, until he left him no survivor.
And he rose and went and came to Samaria. He was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds on the way,

and Jehu found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, "Who are you?" And they said, "We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down for the welfare of the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
And he said, "Seize them alive." And they seized them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked — forty-two men — and he spared not one of them.

And he went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him, and he blessed him and said to him, "Is your heart right, as my heart is with your heart?" And Jehonadab said, "It is, it is." "Give your hand." And he gave his hand, and he took him up to himself into the chariot.
And he said, "Come with me and see my zeal for YHWH." And they made him ride in his chariot.
And he came to Samaria and struck down all who remained of Ahab in Samaria, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of YHWH that he had spoken to Elijah.
And Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served the Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

"And now, summon to me all the prophets of the Baal, all those who serve him and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to the Baal. Whoever is missing shall not live." And Jehu acted with guile, so as to destroy those who serve the Baal.
And Jehu said, "Set apart as holy a solemn assembly for the Baal." And they proclaimed it.

And Jehu sent throughout all Israel, and all those who serve the Baal came; and no one was left who did not come. And they came into the house of the Baal, and the house of the Baal was filled from mouth to mouth.
And he said to the one who was over the wardrobe, "Bring out clothing for all those who serve the Baal." And he brought out the clothing for them.

And Jehu came, and Jehonadab son of Rechab, into the house of the Baal; and he said to those who serve the Baal, "Search and see, lest there be here with you any of the servants of YHWH — only those who serve the Baal, they alone."

And they came in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. And Jehu had stationed for himself outside eighty men, and he had said, "The man who lets escape any of the men whom I am bringing into your hands — his life for his life."

And it was, when he had finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the runners and to the officers, "Go in, strike them down; let no one come out." And they struck them with the mouth of the sword; and the runners and the officers threw them out, and they went to the city of the house of the Baal.
And they brought out the pillars of the house of the Baal and burned it.
And they pulled down the pillar of the Baal, and they pulled down the house of the Baal and made it into latrines, to this day.
And Jehu destroyed the Baal from Israel.
Only from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, Jehu did not turn aside from after them — the calves of gold that were at Beth-el and that were at Dan.

And YHWH said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in my heart, sons of the fourth generation shall sit for you on the throne of Israel."
But Jehu did not take care to walk in the law of YHWH, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.
In those days YHWH began to cut off in Israel; and Hazael struck them down in all the territory of Israel,
from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun: all the land of Gilead, the Gadites and the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the wadi Arnon, and Gilead and Bashan.
And the rest of the matters of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Jehu lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
And the days that Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years, in Samaria.

2 kings_11.t: And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead; and she rose and destroyed all the offspring of the kingdom.

And Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the sons of the king who were being put to death — him and his nurse — into the chamber of the beds; and they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
And he was with her in the house of YHWH, hiding himself, six years; and Athaliah was reigning over the land.

And in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the runners, and brought them to himself into the house of YHWH; and he cut a covenant with them and made them swear in the house of YHWH, and he showed them the son of the king.
And he commanded them, saying, "This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you, those coming in on the sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the king;
"and a third at the gate of Sur, and a third at the gate behind the runners; and you shall keep the watch of the house by turns.
"And the two divisions among you, all those going out on the sabbath — they shall keep the watch of the house of YHWH for the king.

"And you shall surround the king all around, each with his weapons in his hand; and the one who comes into the ranks shall be put to death. And be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."

And the commanders of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and they took each his men, those coming in on the sabbath, with those going out on the sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
And the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spear and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of YHWH.
And the runners stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king.
And he brought out the son of the king and put on him the crown and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they struck the palm and said, "Long live the king!"
And Athaliah heard the sound of the runners, of the people; and she came to the people, to the house of YHWH.

And she looked, and behold — the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, and the commanders and the trumpets were with the king, and all the people of the land was rejoicing and blowing the trumpets. And Athaliah tore her clothes and called out, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"

And Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the force, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever comes after her, put to death with the sword" — for the priest had said, "Let her not be put to death in the house of YHWH."
And they put hands on her, and she went by the way of the entrance of the horses to the house of the king; and she was put to death there.
And Jehoiada cut the covenant between YHWH and the king and the people, that they should be a people for YHWH; and between the king and the people.

And all the people of the land came to the house of the Baal and pulled it down; his altars and his images they broke thoroughly, and Mattan the priest of the Baal they killed before the altars. And the priest appointed overseers over the house of YHWH.

And he took the commanders of hundreds and the Carites and the runners and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of YHWH; and they came by the way of the gate of the runners to the house of the king, and he sat on the throne of the kings.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city had rest; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword at the house of the king.
A son of seven years was Jehoash when he became king.

2 kings_12.t: In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king; and forty years he reigned in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
And Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of YHWH all his days, in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and making smoke at the high places.

And Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money of the holy gifts that is brought into the house of YHWH — the money of each that passes along, the money of persons at his valuation, all the money that comes upon a man's heart to bring into the house of YHWH —
"let the priests take it for themselves, each from his acquaintance; and they shall repair the damage of the house, wherever damage is found there."
And it was, in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, that the priests had not repaired the damage of the house.

And King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and he said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage of the house? And now, do not take money from your acquaintances, but give it for the damage of the house."
And the priests agreed not to take money from the people and not to repair the damage of the house.

And Jehoiada the priest took one chest and bored a hole in its lid, and he put it beside the altar, on the right as a man comes into the house of YHWH; and the priests who kept the threshold put there all the money that was brought into the house of YHWH.
And it was, when they saw that the money in the chest was much, that the scribe of the king and the high priest came up and tied it up and counted the money that was found in the house of YHWH.

And they put the money that was weighed out into the hands of those doing the work, who were appointed over the house of YHWH; and they paid it out to the craftsmen of wood and to the builders who were working on the house of YHWH,
and to the masons and to the cutters of stone, and to buy timber and hewn stone to repair the damage of the house of YHWH, and for all that was laid out on the house to repair it.
Only there was not made for the house of YHWH bowls of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any article of gold or article of silver, from the money that was brought into the house of YHWH;
for they gave it to those doing the work, and they repaired with it the house of YHWH.
And they did not settle accounts with the men into whose hands they put the money to give to those doing the work, for they were working in good faith.
Money of a guilt offering and money of sin offerings was not brought into the house of YHWH; it belonged to the priests.
Then Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it; and Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

And Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah his fathers, the kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of YHWH and of the house of the king, and he sent them to Hazael king of Aram; and he went up from against Jerusalem.
And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And his servants rose and conspired a conspiracy, and they struck down Joash at Beth-millo, which goes down to Silla.

And Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him down, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_13.t: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria — seventeen years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and he walked after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn aside from it.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, all the days.
And Jehoahaz entreated the face of YHWH, and YHWH listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, that the king of Aram oppressed them.
And YHWH gave Israel a deliverer, and they went out from under the hand of Aram; and the sons of Israel dwelt in their tents as yesterday and the day before.
Nevertheless they did not turn aside from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; in it he walked. And also the Asherah remained in Samaria.
For he had not left to Jehoahaz a people except fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust to be trampled.
And the rest of the matters of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria — sixteen years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin — in it he walked.

And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did, and his might, with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Joash lay down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

And Elisha had become sick with the sickness of which he would die; and Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over his face and said, "My father, my father! The chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!"
And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." And he took to himself a bow and arrows.
And he said to the king of Israel, "Make your hand ride upon the bow." And he made his hand ride; and Elisha put his hands on the hands of the king.

And he said, "Open the window eastward." And he opened it. And Elisha said, "Shoot." And he shot. And he said, "An arrow of victory for YHWH, and an arrow of victory over Aram! And you shall strike Aram at Aphek until you make an end."
And he said, "Take the arrows." And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." And he struck three times and stopped.
And the man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times! Then you would have struck Aram until you made an end; but now you shall strike Aram three times."
And Elisha died, and they buried him. And marauding bands of Moab used to come into the land at the coming of the year.

And it was, as they were burying a man, that behold — they saw the marauding band, and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha; and he went and touched the bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood on his feet.
And Hazael king of Aram had oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

And YHWH showed favour to them and had compassion on them and turned to them, on account of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; and he was not willing to destroy them, and he did not cast them out from his face until now.
And Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.

And Jehoash son of Jehoahaz returned and took back the cities from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, which he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in battle. Three times Joash struck him down, and he restored the cities of Israel.

2 kings_14.t: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.
A son of twenty-five years was he when he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH — only not like David his father. According to all that Joash his father had done, he did.
Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and making smoke at the high places.
And it was, when the kingdom was secure in his hand, that he struck down his servants who had struck down the king his father.

But the sons of those who struck him down he did not put to death, according to what is written in the book of the law of Moses, which YHWH commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; but each shall be put to death for his own sin."
He struck Edom in the Valley of Salt — ten thousand — and seized Sela in the battle, and he called its name Joktheel, to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."

And Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thornbush that was in the Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in the Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And a wild animal that was in the Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
"Striking you have struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be honoured and stay at your house! And why should you engage in strife with harm, and fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah did not listen. And Jehoash king of Israel went up, and they looked one another in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
And Judah was defeated before Israel, and they fled, each to his tents.

And Jehoash king of Israel seized Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh; and he came to Jerusalem and made a breach in the wall of Jerusalem, at the gate of Ephraim as far as the gate of the corner — four hundred cubits.

And he took all the gold and the silver and all the articles that were found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the house of the king, and the sons of the pledges; and he returned to Samaria.

And the rest of the matters of Jehoash, which he did, and his might, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoash lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.
