And the rest of the matters of Amaziah — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And they conspired a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they carried him on the horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
And all the people of Judah took Azariah — and he was a son of sixteen years — and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria — forty-one years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath as far as the sea of the Arabah, according to the word of YHWH the God of Israel, which he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah son of Amittai the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher.
For YHWH saw the affliction of Israel — very bitter — and there was none shut up and none freed, and there was no helper for Israel.
And YHWH had not spoken to wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens; and he delivered them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

And the rest of the matters of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam lay down with his fathers, with the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_15.t: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
A son of sixteen years was he when he became king, and fifty-two years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and making smoke at the high places.

And YHWH struck the king, and he was afflicted with leprosy until the day of his death; and he dwelt in a house of separateness. And Jotham the son of the king was over the house, judging the people of the land.
And the rest of the matters of Azariah, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Azariah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David; and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria — six months.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, as his fathers had done; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
And Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him and struck him down before the people and killed him, and he reigned in his place.
And the rest of the matters of Zechariah — behold, they are written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
That was the word of YHWH that he had spoken to Jehu, saying, "Sons of the fourth generation shall sit for you on the throne of Israel." And so it was.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a month of days in Samaria.
And Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria and struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, and killed him; and he reigned in his place.
And the rest of the matters of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he conspired — behold, they are written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
Then Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territories, from Tirzah — because it did not open, he struck it; all its pregnant women he ripped open.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel — ten years, in Samaria.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, all his days.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hands might be with him, to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.

And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all the mighty men of wealth, to give to the king of Assyria — fifty shekels of silver for each man. And the king of Assyria turned back and did not remain there in the land.
And the rest of the matters of Menahem, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem lay down with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria — two years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

And Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria, in the fortress of the house of the king, with Argob and with Arieh; and with him were fifty men of the Gileadites. And he killed him and reigned in his place.
And the rest of the matters of Pekahiah, and all that he did — behold, they are written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria — twenty years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon and Abel-beth-maacah and Janoah and Kedesh and Hazor and Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he took them into exile to Assyria.
And Hoshea son of Elah conspired a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah and struck him down and killed him, and he reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
And the rest of the matters of Pekah, and all that he did — behold, they are written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah became king.
A son of twenty-five years was he when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH; according to all that Uzziah his father had done, he did.
Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and making smoke at the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of YHWH.
And the rest of the matters of Jotham, which he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
In those days YHWH began to send against Judah Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah.
And Jotham lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_16.t: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah became king.
A son of twenty years was Ahaz when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem. And he did not do what was right in the eyes of YHWH his God, like David his father.

And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and he even made his son pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations that YHWH had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
And he sacrificed and made smoke at the high places and on the hills and under every luxuriant tree.
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem for battle, and they laid siege against Ahaz; but they were not able to do battle.
At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram and cleared the Judeans out of Elath; and Edomites came to Elath and have dwelt there to this day.

And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and deliver me from the palm of the king of Aram and from the palm of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
And Ahaz took the silver and the gold that was found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the house of the king, and he sent it to the king of Assyria as a bribe.
And the king of Assyria listened to him; and the king of Assyria went up to Damascus and seized it and took it into exile to Kir; and Rezin he put to death.

And King Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria at Damascus, and he saw the altar that was in Damascus. And King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern, according to all its workmanship.
And Uriah the priest built the altar; according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so Uriah the priest did, before King Ahaz came from Damascus.
And the king came from Damascus, and the king saw the altar; and the king drew near to the altar and offered up on it.
And he made his burnt offering and his grain offering smoke, and poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
And the altar of bronze that was before YHWH — he brought it near from the front of the house, from between the altar and the house of YHWH, and he put it on the side of the altar, northward.

And King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "On the great altar make smoke the burnt offering of the morning and the grain offering of the evening, and the burnt offering of the king and his grain offering, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land and their grain offering and their drink offerings; and all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice you shall sprinkle on it. And the altar of bronze shall be mine, to consult."
And Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded.
And King Ahaz cut off the rims of the stands and removed the washbasin from upon them; and the sea he took down from upon the bronze oxen that were under it, and he put it on a pavement of stones.
And the covered structure for the sabbath that they had built in the house, and the outer entrance of the king, he removed from the house of YHWH, because of the king of Assyria.
And the rest of the matters of Ahaz, which he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Ahaz lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_17.t: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel — nine years.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH — only not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
Against him Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up, and Hoshea became his subject and rendered him tribute.

And the king of Assyria found treason in Hoshea, in that he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not brought up tribute to the king of Assyria as year by year; and the king of Assyria arrested him and confined him in a prison house.
And the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and he came up to Samaria and laid siege against it three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria captured Samaria, and he took Israel into exile to Assyria and settled them in Halah and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and the cities of Media.
And it was because the sons of Israel had sinned against YHWH their God, who brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and they had feared other gods,
and they had walked in the customs of the nations that YHWH had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they had made.
And the sons of Israel did secretly things that were not right against YHWH their God; and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from a tower of watchmen to a fortified city.
And they erected for themselves pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every luxuriant tree,
and they made smoke there at all the high places, like the nations that YHWH had taken into exile from before them; and they did evil things to provoke YHWH to anger.
And they served the idols, of which YHWH had said to them, "You shall not do this thing."

And YHWH warned Israel and Judah by the hand of every prophet, every seer, saying, "Turn back from your evil ways and keep my commandments, my statutes, according to all the law that I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by the hand of my servants the prophets."
But they did not listen, and they stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who did not trust in YHWH their God.

And they rejected his statutes and his covenant that he had made with their fathers, and his testimonies with which he had warned them; and they walked after emptiness and became empty, and after the nations that were around them, which YHWH had commanded them not to do as they did.

And they forsook all the commandments of YHWH their God, and they made for themselves a cast image, two calves; and they made an Asherah and bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served the Baal.

And they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, and they divined divinations and practised divination; and they sold themselves to do the evil in the eyes of YHWH, to provoke him to anger.
And YHWH was very angry with Israel, and he removed them from his face; no one was left, only the tribe of Judah alone.
Also Judah did not keep the commandments of YHWH their God, and they walked in the customs of Israel, which they had made.
And YHWH rejected all the offspring of Israel and afflicted them and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until he had thrown them out from before him.
For he tore Israel from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following YHWH and caused them to sin a great sin.
And the sons of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam that he did; they did not turn aside from it,
until YHWH removed Israel from his face, just as he had spoken by the hand of all his servants the prophets. And Israel went into exile from its land to Assyria, to this day.

And the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon and from Cuthah and from Avva and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel; and they took possession of Samaria and dwelt in its cities.
And it was, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear YHWH; and YHWH sent lions among them, and they were killing among them.

And they said to the king of Assyria, "The nations that you took into exile and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom of the god of the land; and he has sent lions among them, and there they are, killing them, because they do not know the custom of the god of the land."

And the king of Assyria commanded, saying, "Take there one of the priests whom you took into exile from there, and let them go and dwell there; and let him teach them the custom of the god of the land."
And one of the priests whom they had taken into exile from Samaria came and dwelt in Beth-el, and he was teaching them how they should fear YHWH.
And they were making, nation by nation, its own gods; and they placed them in the house of the high places that the Samaritans had made, nation by nation, in their cities where they were dwelling.
And the people of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, and the people of Cuthah made Nergal, and the people of Hamath made Ashima,
and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites were burning their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
And they were fearing YHWH, and they appointed for themselves from among themselves priests of the high places, and they were offering for them in the house of the high places.
They were fearing YHWH, and they were serving their own gods, according to the custom of the nations from among whom they had been taken into exile.

To this day they are doing according to the former customs. They do not fear YHWH, and they do not do according to their statutes and their judgement, or according to the law and the commandment that YHWH commanded the sons of Jacob, whose name he made Israel.
And YHWH made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, "You shall not fear other gods, and you shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not sacrifice to them.
"But YHWH, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm — him you shall fear, and to him you shall bow down, and to him you shall sacrifice.
"And the statutes and the judgements and the law and the commandment that he wrote for you — you shall take care to do them all the days; and you shall not fear other gods.
"And the covenant that I made with you, you shall not forget; and you shall not fear other gods.
"But YHWH your God you shall fear, and he will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."
But they did not listen; rather, according to their former custom they were doing.
And these nations were fearing YHWH, and they were serving their images; also their children and their children's children — just as their fathers did, so they are doing, to this day.

2 kings_18.t: And it was in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel that Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.
A son of twenty-five years was he when he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Abi, daughter of Zechariah.
And he did what was right in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that David his father had done.

He removed the high places and broke the pillars and cut down the Asherah; and he crushed the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for until those days the sons of Israel had been making smoke to it; and it was called Nehushtan.
In YHWH, the God of Israel, he trusted; and after him there was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him.
And he clung to YHWH; he did not turn aside from following him, and he kept his commandments that YHWH had commanded Moses.
And YHWH was with him; in all that he went out to, he prospered. And he rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.
He struck the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territories, from a tower of watchmen to a fortified city.
And it was in the fourth year of King Hezekiah — it was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel — that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and laid siege against it.
And they captured it at the end of three years; in the sixth year of Hezekiah — it was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel — Samaria was captured.
And the king of Assyria took Israel into exile to Assyria and led them to Halah and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and the cities of Media,
because they had not listened to the voice of YHWH their God and had transgressed his covenant — all that Moses the servant of YHWH had commanded; and they did not listen and did not do it.
And in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.

And Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, "I have sinned. Turn back from me; what you impose on me I will bear." And the king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
And Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of YHWH and in the treasuries of the house of the king.
At that time Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of YHWH, and the doorposts that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and he gave them to the king of Assyria.

And the king of Assyria sent the Tartan and the Rab-saris and the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a massive force, to Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem; and they went up and came and stood at the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway of the launderer's field.
And they called out to the king; and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the house, went out to them, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
And the Rabshakeh said to them, "Say now to Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this trust in which you trust?
"You have said — only a word of the lips — 'counsel and strength for war.' Now, on whom do you rely, that you have rebelled against me?
"Now behold, you rely for yourself on the staff of this crushed reed, on Egypt — which, if a man leans on it, goes into his palm and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who rely on him.

"And if you say to me, 'In YHWH our God we trust' — is he not the one whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has removed, and has said to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'Before this altar you shall bow down in Jerusalem'?
"And now, make a wager, please, with my master, with the king of Assyria: let me give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them.
"And how will you turn back the face of one governor, of the least of my master's servants? And you rely for yourself on Egypt for chariotry and for horsemen.
"Now, is it apart from YHWH that I have come up against this place to destroy it? YHWH said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, and Shebna and Joah, said to the Rabshakeh, "Speak, please, to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; and do not speak with us in Judean in the ears of the people who are on the wall."

And the Rabshakeh said to them, "Is it to your master and to you that my master sent me to speak these words? Is it not to the men sitting on the wall, to eat their own excrement and to drink the water of their own feet with you?"
And the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a great voice in Judean, and he spoke and said, "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria.
"Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you from his hand.
"And do not let Hezekiah make you trust in YHWH, saying, 'Delivering, YHWH will deliver us, and this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'

"Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make a blessing with me and come out to me; and eat, each his own vine and each his own fig tree, and drink, each the water of his own cistern,

"until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees, of fresh oil, and of honey — and live, and do not die. And do not listen to Hezekiah, for he misleads you, saying, 'YHWH will deliver us.'
"Delivering, have the gods of the nations delivered each his own land, from the hand of the king of Assyria?
"Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? For have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
"Who among all the gods of the lands are those who have delivered their land from my hand, that YHWH should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
And the people kept silent and did not answer him a word, for it was the command of the king, saying, "You shall not answer him."
And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with clothes torn; and they told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

2 kings_19.t: And it was, when King Hezekiah heard, that he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of YHWH.
And he sent Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz.
And they said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of distress and rebuke and insult; for children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth.

"Perhaps YHWH your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words that YHWH your God has heard. And you shall lift up a prayer for the remnant that is found."
And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

And Isaiah said to them, "Thus you shall say to your master: Thus says YHWH: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
"Behold, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his own land; and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land."
And the Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, saying, "Behold, he has come out to fight against you." And he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,
"Thus you shall say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you are trusting, deceive you, saying, 'Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'
"Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction — and shall you be delivered?
"Did the gods of the nations deliver them — the nations that my fathers destroyed: Gozan and Haran and Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
"Where is he, the king of Hamath and the king of Arpad and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah?"
And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; and he went up to the house of YHWH, and Hezekiah spread it out before YHWH.
And Hezekiah prayed before YHWH and said, "YHWH, God of Israel, who sits upon the cherubim, you are the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you made the heavens and the earth.
"Incline your ear, YHWH, and hear; open your eyes, YHWH, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to taunt the living God.
"Truly, YHWH, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their land,
"and have put their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone — and they destroyed them.
"And now, YHWH our God, deliver us, please, from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, YHWH, are God, you alone."
And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: What you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard."
This is the word that YHWH has spoken concerning him: "She despises you, she mocks you, the virgin daughter of Zion; behind you she shakes her head, the daughter of Jerusalem.
"Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? And against whom have you lifted up your voice and raised your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

"By the hand of your messengers you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: 'With the abundance of my chariotry I have gone up the heights of the mountains, the remotest parts of Lebanon; and I cut down the height of its cedars, the choicest of its pines; and I came to its farthest lodging place, the forest of its plantation.
"'I have dug and drunk foreign waters, and I dry up with the sole of my feet all the canals of Egypt.'
"Have you not heard? Long ago I did it, from days of antiquity I formed it; now I have brought it about, and you are to make fortified cities crash into ruined heaps.
"And their inhabitants, short of hand, were dismayed and put to shame; they were the vegetation of the field, and the greenery of grass, grass of the housetops, and blight before the standing grain.
"And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, and your raging against me.

"Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle on your lips, and I will bring you back by the way by which you came."

"And this shall be the sign for you: you shall eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; and in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
"And the escaped remnant of the house of Judah that remains shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
"For from Jerusalem a remnant shall go out, and an escaped remnant from Mount Zion. The zeal of YHWH of hosts will do this."

Therefore thus says YHWH concerning the king of Assyria: "He shall not come into this city, and he shall not shoot an arrow there; and he shall not confront it with a shield, and he shall not pour out a siege mound against it.
"By the way by which he came, by it he shall return; and into this city he shall not come — the declaration of YHWH.
"And I will defend this city, to deliver it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."

And it was on that night that the messenger of YHWH went out and struck down in the camp of Assyria a hundred and eighty-five thousand; and they rose early in the morning, and behold — all of them were dead corpses.
And Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and went and returned, and he stayed in Nineveh.

And it was, as he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword; and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_20.t: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death; and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said to him, "Thus says YHWH: Give command to your household, for you are dying and shall not live."
And he turned his face to the wall and prayed to YHWH, saying,
"I beg you, YHWH, remember, please, that I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and that I have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept a great weeping.
And it was — Isaiah had not gone out of the middle court — that the word of YHWH came to him, saying,

"Go back and say to Hezekiah the ruler of my people: Thus says YHWH, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. Behold, I am healing you; on the third day you shall go up to the house of YHWH.

"And I will add to your days fifteen years; and from the palm of the king of Assyria I will deliver you and this city, and I will defend this city for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
And Isaiah said, "Take a cake of figs." And they took it and put it on the boil, and he lived.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What is the sign that YHWH will heal me, and that I shall go up on the third day to the house of YHWH?"
And Isaiah said, "This is the sign for you from YHWH, that YHWH will do the thing that he has spoken: Shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it go back ten steps?"
And Hezekiah said, "It is a trifling thing for the shadow to stretch out ten steps. No — let the shadow go back ten steps."
And Isaiah the prophet called out to YHWH, and he brought the shadow back on the steps, by which it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz, backwards ten steps.
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

And Hezekiah listened to them, and he showed them all his treasure house — the silver and the gold and the spices and the good oil — and his armoury, and all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing that Hezekiah did not show them in his house and in all his realm.
And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and where did they come to you from?" And Hezekiah said, "They came from a distant land, from Babylon."
And he said, "What did they see in your house?" And Hezekiah said, "They saw all that is in my house. There was nothing that I did not show them in my storehouses."
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of YHWH.
"Behold, days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be carried off to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says YHWH.
"And some of your sons who come forth from you, whom you will father, they shall take away; and they shall be court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon."
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of YHWH that you have spoken is good." And he said, "Is it not so, if there shall be peace and faithfulness in my days?"

And the rest of the matters of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought the water into the city — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Hezekiah lay down with his fathers; and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_21.t: A son of twelve years was Manasseh when he became king, and fifty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Hephzibah.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to the abominations of the nations that YHWH had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.

And he turned and rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he set up altars to the Baal and made an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel had done; and he bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
And he built altars in the house of YHWH, of which YHWH had said, "In Jerusalem I will put my name."
And he built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courtyards of the house of YHWH.

And he made his son pass through the fire, and he practised soothsaying and divination, and he dealt with mediums and with spiritists. He did much, to do the evil in the eyes of YHWH, to provoke him to anger.

And he put the carved image of the Asherah that he had made in the house, of which YHWH had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever.

"And I will not again make the foot of Israel wander from the ground that I gave to their fathers — only if they take care to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that my servant Moses commanded them."
But they did not listen; and Manasseh misled them to do evil more than the nations that YHWH had destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
And YHWH spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,
"Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations — he has done more evil than all that the Amorite who was before him did — and has also caused Judah to sin with his idols,
"therefore thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing calamity on Jerusalem and Judah, such that everyone who hears of it — both his ears shall tingle.
"And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab; and I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a bowl — wiping it and turning it upside down.
"And I will abandon the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies; and they shall become spoil and plunder for all their enemies,
"because they have done the evil in my eyes and have been provoking me to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day."
And also innocent blood Manasseh shed very much, until he had filled Jerusalem from mouth to mouth — apart from his sin by which he caused Judah to sin, to do the evil in the eyes of YHWH.
And the rest of the matters of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Manasseh lay down with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amon his son reigned in his place.
A son of twenty-two years was Amon when he became king, and two years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, as Manasseh his father had done.
And he walked in all the way in which his father had walked, and he served the idols that his father had served and bowed down to them.
And he forsook YHWH, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of YHWH.
And the servants of Amon conspired against him, and they killed the king in his own house.
And the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
And the rest of the matters of Amon, which he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And they buried him in his grave in the garden of Uzza; and Josiah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_22.t: A son of eight years was Josiah when he became king, and thirty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath.
And he did the right in the eyes of YHWH, and he walked in all the way of David his father, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
And it was in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of YHWH, saying,
"Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, that he may complete the reckoning of the silver that has been brought to the house of YHWH, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people;

"and let them put it into the hand of the doers of the work who are appointed over the house of YHWH; and let them give it to the doers of the work who are in the house of YHWH, to repair the breach of the house —
"to the craftsmen and to the builders and to the masons, and to buy timber and hewn stones to repair the house."
Only the silver put into their hand was not reckoned with them, for they were working in good faith.
And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the law in the house of YHWH." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

And Shaphan the scribe came to the king and brought the king back word, and said, "Your servants have poured out the silver that was found in the house, and they have put it into the hand of the doers of the work who are appointed over the house of YHWH."
And Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." And Shaphan read it aloud before the king.
And it was, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, that he tore his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,

"Go, consult YHWH for me and for the people and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the rage of YHWH that has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us."

And Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam and Achbor and Shaphan and Asaiah, went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments — and she was dwelling in Jerusalem in the Second District — and they spoke to her.
And she said to them, "Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
"Thus says YHWH: Behold, I am bringing calamity on this place and on its inhabitants — all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read.
"Because they have forsaken me and have made smoke to other gods, so as to provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands, my rage will be kindled against this place and will not be quenched.
"And to the king of Judah, who sent you to consult YHWH — thus you shall say to him: Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you have heard:

"Because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before YHWH when you heard what I had spoken against this place and against its inhabitants — that they would become a horror and a curse — and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard, the declaration of YHWH.

"Therefore, behold, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your graves in peace, and your eyes shall not look on all the calamity that I am bringing on this place." And they brought the king back word.

2 kings_23.t: And the king sent, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up to the house of YHWH, and every man of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, from small to great; and he read aloud in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of YHWH.

And the king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before YHWH — to walk after YHWH and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all heart and with all soul, to establish the words of this covenant that were written on this book. And all the people took their stand in the covenant.

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second rank and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of YHWH all the articles made for the Baal and for the Asherah and for all the host of the heavens; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried their dust to Bethel.

And he put down the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed, and who had made smoke at the high places in the cities of Judah and the surroundings of Jerusalem; and those who made smoke to the Baal, to the sun and to the moon and to the constellations and to all the host of the heavens.

And he brought out the Asherah from the house of YHWH, outside Jerusalem to the wadi Kidron, and burned it at the wadi Kidron and crushed it to dust, and threw its dust on the burial place of the sons of the people.
And he broke down the houses of the male shrine prostitutes that were in the house of YHWH, where the women were weaving hangings for the Asherah.

And he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah, and made unclean the high places where the priests had made smoke, from Geba to Beersheba; and he broke down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man's left at the gate of the city.
Nevertheless the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of YHWH in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
And he made unclean the Topheth that is in the valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one would make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to the Molech.

And he removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, at the entrance of the house of YHWH, by the chamber of Nathan-melech the court official, which was in the precincts; and the chariots of the sun he burned with fire.

And the altars that were on the roof, the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courtyards of the house of YHWH, the king pulled down; and he smashed them there and threw their dust into the wadi Kidron.

And the high places that were east of Jerusalem, to the south of the Mount of the Destroyer, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Astarte the detestable thing of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king made unclean.
And he broke the pillars and cut down the Asherim, and filled their places with the bones of humankind.

And also the altar that was at Bethel, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made — also that altar and the high place he tore down; and he burned the high place, crushed it to dust, and burned the Asherah.

And Josiah turned and saw the graves that were there on the mountain, and he sent and took the bones from the graves and burned them on the altar and made it unclean, according to the word of YHWH that the man of God had proclaimed, who proclaimed these words.

And he said, "What is that monument that I see?" And the men of the city said to him, "It is the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel."
And he said, "Leave him alone; let no one disturb his bones." And they left his bones undisturbed, with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.

And also all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke to anger, Josiah removed; and he did to them according to all the deeds that he had done at Bethel.
And he slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there, on the altars, and burned the bones of humankind on them; and he returned to Jerusalem.
And the king commanded all the people, saying, "Keep the Passover to YHWH your God, as it is written on this book of the covenant."
For such a Passover had not been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah;
but in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to YHWH in Jerusalem.

And also the mediums and the spiritists and the teraphim and the idols and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, Josiah burned away, in order to establish the words of the law written on the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of YHWH.

And like him there was no king before him who turned back to YHWH with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his muchness, according to all the law of Moses; and after him none arose like him.
Nevertheless YHWH did not turn back from the burning of his great anger, with which his anger burned against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.
And YHWH said, "Judah also I will remove from before my face, as I removed Israel; and I will reject this city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"
And the rest of the matters of Josiah, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria, to the river Euphrates. And King Josiah went to meet him; and he killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.

And his servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own grave. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
A son of twenty-three years was Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his fathers had done.
And Pharaoh Neco confined him at Riblah in the land of Hamath, from reigning in Jerusalem; and he laid a fine on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
And Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; and Jehoahaz he took, and he came to Egypt and died there.

And the silver and the gold Jehoiakim gave to Pharaoh; only he assessed the land to give the silver at the mouth of Pharaoh — each man according to his assessment he exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
A son of twenty-five years was Jehoiakim when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Zebidah, daughter of Pedaiah, from Rumah.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his fathers had done.

2 kings_24.t: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.

And YHWH sent against him the raiding bands of the Chaldeans and the raiding bands of Aram and the raiding bands of Moab and the raiding bands of the sons of Ammon; and he sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of YHWH that he had spoken by the hand of his servants the prophets.
Surely at the mouth of YHWH it came upon Judah, to remove them from before his face, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
and also for the innocent blood that he had shed, and he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; and YHWH was not willing to forgive.
And the rest of the matters of Jehoiakim, and all that he did — are they not written on the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Jehoiakim lay down with his fathers; and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
And the king of Egypt did not come out from his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken all that had belonged to the king of Egypt, from the wadi of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
A son of eighteen years was Jehoiachin when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that his father had done.
At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came into a state of siege.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city while his servants were laying siege to it.

And Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his officials and his court officials; and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of YHWH and the treasures of the house of the king; and he cut up all the articles of gold that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple of YHWH, just as YHWH had spoken.

And he took into exile all Jerusalem, and all the officials, and all the mighty men of valour — ten thousand exiles — and every craftsman and smith; none was left except the poorest of the people of the land.

And he took Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon; and the mother of the king and the wives of the king and his court officials and the leading men of the land he led away into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
And all the men of valour, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand — all of them warriors, makers of war — the king of Babylon brought into exile to Babylon.
And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
A son of twenty-one years was Zedekiah when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
For it was because of the anger of YHWH that it came about in Jerusalem and in Judah, until he cast them out from before his face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

2 kings_25.t: And it was in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem; and he encamped against it, and they built a siege wall against it all around.
And the city came into a state of siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth of the month the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

And the city was broken into; and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were around the city; and he went by the way of the Arabah.
And the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and they overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
And they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah; and they pronounced judgement on him.
And they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; and he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him with bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.

And in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month — that was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard, the servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of YHWH and the house of the king and all the houses of Jerusalem; and every great house he burned with fire.
And the walls of Jerusalem all around, all the army of the Chaldeans who were with the chief of the guard broke down.
And the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the deserters who had fallen away to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard took into exile.
But some of the poorest of the land the chief of the guard left behind, to be vinedressers and ploughmen.
And the pillars of bronze that were in the house of YHWH, and the stands, and the sea of bronze that was in the house of YHWH, the Chaldeans broke; and they carried their bronze to Babylon.
And the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the pans, and all the articles of bronze with which they served, they took.
And the fire-pans and the basins — what was gold, gold, and what was silver, silver — the chief of the guard took.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of YHWH — there was no weighing the bronze of all these articles.

Eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and a capital of bronze was on it; and the height of the capital was three cubits, and a network and pomegranates were on the capital all around, all of bronze. And the second pillar had the like, with the network.
And the chief of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold;

and from the city he took one court official who was officer over the men of war, and five men of those who saw the king's face who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. And Judah went into exile from its land.
And the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left behind — he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

And all the commanders of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah — Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you."

And it was in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the seed of the kingship, came, and ten men with him; and they struck down Gedaliah, and he died — and the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
And all the people, from small to great, and the commanders of the armies arose and came to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

And it was in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of the house of imprisonment.
And he spoke good things with him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed his prison clothes, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.
And his allowance, a continual allowance, was given him from the king, the matter of a day in its day, all the days of his life.

2 samuel_1.t: And it was, after the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking Amalek, that David stayed in Ziklag two days.

And it was on the third day, and behold, a man coming from the camp, from Saul, and his garments torn and earth on his head. And it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the ground and bowed down.
And David said to him, "From where do you come?" And he said to him, "From the camp of Israel I have escaped."
And David said to him, "What was the matter? Tell me, please." And he said, "The people fled from the battle, and also many of the people fell and died, and also Saul and Jonathan his son died."
And David said to the young man who was telling him, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"

And the young man who was telling him said, "Chancing I chanced to be on Mount Gilboa, and behold, Saul leaning on his spear, and behold, the chariotry and the masters of the horsemen had overtaken him."
And he turned behind him and saw me, and he called to me, and I said, "Here I am."
And he said to me, "Who are you?" And I said to him, "I am an Amalekite."
And he said to me, "Stand over me, please, and kill me, for the shudder has seized me, for all my life is still in me."

And I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he would not live after his falling. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them to my lord here.
And David took hold of his garments and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
And they mourned and wept and fasted until the evening over Saul and over Jonathan his son and over the people of YHWH and over the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
And David said to the young man who was telling him, "From where are you?" And he said, "I am the son of a sojourning man, an Amalekite."
And David said to him, "How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the anointed of YHWH?"
And David called to one of the young men and said, "Draw near, fall upon him." And he struck him down and he died.
And David said to him, "Your blood be on your head, for your own mouth testified against you, saying, 'I killed the anointed of YHWH.'"
And David lamented this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
and he said to teach the sons of Judah the Bow. Behold, it is written in the scroll of Jashar:
The beauty, O Israel, upon your high places is slain! How the mighty have fallen!
Do not tell it in Gath, do not bear the news in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
O mountains in Gilboa, let there be no dew and no rain upon you, nor fields of contributions; for there was defiled the shield of the mighty, the shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and the lovely, in their lives and in their death they were not parted. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with luxuries, who put ornaments of gold upon your clothing.
How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan, upon your high places, is slain.
I am in distress over you, my brother Jonathan. You were very pleasant to me. Your love to me was more wonderful than the love of women.
How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!

2 samuel_2.t: And it was after this that David enquired of YHWH, saying, "Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" And YHWH said to him, "Go up." And David said, "Where shall I go up?" And he said, "To Hebron."
And David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
And his men who were with him David brought up, each man and his household, and they settled in the cities of Hebron.
And the men of Judah came and anointed David there as king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, "The men of Jabesh Gilead are the ones who buried Saul."
And David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh Gilead and said to them, "Blessed are you to YHWH, that you did this loyalty with your lord, with Saul, and buried him."
"And now, may YHWH do with you steadfast love and faithfulness, and I also will do this good with you, because you did this thing."
"And now let your hands be strong and become sons of valour, for your lord Saul is dead; and me also the house of Judah has anointed as king over them."
And Abner son of Ner, commander of the army that belonged to Saul, had taken Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim,
and made him king over Gilead and over the Ashurites and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim and over Benjamin and over all Israel.
Ish-bosheth son of Saul was a son of forty years when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah was after David.
And the number of the days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
And Abner son of Ner went out, and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
And Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out, and they met them at the pool of Gibeon together. And these sat at the pool on this side and these at the pool on that side.
And Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men arise, please, and play before us." And Joab said, "Let them arise."
And they arose and crossed over by number, twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.
And each took hold of the head of his fellow, with his sword in the side of his fellow, and they fell together. And that place was called Helkath Hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
And the battle was very hard on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were struck down before the servants of David.
And the three sons of Zeruiah were there — Joab and Abishai and Asahel — and Asahel was swift on his feet, like one of the gazelles that are in the open country.
And Asahel pursued after Abner, and he did not turn aside to go to the right or to the left from after Abner.
And Abner turned behind him and said, "Is this you, Asahel?" And he said, "I am."

And Abner said to him, "Turn aside for yourself to your right or to your left, and seize for yourself one of the young men, and take for yourself his spoils." But Asahel was not willing to turn aside from after him.
And Abner said again to Asahel, "Turn aside for yourself from after me. Why should I strike you down to the ground? And how could I lift up my face to Joab your brother?"

And he refused to turn aside, and Abner struck him with the butt of the spear into the belly, and the spear came out from behind him, and he fell there and died in his place. And it happened that everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.
And Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner, and the sun went down. And they came to the hill of Ammah, which is before Giah on the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
And the sons of Benjamin gathered themselves behind Abner and became one band, and they stood on the top of one hill.

And Abner called to Joab and said, "Shall the sword devour for ever? Do you not know that it will be bitter at the last? And how long will you not say to the people to turn back from after their brothers?"
And Joab said, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, then only from the morning would the people have gone up, each from after his brother."
And Joab blew on the horn, and all the people stood still and no longer pursued after Israel, and they did not fight any more.
And Abner and his men went through the Arabah all that night, and they crossed the Jordan and went through all the Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
And Joab returned from after Abner and gathered all the people, and there were missing from the servants of David nineteen men, and Asahel.
And the servants of David had struck down from Benjamin and among the men of Abner three hundred and sixty men who died.
And they carried Asahel up and buried him in the tomb of his father, which is at Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all the night, and it grew light for them at Hebron.

2 samuel_3.t: And the war was long between the house of Saul and the house of David, and David went on and grew strong, and the house of Saul went on and grew weak.
And sons were born to David in Hebron. And his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelite;
and his second, Kileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
and the fourth, Adonijah son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah son of Abital;
and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah the wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.
And it was, while the war was between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.
And Saul had a concubine, and her name was Rizpah daughter of Aiah. And he said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

And Abner burned with great anger over the words of Ish-bosheth, and he said, "Am I a dog's head that belongs to Judah? Today I show loyalty to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and I have not delivered you into the hand of David — and you charge against me the guilt of the woman today!"
"So may God do to Abner and so may he add to him, if — just as YHWH swore to David — I do not do so for him:
"to take the kingdom away from the house of Saul and to raise up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."
And he was not able to answer Abner a word any more, because of his fear of him.

And Abner sent messengers to David in his own place, saying, "To whom does the land belong?" — saying, "Cut your covenant with me, and behold, my hand will be with you to bring all Israel round to you."
And he said, "Good. I will cut a covenant with you. Only one thing I am asking of you, namely: you shall not see my face unless, before you come to see my face, you bring Michal daughter of Saul."
And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
And Ish-bosheth sent and took her from a husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.
And her husband went with her, going and weeping after her, as far as Bahurim. And Abner said to him, "Go, return." And he returned.
And the word of Abner was with the elders of Israel, saying, "Both yesterday and the day before you were seeking David as king over you.
"And now, act! For YHWH has said to David, saying, 'By the hand of David my servant I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin. And Abner also went to speak in the ears of David at Hebron all that was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of the whole house of Benjamin.
And Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made a feast for Abner and for the men who were with him.

And Abner said to David, "Let me arise and go and gather to my lord the king all Israel, and let them cut a covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your being desires." And David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a raid, and they brought much plunder with them. And Abner was not with David at Hebron, for he had sent him away and he had gone in peace.
And Joab and all the army that was with him came, and they told Joab, saying, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away and he went in peace."
And Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Behold, Abner came to you! Why is it that you sent him away, and he has gone right away?"
"You know Abner son of Ner — that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing."
And Joab went out from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. And David did not know.
And Abner returned to Hebron, and Joab turned him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him in quiet, and he struck him there in the belly, and he died for the blood of Asahel his brother.
And David heard afterwards and said, "I and my kingdom are innocent before YHWH for ever of the blood of Abner son of Ner.

"Let them whirl upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house, and let there not fail from the house of Joab one with a discharge, and one with leprosy, and one who takes hold of the spindle, and one who falls by the sword, and one lacking bread."
And Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner because he had put to death Asahel their brother at Gibeon in the battle.
And David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your garments and gird on sackcloth and mourn before Abner." And King David was walking behind the bier.
And they buried Abner in Hebron, and the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.
And the king lamented over Abner and said: "Should Abner die as a fool dies?
Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not brought into bronze fetters. As one falls before sons of injustice you fell." And all the people wept over him again.
And all the people came to make David eat bread while it was still day, and David swore, saying, "So may God do to me and so may he add, if I taste bread or anything at all before the sun goes down."
And all the people took note, and it was good in their eyes; as everything the king did was good in the eyes of all the people.
And all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it had not been from the king to put Abner son of Ner to death.
And the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a leader and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?
"And I today am weak, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me. May YHWH repay the doer of evil according to his evil."

2 samuel_4.t: And the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, and his hands dropped, and all Israel was dismayed.

And the son of Saul had two men, commanders of raiding bands: the name of the one was Baanah and the name of the second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin — for Beeroth too is reckoned to Benjamin,
and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have been sojourners there to this day.

And Jonathan son of Saul had a son stricken of feet. He was a son of five years when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and his nurse lifted him up and fled; and it was, in her haste to flee, that he fell and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and came at the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, and he was lying down for the lying-down of noon.
And they came into the middle of the house as takers of wheat, and struck him in the belly. And Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

And they came into the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedchamber, and they struck him and killed him and removed his head. And they took his head and went by way of the Arabah all the night.

And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron, and they said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. And YHWH has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his offspring."
And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As YHWH lives, who has ransomed my life from every trouble —
"when the one who told me, saying, 'Behold, Saul is dead,' and in his own eyes he was a bearer of good news — I took hold of him and killed him in Ziklag, which was my giving him good news;
"how much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house upon his bed! And now, shall I not require his blood from your hand and remove you from the earth?"

And David commanded the young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and their feet and hanged them by the pool in Hebron. And the head of Ish-bosheth they took and buried in the tomb of Abner at Hebron.

2 samuel_5.t: And all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, saying, "Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.

"Both yesterday and the day before, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in. And YHWH said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall become ruler over Israel.'"
And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David cut a covenant with them at Hebron before YHWH, and they anointed David king over Israel.
David was a son of thirty years when he became king; forty years he reigned.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

And the king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusite, the inhabitant of the land. And he said to David, saying, "You will not come in here — the blind and the lame will turn you back" — that is to say, "David will not come in here."
But David captured the stronghold of Zion — that is the City of David.

And David said on that day, "Anyone who strikes a Jebusite, let him reach by the water shaft the lame and the blind, who are hated of David's being." Therefore they say, "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house."
And David dwelt in the stronghold and called it the City of David. And David built round about, from the Millo and inward.
And David went on and grew great, and YHWH, God of hosts, was with him.
And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar timber, and craftsmen in wood and craftsmen in wall-stone, and they built a house for David.
And David knew that YHWH had established him as king over Israel, and that he had lifted up his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
And David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
And these are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua and Shobab and Nathan and Solomon,
and Ibhar and Elishua and Nepheg and Japhia,
and Elishama and Eliada and Eliphelet.
And the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, and all the Philistines went up to seek David. And David heard and went down to the stronghold.
And the Philistines came and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
And David enquired of YHWH, saying, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?" And YHWH said to David, "Go up, for giving I will give the Philistines into your hand."

And David came to Baal Perazim, and David struck them down there. And he said, "YHWH has burst through my enemies before me like a bursting of waters." Therefore the name of that place was called Baal Perazim.
And they abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.
And the Philistines went up once more and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
And David enquired of YHWH, and he said, "You shall not go up. Go round to behind them, and come at them opposite the balsam trees.
"And it shall be, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then you shall act decisively, for then YHWH has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines."
And David did so, just as YHWH had commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines from Geba until you come to Gezer.

2 samuel_6.t: And David gathered again all the chosen men in Israel, thirty thousand.

And David arose and went, and all the people who were with him, from Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of YHWH of hosts, who sits on the cherubim.
And they made the ark of God ride on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart,
and they carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, with the ark of God, and Ahio was walking before the ark.
And David and all the house of Israel were making music before YHWH with all kinds of fir wood, and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with rattles and with cymbals.
And they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, and Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen had let it slip.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
And David burned with anger because YHWH had burst out a bursting against Uzzah, and that place was called Perez-uzzah to this day.
And David feared YHWH on that day and said, "How shall the ark of YHWH come to me?"
And David was not willing to bring the ark of YHWH round to himself, to the City of David, and David turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
And the ark of YHWH remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and YHWH blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

And it was told to King David, saying, "YHWH has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God." And David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing.
And it was, when those bearing the ark of YHWH had stepped six steps, that he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
And David was whirling with all his strength before YHWH, and David was girded with a linen ephod.
And David and all the house of Israel were bringing up the ark of YHWH with shouting and with the sound of the horn.

And it was, as the ark of YHWH was coming into the City of David, that Michal daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and whirling before YHWH, and she despised him in her heart.
And they brought the ark of YHWH and set it in its place, in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it. And David offered up burnt offerings before YHWH, and peace offerings.
And David finished offering up the burnt offering and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of YHWH of hosts.
And he distributed to all the people, to the whole multitude of Israel, from man to woman, to each one cake of bread and one date-cake and one raisin-cake. And all the people went, each to his house.

And David returned to bless his household. And Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How the king of Israel has honoured himself today — who uncovered himself today before the eyes of his servants' maidservants, as one of the empty men shamelessly uncovers himself!"

And David said to Michal, "Before YHWH, who chose me rather than your father and rather than all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of YHWH, over Israel — and I will make music before YHWH!
"And I will be more lightly esteemed than this, and I will be lowly in my own eyes; but with the maidservants of whom you spoke, with them I shall be honoured."
And Michal daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.

2 samuel_7.t: And it was, when the king was dwelling in his house and YHWH had given him rest round about from all his enemies,
the king said to Nathan the prophet, "See now, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, and the ark of God is dwelling within the curtain."
