And Nathan said to the king, "All that is in your heart, go, do — for YHWH is with you."
And it was in that night, and the word of YHWH came to Nathan, saying,
"Go and say to my servant, to David: Thus says YHWH: Will you build me a house for me to dwell in?
"For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt until this day, but I have been going about in a tent and in a tabernacle.

"In all my going about among all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, Why have you not built me a house of cedar?"
"And now, thus you shall say to my servant, to David: Thus says YHWH of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people, over Israel.
"And I have been with you in all that you went, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you, and I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth.

"And I will appoint a place for my people, for Israel, and I will plant them, and they will dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more; and the sons of injustice will not afflict them again, as at the first,
"even from the day I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. And YHWH declares to you that YHWH will make you a house.
"When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will come out from your inward parts, and I will establish his kingdom.
"He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
"I will be a father to him and he will be a son to me — who, when he does wrong, I will reprove him with the rod of men and with the wounds of the sons of humankind.
"But my steadfast love will not depart from him, as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
"And your house and your kingdom will be established for ever before you; your throne will be established for ever."
According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
And King David went in and sat before YHWH and said, "Who am I, Lord YHWH, and who is my house, that you have brought me this far?
"And this was still a small thing in your eyes, Lord YHWH, and you have spoken also concerning the house of your servant for a long time to come. And this is the instruction of humankind, Lord YHWH.
"And what more can David say to you? For you know your servant, Lord YHWH.
"For the sake of your word and according to your own heart you have done all this greatness, to make your servant know it.
"Therefore you are great, Lord YHWH, for there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, in all that we have heard with our ears.

"And who is like your people, like Israel, one nation in the earth, whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, and to make himself a name, and to do for you the great things and awesome deeds for your land, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, nations and their gods?
"And you established for yourself your people Israel as a people for yourself for ever; and you, YHWH, became God for them.
"And now, YHWH God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house — establish it for ever, and do as you have spoken.
"And let your name be great for ever, so that it is said, 'YHWH of hosts is God over Israel', and let the house of your servant David be established before you.
"For you, YHWH of hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, 'I will build you a house.' Therefore your servant has found his heart to pray this prayer to you.
"And now, Lord YHWH, you are God, and your words are faithfulness, and you have spoken this good thing to your servant.

"And now, be willing and bless the house of your servant, that it may be before you for ever; for you, Lord YHWH, have spoken, and from your blessing may the house of your servant be blessed for ever."

2 samuel_8.t: And it was after this that David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.

And he struck Moab and measured them with the line, making them lie down on the ground; and he measured two lines to put to death and one full line to let live. And Moab became servants to David, bearers of tribute.
And David struck Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to restore his hand at the River Euphrates.
And David captured from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left of them a hundred chariots.
And Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck down among Aram twenty-two thousand men.
And David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and Aram became servants to David, bearers of tribute. And YHWH gave David victory wherever he went.
And David took the shields of gold that belonged to the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took very much bronze.
And Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer,

Toi sent Joram his son to King David to ask him of his welfare and to bless him, because he had waged war against Hadadezer and struck him — for Hadadezer had been a man of wars with Toi. And in his hand were vessels of silver and vessels of gold and vessels of bronze.
These also King David consecrated to YHWH, with the silver and the gold that he had consecrated from all the nations that he subdued —
from Aram and from Moab and from the sons of Ammon and from the Philistines and from Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
And David made a name when he returned from striking Aram in the Valley of Salt — eighteen thousand.
And he put garrisons in Edom — in all Edom he put garrisons — and all Edom became servants to David. And YHWH gave David victory wherever he went.
And David reigned over all Israel, and David was doing judgement and righteousness for all his people.
And Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was secretary;
and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were priests.

2 samuel_9.t: And David said, "Is there yet anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may do loyalty with him for Jonathan's sake?"
And the house of Saul had a servant, and his name was Ziba, and they summoned him to David. And the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "Your servant."
And the king said, "Is there no one still of the house of Saul, that I may do the loyalty of God with him?" And Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, stricken of feet."
And the king said to him, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
And King David sent and took him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
And Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came to David and fell on his face and bowed down. And David said, "Mephibosheth." And he said, "Here is your servant."

And David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for doing I will do loyalty with you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you shall eat bread at my table continually."
And he bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you have turned to the dead dog that I am?"
And the king summoned Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son.

"And you shall work the ground for him — you and your sons and your servants — and you shall bring in, and it shall be food for your master's son, and he shall eat it. But Mephibosheth your master's son shall eat bread at my table continually." And Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
And Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant will do." And Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.
And Mephibosheth had a young son, and his name was Mica. And all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
And Mephibosheth was dwelling in Jerusalem, for he was eating continually at the king's table. And he was lame in both his feet.

2 samuel_10.t: And it was after this that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

And David said, "I will do loyalty with Hanun son of Nahash, as his father did loyalty with me." And David sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And the servants of David came to the land of the sons of Ammon.

And the leaders of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Is David honouring your father in your eyes, that he has sent you comforters? Has David not sent his servants to you in order to explore the city and to spy on it and to overthrow it?"
And Hanun took the servants of David and shaved off half their beards and cut off their robes in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.
And they told David, and he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly humiliated. And the king said, "Remain at Jericho until your beards grow back, and then return."

And the sons of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, and the sons of Ammon sent and hired Aram of Beth-rehob and Aram of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah, a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.
And David heard, and he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.
And the sons of Ammon went out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the gate, while Aram of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.
And Joab saw that the face of the battle was against him from before and from behind, and he chose from all the chosen men of Israel and drew them up to meet Aram.
And the rest of the people he put into the hand of Abishai his brother, and he drew them up to meet the sons of Ammon.
And he said, "If Aram is too strong for me, then you shall be my deliverance; and if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to deliver you.
"Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And YHWH will do what is good in his eyes."
And Joab drew near, and the people who were with him, for the battle against Aram, and they fled before him.
And the sons of Ammon saw that Aram had fled, and they fled before Abishai and went into the city. And Joab returned from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
And Aram saw that it had been defeated before Israel, and they gathered themselves together.
And Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army before them.
And it was told to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. And Aram drew up to meet David, and they fought with him.
And Aram fled before Israel, and David killed of Aram seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen; and Shobach the commander of its army he struck down, and he died there.

And all the kings, the servants of Hadadezer, saw that they had been defeated before Israel, and they made peace with Israel and served them. And Aram was afraid to deliver the sons of Ammon any more.

2 samuel_11.t: And it was, at the turn of the year, at the time when the messengers go out, that David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they destroyed the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. And David was staying in Jerusalem.
And it was, at the time of evening, that David rose from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing. And the woman was very good of appearance.
And David sent and enquired about the woman, and one said, "Is this not Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
And David sent messengers and took her, and she came to him, and he lay with her — and she was consecrating herself from her uncleanness — and she returned to her house.
And the woman conceived, and she sent and told David and said, "I am pregnant."
And David sent to Joab, "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
And Uriah came to him, and David asked after the welfare of Joab and the welfare of the people and the welfare of the war.
And David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." And Uriah went out from the king's house, and the king's gift went out after him.
And Uriah lay down at the entrance of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.
And they told David, saying, "Uriah did not go down to his house." And David said to Uriah, "Have you not come from a journey? Why have you not gone down to your house?"

And Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in booths, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are camping on the open field. And shall I go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? By your life and by the life of your being, I will not do this thing."
And David said to Uriah, "Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you off." And Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the next.

And David summoned him, and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk. And in the evening he went out to lie down on his bed with the servants of his lord, and to his house he did not go down.
And it was in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
And he wrote in the letter, saying, "Set Uriah at the front of the fiercest fighting, and draw back from behind him, so that he is struck down and dies."
And it was, when Joab was watching the city, that he put Uriah at the place where he knew there were men of valour.
And the men of the city went out and fought with Joab, and some of the people, some of the servants of David, fell; and Uriah the Hittite also died.
And Joab sent and told David all the matters of the battle.
And he commanded the messenger, saying, "When you have finished speaking all the matters of the battle to the king,
"then, if the king's anger rises and he says to you, 'Why did you draw near to the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from on the wall?

"'Who struck down Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman throw an upper millstone on him from on the wall, and he died at Thebez? Why did you draw near to the wall?' — then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.'"
And the messenger went and came and told David all that Joab had sent him with.
And the messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us and came out to us into the open field, and we were on them as far as the entrance of the gate.
"And the archers shot at your servants from on the wall, and some of the king's servants died. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead."

And David said to the messenger, "Thus you shall say to Joab: 'Do not let this thing be evil in your eyes, for the sword devours now this one and now that one. Press your battle against the city and tear it down.' And encourage him."
And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, and she mourned over her lord.
And the mourning passed, and David sent and gathered her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. And the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of YHWH.

2 samuel_12.t: And YHWH sent Nathan to David. And he came to him and said to him, "Two men were in one city, one rich and one poor.
"The rich man had very many flocks and herds.

"But the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb that he had bought. And he kept it alive, and it grew up together with him and with his children: from his morsel it would eat, and from his cup it would drink, and in his bosom it would lie, and it was to him like a daughter.

"And a traveller came to the rich man, and he spared to take from his own flock and from his own herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him; and he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
And David's anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As YHWH lives, the man who did this is a son of death!
"And he shall restore the ewe lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity."
And Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says YHWH, God of Israel: I anointed you as king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul,

"and I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if that were too little, I would add to you this much and this much again.

"Why have you despised the word of YHWH, to do what is evil in my eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck down with the sword, and his wife you took for yourself as a wife, and him you killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon.
"And now, the sword will not depart from your house for ever, because you despised me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to become your wife.

"Thus says YHWH: Behold, I am raising up evil against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbour, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
"For you acted in secret, and I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun."
And David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against YHWH." And Nathan said to David, "YHWH also has passed over your sin; you will not die.
"Nevertheless, because by this thing you have utterly scorned the enemies of YHWH, the son also who is born to you shall surely die."
And Nathan went to his house. And YHWH struck the child that the wife of Uriah had borne to David, and it became sick.
And David sought God for the boy, and David fasted a fast, and he went in and spent the night and lay on the ground.
And the elders of his house stood over him to raise him from the ground, but he was not willing, and he did not eat food with them.

And it was on the seventh day that the child died. And the servants of David were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "Behold, while the child was alive we spoke to him and he did not listen to our voice; and how shall we say to him, 'The child is dead'? He may do harm."
And David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, and David understood that the child was dead. And David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."

And David rose from the ground and washed and anointed himself and changed his garments, and he came into the house of YHWH and bowed down. And he came to his own house and asked, and they set food before him and he ate.
And his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? For the child's sake, while he was alive, you fasted and wept; and when the child died, you rose and ate food."
And he said, "While the child was still alive I fasted and wept, for I said, 'Who knows? YHWH may show me favour, and the child may live.'
"But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I am going to him, and he will not return to me."
And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and he went in to her and lay with her. And she bore a son, and she called his name Solomon. And YHWH loved him,
and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, for the sake of YHWH.
And Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon and captured the royal city.
And Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah; I have also captured the city of waters.
"And now gather the rest of the people and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture the city myself and my name be called over it."
And David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and he fought against it and captured it.

And he took the crown of their king from off his head — and its weight was a talent of gold, and there was a precious stone in it — and it came onto David's head. And he brought out the plunder of the city, very much.

And the people who were in it he brought out and set at the saws and at the iron picks and at the iron axes, and he made them pass through the brick mould. And so he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

2 samuel_13.t: And it was after this: Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister, and her name was Tamar; and Amnon son of David loved her.
And it was distress to Amnon, to the point of making himself ill, over Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin; and it was impossible in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
And Amnon had a friend, and his name was Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
And he said to him, "Why are you so weak, son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother — I love her."

And Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and make yourself ill. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Let Tamar my sister come, please, and give me food to eat; and let her prepare the food before my eyes, so that I may see it and eat from her hand.'"

And Amnon lay down and made himself ill. And the king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, "Let Tamar my sister come, please, and make two cakes before my eyes, so that I may eat from her hand."
And David sent to Tamar at the house, saying, "Go, please, to the house of Amnon your brother, and make the food for him."
And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And she took the dough and kneaded it and made cakes before his eyes, and she cooked the cakes.
And she took the pan and poured out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Send everyone out from me!" And everyone went out from him.
And Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the chamber, so that I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the cakes that she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother, into the chamber.
And she brought them near to him to eat, and he took hold of her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
And she said to him, "No, my brother! Do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this outrage.
"And I — where would I carry my reproach? And you, you would be like one of the fools in Israel. And now, speak, please, to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
And he was not willing to listen to her voice, and he was stronger than she, and he violated her and lay with her.
And Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up, go."
And she said to him, "No! This great evil — sending me away — is worse than the other that you did to me." But he was not willing to listen to her.
And he summoned his young man who served him and said, "Send this one away from me, outside, and bolt the door after her."
And on her was a tunic of palms and soles, for so the daughters of the king, the virgins, wore robes. And his servant brought her outside and bolted the door after her.
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and the tunic of palms and soles that was on her she tore, and she put her hand on her head and went away, going and crying out.

And Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? And now, my sister, be silent. He is your brother. Do not set your heart to this matter." And Tamar remained, and desolate, in the house of Absalom her brother.
And King David heard all these things, and it burned in him greatly.
And Absalom did not speak with Amnon either bad or good, for Absalom hated Amnon over the matter that he had violated Tamar his sister.
And it was, after two full years, that Absalom had shearers at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the sons of the king.
And Absalom came to the king and said, "Behold now, your servant has shearers. Let the king and his servants go, please, with your servant."
And the king said to Absalom, "No, my son. Let us not all go, please, and be a burden on you." And he urged him, but he was not willing to go, and he blessed him.
And Absalom said, "If not, let Amnon my brother go, please, with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
And Absalom urged him, and he sent with him Amnon and all the sons of the king.

And Absalom commanded his young men, saying, "See now, when Amnon's heart is merry with wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then you shall put him to death. Do not be afraid. Have I not myself commanded you? Be strong and become sons of valour."
And Absalom's young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. And all the sons of the king rose, and each mounted his mule, and they fled.
And it was, while they were on the road, that the report came to David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king, and not one of them is left."
And the king rose and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants were standing with garments torn.

And Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered and said, "Let not my lord say that they have put to death all the young men, the sons of the king; for Amnon alone is dead. For by Absalom's own mouth it has been determined from the day he violated Tamar his sister.
"And now let not my lord the king set to his heart a word, saying, 'All the sons of the king are dead' — for Amnon alone is dead."
And Absalom fled. And the young man on watch lifted his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming from the road behind him, from the side of the mountain.
And Jonadab said to the king, "Behold, the sons of the king have come. According to the word of your servant, so it has happened."
And it was, when he had finished speaking, that behold, the sons of the king came, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the king also, and all his servants, wept a very great weeping.
And Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And he mourned for his son all the days.
And Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
And David the king ceased from going out against Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, that he was dead.

2 samuel_14.t: And Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart was toward Absalom.

And Joab sent to Tekoa and took from there a wise woman, and he said to her, "Play the mourner, please, and put on mourning garments, and do not anoint yourself with oil, and be like a woman who has been mourning many days for a dead man.
"And you shall go to the king and speak to him according to this word." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
And the woman of Tekoa said to the king, and she fell on her face to the ground and bowed down, and she said, "Save, O king!"
And the king said to her, "What is it with you?" And she said, "Truly I am a widow woman, and my husband is dead.
"And your maidservant had two sons, and the two of them struggled together in the field, and there was no one to deliver between them; and the one struck the other and killed him.

"And behold, the whole clan has risen against your maidservant, and they have said, 'Give up the one who struck down his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and we will destroy the heir also' — and so they would quench my coal that is left, so as to leave my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the ground."
And the king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give command concerning you."
And the woman of Tekoa said to the king, "On me, my lord the king, be the iniquity, and on my father's house; and let the king and his throne be innocent."
And the king said, "Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he will not touch you again."

And she said, "Let the king remember, please, YHWH your God, that the avenger of blood may not multiply destruction, and that they may not destroy my son." And he said, "As YHWH lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
And the woman said, "Let your maidservant speak, please, a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."

And the woman said, "And why have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is like one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring back his own banished one.

"For we shall surely die, and we are like water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up. And God does not take away a life, but he devises plans so that the banished one may not remain banished from him.

"And now, that I have come to speak this word to the king my lord — it is because the people made me afraid. And your maidservant said, 'Let me speak, please, to the king; perhaps the king will do the word of his servant.
"'For the king will hear, to deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy both me and my son together from the inheritance of God.'
"And your maidservant said, 'Let the word of my lord the king be for rest, for like the messenger of God, so is my lord the king, to hear the good and the bad.' And may YHWH your God be with you."
And the king answered and said to the woman, "Do not hide from me, please, a thing that I am asking you." And the woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

And the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman answered and said, "As your being lives, my lord the king, there is no turning to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken. For your servant Joab — he commanded me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your maidservant.
"In order to change the face of the matter your servant Joab did this thing. And my lord is wise, like the wisdom of the messenger of God, to know all that is in the land."
And the king said to Joab, "Behold now, I have done this thing. Go, bring back the young man, Absalom."

And Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed down and blessed the king, and Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favour in your eyes, my lord the king, in that the king has done the word of his servant."
And Joab rose and went to Geshur, and he brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
And the king said, "Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face." And Absalom turned to his own house, and the face of the king he did not see.
And like Absalom there was no man so beautiful in all Israel, to be praised greatly: from the sole of his foot to his crown there was no blemish in him.

And when he shaved his head — and it was at the end of days, from time to time, that he would shave it, for it was heavy on him, and so he shaved it — he would weigh the hair of his head, two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
And three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, and her name was Tamar. She was a woman beautiful of appearance.
And Absalom dwelt in Jerusalem two full years, and the face of the king he did not see.
And Absalom sent to Joab, to send him to the king, but he was not willing to come to him. And he sent again a second time, but he was not willing to come.
And he said to his servants, "See, Joab's portion of land is beside mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." And Absalom's servants set the portion of land on fire.
And Joab rose and came to Absalom at the house and said to him, "Why have your servants set my portion of land on fire?"

And Absalom said to Joab, "Behold, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, so that I may send you to the king to say, Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be still there.' And now let me see the face of the king; and if there is iniquity in me, let him put me to death."
And Joab came to the king and told him. And he summoned Absalom, and he came to the king and bowed down to him on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.

2 samuel_15.t: And it was after this that Absalom acquired for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men running before him.

And Absalom would rise early and stand beside the way of the gate. And it was, when any man had a dispute to come to the king for judgement, that Absalom would call to him and say, "From what city are you?" And he would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
And Absalom would say to him, "See, your case is good and right, but there is no one from the king to hear you."
And Absalom would say, "Who would make me a judge in the land, that every man who has a case or a judgement might come to me, and I would give him justice!"
And it was, when a man drew near to bow down to him, that he would put out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.
And Absalom did according to this manner to all Israel who came for judgement to the king. And Absalom stole the heart of the men of Israel.
And it was at the end of forty years that Absalom said to the king, "Let me go, please, and pay my vow that I vowed to YHWH in Hebron.
"For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelt at Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If YHWH will surely bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve YHWH.'"
And the king said to him, "Go in peace." And he rose and went to Hebron.
And Absalom sent scouts through all the tribes of Israel, saying, "When you hear the sound of the horn, then you shall say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron.'"
And with Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem, invited and going in their innocence; and they did not know anything.

And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, from his city, from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong, and the people with Absalom went on increasing.
And the messenger came to David, saying, "The heart of the men of Israel is after Absalom."

And David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Rise and let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from before Absalom. Hurry to go, lest he hurry and overtake us and thrust disaster upon us and strike the city with the mouth of the sword."
And the king's servants said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king chooses — behold, your servants."
And the king went out, and all his household at his feet; and the king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.
And the king went out, and all the people at his feet, and they halted at the far house.

And all his servants were passing by at his side, and all the Kerethites and all the Pelethites; and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come at his foot from Gath, were passing on before the face of the king.
And the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you also go with us? Return and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.

"Yesterday was your coming, and today should I make you wander with us in going, when I am going wherever I am going? Return, and take your brothers back with you. Loyalty and faithfulness be with you."
And Ittai answered the king and said, "As YHWH lives and as my lord the king lives, in whatever place my lord the king is — whether for death or for life — there your servant will be."
And David said to Ittai, "Go and pass on." And Ittai the Gittite passed on, and all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
And all the land was weeping with a loud voice as all the people passed by; and the king was crossing the Wadi Kidron, and all the people were passing on toward the way of the wilderness.

And behold, Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
And the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back to the city. If I find favour in the eyes of YHWH, he will bring me back and let me see it and its habitation.
"And if he says thus, 'I have no delight in you' — here I am; let him do to me as is good in his eyes."
And the king said to Zadok the priest, "Are you a seer? Return to the city in peace, and Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons, with you.
"See, I will delay at the desert plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to tell me."
And Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.

And David was going up the ascent of the olive trees, going up and weeping, and his head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered each his head, and they went up, going up and weeping.
And someone told David, saying, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "Make foolish, please, the counsel of Ahithophel, YHWH."
And it was, when David came to the top, where he would bow down to God, that behold, Hushai the Arkite came to meet him, his tunic torn and earth on his head.
And David said to him, "If you pass over with me, you will become a burden to me.
"But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I am your servant, O king; I was your father's servant then, and now I am your servant' — then you will frustrate for me the counsel of Ahithophel.
"And are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests with you there? And it shall be that every word you hear from the king's house you shall tell to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests.
"Behold, their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz for Zadok and Jonathan for Abiathar, and by their hand you shall send to me every word that you hear."
And Hushai, David's friend, came to the city; and Absalom was coming to Jerusalem.

2 samuel_16.t: And David had passed on a little beyond the top, and behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him, with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves of bread and a hundred bunches of raisins and a hundred of summer fruit and a skin of wine.

And the king said to Ziba, "What are these to you?" And Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride, and the bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for the weary in the wilderness to drink."

And the king said, "And where is your master's son?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"
And the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that belonged to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down. May I find favour in your eyes, my lord the king."
And King David came as far as Bahurim, and behold, from there a man was coming out from the clan of the house of Saul, and his name was Shimei son of Gera; he came out, coming out and cursing.
And he stoned David with stones, and all the servants of King David — and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left.
And thus said Shimei in his cursing: "Get out, get out, man of blood, man of worthlessness!

"YHWH has brought back upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned; and YHWH has given the kingship into the hand of Absalom your son. And here you are in your own calamity, for you are a man of blood."
And Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me pass over, please, and take off his head."
And the king said, "What is it to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah? So let him curse; for YHWH has said to him, 'Curse David.' And who shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"

And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Behold, my son, who came out from my own inward parts, is seeking my life; how much more now this Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for YHWH has spoken to him.
"Perhaps YHWH will look upon my eye, and YHWH will repay me good in place of his cursing this day."
And David and his men went on the road, and Shimei was going along the side of the mountain opposite him, going and cursing; and he stoned with stones opposite him and threw dust.
And the king came, and all the people who were with him, exhausted; and he refreshed himself there.
And Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
And it was, when Hushai the Arkite, David's friend, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
And Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
And Hushai said to Absalom, "No; but the one whom YHWH and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen — his I will be, and with him I will remain.
"And a second thing: whom should I serve? Should it not be before his son? As I served before your father, so I will be before you."
And Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel: what shall we do?"

And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house; and all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strong."
And they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines before the eyes of all Israel.
And the counsel of Ahithophel that he counselled in those days was as when a man enquires of the word of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.

2 samuel_17.t: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose, please, twelve thousand men, and let me rise and pursue after David tonight.
"And I will come upon him while he is weary and slack of hands, and I will terrify him, and all the people who are with him will flee; and I will strike down the king alone.
"And I will bring all the people back to you. As the whole returns — the man whom you are seeking — all the people will be at peace."
And the word was right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
And Absalom said, "Call, please, also for Hushai the Arkite, and let us hear what is in his mouth, his also."
And Hushai came to Absalom, and Absalom said to him, saying, "According to this word Ahithophel has spoken. Shall we do his word? If not, you speak."
And Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel that Ahithophel has counselled is not good this time."

And Hushai said, "You know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are bitter of being, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the open country. And your father is a man of war, and he will not spend the night with the people.

"Behold, now he is hidden in one of the ravines or in one of the places; and it will be, when some of them fall at the first, that whoever hears will hear and say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'
"And even the man who is a son of valour, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will surely melt; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and that those with him are sons of valour.
"But I counsel that all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude, and that you yourself go into the battle.

"And we will come upon him in one of the places where he is found, and we will settle on him as the dew falls on the ground; and there will not be left of him and of all the men who are with him even one.
"And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it to the wadi until not even a pebble is found there."

And Absalom and every man of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Arkite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For YHWH had commanded to frustrate the good counsel of Ahithophel, in order that YHWH might bring disaster upon Absalom.
And Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, "Thus and thus Ahithophel counselled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I have counselled.

"And now send quickly and tell David, saying, 'Do not spend the night at the desert plains of the wilderness, but surely cross over, lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people who are with him.'"
And Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, and the maidservant would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David; for they could not be seen coming into the city.
But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them went quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, and he had a well in his courtyard, and they went down there.
And the woman took and spread the covering over the face of the well and spread out grain on it; and nothing was known.

And Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have crossed over the brook of water." And they searched and did not find them, and they returned to Jerusalem.

And it was, after they had gone, that they came up out of the well and went and told King David. And they said to David, "Rise and cross over the water quickly, for thus Ahithophel has counselled against you."
And David rose, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By the light of the morning not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.

And Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been done, and he saddled the donkey and rose and went to his house, to his city, and gave orders concerning his household, and hanged himself; and he died and was buried in the tomb of his father.
And David had come to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.

And Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. And Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Jether the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
And it was, when David came to Mahanaim, that Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,
brought bedding and basins and potter's vessels, and wheat and barley and flour and roasted grain, and beans and lentils and roasted grain,

and honey and curds and sheep and cheese of the herd. They brought them near to David and to the people who were with him, to eat; for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."

2 samuel_18.t: And David mustered the people who were with him, and he set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

And David sent out the people, a third under the hand of Joab, and a third under the hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "Going out I will go out with you also, I myself."

But the people said, "You shall not go out. For if we flee, they will not set their heart on us; and if half of us die, they will not set their heart on us. For you are now like ten thousand of us. And now it is better that you be for us a help from the city."
And the king said to them, "What is good in your eyes I will do." And the king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man, with Absalom." And all the people heard when the king commanded all the commanders concerning Absalom.
And the people went out into the open country to meet Israel, and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.
And the people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and the slaughter there was great on that day — twenty thousand.
And the battle there was scattered over the face of all the land, and the forest consumed more of the people that day than the sword consumed.

And Absalom happened to meet the servants of David. And Absalom was riding on the mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of the great oak, and his head caught fast in the oak, and he was put between the heavens and the earth, and the mule that was under him passed on.
And a certain man saw it and told Joab and said, "Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in the oak."
And Joab said to the man who told him, "And behold, you saw! And why did you not strike him there to the ground? And it would have been on me to give you ten pieces of silver and one belt."

And the man said to Joab, "Even if I were weighing out a thousand pieces of silver on my palms, I would not put out my hand against the son of the king; for in our ears the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Whoever you are, protect the young man, Absalom.'
"Or if I had dealt falsely against my own life — and nothing is hidden from the king — then you yourself would have stood aloof."
And Joab said, "Not so! I will not wait before you." And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom, while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.
And ten young men, bearers of Joab's weapons, surrounded him and struck Absalom and killed him.
And Joab blew on the horn, and the people turned back from pursuing after Israel, for Joab restrained the people.
And they took Absalom and threw him into the great pit in the forest, and they raised over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each to his tents.

And Absalom, in his lifetime, had taken and set up for himself the pillar that is in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to cause my name to be remembered." And he called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.
And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run, please, and bear the news to the king, that YHWH has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies."
And Joab said to him, "You are not a man of news this day. You may bear news on another day, but this day you shall not bear news, because the king's son is dead."
And Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." And the Cushite bowed down to Joab and ran.

And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said again to Joab, "Come what may, let me also run, please, after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why is it that you would run, my son, when you have no news that will find you a reward?"
"Come what may, I will run." And he said to him, "Run." And Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and passed the Cushite.
And David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went to the roof of the gate, to the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man running alone.
And the watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, there is news in his mouth." And he came on, coming and drawing near.
And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, "Behold, another man running alone." And the king said, "This one also is bearing news."
And the watchman said, "I see the running of the first as the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok." And the king said, "This is a good man, and he comes with good news."

And Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, "Peace!" And he bowed down to the king with his face to the ground and said, "Blessed be YHWH your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted their hand against my lord the king."
And the king said, "Is there peace for the young man, for Absalom?" And Ahimaaz said, "I saw the great commotion when the king's servant Joab sent your servant, and I do not know what it was."
And the king said, "Turn aside and stand here." And he turned aside and stood.
And behold, the Cushite came, and the Cushite said, "Let my lord the king receive the news, for YHWH has vindicated you this day from the hand of all who rose up against you."

And the king said to the Cushite, "Is there peace for the young man, for Absalom?" And the Cushite said, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who have risen against you for harm, be like the young man."

And the king was shaken, and he went up to the upper room of the gate and wept. And thus he said as he went: "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died, I in your place! Absalom, my son, my son!"

2 samuel_19.t: And it was told to Joab, "Behold, the king is weeping and mourning over Absalom."
And the deliverance on that day became mourning for all the people, for the people heard on that day, "The king is grieved over his son."
And the people stole into the city on that day, as people steal in who are ashamed when they flee in battle.
And the king covered his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

And Joab came to the king at the house and said, "You have put to shame today the faces of all your servants, who this day saved your life, and the life of your sons and your daughters, and the life of your wives and the life of your concubines,

"by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For you have made known today that commanders and servants are nothing to you; for I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us today were dead, then it would be right in your eyes.

"And now rise, go out and speak to the heart of your servants. For I swear by YHWH that if you do not go out, not a man will lodge with you tonight; and this will be worse for you than all the harm that has come upon you from your youth until now."

And the king rose and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, saying, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." And all the people came before the king. And Israel had fled, each to his tents.

And all the people were quarrelling throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies, and he rescued us from the hand of the Philistines; and now he has fled from the land because of Absalom.
"And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in the battle. And now, why are you silent about bringing back the king?"

And King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why should you be the last to bring back the king to his house?' — and the word of all Israel had come to the king, to his house.
"You are my brothers, you are my bone and my flesh. And why should you be the last to bring back the king?"
"And to Amasa you shall say, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? So may God do to me and so may he add, if you shall not be commander of the army before me all the days, in place of Joab.'"
And he turned the heart of every man of Judah as one man, and they sent to the king, "Return, you and all your servants."
And the king returned and came to the Jordan; and Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.
And Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite who was from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
And a thousand men from Benjamin were with him; and Ziba, the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him. And they rushed to the Jordan before the king.
And the ford crossed over to bring over the king's household and to do what was good in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell before the king as he was crossing the Jordan,

and he said to the king, "Let my lord not reckon guilt to me, and do not remember what your servant did perversely on the day my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
"For your servant knows that I have sinned; and behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down to meet my lord the king."
And Abishai son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of YHWH?"

And David said, "What is it to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should become an opponent to me today? Shall anyone be put to death in Israel today? For do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"
And the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king swore to him.
And Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king. And he had not dressed his feet nor trimmed his moustache nor washed his clothes, from the day the king went until the day he came in peace.
And it was, when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
And he said, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, 'Let me saddle the donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go with the king' — for your servant is lame.
"And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like the messenger of God; so do what is good in your eyes.
"For all my father's house were nothing but men of death to my lord the king; yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. And what right have I still, to cry out further to the king?"
And the king said to him, "Why do you speak any more of your affairs? I have said: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take the whole, now that my lord the king has come in peace to his house."
And Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim, and he crossed the Jordan with the king to send him off at the Jordan.
And Barzillai was very old, a son of eighty years, and he had supplied the king while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.
And the king said to Barzillai, "You cross over with me, and I will supply you with me in Jerusalem."
And Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

"I am a son of eighty years today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat and what I drink? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? And why should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?
"Your servant would cross the Jordan with the king only a little way. And why should the king reward me with this reward?

"Let your servant return, please, and let me die in my own city, near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Kimham: let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your eyes."
And the king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes; and all that you choose from me I will do for you."
And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed over. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.
And the king crossed over to Gilgal, and Kimham crossed over with him. And all the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.

And behold, all the men of Israel were coming to the king, and they said to the king, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and brought the king and his household over the Jordan, and all David's men with him?"

And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is near to me. And why is it that this has angered you? Have we eaten at all at the king's expense, or has anything been taken away for us?"

And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, "I have ten shares in the king, and in David also I am more than you. And why have you treated me with contempt? Was not my word first, to bring back my king?" And the word of the men of Judah was harder than the word of the men of Israel.

2 samuel_20.t: And there a worthless man happened to be, and his name was Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. And he blew on the horn and said, "We have no portion in David, and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each to his tents, O Israel!"
And every man of Israel went up from after David, after Sheba son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clung to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

And David came to his house at Jerusalem, and the king took the ten women, concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a house of confinement; and he provided for them, but he did not go in to them. And they were shut up until the day of their death, in living widowhood.
And the king said to Amasa, "Summon for me the men of Judah within three days, and you yourself stand here."
And Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the appointed time that he had appointed for him.

And David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. You take your master's servants and pursue after him, lest he find for himself fortified cities and tear out our eye."
And Joab's men went out after him, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites and all the mighty men; and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.

They were by the great stone that is in Gibeon, and Amasa came before them. And Joab was girded with his robe as his clothing, and over it a belt with a sword fastened on his loins in its sheath; and he went forward, and it fell out.
And Joab said to Amasa, "Is it peace with you, my brother?" And Joab's right hand took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.

And Amasa did not take heed of the sword that was in Joab's hand, and he struck him with it in the belly and poured out his bowels to the ground; and he did not repeat it to him, and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba son of Bichri.
And a man stood over him, one of Joab's young men, and said, "Whoever delights in Joab, and whoever is for David — after Joab!"

And Amasa was wallowing in the blood in the middle of the highway. And the man saw that all the people stopped, and he moved Amasa from the highway to the field and threw a garment over him, since he saw that everyone who came upon him stopped.
When he had been removed from the highway, every man passed on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.
And he passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-maacah and all the Berites; and they assembled and also went after him.

And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah, and they poured out a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart. And all the people who were with Joab were battering to bring down the wall.
And a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Say, please, to Joab, 'Draw near here, that I may speak to you.'"
And he drew near to her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" And he said, "I am." And she said to him, "Listen to the words of your maidservant." And he said, "I am listening."
And she said, "They used to speak in former times, saying, 'Let them surely ask at Abel', and so they settled the matter.
"I am of the peaceable and faithful of Israel. You are seeking to put to death a city and a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the inheritance of YHWH?"
And Joab answered and said, "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy!

"The matter is not so; but a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri is his name, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Give him alone, and I will go away from the city." And the woman said to Joab, "Behold, his head will be thrown to you over the wall."

And the woman went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. And he blew on the horn, and they scattered from the city, each to his tents. And Joab returned to Jerusalem, to the king.
And Joab was over all the army of Israel; and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and over the Pelethites;
and Adoram was over the forced labour; and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
and Sheva was secretary; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
and Ira the Jairite also was priest to David.

2 samuel_21.t: And there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year, and David sought the face of YHWH. And YHWH said, "It is because of Saul and because of the house of blood, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

And the king summoned the Gibeonites and said to them — now the Gibeonites were not of the sons of Israel but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the sons of Israel had sworn an oath to them, and Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah —
and David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, that you may bless the inheritance of YHWH?"

And the Gibeonites said to him, "It is not a matter of silver and gold for us with Saul and with his house, and it is not for us to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "What you say I will do for you."
And they said to the king, "The man who made an end of us and who planned against us that we should be destroyed from standing in all the territory of Israel —
"let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we will impale them before YHWH at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of YHWH." And the king said, "I will give them."
And the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul, because of the oath of YHWH that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

And the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul — Armoni and Mephibosheth — and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite,

and he gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they impaled them on the mountain before YHWH. And the seven of them fell together; and they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

And Rizpah daughter of Aiah took the sackcloth and spread it out for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured out on them from the heavens. And she did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
And it was told to David what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done.

And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the open square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them up on the day the Philistines struck down Saul on Gilboa.
And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of the impaled men.

And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father; and they did all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.
And there was war again for the Philistines with Israel, and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought with the Philistines; and David was weary.
And Ishbi-benob, who was among those born of the Raphah — and the weight of his spear was three hundred in weight of bronze, and he was girded with a new sword — he said he would strike David down.

But Abishai son of Zeruiah helped him and struck the Philistine down and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, "You shall not go out with us to battle any more, and you shall not quench the lamp of Israel."
And it was after this that there was war again at Gob with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was among those born of the Raphah.
And there was war again at Gob with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, the wood of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

And there was war again at Gath, and there was a man of great stature, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number; and he also was born to the Raphah.
And he taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimei, David's brother, struck him down.
These four were born to the Raphah in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

2 samuel_22.t: And David spoke to YHWH the words of this song on the day YHWH delivered him from the palm of all his enemies and from the palm of Saul.
And he said: YHWH is my rock and my stronghold, and my deliverer, mine;
God of my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my fastness and my place of escape, my saviour — from violence you save me.
The one to be praised — I call upon YHWH, and from my enemies I am saved.
For the breakers of death surrounded me, the torrents of worthlessness overwhelmed me;
the cords of Sheol surrounded me, the snares of death confronted me.
In my distress I called upon YHWH, and to my God I called; and he heard my voice from his temple, and my cry for help was in his ears.
And the earth shook and quaked, the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, because he was angry.
Smoke went up in his nostrils, and fire from his mouth consumed; coals burned from him.
And he stretched out the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.
And he rode on a cherub and flew, and he appeared on the wings of the wind.
And he put darkness around him as shelters, a sieve of waters, dark clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before him coals of fire burned.
YHWH thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.
And he sent out arrows and scattered them, lightning, and routed them.
And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were uncovered, at the rebuke of YHWH, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He reached from on high, he took me, he drew me out of many waters.
He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hate me, for they were too strong for me.
They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but YHWH was a support to me.
And he brought me out to a broad place; he rescued me, for he delighted in me.
YHWH dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the purity of my hands he repaid me.
For I have kept the ways of YHWH, and have not acted wickedly away from my God.
For all his judgements are before me, and his statutes — I do not turn aside from it.
And I was blameless toward him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
And YHWH repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my purity before his eyes.
With the loyal you show yourself loyal, with the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless;
with the pure you show yourself pure, and with the crooked you show yourself twisted.
And an afflicted people you save, but your eyes are on the haughty — you bring them low.
For you are my lamp, YHWH, and YHWH lightens my darkness.
For by you I run at a raiding band, by my God I leap a wall.
The God — his way is blameless, the speech of YHWH is refined; he is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
For who is God apart from YHWH, and who is a Rock apart from our God?
The God is my strong refuge, and he set free my way, blameless.
making my feet like the does, and on my high places he makes me stand.
training my hands for battle, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
And you gave me the shield of your salvation, and your answering makes me great.
You enlarge my step under me, and my ankles do not slip.
Let me pursue my enemies, and I destroyed them, and I did not turn back until they were finished.
And I finished them and shattered them, and they did not rise; and they fell under my feet.
And you girded me with strength for battle; you made those who rose against me bow down under me.
And my enemies — you gave me their neck; those who hate me — and I destroyed them.
They looked, and there was no deliverer; to YHWH, and he did not answer them.
And I beat them fine as the dust of the earth; like the mud of the streets I crushed them, I stamped them out.
And you rescued me from the strifes of my people; you kept me as head of nations — a people I did not know serves me.
Sons of foreignness cringe to me; at the hearing of the ear they obey me.
Sons of foreignness wither, and they gird themselves out of their strongholds.
YHWH lives, and blessed be my Rock, and exalted be the God of the Rock of my salvation —
the God who gives me vengeance and brings peoples down under me,
and who brings me out from my enemies. And from those who rise against me you lift me up; from the man of violence you rescue me.
Therefore I will give you thanks, YHWH, among the nations, and to your name I will make music —
a tower of salvation for his king, and doing steadfast love for his anointed, for David and for his offspring for ever.

2 samuel_23.t: And these are the last words of David: The declaration of David son of Jesse, and the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the pleasant one of the songs of Israel.
The spirit of YHWH has spoken by me, and his word is on my tongue.
The God of Israel said, to me the Rock of Israel spoke: One ruling over humankind, righteous, ruling in the fear of God —
and like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds; from brightness, from rain, grass from the earth.
For is not my house so with God? For a perpetual covenant he has made with me, ordered in every part and kept. For all my salvation and every desire — will he not make it grow?
But worthlessness — like a thorn chased away are they all, for not by hand are they taken;
and the man who touches them arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear; and with fire they are utterly burned where they sit.
These are the names of the mighty men who belonged to David: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the three; he was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.
And after him was Eleazar son of Dodo son of Ahohi, one of the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle; and the men of Israel had gone up.

He rose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary and his hand clung to the sword. And YHWH brought about a great deliverance on that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.

And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered into a band, and there was a portion of the field full of lentils, and the people fled from before the Philistines.
But he took his stand in the middle of the portion and delivered it, and struck the Philistines. And YHWH brought about a great deliverance.
And three of the thirty chiefs went down and came at harvest time to David, to the cave of Adullam; and a company of Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
And David was then in the stronghold, and a garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.
And David craved and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is at the gate?"

And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem, which was at the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. But he was not willing to drink it, and he poured it out to YHWH.

And he said, "Far be it from me, YHWH, that I should do this! Is it the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" And he was not willing to drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
And Abishai the brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah — he was chief of the three, and he wielded his spear against three hundred slain; and he had a name among the three.
Was he not the most honoured of the three? And he became their commander; but to the three he did not come.

And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man, great in deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck down the two ariels of Moab; and he went down and struck down the lion inside the pit on the day of the snow.

And he struck down an Egyptian man, a man of appearance; and in the Egyptian's hand was a spear, but he went down to him with a staff and seized the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
He was honoured above the thirty, but to the three he did not come. And David set him over his bodyguard.
Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite;
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite;
Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite;
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite;
Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin;
Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Gaash;
Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite;
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Ararite;
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai son of the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite;
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite;
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armour-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite — thirty-seven in all.

2 samuel_24.t: And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel again, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."

And the king said to Joab the commander of the army who was with him, "Go about, please, through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and enrol the people, that I may know the number of the people."

And Joab said to the king, "May YHWH your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king are seeing it. But my lord the king — why does he delight in this thing?"
But the word of the king prevailed over Joab and over the commanders of the army, and Joab and the commanders of the army went out from before the king to enrol the people, Israel.
And they crossed the Jordan and encamped at Aroer, south of the city that is in the middle of the wadi of Gad, and on to Jazer.
And they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan-jaan and round to Sidon.
And they came to the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites; and they went out to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
And they went about through all the land, and they came at the end of nine months and twenty days to Jerusalem.
And Joab gave the number of the muster of the people to the king. And Israel was eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

And David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. And David said to YHWH, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, YHWH, take away, please, the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
And David rose in the morning, and the word of YHWH came to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,
"Go and speak to David: Thus says YHWH: Three things I am laying upon you. Choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you."

And Gad came to David and told him and said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or three months of your fleeing before your foes while he pursues you? Or three days of pestilence in your land? Now know and see what word I shall bring back to the one who sent me."
And David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall, please, into the hand of YHWH, for his compassions are many; but into the hand of humankind let me not fall."
And YHWH gave a pestilence in Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and of the people from Dan to Beersheba seventy thousand men died.

And the messenger stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, and YHWH relented concerning the harm and said to the messenger who was destroying among the people, "Enough! Now let your hand drop." And the messenger of YHWH was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

And David said to YHWH when he saw the messenger who was striking the people, and he said, "Behold, I have sinned and I have done wrong; but these sheep — what have they done? Let your hand, please, be against me and against my father's house."
