And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, "Go up, raise an altar to YHWH on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
And David went up according to the word of Gad, just as YHWH had commanded.
And Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants passing over toward him, and Araunah went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
And Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" And David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to YHWH, that the plague may be restrained from the people."
And Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what is good in his eyes. See, the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the gear of the oxen for the wood."
"The whole Araunah the king gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May YHWH your God accept you favourably."

And the king said to Araunah, "No, but buying I will buy it from you for a price; and I will not offer up to YHWH my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." And David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And David built there an altar to YHWH and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings. And YHWH was entreated for the land, and the plague was restrained from Israel.

amos_1.t: The words of Amos, who was among the sheep-breeders from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
And he said: YHWH roars from Zion, and from Jerusalem he gives his voice, and the pastures of the shepherds dry up, and the top of Carmel withers.
Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.
And I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben Hadad.

And I will break the bar of Damascus, and I will cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, and the holder of a sceptre from Beth Eden, and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says YHWH.
Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried into exile a complete exile, to deliver them up to Edom.
And I will send fire into the wall of Gaza, and it will consume her fortresses.
And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and the holder of a sceptre from Ashkelon, and I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says Lord YHWH.
Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they delivered up a complete exile to Edom, and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
And I will send fire into the wall of Tyre, and it will consume her fortresses.

Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and ruined his compassions, and his anger tore for ever, and his fury he kept perpetually.
And I will send fire into Teman, and it will consume the fortresses of Bozrah.
Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of the people of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead, so as to enlarge their territory.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will consume her fortresses, with a shout of alarm on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
And their king will go into exile, he and his officials together, says YHWH.

amos_2.t: Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
And I will send fire into Moab, and it will consume the fortresses of Kerioth, and Moab will die in an uproar, with a shout of alarm, with the sound of a horn.
And I will cut off the judge from her midst, and all her officials I will kill with him, says YHWH.

Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the law of YHWH and did not keep his statutes, and their lies led them astray, after which their fathers walked.
And I will send fire into Judah, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem.
Thus says YHWH: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sold the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals.
Those who trample on the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and the way of the humble they turn aside; and a man and his father go to the same young woman, so as to profane my holy name.
And on garments taken in pledge they stretch out beside every altar, and the wine of those who have been fined they drink in the house of their gods.
And I myself destroyed the Amorite from before them, whose height was like the height of cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; and I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath.
And I myself brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you in the wilderness forty years, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
And I raised up some of your sons as prophets, and some of your young men as nazirites. Is this not so, people of Israel? — the declaration of YHWH.
And you made the nazirites drink wine, and on the prophets you laid a command, saying: You shall not prophesy.
Here I am, about to press under you, just as the cart that is full of cut grain presses.
And a place of escape will be lost from the swift, and the strong will not make his power firm, and the mighty will not save his being.
And the handler of the bow will not stand, and the swift on his feet will not save himself, and the rider of the horse will not save his being.
And the one strong of his heart among the warriors will flee naked on that day — the declaration of YHWH.

amos_3.t: Hear this word that YHWH has spoken against you, people of Israel, against the whole clan that I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
Only you have I known of all the clans of the earth. Therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities.
Do two walk together unless they have met by appointment?
Does a lion roar in the forest and there is no prey for him? Does a young lion give his voice from his den unless he has caught something?
Does a bird fall on a trap of the earth and there is no snare for it? Does a trap go up from the ground and it certainly catches nothing?
If a horn is blown in a city, do the people not tremble? If there is calamity in a city, has YHWH not done it?
For Lord YHWH does not do a thing unless he has revealed his secret counsel to his servants the prophets.
A lion has roared — who will not fear? Lord YHWH has spoken — who will not prophesy?

Proclaim to the fortresses in Ashdod and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: Gather yourselves on the mountains of Samaria and see the great disturbances within her and the acts of oppression in her midst.
And they do not know how to do what is straightforward — the declaration of YHWH — those who store up violence and devastation in their fortresses.
Therefore thus says Lord YHWH: An adversary — and all around the land! — and he will bring down your strength from you, and your fortresses will be plundered.

Thus says YHWH: Just as the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two shin-bones or a piece of an ear, so will the people of Israel be rescued — those who dwell in Samaria with the corner of a bed and with the silk of a couch.
Hear and warn the house of Jacob — the declaration of Lord YHWH, the God of hosts.
For on the day I visit the transgressions of Israel upon him, I will also visit upon the altars of Bethel, and the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
And I will strike the winter house upon the summer house, and the houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end — the declaration of YHWH.

amos_4.t: Hear this word, cows of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their masters: Bring, and let us drink!
Lord YHWH has sworn by his holiness: Here, days are coming upon you when one will lift you away with hooks, and your posterity with fish-hooks.
And through breaches you will go out, each one straight ahead, and you will be flung out to Harmon — the declaration of YHWH.
Come to Bethel and transgress! To Gilgal — increase transgressing! And bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes on the third day.
And burn as smoke a thanksgiving offering from what is leavened, and proclaim freewill offerings, make them heard! For so you love it, people of Israel — the declaration of Lord YHWH.
And I myself gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places, and you did not return to me — the declaration of YHWH.

And I myself withheld the rain from you while there were yet three months to the harvest, and I sent rain on one city and on one city I did not send rain. One portion of ground was rained on, and a portion on which it did not rain dried up.
And two, three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and they were not satisfied, and you did not return to me — the declaration of YHWH.

I struck you with blight and with mildew. The multitude of your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees the locust ate, and you did not return to me — the declaration of YHWH.

I sent among you pestilence in the manner of Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, along with the capture of your horses, and I made the stench of your camp go up, and into your nostrils, and you did not return to me — the declaration of YHWH.
I overthrew among you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand plucked from the burning, and you did not return to me — the declaration of YHWH.
Therefore thus I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

For here is the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and tells to humankind what his thought is, who makes dawn darkness and treads on the high places of the earth — YHWH, God of hosts, is his name.

amos_5.t: Hear this word that I am lifting up over you — a lamentation, house of Israel:
She has fallen, she will not rise again — the virgin Israel. She is left abandoned on her ground; there is no one raising her up.
For thus says Lord YHWH: The city that goes out a thousand will have a hundred left, and the one that goes out a hundred will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
For thus says YHWH to the house of Israel: Seek me and live!
And do not seek Bethel, and do not go to Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba, for Gilgal will certainly go into exile, and Bethel will become trouble.
Seek YHWH and live, lest he rush like fire on the house of Joseph, and it consume, and there be none to extinguish it for Bethel.
You who turn justice into wormwood and thrust righteousness down to the ground!
The maker of Kimah and Kesil, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth — YHWH is his name;
who flashes devastation on the strong, and devastation comes upon a fortress.
They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and the one who speaks blamelessly they abhor.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take from him a portion of grain, you have built houses of hewn stone but you will not dwell in them; you have planted vineyards of delight but you will not drink their wine.
For I know your transgressions are many and your sins are numerous — you who oppose the righteous, who take a ransom, and who turn aside the needy in the gate.
Therefore the prudent will be silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and so it may be: YHWH, God of hosts, will be with you just as you have said.
Hate evil and love good, and set up justice in the gate. Perhaps YHWH, God of hosts, will show favour to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says YHWH, God of hosts, the Lord: In all the open squares there will be wailing, and in all the streets they will say, Alas! Alas! And they will call the farmer to mourning, and wailing to those who know lamentation.
And in all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says YHWH.
Woe to those who desire the day of YHWH! Why this for you — the day of YHWH? It is darkness and not light.
As when a man flees from before the lion and the bear meets him, and he comes to the house and leans his hand on the wall and the serpent bites him.
Is not the day of YHWH darkness and not light, and gloom with no brightness in it?
I hate, I reject your festivals, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
For though you offer up to me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them, and the peace offering of your fatlings I will not look upon.
Remove from me the noise of your songs, and the music of your harps I will not hear.
And let justice roll on like the waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing wadi.
Did you bring near to me sacrifices and grain offering in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?
And you will lift up Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your gods, which you made for yourselves.
And I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says YHWH — God of hosts is his name.

amos_6.t: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those who trust in the mountain of Samaria, the distinguished of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
Cross over to Calneh and see, and go from there to Hamath Rabbah, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms, or is their territory greater than your territory?
You who push away the evil day and bring near a seat of violence,
who lie on beds of ivory and sprawl on their couches, and eat lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall;
who improvise on the mouth of the harp; like David they have devised for themselves instruments of song;
who drink wine in bowls and smear themselves with the best of oils, and are not sickened over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of those who go into exile, and the revelry of the sprawlers will come to an end.
Lord YHWH has sworn by his own being — the declaration of YHWH, God of hosts: I loathe the pride of Jacob, and his fortresses I hate, and I will deliver up the city and all that fills it.
And it will be, if ten men remain in one house, they will die.

And his kinsman will lift him up, and the one who burns him, to bring the bones out of the house. And he will say to the one who is in the innermost parts of the house: Is anyone still with you? And he will say: No one. And he will say: Hush! For it is not to be brought to remembrance by the name of YHWH.
For here, YHWH is commanding, and the great house will be struck to fragments, and the small house to rubble.
Do horses run on the rock? Does one plough there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You who rejoice in Lo Debar, who say: Was it not by our own strength that we took Karnaim for ourselves?
For here I am, raising up against you, house of Israel — the declaration of YHWH, God of hosts — a nation, and they will oppress you from Lebo Hamath to the wadi of the Arabah.

amos_7.t: Thus Lord YHWH showed me: and here, he was forming locusts at the beginning of the coming up of the late growth — and here, a late growth after the king's mowings.
And it was, when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, that I said: Lord YHWH, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand? For he is small.
YHWH relented concerning this: It will not be, said YHWH.
Thus Lord YHWH showed me: and here, Lord YHWH was calling for a contention by fire, and it consumed the great deep and consumed the portion of land.
And I said: Lord YHWH, cease, please! How will Jacob stand? For he is small.
YHWH relented concerning this: This also will not be, said Lord YHWH.
Thus he showed me: and here, the Lord was standing on a wall of a plumb line, and in his hand was a plumb line.
And YHWH said to me: What are you seeing, Amos? And I said: A plumb line. And the Lord said: Here I am, setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel. I will not pass by it again.
And the high places of Isaac will be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying: Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to endure all his words.
For thus Amos has said: By the sword Jeroboam will die, and Israel will certainly go into exile from off its ground.
And Amaziah said to Amos: Seer, go, flee for yourself to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and there you shall prophesy.
And at Bethel you shall not prophesy again, for it is a sanctuary of a king and it is a house of a kingdom.
And Amos answered and said to Amaziah: Not a prophet, I; and not a son of a prophet, I; for a herdsman, I, and a tender of sycamore figs.
And YHWH took me from after the flock, and YHWH said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel.
And now hear the word of YHWH: You are saying, You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not preach against the house of Isaac.

Therefore thus says YHWH: Your wife will be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, and your ground will be divided by the measuring-line, and you yourself will die on unclean ground, and Israel will certainly go into exile from off its ground.

amos_8.t: Thus Lord YHWH showed me: and here, a basket of summer fruit.
And he said: What are you seeing, Amos? And I said: A basket of summer fruit. And YHWH said to me: The end has come upon my people Israel. I will not pass by it again.
And the songs of the temple will wail on that day — the declaration of Lord YHWH. Many the corpses! In every place one has thrown them. Hush!
Hear this, you who trample on the needy and put an end to the afflicted of the land,
saying: When will the new moon pass, so that we may sell grain, and the sabbath, so that we may open the wheat — making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying balances of deceit,
to buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and we will sell the refuse of the wheat.
YHWH has sworn by the pride of Jacob: I will never forget any of their deeds.
Shall not the land tremble over this, and everyone who dwells in it mourn? And all of it will rise like the Nile, and be tossed and sink like the River of Egypt.
And it will be on that day — the declaration of Lord YHWH — that I will make the sun go in at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

And I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation, and I will bring sackcloth up on all loins and baldness on every head, and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
Here, days are coming — the declaration of Lord YHWH — when I will send a famine in the land: not a famine for bread and not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of YHWH.
And they will stagger from sea to sea, and from the north and to the east they will rove about, seeking the word of YHWH, and they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say: As your god lives, Dan! and: As the way of Beersheba lives! — they will fall and not rise again.

amos_9.t: I saw the Lord standing on the altar, and he said: Strike the capital, so that the thresholds shake, and break them off on the head of all of them, and their posterity I will kill with the sword. No one fleeing among them will flee, and no escapee among them will escape.
If they dig into Sheol, from there my hand will take them; and if they go up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.

And if they hide themselves on the top of Carmel, from there I will search and take them; and if they conceal themselves from before my eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. And I will set my eye on them for evil and not for good.
And Lord YHWH of hosts, who touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn, and all of it rises like the River and sinks like the River of Egypt;
who builds his stairs in the heavens and has founded his vault upon the earth, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth — YHWH is his name.
Are you not like the sons of the Cushites to me, people of Israel? — the declaration of YHWH. Did I not bring up Israel from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
Here, the eyes of Lord YHWH are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the ground — except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob — the declaration of YHWH.
For here I am, commanding, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as one shakes with a sieve, and not a pebble will fall to the ground.
By the sword all the sinners of my people will die — those who say: The calamity will not draw near or meet us.
On that day I will raise up the falling booth of David, and I will wall up their breaches, and his ruins I will raise up, and I will rebuild her as in the days of antiquity,
so that they may dispossess the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom my name is called — the declaration of YHWH, who does this.

Here, days are coming — the declaration of YHWH — when the ploughman will draw near to the reaper, and the treader of grapes to the sower of seed, and the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.

And I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel, and they will rebuild desolated cities and dwell in them, and they will plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
And I will plant them on their ground, and they will not be plucked up again from off their ground that I have given to them, says YHWH your God.

daniel_1.t: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and laid siege against it.

And the Lord gave into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, and some of the articles of the house of God; and he brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and the articles he brought to the treasury house of his god.
And the king said to Ashpenaz the chief of his officials to bring some of the sons of Israel, and some of the royal offspring and some of the nobles —

youths in whom there was no blemish, good of appearance, having insight in all wisdom, knowing knowledge and understanding understanding, and in whom there was ability to stand in the king's palace — and to teach them the writing and the tongue of the Chaldeans.

And the king assigned them the matter of a day in its day from the king's delicacies and from the wine of his drinking, and to bring them up three years; and from their end they were to stand before the king.
And there were among them, from the sons of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
And the chief of the officials assigned them names: he assigned to Daniel Belteshazzar, and to Hananiah Shadrach, and to Mishael Meshach, and to Azariah Abed-nego.

And Daniel set upon his heart that he would not defile himself with the king's delicacies or with the wine of his drinking; and he requested of the chief of the officials that he might not defile himself.
And God gave Daniel to favour and to compassion before the chief of the officials.

And the chief of the officials said to Daniel: I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and your drink. Why should he see your faces looking worse than the youths who are of your age, and you would make my head forfeit to the king?
And Daniel said to the guardian whom the chief of the officials had assigned over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah:
Put your servants to the test, please, ten days; and let them give us some of the vegetables, and we will eat, and water, and we will drink.
And let our appearance be seen before you, and the appearance of the youths who are eating the king's delicacies; and as you see, deal with your servants.
And he listened to them in this matter, and he put them to the test ten days.
And at the end of ten days their appearance was seen to be good and fat of flesh, more than all the youths who were eating the king's delicacies.
And the guardian was taking away their delicacies and the wine of their drinking, and giving them vegetables.
And these youths, the four of them — God gave them knowledge and insight in all writing and wisdom; and Daniel understood in every vision and dreams.
And at the end of the days that the king had said to bring them, the chief of the officials brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king spoke with them, and none was found among all of them like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah; and they stood before the king.
And every matter of wisdom of understanding that the king sought from them, he found them ten hands above all the soothsayer-priests and the conjurers who were in all his kingdom.
And Daniel was there until the first year of Cyrus the king.

daniel_2.t: And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep came upon him.
And the king said to summon the soothsayer-priests and the conjurers and the sorcerers and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. And they came and stood before the king.
And the king said to them: I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.
And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: King, live for ever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation.

The king answered and said to the Chaldeans: The word from me is firm. If you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be made limbs, and your houses will be made a refuse heap.
And if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from before me gifts and a reward and great honour. Therefore declare to me the dream and its interpretation.
They answered a second time and said: Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare the interpretation.
The king answered and said: For certain I know that you are gaining time, because you have seen that the word from me is firm —

that if you do not make known to me the dream, your law is one; and a lying and corrupt word you have agreed together to say before me until the time changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I shall know that you can declare to me its interpretation.

The Chaldeans answered before the king and said: There is not a person on the earth who can declare the king's matter, because no king, great or powerful, has asked a thing like this of any magician or conjurer or Chaldean.
And the matter that the king is asking is difficult, and there is no other who can declare it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.
Because of this the king was angry and exceedingly furious, and he said to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
And the law went out, and the wise men were about to be killed; and they sought Daniel and his companions, to be killed.
Then Daniel returned counsel and discretion to Arioch, the chief of the king's executioners, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He answered and said to Arioch the king's captain: Why is the law from before the king so harsh? Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
And Daniel went in and asked from the king that he would give him time, and he would declare the interpretation to the king.
Then Daniel went to his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, his companions,
and to ask compassion from before the God of the heavens concerning this secret, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of the heavens.
Daniel answered and said: Let the name of God be blessed from age to age, for wisdom and power are his.
And he changes the times and the appointed times; he removes kings and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who know discernment.
He reveals the deep things and the hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.
To you, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and power; and now you have made known to me what we asked of you, for you have made known to us the king's matter.

Because of this Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and said to him as follows: Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.
Then Arioch in haste brought Daniel in before the king, and said to him as follows: I have found a man from the sons of the exile of Judah who will make known the interpretation to the king.
The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar: Are you able to make known to me the dream that I have seen, and its interpretation?
Daniel answered before the king and said: The secret that the king is asking — wise men, conjurers, magicians and astrologers are not able to declare it to the king.

Nevertheless there is a God in the heavens who reveals secrets, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be at the end of the days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed — this is it.
You, King — your thoughts came up upon your bed about what will be after this, and the revealer of secrets has made known to you what will be.

And as for me — not by wisdom that is in me more than in all the living has this secret been revealed to me, but for the sake that they should make known the interpretation to the king, and that you should know the thoughts of your heart.
You, King, were seeing, and behold, a single great image. That image was great, and its splendour extraordinary, standing before you, and its appearance was terrible.
That image — its head was of good gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its loins of bronze,
its legs of iron, its feet — part of them of iron and part of them of clay.
You were seeing until a stone was cut out that was not by hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay, and it shattered them.

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were shattered as one, and they became like chaff from the summer threshing floors, and the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled all the earth.
This is the dream, and its interpretation we will tell before the king.
You, King, are the king of kings, to whom the God of the heavens has given the kingdom, the power, the strength and the honour;
and wherever the sons of humankind dwell, the animals of the field and the birds of the heavens he has given into your hand, and he has made you ruler over all of them. You are the head of gold.
And after you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you; and a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
And a fourth kingdom will be strong as iron; because iron shatters and crushes everything, and like iron that breaks in pieces, it will shatter and crush all these.

And that you saw the feet and the toes, part of them of a potter's clay and part of them of iron — it will be a divided kingdom; and some of the firmness of the iron will be in it, because you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud.
And the toes of the feet, part of them iron and part of them clay — from part the kingdom will be strong, and from it it will be breakable.
And that you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud — they will be mixing with the offspring of humankind, and they will not be clinging, this one with that one, just as iron does not mix with clay.

And in the days of those kings the God of the heavens will set up a kingdom that for ever will not be destroyed, and the kingdom will not be left to another people. It will shatter and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it will stand for ever.

Because you saw that from the mountain a stone was cut out that was not by hands, and it shattered the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold — the great God has made known to the king what will be after this. And the dream is certain and its interpretation trustworthy.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and he said to offer an offering and soothing offerings to him.
The king answered Daniel and said: In truth your God is the God of gods and the lord of kings and a revealer of secrets, for you have been able to reveal this secret.
Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over all the province of Babylon and chief of the prefects over all the wise men of Babylon.
And Daniel asked of the king, and he appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego; and Daniel was in the gate of the king.

daniel_3.t: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold; its height was sixty cubits, its width six cubits. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

And King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counsellors, the ministers, the judges, the magistrates and all the authorities of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counsellors, the ministers, the judges, the magistrates and all the authorities of the provinces were gathered for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up; and they were standing before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
And the herald was proclaiming with power: To you it is said, peoples, nations and languages!

At the time when you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and all kinds of music, you shall fall down and pay homage to the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
And whoever does not fall down and pay homage — at that moment he will be thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire.

Therefore, at that time, as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp and all kinds of music, all the peoples, nations and languages were falling down, paying homage to the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Therefore, at that time, Chaldean men approached and ate the pieces of the Jews.
They answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar: King, live for ever!

You, King, made a decree that every person who hears the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp and the pipe and all kinds of music shall fall down and pay homage to the image of gold;
and whoever does not fall down and pay homage will be thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire.

There are Jewish men whom you have appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. These men have paid no attention to you, King. They do not serve your god, and to the image of gold that you have set up they do not pay homage.
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and anger, said to bring Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. Then these men were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them: Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, that you do not serve my gods and do not pay homage to the image of gold that I have set up?

Now, if you are ready, at the time when you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp and the pipe and all kinds of music, you shall fall down and pay homage to the image that I have made. And if you do not pay homage, at that moment you will be thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire — and who is the god who will deliver you from my hands?
Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego answered and said to the king: Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need concerning this matter to send back a word to you.
If it is so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of burning fire, and from your hand, King, he will deliver.
And if not, let it be known to you, King, that we do not serve your god, and to the image of gold that you have set up we will not pay homage.

Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with anger, and the image of his face was changed against Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. He answered and said to heat the furnace one seven times more than it was proper to heat it.
And to mighty men of power who were in his army he said to bind Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, to throw them into the furnace of burning fire.
Then these men were bound in their mantles, their trousers, their caps and their clothes, and they were thrown into the midst of the furnace of burning fire.
Because of this — because the word of the king was harsh and the furnace was exceedingly heated — those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, the flame of the fire killed them.
And these men, the three of them — Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego — fell into the midst of the furnace of burning fire, bound.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar was alarmed and rose in haste. He answered and said to his counsellors: Did we not throw three men, bound, into the midst of the fire? They answered and said to the king: Certain, King.
He answered and said: Look — I see four men, loosed, walking in the midst of the fire, and there is no hurt on them; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.

Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the furnace of burning fire. He answered and said: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come! Then Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego came out from the midst of the fire.

And the satraps, the prefects and the governors and the king's counsellors were gathered, seeing these men — that the fire had had no power over their bodies, and the hair of their head was not singed, and their mantles were not changed, and the smell of fire had not touched them.

Nebuchadnezzar answered and said: Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, who sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him — and they violated the word of the king and gave up their bodies, so as not to serve and not to pay homage to any god except their own God.

And from me a decree is made, that any people, nation or language that speaks negligence against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego will be made limbs, and his house will be made a refuse heap; because there is no other god who is able to rescue like this.
Then the king caused Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego to prosper in the province of Babylon.

daniel_4.t: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all the peoples, nations and languages who dwell in all the earth: May your peace increase.
The signs and the wonders that the Most High God has done with me — it has seemed good before me to declare.
How great are his signs, and how strong his wonders! His kingdom is a kingdom of perpetuity, and his dominion is with generation and generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
I saw a dream, and it made me afraid; and imaginings upon my bed and the visions of my head alarmed me.
And from me a decree was made to bring in before me all the wise men of Babylon, that they should make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then the magicians, the conjurers, the Chaldeans and the astrologers were going in; and I was telling the dream before them, but they were not making known to me its interpretation.
And at last there came in before me Daniel, whose name is Belteshazzar, like the name of my god, and in whom is a spirit of holy gods; and I told the dream before him:
Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, because I know that a spirit of holy gods is in you and no secret oppresses you — the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation: tell.
And the visions of my head upon my bed: I was seeing, and behold, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was great.
The tree grew great and grew strong, and its height reached to the heavens, and the sight of it to the end of all the earth.

Its foliage was beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and food for all was in it. Under it the animals of the field had shade, and in its branches the birds of the heavens nested, and from it all flesh was fed.
I was seeing in the visions of my head upon my bed, and behold, a watcher, a holy one, was coming down from the heavens.

He was proclaiming with power and saying as follows: Cut down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its foliage and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.

Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the ground, and with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; and let it become wet with the dew of the heavens, and let its portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.
Let his heart be changed from a human's, and let the heart of an animal be given to him; and let seven times pass over him.

By the decree of the watchers is the command, and by the word of the holy ones is the affair — to the end that the living may know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind, and gives it to whomever he pleases, and sets over it the lowliest of humankind.

This dream I saw — I, King Nebuchadnezzar. And you, Belteshazzar, tell its interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make the interpretation known to me; but you are able, because a spirit of holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king answered and said: Belteshazzar, do not let the dream and its interpretation alarm you. Belteshazzar answered and said: My lord, let the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your adversaries.
The tree that you saw, which grew great and grew strong, and whose height reached to the heavens and the sight of it to all the earth,
and whose foliage was beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and food for all was in it; under it the animals of the field dwelt, and in its branches the birds of the heavens dwelt —
it is you, King, who have grown great and grown strong; and your greatness has grown great and reached to the heavens, and your dominion to the end of the earth.

And that the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens and saying: Cut down the tree and destroy it — nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the ground, and with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field, and let it become wet with the dew of the heavens, and let its portion be with the animals of the field, until seven times pass over it —
this is the interpretation, King, and it is the decree of the Most High that has reached my lord the king:

And you they will chase away from humankind, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field, and they will feed you grass like oxen, and with the dew of the heavens they will make you wet; and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind, and gives it to whomever he pleases.
And that they said to leave the stump of the roots of the tree — your kingdom will be enduring for you, from the time that you know that the heavens have mastery.

Therefore, King, let my advice be acceptable to you: break off your sin by doing righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor — whether there may be a prolonging of your prosperity.
All of it came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he was walking about on the palace of the kingdom of Babylon.
The king answered and said: Is this not Babylon the great, which I myself have built as a royal house by the strength of my power and for the honour of my majesty?
The word was still in the king's mouth when a voice fell from the heavens: To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has passed away from you,

and from humankind they are about to chase you away, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field; they will feed you grass like oxen, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind, and gives it to whomever he pleases.

At that moment the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. And from humankind he was chased away, and he ate grass like oxen, and his body became wet with the dew of the heavens, until his hair grew long like eagles' and his nails like birds'.

And at the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my understanding returned to me; and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified the one who lives for ever, whose dominion is a dominion of perpetuity and whose kingdom is with generation and generation.

And all the inhabitants of the earth are reckoned as nothing, and he does according to his pleasure with the army of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth; and there is none who can strike his hand or say to him, What have you done?

At that time my understanding returned to me, and for the honour of my kingdom my majesty and my splendour returned to me; and my counsellors and my nobles sought me, and I was established over my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and lift up and glorify the King of the heavens, all of whose deeds are truth and whose ways are justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to bring low.

daniel_5.t: King Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and before the thousand he was drinking wine.

Belshazzar, in the taste of the wine, said to bring the vessels of gold and silver that Nebuchadnezzar his father had brought out from the temple that was in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink with them.

Then they brought the vessels of gold that they had brought out from the temple that was the house of God, which was in Jerusalem; and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank with them.
They drank the wine, and they praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.

At that moment the fingers of a human hand came out and were writing opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace; and the king was seeing the palm of the hand that was writing.
Then the king — his brightness changed him, and his thoughts alarmed him, and the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees knocked one against the other.

The king was calling with power to bring in the conjurers, the Chaldeans and the astrologers. The king answered and said to the wise men of Babylon: Any person who reads this writing and declares its interpretation to me will be clothed with purple, and a necklace of gold will be on his neck, and he will rule as third in the kingdom.
Then all the king's wise men went in, but they were not able to read the writing or to make its interpretation known to the king.
Then King Belshazzar was exceedingly alarmed, and his brightness was changing upon him, and his nobles were dumbfounded.

The queen, on account of the words of the king and his nobles, came into the house of the feast. The queen answered and said: King, live for ever! Do not let your thoughts alarm you, and do not let your brightness be changed.

There is a man in your kingdom in whom is a spirit of holy gods; and in the days of your father, illumination and insight and wisdom like the wisdom of gods were found in him. And King Nebuchadnezzar your father made him chief of the magicians, conjurers, Chaldeans and astrologers — your father the king —

because an extraordinary spirit and understanding and insight, interpreting dreams and declaring riddles and loosening knots, were found in him — in Daniel, whose name the king made Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be summoned, and he will declare the interpretation.
Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king answered and said to Daniel: Are you that Daniel who is from the sons of the exile of Judah, whom the king my father brought from Judah?
And I have heard concerning you that a spirit of gods is in you, and that illumination and insight and extraordinary wisdom have been found in you.

And now the wise men and the conjurers have been brought in before me, that they should read this writing and make its interpretation known to me; but they were not able to declare the interpretation of the matter.

And I have heard concerning you that you are able to interpret interpretations and to loosen knots. Now if you are able to read the writing and to make its interpretation known to me, you will be clothed with purple, and a necklace of gold will be on your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom.

Then Daniel answered and said before the king: Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless I will read the writing to the king and make the interpretation known to him.
You, King — the Most High God gave the kingdom and the greatness and the honour and the majesty to Nebuchadnezzar your father.

And from the greatness that he gave him, all the peoples, nations and languages were trembling and fearing before him. Whom he pleased he was killing, and whom he pleased he was letting live; and whom he pleased he was lifting up, and whom he pleased he was bringing low.
And when his heart rose up and his spirit grew strong to act presumptuously, he was deposed from the throne of his kingdom, and the honour was removed from him.

And from the sons of humankind he was chased away, and his heart was made like the animals', and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. They fed him grass like oxen, and his body became wet with the dew of the heavens, until he knew that the Most High God has mastery over the kingdom of humankind, and appoints over it whomever he pleases.
And you, his son Belshazzar, have not brought your heart low, though you knew all this.

And against the lord of the heavens you have lifted yourself up. And they have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines are drinking wine with them; and you have praised the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know. And the God in whose hand is your breath, and to whom all your ways belong, you have not glorified.
Then from before him the palm of the hand was sent out, and this writing was inscribed.
And this is the writing that was inscribed: mene mene teqel and pharsin.
This is the interpretation of the matter: mene — God has numbered your kingdom and finished it.
Teqel — you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.
Peres — your kingdom has been broken in two and given to the Medes and the Persians.
Then Belshazzar said, and they clothed Daniel with purple, and a necklace of gold was on his neck; and they made proclamation concerning him that he should have mastery as third in the kingdom.
In that night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.
And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.

daniel_6.t: It seemed good before Darius, and he appointed over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps who were to be throughout all the kingdom;
and above them three overseers, of whom Daniel was one, to whom these satraps were to give the report, so that the king should not suffer injury.
Then this Daniel was distinguishing himself above the overseers and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit was in him; and the king was planning to appoint him over all the kingdom.

Then the overseers and the satraps were seeking to find an occasion against Daniel from the side of the kingdom; but they were not able to find any occasion or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found concerning him.
Then these men were saying: We will not find any occasion against this Daniel, unless we find it against him in the law of his God.
Then these overseers and satraps came as a crowd to the king, and said to him as follows: Darius the king, live for ever!

All the overseers of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counsellors and the governors, have taken counsel together to establish a royal statute and to make stringent a prohibition, that anyone who asks a petition of any god or person for thirty days, except of you, King, will be thrown into the den of lions.
Now, King, establish the prohibition and sign the writing, which is not to be changed, according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which does not pass away.
Because of this King Darius signed the writing and the prohibition.

And Daniel, when he knew that the writing was signed, went into his house — and windows were opened for him in his upper room facing Jerusalem — and three times in the day he was kneeling on his knees and praying and giving praise before his God, just as he had been doing before this.
Then these men came as a crowd and found Daniel asking and imploring favour before his God.

Then they approached and said before the king concerning the king's prohibition: Did you not sign a prohibition, that any person who asks of any god or person for thirty days, except of you, King, will be thrown into the den of lions? The king answered and said: The word is certain, according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which does not pass away.

Then they answered and said before the king: Daniel, who is from the sons of the exile of Judah, has paid no attention to you, King, nor to the prohibition that you signed; and three times in the day he asks his petition.
Then the king, when he heard the word, was exceedingly displeased at it; and he set his mind on Daniel to deliver him, and until the going in of the sun he was striving to rescue him.

Then these men came as a crowd to the king and said to the king: Know, King, that the law of the Medes and the Persians is that any prohibition or statute that the king establishes is not to be changed.
Then the king said, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king answered and said to Daniel: Your God, whom you serve continually — may he deliver you.
And a stone was brought and set over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing would be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, and no diversions were brought in before him; and his sleep fled from him.
Then the king arose at dawn, at daylight, and went in haste to the den of lions.

And as he approached the den, to Daniel, he cried out with a pained voice. The king answered and said to Daniel: Daniel, servant of the living God, your God whom you serve continually — has he been able to deliver you from the lions?
Then Daniel spoke with the king: King, live for ever!
My God sent his angel and closed the mouth of the lions, and they did not harm me, because before him innocence was found in me; and also before you, King, I have done no hurtful act.
Then the king was exceedingly glad at it, and said to take Daniel up from the den. And Daniel was taken up from the den, and no hurt was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

And the king said, and they brought those men who had eaten the pieces of Daniel, and they threw them into the den of lions — they, their sons and their wives. And they had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions had power over them and shattered all their bones.
Then Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages who dwell in all the earth: May your peace increase.

From before me a decree is made, that in all the dominion of my kingdom they are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for he is the living God and enduring for ever, and his kingdom is one that will not be destroyed, and his dominion is to the end.
He delivers and rescues, and does signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth — he who has delivered Daniel from the hand of the lions.
And this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

daniel_7.t: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head upon his bed. Then he wrote the dream; he told the head of the matters.
Daniel answered and said: I was seeing in my vision with the night, and behold, the four winds of the heavens were stirring up the great sea.
And four great beasts were coming up from the sea, different this one from that one.

The first was like a lion, and it had eagle's wings. I was seeing until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted away from the earth and made to stand on two feet like a human; and a human heart was given to it.

And behold, another beast, a second, like a bear, and it was raised up on one side; and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. And they were saying to it as follows: Arise, devour much flesh.
After this I was seeing, and behold, another, like a leopard, and it had four wings of a bird on its back; and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.

After this I was seeing in the visions of the night, and behold, a fourth beast, fearful and terrible and exceedingly strong; and it had great teeth of iron. It was devouring and shattering, and trampling the rest with its feet. And it was different from all the beasts that were before it, and it had ten horns.

I was considering the horns, and behold, another horn, a small one, came up between them; and three of the former horns were uprooted from before it. And behold, there were eyes like the eyes of humankind in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things.
I was seeing until thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white like snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was flames of fire, its wheels burning fire.
A river of fire was flowing and coming out from before him. A thousand of thousands were ministering to him, and a myriad of myriads were standing before him. The court sat, and books were opened.
I was seeing then, because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I was seeing until the beast was killed and its body destroyed and given to the burning of fire.
And as for the rest of the beasts, they removed their dominion; and a prolonging in life was given to them until a time and a season.
I was seeing in the visions of the night, and behold, with the clouds of the heavens one like a son of man was coming; and he came to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before him.

And to him were given dominion and honour and a kingdom, and all the peoples, nations and languages will serve him. His dominion is a dominion of perpetuity that will not pass away, and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed.
My spirit, I Daniel, was distressed in the midst of the sheath, and the visions of my head alarmed me.
I approached one of those standing there, and I was asking the truth from him about all this. And he told me, and made known to me the interpretation of the matters:
These great beasts, which are four — four kings will arise from the earth.
And the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and will take possession of the kingdom for ever, and for ever and ever.

Then I desired to make certain concerning the fourth beast, which was different from all of them — exceedingly terrible, its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze; devouring, shattering, and trampling the rest with its feet —

and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other one that came up, before which three fell — that horn which had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than its companions'.
I was seeing, and that horn was making war with the holy ones and prevailing against them,
until the Ancient of Days came, and judgement was given for the holy ones of the Most High; and the appointed time arrived, and the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
He said as follows: The fourth beast — a fourth kingdom will be on the earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms; and it will devour all the earth and tread it down and shatter it.
And the ten horns — from that kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former ones, and he will bring low three kings.

And he will speak words to the side of the Most High, and he will wear out the holy ones of the Most High, and he will think to change appointed times and law; and they will be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
And the court will sit, and they will remove his dominion, to annihilate and to destroy it until the end.

And the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens were given to a people, the holy ones of the Most High. His kingdom is a kingdom of perpetuity, and all the empires will serve and obey him.
Here is the end of the matter. I, Daniel — my thoughts alarmed me exceedingly, and my brightness was changed upon me; and I kept the matter in my heart.

daniel_8.t: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me — I, Daniel — after the one that appeared to me at the beginning.
And I saw in the vision — and it happened, when I saw, that I was in Susa the citadel, which is in Elam the province — and I saw in the vision, and I was by the canal of Ulai.

And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a single ram standing before the canal, and it had two horns; and the two horns were high, and the one was higher than the second, and the higher one came up last.

I saw the ram thrusting westward and northward and southward, and no living creatures could stand before it, and there was none who could deliver from its hand; and it did according to its pleasure and magnified itself.

And I was observing, and behold, a he-goat of the goats coming from the west over the face of all the earth, and it was not touching the earth; and the he-goat had a horn of conspicuousness between its eyes.
And it came to the ram, the possessor of the two horns, which I had seen standing before the canal, and it ran at it in the rage of its strength.

And I saw it reaching beside the ram, and it was enraged at it, and it struck the ram and broke its two horns; and there was no strength in the ram to stand before it. And it threw it to the ground and trampled it, and there was none who could deliver the ram from its hand.
And the he-goat magnified itself exceedingly; and when it became mighty, the great horn was broken, and four conspicuous ones came up in its place, towards the four winds of the heavens.
And from one of them came out a single horn from a small thing, and it became exceedingly great towards the south and towards the east and towards the beauty.
And it became great as far as the host of the heavens, and it made fall to the ground some of the host and some of the stars, and it trampled them.
And it magnified itself as far as the Prince of the host, and from him the perpetual was removed, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
And an army will be set over the perpetual in transgression, and it will throw truth to the ground; and it will act and succeed.

And I heard one holy one speaking, and one holy one said to the certain one who was speaking: Until when is the vision — the perpetual, and the transgression that desolates, giving over both the sanctuary and the host to trampling?
And he said to me: Until evening, morning — two thousand and three hundred; and the sanctuary will be put right.
And it happened, when I, Daniel, saw the vision and sought understanding, that behold, there was standing before me one like the appearance of a man.
And I heard the voice of a person between the Ulai; and he called and said: Gabriel, explain the vision to this one.
And he came beside where I was standing; and when he came I was terrified, and I fell on my face. And he said to me: Understand, son of humankind, that the vision is for the time of the end.
And while he was speaking with me I was dazed, upon my face, to the ground. And he touched me and made me stand where I had been standing.
And he said: Here I am, making known to you what will be at the end of the indignation; for it is for the appointed time of the end.
The ram that you saw, the possessor of the two horns — the kings of Media and Persia.
And the he-goat, the hairy one, is the king of Greece; and the great horn that is between its eyes is the first king.
And the broken one, and four that arose in its place — four kingdoms will arise from a nation, but not with its power.
And at the end of their reign, when the rebels are completed, a king strong of face and understanding intrigues will arise.
And his power will be mighty, but not by his own power; and he will destroy wonders, and he will succeed and act, and he will destroy the mighty and a people of holy ones.

And on his insight, and deceit will succeed in his hand; and in his heart he will magnify himself, and in prosperity he will destroy many. And against a prince of princes he will stand, and by no hand he will be broken.
And the vision of the evening and the morning that has been told is truth; and you — keep the vision secret, for it is for many days.
And I, Daniel, was done in and was sick for days; then I arose and did the king's work. And I was appalled at the thing seen, and there was none who gave understanding.

daniel_9.t: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, from the offspring of Media, who had been made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans —
in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, observed in the books the number of the years that the word of YHWH had come to Jeremiah the prophet, to complete for the ruins of Jerusalem seventy years.
And I set my face to the Lord God, to seek prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

And I prayed to YHWH my God and confessed, and I said: I beg you, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love for those who love him and for those who keep his commandments —
we have sinned and committed iniquity, we have acted wickedly and rebelled, and we have turned aside from your commandments and from your judgements.
And we have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our leaders and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.

To you, Lord, belongs the righteousness, and to us the shame of faces, as at this day — to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to all Israel, near and far, in all the lands where you have banished them, in their unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against you.
YHWH, to us belongs the shame of faces — to our kings, to our leaders and to our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.
To the Lord our God belong the compassion and the forgivenesses, for we have rebelled against him,
and we have not listened to the voice of YHWH our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by the hand of his servants the prophets.

And all Israel have transgressed your law and turned aside, not listening to your voice. And the curse and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God has poured out upon us, because we have sinned against him.

And he has carried out his word that he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing upon us a great calamity, such as has not been done under all the heavens as it has been done in Jerusalem.

Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this calamity has come upon us; and we have not entreated the face of YHWH our God by turning from our iniquity and by giving attention to your faithfulness.
And YHWH kept watch over the calamity and brought it upon us; for YHWH our God is righteous in all his deeds that he has done, and we have not listened to his voice.
And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out from the land of Egypt with a strong hand, and made for yourself a name as at this day — we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.

Lord, according to all your righteousnesses, let your anger and your rage turn back, please, from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain; for by our sins and by the iniquities of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a reproach to all who are around us.
And now, listen, our God, to the prayer of your servant and to his supplications, and make your face shine upon your desolate sanctuary, for the Lord's sake.

Incline your ear, my God, and listen; open your eyes and see our desolations, and the city over which your name has been called. For not on our righteousnesses are we making our supplications fall before you, but on your great compassion.
Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, be attentive and act — do not delay! — for your own sake, my God; for your name has been called over your city and over your people.
And while I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and making my supplication fall before YHWH my God concerning the holy mountain of my God —
and while I was still speaking in the prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, wearied with weariness, was approaching me about the time of the evening offering.
And he gave understanding and spoke with me, and he said: Daniel, now I have come out to give you insight and understanding.
At the beginning of your supplications a word went out, and I have come to declare it, for you are precious. So understand the word and understand the thing seen.

Seventy weeks have been decreed upon your people and upon your holy city, to put an end to the transgression, and to complete sin, and to atone for iniquity, and to bring in righteousness of perpetuity, and to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a holy place of holy places.

And you shall know and understand: from the going out of a word to restore and to rebuild Jerusalem, until an anointed one, a prince, seven weeks; and sixty-two weeks it will return and be built, open place and moat, and in the distress of the times.

And after the sixty-two weeks an anointed one will be cut off, and there is nothing for him. And the city and the sanctuary the people of a prince who is coming will destroy; and its end will be in the flood, and until the end, war — desolations are determined.

And he will make a covenant strong for the many, one week; and in the half of the week he will cause sacrifice and offering to cease. And on a wing of detestable things, one desolating — and until a complete destruction, and what is determined, it will be poured out on the desolator.

daniel_10.t: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. And the word was truth, and a great war. And he understood the word, and understanding was his in the thing seen.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three sevens of days.
Food of desirable things I did not eat, and meat and wine did not come into my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all, until the completing of three sevens of days.
And on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was on the side of the great river — that is the Tigris.
And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a single man clothed in linen, and his loins girded with the gold of Uphaz.

And his body was like beryl, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire; and his arms and his feet like the appearance of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
And I, Daniel, alone saw the thing seen; and the men who were with me did not see the thing seen. But a great terror fell on them, and they fled into hiding.
And I was left alone, and I saw this great thing seen; and no strength remained in me, and my vigour was turned upon me to destruction, and I retained no strength.
And I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I was dazed on my face, and my face to the ground.
And behold, a hand touched me and shook me onto my knees and the palms of my hands.

And he said to me: Daniel, man of precious things, understand the words that I am speaking to you, and stand where you are standing, for now I have been sent to you. And when he spoke this word with me, I stood up trembling.

And he said to me: Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard; and I have come because of your words.
And the prince of the kingdom of Persia was standing before me twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left over there beside the kings of Persia.
And I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people at the end of the days; for the vision is still for the days.
And while he was speaking with me according to these words, I set my face to the ground and was dumb.

And behold, one like the likeness of the sons of humankind was touching my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke, and said to the one standing before me: My lord, by the thing seen my pangs have turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.
And how is this servant of my lord able to speak with this my lord? And as for me, from now no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me.
And he repeated and touched me, like the appearance of a human, and strengthened me.
And he said: Do not fear, man of precious things; peace to you. Be strong, and be strong. And as he spoke with me I strengthened myself, and I said: Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.
And he said: Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia; and as I am going out, behold, the prince of Greece is coming.
But I will tell you what is inscribed in a writing of truth. And there is none who shows himself strong with me against these, except Michael your prince.

daniel_11.t: And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede — my standing was as a strengthener and a protection for him.

And now I will tell you truth. Behold, three more kings are about to arise for Persia, and the fourth will gain great wealth, more than all; and by his strength, through his wealth, he will stir up everyone — the kingdom of Greece.
And a mighty king will arise, and he will have dominion with great dominion, and he will do according to his pleasure.

And as he arises, his kingdom will be broken up and divided to the four winds of the heavens, and not to his posterity, and not according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom will be plucked up, and to others besides these.
And the king of the south will become strong, and one of his commanders; and he will become strong over him and will exercise dominion — his dominion will be a great dominion.

And at the end of years they will make an alliance; and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement. But she will not retain the power of the arm, and he will not stand, nor his arm; and she will be given up, she and those who brought her, and the one who fathered her, and the one who strengthened her in the times.
And one from the shoot of her roots will arise in his place, and he will come to the army and go into the stronghold of the king of the north; and he will act against them and prevail.
And also their gods, with their molten images, with their vessels of desire, silver and gold, he will bring into captivity to Egypt; and he will stand for years away from the king of the north.
And he will come into the kingdom of the king of the south, and he will return to his own land.
And his sons will wage war and gather a multitude of great armies; and it will surely come and overflow and pass over, and it will return and wage war as far as his stronghold.
And the king of the south will be enraged, and he will go out and fight with him, with the king of the north; and he will raise up a great multitude, and the multitude will be given into his hand.
And the multitude will be carried off, and his heart will be lifted up; and he will make tens of thousands fall, but he will not prevail.
And the king of the north will return and raise up a multitude greater than the first; and at the end of the times, years, he will surely come with a large army and with much equipment.
And in those times many will arise against the king of the south; and the sons of the violent ones of your people will exalt themselves to fulfil the vision, but they will stumble.

And the king of the north will come and pour out a siege mound, and he will capture a city of fortifications; and the forces of the south will not stand, nor the people of his chosen ones, and there will be no strength to stand.
And the one who comes against him will do according to his pleasure, and there will be none standing before him; and he will stand in the land of beauty, and complete destruction will be in his hand.

And he will set his face to come with the power of all his kingdom, and upright things with him; and he will act. And the daughter of women he will give him, to destroy her; but she will not stand, and she will not be for him.
And he will set his face to the coastlands and capture many. And a commander will put an end to his scorn for him; without his scorn, he will turn it back on him.
And he will turn his face to the strongholds of his own land; and he will stumble and fall, and will not be found.
And there will arise in his place one who sends through an oppressor, the splendour of a kingdom; and in a few days he will be broken, but not in anger and not in battle.
And there will arise in his place a despicable one, and they will not have given to him the honour of royalty; and he will come in quietness and take hold of royalty by intrigues.
And the forces of the flood will be swept away from before him and will be broken; and also a prince of a covenant.
And from the time of an alliance made with him he will act deceitfully; and he will rise and become mighty with a small nation.

In quietness, and into the fertile places of the province, he will come; and he will do what his fathers and his fathers' fathers did not do: plunder and booty and property he will scatter among them; and against strongholds he will plan his plans — but only for a time.

And he will stir up his strength and his heart against the king of the south with a large army; and the king of the south will get ready for the battle with an exceedingly large and mighty army. But he will not stand, for they will plan plans against him.
And those who eat his delicacies will break him; and his army will overflow, and many slain will fall.
And the two kings — their heart is to do evil, and at one table they will speak falsehood. But it will not succeed, for the end is still for the appointed time.
