deuteronomy_18.t: There shall not be for the priests, the Levites—all the tribe of Levi—a share and an inheritance with Israel; the food offerings of YHWH and his inheritance they shall eat.
And an inheritance shall not be for him in the midst of his brothers; YHWH—he is his inheritance, just as he spoke to him.
And this shall be the priests' right from the people, from those who sacrifice the sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: he shall give to the priest the arm and the two cheeks and the stomach.
The first of your grain, your new wine, and your fresh oil, and the first of the fleece of your flock, you shall give to him.
For in him YHWH your God has chosen out of all your tribes, to stand to serve in the name of YHWH—he and his sons all the days.
And if the Levite comes from one of your gates, out of all Israel, where he is sojourning, and comes with all the desire of his self to the place which YHWH chooses,
then he shall serve in the name of YHWH his God like all his brothers the Levites who stand there before YHWH.
Share like share they shall eat, besides his sales upon the fathers.
When you come into the land which YHWH your God is giving to you, you shall not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who makes his son and his daughter pass in the fire, one who divines divinations, a soothsayer, and an augurer, and a sorcerer,
and one who binds a binding, and one who consults a medium or a spiritist, and one who enquires of the dead.
For everyone doing these is an abomination of YHWH, and on account of these abominations YHWH your God is dispossessing them from before you.
Blameless you shall be with YHWH your God.
For these nations which you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers and to diviners; but you—not so has YHWH your God given to you.
A prophet from your midst, from your brothers, like me, YHWH your God will raise up for you; to him you shall listen.

according to all that you asked from YHWH your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, 'Let me not go on hearing the voice of YHWH my God, and this great fire let me not see again, and I will not die.'
And YHWH said to me, 'They have done well [in] what they have spoken.'
'A prophet I will raise up for them from the midst of their brothers, like you, and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.'
'And it shall be, the man who does not listen to my words which he speaks in my name—I myself will require it from him.'
'But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name which I have not commanded him to speak, and who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet shall die.'
'And if you say in your heart, "How shall we know the word which YHWH has not spoken?"'

'What the prophet speaks in the name of YHWH and the thing does not happen and does not come—that is the word which YHWH has not spoken; with presumption the prophet spoke it. You shall not be afraid of him.'

deuteronomy_19.t: When YHWH your God cuts off the nations whose land YHWH your God is giving to you, and you dispossess them and dwell in their cities and in their houses,
three cities you shall set apart for yourself in the midst of your land which YHWH your God is giving to you to take possession of it.
You shall prepare for yourself the way, and you shall divide into three the territory of your land which YHWH your God gives you to inherit; and it shall be for every killer to flee there.
And this is the case of the killer who flees there and lives: whoever strikes his neighbour without knowledge, and he was not hating him from yesterday, the third day.

and whoever goes with his neighbour into the forest to cut wood, and his hand is driven with the axe to cut down the tree, and the iron slips off from the wood and finds his neighbour and he dies—he shall flee to one of these cities and live.

lest the avenger of blood pursue after the killer because his heart is hot, and overtake him because the way is long, and strike him fatally—though he has no sentence of death, for he was not hating him from yesterday, the third day.
Therefore I am commanding you, saying: three cities you shall set apart for yourself.
And if YHWH your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your fathers, and gives to you all the land which he spoke to give to your fathers—

if you keep all this commandment to do it, which I am commanding you today, to love YHWH your God and to walk in his ways all the days—then you shall add for yourself three more cities to these three.
so that innocent blood is not shed in the midst of your land which YHWH your God is giving to you as an inheritance, and bloods be upon you.
But if a man is hating his neighbour, and lies in wait for him, and rises against him, and strikes him fatally so that he dies, and flees to one of these cities,
then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there and give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall die.
Your eye shall not pity him. And you shall purge the blood of the innocent from Israel, and it shall be good for you.
You shall not move back your neighbour's boundary, which the former ones set, in your inheritance which you inherit in the land which YHWH your God is giving to you to take possession of it.
One witness shall not stand against a man for any iniquity or for any sin, in any sin that he sins; on the mouth of two witnesses or on the mouth of three witnesses a matter shall stand.
If a witness of violence stands against a man, to testify against him a turning-aside,
then the two men who have the dispute shall stand before YHWH, before the priests and the judges who are in those days.
And the judges shall investigate thoroughly, and behold, the witness is a false witness—falsehood he has testified against his brother—
then you shall do to him just as he schemed to do to his brother, and you shall purge the evil from your midst.
And those who remain shall hear and fear, and they shall not again do such an evil thing as this in your midst.
And your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

deuteronomy_20.t: When you go out to the war against your enemies and see horse and chariot, a people greater than you, you shall not be afraid of them, for YHWH your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, that the priest shall come near and speak to the people.

And he shall say to them, 'Hear, Israel! You are drawing near today to the battle against your enemies. Let your heart not be faint; do not be afraid, and do not panic, and do not be in dread before them.
For YHWH your God is the one going with you, to fight for you with your enemies, to save you.'

And the officers shall speak to the people, saying, 'Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
And who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not made common use of it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man make common use of it.
And who is the man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.

And the officers shall speak again to the people and say, 'Who is the man who is afraid and soft of heart? Let him go and return to his house, and let him not melt the heart of his brothers like his heart.'
And it shall be, when the officers finish speaking to the people, that they shall appoint commanders of armies at the head of the people.
When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call out to it for peace.
And it shall be, if it answers you peace and opens to you, then all the people found in it shall become forced labour for you and shall serve you.
And if it does not make peace with you and makes war with you, then you shall besiege it.
And YHWH your God will give it into your hand, and you shall strike every male in it with the mouth of the sword.

Only the women and the little ones and the livestock and all that is in the city, all its spoil, you shall plunder for yourself, and you shall consume the spoil of your enemies which YHWH your God has given to you.
Thus you shall do to all the cities very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations.
Only from the cities of these peoples which YHWH your God is giving to you as an inheritance, you shall not let live any breathing thing.
For devoting to destruction you shall devote them to destruction—the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite—as YHWH your God has commanded you,
so that they do not teach you to do according to all their abominations which they have done for their gods, and you sin against YHWH your God.

When you besiege a city many days, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an axe against them; for from them you shall eat, and you shall not cut them down—for is the tree of the field a man, to come before you in the siege?
Only a tree which you know is not a tree of food—that one you may destroy and cut down, and you shall build siege works against the city that is making war with you, until it falls.

deuteronomy_21.t: If one slain is found in the land which YHWH your God is giving to you to take possession of it, fallen in the open country, and it is not known who struck him,
then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure to the cities which are around the slain one.
And the city nearest to the slain one—the elders of that city shall take a heifer of the herd which has not been worked with, which has not pulled in a yoke,
and the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to an ever-flowing wadi which is not tilled and not sown, and they shall break the heifer's neck there in the wadi.

And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall draw near, for in them YHWH your God has chosen, to serve him and to bless in the name of YHWH; and by their mouth shall be every dispute and every affliction.
And all the elders of that city, those nearest to the slain one, shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi,
and they shall answer and say, 'Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see.
Atone for your people Israel, whom you ransomed, YHWH, and do not put innocent blood in the midst of your people Israel.' And the blood shall be atoned for them.
And you shall purge the innocent blood from your midst, for you will do what is right in the eyes of YHWH.
When you go out to the war against your enemies, and YHWH your God gives him into your hand and you take his captives captive,
and you see among the captives a woman beautiful of form, and you desire her, and you take her for yourself as a wife,
then you shall bring her into the midst of your house, and she shall shave her head and do her nails,

and she shall remove the clothing of her captivity from upon her and dwell in your house and weep for her father and her mother a month of days. And after that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall become your wife.
And if you do not delight in her, then you shall let her go for herself, and you shall certainly not sell her for money. You shall not deal with her as a slave, because you have humbled her.
If a man has two wives, the one loved and the one hated, and they bear him sons, the loved one and the hated one, and the firstborn son belongs to the hated one,
then on the day he causes his sons to inherit what he has, he shall not be able to treat the son of the loved one as firstborn over the face of the son of the hated one, the firstborn.

But he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated one, by giving him a mouth of two in all that is found belonging to him; for he is the beginning of his vigour—to him belongs the right of the birthright.
If a man has a son who is stubborn and rebellious, who does not listen to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and they discipline him and he does not listen to them,
then his father and his mother shall seize him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place,
and they shall say to the elders of his city, 'This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He does not listen to our voice. He is a glutton and a drunkard.'
And all the men of his city shall stone him with stones, and he shall die. So you shall purge the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear and fear.
And if there is in a man a sin of a sentence of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his corpse shall not remain overnight on the tree, but burying you shall bury him on that day, for a hanged man is a curse of God; and you shall not defile your land which YHWH your God is giving to you as an inheritance.

deuteronomy_22.t: You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep going astray and hide yourself from them; returning you shall return them to your brother.

And if your brother is not near you and you do not know him, then you shall gather it into the midst of your house, and it shall be with you until your brother seeks it, and you shall return it to him.

And thus you shall do for his donkey, and thus you shall do for his garment, and thus you shall do for every lost thing of your brother's which is lost from him and you find. You are not able to hide yourself.
You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the way and hide yourself from them; raising you shall raise it up with him.
A man's gear shall not be on a woman, and a man shall not wear a woman's garment, for everyone who does these is an abomination of YHWH your God.
If a bird's nest happens to be before you on the way, in any tree or on the ground—chicks or eggs—and the mother is lying on the chicks or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young.
Letting go you shall let go the mother, and the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well for you and you may prolong days.
When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, and you shall not put bloods on your house if the falling one falls from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds, lest the whole yield be set apart as holy—the seed which you sow and the produce of the vineyard.
You shall not plough with an ox and a donkey together.
You shall not wear sha'atnez—wool and linen together.
Tassels you shall make for yourself on the four corners of your covering with which you cover yourself.
If a man takes a wife and goes in to her and hates her,
and makes charges of words against her and brings out a bad name upon her, and says, 'This woman I took, and I drew near to her, and I did not find in her tokens of virginity,'
then the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring out the tokens of the young woman's virginity to the elders of the city, to the gate.
And the father of the young woman shall say to the elders, 'My daughter I gave to this man as a wife, and he hated her.

And behold, he has made charges of words, saying, "I did not find in your daughter tokens of virginity." And these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity.' And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city shall take the man and discipline him.

And they shall fine him a hundred of silver and give it to the father of the young woman, because he brought out a bad name upon a virgin of Israel. And she shall be his wife; he is not able to send her away all his days.
But if this thing was true, tokens of virginity were not found for the young woman,

then they shall bring out the young woman to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die, because she has done folly in Israel by whoring in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.
If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman and the woman. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
If there is a young woman, a virgin betrothed to a man, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her,

then you shall bring both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them with stones, and they shall die—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbour's wife. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.
But if the man finds the betrothed young woman in the open country, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
And to the young woman you shall do nothing; the young woman has no sin of death, for as when a man rises against his neighbour and murders him as to life, so is this matter.
For he found her in the open country; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to save her.
If a man finds a young woman, a virgin who is not betrothed, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found,
then the man who lay with her shall give to the father of the young woman fifty of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he violated her. He is not able to send her away all his days.
A man shall not take his father's wife, and he shall not uncover his father's skirt.

deuteronomy_23.t: No man wounded by crushing or with his penis cut off shall enter the assembly of YHWH.
One of illegitimate birth shall not enter the assembly of YHWH; even to the tenth generation none of his shall enter the assembly of YHWH.
No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of YHWH; even to the tenth generation none of theirs shall enter the assembly of YHWH, for ever.
because they did not meet you with food and with water on the way when you came out from Egypt, and because he hired against you Balaam son of Beor from Pethor of Aram-naharaim to curse you.
But YHWH your God was not willing to listen to Balaam, and YHWH your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because YHWH your God loved you.
You shall not seek their peace or their good all your days, for ever.
You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, for you were a sojourner in his land.
Children who are born to them, a third generation, shall enter the assembly of YHWH for them.
When a camp goes out against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.
If there is among you a man who is not clean because of a happening of the night, then he shall go outside the camp; he shall not come into the midst of the camp.
And it shall be, toward the turning of evening he shall wash with water, and as the sun goes in he shall come into the midst of the camp.
And you shall have a hand outside the camp, and you shall go out there, outside.
And you shall have a peg with your equipment, and it shall be, when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and turn back and cover your excrement.

For YHWH your God walks about in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and to give your enemies before you; and your camp shall be holy, so that he does not see the nakedness of a thing among you and turn back from after you.
You shall not hand over a slave to his master, who delivers himself to you from his master.
With you he shall dwell, in your midst, in the place which he chooses within one of your gates, where it is good for him. You shall not maltreat him.
There shall not be a shrine prostitute among the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be a shrine prostitute among the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring the fee of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of YHWH your God for any vow, for both of them are an abomination of YHWH your God.
You shall not charge interest to your brother—interest of money, interest of food, interest of anything on which interest is charged.

To the foreigner you may charge interest, but to your brother you shall not charge interest, so that YHWH your God may bless you in every undertaking of your hand in the land which you are entering to take possession of it.
When you vow a vow to YHWH your God, you shall not delay to pay it, for requiring YHWH your God will require it from you, and there will be sin on you.
But if you refrain from vowing, there will be no sin on you.
The utterance of your lips you shall keep and do, just as you have vowed to YHWH your God a freewill offering, which you have spoken with your mouth.
When you go into your neighbour's vineyard, you may eat grapes according to your appetite, your fill, but you shall not put any into your vessel.
When you go into your neighbour's standing grain, you may pluck ears with your hand, but you shall not wield a sickle against your neighbour's standing grain.

deuteronomy_24.t: When a man takes a wife and marries her, and it happens that she does not find favour in his eyes because he has found in her the nakedness of a thing, and he writes her a document of severance and gives it into her hand and sends her away from his house,
and she goes out from his house and goes and becomes another man's,
and the latter man hates her and writes her a document of severance and gives it into her hand and sends her away from his house, or if the latter man who took her to himself as a wife dies—

her first husband, who sent her away, is not able to return to take her to be his wife after she has been made unclean; for that is an abomination before YHWH, and you shall not cause the land which YHWH your God is giving to you as an inheritance to sin.

When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army, and nothing shall pass upon him for any matter. He shall be free for his house one year, and he shall gladden his wife whom he has taken.
No one shall take in pledge a hand-mill or an upper millstone, for he is taking a life in pledge.

If a man is found stealing a person from among his brothers, from the sons of Israel, and deals with him as merchandise and sells him, then that thief shall die. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.
Take heed in the affliction of leprosy, to be very careful and to do according to all that the priests, the Levites, instruct you; just as I commanded them, you shall be careful to do.
Remember what YHWH your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out from Egypt.
When you lend your neighbour a loan of anything, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.
Outside you shall stand, and the man to whom you are lending shall bring the pledge out to you, outside.
And if he is a poor man, you shall not lie down in his pledge.
Returning you shall return the pledge to him when the sun goes in, and he shall lie down in his garment and bless you; and it shall be righteousness for you before YHWH your God.
You shall not oppress a hired labourer who is poor and needy, whether from your brothers or from your sojourner who is in your land, in your gates.

On his day you shall give his wages, and the sun shall not go in upon them, for he is poor and to it he is lifting up his self; so that he does not call out against you to YHWH, and there be sin on you.
Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.
You shall not turn aside the justice of a sojourner, a fatherless one, and you shall not take a widow's garment in pledge.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt and YHWH your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to fetch it. It shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless and for the widow, so that YHWH your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs behind you. It shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless and for the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean behind you. It shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless and for the widow.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

deuteronomy_25.t: If there is a dispute between men and they come to the judgement and they judge them, then they shall declare the righteous righteous and condemn the guilty as guilty.
And it shall be, if the guilty one is a son of striking, then the judge shall make him lie down and he shall be struck before him, according to the sufficiency of his guilt, by number.
Forty he may strike him; he shall not add, lest he add to strike him beyond these a great beating, and your brother be dishonoured before your eyes.
You shall not muzzle an ox in its threshing.

If brothers dwell together and one of them dies and he has no son, the wife of the dead man shall not go outside to a strange man. Her husband's brother shall go in to her and take her to himself as a wife and do the duty of a husband's brother for her.
And it shall be, the firstborn whom she bears shall stand upon the name of his dead brother, so that his name is not wiped out from Israel.

And if the man does not desire to take his brother's widow, then his brother's widow shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, 'My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he is not willing to do the duty of a husband's brother for me.'
Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak to him. And if he stands and says, 'I do not desire to take her,'

then his brother's widow shall draw near to him before the eyes of the elders, and pull his sandal off his foot, and spit in his face; and she shall answer and say, 'Thus shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house.'
And his name shall be called in Israel, 'The house of the one whose sandal was drawn off.'
If men struggle together, a man and his brother, and the wife of the one draws near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and puts out her hand and takes hold of his genitals,
then you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not pity.
You shall not have in your bag a stone and a stone, a large and a small.
You shall not have in your house an ephah and an ephah, a large and a small.
A full and righteous stone you shall have; a full and righteous ephah you shall have; so that your days may be long on the land which YHWH your God is giving to you.
For everyone who does these is an abomination of YHWH your God, everyone who does injustice.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out from Egypt,
how he met you on the way and attacked your rear, all the stragglers behind you, when you were exhausted and weary; and he did not fear God.

And it shall be, when YHWH your God gives you rest from all your enemies round about, in the land which YHWH your God is giving to you as an inheritance to take possession of it, you shall wipe out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens. You shall not forget.

deuteronomy_26.t: And it shall be, when you come into the land which YHWH your God is giving to you as an inheritance, and you possess it and dwell in it,

then you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground which you bring in from your land which YHWH your God is giving to you, and put it in a basket, and go to the place which YHWH your God chooses to make his name dwell there.
And you shall come to the priest who is in those days and say to him, 'I declare today to YHWH your God that I have come into the land which YHWH swore to our fathers to give to us.'
And the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of YHWH your God.

And you shall answer and say before YHWH your God, 'A wandering Aramean was my father, and he went down to Egypt and sojourned there few in number, and he became there a nation great, mighty and numerous.
And the Egyptians did harm to us and afflicted us and put hard labour upon us.
And we cried out to YHWH, the God of our fathers, and YHWH heard our voice and saw our affliction and our toil and our oppression.
And YHWH brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great terror, and with signs and with wonders.
And he brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, behold, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground which you have given me, YHWH.' And you shall set it down before YHWH your God and bow down before YHWH your God.
And you shall rejoice in all the good which YHWH your God has given to you and to your house—you and the Levite and the sojourner who is in your midst.

When you finish tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, then you shall give it to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the fatherless and to the widow, and they shall eat in your gates and be satisfied.

And you shall say before YHWH your God, 'I have removed the holy portion from the house, and I have also given it to the Levite and to the sojourner, to the fatherless and to the widow, according to all your commandment which you commanded me. I have not transgressed any of your commandments and I have not forgotten.

I have not eaten of it in my mourning, and I have not removed any of it while unclean, and I have not given any of it to the dead. I have listened to the voice of YHWH my God; I have done according to all that you commanded me.
Look down from your holy habitation, from the heavens, and bless your people Israel and the ground which you have given us, as you swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.'
This day YHWH your God is commanding you to do these statutes and the ordinances. And you shall keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have declared YHWH today to be God for you, and to walk in his ways and to keep his statutes and his commandments and his ordinances, and to listen to his voice.
And YHWH has declared you today to be for him a people of possession, as he spoke to you, and to keep all his commandments,
and to set you high above all the nations which he has made, for praise and for a name and for honour, and that you should be a people holy to YHWH your God, as he has spoken.

deuteronomy_27.t: And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, 'Keep all the commandment which I am commanding you today.
And it shall be, on the day when you cross the Jordan into the land which YHWH your God is giving to you, you shall set up for yourself large stones and coat them with lime.

And you shall write on them all the words of this law when you cross over, so that you may come into the land which YHWH your God is giving to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as YHWH the God of your fathers has spoken to you.
And it shall be, when you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones which I am commanding you today, on Mount Ebal, and you shall coat them with lime.
And you shall build there an altar to YHWH your God, an altar of stones; you shall not wield iron on them.
Of whole stones you shall build the altar of YHWH your God, and you shall offer up on it burnt offerings to YHWH your God.
And you shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there and rejoice before YHWH your God.
And you shall write on the stones all the words of this law, making it very plain.
And Moses and the priests, the Levites, spoke to all Israel, saying, 'Be silent and hear, Israel! This day you have become a people for YHWH your God.
And you shall listen to the voice of YHWH your God and do his commandments and his statutes which I am commanding you today.'
And Moses commanded the people on that day, saying,
'These shall stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Joseph and Benjamin.
And these shall stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad and Asher and Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.
And the Levites shall answer and say to every man of Israel in a high voice:
'Cursed be the man who makes a carved image or a cast image, an abomination of YHWH, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' And all the people shall answer and say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who dishonours his father and his mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who moves back his neighbour's boundary.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who leads a blind man astray on the way.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who turns aside the justice of a sojourner, a fatherless one and a widow.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's skirt.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with any animal.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his mother-in-law.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who strikes his neighbour in secret.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who takes a bribe to strike down a person—innocent blood.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

deuteronomy_28.t: And it shall be, if listening you listen to the voice of YHWH your God, being careful to do all his commandments which I am commanding you today, then YHWH your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to the voice of YHWH your God.
Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the open country.
Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading trough.
Blessed shall you be in your coming in, and blessed shall you be in your going out.
YHWH will make your enemies who rise against you defeated before you: by one road they shall come out against you, and by seven roads they shall flee before you.
YHWH will command the blessing with you in your barns and in every undertaking of your hand, and he will bless you in the land which YHWH your God is giving to you.
YHWH will establish you for himself as a holy people, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of YHWH your God and walk in his ways.
And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of YHWH is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you.
And YHWH will make you abound for good in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, on the land which YHWH swore to your fathers to give to you.

YHWH will open for you his good storehouse, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its appointed time and to bless all the work of your hand; and you shall lend to many nations, and you shall not borrow.
And YHWH will make you the head and not the tail, and you shall be only upward and not downward, if you listen to the commandments of YHWH your God which I am commanding you today, to keep and to do,
and you do not turn aside from all the words which I am commanding you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

And it shall be, if you do not listen to the voice of YHWH your God, being careful to do all his commandments and his statutes which I am commanding you today, then all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you.
Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed shall you be in the open country.
Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading trough.
Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Cursed shall you be in your coming in, and cursed shall you be in your going out.

YHWH will send upon you the curse, the panic and the rebuke, in every undertaking of your hand which you do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds, in that you have forsaken me.
YHWH will make the pestilence cling to you until he has finished you off from upon the land which you are entering to take possession of it.
YHWH will strike you with wasting and with fever and with inflammation and with burning heat, and with the sword and with blight and with mildew; and they shall pursue you until you perish.
And your heavens which are over your head shall be bronze, and the ground which is under you, iron.
YHWH will make the rain of your land dust and powder; from the heavens it shall come down upon you until you are destroyed.

YHWH will make you defeated before your enemies: by one road you shall go out against him, and by seven roads you shall flee before him. And you shall become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And your corpse shall become food for every bird of the heavens and for the animals of the earth, and there shall be no one to frighten them away.
YHWH will strike you with the boils of Egypt, and with tumours, and with scab, and with itch, from which you will not be able to be healed.
YHWH will strike you with madness and with blindness and with bewilderment of heart.
And you shall be groping at noon as the blind man gropes in the darkness, and you shall not make your ways succeed. And you shall be only oppressed and robbed all the days, with no one to save.
A woman you shall betroth, and another man shall lie with her. A house you shall build, and you shall not dwell in it. A vineyard you shall plant, and you shall not make common use of it.

Your ox slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat of it. Your donkey seized from before you, and it shall not be returned to you. Your flock given to your enemies, and you shall have no one to save.
Your sons and your daughters given to another people, and your eyes looking and failing for them all the day, and your hand without power.
The fruit of your ground and all your toil a people whom you have not known shall eat, and you shall be only oppressed and crushed all the days.
And you shall be driven mad by the sight of your eyes which you see.
YHWH will strike you with evil boils on the knees and on the legs, from which you will not be able to be healed, from the sole of your foot to your scalp.
YHWH will lead you and your king whom you set over you to a nation which you have not known, you or your fathers, and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone.
And you shall become a horror, a byword and a taunt among all the peoples where YHWH drives you.
Much seed you shall carry out to the field, and little you shall gather in, for the locust shall consume it.
Vineyards you shall plant and work, but wine you shall not drink and you shall not gather, for the worm shall eat it.
Olive trees you shall have in all your territory, but with oil you shall not anoint yourself, for your olives shall drop off.
Sons and daughters you shall father, but they shall not be yours, for they shall go into captivity.
All your trees and the fruit of your ground the cricket shall take possession of.
The sojourner who is in your midst shall go up above you higher and higher, and you shall go down lower and lower.
He shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him. He shall become the head, and you shall become the tail.

And all these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of YHWH your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded you.
And they shall be upon you as a sign and a wonder, and upon your offspring, for ever.
Because you did not serve YHWH your God with joy and with goodness of heart, out of the abundance of everything,

you shall serve your enemies whom YHWH will send against you, in hunger and in thirst and in nakedness and in lack of everything; and he will put a yoke of iron on your neck until he has destroyed you.
YHWH will raise up against you a nation from far off, from the end of the earth, as the eagle swoops; a nation whose language you will not understand,
a nation fierce of face, which will not lift up the face for the old and will not show favour to the young.

And it shall eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed, leaving you no grain, new wine or fresh oil, no offspring of your cattle or young of your flock, until it has made you perish.

And it shall besiege you in all your gates until your high and fortified walls come down, in which you are trusting, throughout all your land; and it shall besiege you in all your gates throughout all your land which YHWH your God has given to you.
And you shall eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom YHWH your God has given to you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you.
The man among you who is gentle and very delicate—his eye shall be evil toward his brother and toward the wife of his bosom and toward the rest of his children whom he has left,

so as not to give to any one of them of the flesh of his children whom he eats, because nothing is left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in all your gates.

The gentle and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground out of delicacy and gentleness—her eye shall be evil toward the husband of her bosom and toward her son and toward her daughter,

and toward her afterbirth which comes out from between her feet, and toward her children whom she bears; for she shall eat them in secret, in the lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in your gates.
If you are not careful to do all the words of this law which are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome name, YHWH your God,
then YHWH will make your plagues extraordinary, and the plagues of your offspring—great and lasting plagues, and evil and lasting sicknesses.
And he will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt which you dreaded, and they shall cling to you.
Also every sickness and every plague which is not written in the book of this law—YHWH will bring them up upon you until you are destroyed.
And you shall be left few in number, in place of your having been like the stars of the heavens for multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of YHWH your God.

And it shall be, just as YHWH rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so YHWH will rejoice over you to make you perish and to destroy you; and you shall be torn away from upon the land which you are entering to take possession of it.
And YHWH will scatter you among all the peoples, from the end of the earth to the end of the earth, and there you shall serve other gods whom you have not known, you or your fathers—wood and stone.
And among those nations you shall find no rest, and there shall be no resting place for the sole of your foot; and YHWH will give you there a trembling heart, failing of eyes and despair of self.
And your life shall be hung up before you, and you shall be in dread night and day, and you shall not trust in your life.

In the morning you shall say, 'Who will give the evening?' and in the evening you shall say, 'Who will give the morning?'—from the dread of your heart which you will dread and from the sight of your eyes which you will see.

And YHWH will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I said to you, 'You shall not see it again'; and there you shall sell yourselves to your enemies as male slaves and female slaves, and there will be no buyer.

deuteronomy_29.t: These are the words of the covenant which YHWH commanded Moses to cut with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which he made with them at Horeb.
And Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, 'You have seen all that YHWH did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land—
the great trials which your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders.
But YHWH has not given you a heart to know, or eyes to see, or ears to hear, until this day.
And I led you forty years in the wilderness; your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandal did not wear out on your foot.
You ate no bread, and wine and strong drink you did not drink, so that you might know that I am YHWH your God.
And you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, and we struck them down.
And we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites and the Gadites and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.
And you shall keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may act wisely in all that you do.
You are standing today, all of you, before YHWH your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders and your officers, every man of Israel,
your little ones, your wives, and your sojourner who is in the midst of your camps, from the cutter of your wood to the drawer of your water—
for you to pass into the covenant of YHWH your God and into his oath, which YHWH your God is making with you today,
so as to establish you today for himself as a people, and that he may be God for you, just as he spoke to you and just as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
And not with you alone am I cutting this covenant and this oath,
but with the one who is here with us, standing today before YHWH our God, and with the one who is not here with us today.
For you know how we dwelt in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed,
and you saw their detestable things and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were with them.

Lest there be among you a man or a woman or a clan or a tribe whose heart is turning away today from YHWH our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations—lest there be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood,

and it shall be, when he hears the words of this oath, he blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I shall have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart'—to sweep away the watered along with the thirsty.

YHWH will not be willing to forgive him; for then the anger of YHWH and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and every oath written in this book will lie down upon him, and YHWH will wipe out his name from under the heavens.
And YHWH will separate him for harm out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the oaths of the covenant written in this book of the law.

And the later generation—your children who rise up after you—and the foreigner who comes from a distant land will say, when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases with which YHWH has made it sick,

'The whole of its land is sulphur and salt, a burning waste; it is not sown and it does not sprout, and no vegetation comes up in it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which YHWH overthrew in his anger and in his rage'—
and all the nations will say, 'On what account has YHWH done thus to this land? What is this great heat of anger?'
And they will say, 'Because they forsook the covenant of YHWH, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them out from the land of Egypt,
and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods whom they had not known and whom he had not allotted to them.
So the anger of YHWH burned against that land, to bring upon it every curse written in this book.
And YHWH uprooted them from upon their ground in anger and in rage and in great wrath, and cast them into another land, as at this day.'
The hidden things belong to YHWH our God, and the revealed things to us and to our children for ever, to do all the words of this law.

deuteronomy_30.t: And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before you, and you bring them back to your heart among all the nations where YHWH your God has driven you,
and you turn back to YHWH your God and listen to his voice, according to all that I am commanding you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,
then YHWH your God will turn back your turning and have compassion on you, and he will turn back and gather you from all the peoples where YHWH your God has scattered you.
If your banished ones are at the end of the heavens, from there YHWH your God will gather you, and from there he will take you.
And YHWH your God will bring you to the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; and he will do you good and make you more numerous than your fathers.
And YHWH your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, to love YHWH your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
And YHWH your God will put all these oaths upon your enemies and upon those who hate you, who persecuted you.
And you shall turn back and listen to the voice of YHWH, and do all his commandments which I am commanding you today.

And YHWH your God will make you abound for good in every work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground; for YHWH will turn back to rejoice over you for good, just as he rejoiced over your fathers,
if you listen to the voice of YHWH your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes written in this book of the law, if you turn back to YHWH your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
For this commandment which I am commanding you today is not too wonderful for you, and it is not far off.
It is not in the heavens, to say, 'Who will go up for us to the heavens and fetch it for us and make us hear it, that we may do it?'
And it is not beyond the sea, to say, 'Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea and fetch it for us and make us hear it, that we may do it?'
For the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.
See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil,

which I am commanding you today, to love YHWH your God, to walk in his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances; and you shall live and increase, and YHWH your God will bless you in the land which you are entering to take possession of it.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn aside and bow down to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that perishing you shall perish; you shall not prolong days on the land which you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call as witnesses against you today the heavens and the earth: life and death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse. So choose life, that you may live, you and your offspring,

by loving YHWH your God, by listening to his voice and by clinging to him; for he is your life and the length of your days, to dwell on the land which YHWH swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them.

deuteronomy_31.t: And Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
And he said to them: I am a son of a hundred and twenty years today; I am no longer able to go out and to come in, and YHWH has said to me, You shall not cross this Jordan.
YHWH your God — he is crossing over before you; he will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua — he is crossing over before you, just as YHWH has spoken.
And YHWH will do to them just as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorite, and to their land, whom he destroyed.
And YHWH will deliver them up before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment that I have commanded you.
Be strong and be bold; do not fear and do not be terrified before them, for YHWH your God — he is the one going with you; he will not abandon you and will not forsake you.

And Moses summoned Joshua and said to him before the eyes of all Israel: Be strong and be bold, for you shall go with this people into the land that YHWH swore to their ancestors to give to them, and you shall give it to them as an inheritance.
And YHWH — he is the one going before you; he will be with you; he will not abandon you and will not forsake you. Do not fear and do not be dismayed.
And Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carry the ark of the covenant of YHWH, and to all the elders of Israel.
And Moses commanded them, saying: At the end of seven years, at the appointed time of the year of remission, at the Festival of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the face of YHWH your God in the place that he will choose, you shall read this law aloud before all Israel in their ears.

Assemble the people — the men and the women and the little ones, and your sojourner who is in your gates — so that they may hear and so that they may learn, and they shall fear YHWH your God and take care to do all the words of this law,
and their children who have not known it shall hear and learn to fear YHWH your God all the days that you are alive on the ground where you are crossing the Jordan to go, to take possession of it.

And YHWH said to Moses: Here, your days have drawn near to die. Summon Joshua, and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, that I may commission him. And Moses went, and Joshua, and they presented themselves at the tent of meeting.
And YHWH appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

And YHWH said to Moses: Here, you are about to lie down with your ancestors, and this people will rise and go whoring after the foreign gods of the land into whose midst it is going, and it will forsake me and break my covenant that I made with it.

And my anger will burn against it on that day, and I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and it will be for devouring, and many calamities and troubles will come upon it. And it will say on that day: Is it not because my God is not in my midst that these calamities have come upon me?
And I — hiding I will hide my face on that day, because of all the evil that it has done, for it has turned to other gods.
And now, write for yourselves this song and teach it to the sons of Israel; put it in their mouth, so that this song may be a witness for me against the sons of Israel.

For I will bring it to the ground that I swore to its ancestors, flowing with milk and honey, and it will eat and be satisfied and grow fat, and it will turn to other gods and they will serve them, and they will spurn me and it will break my covenant.

And it shall be, when many calamities and troubles come upon it, that this song will testify before it as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouth of its offspring; for I know its intention, which it is making today, before I bring it into the land that I swore.
And Moses wrote down this song on that day and taught it to the sons of Israel.
And he commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said: Be strong and be bold, for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I — I will be with you.
And it was, when Moses finished writing down the words of this law on a book until they were complete,
that Moses commanded the Levites who carry the ark of the covenant of YHWH, saying:
Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of YHWH your God, and it shall be there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Here, while I am still alive with you today you have been rebellious with YHWH — and how much more after my death!
Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, that I may speak these words in their ears and call as witnesses against them the heavens and the earth.

For I know that after my death, corrupting you will act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you; and the evil will happen to you in the latter days, because you will do the evil in the eyes of YHWH, provoking him to anger by the work of your hands.
And Moses spoke in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song until they were complete.

deuteronomy_32.t: Give ear, heavens, and let me speak, and let the earth hear the sayings of my mouth.
May my teaching drop like the rain, may my speech distil like the dew, like showers on grass and like copious showers on vegetation.
For the name of YHWH I proclaim; ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock—his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he.
He has acted corruptly toward him—not his children—their blemish; a generation crooked and twisted.
Is it to YHWH that you repay this, foolish people and not wise? Is he not your father who created you? He made you and established you.
Remember the days of old, consider the years of generation and generation; ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of humankind, he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God.
For YHWH's share is his people; Jacob is the measured portion of his inheritance.
He found him in a land of wilderness, and in a howling waste of desolation; he encircled him, he cared for him, he guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that hovers over its young, he spreads his wings, he takes him, he carries him on his pinion.
YHWH alone guided him, and there was no foreign god with him.
He made him ride on the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field; and he made him suck honey from a rock, and oil from the flint of rock.
Curds of the herd and milk of the flock, with the fat of lambs, and rams, sons of Bashan, and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of wheat; and the blood of the grape you drank as wine.
And Jeshurun grew fat and kicked— you grew fat, you grew thick, you were gorged— and he abandoned the God who made him, and treated with contempt the Rock of his salvation.
They made him jealous with strange ones, with abominations they provoked him to anger.
They sacrificed to demons, not God— gods they had not known, new ones that came from nearby, whom your fathers had not dreaded.
The Rock who fathered you, you neglected, and you forgot God who writhed in labour with you.
And YHWH saw and spurned, from the provocation of his sons and his daughters.
And he said: I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end will be; for they are a generation of perversities, children in whom there is no faithfulness.
They made me jealous with a no-god, they provoked me to anger with their vanities; and I—I will make them jealous with a no-people, with a foolish nation I will provoke them to anger.
For a fire has been kindled in my nostril, and it burns to the lowest Sheol, and it consumes the earth and its produce, and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap calamities upon them; my arrows I will use up on them.
Wasted with hunger, and devoured by burning plague and bitter destruction; and the tooth of beasts I will send against them, with the venom of things that crawl in the dust.
Outside the sword shall bereave, and inside, terror— both young man and virgin, the nursing child with the grey-haired man.
I said, I will cut them to pieces, I will make their memory cease from humankind—
were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy, lest their adversaries misread it, lest they say, Our hand is raised high, and it was not YHWH who did all this.
For they are a nation lost to counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise they would comprehend this, they would understand their end.
How could one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, if their Rock had not sold them, and YHWH had not handed them over?
For their rock is not like our Rock— and our enemies are judges.
For their vine is from the vine of Sodom and from the terraces of Gomorrah; their grapes are grapes of poison, their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents and the cruel poison of cobras.
Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my storehouses?
Vengeance is mine, and recompense, for the time when their foot slips; for the day of their disaster is near, and what is prepared for them hastens.
For YHWH will judge his people and have compassion on his servants, when he sees that the hand is gone, and there is none remaining, bond or free.
And he will say: Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices, who drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise and help you; let them be a shelter over you!
See now that I, I am he, and there is no god beside me. I put to death and I make alive; I have wounded and I heal, and there is none who delivers from my hand.
For I lift my hand to the heavens and say: As I live for ever,
if I sharpen the lightning of my sword and my hand takes hold on judgement, I will return vengeance to my foes and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh— from the blood of the slain and the captives, from the head of the long-haired leaders of the enemy.
Rejoice, nations, with his people, for the blood of his servants he will avenge, and vengeance he will return to his foes, and he will make atonement for his land, his people.
And Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.
And Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel.
And he said to them, 'Set your heart to all the words which I am testifying against you today, which you shall command your children to be careful to do—all the words of this law.
For it is not an empty word for you; for it is your life, and by this word you shall prolong days on the land which you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of it.'
And YHWH spoke to Moses on that very day, saying,
'Go up to this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, which is opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan which I am giving to the sons of Israel as a holding.
And die on the mountain which you are going up, and be gathered to your peoples, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his peoples,
because you acted unfaithfully against me among the sons of Israel at the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat me as holy among the sons of Israel.
For from opposite you shall see the land, but you shall not go there, into the land which I am giving to the sons of Israel.'

deuteronomy_33.t: And this is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death.
And he said: YHWH came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran, and he came from the ten thousands of holy ones, from his right hand, fire of law for them.
Also he loves peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand, and they were led to your foot; he takes from your words.
A law Moses commanded us, a possession of the assembly of Jacob.
And he became king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered themselves, together the tribes of Israel.
Let Reuben live and not die, and let his men be a number.
And this is for Judah, and he said: Hear, O YHWH, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. With his own hands he contended for himself, and may you be a help against his foes.
And of Levi he said: Your Thummim and your Urim belong to your loyal one, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah;
who said of his father and of his mother, I have not seen him, and his brothers he did not recognise, and his children he did not acknowledge; for they kept your speech and observed your covenant.
They will teach your judgements to Jacob and your law to Israel; they will put incense in your nostrils and the whole offering on your altar.
Bless, O YHWH, his substance, and be pleased with the work of his hands. Shatter the loins of those who rise against him, and of those who hate him, that they rise no more.
Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of YHWH dwells in safety upon him; he covers over him all the day, and between his shoulders he dwells.
And of Joseph he said: Blessed of YHWH is his land, with the choice gift of heaven, with dew, and with the deep that lies beneath,
and with the choice gift of the yields of the sun, and with the choice gift of the produce of the months,
and with the top of the ancient mountains, and with the choice gift of the everlasting hills,
and with the choice gift of the earth and its fullness, and the favour of the one who dwelt in the bush. May it come upon the head of Joseph, upon the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

His firstborn bull — splendour is his, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox; with them he will gore peoples, all together, to the ends of the earth. And they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
And of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, O Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
Peoples they will summon to the mountain; there they will sacrifice sacrifices of righteousness. For they will suck the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.
And of Gad he said: Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad. Like a lion he dwells, and he tears the arm, also the crown of the head.
And he saw the choicest for himself, for there the portion of a commander was reserved; and he came at the heads of the people, the righteousness of YHWH he executed, and his judgements with Israel.
And of Dan he said: Dan is a lion's cub; he leaps forth from Bashan.
And of Naphtali he said: Naphtali is satisfied with favour and full of the blessing of YHWH; the west and the south take possession.
And of Asher he said: Blessed above sons is Asher; let him be the favoured of his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
Iron and bronze are your bolts, and as your days, so your strength.
There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your help, and in his majesty the clouds.
A dwelling is the God of ancient time, and beneath are the everlasting arms; and he drove out the enemy from before you, and he said, Destroy.
And Israel dwelt in safety, alone, the spring of Jacob, to a land of grain and new wine; also his heavens drop dew.

How blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by YHWH, the shield of your help and the one who is the sword of your eminence? And your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread on their high places.

deuteronomy_34.t: And Moses went up from the desert plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho; and YHWH showed him all the land — the Gilead as far as Dan,
and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
and the Negev, and the district — the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees — as far as Zoar.

And YHWH said to him, This is the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, To your offspring I will give it. I have let you see it with your own eyes, but there you shall not cross over.
And Moses the servant of YHWH died there, in the land of Moab, on the mouth of YHWH.
And he buried him in the valley, in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor; and no one knows his burial place to this day.
And Moses was a son of one hundred and twenty years at his death; his eye had not grown dim, and his vigour had not fled.
And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in the desert plains of Moab thirty days; and the days of weeping of the mourning for Moses were completed.
And Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him; and the sons of Israel listened to him, and did just as YHWH had commanded Moses.
And there has not arisen a prophet again in Israel like Moses, whom YHWH knew face to face,
for all the signs and the wonders which YHWH sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,
and for all the mighty hand, and for all the great terror which Moses did before the eyes of all Israel.

ecclesiastes_1.t: The words of Qoheleth, son of David, king in Jerusalem.
Vapour of vapours, said Qoheleth, vapour of vapours; everything is vapour.
What profit is there for a person in all his toil at which he toils under the sun?
A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands for ever.
And the sun rises and the sun goes, and to its place it pants, rising there again.
Going to the south and circling to the north, circling, circling, the wind goes, and on its circuits the wind returns.
All the rivers go to the sea, and the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers go, there they return to go again.
All things are wearisome; no one is able to speak. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor is the ear filled from hearing.
What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done, and there is nothing new under the sun.
Is there a thing of which one says, "See, this is new"? It has already been, in the ages that were before us.
There is no remembrance of the former things, and also of the later things that will be — there will be no remembrance of them with those who will be at the last.
I, Qoheleth, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
And I gave my heart to seek out and to search by wisdom concerning all that has been done under the heavens. It is an evil task that God has given to the children of humankind to be busied with.
I have seen all the works that have been done under the sun, and here, everything is vapour and a chasing of wind.
What is bent cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
I spoke, I, with my heart, saying: "Here, I have made great and increased wisdom beyond all who were before me over Jerusalem, and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge."
And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I knew that this too is a striving after wind.
For in much wisdom is much vexation, and one who increases knowledge increases pain.

ecclesiastes_2.t: I said, I, in my heart, "Come now, let me test you with pleasure; look on good." And here, that too was vapour.
Of laughter I said, "It is madness," and of pleasure, "What does this accomplish?"

I searched in my heart to gratify my flesh with wine — my heart guiding me with wisdom — and to take hold of folly, until I might see what is good for the children of humankind to do under the heavens the number of the days of their lives.
I made my works great: I built myself houses; I planted myself vineyards.
I made myself gardens and parks, and I planted in them trees of every fruit.
I made myself pools of water, to water from them a forest sprouting trees.
I acquired male and female slaves, and I had house-born slaves; also livestock, herds and flocks in abundance I had, more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered myself also silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I got myself male singers and female singers, and the delights of the children of humankind — a breast and breasts.
And I became great and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom stood by me.
And all that my eyes asked I did not withhold from them; I did not restrain my heart from any pleasure, for my heart was glad from all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.
Then I turned, I, to all my works that my hands had done, and to the toil that I had toiled to do, and here, everything was vapour and a chasing of wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
And I turned, I, to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what is the person who will come after the king, other than what they have already done?
And I saw, I, that there is profit for wisdom over folly, like the profit of light over darkness.
The wise one — his eyes are in his head, but the dullard walks in darkness. And I knew, also I, that one happening happens to them all.
And I said, I, in my heart, "As the happening of the dullard, so it will happen to me also. And why then have I been so exceedingly wise?" And I spoke in my heart that this too is vapour.
For there is no remembrance of the wise one, with the dullard, for ever, since already in the days that are coming everything is forgotten. And how the wise one dies, with the dullard!
And I hated life, for the work that is done under the sun was evil upon me; for everything is vapour and a chasing of wind.
And I hated, I, all my toil that I was toiling at under the sun, because I must leave it to the person who will come after me.
And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will have power over all my toil that I have toiled at and worked at with wisdom under the sun. This too is vapour.
And I turned, I, to make my heart despair over all the toil that I had toiled at under the sun.
For there is a person whose toil is with wisdom and with knowledge and with skill, and to a person who has not toiled at it he must give it as his portion. This too is vapour, and a great evil.
For what does a person get in all his toil and in the striving of his heart at which he toils under the sun?
For all his days are pains, and his task is vexation; also in the night his heart does not lie down. This too is vapour.
There is no good for a person that he should eat and drink and show his being good in his toil. This too I saw, I, that it is from the hand of God.
For who eats and who enjoys apart from me?

For to a person who is good before him he gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and collecting, to give to one who is good before God. This too is vapour and a chasing of wind.

ecclesiastes_3.t: For everything there is an appointed time, and a time for every matter under the heavens:
a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted;
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build;
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance;
a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to be far from embracing;
a time to seek and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to throw away;
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak;
a time to love and a time to hate, a time of war and a time of peace.
What profit has the worker in that at which he toils?
I have seen the task that God has given to the children of humankind to be busied with.
He has made everything beautiful in its time; also he has put the age into their heart, yet so that a person cannot find out the work that God has done from beginning to end.
I know that there is no good among them except to rejoice and to do good in one's life.
And also, that every person should eat and drink and see good in all his toil — that is a gift of God.
I know that all that God does will be for ever; to it there is nothing to add, and from it there is nothing to take away; and God has acted so that they should fear before him.
What is has already been, and what is to be has already been; and God seeks what has been pursued.
And again I have seen under the sun: in the place of judgement, there was wickedness, and in the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.
I said, I, in my heart: "God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter, and over every deed, there."
I said, I, in my heart, concerning the children of humankind, that God is testing them, and to see that they themselves are animals.

For the happening of the children of humankind and the happening of the animal — one happening is theirs. As this one dies, so this one dies; and one breath belongs to them all, and there is no advantage of humankind over the animal, for everything is vapour.
Everything goes to one place. Everything came from the dust, and everything returns to the dust.
Who knows the spirit of the children of humankind, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?
And I saw that there is no good beyond that a person should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who will bring him to see what will be after him?

ecclesiastes_4.t: And I turned again, I, and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And here, the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; and from the hand of their oppressors, power — and they have no comforter.
And I congratulated, I, the dead who have already died, more than the living who are still alive;
and better than both of them is the one who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
And I considered, I, all toil and all skill in work, that it is a person's envy of his neighbour. This too is vapour and a chasing of wind.
The dullard folds his hands and eats his own flesh.
Better a handful with quietness than two hands full of toil and a chasing of wind.
And I turned again, I, and saw vapour under the sun:

There is one alone, without a second; he has neither son nor brother, and there is no end to all his toil; also his eye is not satisfied with wealth. "And for whom am I toiling and depriving my being of good?" This too is vapour, and an evil task it is.
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
For if they fall, the one will raise his companion; but woe to the one who falls and has no second to raise him.
Also, if two lie down, they have warmth; but how can one be warm?
And though one may overpower him who is alone, the two will stand against him; and a threefold cord is not quickly torn apart.
Better a poor and wise youth than an old and dull king who no longer knows how to be warned.
For out of the house of prisoners he came out to reign, for even in his own kingdom he had been born poor.
I saw all the living who walk about under the sun with the second youth who stands up in his place.
There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them; yet the later ones will not rejoice in him. For this too is vapour and a striving after wind.

ecclesiastes_5.t: Guard your foot when you go to the house of God, and draw near to listen rather than to give the sacrifice of dullards, for they do not know that they are doing evil.
Do not be hasty with your mouth, and let your heart not hurry to bring out a word before God; for God is in the heavens and you are on the earth. Therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with abundance of business, and a dullard's voice with a multitude of words.
When you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it, for there is no pleasure in dullards. What you vow, pay.
Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the messenger, "It was an inadvertence." Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
For in a multitude of dreams and vapours and many words — rather, fear God.

If you see the oppression of a poor person and the robbery of justice and righteousness in a province, do not be astonished at the matter; for a high one watches over a high one, and there are high ones over them.
And the profit of a land is in everything; a king is served by a field.
