One who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor one who loves abundance with income. This too is vapour.
When the good increases, those who consume it increase; and what profit is there for its owner except the sight of his eyes?
Sweet is the sleep of the labourer, whether he eats little or much; but the plenty of the rich does not permit him to sleep.
There is a severe evil that I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his own harm.
And that wealth was lost in an evil business, and he fathered a son, and there was nothing in his hand.
As he came out from his mother's womb, naked he will return, to go as he came; and he will carry nothing from his toil that he may take in his hand.
And this too is a severe evil: exactly as he came, so he will go; and what profit is there for him that he toils for the wind?
Also all his days he eats in darkness, and he is greatly vexed, with sickness and anger.

Here is what I have seen, I, to be good, that is beautiful: to eat and to drink and to see good in all one's toil that one toils at under the sun the number of the days of one's life that God has given — for that is one's portion.
Also every person to whom God has given wealth and riches, and has given him power to eat from it and to receive his portion and to rejoice in his toil — this is a gift of God.
For he will not much remember the days of his life, for God is keeping him busy with the joy of his heart.

ecclesiastes_6.t: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon humankind:

A person to whom God gives wealth and riches and honour, and he lacks nothing for his appetite of all that he desires, yet God does not give him power to eat from it, for a foreign man eats it — this is vapour, and it is an evil affliction.

If a man fathers a hundred and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his being is not satisfied from the good, and also he has no burial — I say: better than he is the stillborn.
For in vapour it came, and in darkness it goes, and in darkness its name is covered.
Also it has not seen the sun and has not known. This one has rest more than that one.
And though he lived a thousand years twice over and saw no good — do not all go to one place?
All a person's toil is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
For what advantage has the wise one over the dullard? What has the poor one who knows how to walk before the living?
Better the sight of the eyes than the going of the appetite. This too is vapour and a chasing of wind.
Whatever has been, its name has already been called, and it is known what humankind is; and one cannot contend with one stronger than he.
For there are many words that increase vapour. What advantage is there for a person?
For who knows what is good for a person in life, the number of the days of his vapour-life, and he spends them like a shadow? For who can tell a person what will be after him under the sun?

ecclesiastes_7.t: Better a name than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one's being born.
Better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for that is the end of every person, and the living will take it to his heart.
Better vexation than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning, but the heart of dullards is in a house of gladness.
Better to listen to the rebuke of a wise one than to be one who listens to the song of dullards.
For like the sound of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the dullard. And this too is vapour.
For oppression makes a wise one look foolish, and a bribe destroys the heart.
Better the end of a matter than its beginning; better one long of spirit than one proud of spirit.
Do not be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger settles in the bosom of dullards.
Do not say, "Why was it that the former days were better than these?" for it is not from wisdom that you have asked about this.
Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and an advantage to those who see the sun.
For wisdom is a shade, and money is a shade, and the profit of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
Consider the work of God: for who is able to straighten what he has bent?
In a day of good, be in good; and in a day of adversity, consider: God has made this alongside that, so that a person may not find out anything after him.
All this I have seen in the days of my vapour: there is a righteous one perishing in his righteousness, and there is a wicked one prolonging his life in his evil.
Do not be righteous overmuch, and do not make yourself wise to excess. Why should you destroy yourself?
Do not be wicked overmuch, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
It is good that you should take hold of this, and also from that not withdraw your hand; for one who fears God will come out with both of them.
Wisdom gives strength to the wise one more than ten rulers who are in a city.
For there is no righteous person on the earth who does good and does not sin.
Also, do not give your heart to all the words that people speak, so that you may not hear your servant cursing you.
For also, many times your heart knows that you too have cursed others.
All this I have tested by wisdom. I said, "Let me be wise" — but it was far from me.
Far off is what has been, and deep, deep — who can find it out?
I turned, I and my heart, to know and to search and to seek wisdom and a reckoning, and to know the wickedness of stupidity and the folly that is madness.
And I was finding more bitter than death the woman who is snares, and whose heart is nets, and whose hands are fetters. One who is good before God escapes from her, but a sinner is captured by her.
"See, this I have found," said Qoheleth, "one to one, to find a reckoning —
which my being has still sought and I have not found: one man among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
Only see this that I have found: that God made humankind upright, but they have sought many schemes."

ecclesiastes_8.t: Who is like the wise one? And who knows the interpretation of a matter? A person's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
I: keep the king's mouth, and that because of the oath of God.
Do not be hasty; go from his presence. Do not stand in an evil matter, for he does all that he desires.
Inasmuch as a king's word is mastery, who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
One who keeps a command will not know an evil thing, and a wise heart will know a time and a custom.
For there is a time and a custom for every matter, for the trouble of humankind is great upon him.
For he does not know what will be, for who can tell him how it will be?
There is no one having mastery over the wind, to restrain the wind, and there is no mastery over the day of death, and there is no discharge in the battle, and wickedness will not rescue its owners.
All this I have seen, giving my heart to every deed that is done under the sun, a time when one person domineers over another to his harm.
And in such circumstances I have seen the wicked buried, and they came; and from a holy place they used to go, and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This too is vapour.
Because sentence upon an evil deed is not executed quickly, therefore the heart of the children of humankind is full within them to do evil.
Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs his days, yet I also know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before him.
But it will not be well with the wicked, and he will not prolong days, like a shadow, because he does not fear before God.

There is a vapour that is done on the earth: that there are righteous ones to whom it happens according to the deed of the wicked, and there are wicked ones to whom it happens according to the deed of the righteous. I said that this too is vapour.

So I commended gladness, because there is no good for a person under the sun except to eat and to drink and to be glad; and this will accompany him in his toil the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.
When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on the earth — for neither by day nor by night does one see sleep with one's eyes —

then I saw all the work of God, that a person is not able to find out the work that is done under the sun, inasmuch as a person toils to seek and does not find out; and even if the wise one says he knows, he is not able to find out.

ecclesiastes_9.t: For all this I gave to my heart, and to make all this clear: that the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether love or hatred, a person does not know; everything is before them.

Everything is as it is for everyone: one happening for the righteous and for the wicked, for the good, and for the clean and for the unclean, and for the one who sacrifices and for the one who does not sacrifice; as the good one, so the sinner; the one who swears an oath, as the one who fears an oath.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: that there is one happening for all, and also the heart of the children of humankind is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that — to the dead.
For whoever is joined to all the living, there is hope; for a living dog is better than the dead lion.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing at all, and there is no longer any reward for them, for their memory is forgotten.
Both their love and their hatred and their envy have already perished, and they have no portion for ever in all that is done under the sun.
Go, eat your bread with gladness, and drink your wine with a good heart, for God has already taken pleasure in your deeds.
At every time let your garments be white, and let oil not be lacking on your head.

See life with a wife whom you love, all the days of your vapour-life that he has given you under the sun, all the days of your vapour; for that is your portion in life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.
All that your hand finds to do, do with your strength, for there is no work or reckoning or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.

I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the mighty, nor also bread to the wise, nor also wealth to the discerning, nor also favour to the knowledgeable; for time and chance happen to them all.

For also, a person does not know his time. Like fish that are caught in an evil net, and like birds that are caught in the snare, so the children of humankind are ensnared at an evil time, when it falls upon them suddenly.
This too I have seen as wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:
A small city, and the men in it few; and a great king came against it and surrounded it, and built great siege works against it.
And there was found in it a poor wise man, and he delivered the city by his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
And I said, I: "Wisdom is better than strength," yet the wisdom of the poor is despised, and his words are not listened to.
The words of the wise, in quietness, are heard more than the cry of a ruler among dullards.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

ecclesiastes_10.t: Dead flies make the perfumer's oil stink and ferment; a little folly outweighs wisdom, outweighs honour.
A wise one's heart is to his right, but a dullard's heart is to his left.
And also on the way, when a fool goes, his heart is lacking, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness lays great sins to rest.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an inadvertence that goes out from before the ruler:
Folly is set in many high places, and the rich sit in a low place.
I have seen slaves on horses, and princes walking on the ground like slaves.
One who digs a pit will fall into it, and one who breaks through a wall — a snake will bite him.
One who quarries stones will be hurt by them; one who splits logs will be endangered by them.
If the iron is blunt and one has not sharpened the edges, then one must exert more strength; but the advantage of giving success is wisdom.
If the snake bites without charming, then there is no profit for the master of the tongue.
The words of a wise one's mouth are favour, but a dullard's lips swallow him.
The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly, and the end of his mouth is evil madness.
And the fool multiplies words. A person does not know what will be, and what will be after him — who can tell him?
The toil of dullards wearies him, for he does not know how to go to a city.
Woe to you, land, whose king is a youth, and whose princes eat in the morning!
How blessed are you, land, whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes eat at the proper time, for strength and not for drinking!
Through laziness the rafters sink, and through lowering of hands the house leaks.
For laughter they make food, and wine gladdens life, and money answers everything.
Even in your thought do not curse a king, and in the chambers of your bedroom do not curse a rich person; for a bird of the heavens will carry the sound, and an owner of wings will tell the matter.

ecclesiastes_11.t: Send your bread upon the face of the waters, for in the multitude of days you will find it.
Give a portion to seven, and also to eight, for you do not know what calamity will be on the earth.
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty it on the earth; and whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, the place where the tree falls, there it will be.
One who watches the wind will not sow, and one who looks at the clouds will not reap.
As you do not know what the way of the wind is, or how bones form in the womb of the full woman, so you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.
In the morning sow your seed, and at evening do not let your hand rest, for you do not know which will succeed, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.
And the light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
For if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in all of them, and let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. All that comes is vapour.

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart make you glad in the days of your young manhood; and walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgement.
And remove vexation from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for youth and the dawn of life are vapour.

ecclesiastes_12.t: And remember your Creator in the days of your young manhood, before the days of evil come and the years arrive of which you will say, "I have no pleasure in them";
before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;
in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the men of strength bend themselves, and the grinding women cease because they are few, and those who look through the windows grow dim;
and the doors on the street are shut, when the sound of the grinding is low, and one rises at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low;

also they are afraid of what is high, and terrors are in the way; and the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper-berry fails; for a person goes to his perpetual house, and the mourners go about in the street;
before the silver cord is snapped, and the golden bowl is crushed, and the jar is broken at the spring, and the wheel is crushed at the well;
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
Vapour of vapours, said the Qoheleth; everything is vapour.
And besides, that Qoheleth was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; and he weighed and searched out and arranged in order many proverbs.
Qoheleth sought to find words of delight, and what was written was uprightness — words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads, and like nails firmly fixed are the masters of collections; they are given from one Shepherd.
And besides these, my son, be warned: of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of flesh.
The end of the matter; everything has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of humankind.
For God will bring every deed into judgement, concerning every hidden thing, whether good or evil.

esther_1.t: And it was in the days of Ahasuerus — that Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush, a hundred and twenty-seven provinces —
in those days, when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his royalty which was in Susa the citadel,
in the third year of his reign he made a feast for all his officials and his servants — the army of Persia and Media, the nobles and the officials of the provinces before him —
when he showed the wealth of the splendour of his kingdom and the honour of the glory of his greatness, many days — a hundred and eighty days.

And when these days were completed, the king made for all the people found in Susa the citadel, from the greatest to the least, a feast of seven days, in the court of the garden of the king's pavilion.

White cloth, cotton and violet, held with cords of fine linen and purple on rods of silver and pillars of marble; couches of gold and silver on a pavement of porphyry and marble and mother-of-pearl and precious stones.
And drinks were served in vessels of gold, and the vessels differed one from another, and royal wine was abundant according to the hand of the king.
And the drinking was according to the law: no one compelled; for so the king had appointed for every chief of his household, to do according to the pleasure of each man.
Also Vashti the queen made a feast of women in the house of royalty which belonged to King Ahasuerus.

On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was good with wine, he said to Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha and Abagtha, Zethar and Carcas, the seven eunuchs who served before the face of King Ahasuerus,
to bring Vashti the queen before the king with a crown of royalty, to show the peoples and the officials her beauty — for she was good of appearance.
But Queen Vashti refused to come at the word of the king which was by the hand of the eunuchs. And the king became very angry, and his rage burned within him.
And the king said to the wise men who knew the times — for so was the king's manner before all who knew law and judgement —
and those close to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who saw the face of the king, who sat foremost in the kingdom —
"According to the law, what is to be done with Queen Vashti, because she did not do the command of King Ahasuerus by the hand of the eunuchs?"

And Memucan said before the king and the officials, "Not against the king alone has Queen Vashti done wrong, but against all the officials and against all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

"For the matter of the queen will go out to all the women, to make their husbands despicable in their eyes, when they say, 'King Ahasuerus said to bring Queen Vashti before him, and she did not come.'
"And this very day the noble ladies of Persia and Media who have heard the matter of the queen will say the same to all the king's officials — and there will be contempt and anger enough.

"If it is good to the king, let a royal word go out from before him, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it does not pass away: that Vashti shall not come before King Ahasuerus, and let the king give her royal position to another woman better than she.
"And the king's decree which he will make will be heard in all his kingdom — for it is great — and all the women will give honour to their husbands, from the greatest to the least."
And the word was good in the eyes of the king and the officials, and the king did according to the word of Memucan.

And he sent documents to all the provinces of the king, to each province according to its writing and to each people according to its language, that every man should be ruler in his own house and speak according to the language of his people.

esther_2.t: After these things, when the rage of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
And the king's young men who served him said, "Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king,

"and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them gather every beautiful young virgin to Susa the citadel, to the house of the women, into the hand of Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women; and let their ointments be given them.
"And the young woman who is good in the eyes of the king shall reign in place of Vashti." And the word was good in the eyes of the king, and he did so.
There was a Jewish man in Susa the citadel, and his name was Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,
who had been taken into exile from Jerusalem with the exiles who were taken into exile with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile.

And he was bringing up Hadassah — that is Esther — the daughter of his uncle, for she had neither father nor mother. And the young woman was beautiful of form and good of appearance; and at the death of her father and her mother, Mordecai took her to himself as a daughter.

And it was, when the king's word and his law were heard, and when many young women were gathered to Susa the citadel into the hand of Hegai, that Esther was taken to the house of the king, into the hand of Hegai, keeper of the women.

And the young woman was good in his eyes, and she bore loyalty before him, and he hurried her ointments and her portions, to give them to her, and the seven chosen young women to give her from the house of the king; and he moved her and her young women to the best place of the house of the women.
Esther had not told her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had commanded her that she should not tell.
And every single day Mordecai was walking back and forth before the court of the house of the women, to know the welfare of Esther and what was being done with her.

And when the turn of each young woman came to go in to King Ahasuerus, at the end of her having twelve months according to the regulation of the women — for so were the days of their ointments completed: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with balsam oils and with the ointments of the women —
then in this way the young woman would go in to the king: everything she asked for was given her to go with her from the house of the women to the house of the king.

In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to the second house of the women, into the hand of Shaashgaz the king's eunuch, keeper of the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was summoned by name.

And when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai — who had taken her to himself as a daughter — came to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, said. And Esther was bearing favour in the eyes of all who saw her.
And Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, to the house of his royalty, in the tenth month — that is the month of Tebeth — in the seventh year of his reign.

And the king loved Esther more than all the women, and she bore favour and loyalty before him more than all the virgins; and he set a crown of royalty on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
And the king made a great feast for all his officials and his servants — the feast of Esther — and he granted a remission to the provinces and gave a gift according to the hand of the king.
And when virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
Esther was not telling her kindred or her people, just as Mordecai had commanded her; and Esther was doing what Mordecai said, just as when she was under his guardianship.

In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs from the keepers of the threshold, became angry and sought to stretch out a hand against King Ahasuerus.
And the matter became known to Mordecai, and he told it to Esther the queen, and Esther spoke to the king in the name of Mordecai.
And the matter was investigated and found out, and the two of them were hanged on a gallows; and it was written in the book of the events of the days before the king.

esther_3.t: After these things King Ahasuerus made Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite great, and exalted him, and set his seat above all the officials who were with him.
And all the king's servants who were at the king's gate were kneeling and bowing down to Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. But Mordecai would not kneel and would not bow down.
And the king's servants who were at the king's gate said to Mordecai, "Why are you transgressing the king's commandment?"
And it was, when they spoke to him day after day and he did not listen to them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's words would stand — for he had told them that he was a Jew.
And Haman saw that Mordecai was not kneeling and bowing down to him, and Haman was filled with rage.

But it was contemptible in his eyes to stretch out a hand against Mordecai alone, for they had told him the people of Mordecai. So Haman sought to annihilate all the Jews who were in all the kingdom of Ahasuerus — the people of Mordecai.

In the first month — that is the month of Nisan — in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur (that is, the lot) before Haman, from day to day and from month to month, the twelfth — that is the month of Adar.

And Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is one people scattered and separated among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom, and their laws differ from every people's, and the king's laws they do not keep; and for the king it is not fitting to let them remain.
"If it is good to the king, let it be written to destroy them; and ten thousand talents of silver I will weigh out into the hands of those who do the work, to bring into the king's treasuries."
And the king removed his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the adversary of the Jews.
And the king said to Haman, "The silver is given to you, and the people, to do with them as is good in your eyes."

And the king's scribes were summoned in the first month, on the thirteenth day of it, and it was written according to all that Haman commanded, to the king's satraps and to the governors who were over each province, and to the officials of each people — each province according to its writing and each people according to its language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king's signet ring.

And documents were sent by the hand of the runners to all the king's provinces: to annihilate, to kill and to destroy all the Jews, from young to old, little ones and women, in one day, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month — that is the month of Adar — and to take their spoil as plunder.
A copy of the writing was to be given out as law in every single province, disclosed to all the peoples, so that they would be ready for that day.
The runners went out, hurried by the king's word, and the law was given in Susa the citadel. And the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was in confusion.

esther_4.t: And Mordecai knew all that had been done, and Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city and cried out a loud and bitter cry.
And he came as far as before the king's gate, for none may enter the king's gate in sackcloth clothing.

And in every single province, the place where the king's word and his law were reaching, there was great mourning for the Jews, and fasting and weeping and wailing; sackcloth and ashes were spread as a bed for many.
And Esther's maids and her eunuchs came and told her, and the queen was greatly distressed; and she sent garments to clothe Mordecai and to remove his sackcloth from him, but he did not accept them.
And Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and commanded him concerning Mordecai, to know what this was and why this was.
And Hathach went out to Mordecai, to the open square of the city which was before the king's gate.
And Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact amount of the silver that Haman had said he would weigh out to the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.

And he gave him a copy of the writing of the law which had been given in Susa to annihilate them, to show Esther and to tell her, and to command her to go to the king, to seek his favour and to make request before him for her people.
And Hathach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
And Esther said to Hathach and commanded him to Mordecai:

"All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who goes to the king, into the inner court, who is not summoned, there is one law: to be put to death — except for the one to whom the king extends the golden sceptre, and he lives. And I have not been summoned to come to the king these thirty days."
And they told Mordecai the words of Esther.
And Mordecai said to bring back to Esther: "Do not imagine in your own being that you will escape in the house of the king, out of all the Jews.

"For if you keep altogether silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, and you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether for a time like this you have reached royalty?"
And Esther said to bring back to Mordecai:

"Go, gather all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me: do not eat and do not drink, three days, night and day. I also and my maids will fast in the same way. And then I will go to the king, which is not according to the law — and if I have perished, I have perished."
And Mordecai passed on and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

esther_5.t: And it was on the third day that Esther put on royalty and stood in the inner court of the king's house, opposite the king's house; and the king was sitting on the throne of his royalty in the house of royalty, opposite the entrance of the house.

And it was, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she bore favour in his eyes, and the king extended to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. And Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre.
And the king said to her, "What is it to you, Queen Esther? And what is your request? Up to half the kingdom, and it shall be given you."
And Esther said, "If it is good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast that I have made for him."
And the king said, "Bring Haman quickly, to do the word of Esther." And the king and Haman came to the feast that Esther had made.
And the king said to Esther at the feast of wine, "What is your petition, and it shall be given you? And what is your request? Up to half the kingdom, and it shall be done."
And Esther answered and said, "My petition and my request —

"if I have found favour in the eyes of the king, and if it is good to the king to grant my petition and to do my request — let the king and Haman come to the feast that I will make for them, and tomorrow I will do according to the word of the king."
And Haman went out that day joyful and good of heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and he did not rise and did not tremble before him, Haman was filled with rage against Mordecai.
But Haman restrained himself and came to his house, and he sent and brought his friends and Zeresh his wife.

And Haman recounted to them the splendour of his wealth and the multitude of his sons, and all how the king had made him great, and how he had exalted him above the officials and the servants of the king.
And Haman said, "Moreover, Queen Esther let no one come with the king to the feast she had prepared except me; and tomorrow too I am invited by her, with the king.
"But all this is not enough for me, at any time when I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

And Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, "Let a gallows be made, fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king, and let them hang Mordecai on it; and go with the king to the feast joyful." And the word was good before Haman, and he made the gallows.

esther_6.t: On that night the king's sleep fled, and he said to bring the book of the records, the events of the days; and they were read aloud before the king.
And it was found written that Mordecai had told about Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs from the keepers of the threshold, who had sought to stretch out a hand against King Ahasuerus.
And the king said, "What honour and greatness has been done for Mordecai for this?" And the king's young men who served him said, "Nothing has been done with him."
And the king said, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had come to the outer court of the king's house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
And the king's young men said to him, "Here is Haman, standing in the court." And the king said, "Let him come in."

And Haman came in, and the king said to him, "What is to be done for the man in whose honour the king delights?" And Haman said in his heart, "To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to me?"
And Haman said to the king, "The man in whose honour the king delights —
"let them bring royal clothing that the king has worn, and a horse that the king has ridden, and on whose head a royal crown has been set;

"and let the clothing and the horse be put into the hand of a man from the king's officials, the nobles, and let them clothe the man in whose honour the king delights, and make him ride on the horse in the open square of the city, and proclaim before him, 'Thus it is done for the man in whose honour the king delights.'"
And the king said to Haman, "Hurry, take the clothing and the horse as you have said, and do so for Mordecai the Jew who sits at the king's gate. Do not let a word fall from all that you have said."

And Haman took the clothing and the horse, and clothed Mordecai, and made him ride in the open square of the city, and proclaimed before him, "Thus it is done for the man in whose honour the king delights."
And Mordecai returned to the king's gate; but Haman hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered.

And Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and to all his friends everything that had happened to him. And his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of the offspring of the Jews, you will not prevail against him — for falling you will fall before him."
They were still speaking with him when the king's eunuchs arrived, and they hurried to bring Haman to the feast that Esther had made.

esther_7.t: And the king and Haman came to drink with Esther the queen.

And the king said to Esther also on the second day, at the feast of wine, "What is your petition, Queen Esther, and it shall be given you? And what is your request? Up to half the kingdom, and it shall be done."
And Queen Esther answered and said, "If I have found favour in your eyes, O king, and if it is good to the king — let my life be given me for my petition, and my people for my request.

"For we have been sold, I and my people, to annihilate, to kill and to destroy. And if we had been sold as male and female slaves, I would have kept silent — for the distress would not be worth the king's injury."
And King Ahasuerus said — and he said to Queen Esther — "Who is he, and where is he, who has filled his heart to do this?"
And Esther said, "A man, an adversary and an enemy — this evil Haman!" And Haman was terrified before the king and the queen.

And the king rose in his rage from the feast of wine into the garden of the pavilion; but Haman stood to plead for his life from Queen Esther, for he saw that harm was determined against him from the king.

And the king returned from the garden of the pavilion to the house of the feast of wine, and Haman was falling on the couch that Esther was on. And the king said, "Will he even subdue the queen with me in the house?" The word went out from the king's mouth, and they covered Haman's face.

And Harbona, one of the eunuchs, said before the king, "Moreover, here is the gallows that Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, standing at Haman's house, fifty cubits high." And the king said, "Hang him on it."
And they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. And the rage of the king subsided.

esther_8.t: On that day King Ahasuerus gave to Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews; and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her.
And the king removed his signet ring, which he had taken away from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai; and Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
And Esther spoke again before the king, and fell before his feet and wept, and pleaded with him to take away the evil of Haman the Agagite and his plan which he had planned against the Jews.
And the king extended to Esther the golden sceptre, and Esther arose and stood before the king.

And she said, "If it is good to the king, and if I have found favour before him, and the matter is proper before the king, and I am good in his eyes — let it be written to revoke the letters, the plan of Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king's provinces.
"For how could I bear to look on the evil that will find my people? And how could I bear to look on the destruction of my kindred?"

And King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "See, I have given the house of Haman to Esther, and him they have hanged on the gallows, because he stretched out his hand against the Jews.

"And you, write concerning the Jews as is good in your eyes, in the name of the king, and seal it with the king's signet ring; for a writing that is written in the name of the king and sealed with the king's signet ring cannot be revoked."

And the king's scribes were summoned at that time, in the third month — that is the month of Sivan — on the twenty-third of it, and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded, to the Jews and to the satraps and the governors and the officials of the provinces from India to Cush, a hundred and twenty-seven provinces — each province according to its writing and each people according to its language, and to the Jews according to their writing and their language.
And he wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed it with the king's signet ring, and sent letters by the hand of the couriers on horses, riders of the royal steeds, sons of the mares.

In them the king permitted the Jews who were in every single city to assemble and to make a stand for their life: to annihilate and to kill and to destroy every armed force of a people or province attacking them, little ones and women, and to take their spoil as plunder —
on one day, in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month — that is the month of Adar.
A copy of the writing was to be given out as law in every single province, disclosed to all the peoples, and that the Jews should be ready for that day, to avenge themselves on their enemies.
The couriers, riders of the royal steeds, went out hastened and hurried by the king's word; and the law was given in Susa the citadel.
And Mordecai went out from before the king in royal clothing of violet and white, and a great crown of gold, and a robe of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted for joy and rejoiced.
For the Jews there was light and gladness and joy and honour.

And in every single province and in every single city, the place where the king's word and his law were reaching, there was gladness and joy for the Jews, a feast and a good day; and many from the peoples of the land were becoming Jews, for the dread of the Jews had fallen on them.

esther_9.t: And in the twelfth month — that is the month of Adar — on the thirteenth day of it, when the king's word and his law drew near to be done, on the day when the enemies of the Jews had hoped to master them — and it was reversed: the Jews themselves mastered those who hated them —

the Jews assembled in their cities, in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, to stretch out a hand against those who sought their harm; and no one stood before them, for the dread of them had fallen on all the peoples.
And all the officials of the provinces, and the satraps and the governors and those who did the king's work, were supporting the Jews, for the dread of Mordecai had fallen on them.
For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his report was going out into all the provinces; for the man Mordecai was going on and growing great.
And the Jews struck down all their enemies with a striking of sword and slaughter and destruction, and did to those who hated them according to their pleasure.
And in Susa the citadel the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
and Parshandatha and Dalphon and Aspatha
and Poratha and Adalia and Aridatha
and Parmashta and Arisai and Aridai and Vaizatha —
the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the adversary of the Jews, they killed; but on the plunder they did not stretch out their hand.
On that day the number of those killed in Susa the citadel came before the king.

And the king said to Queen Esther, "In Susa the citadel the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men, and the ten sons of Haman. In the rest of the king's provinces, what have they done? And what is your petition? It shall be given you. And what is your further request? It shall be done."

And Esther said, "If it is good to the king, let it be permitted tomorrow also to the Jews who are in Susa to do according to the law of this day; and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows."
And the king said that it should be done so; and a law was given in Susa, and the ten sons of Haman they hanged.
And the Jews who were in Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, and killed in Susa three hundred men; but on the plunder they did not stretch out their hand.

And the rest of the Jews who were in the king's provinces assembled and made a stand for their life, and had rest from their enemies, and killed among those who hated them seventy-five thousand; but on the plunder they did not stretch out their hand.
on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar; and they rested on the fourteenth of it, and made it a day of feasting and joy.
And the Jews who were in Susa assembled on the thirteenth of it and on the fourteenth of it, and rested on the fifteenth of it, and made it a day of feasting and joy.

Therefore the Jews of the open country, who live in the towns of the open regions, observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as joy and feasting, and a good day, and the sending of portions to one another.
And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, the near and the far,
to impose on them that they should observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and the fifteenth day of it, in every single year,

as the days on which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned for them from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day — to make them days of feasting and joy, and the sending of portions to one another, and gifts to the needy.
And the Jews accepted what they had begun to do, and what Mordecai had written to them.
For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the adversary of all the Jews, had planned against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur — that is, the lot — to crush them and to destroy them.
But when it came before the king, he said with the letter, "Let his evil plan, which he planned against the Jews, return on his own head"; and they hanged him and his sons on the gallows.
Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of the Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and what they had seen concerning this, and what had happened to them,

the Jews imposed and accepted on themselves and on their offspring and on all who joined themselves to them, so that it should not pass away, that they would observe these two days according to their writing and according to their appointed time, in every single year;

and that these days would be remembered and observed in every generation, every clan, every province and every city; and that these days of Purim would not pass away from among the Jews, and their remembrance would not cease from their offspring.
And Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
And he sent letters to all the Jews, to the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus — words of peace and faithfulness —

to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had imposed on them, and just as they had imposed on themselves and on their offspring — the words of the fasts and their cry of distress.
And the command of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.

esther_10.t: And King Ahasuerus laid a levy on the land and on the islands of the sea.

And all the work of his power and his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, with which the king made him great — are they not written on the book of the events of the days of the kings of Media and Persia?
For Mordecai the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and acceptable to the multitude of his brothers — seeking good for his people, and speaking peace to all his offspring.

exodus_1.t: And these [are] the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob; each man and his household they came.
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah;
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin;
Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
And it was, every person coming out of the thigh of Jacob [was] seventy persons; and Joseph was in Egypt.
And Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
And the sons of Israel were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and became mighty with muchness, muchness; and the land was filled with them.
And there arose a new king over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
And he said to his people, 'Look, the people of the sons of Israel [is] more numerous and mightier than we.'
'Come, let us deal wisely with it, lest it multiply, and it will be that when war happens, it too will be added to those who hate us, and it will fight against us and go up from the land.'
And they set over it overseers of forced-labour gangs, so as to afflict it with their burdens; and it built storage cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses.
And just as they afflicted it, so it multiplied and so it spread; and they felt dread because of the sons of Israel.
And Egypt made the sons of Israel serve with harshness.
And they made their lives bitter with hard labour, with mortar and with bricks and with every labour in the field — all their labour that they made them labour with harshness.
And the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one [was] Shiphrah and the name of the second [was] Puah,
and he said, 'When you assist the Hebrew women as midwives, you shall look at the two stones: if it is a son, you shall kill him; and if it is a daughter, she shall live.'
And the midwives feared God, and they did not do as the king of Egypt had spoken to them; and they let the male children live.
And the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, 'Why have you done this thing and let the male children live?'
And the midwives said to Pharaoh, 'Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous — before the midwife comes to them, they have given birth.'
And God did good to the midwives; and the people multiplied and became very mighty.
And it was, because the midwives feared God, that he made them households.
And Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, 'Every son that is born you shall throw into the River, and every daughter you shall let live.'

exodus_2.t: And a man from the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi.
And the woman conceived and bore a son; and she saw him, that he [was] good, and she hid him three months.

And she was not able to hide him any longer, and she took for him a chest of papyrus and sealed it with bitumen and with pitch; and she put the child in it and put [it] among the reeds at the bank of the River.
And his sister stationed herself at a distance, to know what would be done to him.
And the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe at the River, and her attendants were walking beside the River; and she saw the chest among the reeds and sent her maid, and she fetched it.
And she opened [it] and saw him — the child — and here, a boy weeping; and she had compassion on him and said, 'This is one of the children of the Hebrews.'
And his sister said to the daughter of Pharaoh, 'Shall I go and call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrew women, so that she may nurse the child for you?'
And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, 'Go.' And the young woman went and called the mother of the child.
And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, 'Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will give your wages.' And the woman took the child and nursed him.
And the child grew, and she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he became a son to her; and she called his name Moses, and she said, 'Because I drew him out of the water.'
And it was in those days, and Moses grew up and went out to his brothers and looked on their burdens; and he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his brothers.
And he turned this way and that way and saw that there was no man; and he struck the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
And he went out on the second day, and here, two Hebrew men struggling together; and he said to the guilty one, 'Why are you striking your companion?'
And he said, 'Who appointed you a man, a chief and a judge over us? Are you saying [you will] kill me as you killed the Egyptian?' And Moses was afraid and said, 'Truly the matter is known.'
And Pharaoh heard this matter and sought to kill Moses; and Moses fled from before Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian, and he sat down by the well.
And the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
And the shepherds came and drove them away; and Moses arose and delivered them and watered their flock.
And they came to Reuel their father, and he said, 'Why have you hurried to come today?'
And they said, 'An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and he even drew, drew water for us and watered the flock.'
And he said to his daughters, 'And where is he? Why is this — you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.'
And Moses was willing to dwell with the man; and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses.
And she bore a son, and he called his name Gershom, for he said, 'A sojourner I have been in a foreign land.'
And it was in those many days that the king of Egypt died; and the sons of Israel groaned from the labour and cried out, and their cry for help went up to God from the labour.
And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
And God saw the sons of Israel, and God knew.

exodus_3.t: And Moses was pasturing the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he drove the flock behind the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
And the messenger of YHWH appeared to him in a flame of fire from the middle of the bush; and he looked, and here, the bush burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
And Moses said, 'Let me turn aside now and see this great sight — why the bush is not burning up.'
And YHWH saw that he had turned aside to look, and God called to him from the middle of the bush and said, 'Moses, Moses.' And he said, 'Here I am.'
And he said, 'Do not draw near here. Take off your sandals from on your feet, for the place on which you are standing, it is ground of holiness.'
And he said, 'I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
And YHWH said, 'Seeing I have seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their cry of distress because of its taskmasters, for I know its pains.'

'And I have come down to deliver it from the hand of Egypt and to bring it up from that land to a good and spacious land, to a land flowing with milk and honey — to the place of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.'
'And now, here, the cry of distress of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which Egypt is oppressing them.'
'And now, go, and I will send you to Pharaoh; and bring out my people, the sons of Israel, from Egypt.'
And Moses said to God, 'Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and that I should bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt?'
And he said, 'Because I will be with you; and this is the sign for you that I have sent you: when you bring the people out from Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain.'

And Moses said to God, 'Here, I am going to the sons of Israel and I will say to them, "The God of your fathers has sent me to you," and they will say to me, "What is his name?" — what shall I say to them?'
And God said to Moses, 'I will be that which I will be.' And he said, 'Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: I-will-be has sent me to you.'

And God said further to Moses, 'Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: YHWH, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation.'

'Go, and you shall gather the elders of Israel and say to them, "YHWH, the God of your fathers, has appeared to me — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — saying: Attending I have attended to you and to what has been done to you in Egypt."'

'And I have said, "I will bring you up from the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey."'

'And they will listen to your voice; and you shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, "YHWH, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now let us go, please, a journey of three days into the wilderness, and let us sacrifice to YHWH our God."'
'And I know that the king of Egypt will not permit you to go — and not by a strong hand.'
'And I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders that I will do in its midst; and after that he will let you go.'
'And I will give this people favour in the eyes of Egypt; and it will be that when you go, you will not go empty.'

'And each woman shall ask of her neighbour and of the woman sojourning in her house articles of silver and articles of gold and clothing; and you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters, and you shall plunder Egypt.'

exodus_4.t: And Moses answered and said, 'And here — they will not believe me and will not listen to my voice, for they will say, "YHWH has not appeared to you."'
And YHWH said to him, 'What is this in your hand?' And he said, 'A staff.'
And he said, 'Throw it to the ground.' And he threw it to the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
And YHWH said to Moses, 'Stretch out your hand and take hold of its tail.' And he stretched out his hand and took hold of it, and it became a staff in his palm.
'— so that they may believe that YHWH, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.'
And YHWH said to him further, 'Put your hand now into your bosom.' And he put his hand into his bosom and brought it out, and here — his hand was scale-diseased, like the snow.
And he said, 'Return your hand to your bosom.' And he returned his hand to his bosom and brought it out from his bosom, and here — it had turned back like his flesh.
'And it will be, if they do not believe you and do not listen to the voice of the former sign, then they will believe the voice of the latter sign.'

'And it will be, if they do not believe even these two signs and do not listen to your voice, then you shall take from the waters of the River and pour them out on the dry ground; and the waters that you take from the River will become blood on the dry ground.'

And Moses said to YHWH, 'Please, my Lord — I am not a man of words, neither from yesterday nor from the day before, nor from the time you spoke to your servant; for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue.'
And YHWH said to him, 'Who made a mouth for the human being? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, YHWH?'
'And now, go; and I will be with your mouth and will teach you what you shall speak.'
And he said, 'Please, my Lord — send, please, by the hand of whomever you will send.'

And the anger of YHWH burned against Moses, and he said, 'Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that speaking he will speak. And also, here, he is coming out to meet you, and he will see you and be glad in his heart.'
'And you shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth; and I will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you both what you shall do.'
'And he will speak for you to the people; and it will be that he will become a mouth for you, and you will become God for him.'
'And this staff you shall take in your hand, with which you shall do the signs.'

And Moses went and returned to Jether his father-in-law and said to him, 'Let me go now and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive.' And Jethro said to Moses, 'Go in peace.'
And YHWH said to Moses in Midian, 'Go, return to Egypt, for all the men who sought your life have died.'
And Moses took his wife and his sons and made them ride on the donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt; and Moses took the staff of God in his hand.

And YHWH said to Moses, 'When you go to return to Egypt, see all the wonders that I have put in your hand, and do them before Pharaoh. But I will make his heart strong, and he will not let the people go.'
'And you shall say to Pharaoh, "Thus says YHWH: Israel is my son, my firstborn."'
'And I said to you, "Let my son go, that he may serve me" — and you refused to let him go. Here, I am about to kill your son, your firstborn.'
And it was on the way, at the lodging place, that YHWH met him and sought to kill him.
And Zipporah took a flint and cut off the foreskin of her son and made it touch his feet; and she said, 'Truly you are a bridegroom of bloods to me.'
And he withdrew from him. Then she said, 'A bridegroom of bloods,' with respect to the circumcision.
And YHWH said to Aaron, 'Go to meet Moses, to the wilderness.' And he went and met him at the mountain of God, and he kissed him.
And Moses told Aaron all the words of YHWH with which he had sent him, and all the signs that he had commanded him.
And Moses and Aaron went, and they gathered all the elders of the sons of Israel.
And Aaron spoke all the words that YHWH had spoken to Moses, and he did the signs before the eyes of the people.
And the people believed; and they heard that YHWH had attended to the sons of Israel and that he had seen their affliction, and they bowed low and prostrated themselves.

exodus_5.t: And afterwards Moses and Aaron went and said to Pharaoh, 'Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Let my people go, that they may hold a festival to me in the wilderness.'
And Pharaoh said, 'Who is YHWH, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go? I do not know YHWH, and I will also not let Israel go.'

And they said, 'The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Let us go, please, a journey of three days into the wilderness, and let us sacrifice to YHWH our God, lest he fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword.'
And the king of Egypt said to them, 'Why, Moses and Aaron, are you causing the people to refrain from its works? Go to your burdens.'
And Pharaoh said, 'Here, the people of the land are now many, and you would make them cease from their burdens.'
And Pharaoh commanded on that day the taskmasters over the people and its foremen, saying,
'You shall not continue to give straw to the people to make the bricks as yesterday and the day before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.'

'And the measure of the bricks that they were making yesterday and the day before you shall place on them; you shall not reduce from it. For they are idle — therefore they are crying out, saying, "Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God."'
'Let the labour be heavy on the men, and let them work at it; and let them not pay attention to words of falsehood.'
And the taskmasters of the people and its foremen went out and said to the people, saying, 'Thus says Pharaoh: I am not giving you straw.'
'You — go, get straw for yourselves from wherever you find it; for nothing is reduced from your labour.'
And the people scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for the straw.
And the taskmasters were pressing them, saying, 'Complete your works, the matter of a day in its day, as when there was straw.'

And the foremen of the sons of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were struck, saying, 'Why have you not completed your prescribed portion of brickmaking as yesterday and the day before, both yesterday and today?'
And the foremen of the sons of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, 'Why do you do thus to your servants?'
'Straw is not given to your servants, and they say to us, "Make bricks!" And here, your servants are being struck — and you have sinned, your people.'
And he said, 'You are idle, idle! Therefore you are saying, "Let us go, let us sacrifice to YHWH."'
'And now, go, work! And straw will not be given to you, and you shall give the measure of bricks.'
And the foremen of the sons of Israel saw themselves in trouble, when it was said, 'You shall not reduce from your bricks, the matter of a day in its day.'
And they met Moses and Aaron standing to meet them as they came out from Pharaoh.
And they said to them, 'May YHWH look upon you and judge — you who have made our odour stink in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us.'
And Moses returned to YHWH and said, 'My Lord, why have you done harm to this people? Why is this — you sent me?'
'And from the time I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has done harm to this people; and delivering, you have not delivered your people.'

exodus_6.t: And YHWH said to Moses, 'Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh: for by a strong hand he will let them go, and by a strong hand he will drive them out from his land.'
And God spoke to Moses and said to him, 'I am YHWH.'
'And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty; and by my name YHWH I did not make myself known to them.'
'And I also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings in which they sojourned.'
'And I have also heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom Egypt is making to serve, and I have remembered my covenant.'

'Therefore say to the sons of Israel: I am YHWH, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of Egypt, and I will deliver you from their labour, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great acts of judgement.'
'And I will take you to myself for a people, and I will be God for you; and you will know that I am YHWH your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt.'
'And I will bring you into the land that I lifted my hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you as a possession. I am YHWH.'
And Moses spoke thus to the sons of Israel; but they did not listen to Moses, from shortness of spirit and from hard labour.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
'Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he may let the sons of Israel go out from his land.'
And Moses spoke before YHWH, saying, 'Here — the sons of Israel have not listened to me; and how will Pharaoh listen to me, and I am uncircumcised of lips?'
And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron and commanded them concerning the sons of Israel and concerning Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the sons of Israel out from the land of Egypt.
These are the heads of their fathers' houses. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These are the clans of Reuben.
And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jakin and Zohar, and Shaul the son of the Canaanite woman. These are the clans of Simeon.
And these are the names of the sons of Levi by their generations: Gershon and Kohath and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, by their clans.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel. And the years of the life of Kohath were a hundred and thirty-three years.
And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levite by their generations.
And Amram took Jochebed his father's sister as his wife, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
And the sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zikri.
And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael and Elzaphan and Sithri.
And Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as his wife, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And the sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph. These are the clans of the Korahite.
And Eleazar the son of Aaron took for himself one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife, and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers of the Levites by their clans.
That is the Aaron and Moses to whom YHWH said, 'Bring the sons of Israel out from the land of Egypt by their hosts.'
They are the ones speaking to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the sons of Israel out from Egypt. That is Moses and Aaron.
And it was on the day YHWH spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
that YHWH spoke to Moses, saying, 'I am YHWH. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you.'
And Moses said before YHWH, 'Here — I am uncircumcised of lips; and how will Pharaoh listen to me?'

exodus_7.t: And YHWH said to Moses: See, I have made you God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
You shall speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, and he shall let the sons of Israel go from his land.
And I myself will make hard the heart of Pharaoh, and I will multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I will set my hand against Egypt, and I will bring out my hosts, my people the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with great acts of judgement.
And Egypt will know that I am YHWH when I stretch out my hand over Egypt and bring out the sons of Israel from among them.
And Moses and Aaron did just as YHWH commanded them; so they did.
And Moses was a son of eighty years, and Aaron a son of eighty-three years, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
And YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, Give for yourselves a wonder — then you shall say to Aaron, Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh; let it become a dragon.
And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and they did so, just as YHWH had commanded; and Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a dragon.
And Pharaoh also called for the wise men and for the sorcerers, and they also — the ritual experts of Egypt — did the same by their secret arts.
And they threw down each man his staff, and they became dragons; and the staff of Aaron swallowed their staffs.
And the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not listen to them, just as YHWH had said.
And YHWH said to Moses: The heart of Pharaoh is heavy; he has refused to let the people go.

Go to Pharaoh in the morning — see, he is going out to the water — and you shall station yourself to meet him on the bank of the Nile; and the staff that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand.
And you shall say to him: YHWH, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness. And see, you have not listened until now.
Thus says YHWH: By this you shall know that I am YHWH. See, I am about to strike with the staff that is in my hand upon the waters that are in the Nile, and they will be turned to blood.
And the fish that is in the Nile will die, and the Nile will stink, and Egypt will grow weary of drinking water from the Nile.

And YHWH said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt — over their rivers, over their canals, and over their ponds, and over every pool of their waters — and they will become blood; and there will be blood in all the land of Egypt, and in the wood and in the stone.

And Moses and Aaron did so, just as YHWH had commanded; and he raised the staff and struck the waters that were in the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants, and all the waters that were in the Nile were turned to blood.
And the fish that was in the Nile died, and the Nile stank, and Egypt was not able to drink water from the Nile; and the blood was in all the land of Egypt.
And the ritual experts of Egypt did the same by their secret arts; and the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not listen to them, just as YHWH had said.
And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart even to this.
And all Egypt dug around the Nile for water to drink, for they were not able to drink from the waters of the Nile.
And seven days were completed after YHWH struck the Nile.

exodus_8.t: And YHWH said to Moses: Go to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says YHWH: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
And if you refuse to let them go, see, I am about to strike down all your territory with frogs.

And the Nile will swarm with frogs, and they will go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber and onto your bed, and into the house of your servants and among your people, and into your ovens and into your kneading troughs.
And upon you and upon your people and upon all your servants the frogs will go up.
And YHWH said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the ponds, and bring up the frogs onto the land of Egypt.
And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frog came up and covered the land of Egypt.
And the ritual experts did the same by their secret arts, and they brought up the frogs onto the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron and said: Plead with YHWH, that he may remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice to YHWH.

And Moses said to Pharaoh: Take the honour over me — for when shall I plead for you and for your servants and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the Nile will they remain.
And he said: For tomorrow. And he said: According to your word — so that you may know that there is none like YHWH our God.
And the frogs will depart from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people; only in the Nile will they remain.
And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to YHWH concerning the matter of the frogs that he had set upon Pharaoh.
And YHWH did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.
And they piled them up, heaps, heaps; and the land stank.
And Pharaoh saw that there was relief, and he made his heart heavy, and he did not listen to them, just as YHWH had said.
And YHWH said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, and it will become gnats in all the land of Egypt.

And they did so; and Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and the gnat was on humankind and on livestock. All the dust of the earth became gnats in all the land of Egypt.
And the ritual experts did the same by their secret arts, to bring forth the gnats, but they were not able; and the gnat was on humankind and on livestock.
And the ritual experts said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God. And the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not listen to them, just as YHWH had said.
And YHWH said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh — see, he is going out to the water — and say to him: Thus says YHWH: Let my people go, that they may serve me.

For if you are not letting my people go, see, I am about to send upon you and upon your servants and upon your people and into your houses the swarm; and the houses of Egypt will be filled with the swarm, and also the ground on which they are.
And I will distinguish on that day the land of Goshen, where my people are standing, so that there will be no swarm there — so that you may know that I am YHWH in the midst of the land.
And I will set a division between my people and your people; tomorrow this sign will happen.
And YHWH did so, and a heavy swarm came into the house of Pharaoh and the house of his servants; and in all the land of Egypt the land was ruined because of the swarm.
And Pharaoh called to Moses and to Aaron and said: Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.
And Moses said: It is not right to do so, for we would sacrifice the abomination of Egypt to YHWH our God. If we sacrifice the abomination of Egypt before their eyes, will they not stone us?
A journey of three days we will go into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to YHWH our God, just as he says to us.
And Pharaoh said: I will let you go, and you shall sacrifice to YHWH your God in the wilderness; only going far you shall not go far. Plead for me.

And Moses said: See, I am going out from you, and I will plead with YHWH, and the swarm will depart from Pharaoh, from his servants and from his people tomorrow. Only let not Pharaoh again deal deceitfully, by not letting the people go to sacrifice to YHWH.
And Moses went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with YHWH.
And YHWH did according to the word of Moses, and he removed the swarm from Pharaoh, from his servants and from his people; not one remained.
And Pharaoh made his heart heavy also at this time, and he did not let the people go.

exodus_9.t: And YHWH said to Moses: Go to Pharaoh and speak to him: Thus says YHWH, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
For if you refuse to let them go, and you are still keeping a strong hold on them —
see, the hand of YHWH is about to be on your livestock that are in the field — on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the cattle and on the flocks — a very heavy pestilence.
And YHWH will distinguish between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, and nothing will die of all that belongs to the sons of Israel.
And YHWH set an appointed time, saying: Tomorrow YHWH will do this thing in the land.
And YHWH did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of Egypt died; but of the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died.
And Pharaoh sent, and see, not even one of the livestock of Israel had died. And the heart of Pharaoh was heavy, and he did not let the people go.
And YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron: Take for yourselves the fullness of your two hands of soot of a furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the heavens before the eyes of Pharaoh.
And it will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become on humankind and on livestock boils breaking out in blisters in all the land of Egypt.
And they took the soot of the furnace and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses sprinkled it toward the heavens, and it became boils, blisters breaking out, on humankind and on livestock.
And the ritual experts were not able to stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the ritual experts and on all Egypt.
And YHWH made the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he did not listen to them, just as YHWH had said to Moses.
And YHWH said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says YHWH, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
For at this time I am sending all my plagues to your heart, and on your servants and on your people, in order that you may know that there is none like me in all the earth.
For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with the pestilence, and you would have been wiped out from the earth.
But for this reason I have kept you alive: in order to make you see my power, and so that my name may be recounted in all the earth.
You are still exalting yourself over my people, not letting them go.
See, at about this time tomorrow I am about to rain down very heavy hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.

And now send, bring to shelter your livestock and all that you have in the field. Every human and animal that is found in the field and is not gathered into the house — the hail will come down on them, and they will die.
The one among the servants of Pharaoh who feared the word of YHWH made his servants and his livestock flee into the houses.
And whoever did not set his heart to the word of YHWH left his servants and his livestock in the field.

And YHWH said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, and let there be hail in all the land of Egypt — on humankind and on livestock and on all the vegetation of the field, in the land of Egypt.
And Moses stretched out his staff toward the heavens, and YHWH gave thunder and hail, and fire went to the ground; and YHWH rained hail on the land of Egypt.
And there was hail, and fire flashing in the midst of the hail — very heavy, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt everything that was in the field, from humankind to livestock; and the hail struck all the vegetation of the field, and it shattered every tree of the field.
Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, there was no hail.
And Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and for Aaron, and said to them: I have sinned this time. YHWH is the righteous one, and I and my people are the guilty ones.
Plead with YHWH — and enough of there being thunder of God and hail — and I will let you go, and you shall not stay any longer.
And Moses said to him: As I go out of the city I will spread out my hands to YHWH; the thunder will cease and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth belongs to YHWH.
