But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear before YHWH God.
And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was in bud.
But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they are late crops.
And Moses went out from Pharaoh, out of the city, and spread out his hands to YHWH; and the thunder and the hail ceased, and rain was not poured out on the ground.
And Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, and he sinned again, and he made his heart heavy, he and his servants.
And the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not let the sons of Israel go, just as YHWH had said by the hand of Moses.

exodus_10.t: And YHWH said to Moses: Go to Pharaoh, for I myself have made his heart heavy and the heart of his servants, so that I may set these signs of mine in his midst,
and so that you may recount in the ears of your son and your son's son how I dealt ruthlessly with Egypt, and my signs that I set among them; and you will know that I am YHWH.
And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and said to him: Thus says YHWH, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, that they may serve me.
For if you refuse to let my people go, see, I am about to bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.

And it will cover the eye of the land, and no one will be able to see the land; and it will eat the remainder of what escaped, what is left to you from the hail, and it will eat every tree that sprouts for you from the field.

And your houses will be filled, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all Egypt — such as your fathers and your fathers' fathers have not seen from the day they were on the land until this day. And he turned and went out from Pharaoh.
And the servants of Pharaoh said to him: How long will this one be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve YHWH their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt has perished?
And Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them: Go, serve YHWH your God. Who and who are the ones going?
And Moses said: With our young and with our old we will go; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds we will go, for it is a festival of YHWH for us.
And he said to them: May YHWH be so with you, as I let you go and your little ones! See that evil is before your faces.
Not so! Go, the men, and serve YHWH, for that is what you are seeking. And they were driven out from the face of Pharaoh.
And YHWH said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, so that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat all the vegetation of the land, all that the hail left.
And Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and YHWH drove an east wind in the land all that day and all the night. The morning came, and the east wind carried the locusts.
And the locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled in all the territory of Egypt, very heavy. Before it there had not been such locusts as it, and after it there will not be such.

And it covered the eye of all the land, and the land grew dark; and it ate all the vegetation of the land and all the fruit of the tree that the hail had left. And no greenery was left on the tree or on the vegetation of the field in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh hurried to call for Moses and for Aaron, and said: I have sinned against YHWH your God and against you.
And now, forgive my sin only this time, and plead with YHWH your God, that he may remove from upon me only this death.
And he went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with YHWH.
And YHWH turned a very strong sea wind, and it carried away the locusts and drove them into the Sea of Reeds. Not one locust remained in all the territory of Egypt.
And YHWH made the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he did not let the sons of Israel go.
And YHWH said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt — and let the darkness be felt.
And Moses stretched out his hand toward the heavens, and there was darkness of gloom in all the land of Egypt three days.
They did not see one another, and no one rose from where he was for three days; but for all the sons of Israel there was light in their dwellings.
And Pharaoh called to Moses and said: Go, serve YHWH; only your flocks and your herds shall be detained. Even your little ones may go with you.
And Moses said: You yourself must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, and we will offer them to YHWH our God.
And also our livestock must go with us; not a hoof shall remain, for from it we will take to serve YHWH our God; and we ourselves do not know with what we will serve YHWH until we come there.
And YHWH made the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he was not willing to let them go.
And Pharaoh said to him: Go from me! Take heed to yourself — do not see my face again, for on the day you see my face you will die.
And Moses said: Rightly you have spoken. I will not see your face again.

exodus_11.t: And YHWH said to Moses: Yet one affliction I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt; after that he will let you go from here. When he lets you go completely, driving out he will drive you out from here.
Speak now in the ears of the people, and let each man ask from his neighbour and each woman from her neighbour articles of silver and articles of gold.
And YHWH gave the people favour in the eyes of Egypt. Also the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh and in the eyes of the people.
And Moses said: Thus says YHWH: About the middle of the night I am going out into the midst of Egypt.

And every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the firstborn of the maidservant who is behind the hand-mill, and every firstborn of livestock.
And there will be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as has not happened and such as will not happen again.
But against all the sons of Israel not a dog will sharpen its tongue, from human to livestock — so that you may know that YHWH makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.

And all these your servants will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, Go out, you and all the people who are at your feet. And after that I will go out. And he went out from Pharaoh in heat of anger.
And YHWH said to Moses: Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that my wonders may be many in the land of Egypt.
And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh; and YHWH made the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he did not let the sons of Israel go from his land.

exodus_12.t: And YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying:
This month shall be for you the beginning of months; it shall be the first for you of the months of the year.
Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month let them take for themselves each man a flock animal for a father's household, a flock animal for the household.

And if the household is too small for a flock animal, then he and his neighbour who is near his house shall take according to the number of persons; each according to what he eats you shall reckon for the flock animal.
A flock animal unblemished, male, a year old, shall be yours; from the sheep or from the goats you shall take it.
And it shall be for you for safekeeping until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it between the two evenings.
And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they eat it.
And they shall eat the flesh in this night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread; with bitter herbs they shall eat it.
Do not eat any of it raw, or boiled — boiled in water — but roasted with fire: its head with its legs and with its entrails.
And you shall not leave any of it until morning; and what is left of it until morning you shall burn with fire.
And thus you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand. And you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to YHWH.

And I will pass through the land of Egypt in this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from humankind to livestock; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute acts of judgement. I am YHWH.
And the blood shall be for you a sign on the houses where you are; and I will see the blood and pass over you, and there shall be no blow among you for destruction when I strike in the land of Egypt.
And this day shall be for you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a festival to YHWH; throughout your generations, as a statute of perpetuity, you shall celebrate it.

Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. Surely on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses, for anyone who eats what is leavened — that person shall be cut off from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
And on the first day there shall be a holy assembly, and on the seventh day a holy assembly for you. No work shall be done on them; only what is eaten by every person — that alone may be done by you.
And you shall keep the unleavened bread, for on this very day I brought your hosts out from the land of Egypt; and you shall keep this day throughout your generations, a statute of perpetuity.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.
Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses, for anyone who eats anything leavened — that person shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether a sojourner or a native of the land.
You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.
And Moses called for all the elders of Israel and said to them: Draw out and take for yourselves flock animals according to your clans, and slaughter the Passover.

And you shall take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the bowl, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood that is in the bowl. And none of you shall go out from the door of his house until morning.

And YHWH will pass through to strike down Egypt, and he will see the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, and YHWH will pass over the door and will not allow the destroyer to come into your houses to strike down.
And you shall keep this word as a decree for you and for your sons until perpetuity.
And it shall be, when you come into the land that YHWH will give you, just as he said, that you shall keep this service.
And it shall be, when your sons say to you: What is this service to you? —

then you shall say: It is a sacrifice of Passover to YHWH, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when he struck down Egypt, and our houses he delivered. And the people bowed low and bowed down.
And the sons of Israel went and did just as YHWH had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.

And it was in the middle of the night, and YHWH struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the house of the pit, and every firstborn of livestock.
And Pharaoh rose in the night, he and all his servants and all Egypt, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was no house where there was not one dead.
And he called for Moses and for Aaron in the night and said: Rise, go out from among my people, both you and the sons of Israel; and go, serve YHWH as you have said.
Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and go. And bless me also.
And Egypt was strong upon the people, to hurry to let them go from the land, for they said: We are all dying.
And the people carried off their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs bound up in their clothes on their shoulder.
And the sons of Israel did according to the word of Moses, and they asked from Egypt articles of silver and articles of gold and clothing.
And YHWH gave the people favour in the eyes of Egypt, and they granted their request; and they plundered Egypt.
And the sons of Israel set out from Rameses toward Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot — the men — apart from the little ones.
And also a large mixed company went up with them, and flocks and herds, very heavy livestock.

And they baked the dough that they had brought out from Egypt into unleavened cakes, for it was not leavened, because they had been driven out from Egypt and were not able to delay; and they had not made provisions for themselves.
And the dwelling of the sons of Israel, which they dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
And it was at the end of four hundred and thirty years — and it was on this very day — that all the hosts of YHWH went out from the land of Egypt.
It was a night of vigil for YHWH, to bring them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night for YHWH — a vigil for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
And YHWH said to Moses and Aaron: This is the statute of the Passover. No son of a foreigner shall eat of it.
And every slave of a man, the purchase of silver — you shall circumcise him, then he shall eat of it.
A resident alien and a hired worker shall not eat of it.
In one house it shall be eaten. You shall not bring any of the flesh out of the house to the outside, and you shall not break a bone in it.
All the congregation of Israel shall do it.

And when a sojourner sojourns with you and would keep a Passover to YHWH, let every male of his be circumcised, and then let him draw near to keep it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man shall eat of it.
One law shall be for the native and for the sojourner who sojourns among you.
And all the sons of Israel did just as YHWH had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.
And it was on this very day that YHWH brought the sons of Israel out from the land of Egypt by their hosts.

exodus_13.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Set apart as holy to me every firstborn, the opener of every womb among the sons of Israel, among humankind and among the livestock; to me it [is].

And Moses said to the people, Remember this day, on which you went out from Egypt, from a house of slaves, for by strength of hand YHWH brought you out from here; and leavened bread shall not be eaten.
Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.

And it shall be, when YHWH brings you into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, which he swore to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, then you shall serve this service in this month.
Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day a festival to YHWH.
Unleavened bread shall be eaten the seven days, and leavened bread shall not be seen for you, and leaven shall not be seen for you in all your territory.
And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, It is because of what YHWH did for me when I came out from Egypt.
And it shall be for you as a sign on your hand and as a reminder between your eyes, so that the law of YHWH may be in your mouth, for with a strong hand YHWH brought you out from Egypt.
And you shall keep this statute at its appointed time, from days to days.
And it shall be, when YHWH brings you into the land of the Canaanite, just as he swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
then you shall make every opener of a womb pass over to YHWH, and every opener of the offspring of a beast that is yours — the males shall be YHWH's.
And every opener of a donkey you shall redeem with a sheep, and if you do not redeem [it], then you shall break its neck. And every firstborn of humankind among your sons you shall redeem.
And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, What is this? then you shall say to him, With strength of hand YHWH brought us out from Egypt, from a house of slaves.

And it was, when Pharaoh made it hard to send us out, that YHWH killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of humankind to the firstborn of beast. Therefore I am sacrificing to YHWH every opener of a womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.
And it shall be as a sign on your hand and as marks between your eyes, for with strength of hand YHWH brought us out from Egypt.

And it was, when Pharaoh sent the people out, that God did not lead them the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near, for God said, Lest the people regret when they see battle and return to Egypt.
And God turned the people around by the way of the wilderness of the Sea of Reeds; and the sons of Israel went up arrayed for battle from the land of Egypt.
And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had certainly made the sons of Israel swear, saying, God will surely visit you, and you shall bring up my bones from here with you.
And they set out from Succoth and encamped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.
And YHWH was going before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give light to them, to go by day and night.
The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people.

exodus_14.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-zephon; opposite it you shall encamp, by the sea.
And Pharaoh will say of the sons of Israel, They are wandering in confusion in the land; the wilderness has shut upon them.
And I will make strong the heart of Pharaoh, and he will pursue after them, and I will get honour by Pharaoh and by all his army; and Egypt will know that I am YHWH. And they did so.

And it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned toward the people, and they said, What is this we have done, that we have sent Israel away from serving us?
And he harnessed his chariot, and his people he took with him.
And he took six hundred chosen chariots and all the chariotry of Egypt, and officers over all of it.
And YHWH made strong the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the sons of Israel; and the sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.
And Egypt pursued after them and overtook them encamped by the sea — all the horse of the chariotry of Pharaoh, and his horsemen and his army — at Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
And Pharaoh drew near, and the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes, and there — Egypt marching after them! And they were exceedingly afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH.
And they said to Moses, Is it because there were no graves in Egypt that you took us to die in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us, bringing us out from Egypt?
Is this not the word we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, Leave us alone, and let us serve Egypt? For it is better for us to serve Egypt than for us to die in the wilderness.
And Moses said to the people, Do not be afraid. Stand firm and see the deliverance of YHWH, which he will work for you today; for the Egypt you have seen today, you will not see again, ever.
YHWH will fight for you, and you — you shall keep silent.
And YHWH said to Moses, Why are you crying out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, that they set out.
And you — raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, that the sons of Israel may go into the middle of the sea on dry ground.
And I — here I am making strong the heart of Egypt, that they may go in after them; and I will get honour by Pharaoh and by all his army, by his chariotry and by his horsemen.
And Egypt will know that I am YHWH, when I get honour by Pharaoh, by his chariotry and by his horsemen.
And the messenger of God, who had been going before the camp of Israel, set out and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud set out from before them and stood behind them.
And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night; and the one did not draw near to the other all night.
And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and YHWH drove the sea back with a strong east wind all night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided.
And the sons of Israel went into the middle of the sea on dry ground, and the waters were a wall for them on their right and on their left.
And Egypt pursued and went in after them — all the horse of Pharaoh, his chariotry and his horsemen — into the middle of the sea.
And it was in the morning watch that YHWH looked down on the camp of Egypt through the pillar of fire and cloud, and he threw the camp of Egypt into confusion.
And he turned aside the wheel of his chariots, and made him drive with heaviness. And Egypt said, Let me flee from before Israel, for YHWH is fighting for them against Egypt.
And YHWH said to Moses, Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may return over Egypt, over its chariotry and over its horsemen.

And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned at the turning of morning to its steady flow, and Egypt were fleeing to meet it; and YHWH shook Egypt off into the middle of the sea.
And the waters returned and covered the chariotry and the horsemen, all the army of Pharaoh that had gone after them into the sea; not one of them remained.
And the sons of Israel walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea, and the waters were a wall for them on their right and on their left.
And YHWH delivered Israel on that day from the hand of Egypt; and Israel saw Egypt dead on the shore of the sea.
And Israel saw the great hand that YHWH had used against Egypt, and the people feared YHWH, and they believed in YHWH and in Moses his servant.

exodus_15.t: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to YHWH, and they said, saying: Let me sing to YHWH, for he is highly exalted; horse and its rider he has thrown into the sea.
My strength and my song is Yah, and he has become for me deliverance. This is my God, and I will glorify him, the God of my father, and I will exalt him.
YHWH is a man of war; YHWH is his name.
The chariots of Pharaoh and his army he cast into the sea, and the choicest of his officers were sunk in the Sea of Reeds.
The deeps cover them; they went down into the depths like a stone.
Your right hand, YHWH, glorious in power; your right hand, YHWH, it shatters the enemy.
And in the greatness of your majesty you tear down those who rise against you; you send out your burning anger — it consumes them like stubble.
And by the breath of your nostrils the waters were piled up; the streams stood up like a heap; the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.
The enemy said: I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide plunder; my throat will be full of them. I will draw my sword; my hand will dispossess them.
You blew with your breath — the sea covered them; they sank like lead in mighty waters.
Who is like you among the gods, YHWH? Who is like you — glorious in holiness, fearsome in praises, doing wonder?
You stretched out your right hand — the earth swallowed them.
You led in your steadfast love the people whom you redeemed; you guided them in your strength to the abode of your holiness.
Peoples have heard — they tremble; writhing has seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom were terrified; the rams of Moab — trembling seizes them; all the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away.
Terror and dread fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm they are still as a stone, until your people pass over, YHWH, until the people pass over whom you purchased.
You will bring them and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, the place for your dwelling that you made, YHWH, the sanctuary, my Lord, that your hands established.
YHWH will reign forever and ever.

For the horses of Pharaoh went with his chariotry and with his horsemen into the sea, and YHWH brought back over them the waters of the sea; and the sons of Israel walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea.
And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.
And Miriam sang in response to them: Sing to YHWH, for he is highly exalted; horse and its rider he has thrown into the sea.
And Moses led Israel out from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness and did not find water.
And they came to Marah, and they could not drink water from Marah, for it was bitter. Therefore its name was called Marah.
And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
And he cried out to YHWH, and YHWH showed him a tree, and he threw it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There he made for him a statute and an ordinance, and there he tested him.

And he said, If you will surely listen to the voice of YHWH your God, and do what is right in his eyes, and give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, then every sickness that I put on Egypt I will not put on you; for I am YHWH who heals you.
And they came to Elim, and there were twelve springs of water there and seventy palm trees; and they encamped there by the water.

exodus_16.t: And they set out from Elim, and all the congregation of the sons of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.
And the whole congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.

And the sons of Israel said to them, Who would give that we had died by the hand of YHWH in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pot of meat, when we ate bread to the full! For you have brought us out into this wilderness to put this whole assembly to death by hunger.

And YHWH said to Moses, Here I am raining down for you bread from the heavens, and the people shall go out and gather a day's matter in its day, so that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not.
And it shall be on the sixth day that they shall prepare what they bring in, and it shall be double what they gather day by day.
And Moses and Aaron said to all the sons of Israel, At evening you shall know that YHWH brought you out from the land of Egypt,
and in the morning you shall see the glory of YHWH, because he has heard your grumblings against YHWH. And we — what are we, that you grumble against us?

And Moses said, When YHWH gives you meat to eat at evening, and bread in the morning to be full, because YHWH has heard your grumblings that you are grumbling against him — and we, what are we? Your grumblings are not against us, but against YHWH.
And Moses said to Aaron, Say to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, Draw near before YHWH, for he has heard your grumblings.
And it was, as Aaron spoke to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, that they turned toward the wilderness, and there — the glory of YHWH appeared in the cloud!
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:

I have heard the grumblings of the sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, Between the two evenings you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be full of bread; and you shall know that I am YHWH your God.
And it was in the evening that the quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
And the layer of dew went up, and there — on the face of the wilderness a fine flaking thing, fine as frost on the ground!
And the sons of Israel saw, and they said each to his brother, What is it? — for they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, It is the bread that YHWH has given you to eat.

This is the matter that YHWH has commanded: Gather from it, each according to the mouth of his eating — an omer for a head, by the number of your persons — each of you shall take for those in his tent.
And the sons of Israel did so, and they gathered — the one who made much and the one who made little.
And they measured with the omer, and the one who made much had no surplus, and the one who made little had no lack; each gathered according to the mouth of his eating.
And Moses said to them, Let no one leave any of it over until morning.
And they did not listen to Moses, and some men left part of it over until morning, and it bred worms and stank; and Moses was angry with them.
And they gathered it morning by morning, each according to the mouth of his eating; and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
And it was on the sixth day that they gathered double bread, two omers for each one; and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

And he said to them, This is what YHWH said: Tomorrow is a sabbath observance, a sabbath of holiness to YHWH. What you would bake, bake, and what you would boil, boil; and all the surplus set aside for yourselves, to be kept until morning.
And they set it aside until morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not stink, and there was no maggot in it.
And Moses said, Eat it today, for today is a sabbath to YHWH. Today you will not find it in the field.
Six days you shall gather it, and on the seventh day, a sabbath — there will be none on it.
And it was on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, and they did not find any.
And YHWH said to Moses, How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?
See that YHWH has given you the sabbath; therefore on the sixth day he is giving you bread for two days. Stay, each in his place; let no one go out from his place on the seventh day.
And the people rested on the seventh day.
And the house of Israel called its name manna; and it was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like a wafer with honey.

And Moses said, This is the matter that YHWH has commanded: A full omer of it is to be kept for your generations, so that they may see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out from the land of Egypt.
And Moses said to Aaron, Take one jar and put there a full omer of manna, and set it before YHWH, to be kept for your generations.
As YHWH had commanded Moses, Aaron set it before the testimony, to be kept.
And the sons of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
And the omer is a tenth of the ephah.

exodus_17.t: And all the congregation of the sons of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin by their stages, at the mouth of YHWH; and they encamped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
And the people quarrelled with Moses, and they said, Give us water, that we may drink. And Moses said to them, Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test YHWH?
And the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, Why is this — you have brought us up from Egypt to put me and my children and my livestock to death by thirst?
And Moses cried out to YHWH, saying, What shall I do for this people? A little more and they will stone me.
And YHWH said to Moses, Pass on before the people and take with you some of the elders of Israel; and your staff, with which you struck the River, take in your hand and go.

Here I am standing before you there on the rock at Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and the people will drink. And Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Israel.
And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the quarrel of the sons of Israel, and because they tested YHWH, saying, Is YHWH in our midst or not?
And Amalek came and joined battle with Israel at Rephidim.
And Moses said to Joshua, Choose men for us and go out, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will be standing on the top of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand.
And Joshua did as Moses had said to him, to fight against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
And it was, whenever Moses lifted up his hand, that Israel prevailed; and whenever he let his hand rest, Amalek prevailed.

And the hands of Moses were heavy, and they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on this side and one on that side. And his hands were steadiness until the sun went in.
And Joshua weakened Amalek and his people with the mouth of the sword.
And YHWH said to Moses, Write this as a reminder in the book, and put it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly wipe out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens.
And Moses built an altar and called its name, YHWH is my standard.
And he said, For a hand is on the throne of Yah: war for YHWH against Amalek from generation to generation.

exodus_18.t: And Jethro, the priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, that YHWH had brought Israel out from Egypt.
And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, had taken Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after her sending away,
and her two sons, of whom the name of the one was Gershom, for he had said, I have become a sojourner in a foreign land;
and the name of the one was Eliezer, for the God of my father was my help, and he delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, came, and his sons and his wife, to Moses, to the wilderness where he was encamped, at the mountain of God.
And he said to Moses, I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.
And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed down and kissed him; and they asked each of his neighbour after welfare, and they went into the tent.
And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that YHWH had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt on account of Israel, all the hardship that had come upon them on the way, and that YHWH had delivered them.
And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that YHWH had done for Israel, whom he had delivered from the hand of Egypt.
And Jethro said, Blessed be YHWH, who has delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who has delivered the people from under the hand of Egypt.
Now I know that YHWH is greater than all the gods — for in the very matter in which they acted presumptuously against them.
And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God.
And it was on the next day that Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood by Moses from the morning until the evening.

And the father-in-law of Moses saw all that he was doing for the people, and he said, What is this thing that you are doing for the people? Why are you sitting alone, and all the people standing by you from morning until evening?
And Moses said to his father-in-law, Because the people come to me to consult God.
When they have a matter, it comes to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbour, and I make known the statutes of God and his laws.
And the father-in-law of Moses said to him, The thing that you are doing is not good.
You will surely wear yourself out, both you and this people who are with you, for the thing is too heavy for you; you are not able to do it alone.
Now listen to my voice; let me advise you, and may God be with you. You be for the people in front of God, and you bring the matters to God.
And you shall warn them of the statutes and the laws, and make known to them the way in which they shall walk and the work that they shall do.

And you shall look out from all the people men of ability, fearing God, men of truth, hating unjust gain, and you shall set over them officials of thousands, officials of hundreds, officials of fifties and officials of tens.

And they shall judge the people at all times; and it shall be that every great matter they will bring to you, and every small matter they themselves will judge. Lighten it from upon yourself, and they will bear it with you.
If you do this thing, and God commands you, then you will be able to stand; and also all this people will go to its place in peace.
And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said.
And Moses chose men of ability from all Israel and appointed them heads over the people: officials of thousands, officials of hundreds, officials of fifties and officials of tens.
And they judged the people at all times: the hard matter they would bring to Moses, and every small matter they themselves would judge.
And Moses sent his father-in-law off, and he went for himself to his own land.

exodus_19.t: In the third month of the going out of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
And they set out from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai, and they encamped in the wilderness; and Israel encamped there before the mountain.
And Moses went up to God, and YHWH called to him from the mountain, saying, Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell the sons of Israel:
You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
And now, if you will surely listen to my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be for me a treasured possession out of all the peoples — for all the earth is mine —
and you yourselves shall be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the sons of Israel.
And Moses came and called the elders of the people, and he set before them all these words that YHWH had commanded him.
And all the people answered together and said, All that YHWH has spoken we will do. And Moses brought back the words of the people to YHWH.

And YHWH said to Moses, Here I am coming to you in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also trust in you forever. And Moses told the words of the people to YHWH.
And YHWH said to Moses, Go to the people and set them apart as holy today and tomorrow, and let them wash their clothes.
And let them be prepared for the third day, for on the third day YHWH will come down before the eyes of all the people on Mount Sinai.
And you shall set a boundary for the people all around, saying, Take heed to yourselves not to go up on the mountain or touch its edge. Everyone who touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
No hand shall touch him, for he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether animal or man, he shall not live. When the ram's horn sounds long, they may go up on the mountain.
And Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and he set the people apart as holy, and they washed their clothes.
And he said to the people, Be prepared for three days; do not draw near to a woman.

And it was on the third day, when the morning came, that there were thunders and lightnings and a heavy cloud on the mountain, and a very strong sound of a ram's horn; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the lower part of the mountain.
And Mount Sinai was smoking, all of it, because YHWH had come down on it in fire; and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and all the mountain trembled exceedingly.
And the sound of the ram's horn was going and growing very strong. Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.
And YHWH came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain; and YHWH summoned Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
And YHWH said to Moses, Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to YHWH to see, and many of them fall.
And also the priests who draw near to YHWH shall set themselves apart as holy, lest YHWH break out against them.
And Moses said to YHWH, The people are not able to go up to Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, Set a boundary for the mountain and set it apart as holy.
And YHWH said to him, Go, go down, and you shall come up, you and Aaron with you; but the priests and the people shall not break through to come up to YHWH, lest he break out against them.
And Moses went down to the people and said to them.

exodus_20.t: And God spoke all these words, saying,
I am YHWH your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from a house of slaves.
There shall not be for you other gods before my face.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any form that is in the heavens above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the waters under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them; for I, YHWH your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, upon a third generation and upon a fourth generation, of those who hate me,
and doing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love me and to those who keep my commandments.
You shall not take up the name of YHWH your God for emptiness, for YHWH will not leave unpunished the one who takes up his name for emptiness.
Remember the day of the sabbath, to set it apart as holy.
Six days you shall labour and do all your work,

and the seventh day is a sabbath to YHWH your God. You shall not do any work — you, and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and your livestock, and your sojourner who is within your gates.
For in six days YHWH made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and he rested on the seventh day. Therefore YHWH blessed the day of the sabbath and set it apart as holy.
Honour your father and your mother, so that your days may be long upon the land that YHWH your God is giving you.
You shall not murder.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not testify against your neighbour as a false witness.

You shall not covet the house of your neighbour. You shall not covet the wife of your neighbour, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbour's.
And all the people were seeing the thunders and the torches and the sound of the ram's horn and the mountain smoking; and the people saw, and they trembled, and they stood at a distance.
And they said to Moses, You speak with us, and let us listen; and let God not speak with us, lest we die.
And Moses said to the people, Do not be afraid, for God has come in order to test you, and so that the fear of him may be upon your faces, so that you may not sin.
And the people stood at a distance, and Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was.
And YHWH said to Moses, Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: You yourselves have seen that from the heavens I spoke with you.
You shall not make alongside me gods of silver, and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves.

An altar of soil you shall make for me, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
And if you make for me an altar of stones, you shall not build them of hewn stone, for you have wielded your tool upon it and profaned it.
And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, so that your nakedness may not be uncovered upon it.

exodus_21.t: And these are the judgements that you shall set before them.
When you buy a Hebrew slave, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out to freedom, for nothing.
If with his body he comes in, with his body he shall go out. If he is the husband of a wife, then his wife shall go out with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out with his body.
And if saying the slave says: I love my master, my wife and my children; I will not go out free,
then his master shall bring him near to God, and he shall bring him near to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with the awl, and he shall serve him forever.
And when a man sells his daughter as a female slave, she shall not go out as the male slaves go out.

If she is bad in the eyes of her master, who has designated her for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. To a foreign people he shall not have power to sell her, since he has dealt treacherously with her.
And if for his son he designates her, according to the custom of daughters he shall do for her.
If he takes another for himself, her flesh, her covering, and her onah he shall not diminish.
And if these three he does not do for her, then she shall go out for nothing, without money.
One who strikes a person so that he dies — dying he shall be put to death.
But one who did not lie in wait, and God let it fall to his hand — then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
And when a man acts presumptuously against his neighbour, to kill him with shrewdness, from my altar you shall take him to die.
And one who strikes his father or his mother — dying he shall be put to death.
And one who steals a person and sells him, or he is found in his hand — dying he shall be put to death.
And one who curses his father or his mother — dying he shall be put to death.
And when men quarrel, and a man strikes his neighbour with a stone or with a fist, and he does not die but falls to bed,
if he rises and walks about outside on his staff, then the one who struck shall be clear; only his sitting still he shall pay for, and healing he shall have him healed.
And when a man strikes his slave or his female slave with the rod, and he dies under his hand, avenging he shall be avenged.
Nevertheless, if he stands a day or two days, he shall not be avenged, for he is his money.

And when men struggle together and they strike a pregnant woman, and her children come out, and there is no harm, being fined he shall be fined, according as the woman's husband imposes on him, and he shall give by assessment.
And if there is harm, then you shall give life in place of life,
eye in place of eye, tooth in place of tooth, hand in place of hand, foot in place of foot,
burning in place of burning, wound in place of wound, bruise in place of bruise.
And when a man strikes the eye of his slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, he shall send him out free in place of his eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his slave or the tooth of his female slave, he shall send him out free in place of his tooth.
And when an ox gores a man or a woman and he dies, stoning the ox shall be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten, and the owner of the ox is clear.

But if the ox was prone to gore from yesterday and the day before, and its owner has been warned and did not keep it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.
If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give the redemption of his life according to all that is imposed on him.
Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this judgement it shall be done to him.
If the ox gores a slave or a female slave, thirty shekels of silver he shall give to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.
And when a man opens a pit, or when a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls in there,
the owner of the pit shall make compensation; silver he shall return to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
And when a man's ox strikes his neighbour's ox and it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and divide its silver, and the dead one also they shall divide.

Or if it was known that the ox was prone to gore from yesterday and the day before, and its owner did not keep it in, making compensation he shall make compensation, ox in place of the ox, and the dead one shall be his.

exodus_22.t: When a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, five cattle he shall repay in place of the ox, and four sheep in place of the sheep.
If the thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
If the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt for him. Making restitution he shall make restitution; if he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
If being found the stolen thing is found in his hand alive — from ox to donkey to sheep — twofold he shall make restitution.

When a man causes a field or a vineyard to be grazed over, and he lets his beast loose and it grazes in another's field, from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard he shall make compensation.
When fire goes out and finds thornbushes, and a stack of sheaves or the standing grain or the field is consumed, making compensation he shall make compensation, the one who kindled the fire.
When a man gives his neighbour silver or articles to keep, and it is stolen from the man's house — if the thief is found, he shall make restitution twofold.
If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall be brought near to God — whether he has not stretched out his hand against his neighbour's property.

For every matter of transgression — over an ox, over a donkey, over a sheep, over a garment, over any lost thing of which one says, This is it — to God the case of both of them shall come; the one whom God condemns shall make restitution twofold to his neighbour.
When a man gives his neighbour a donkey or an ox or a sheep or any animal to keep, and it dies or is maimed or is driven away, with no one seeing,
an oath of YHWH shall be between the two of them — whether he has not stretched out his hand against his neighbour's property; and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not make compensation.
And if being stolen it is stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
If being torn it is torn in pieces, let him bring it as evidence; for the torn animal he shall not make restitution.
And when a man borrows from his neighbour, and it is maimed or dies, its owner not being with it, making restitution he shall make restitution.
If its owner was with it, he shall not make restitution. If it was hired, it came for its hire.
And when a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, paying the bride-price he shall pay the bride-price for her, for himself as a wife.
If refusing her father refuses to give her to him, he shall weigh out silver according to the bride-price of virgins.
A sorceress you shall not let live.
Anyone lying with an animal — dying he shall be put to death.
One who sacrifices to the gods shall be devoted to destruction — except to YHWH alone.
And a sojourner you shall not maltreat, and you shall not oppress him, for sojourners you were in the land of Egypt.
Any widow or fatherless one you shall not afflict.
If afflicting you afflict him — for if crying out he cries out to me, hearing I will hear his cry.
And my anger shall burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children fatherless.
If you lend silver to my people, to the poor with you, you shall not be to him as a creditor; you shall not lay interest on him.
If taking as a pledge you take your neighbour's cloak as a pledge, before the sun goes down you shall return it to him,
for it is his covering alone; it is his cloak for his skin. In what shall he lie down? And it shall be, when he cries out to me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.
God you shall not revile, and a leader among your people you shall not curse.
Your fullness and your outflow you shall not delay. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.
Thus you shall do with your ox, with your sheep: seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
And men of holiness you shall be to me. And flesh in the field, a torn animal, you shall not eat; to the dog you shall throw it.

exodus_23.t: You shall not lift up a false report. You shall not put your hand with a wicked man to be a witness of violence.
You shall not be after many to do evil, and you shall not testify concerning a dispute to turn aside after many, to thrust aside.
And a poor man you shall not favour in his dispute.
When you meet your enemy's ox or his donkey wandering off, returning you shall return it to him.
When you see the donkey of one who hates you lying down under its load, and you would refrain from leaving it to him — leaving you shall leave it with him.
You shall not turn aside the justice of your needy one in his dispute.
From a word of falsehood keep far, and the innocent and the righteous do not kill, for I will not declare the wicked righteous.
And a bribe you shall not take, for the bribe blinds the clear-sighted and perverts the words of the righteous.
And a sojourner you shall not oppress. And you — you know the life of the sojourner, for sojourners you were in the land of Egypt.
And six years you shall sow your land and gather in its produce.

And the seventh you shall let drop and leave it, and the needy of your people shall eat, and what they leave the animal of the field shall eat. Thus you shall do with your vineyard, with your olive grove.
Six days you shall do your works, and on the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female slave and the sojourner may take breath.
And in all that I have said to you keep yourselves. And the name of other gods you shall not bring to remembrance; it shall not be heard on your mouth.
Three feet you shall keep festival to me in the year.

The Festival of Unleavened Bread you shall keep: seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And they shall not appear before my face empty-handed.
And the Festival of Harvest, the firstfruits of your works that you sow in the field; and the Festival of Ingathering at the going out of the year, when you gather in your works from the field.
Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear before the face of the Lord YHWH.
You shall not sacrifice the blood of my sacrifice with what is leavened, and the fat of my festival sacrifice shall not remain overnight until morning.
The beginning of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of YHWH your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
Behold, I am sending a messenger before you, to keep you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
Take care before him and listen to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not lift away your transgression, for my name is within him.
But if listening you listen to his voice and do all that I say, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
For my messenger shall go before you and bring you to the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Canaanite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, and I will annihilate it.

You shall not bow down to their gods and shall not be made to serve them, and you shall not do according to their works, for tearing down you shall tear them down, and shattering you shall shatter their pillars.
And you shall serve YHWH your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.
There shall not be one miscarrying or barren in your land. The number of your days I will fill.
My terror I will send before you, and I will throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will give all your enemies to you as the neck.
And I will send the hornet before you, and it shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite and the Hittite from before you.
I will not drive it out from before you in one year, lest the land become a waste and the animal of the field become many against you.
Little, little I will drive it out from before you, until you are fruitful and possess the land.

And I will set your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out from before you.
You shall not cut a covenant with them or with their gods.
They shall not dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me, for you would serve their gods, for it would become a snare to you.

exodus_24.t: And to Moses he said: Come up to YHWH, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and you shall bow down from a distance.
And Moses alone shall draw near to YHWH; and they shall not draw near, and the people shall not come up with him.
And Moses came and recounted to the people all the words of YHWH and all the judgements. And all the people answered with one voice and said: All the words that YHWH has spoken we will do.
And Moses wrote all the words of YHWH. And he rose early in the morning and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
And he sent the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings to YHWH: bulls.
And Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and half of the blood he dashed on the altar.
And he took the Book of the Covenant and read it in the ears of the people. And they said: All that YHWH has spoken we will do, and we will obey.
And Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people and said: Behold, the blood of the covenant that YHWH has cut with you concerning all these words.
And Moses went up, and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
And they saw the God of Israel, and under his feet was like a work of sapphire pavement, and like the very substance of the heavens for clearness.
And against the nobles of the sons of Israel he did not stretch out his hand; and they beheld God, and they ate and drank.
And YHWH said to Moses: Come up to me to the mountain and be there, and let me give you the tablets of stone and the law and the commandment that I have written, to teach them.
And Moses arose, and Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
And to the elders he said: Remain for us in this place until we return to you. And behold, Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever is a master of matters, let him draw near to them.
And Moses went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
And the glory of YHWH settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. And on the seventh day he called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.
And the appearance of the glory of YHWH was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain, to the eyes of the sons of Israel.
And Moses went into the midst of the cloud and went up to the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

exodus_25.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, that they take for me a contribution. From every man whose heart impels him you shall take my contribution.
And this is the contribution that you shall take from them: gold and silver and bronze,
and violet and purple and scarlet, and fine linen and goat hair,
and ram skins dyed red, and fine leather, and acacia wood,
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense,
onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
And they shall make for me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst.
According to all that I am showing you — the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its articles — so you shall make it.
And they shall make an ark of acacia wood: two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold; from inside and from outside you shall overlay it. And you shall make on it a moulding of gold all around.
And you shall cast for it four rings of gold and put them on its four feet: two rings on its one side and two rings on its second side.
And you shall make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
And you shall bring the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.
In the rings of the ark the poles shall be; they shall not be removed from it.
And you shall put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.
And you shall make a mercy seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half its length and a cubit and a half its breadth.
And you shall make two cherubim of gold; of hammered work you shall make them, from the two ends of the mercy seat.
And make one cherub from the end on this side and one cherub from the end on that side. From the mercy seat you shall make the cherubim, on its two ends.
And the cherubim shall be spreading wings upward, covering with their wings over the mercy seat, and their faces each toward his brother; toward the mercy seat shall be the faces of the cherubim.
And you shall put the mercy seat on the ark from above, and into the ark you shall put the testimony that I will give you.
And I will meet with you there and speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the testimony, all that I command you for the sons of Israel.
And you shall make a table of acacia wood: two cubits its length and a cubit its breadth and a cubit and a half its height.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold and make for it a moulding of gold all around.
And you shall make for it a rim of a handbreadth all around, and you shall make a moulding of gold for its rim all around.
And you shall make for it four rings of gold and put the rings on the four corners that belong to its four legs.
Close to the rim the rings shall be, as holders for poles, to carry the table.
And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table shall be carried by them.
And you shall make its dishes and its pans and its jars and its bowls, with which it shall be poured out; of pure gold you shall make them.
And you shall put on the table bread of the face, before my face, continually.
And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; of hammered work the lampstand shall be made — its base and its shaft, its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms shall be from it.
And six branches going out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from its one side and three branches of the lampstand from its second side.

Three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom; and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom — so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
And on the lampstand four cups shaped like almond blossoms, its bulbs and its blossoms.
And a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it — for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
Their bulbs and their branches shall be from it; all of it one hammered work of pure gold.
And you shall make its lamps, seven; and its lamps shall be set up, and it shall give light across the space before it.
And its tongs and its firepans shall be of pure gold.
Of a talent of pure gold one shall make it, with all these articles.
And see and make them by their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain.

exodus_26.t: And the tabernacle you shall make of ten curtains: fine twisted linen and violet and purple and scarlet; with cherubim, the work of a designer, you shall make them.
The length of the one curtain shall be twenty-eight by the cubit, and the breadth four by the cubit, the one curtain; one measure for all the curtains.
Five of the curtains shall be joined each to her sister, and five curtains joined each to her sister.
And you shall make loops of violet on the edge of the one curtain, from the end in the set; and so you shall do on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
Fifty loops you shall make on the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make at the end of the curtain that is in the second set; the loops shall be opposite each to her sister.
And you shall make fifty clasps of gold, and you shall join the curtains each to her sister with the clasps; and the tabernacle shall be one.
And you shall make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle; eleven curtains you shall make them.
The length of the one curtain shall be thirty by the cubit, and the breadth four by the cubit, the one curtain; one measure for the eleven curtains.
And you shall join five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you shall fold double the sixth curtain toward the front of the face of the tent.
And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain, the outermost in the set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
And you shall make clasps of bronze, fifty, and you shall put the clasps into the loops and join the tent, and it shall be one.
And the overhang of the surplus in the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that is over, shall hang over the rear of the tabernacle.
And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side, in the surplus in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and on that, to cover it.
And you shall make a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above.
And you shall make the frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
Ten cubits shall be the length of the frame, and a cubit and a half the breadth of the one frame.
Two hands for the one frame, joined each to her sister; so you shall do for all the frames of the tabernacle.
And you shall make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side, southward.
And forty bases of silver you shall make under the twenty frames: two bases under the one frame for its two hands, and two bases under the one frame for its two hands.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, for the north side, twenty frames,
and their forty bases of silver: two bases under the one frame and two bases under the one frame.
And for the rear of the tabernacle, westward, you shall make six frames.
And two frames you shall make for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
And they shall be twins from below, and together they shall be complete at its top, into the one ring. So it shall be for both of them; for the two corners they shall be.
And there shall be eight frames, with their bases of silver, sixteen bases: two bases under the one frame and two bases under the one frame.
And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the frames of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the side of the tabernacle at the rear, westward.
And the middle bar, in the middle of the frames, shall pass through from end to end.
And the frames you shall overlay with gold, and their rings you shall make of gold, as holders for the bars; and you shall overlay the bars with gold.
And you shall set up the tabernacle according to its plan, which you have been shown on the mountain.
And you shall make a veil of violet and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen; the work of a designer one shall make it, with cherubim.
And you shall put it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold, on four bases of silver.
And you shall put the veil under the clasps, and you shall bring there, inside the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall separate for you between the holy place and the holy of holies.
And you shall put the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies.
And you shall set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle southward; and the table you shall put on the north side.
And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent: violet and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia and overlay them with gold, their hooks of gold; and you shall cast for them five bases of bronze.

exodus_27.t: And you shall make the altar of acacia wood: five cubits length and five cubits breadth — the altar shall be square — and three cubits its height.
And you shall make its horns on its four corners; from it its horns shall be, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
And you shall make its pots for taking away its ashes, and its shovels and its basins and its forks and its firepans; all its articles you shall make of bronze.
And you shall make for it a grating, a network of bronze; and you shall make on the network four rings of bronze at its four ends.
And you shall put it under the ledge of the altar, below, and the network shall reach to the middle of the altar.
And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
And its poles shall be put into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Hollow of boards you shall make it; as he showed you on the mountain, so they shall do.
And you shall make the courtyard of the tabernacle: for the south side, southward, hangings for the courtyard of fine twisted linen, a hundred by the cubit in length for the one side.
And its pillars twenty and their bases twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
And so for the north side in length: hangings a hundred long, and its pillars twenty and their bases twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
And the breadth of the courtyard on the west side: hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten and their bases ten.
And the breadth of the courtyard on the east side, eastward: fifty cubits.
And fifteen cubits of hangings for the one shoulder, their pillars three and their bases three.
And for the second shoulder, fifteen of hangings, their pillars three and their bases three.
And for the gate of the courtyard a screen of twenty cubits: violet and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer; their pillars four and their bases four.
All the pillars of the courtyard all around shall be furnished with bands of silver; their hooks of silver and their bases of bronze.
The length of the courtyard a hundred by the cubit, and the breadth fifty by fifty, and the height five cubits, of fine twisted linen; and their bases of bronze.
For all the articles of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its tent pegs and all the tent pegs of the courtyard: bronze.
And you — you shall command the sons of Israel, that they bring to you pure beaten olive oil for the light, to set up a lamp continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is over the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall arrange it from evening until morning before YHWH: a statute of perpetuity for their generations, from the sons of Israel.

exodus_28.t: And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from among the sons of Israel, for his serving as priest to me — Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
And you shall make garments of holiness for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.

And you, you shall speak to all the wise of heart, whom I have filled him [with] a spirit of wisdom, and they shall make the garments of Aaron, to set him apart as holy, for his serving as priest to me.

And these are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece and an ephod and a robe and a tunic of checker-work, a turban and a sash. And they shall make garments of holiness for Aaron your brother and for his sons, for his serving as priest to me.
And they, they shall take the gold and the violet and the purple and the scarlet and the fine linen.
And they shall make the ephod: gold, violet and purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, the work of a designer.
Two joined shoulder-pieces it shall have, at its two ends, and it shall be joined.
And the band of its ephod-work, which is on it — like its workmanship, from it it shall be: gold, violet and purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
And you shall take two stones of onyx, and you shall engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six who remain on the second stone, according to their generations.
The work of a craftsman in stone, engravings of a seal, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; surrounded with settings of gold you shall make them.
And you shall put the two stones on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel. And Aaron shall bear their names before YHWH on his two shoulders, for remembrance.
And you shall make settings of gold,
and two chains of pure gold — as cords you shall make them, the work of braiding — and you shall put the chains of the braids on the settings.
And you shall make a breastpiece of judgement, the work of a designer; like the work of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, violet and purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen you shall make it.
Square it shall be, doubled; a span its length and a span its breadth.
And you shall fill in it a setting of stones, four rows of stone. A row of ruby, topaz and emerald — the one row.
And the second row: turquoise, sapphire and diamond.
And the third row: jacinth, agate and amethyst.
And the fourth row: beryl and onyx and jasper. Set in gold shall they be in their settings.
And the stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names; engravings of a seal, each according to its name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
And you shall make on the breastpiece chains of twisting, the work of braiding, of pure gold.
And you shall make on the breastpiece two rings of gold, and you shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
And you shall put the two braids of gold on the two rings, at the ends of the breastpiece.
And the two ends of the two braids you shall put on the two settings, and you shall put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, at the front of its face.
And you shall make two rings of gold, and you shall put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its edge which is toward the side of the ephod, inward.
And you shall make two rings of gold, and you shall put them on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod, below, at the front of its face, close to its joining, above the band of the ephod.
And they shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of violet, so as to be on the band of the ephod, and the breastpiece shall not come loose from the ephod.
And Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgement, over his heart, when he comes into the holy place, for remembrance before YHWH continually.

And you shall put into the breastpiece of judgement the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be over Aaron's heart when he comes before YHWH; and Aaron shall bear the judgement of the sons of Israel over his heart before YHWH continually.
And you shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of violet.
And the opening for its head shall be in the middle of it. An edge shall be around its opening, the work of a weaver; like the opening of a corselet it shall have, so that it is not torn.
And you shall make on its skirts pomegranates of violet and purple and scarlet, on its skirts all around, and bells of gold between them all around:
a bell of gold and a pomegranate, a bell of gold and a pomegranate, on the skirts of the robe all around.
And it shall be on Aaron to serve, and its sound shall be heard when he comes into the holy place before YHWH and when he goes out, and he shall not die.
And you shall make a plate of pure gold, and you shall engrave on it, engravings of a seal: Holiness to YHWH.
And you shall put it on a cord of violet, and it shall be on the turban; at the front of the face of the turban it shall be.

And it shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel set apart as holy, for all their holy gifts. And it shall be on his forehead continually, for acceptance for them before YHWH.
And you shall weave the tunic in checker-work of fine linen, and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and a sash you shall make, the work of an embroiderer.
And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics, and you shall make for them sashes, and headdresses you shall make for them, for glory and for beauty.
And you shall clothe them — Aaron your brother and his sons with him — and you shall anoint them and fill their hand and set them apart as holy, and they shall serve me as priests.
And make for them undergarments of linen to cover the flesh of nakedness; from the hips and to the thighs they shall be.

And they shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they come into the tent of meeting, or when they draw near to the altar to serve in the holy place, and they shall not bear iniquity and die. A statute of perpetuity for him and for his offspring after him.

exodus_29.t: And this is the thing that you shall do to them, to set them apart as holy, to serve me as priests: take one young bull, a son of the herd, and two rams, unblemished;
and unleavened bread, and cakes of unleavened bread mixed with oil, and wafers of unleavened bread smeared with oil — of fine wheat flour you shall make them.
And you shall put them in one basket, and you shall bring them near in the basket, and the bull and the two rams.
And Aaron and his sons you shall bring near to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and you shall wash them with water.
And you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic and the robe of the ephod and the ephod and the breastpiece, and you shall gird him with the band of the ephod.
And you shall put the turban on his head, and you shall put the crown of holiness on the turban.
And you shall take the oil of anointing and pour it on his head, and you shall anoint him.
And his sons you shall bring near, and you shall clothe them with tunics.

And you shall gird them with a sash — Aaron and his sons — and you shall bind headdresses on them, and priesthood shall be theirs as a statute of perpetuity. And you shall fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons.
And you shall bring the bull near before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.
And you shall slaughter the bull before YHWH, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And you shall take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and all the blood you shall pour out at the base of the altar.
And you shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, and the lobe on the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and you shall make them smoke on the altar.
And the flesh of the bull and its hide and its offal you shall burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
And the one ram you shall take, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
And you shall slaughter the ram, and you shall take its blood and dash it against the altar all around.
And the ram you shall cut into its pieces, and you shall wash its entrails and its legs and put them with its pieces and with its head.
And you shall make the whole ram smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering to YHWH, an odour of soothing; it is a food offering to YHWH.
And you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
