And a grain offering you shall provide with it, morning by morning: a sixth of the ephah, and oil a third of the hin, to moisten the fine flour — a grain offering to YHWH, statutes of perpetuity, continually.
They shall provide the lamb and the grain offering and the oil, morning by morning: a continual burnt offering.
Thus says Lord YHWH: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance; it shall belong to his sons — it is their holding by inheritance.

And if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty, and then it shall return to the prince. Surely his inheritance — it is his sons', it shall be theirs.

And the prince shall not take from the inheritance of the people, oppressing them out of their holding. From his own holding he shall give his sons an inheritance, so that my people shall not be scattered, each from his holding.
And he brought me by the entrance that was at the side of the gate, to the holy rooms for the priests, which face north; and there! there was a place there, in the far corners westward.

And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, where they shall bake the grain offering, so as not to bring them out to the outer court and set the people apart as holy."
And he brought me out to the outer court and made me pass by the four corners of the court; and there! a court in a corner of the court, a court in a corner of the court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty in length and thirty in breadth: one measurement for the four of them, set in corners.
And a row of stones ran around in them, around the four of them; and boiling places were made under the rows all around.
And he said to me, "These are the house of those who boil, where those who serve the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people."

ezekiel_47.t: And he brought me back to the entrance of the house; and there! waters were going out from under the threshold of the house eastward, for the front of the house was east. And the waters were going down from under the south side of the house, from the south of the altar.
And he brought me out by way of the north gate and led me round by the way outside, to the outer gate, by the way that faces east; and there! waters were trickling from the south side.
When the man went out eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured out a thousand by the cubit and made me pass through the waters: waters of ankles.
And he measured out a thousand and made me pass through the waters: waters of knees. And he measured out a thousand and made me pass through: waters of loins.
And he measured out a thousand — a river that I was not able to pass through, for the waters had risen: waters of swimming, a river that could not be passed through.
And he said to me, "Do you see, son of man?" And he led me and brought me back to the bank of the river.
When I had returned, there! at the bank of the river were very many trees, on this side and on that.
And he said to me: "These waters are going out to the eastern region and will go down to the Arabah and come to the sea; to the sea they are brought out, and the waters will be healed.

And it shall be that every living creature that swarms, wherever the two rivers go, shall live; and the fish shall be very many, for these waters have come there and they shall be healed. And everything shall live wherever the river goes.

And it shall be that fishermen shall stand beside it; from En-gedi to En-eglaim there shall be a spreading place for nets. Their fish shall be after their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.
Its swamps and its marshes shall not be healed; they are given over to salt.

And by the river, on its bank, on this side and on that, shall grow up every tree for food. Its leafage shall not wither and its fruit shall not fail; month by month it shall bear early fruit, for its waters — they come out from the sanctuary. And its fruit shall be for food, and its leafage for healing.
Thus says Lord YHWH: This is the boundary by which you shall give the land as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of Israel: Joseph, measured portions.
And you shall divide it as an inheritance, each like his brother, which I lifted my hand to give to your fathers; and this land shall fall to you as an inheritance.
And this is the boundary of the land. To the north side: from the Great Sea, the road of Hethlon, to Lebo-zedad,
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath; Hazer-hattikon, which is on the border of Hauran.
And the boundary shall be from the sea: Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus, and north northward, and the territory of Hamath. And this is the north side.

And the east side: from between Hauran and between Damascus and between Gilead and between the land of Israel — the Jordan; from the border to the eastern sea you shall measure. And this is the east side.
And the south side, southward: from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the Wadi, to the Great Sea. And this is the south side, southward.
And the west side: the Great Sea, from the border to opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
And you shall divide this land for yourselves, according to the tribes of Israel.

And it shall be that you shall make it fall as an inheritance for yourselves and for the sojourners who sojourn among you, who have fathered children among you. And they shall be to you as the native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they shall fall into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
And it shall be that in the tribe with which the sojourner sojourns, there you shall give him his inheritance — the declaration of Lord YHWH.

ezekiel_48.t: And these are the names of the tribes. From the northern end, beside the road of Hethlon, to Lebo-hamath, Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus northward, beside Hamath — and the east side and the west side shall be his: Dan, one.
And beside the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side: Asher, one.
And beside the border of Asher, from the east side and to the west side: Naphtali, one.
And beside the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side: Manasseh, one.
And beside the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side: Ephraim, one.
And beside the border of Ephraim, from the east side and to the west side: Reuben, one.
And beside the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side: Judah, one.

And beside the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the contribution that you shall offer up: five and twenty thousand in breadth, and in length like one of the portions, from the east side to the west side; and the sanctuary shall be in the midst of it.
The contribution that you shall offer up to YHWH: the length, five and twenty thousand; and the breadth, ten thousand.

And to these shall the holy contribution belong, to the priests: northward, five and twenty thousand; and westward, a breadth of ten thousand; and eastward, a breadth of ten thousand; and southward, a length of five and twenty thousand. And the sanctuary of YHWH shall be in the midst of it.
It is for the priests, the consecrated one from the sons of Zadok, who kept my charge, who did not go astray when the sons of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray.
And it shall be for them a contribution from the contribution of the land, a holy of holies, beside the border of the Levites.
And the Levites, alongside the border of the priests: five and twenty thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth. All the length, five and twenty thousand; and the breadth, ten thousand.
And they shall not sell any of it, and none shall exchange it, nor shall the choicest of the land be made to pass over; for it is holy to YHWH.
And the five thousand that remain in the breadth, over against the five and twenty thousand, is common land for the city, for dwelling and for pasture land; and the city shall be in the midst of it.

And these are its measurements: the north side, four thousand five hundred; and the south side, four thousand five hundred; and on the east side, four thousand five hundred; and the west side, four thousand five hundred.
And the city shall have pasture land: northward, two hundred and fifty; and southward, two hundred and fifty; and eastward, two hundred and fifty; and westward, two hundred and fifty.

And what remains in the length, alongside the holy contribution — ten thousand eastward and ten thousand westward; and it shall be alongside the holy contribution — its produce shall be for food for those who work the city.
And those who work the city shall work it, from all the tribes of Israel.
All the contribution: five and twenty thousand by five and twenty thousand. A fourth: you shall offer up the holy contribution together with the holding of the city.

And what remains shall be for the prince, on this side and on that of the holy contribution and of the holding of the city, in front of the five and twenty thousand of the contribution as far as the eastern border; and westward, in front of the five and twenty thousand as far as the western border, alongside the portions — for the prince. And the holy contribution and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst of it.

And from the holding of the Levites and from the holding of the city, in the midst of what belongs to the prince, it shall be: between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin it shall be for the prince.
And the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one.
And beside the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side: Simeon, one.
And beside the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side: Issachar, one.
And beside the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side: Zebulun, one.
And beside the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side: Gad, one.
And beside the border of Gad, to the south side southward: the border shall be from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the Wadi, to the Great Sea.
This is the land that you shall make fall as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel; and these are their portions — the declaration of Lord YHWH.
And these are the exits of the city. On the north side, four thousand five hundred by measure —
and the gates of the city shall be by the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates northward — the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
And to the east side, four thousand five hundred, and three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
And the south side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
The west side, four thousand five hundred; their gates, three: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
The circuit: eighteen thousand. And the name of the city from that day: YHWH Is There.

ezra_1.t: And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, for the completing of the word of YHWH from the mouth of Jeremiah, YHWH stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation through all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:
"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: 'All the kingdoms of the earth YHWH the God of the heavens has given me, and he himself has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
"'Who among you is from all his people? May his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of YHWH the God of Israel — he is the God who is in Jerusalem.

"'And everyone who remains, from any of the places where he is sojourning — let the people of his place support him with silver and with gold and with property and with cattle, along with the freewill offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.'"
And the heads of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin arose, and the priests and the Levites — everyone whose spirit God had stirred — to go up to build the house of YHWH which is in Jerusalem.
And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with property and with cattle and with precious things, besides all that was freely offered.
And King Cyrus brought out the articles of the house of YHWH which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from Jerusalem and put in the house of his gods.
And Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
And this was their number: dishes of gold, thirty; dishes of silver, a thousand; knives, twenty-nine;
bowls of gold, thirty; bowls of silver of a second sort, four hundred and ten; other articles, a thousand.
All the articles of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all of it up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

ezra_2.t: And these are the sons of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile to Babylon, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city —
those who came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;
the sons of Pahath-moab, belonging to the sons of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
the sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
the sons of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;
the sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
the sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;
the sons of Bigvai, two thousand and fifty-six;
the sons of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Ater, belonging to Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
the sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Jorah, a hundred and twelve;
the sons of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Gibbar, ninety-five;
the sons of Bethlehem, a hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Netophah, fifty-six;
the men of Anathoth, a hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Azmaveth, forty-two;
the sons of Kiriath-arim, Kephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the sons of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, a hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Nebo, fifty-two;
the sons of Magbish, a hundred and fifty-six;
the sons of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the sons of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five;
the sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, belonging to the sons of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
The singers: the sons of Asaph, a hundred and twenty-eight.
The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai — all of them a hundred and thirty-nine.
The given ones: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon,
the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,
the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan,
the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah,
the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai,
the sons of Asnah, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephussim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Peruda,
the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the sons of Ami.
All the given ones and the sons of the servants of Solomon: three hundred and ninety-two.
And these are those who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, Immer, but were not able to declare their fathers' house and their offspring, whether they were from Israel:
the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda: six hundred and fifty-two.
And from the sons of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai — who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These sought their register among those enrolled by genealogy, and they were not found; and they were excluded from the priesthood as defiled.
And the Tirshatha said to them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand with Urim and with Thummim.
The whole assembly together: forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male servants and their female servants — these were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred male singers and female singers.
Their horses: seven hundred and thirty-six. Their mules: two hundred and forty-five.
Their camels: four hundred and thirty-five. Donkeys: six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And some of the heads of the fathers, when they came to the house of YHWH which is in Jerusalem, offered freewill offerings for the house of God, to erect it on its site.
According to their ability they gave to the treasury of the work: gold, sixty-one thousand darics; and silver, five thousand minas; and a hundred priestly tunics.
And the priests and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers and the gatekeepers and the given ones, settled in their cities; and all Israel in their cities.

ezra_3.t: And the seventh month arrived, and the sons of Israel were in the cities; and the people gathered as one man to Jerusalem.

And Jeshua son of Jozadak arose, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer up burnt offerings on it, as is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.

And they established the altar on its foundations, for terror was on them because of the peoples of the lands; and they offered up burnt offerings on it to YHWH, burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening.
And they kept the festival of booths, as is written, and the burnt offering of a day on its day, by number, according to the ordinance of each day's matter on its day;
and after this the continual burnt offering, and for the new moons and for all the appointed times of YHWH that are set apart as holy, and for everyone who freely offered a freewill offering to YHWH.
From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer up burnt offerings to YHWH; but the temple of YHWH had not been founded.

And they gave silver to the masons and to the craftsmen, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and to the Tyrians, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the permission of Cyrus king of Persia granted to them.

And in the second year of their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem; and they appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to oversee the work of the house of YHWH.

And Jeshua stood, his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, as one, to oversee those doing the work in the house of God; the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers, the Levites.
And the builders founded the temple of YHWH; and they appointed the priests, robed, with trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise YHWH by the hands of David king of Israel.

And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to YHWH: "For he is good, for his steadfast love is upon Israel for ever." And all the people shouted a great shout, praising YHWH, because the house of YHWH had been founded.

And many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers, the old men who had seen the first house, when it was founded — this house, with their own eyes — were weeping with a loud voice; and many were lifting up their voice with a shout of joy and gladness.
And the people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of gladness from the sound of the weeping of the people; for the people were shouting a great shout, and the sound was heard far off.

ezra_4.t: And the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the exile were building a temple to YHWH the God of Israel.

And they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the fathers and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and to him we have been sacrificing since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."

But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers of Israel said to them, "It is not for you and for us to build a house for our God; for we ourselves together will build for YHWH the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us."
And the people of the land were making slack the hands of the people of Judah, and terrifying them from building,
and hiring counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
And in the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of his colleagues wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Aramaic and translated into Aramaic.
Rehum master of the decree and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter concerning Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king, as follows —

then Rehum master of the decree and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates — the judges and the officials, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Erechites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehavites, the Elamites,
and the rest of the nations whom the great and honourable Osnappar took into exile and settled in the city of Samaria and the rest of Beyond the River — and now:
This is the copy of the letter that they sent to him: "To Artaxerxes the king, your servants, the men of Beyond the River — and now:

"Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from beside you have come to us, to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and evil city; they have finished the walls and are repairing the foundations.
"Now let it be known to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, they will not give tribute, tax or toll, and it will certainly injure the kings' revenue.
"Now, because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not proper for us to see the king's dishonour, therefore we have sent and made it known to the king,

"that a search be made in the book of records of your fathers. And you will find in the book of records and know that this city is a rebellious city, injurious to kings and provinces, and that they have been making revolt within it from ancient days; therefore this city was laid waste.
"We make known to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, then you will have no possession in Beyond the River."
The king sent word to Rehum master of the decree and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates who dwell in Samaria and the rest of Beyond the River: "Peace. And now:
"the letter that you sent to us has been read out plainly before me.
"And a decree was made by me, and they searched and found that this city has risen up against kings from ancient days, and that rebellion and revolt have been made in it.
"And mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, having mastery over all Beyond the River, and tribute, tax and toll were paid to them.
"Now make a decree to make these men cease, and this city shall not be built until a decree is made by me.
"And be cautious of negligence in doing this. Why should damage grow great, to the injury of kings?"

Then, from the time that the copy of the letter of Artaxerxes the king was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem, to the Jews, and made them cease by force and power.
Then the work of the house of God which is in Jerusalem ceased; and it was ceasing until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

ezra_5.t: And Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and in Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, supporting them.

At that time Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their associates, came to them and spoke thus to them: "Who made a decree for you to build this house and to finish this structure?"
Then we said to them thus: "What are the names of the men who are building this building?"
But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they did not make them cease until the report should go to Darius, and then a letter should be sent back concerning this.
The copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates the officials who were in Beyond the River, sent to Darius the king.
They sent a report to him, and thus was written in it: "To Darius the king: all peace.

"Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God; and it is being built with dressed stone, and timber is being set in the walls, and this work is being done diligently and is prospering in their hands.
"Then we asked those elders, we said to them thus: 'Who made a decree for you to build this house and to finish this structure?'
"And also we asked them their names, to make them known to you, that we might write the name of the men who are at their head.

"And thus they returned us a report, saying: 'We are the servants of the God of the heavens and the earth, and we are building the house that was built many years before this, which a great king of Israel built and finished.

'But because our fathers enraged the God of the heavens, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon the Chaldean, and he destroyed this house and took the people into exile to Babylon.
'Nevertheless, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree to build this house of God.

'And also the articles of the house of God, of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to the temple of Babylon — King Cyrus brought them out from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to one named Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.
'And he said to him: "Take these articles, go, deposit them in the temple that is in Jerusalem; and let the house of God be built on its place."
'Then this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God which is in Jerusalem; and from then until now it has been being built, and it is not finished.'

"And now, if it is good to the king, let a search be made in the king's treasure house there in Babylon, whether it is so that a decree was made by Cyrus the king to build this house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his will concerning this."

ezra_6.t: Then Darius the king made a decree, and they searched in the house of the books where the treasures were deposited there in Babylon.
And there was found at Ecbatana, in the citadel that is in the province of Media, a single scroll; and thus was written in it — a memorandum:

"In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: 'The house of God in Jerusalem — let the house be built, a place where they sacrifice sacrifices, and let its foundations be retained; its height sixty cubits, its width sixty cubits,
'three rows of dressed stone and a row of new timber; and let the expense be given from the king's house.

'And also the articles of the house of God, of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon — let them be sent back, and let each go to the temple in Jerusalem, to its place, and you shall deposit them in the house of God.'"
"Now, Tattenai governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their associates, the officials who are in Beyond the River — be far from there.
"Leave the work of this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God on its place.

"And a decree is made by me as to what you shall do with these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: from the king's property, from the tribute of Beyond the River, the expense shall diligently be given to these men, so that they are not made to cease.

"And whatever is needed — young bulls and rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of the heavens, wheat, salt, wine and oil, according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem — let it be given to them day by day without negligence,
"that they may be offering soothing offerings to the God of the heavens, and praying for the life of the king and his sons.

"And a decree is made by me: that any person who violates this command — let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and impaled on it; and let his house be made a refuse heap for this.

"And may the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who stretches out his hand to violate, to destroy this house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have made a decree; let it be done diligently."
Then Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their associates, in accordance with what Darius the king had sent, did so diligently.

And the elders of the Jews were building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. And they built and finished it according to the decree of the God of Israel and according to the decree of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
And this house was brought to completion by the third day of the month of Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
And the sons of Israel — the priests and the Levites and the rest of the sons of the exile — made the dedication of this house of God with joy.

And they offered for the dedication of this house of God a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and as a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
And they appointed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their classes, over the service of God which is in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
And the sons of the exile kept the passover on the fourteenth of the first month.

For the priests and the Levites had cleansed themselves as one; all of them were clean. And they slaughtered the passover for all the sons of the exile, and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
And the sons of Israel who had returned from the exile ate, and everyone who had separated himself to them from the uncleanness of the nations of the land, to seek YHWH the God of Israel.

And they kept the festival of unleavened bread seven days with joy; for YHWH had made them rejoice, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria towards them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.

ezra_7.t: And after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia — Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest —

that Ezra came up from Babylon. And he was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses which YHWH the God of Israel had given; and the king gave him all his request, according to the hand of YHWH his God upon him.
And some of the sons of Israel, and of the priests and the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers and the given ones, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was the seventh year of the king.
For on the first of the first month was the beginning of the going up from Babylon; and on the first of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
For Ezra had set his heart to seek the law of YHWH and to do it, and to teach statute and ordinance in Israel.
And this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe — a scribe of the words of the commandments of YHWH and his statutes upon Israel:
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of the heavens: perfect. And now:
"A decree is made by me that everyone in my kingdom of the people Israel and its priests and the Levites who volunteers to go to Jerusalem with you — let him go.
"Forasmuch as you are sent from before the king and his seven counsellors, to enquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem by the law of your God which is in your hand,
"and to carry the silver and gold that the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose abode is in Jerusalem,
"and all the silver and gold that you find in all the province of Babylon, with the freewill offering of the people and the priests who offer freely for the house of their God which is in Jerusalem.

"Therefore you shall diligently buy with this silver bulls, rams, lambs, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.
"And whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, you shall do according to the will of your God.
"And the articles that are given you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
"And the rest of what is needed for the house of your God, which falls to you to give, you shall give from the house of the king's treasures.

"And a decree is made by me — I, Artaxerxes the king — to all the treasurers who are in Beyond the River: that whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of the heavens, asks of you, let it be done diligently,
"up to a hundred talents of silver, and up to a hundred cors of wheat, and up to a hundred baths of wine, and up to a hundred baths of oil, and salt without writing.
"Whatever is by the decree of the God of the heavens, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of the heavens; for why should there be wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?

"And we make known to you that on any of the priests and the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim and the servants of this house of God, it is not permitted to impose tribute, tax or toll.

"And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God which is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people who are in Beyond the River — all who know the laws of your God; and whoever does not know, you shall instruct.

"And anyone who does not do the law of your God and the law of the king — let judgement be done on him diligently: whether for death, or for banishment, or for confiscation of property, or for imprisonment."
Blessed be YHWH the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this in the heart of the king, to beautify the house of YHWH which is in Jerusalem,

and who has extended steadfast love towards me before the king and his counsellors and all the king's mighty officials. And I strengthened myself according to the hand of YHWH my God upon me, and I gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.

ezra_8.t: And these are the heads of their fathers, and their genealogical enrolment, who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:
Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush;
of the sons of Shecaniah; of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him were enrolled by genealogy a hundred and fifty males;
of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males;
of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred males;
and of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males;
and of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males;
and of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty males;
of the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
and of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty males;
and of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males;
and of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten males;
and of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones — and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah — and with them sixty males;
and of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with him seventy males.
And I gathered them at the river that goes to Ahava, and we camped there three days. And I looked closely at the people and at the priests, and of the sons of Levi I found none there.
So I sent for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, for Elnathan, for Jarib, for Elnathan, for Nathan, for Zechariah and for Meshullam — leading men — and for Joiarib and for Elnathan, teachers.

And I commanded them concerning Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia, and I put words in their mouth to speak to Iddo and his brothers the given ones at the place Casiphia, to bring us servants for the house of our God.
And they brought us, according to the good hand of our God upon us, a man of insight from the sons of Mahli son of Levi son of Israel — and Sherebiah and his sons and his brothers, eighteen;
and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty;
and of the given ones whom David and the officials had appointed for the service of the Levites — two hundred and twenty given ones; all of them were designated by name.
And I proclaimed a fast there, at the river Ahava, to humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way for us and for our little ones and for all our property.

For I was ashamed to ask from the king an escort and horsemen to help us against an enemy on the way; for we had said to the king, "The hand of our God is upon all who seek him, for good; and his strength and his anger are against all who forsake him."
So we fasted and sought from our God concerning this, and he was entreated by us.
And I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests: Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers.

And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the articles — the contribution for the house of our God, which the king and his counsellors and his officials and all Israel who were present had offered.
And I weighed out into their hand six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and silver articles worth a hundred talents, a hundred talents of gold,
and twenty bowls of gold worth a thousand darics, and two articles of fine gleaming bronze, precious as gold.
And I said to them, "You are holy to YHWH, and the articles are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to YHWH the God of your fathers.
"Watch and keep them until you weigh them out before the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the leaders of the fathers of Israel in Jerusalem, in the rooms of the house of YHWH."
And the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold and the articles, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

And we set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth of the first month, to go to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of an enemy and from an ambusher on the way.
And we came to Jerusalem, and we remained there three days.

And on the fourth day the silver and the gold and the articles were weighed out in the house of our God, into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest — and with him Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui, the Levites —
by number, by weight, for everything; and all the weight was written down at that time.

Those who had come from the captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve male goats as a sin offering — all of it a burnt offering to YHWH.
And they delivered the king's laws to the king's satraps and the governors of Beyond the River; and they supported the people and the house of God.

ezra_9.t: And when these things were finished, the leaders approached me, saying, "The people Israel and the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, according to their abominations — from the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, the Egyptian and the Amorite.

"For they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy offspring have mixed themselves with the peoples of the lands; and the hand of the leaders and the officials has been first in this unfaithfulness."
And when I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe, and I pulled out some of the hair of my head and my beard, and I sat appalled.
And to me were gathered everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel, over the unfaithfulness of the exiles; and I was sitting appalled until the evening offering.
And at the evening offering I arose from my humiliation, and with my garment and my robe torn I bowed on my knees and spread out my palms to YHWH my God.
And I said, "My God, I am ashamed and humiliated to lift up my face to you, my God; for our iniquities have increased above our head, and our guilt has grown great as far as the heavens.

"From the days of our fathers we have been in great guilt until this day; and for our iniquities we have been given — we, our kings, our priests — into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder and to shame of face, as at this day.

"And now, for a brief moment there has been favour from YHWH our God, to leave us those who escape and to give us a tent peg in his holy place, that our God might light up our eyes and give us a little reviving in our servitude.

"For we are slaves; yet in our servitude our God has not forsaken us, and he has extended steadfast love to us before the kings of Persia, giving us a reviving to raise up the house of our God and to set up its ruins, and giving us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
"And now, what shall we say, our God, after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,

"which you commanded by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying, 'The land that you are entering to take possession of it is a land of impurity, by the impurity of the peoples of the lands, by their abominations with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth in their uncleanness.

'And now, do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons; and do not seek their peace or their good for ever — so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons for ever.'
"And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and our great guilt — for you, our God, have withheld below what our iniquity deserved, and have given us such an escaped remnant as this —

"shall we turn back to break your commandments and to intermarry with the peoples of these abominations? Would you not be angry with us to the point of making an end, so that there would be no remnant and no escaped remnant?
"YHWH, God of Israel, you are righteous; for we are left an escaped remnant, as at this day. Here we are before you in our guilt — for there is no standing before you because of this."

ezra_10.t: And while Ezra was praying and while he was confessing, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, there gathered to him from Israel a very great assembly — men and women and children — for the people wept a great weeping.

And Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We have acted unfaithfully against our God, and we have married foreign women from the peoples of the land; and now there is hope for Israel concerning this.

"And now let us make a covenant with our God to send out all the wives and those born of them, by the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.
"Arise, for the matter rests on you, and we are with you. Be strong and act."
And Ezra arose and made the leaders of the priests, the Levites and all Israel swear to act according to this word; and they swore.

And Ezra rose from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib; and he went there. He ate no food and drank no water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
And they sent a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to all the sons of the exile, to assemble at Jerusalem;

and that anyone who would not come within three days, according to the counsel of the leaders and the elders, all his property would be forfeited, and he himself would be separated from the assembly of the exiles.

And all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within three days — it was the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month — and all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, trembling because of the matter and because of the rains.
And Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have acted unfaithfully and have married foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel.
"And now give praise to YHWH the God of your fathers, and do his will; and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women."
And all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, "So — it is on us to do according to your word.

"But the people are many, and it is the season of rains, and there is no strength to stand outside; and the business is not for one day or for two, for we have greatly increased in transgressing in this matter.

"Let our leaders stand for all the assembly; and let everyone in our cities who has married foreign women come at appointed times, and with them the elders of each city and its judges — until the burning of our God's anger is turned back from us, until this matter is settled."
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah stood against this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

And the sons of the exile did so. And Ezra the priest, and men who were heads of the fathers, by their fathers' house, and all of them by name, separated themselves; and they sat on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
And they finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
And there were found among the sons of the priests who had married foreign women: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers — Maaseiah and Eliezer and Jarib and Gedaliah.
And they gave their hand to send out their wives; and being guilty, a ram of the flock for their guilt.
And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
And of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah and Elijah and Shemaiah and Jehiel and Uzziah.
And of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad and Eleasah.
And of the Levites: Jozabad and Shimei and Kelaiah — that is Kelita — Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.
And of the singers: Eliashib. And of the gatekeepers: Shallum and Telem and Uri.
And of Israel: of the sons of Parosh — Ramiah and Izziah and Malkijah and Mijamin and Eleazar and Malkijah and Benaiah.
And of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah and Jehiel and Abdi and Jeremoth and Elijah.
And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah and Jeremoth and Zabad and Aziza.
And of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.
And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch and Adaiah, Jashub and Sheal and Ramoth.
And of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna and Kelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel and Binnui and Manasseh.
And the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshiah, Malkijah, Shemaiah, Simeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, Shemariah.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.
Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram and Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Keluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai and Jaasai,
and Bani and Binnui, Shimei,
and Shelemiah and Nathan and Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azarel and Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, Joseph.
Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai and Joel, Benaiah.
All these had taken foreign women; and there were among them women who had borne children.

genesis_1.t: In beginning created God the heavens and the earth.
And the earth was formlessness and emptiness, and darkness over [the] face of [the] deep, and [the] Spirit of God hovering over [the] face of the waters.
And said God, let there be light, and there was light.
And saw God the light that [it was] good, and separated God between the light and between the darkness.
And called God to the light day, and to the darkness he called night. And there was evening and there was morning, day one.
And said God, let there be an expanse in [the] midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters to waters.
And made God the expanse, and separated between the waters which [were] from under to the expanse and between the waters which [were] from above to the expanse. And it was so.
And called God to the expanse heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a day second.
And said God, let be gathered the waters from under the heavens to one place, and let appear the dry ground. And it was so.
And called God to the dry ground earth, and to [the] gathering of the waters he called seas. And saw God that [it was] good.
And said God, let sprout the earth vegetation, plants bearing seed, trees of fruit producing fruit to its kind, which its seed [is] in it, on the earth. And it was so.
And brought forth the earth vegetation, plants bearing seed to its kind, and trees producing fruit which its seed [was] in it, to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.
And there was evening and there was morning, a day third.
And said God, let there be luminaries in [the] expanse of the heavens to separate between the day and between the night, and they shall be for signs and for seasons and for days and years,
And they shall be for luminaries in [the] expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth. And it was so.
And made God the two the great luminaries, the great luminary for the rule of the day and the small luminary for the rule of the night, and the stars.
And set them God in [the] expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth,
And to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate between the light and between the darkness. And saw God that [it was] good.
And there was evening and there was morning, a day fourth.
And said God, let swarm the waters swarming things, creatures living, and birds let fly above the earth on [the] face of [the] expanse of the heavens.
And created God the great sea monsters and every living creature that creeps, with which swarmed the waters, to their kind, and every bird of wing to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.
And blessed them God saying, be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and the birds let multiply on the earth.
And there was evening and there was morning, a day fifth.
And said God, let bring forth the earth living creatures to its kind, livestock and creeping things and animals of [the] earth to its kind. And it was so.
And made God the animals of the earth to its kind and the livestock to its kind and every creeping thing of the ground to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.

And said God, let us make humankind in our image according to our likeness, and let them rule over [the] fish of the sea and over [the] birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.
And created God the humankind in his image, in [the] image of God he created it, male and female he created them.

And blessed them God, and said to them God, be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over [the] fish of the sea and over [the] birds of the heavens and over every animal that creeps on the earth.
And said God, behold I give to you every plant bearing seed which [is] on [the] face of all the earth and every tree which in it [is the] fruit of a tree bearing seed — to you it shall be for food.
And to every animal of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to every creeping thing on the earth in which [is] living life — every greenery of plants for food. And it was so.
And saw God all that he had made, and behold [it was] very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the day the sixth.

genesis_2.t: And were completed the heavens and the earth and all their host.
And completed God on the seventh day his work which he had done, and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
And blessed God the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all his work which God created to make.
These [are] the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on [the] day YHWH God made earth and heaven.
And every shrub of the field not yet was on the earth, and every plant of the field not yet was sprouting, for not had caused rain YHWH God on the earth, and a human there was not to till the ground.
And a mist went up from the earth and watered all [the] face of the ground.
And formed YHWH God the man dust from the ground, and breathed in his nostrils [the] breath of life, and became the man a living being.
And planted YHWH God a garden in Eden from [the] east, and he put there the man whom he had formed.
And made sprout YHWH God from the ground every tree desirable to appearance and good for food, and [the] tree of life in [the] middle of the garden, and [the] tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
And a river [was] going out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads.
[The] name of the one [is] Pishon; it [is] the one going around all [the] land of Havilah, where there [is] the gold.
And [the] gold of that land [is] good; there [are] the bdellium and the onyx stone.
And [the] name of the second river [is] Gihon; it [is] the one going around all [the] land of Cush.
And [the] name of the third river [is] Tigris; it [is] the one going [the] east of Assyria. And the fourth river, it [is] Euphrates.
And took YHWH God the man and put him in [the] garden of Eden to till it and to keep it.
And commanded YHWH God upon the man saying, from every tree of the garden eating you may eat,
And from [the] tree of the knowledge of good and evil, not you shall eat from it, for in [the] day of your eating from it, dying you shall die.
And said YHWH God, not good [is] the being of the man to his aloneness. I will make for him a helper as opposite him.

And formed YHWH God from the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and brought [them] to the man to see what he would call it, and all which he called it, the man, a living creature, that [was] its name.
And called the man names to all the livestock and to [the] birds of the heavens and to every animal of the field, and for Adam not he found a helper as opposite him.
And caused to fall YHWH God a deep sleep upon the man, and he slept, and he took one of his ribs and closed up flesh in its place.
And built YHWH God the rib which he had taken from the man into a woman, and he brought her to the man.
And said the man, this [one] this time [is] bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. To this [one] it shall be called woman, for from a man was taken this [one].
Upon thus he leaves a man his father and his mother and he clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
And they were both of them naked, the man and his wife, and not they were ashamed.

genesis_3.t: And the serpent was shrewd more than every animal of the field which YHWH God had made. And he said to the woman, indeed has God said, not you shall eat from every tree of the garden?
And said the woman to the serpent, from [the] fruit of [the] trees of the garden we may eat,
And from [the] fruit of the tree which [is] in [the] middle of the garden, God said, not you shall eat from it and not you shall touch it, lest you die.
And said the serpent to the woman, not dying you shall die.
For knowing [is] God that in [the] day of your eating from it, and shall be opened your eyes, and you shall be like God, knowers of good and evil.

And saw the woman that good [was] the tree for food and that a delight [was] it to the eyes, and desirable [was] the tree to make wise, and she took from its fruit and ate, and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.
And were opened [the] eyes of both of them, and they knew that naked [were] they, and they sewed together leaves of a fig tree and made for themselves loin coverings.

And they heard [the] sound of YHWH God walking about in the garden at [the] wind of the day, and hid himself the man and his wife from [the] face of YHWH God in [the] midst of [the] trees of the garden.
And called YHWH God to the man and said to him, where [are] you?
And he said, your sound I heard in the garden, and I was afraid for naked [was] I, and I hid myself.
And he said, who told to you that naked [were] you? ¿From the tree which I commanded you to not eat from it, have you eaten?
And said the man, the woman whom you put with me, she, she gave to me from the tree and I ate.
And said YHWH God to the woman, what [is] this you have done? And said the woman, the serpent, he deceived me, and I ate.

And YHWH God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you from all the livestock and from every animal of the field. On your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
And enmity I will put between you and between the woman, and between your seed and between her seed. He will strike you [at the] head, and you will strike him [at the] heel.
To the woman he said: Multiplying I will multiply your pain and your conceiving; in pain you shall bear sons. And to your husband [is] your desire, and he will rule over you.

And to Adam he said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree of which I commanded you, saying, You shall not eat from it — cursed is the ground on your account. In pain you shall eat [of] it all the days of your life.
And thorn and thistle it shall cause to sprout for you, and you shall eat the vegetation of the field.
By the sweat of your nostrils you shall eat bread until your returning to the ground, for from it you were taken — for dust you are, and to dust you shall return.
And the man called the name of his wife Eve, for she was the mother of all living.
And YHWH God made for Adam and for his wife tunics of skin, and he clothed them.
And YHWH God said: Behold, the man has become like one of us, to know good and evil. And now — lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat and live forever —
And YHWH God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.
And he drove out the man, and he caused to dwell east of the garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the whirling sword, to keep the way of the tree of life.

genesis_4.t: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and she said: I have gotten a man with YHWH.
And she added to bear his brother, Abel. And Abel was a herder of flock, and Cain was a tiller of ground.
And it was, at the end of days, and Cain brought from the fruit of the ground an offering to YHWH.
And Abel, he also brought — from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions. And YHWH regarded Abel and his offering,
but to Cain and to his offering he did not regard. And it burned to Cain exceedingly, and his face fell.
And YHWH said to Cain: Why has it burned to you, and why has your face fallen?
Is it not [so], if you do well, [there is] lifting up? And if you do not do well, at the door sin is crouching; and to you [is] its desire, and you must rule over it.
And Cain said to Abel his brother […]. And it was, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.
And YHWH said to Cain: Where is Abel your brother? And he said: I do not know. Am I the keeper of my brother?
And he said: What have you done? The voice of your brother's bloods — they are crying out to me from the ground.
And now, cursed are you from the ground, which has opened its mouth to take your brother's bloods from your hand.
When you till the ground, it shall not again give its strength to you. A wanderer and a fugitive you shall be on the earth.
And Cain said to YHWH: My punishment is greater than bearing.

Behold, you have driven me out this day from upon the face of the ground, and from your face I shall be hidden. And I shall be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and it will be that everyone who finds me will kill me.
And YHWH said to him: Therefore, everyone who kills Cain — sevenfold he shall be avenged. And YHWH set for Cain a sign, so that everyone who found him would not strike him.
And Cain went out from before YHWH, and he dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he was building a city, and he called the name of the city according to the name of his son, Enoch.
And to Enoch was born Irad; and Irad fathered Mehujael; and Mehujael fathered Methushael; and Methushael fathered Lamech.
And Lamech took for himself two wives; the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.
And Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of the dweller of tent and livestock.
And the name of his brother was Jubal; he was the father of everyone who handles lyre and pipe.
And Zillah, she also bore Tubal-cain, a sharpener of every worker of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
And Lamech said to his wives: Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, give ear to my speech. For a man I have killed for my wound, and a boy for my bruise.
For sevenfold Cain shall be avenged, and Lamech seventy and seven.
And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son, and she called his name Seth, for [she said]: God has set for me another seed in place of Abel, for Cain killed him.
And to Seth, to him also, a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. Then it was begun to call on the name of YHWH.

genesis_5.t: This [is] [the] book of [the] generations of Adam. In [the] day God created Adam, in [the] likeness of God he made him.
Male and female he created them, and he blessed them, and he called their name Adam in [the] day they were created.
And Adam lived thirty and a hundred year, and he fathered [a son] in his own likeness, according to his image, and he called his name Seth.
And the days of Adam, after he fathered Seth, were eight hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundreds year and thirty year, and he died.
And Seth lived five years and a hundred year, and he fathered Enosh.
And Seth lived, after he fathered Enosh, seven years and eight hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Seth were twelve year and nine hundreds year, and he died.
And Enosh lived ninety year, and he fathered Kenan.
And Enosh lived, after he fathered Kenan, fifteen year and eight hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enosh were five years and nine hundreds year, and he died.
And Kenan lived seventy year, and he fathered Mahalalel.
And Kenan lived, after he fathered Mahalalel, forty year and eight hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Kenan were ten years and nine hundreds year, and he died.
And Mahalalel lived five years and sixty year, and he fathered Jared.
And Mahalalel lived, after he fathered Jared, thirty year and eight hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalalel were five and ninety year and eight hundreds year, and he died.
And Jared lived two and sixty year and a hundred year, and he fathered Enoch.
And Jared lived, after he fathered Enoch, eight hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Jared were two and sixty year and nine hundreds year, and he died.
And Enoch lived five and sixty year, and he fathered Methuselah.
And Enoch walked about with God, after he fathered Methuselah, three hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch was five and sixty year and three hundreds year.
And Enoch walked about with God, and he [was] not, for God took him.
And Methuselah lived seven and eighty year and a hundred year, and he fathered Lamech.
And Methuselah lived, after he fathered Lamech, two and eighty year and seven hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Methuselah were nine and sixty year and nine hundreds year, and he died.
And Lamech lived two and eighty year and a hundred year, and he fathered a son.
And he called his name Noah, saying, 'This one will comfort us from our work and from the pain of our hands, from the ground which YHWH has cursed it.'
And Lamech lived, after he fathered Noah, five and ninety year and five hundreds year, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lamech was seven and seventy year and seven hundreds year, and he died.
And Noah was a son of five hundreds year, and Noah fathered Shem, Ham and Japheth.

genesis_6.t: And it was, when humankind began to become numerous upon the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw the daughters of humankind, that they were good, and they took for themselves wives from all whom they chose.
And YHWH said, 'My spirit shall not abide in humankind for ever, in that also he [is] flesh; and his days shall be a hundred and twenty year.'

The Nephilim were on the earth in those days — and also after that — when the sons of God went in to the daughters of humankind and they bore to them. They [were] the mighty ones who [were] from long ago, the men of the name.
And YHWH saw that the evil of humankind was great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day.
And YHWH regretted that he had made humankind on the earth, and he was pained to his heart.

And YHWH said, 'I will wipe humankind, whom I created, from upon the face of the ground — from humankind to livestock, to creeping thing, and to the bird of the heavens — for I regret that I have made them.'
And Noah found favour in the eyes of YHWH.
These [are] [the] generations of Noah. Noah [was] a righteous man, blameless he was in his generations; with God Noah walked about.
And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
And God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
And God said to Noah, 'The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them; and behold, I am about to destroy them with the earth.'
Make for yourself an ark of gopher woods; nests you shall make the ark, and you shall cover it from inside and from outside with the pitch.
And this [is] how you shall make it: three hundreds cubit the length of the ark, fifty cubit its breadth, and thirty cubit its height.
A roof you shall make for the ark, and to a cubit you shall finish it from above; and the entrance of the ark you shall put in its side. Lower, second and third [decks] you shall make it.
And I, behold, I am about to bring the flood — water — upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which [is] the breath of life from under the heavens. All that [is] on the earth shall expire.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall go into the ark — you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.
And of every living thing, of all flesh, two of everything you shall bring into the ark to keep alive with you; male and female they shall be.
Of the bird according to its kind, and of the livestock according to its kind, of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind — two of everything shall come to you, to keep alive.
And you, take for yourself from all food which is eaten, and gather [it] to yourself; and it shall be for you and for them for food.
And Noah did according to all that God commanded him; so he did.

genesis_7.t: And YHWH said to Noah, 'Come, you and all your household, into the ark, for you I have seen [to be] righteous before me in this generation.'
Of all the clean livestock you shall take for yourself seven [and] seven, a man and his woman; and of the livestock which is not clean, two, a man and his woman.
Also of the bird of the heavens, seven [and] seven, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the face of all the earth.
For in seven days more I am causing it to rain upon the earth, forty day and forty night, and I will wipe all the standing thing that I have made from upon the face of the ground.
And Noah did according to all that YHWH commanded him.
And Noah [was] a son of six hundreds year, and the flood — water — was upon the earth.
And Noah went, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
Of the clean livestock, and of the livestock which is not clean, and of the bird, and of everything creeping upon the ground,
two [and] two they came to Noah, into the ark, male and female, just as God commanded Noah.
And it was, at the seven days, that the waters of the flood were upon the earth.

In the year of six hundreds year of the life of Noah, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month — on this day all the springs of the great deep were split open, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
And the rain was upon the earth forty day and forty night.
On the bone of this day Noah went, and Shem and Ham and Japheth the sons of Noah, and the wife of Noah and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark.

they, and every animal according to its kind, and all the livestock according to its kind, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind — every bird, every wing.
And they came to Noah, into the ark, two [and] two of all the flesh in which [is] the breath of life.
And those coming — male and female of all flesh — came, just as God commanded him. And YHWH shut behind him.
And the flood was forty day upon the earth, and the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose from upon the earth.
And the waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark went upon the face of the waters.
And the waters prevailed exceedingly, exceedingly upon the earth, and all the high mountains which [are] under all the heavens were covered.
Fifteen cubit from above the waters prevailed, and the mountains were covered.
And all flesh that creeps upon the earth expired — among the birds and among the livestock and among the animals, and among every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth — and every human.
All in whose nostrils [was] the breath of the breath of life, of all that [was] on the dry land, died.

And he wiped all the standing thing that [was] upon the face of the ground — from humankind to livestock, to creeping thing and to the bird of the heavens — and they were wiped from the earth. And only Noah was left, and those who [were] with him in the ark.
And the waters prevailed upon the earth fifty and a hundred day.

genesis_8.t: And God remembered Noah, and every animal and all the livestock that [were] with him in the ark; and God made a wind pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
And the springs of [the] deep were shut up, and the floodgates of the heavens; and the rain from the heavens was restrained.
And the waters turned back from upon the earth, going and returning; and the waters decreased at the end of a hundred and fifty days.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters were going and decreasing until the tenth month; in the tenth, on the first of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
And it was at the end of forty days, and Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made.
And he sent out the raven, and it went out, going out and returning, until the waters dried up from upon the earth.
And he sent out the dove from with him, to see whether the waters had lightened from upon the face of the ground.

And the dove did not find a resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him, to the ark, for water was upon the face of all the earth; and he sent out his hand and took her and brought her to him, to the ark.
And he waited yet seven other days, and he again sent out the dove from the ark.
And the dove came to him at the time of evening, and there! a freshly plucked olive leaf in her mouth; and Noah knew that the waters had lightened from upon the earth.
And he waited yet seven other days, and he sent out the dove, and she did not again return to him any more.

And it was in the six hundred and first year, in the first, on the first of the month, the waters were dried up from upon the earth; and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and he looked, and there! the face of the ground was dried up.
And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
And God spoke to Noah, saying:
Go out from the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives with you.

Every animal that is with you, of all flesh — among the birds and among the livestock and among every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth — bring out with you; and they shall swarm in the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth.
And Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him.
Every animal, every creeping thing and every bird, everything that creeps upon the earth, by their families, went out from the ark.
And Noah built an altar to YHWH, and he took of every clean livestock animal and of every clean bird, and he offered up burnt offerings on the altar.

And YHWH smelled the soothing odour, and YHWH said to his heart: I will not again curse the ground on account of the human, for the fashioning of the heart of the human [is] evil from his youth; and I will not again strike down every living thing as I have done.
Yet all the days of the earth: seed and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night — they shall not cease.

genesis_9.t: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and he said to them: Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every animal of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens, upon all that the ground creeps with, and upon all the fish of the sea; into your hand they are given.
Every creeping thing that is alive shall be for you for food; like the greenery of plants I have given you everything.
Only flesh with its life — its blood — you shall not eat.

And nevertheless your blood, for your lives, I will require; from the hand of every animal I will require it, and from the hand of a human being, from the hand of each his brother, I will require the life of a human being.
[The one] shedding [the] blood of a human being, by a human being his blood shall be shed, for in [the] image of God he made humankind.
And you — be fruitful and multiply; swarm in the earth and multiply in it.
And God said to Noah and to his sons with him, saying:
And I — here I am, establishing my covenant with you, and with your seed after you,
and with every living creature that is with you — among the birds, among the livestock, and among every animal of the earth with you; from all that came out of the ark, to every animal of the earth.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and all flesh shall not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood, and there shall not be a flood any more to destroy the earth.
And God said: This is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between me and between you and between every living creature that is with you, for generations of perpetuity.
My bow I have set in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between me and between the earth.
And it shall be, when I cloud a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud.
And I will remember my covenant which is between me and between you and between every living creature among all flesh; and the waters shall not become a flood any more to destroy all flesh.
And the bow shall be in the cloud, and I will see it, to remember the covenant of perpetuity between God and between every living creature among all flesh that is upon the earth.
And God said to Noah: This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and between all flesh that is upon the earth.
And the sons of Noah who went out from the ark were Shem and Ham and Japheth; and Ham, he was the father of Canaan.
These three were the sons of Noah, and from these all the earth was scattered.
And Noah began, a man of the ground, and he planted a vineyard.
And he drank from the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself inside his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and he told his two brothers outside.

And Shem and Japheth took the garment and put it on the shoulder of the two of them, and they walked backwards and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backwards, and the nakedness of their father they did not see.
And Noah awoke from his wine, and he knew what his young son had done to him.
And he said: Cursed be Canaan; a slave of slaves he shall be to his brothers.
And he said: Blessed be YHWH, the God of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to them.
May God make space for Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to them.
And Noah lived after the flood three hundred years and fifty years.
And all the days of Noah were nine hundred years and fifty years, and he died.

genesis_10.t: And these are the generations of the sons of Noah — Shem, Ham and Japheth — and sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan and Tubal and Meshech and Tiras.
