And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz and Riphath and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.
From these the coastlands of the nations separated in their lands, each to his tongue, by their families, in their nations.
And the sons of Ham: Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba and Havilah and Sabtah and Raamah and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
And Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
He was a mighty one of hunting before YHWH; therefore it is said: Like Nimrod, a mighty one of hunting before YHWH.
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel and Erech and Akkad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he went out to Asshur, and he built Nineveh and Rehoboth-ir and Calah,
and Resen between Nineveh and between Calah; that is the great city.
And Mizraim fathered the Ludim and the Anamim and the Lehabim and the Naphtuhim,
and the Pathrusim and the Casluhim — from whom the Philistines went out — and the Caphtorim.
And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
and the Jebusite and the Amorite and the Girgashite,
and the Hivite and the Arkite and the Sinite,
and the Arvadite and the Zemarite and the Hamathite; and afterwards the families of the Canaanite were scattered.
And the border of the Canaanite was from Sidon, as you go toward Gerar, as far as Gaza; as you go toward Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
And to Shem also was born — he, the father of all the sons of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder.
The sons of Shem: Elam and Asshur and Arphaxad and Lud and Aram.
And the sons of Aram: Uz and Hul and Gether and Mash.
And Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
And to Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and the name of his brother was Joktan.
And Joktan fathered Almodad and Sheleph and Hazarmaveth and Jerah,
and Hadoram and Uzal and Diklah,
and Obal and Abimael and Sheba,
and Ophir and Havilah and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
And their dwelling was from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, the hill country of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, by their nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, in their nations; and from these the nations separated in the earth after the flood.

genesis_11.t: And all the earth was one lip and one words.
And it was, when they set out from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they dwelt there.
And they said, each to his neighbour: Come, let us brick bricks and burn them to a burning. And the brick was for them as stone, and the bitumen was for them as mortar.
And they said: Come, let us build for ourselves a city, and a tower, and its top in the heavens; and let us make for ourselves a name, lest we be scattered over the face of all the earth.
And YHWH came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of the human had built.
And YHWH said: Here, one people and one lip for all of them, and this is their beginning to do; and now nothing will be withheld from them, all that they plan to do.
Come, let us go down and let us confuse there their lip, so that they will not hear, each the lip of his neighbour.
And YHWH scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they ceased to build the city.
Therefore its name was called Babel, for there YHWH confused the lip of all the earth; and from there YHWH scattered them over the face of all the earth.
These are the generations of Shem. Shem was a son of a hundred years, and he fathered Arphaxad two years after the flood.
And Shem lived, after he fathered Arphaxad, five hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Arphaxad lived thirty-five years, and he fathered Shelah.
And Arphaxad lived, after he fathered Shelah, three years and four hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Shelah lived thirty years, and he fathered Eber.
And Shelah lived, after he fathered Eber, three years and four hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Eber lived thirty-four years, and he fathered Peleg.
And Eber lived, after he fathered Peleg, thirty years and four hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Peleg lived thirty years, and he fathered Reu.
And Peleg lived, after he fathered Reu, nine years and two hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Reu lived thirty-two years, and he fathered Serug.
And Reu lived, after he fathered Serug, seven years and two hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Serug lived thirty years, and he fathered Nahor.
And Serug lived, after he fathered Nahor, two hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and he fathered Terah.
And Nahor lived, after he fathered Terah, nineteen years and a hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran.
And these are the generations of Terah. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran; and Haran fathered Lot.
And Haran died upon the face of Terah his father, in the land of his kindred, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
And Abram and Nahor took for themselves wives. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
And Sarai was barren; there was no child to her.

And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, the son of his son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram his son; and they went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan, and they came as far as Haran, and they dwelt there.
And the days of Terah were five years and two hundred years, and Terah died in Haran.

genesis_12.t: And YHWH said to Abram, "Go for yourself from your land and from your kindred and from the house of your father, to the land that I will show you."
"And let me make you into a great nation, and let me bless you, and let me make your name great; and be a blessing."
"And let me bless those blessing you, and the one treating you with contempt I will curse; and in you all the clans of the ground shall be blessed."
And Abram went just as YHWH had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. And Abram was a son of seventy-five years when he came out from Haran.

And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot the son of his brother, and all their possessions that they had accumulated, and the persons that they had acquired in Haran; and they went out to go to the land of Canaan, and they came to the land of Canaan.
And Abram passed through the land as far as the place of Shechem, as far as the great tree of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land.
And YHWH appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." And he built there an altar to YHWH, who had appeared to him.

And he moved on from there to the hill country east of Bethel, and he pitched his tent — Bethel to the west and Ai to the east — and he built there an altar to YHWH, and he called on the name of YHWH.
And Abram journeyed, going and journeying toward the Negev.
And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was heavy in the land.
And it happened, as he drew near to enter Egypt, that he said to Sarai his wife, "Look now, I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance."
"And it will be, when the Egyptians see you, that they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me, and you they will let live."
"Say, please, that you are my sister, so that it may go well for me on your account, and my life will live because of you."
And it happened, when Abram entered Egypt, that the Egyptians saw the woman, that she was very beautiful.
And the officials of Pharaoh saw her, and they praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken to the house of Pharaoh.
And to Abram he did good on her account, and there were his: sheep and cattle and male donkeys and male servants and female servants and female donkeys and camels.
And YHWH struck Pharaoh with great plagues, and his house, on the matter of Sarai the wife of Abram.
And Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?"
"Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her to myself for a wife? And now, here is your wife — take her and go."
And Pharaoh commanded men concerning him, and they sent him away, and his wife, and all that was his.

genesis_13.t: And Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that was his, and Lot with him, toward the Negev.
And Abram was very heavy in livestock, in silver and in gold.
And he went by his journeyings from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
to the place of the altar that he had made there at the former time; and Abram called there on the name of YHWH.
And also to Lot, who was going with Abram, there were sheep and cattle and tents.
And the land did not bear them, to dwell together, for their possessions were much, and they were not able to dwell together.
And there was quarrelling between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. And the Canaanite and the Perizzite were then dwelling in the land.
And Abram said to Lot, "Let there not be, please, strife between me and between you, and between my herdsmen and between your herdsmen, for we are men, brothers."
"Is not all the land before you? Separate, please, from me. If the left, then let me go right; and if the right, then let me go left."

And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw all the plain of the Jordan, that all of it was well watered — before YHWH destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah — like the garden of YHWH, like the land of Egypt, as you come to Zoar.
And Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot set out from the east; and they separated, each from his brother.
Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt among the cities of the plain, and he moved his tent as far as Sodom.
And the men of Sodom were evil and sinners against YHWH, exceedingly.
And YHWH said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, "Lift up, please, your eyes and look from the place where you are — northward and southward and eastward and westward."
"For all the land that you are seeing — to you I will give it, and to your offspring, forever."
"And I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone is able to count the dust of the earth, then your offspring also will be counted."
"Arise, walk about in the land, to its length and to its breadth, for to you I will give it."
And Abram moved his tent and came and dwelt at the great trees of Mamre, which are at Hebron, and he built there an altar to YHWH.

genesis_14.t: And it happened in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim —
they made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
All these joined together at the valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea).
Twelve years they had served Kedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
And in the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer came, and the kings who were with him, and they defeated the Rephaim at Ashteroth-karnaim, and the Zuzim at Ham, and the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim,
and the Horites in their hill country, Seir, as far as El-paran, which is by the wilderness.
And they turned back and came to En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they defeated all the territory of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who were dwelling in Hazazon-tamar.

And the king of Sodom went out, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar), and they deployed battle against them in the valley of Siddim —
against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar — four kings against the five.
And the valley of Siddim was pits, pits of bitumen; and the king of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell there, and those who remained fled to the hill country.
And they took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their food, and they went.
And they took Lot and his possessions — the son of Abram's brother — and they went; and he was dwelling in Sodom.

And the fugitive came and told Abram the Hebrew — and he was dwelling at the great trees of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and the brother of Aner, and they were possessors of a covenant with Abram.
And Abram heard that his kinsman had been taken captive, and he drew out his trained men, those born of his household, three hundred and eighteen, and he pursued as far as Dan.
And he divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and he struck them, and he pursued them as far as Hobah, which is to the north of Damascus.
And he brought back all the possessions, and also Lot his kinsman and his possessions he brought back, and also the women and the people.
And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after his returning from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, to the valley of Shaveh (that is, the King's Valley).
And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; and he was a priest of God Most High.
And he blessed him and said, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth;
and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your adversaries into your hand." And he gave him a tenth of everything.
And the king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the persons, and the possessions take for yourself."
And Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I raise my hand to YHWH, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth:
"if from a thread and to a sandal-thong, and if I take anything of all that is yours — so you will not say, 'I made Abram rich.'"
"Apart from me — only what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol and Mamre — they, let them take their share."

genesis_15.t: After these things the word of YHWH came to Abram in a vision, saying: "Do not fear, Abram. I am a shield for you; your reward will be very great."
And Abram said, "Lord YHWH, what will you give me, and I am going childless, and the son of the acquisition of my house — he is Damascus Eliezer?"
And Abram said, "Look, to me you have not given offspring, and here, the son of my house is inheriting me."
And here, the word of YHWH was to him, saying: "This one will not inherit you; but rather one who comes out from your inward parts — he will inherit you."
And he brought him outside and said, "Look now toward the heavens and count the stars — if you are able to count them." And he said to him, "So will your offspring be."
And he believed in YHWH, and he reckoned it to him as righteousness.
And he said to him, "I am YHWH, who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to take possession of it."
And he said, "Lord YHWH, by what shall I know that I will take possession of it?"
And he said to him, "Bring me a heifer three years old, and a female goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtledove and a young pigeon."
And he brought him all these, and he cut them in two down the middle, and he set each piece to meet its counterpart; but the bird he did not cut in two.
And the bird of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
And it happened, as the sun was about to go, that a deep sleep fell on Abram; and here, a dread, a great darkness, was falling on him.
And he said to Abram, "Knowing you shall know that your offspring will be a sojourner in a land not theirs, and they will serve them, and they will afflict them, four hundred years."
"And also the nation that they will serve — I am judging; and after that they will come out with great possessions."
"And you, you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age."
"And in the fourth generation they will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet complete."
And it happened, when the sun had gone and it was thick darkness, that here — a smoking fire pot and a torch of fire, which passed between these pieces.
On that day YHWH cut a covenant with Abram, saying: "To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates —
the Kenite and the Kenizzite and the Kadmonite,
and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Rephaim,
and the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Girgashite and the Jebusite."

genesis_16.t: And Sarai, the wife of Abram, had not borne to him; and she had an Egyptian maidservant, and her name was Hagar.
And Sarai said to Abram, "Look now, YHWH has restrained me from bearing. Go, please, to my maidservant; perhaps I will be built up from her." And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
And Sarai, the wife of Abram, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, at the end of ten years of Abram's dwelling in the land of Canaan, and she gave her to Abram her husband, to him for a wife.
And he went to Hagar, and she conceived. And she saw that she had conceived, and her mistress became slight in her eyes.

And Sarai said to Abram, "My wrong is upon you. I myself put my maidservant in your bosom, and she saw that she had conceived, and I became slight in her eyes. May YHWH judge between me and between you."
And Abram said to Sarai, "Here, your maidservant is in your hand. Do to her what is good in your eyes." And Sarai afflicted her, and she fled from before her.
And the messenger of YHWH found her at a spring of water in the wilderness, at the spring on the way to Shur.
And he said, "Hagar, maidservant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" And she said, "From before Sarai my mistress I am fleeing."
And the messenger of YHWH said to her, "Return to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hands."
And the messenger of YHWH said to her, "Multiplying I will multiply your offspring, and it will not be counted for multitude."
And the messenger of YHWH said to her, "Here you are, pregnant, and you will bear a son, and you will call his name Ishmael, for YHWH has heard your affliction."
"And he will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand against everyone, and everyone's hand against him; and in the face of all his brothers he will dwell."
And she called the name of YHWH who spoke to her, "You are a God of seeing," for she said, "Have I really seen here after the one who sees me?"
Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. Here, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bore to Abram a son, and Abram called the name of his son whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
And Abram was a son of eighty-six years when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

genesis_17.t: And Abram was a son of ninety-nine years, and YHWH appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am God Almighty. Walk about before me and be blameless."
"And let me set my covenant between me and between you, and let me increase you exceedingly, exceedingly."
And Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him, saying:
"As for me — here, my covenant is with you, and you will become a father of a multitude of nations."
"And your name will no longer be called Abram, and your name will be Abraham, for a father of a multitude of nations I have made you."
"And I will make you fruitful exceedingly, exceedingly, and I will make you into nations, and kings will come out from you."

"And I will establish my covenant between me and between you, and between your offspring after you throughout their generations, for a covenant of perpetuity, to be God to you and to your offspring after you."
"And I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for a possession of perpetuity; and I will be God to them."
And God said to Abraham, "And you, my covenant you shall keep — you and your offspring after you throughout their generations."
"This is my covenant which you shall keep, between me and between you and between your offspring after you: every male among you shall be circumcised."
"And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it will become a sign of the covenant between me and between you."

"And a son of eight days shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations — one born of the household, and the purchase of silver from any son of a foreigner who is not of your offspring."
"Circumcising he shall be circumcised — the one born of your household and the purchase of your silver — and my covenant shall be in your flesh for a covenant of perpetuity."
"And an uncircumcised male, who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin — that person shall be cut off from his kin. He has broken my covenant."
And God said to Abraham, "Sarai your wife — you shall not call her name Sarai, for Sarah is her name."
"And I will bless her, and also I will give from her to you a son. And I will bless her, and she will become nations; kings of peoples will be from her."
And Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and he said in his heart, "To a son of a hundred years shall a child be born? And shall Sarah, a daughter of ninety years, bear?"
And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live before you!"
And God said, "But Sarah your wife is bearing you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac; and I will establish my covenant with him for a covenant of perpetuity, for his offspring after him."
"And as for Ishmael, I have heard you. Here, I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him exceedingly, exceedingly. Twelve princes he will father, and I will make him into a great nation."
"But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this appointed time in the coming year."
And he finished speaking with him, and God went up from upon Abraham.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all those born of his household, and all the purchase of his silver — every male among the men of Abraham's household — and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on that very day, just as God had spoken with him.
And Abraham was a son of ninety-nine years when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
And Ishmael his son was a son of thirteen years when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
On that very day Abraham was circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
And all the men of his household — one born of the household and the purchase of silver from a son of a foreigner — were circumcised with him.

genesis_18.t: And YHWH appeared to him at the great trees of Mamre, and he [was] sitting [at] the opening of the tent in the heat of the day.
And he lifted his eyes and saw, and there! three men standing over against him. And he saw, and he ran to meet them from the opening of the tent, and he bowed down groundward.
And he said, "My Lord, if now I have found favour in your eyes, do not now pass on from over your servant."
Let a little water be taken, now, and wash your feet, and support yourselves under the tree.
And let me take a morsel of bread, and sustain your heart; afterward you shall pass on — for this is why you have passed by your servant." And they said, "So do, just as you have spoken."
And Abraham hurried toward the tent, to Sarah, and said, "Hurry! Three seahs of flour, fine flour — knead and make cakes."
And to the herd Abraham ran, and took a son of the herd, tender and good, and gave [it] to the young man, and he hurried to prepare it.
And he took curds and milk and the son of the herd which he had prepared, and set [it] before them, and he [was] standing over them under the tree, and they ate.
And they said to him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" And he said, "There — in the tent."
And he said, "Returning I will return to you about the time of life, and there! a son for Sarah your wife." And Sarah [was] listening [at] the opening of the tent, and it [was] behind him.
And Abraham and Sarah [were] old, come into days; it had ceased to be for Sarah the way as with women.
And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, "After I am worn out, has there been pleasure for me? And my lord is old."
And YHWH said to Abraham, "Why this — did Sarah laugh, saying, 'Shall I really, truly bear, and I am old?'"
Is a thing too wondrous for YHWH? At the appointed time I will return to you, about the time of life, and to Sarah a son.
And Sarah denied, saying, "I did not laugh" — for she was afraid. And he said, "No, but you did laugh."
And the men arose from there and looked down upon the face of Sodom, and Abraham [was] walking with them to send them off.
And YHWH, he said, "Am I concealing from Abraham what I am doing?"
And Abraham, becoming he will become a nation great and mighty, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him.

For I have known him, so that he may command his sons and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of YHWH by doing righteousness and justice, so that YHWH may bring upon Abraham what he has spoken concerning him.
And YHWH said, "The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah — indeed it is great, and their sin — indeed it is very heavy.
Let me go down, now, and see: whether according to its outcry which has come to me they have done — a completion; and if not, I will know."
And the men turned from there and went toward Sodom, and Abraham, still he was standing before YHWH.
And Abraham drew near and said, "Will you also sweep away righteous with wicked?
Perhaps there are fifty righteous within the city. Will you also sweep away and not bear with the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are within it?
Far be it from you to do according to this manner, to put to death righteous with wicked, so that as the righteous so the wicked. Far be it from you! Shall the judge of all the earth not do justice?"
And YHWH said, "If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will bear with the whole place for their sake."
And Abraham answered and said, "Here now, I have undertaken to speak to my Lord, and I am dust and ashes.
Perhaps the fifty righteous will lack five — will you destroy the whole city for five?" And he said, "I will not destroy, if I find there forty-five."
And he added again to speak to him, and said, "Perhaps forty will be found there." And he said, "I will not do it for the sake of the forty."
And he said, "Let it not burn to my Lord, now, and let me speak. Perhaps thirty will be found there." And he said, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."
And he said, "Here now, I have undertaken to speak to my Lord. Perhaps twenty will be found there." And he said, "I will not destroy for the sake of the twenty."
And he said, "Let it not burn to my Lord, now, and let me speak only this once. Perhaps ten will be found there." And he said, "I will not destroy for the sake of the ten."
And YHWH went, when he had finished speaking to Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.

genesis_19.t: And the two messengers came toward Sodom in the evening, and Lot [was] sitting in the gate of Sodom. And Lot saw, and he arose to meet them, and he bowed down, face groundward.

And he said, "Here now, my lords, turn aside, now, to the house of your servant, and lodge, and wash your feet; and you shall rise early and go on your way." And they said, "No, for in the open place we will lodge."
And he pressed on them exceedingly, and they turned aside to him and came into his house. And he made for them a feast, and unleavened bread he baked, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house — from young man and unto old, all the people, from the end.
And they called to Lot and said to him, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, and let us know them."
And Lot went out to them, to the entrance, and the door he shut behind him.
And he said, "Do not, now, my brothers, do evil."

"Here now, I have two daughters who have not known a man. Let me bring them out, now, to you, and do to them as is good in your eyes. Only to these men do nothing, for this is why they have come under the shadow of my roof."

And they said, "Approach beyond!" And they said, "The one came to sojourn, and he judges, judging! Now we will do evil to you more than to them." And they pressed hard against the man, against Lot, and drew near to break the door.
And the men stretched out their hand and brought Lot to them, into the house, and the door they shut.
And the men who were at the entrance of the house they struck with dazzlings, from small and unto great, and they wearied themselves to find the entrance.
And the men said to Lot, "Who else do you have here? A son-in-law, and your sons and your daughters, and all who are yours in the city — bring out from the place.
"For we are destroying this place, for their outcry has become great before the face of YHWH, and YHWH has sent us to destroy it."

And Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, the takers of his daughters, and said, "Rise, go out from this place, for YHWH is destroying the city." And he was as one laughing in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
And as the dawn came up, the messengers urged Lot, saying, "Rise, take your wife and your two daughters who are found, lest you be swept away in the iniquity of the city."

And he lingered. And the men took hold on his hand and on the hand of his wife and on the hand of his two daughters, in YHWH's compassion upon him, and they brought him out and set him outside the city.
And it was, when they had brought them outside, that he said, "Escape for your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stop in all the round. Escape to the hill country, lest you be swept away."
And Lot said to them, "Not, now, my Lord!"

"Here now, your servant has found favour in your eyes, and you have made great your loyalty which you have done with me, to keep my life alive. But I am not able to escape to the hill country, lest the calamity cling to me and I die.
"Here now, this city is near, to flee there, and it is a small thing. Let me escape, now, there — is it not a small thing? — and my life will live."
And he said to him, "Here, I have lifted your face also as to this matter, not to overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
"Hurry, escape there, for I am not able to do a thing until your coming there." Therefore he called the name of the city Zoar.
The sun had come out over the earth, and Lot came toward Zoar.
And YHWH rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah sulfur and fire, from YHWH, from the heavens.
And he overthrew those cities and all the round and all the inhabitants of the cities and the growth of the ground.
And his wife looked from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood there before the face of YHWH.
And he looked down upon the face of Sodom and Gomorrah, and upon all the face of the land of the round, and he saw, and there! the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a kiln.
And it was, when God destroyed the cities of the round, that God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Lot had dwelt.
And Lot went up from Zoar and dwelt in the hill country, and his two daughters with him, for he was afraid to dwell in Zoar. And he dwelt in the cave, he and his two daughters.
And the firstborn said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man in the earth to come in to us according to the way of all the earth.
"Come, let us make our father drink wine, and let us lie with him, and let us keep seed alive from our father."
And they made their father drink wine that night, and the firstborn came and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down and when she arose.

And it was on the next day, and the firstborn said to the younger, "Here, I lay last night with my father. Let us make him drink wine also tonight, and go, lie with him, and let us keep seed alive from our father."
And they made their father drink wine also that night, and the younger arose and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down and when she arose.
And the two daughters of Lot conceived from their father.
And the firstborn bore a son, and she called his name Moab. He is the father of Moab until this day.
And the younger, she also, bore a son, and she called his name Ben-ammi. He is the father of the sons of Ammon until this day.

genesis_20.t: And Abraham set out from there toward the land of the Negev, and dwelt between Kadesh and between Shur, and he sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." And Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
And God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night and said to him, "Here, you are about to die on account of the woman whom you have taken, and she is possessed of a possessor."
Now Abimelech had not drawn near to her. And he said, "My Lord, will you kill also a righteous nation?
"Did he not himself say to me, 'She is my sister'? And she, she also, said, 'He is my brother.' In the integrity of my heart and in the innocence of my palms I have done this."
And God said to him in the dream, "I also, I know that in the integrity of your heart you did this, and I also, I withheld you from sinning against me; therefore I did not permit you to touch her.
"And now, return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and live. And if you are not returning her, know that dying you shall die, you and all that is yours."
And Abimelech rose early in the morning and called to all his servants and spoke all these words in their ears, and the men were exceedingly afraid.

And Abimelech called to Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? Deeds which are not done you have done with me."
And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you see, that you have done this thing?"
And Abraham said, "Because I said, 'Surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me on account of the matter of my wife.'"
"And also, truly she is my sister, the daughter of my father, only not the daughter of my mother; and she became mine as a wife."

"And it was, when God caused me to wander from the house of my father, that I said to her, 'This is your loyalty which you shall do with me: at every place where we come, say of me, He is my brother.'"
And Abimelech took sheep and cattle and male servants and female servants and gave them to Abraham, and he returned to him Sarah his wife.
And Abimelech said, "Here is my land before you. Dwell in the good in your eyes."
And to Sarah he said, "Here, I have given a thousand of silver to your brother. Here, it is for you a covering of eyes to all who are with you; and with all — and you are set right."
And Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his female slaves, and they bore children.
For shutting up YHWH had shut up every womb of the house of Abimelech, on account of the matter of Sarah, the wife of Abraham.

genesis_21.t: And YHWH attended to Sarah as he had said, and YHWH did for Sarah as he had spoken.
And Sarah conceived and bore to Abraham a son for his old age, at the appointed time of which God had spoken with him.
And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son, a son of eight days, as God had commanded him.
And Abraham was a son of a hundred years when Isaac his son was born to him.
And Sarah said, "Laughter God has made for me; everyone who hears will laugh for me."
And she said, "Who would have said to Abraham, 'Sarah has suckled sons'? For I have borne a son for his old age."
And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
And she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac."
And the matter was exceedingly evil in the eyes of Abraham, on account of his son.

And God said to Abraham, "Let it not be evil in your eyes on account of the lad and on account of your slave woman. All that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for in Isaac offspring shall be called for you.
"And also the son of the slave woman — into a nation I will make him, for he is your offspring."

And Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave them to Hagar, placing them on her shoulder — and the child — and sent her away. And she went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
And the water was finished from the skin, and she cast the child under one of the bushes.
And she went and sat herself down opposite, at a distance, about a bowshot, for she said, "Let me not look on the death of the child." And she sat opposite, and she lifted up her voice and wept.

And God heard the voice of the lad, and the messenger of God called to Hagar from the heavens and said to her, "What is it to you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the lad where he is.
"Rise, lift up the lad and take hold of your hand on him, for into a great nation I will make him."
And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, and she went and filled the skin with water and gave the lad a drink.
And God was with the lad, and he grew, and he dwelt in the wilderness, and he became a shooter, a bowman.
And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took for him a wife from the land of Egypt.
And it was at that time that Abimelech, and Phicol the commander of his army, said to Abraham, saying, "God is with you in all that you are doing.

"And now, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my offspring, nor with my posterity. According to the loyalty which I have done with you, you shall do with me, and with the land in which you have sojourned."
And Abraham said, "I, I will swear."
And Abraham rebuked Abimelech on account of the well of water which the servants of Abimelech had seized.
And Abimelech said, "I do not know who has done this thing. And also you did not tell me, and also I have not heard of it except today."
And Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them cut a covenant.
And Abraham set seven ewe-lambs of the flock by themselves.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What are they, these seven ewe-lambs which you have set by themselves?"
And he said, "For the seven ewe-lambs you shall take from my hand, so that it may become for me a witness that I dug this well."
Therefore he called that place Beersheba, for there the two of them swore an oath.
And they cut a covenant at Beersheba, and Abimelech, and Phicol the commander of his army, arose, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
And he planted a tamarisk at Beersheba, and there he called on the name of YHWH, God of perpetuity.
And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.

genesis_22.t: And it was, after these things, that the God tested Abraham. And he said to him, "Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."

And he said, "Take, now, your son, your only one, whom you love, Isaac, and go, you, to the land of the Moriah, and offer him up there as a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell you."

And Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey and took his two lads with him, and Isaac his son, and he split wood for a burnt offering, and he arose and went to the place which the God had said to him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from a distance.
And Abraham said to his lads, "Remain here for yourselves with the donkey, and I and the lad will go over there, and we will bow down, and we will return to you."
And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and put it on Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife. And the two of them went together.
And Isaac said to Abraham his father, and he said, "My father!" And he said, "Here I am, my son." And he said, "Here are the fire and the wood — and where is the sheep for a burnt offering?"
And Abraham said, "God will see to the sheep for a burnt offering for himself, my son." And the two of them went together.
And they came to the place which the God had said to him, and Abraham built there the altar and arranged the wood, and he bound Isaac his son and put him on the altar, above the wood.
And Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
And the messenger of YHWH called to him from the heavens and said, "Abraham! Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
And he said, "Do not stretch out your hand against the lad, and do not do anything to him; for now I know that you are one who fears God, and you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me."
And Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw, and there! a ram behind, caught in the thicket by its horns. And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place "YHWH will see", of which it is said today, "On the mountain of YHWH it will be seen."
And the messenger of YHWH called to Abraham a second time from the heavens.
And he said, "By myself I have sworn — the declaration of YHWH — that because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son, your only one,

"that blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and like the sand which is on the shore of the sea; and your offspring shall take possession of the gate of his enemies.
"And all the nations of the earth will bless themselves by your offspring, in consequence that you have listened to my voice."
And Abraham returned to his lads, and they arose and went together to Beersheba. And Abraham dwelt in Beersheba.
And it was, after these things, that it was told to Abraham, saying, "Here, Milcah has borne, she also, sons to Nahor your brother:
"Uz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
"and Kesed and Hazo and Pildash and Jidlaph and Bethuel."
And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor the brother of Abraham.
And his concubine, and her name was Reumah, she also bore: Tebah and Gaham and Tahash and Maacah.

genesis_23.t: And the life of Sarah was a hundred year and twenty year and seven years — the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah died at Kiriath-arba — that is Hebron — in the land of Canaan. And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
And Abraham arose from before the face of his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
"A sojourner and a resident alien am I with you. Give me a holding for a burial place with you, that I may bury my dead from before me."
And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,
"Hear us, my lord. A prince of God you are among us. In the choicest of our burial places bury your dead. No one of us will withhold from you his burial place from burying your dead."
And Abraham arose and bowed down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.
And he spoke with them, saying, "If it is with your desire to bury my dead from before me, hear me, and entreat for me with Ephron the son of Zohar,
"that he may give me the cave of the Machpelah which is his, which is at the end of his field. For full silver let him give it to me, in your midst, as a holding for a burial place."
And Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the ears of the sons of Heth, before all who came in at the gate of his city, saying,
"No, my lord, hear me. The field I have given to you, and the cave which is in it, to you I have given it. Before the eyes of the sons of my people I have given it to you. Bury your dead."
And Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.

And he spoke to Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, saying, "Nevertheless — if you would only hear me — I have given the silver of the field. Take it from me, that I may bury my dead there."
And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
"My lord, hear me. Land of four hundred shekels of silver — between me and between you, what is it? So bury your dead."
And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out to Ephron the silver which he had spoken in the ears of the sons of Heth: four hundred shekels of silver, passing with the merchant.

And the field of Ephron which was in the Machpelah, which was before Mamre, stood — the field and the cave which was in it and every tree which was in the field, which was in all its border round about —
— to Abraham as a purchase, before the eyes of the sons of Heth, among all who came in at the gate of his city.
And after this Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of the Machpelah, before the face of Mamre — that is Hebron — in the land of Canaan.
And the field and the cave which was in it stood to Abraham as a holding for a burial place, from the sons of Heth.

genesis_24.t: And Abraham was old, come into days, and YHWH had blessed Abraham in everything.
And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his household, who ruled over all that was his, "Put, now, your hand under my thigh,
"and I will make you swear by YHWH, God of the heavens and God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in whose midst I am dwelling,
"for to my land and to my kindred you shall go, and take a wife for my son, for Isaac."
And the servant said to him, "Perhaps the woman will not be willing to go after me to this land. Returning shall I return your son to the land from which you came out?"
And Abraham said to him, "Take heed to yourself, lest you return my son there.

"YHWH, God of the heavens, who took me from the house of my father and from the land of my kindred, and who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, 'To your offspring I will give this land' — he will send his messenger before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
"And if the woman is not willing to go after you, then you shall be free from this oath of mine. Only my son you must not return there."
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and he swore to him concerning this matter.
And the servant took ten camels from the camels of his master and went, and all the good of his master was in his hand. And he arose and went to Aram-naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
And he made the camels kneel outside the city, at the well of water, at the time of evening, at the time of the going out of the women who draw.
And he said, "YHWH, God of my master Abraham, cause it to happen before me today, and do loyalty with my master Abraham.
"Here I am standing at the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

"And let it be: the young woman to whom I say, 'Bend down, now, your jar, that I may drink,' and she says, 'Drink, and I will also water your camels' — her you have appointed for your servant, for Isaac; and by this I shall know that you have done loyalty with my master."
And it was, he had not yet finished speaking, and there! Rebekah was coming out — who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham — and her jar was on her shoulder.
And the young woman was very good of appearance, a virgin, and no man had known her. And she went down to the spring and filled her jar and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her and said, "Let me sip, now, a little water from your jar."
And she said, "Drink, my lord." And she hurried and let down her jar upon her hand and gave him drink.
And she finished giving him drink, and she said, "For your camels also I will draw, until they have finished drinking."
And she hurried and emptied her jar into the trough, and she ran again to the well to draw, and she drew for all his camels.
And the man was gazing at her, keeping silent, to know whether YHWH had made his journey successful or not.
And it was, just as the camels had finished drinking, that the man took a gold ring, a beka its weight, and two bracelets for her hands, ten of gold their weight,
and he said, "Whose daughter are you? Tell me, now. Is there in the house of your father room for us to lodge?"
And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor."
And she said to him, "Both straw and much fodder are with us, also room to lodge."
And the man bowed low and bowed down to YHWH.

And he said, "Blessed be YHWH, God of my master Abraham, who has not left his loyalty and his faithfulness from with my master. I — on the way YHWH has led me, to the house of the brothers of my master."
And the young woman ran and told the house of her mother according to these things.
And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. And Laban ran to the man, outside, to the spring.

And it was, when he saw the ring and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, "Thus the man spoke to me," that he came to the man; and there! he was standing with the camels at the spring.
And he said, "Come, blessed of YHWH! Why do you stand outside? And I have cleared the house, and a place for the camels."
And the man came to the house, and he unharnessed the camels, and he gave straw and fodder to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
And there was set before him to eat, and he said, "I will not eat until I have spoken my words." And he said, "Speak."
And he said, "I am the servant of Abraham.
"And YHWH has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great. And he has given him sheep and cattle and silver and gold and male servants and female servants and camels and donkeys.
"And Sarah, the wife of my master, bore a son to my master after her old age, and he has given him all that is his.
"And my master made me swear, saying, 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in whose land I am dwelling,
'but to the house of my father you shall go, and to my family, and take a wife for my son.'
"And I said to my master, 'Perhaps the woman will not go after me.'

"And he said to me, 'YHWH, before whom I have walked, will send his messenger with you and make your journey successful, and you shall take a wife for my son from my family and from the house of my father.
'Then you shall be free from my oath, when you come to my family; and if they do not give her to you, then you shall be free from my oath.'
"And I came today to the spring, and I said, 'YHWH, God of my master Abraham, if now you are making my journey successful, on which I am going —
'here I am standing at the spring of water; and let it be: the young woman who comes out to draw, and I say to her, "Give me drink, now, a little water from your jar,"
'and she says to me, "You also drink, and for your camels also I will draw" — she is the woman whom YHWH has appointed for the son of my master.'
"I had not yet finished speaking to my heart, and there! Rebekah was coming out, and her jar was on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew. And I said to her, 'Give me drink, now.'
"And she hurried and let down her jar from upon her and said, 'Drink, and I will water your camels also.' And I drank, and she also watered the camels.
"And I asked her and said, 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' And I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
"And I bowed low and bowed down to YHWH, and I blessed YHWH, God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the way of truth, to take the daughter of the brother of my master for his son.
"And now, if you are doing loyalty and faithfulness with my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right or to the left."
And Laban and Bethuel answered and said, "From YHWH the matter has come out. We are not able to speak to you evil or good.
"Here is Rebekah before you. Take and go, and let her be a wife to the son of your master, as YHWH has spoken."
And it was, when the servant of Abraham heard their words, that he bowed down groundward to YHWH.
And the servant brought out articles of silver and articles of gold and garments, and gave them to Rebekah; and precious things he gave to her brother and to her mother.
And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they lodged. And they arose in the morning, and he said, "Send me away to my master."
And her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman remain with us days, or ten; after, she shall go."
And he said to them, "Do not delay me, for YHWH has made my journey successful. Send me away, that I may go to my master."
And they said, "Let us call the young woman and ask her mouth."
And they called Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" And she said, "I will go."
And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and the servant of Abraham, and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring take possession of the gate of those who hate him."
And Rebekah arose, and her young women, and they rode on the camels and went after the man. And the servant took Rebekah and went.
And Isaac had come from the coming of Beer-lahai-roi, and he was dwelling in the land of the Negev.
And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward the turning of evening. And he lifted up his eyes and saw, and there! camels were coming.
And Rebekah lifted up her eyes and saw Isaac, and she fell from upon the camel.
And she said to the servant, "Who is that man, walking in the field to meet us?" And the servant said, "He is my master." And she took the veil and covered herself.
And the servant recounted to Isaac all the things which he had done.
And Isaac brought her to the tent, Sarah his mother, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted after his mother.

genesis_25.t: And Abraham added and took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
And she bore to him Zimran and Jokshan and Medan and Midian and Ishbak and Shuah.
And Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan were Asshurim and Letushim and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian: Ephah and Epher and Hanoch and Abida and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham gave all that was his to Isaac.
And to the sons of the concubines who were Abraham's, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from upon Isaac his son, while he was still alive, eastward, to the land of the east.
And these are the days of the years of the life of Abraham which he lived: a hundred year and seventy year and five years.
And Abraham expired and died in a good grey-headedness, old and satisfied, and he was gathered to his kin.
And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him at the cave of Machpelah, at the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre,
the field which Abraham acquired from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
And it was after the death of Abraham, and God blessed Isaac his son; and Isaac dwelt by Beer-lahai-roi.
And these are the generations of Ishmael son of Abraham, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.
And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, by their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar and Adbeel and Mibsam,
and Mishma and Dumah and Massa,
Hadad and Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.
These are they, the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments: twelve chiefs by their peoples.
And these are the years of the life of Ishmael: a hundred year and thirty year and seven years; and he expired and died, and he was gathered to his kin.
And they dwelt from Havilah as far as Shur, which is before Egypt, as you go toward Asshur. Before the face of all his brothers he fell.
And these are the generations of Isaac son of Abraham: Abraham fathered Isaac.
And Isaac was a son of forty years when he took Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram, sister of Laban the Aramean, to himself for a wife.
And Isaac entreated YHWH in the presence of his wife, for she was barren; and YHWH let himself be entreated by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
And the sons crushed one another within her, and she said, "If thus, why this I?" And she went to inquire of YHWH.
And YHWH said to her, "Two nations are in your belly, and two peoples from your inward parts shall be divided; and people shall be stronger than people; and greater shall serve younger."
And her days were filled to give birth, and behold, twins were in her belly.
And the first came out ruddy, all of him like a cloak of hair; and they called his name Esau.
And after that his brother came out, and his hand grasping the heel of Esau; and he called his name Jacob. And Isaac was a son of sixty years when she bore them.
And the lads grew up, and Esau was a man knowing hunting, a man of the open country; and Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.
And Isaac loved Esau, for game was in his mouth; and Rebekah was loving Jacob.
And Jacob cooked a cooking, and Esau came in from the open country, and he was exhausted.
And Esau said to Jacob, "Let me gulp down, please, some of the red, this red" — for he was exhausted; therefore his name was called Edom.
And Jacob said, "Sell, as of today, your birthright to me."
And Esau said, "Behold, I am going to die; and what is this to me, a birthright?"
And Jacob said, "Swear to me as of today." And he swore to him, and he sold his birthright to Jacob.
And Jacob gave to Esau bread and a cooking of lentils, and he ate and he drank and he rose and he went; and Esau despised the birthright.

genesis_26.t: And there was a famine in the land, apart from the former famine which was in the days of Abraham; and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
And YHWH appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall say to you."
"Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and will bless you; for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father."
"And I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and I will give to your offspring all these lands; and all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves by your offspring,"
"as a consequence that Abraham listened to my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes and my laws."
And Isaac dwelt in Gerar.

And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said, "She is my sister" — for he was afraid to say "my wife," lest the men of the place kill me on account of Rebekah, for she was good of appearance.

And it happened, when the days had grown long for him there, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through the window, and he saw, and behold, Isaac was making sport with Rebekah his wife.
And Abimelech called for Isaac and said, "Surely, behold, she is your wife! And how did you say, 'She is my sister'?" And Isaac said to him, "Because I said, lest I die on account of her."
And Abimelech said, "What is this you have done to us? A little more, and one of the people would have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us."
And Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, "Whoever touches this man or his wife, dying he shall be put to death."
And Isaac sowed in that land, and he found in that year a hundred measures; and YHWH blessed him.
And the man became great, and he went on going and growing great, until he was very great.
And there was to him livestock of flock and livestock of herd, and much service; and the Philistines envied him.
And all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped up and filled with earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go from with us, for you have become much too powerful for us."
And Isaac went from there, and he encamped in the wadi of Gerar, and he dwelt there.

And Isaac returned and dug the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, and which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham; and he called them by names, like the names which his father had called them.
And Isaac's servants dug in the wadi, and they found there a well of living water.
And the herdsmen of Gerar disputed with the herdsmen of Isaac, saying, "The water is ours." And he called the name of the well Esek, because they had contended with him.
And they dug another well, and they disputed over that one also; and he called its name Sitnah.

And he moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not dispute over it; and he called its name Rehoboth, and he said, "For now YHWH has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land."
And he went up from there to Beer-sheba.

And YHWH appeared to him in that night and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant."
And he built there an altar and called on the name of YHWH, and he pitched his tent there; and Isaac's servants dug a well there.
And Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his close friend, and Phicol the commander of his army.
And Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and sent me away from you?"
And they said, "Seeing we have seen that YHWH has been with you, and we said, let there be, please, an oath between us — between us and you — and let us cut a covenant with you:"
"that you will not do us harm, just as we have not touched you, and just as we have done with you only good, and sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of YHWH."
And he made them a feast, and they ate and they drank.
And they rose early in the morning and swore, each man to his brother; and Isaac sent them off, and they went from him in peace.
And it happened on that day that Isaac's servants came and told him about the well which they had dug, and they said to him, "We have found water."
And he called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beer-sheba to this day.
And Esau was a son of forty years, and he took as wife Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
And they were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.

genesis_27.t: And it happened, when Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim to see, that he called Esau his elder son and said to him, "My son." And he said to him, "Here I am."
And he said, "Behold now, I am old; I do not know the day of my death."
"And now, take up, please, your gear — your quiver and your bow — and go out to the open country and hunt game for me,"
"and make me savoury food such as I love, and bring it to me, and let me eat, so that my self may bless you before I die."
And Rebekah was listening when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. And Esau went to the open country to hunt game, to bring it.
And Rebekah said to Jacob her son, saying, "Behold, I have heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying,"
"'Bring me game and make me savoury food, and let me eat, and let me bless you before YHWH before my death.'"
"And now, my son, listen to my voice, to what I am commanding you."
"Go, please, to the flock and fetch me from there two good kids of the goats, and I will make them into savoury food for your father, such as he loves;"
"and you shall bring it to your father, and he will eat, so that he may bless you before his death."
And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man."
"Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall be in his eyes like a mocker, and I shall bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing."
And his mother said to him, "Upon me be your curse, my son. Only listen to my voice and go, fetch them for me."
And he went and fetched and brought them to his mother, and his mother made savoury food such as his father loved.
And Rebekah took the garments of Esau her elder son, the choice ones which were with her in the house, and she clothed Jacob her younger son.
And the skins of the kids of the goats she put on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
And she put the savoury food and the bread which she had made into the hand of Jacob her son.
And he came to his father and said, "My father." And he said, "Here I am. Who are you, my son?"
And Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you spoke to me. Rise, please, sit and eat of my game, so that your self may bless me."
And Isaac said to his son, "How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?" And he said, "Because YHWH your God made it happen before me."
And Isaac said to Jacob, "Draw near, please, and let me feel you, my son — whether you are this one, my son Esau, or not."
And Jacob drew near to Isaac his father, and he felt him, and he said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, and the hands are the hands of Esau."
And he did not recognise him, for his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau his brother; and he blessed him.
And he said, "Are you this one, my son Esau?" And he said, "I am."
And he said, "Bring it near to me, and let me eat of my son's game, so that my self may bless you." And he brought it near to him and he ate; and he brought him wine and he drank.
And Isaac his father said to him, "Draw near, please, and kiss me, my son."
And he drew near and kissed him, and he smelled the smell of his garments, and he blessed him and said: "See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which YHWH has blessed."
"And may the God give you of the dew of the heavens, and of the fatnesses of the earth, and abundance of grain and new wine."
"May peoples serve you, and may nations bow down to you. Be lord to your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Those who curse you, cursed; and those who bless you, blessed."

And it happened, just as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and it happened, Jacob had only just gone out, gone out from before the face of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
And he also made savoury food, and he brought it to his father, and he said to his father, "Let my father rise and eat of his son's game, so that your self may bless me."
And Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" And he said, "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau."

And Isaac trembled a great trembling, exceedingly, and said, "Who then is he that hunted game and brought it to me, and I ate of all of it before you came, and I blessed him? Moreover, blessed he shall be."
When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out a great and bitter cry, exceedingly, and he said to his father, "Bless me, me also, my father!"
And he said, "Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing."

And he said, "Is it because his name was called Jacob that he has supplanted me these two times? My birthright he took, and behold, now he has taken my blessing." And he said, "Have you not reserved a blessing for me?"

And Isaac answered and said to Esau, "Behold, I have made him lord over you, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and with grain and new wine I have sustained him. And for you, then, what shall I do, my son?"
And Esau said to his father, "Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me, me also, my father!" And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
And Isaac his father answered and said to him: "Behold, away from the fatnesses of the earth shall your dwelling be, and away from the dew of the heavens above."
"And by your sword you shall live, and your brother you shall serve; and it shall be, when you grow restless, that you shall tear his yoke from upon your neck."

And Esau bore a grudge against Jacob over the blessing with which his father had blessed him; and Esau said in his heart, "The days of mourning for my father are drawing near, and I will kill Jacob my brother."

And the words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah; and she sent and called for Jacob her younger son, and she said to him, "Behold, Esau your brother is consoling himself concerning you, to kill you."
"And now, my son, listen to my voice: rise, flee for yourself to Laban my brother, to Haran,"
"and you shall stay with him a few days, until your brother's fury turns back,"
"until your brother's anger turns back from you and he forgets what you did to him; then I will send and take you from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?"
And Rebekah said to Isaac, "I loathe my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth like these, from the daughters of the land, what is life to me?"

genesis_28.t: And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and he commanded him and said to him, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan."
"Rise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take yourself a wife from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother."
"And may God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful and multiply you, and may you become a company of peoples."
"And may he give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, for your taking possession of the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham."
And Isaac sent Jacob off, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.

And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and had sent him off to Paddan-aram to take himself a wife from there — in his blessing him he had commanded him, saying, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan" —
and Jacob had listened to his father and to his mother and had gone to Paddan-aram;
and Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the eyes of Isaac his father.
And Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, sister of Nebaioth, in addition to his wives, for himself as a wife.
And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba and went toward Haran.
And he came upon the place and stayed the night there, for the sun had gone in; and he took one of the stones of the place and put it at his head, and he lay down in that place.
And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reaching to the heavens; and behold, messengers of God going up and going down on it.
And behold, YHWH standing over it, and he said, "I am YHWH, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying — to you I will give it, and to your offspring."

"And your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall break out westward and eastward and northward and southward; and all the families of the earth shall be blessed in you and in your offspring."
"And behold, I am with you, and I will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this ground; for I will not abandon you until I have done what I have spoken to you."
And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, "Truly YHWH is in this place, and I did not know it."
And he was afraid and said, "How fearsome is this place! This is nothing other than the house of God, and this is the gate of the heavens."
And Jacob rose early in the morning and took the stone which he had put at his head, and he set it up as a pillar, and he poured oil on its top.
And he called the name of that place Beth-el; but Luz was the name of the city formerly.
And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, "If God will be with me and will keep me on this way that I am going, and will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear,"
"and I return in peace to my father's house — then YHWH shall be my God,"
"and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be the house of God; and of all that you give me, tithing I will tithe it to you."

genesis_29.t: And Jacob lifted up his feet and went to the land of the people of the east.

And he looked, and behold, a well in the open country, and behold, three flocks of sheep lying beside it — for from that well they watered the flocks — and the stone over the mouth of the well was large.
And all the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone from over the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put the stone back over the mouth of the well, to its place.
And Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" And they said, "We are from Haran."
And he said to them, "Do you know Laban son of Nahor?" And they said, "We know him."
And he said to them, "Is it well with him?" And they said, "It is well. And behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep."
And he said, "Behold, the day is still great; it is not the time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep and go, pasture them."
And they said, "We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered and they roll the stone from over the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep."
He was still speaking with them, and Rachel came with the sheep that were her father's, for she was a shepherd.

And it happened, when Jacob saw Rachel daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob drew near and rolled the stone from over the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban his mother's brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and he lifted up his voice and wept.
And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's kinsman and that he was Rebekah's son; and she ran and told her father.

And it happened, when Laban heard the report of Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house; and he recounted to Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him, "Surely you are my bone and my flesh." And he stayed with him a month of days.
And Laban said to Jacob, "Is it because you are my kinsman that you should serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?"
And Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
And Leah's eyes were soft, and Rachel was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance.
And Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter."
And Laban said, "It is better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man. Stay with me."
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they were in his eyes like a few days, in his love for her.
And Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife, for my days are completed, that I may go in to her."
And Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a feast.
And it happened in the evening that he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.
And Laban gave to her Zilpah his maidservant, to Leah his daughter as a maidservant.
And it happened in the morning — and behold, she was Leah! And he said to Laban, "What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served with you? And why have you deceived me?"
And Laban said, "It is not done thus in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn."
"Complete the week of this one, and we will give you that one also, for the service which you shall serve with me another seven years more."
And Jacob did so, and completed the week of that one; and he gave him Rachel his daughter, to him as a wife.
And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maidservant, to her as a maidservant.
And he went in also to Rachel, and he loved Rachel also more than Leah; and he served with him another seven years more.
And YHWH saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb; and Rachel was barren.
And Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, "Because YHWH has looked on my affliction — for now my husband will love me."
And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "Because YHWH has heard that I am hated, he has given me this one also." And she called his name Simeon.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me, for I have borne him three sons." Therefore he called his name Levi.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "This time I will praise YHWH." Therefore she called his name Judah. And she stopped bearing.

genesis_30.t: And Rachel saw that she had borne no children to Jacob, and Rachel was jealous of her sister, and she said to Jacob, "Give me children — and if not, I am dead."
And Jacob's anger burned against Rachel, and he said, "Am I in place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?"
And she said, "Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Go in to her, and let her bear upon my knees, and I too shall be built up from her."
And she gave him Bilhah her maidservant as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.
And Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.
And Rachel said, "God has judged me, and he has also listened to my voice and given me a son." Therefore she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again and bore a second son to Jacob.
And Rachel said, "Wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed." And she called his name Naphtali.
And Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, and she took Zilpah her maidservant and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore Jacob a son.
And Leah said, "Fortune has come!" And she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore a second son to Jacob.
And Leah said, "In my happiness! For daughters will call me happy." And she called his name Asher.

And Reuben went in the days of the wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the open country, and he brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah, "Give me, please, some of your son's mandrakes."

And she said to her, "Is it a small thing, your taking my husband, that you would take also my son's mandrakes?" And Rachel said, "Therefore let him lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."

And Jacob came from the open country in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, "You shall come in to me, for hiring I have hired you with my son's mandrakes." And he lay with her that night.
And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.
And Leah said, "God has given my wages, because I gave my maidservant to my husband." And she called his name Issachar.
And Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
And Leah said, "God has endowed me, me, with a good endowment. This time my husband will exalt me, for I have borne him six sons." And she called his name Zebulun.
And afterward she bore a daughter, and she called her name Dinah.
And God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb.
And she conceived and bore a son, and she said, "God has gathered away my reproach."
And she called his name Joseph, saying, "May YHWH add to me another son."
And it happened, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, "Send me off, that I may go to my place and to my land."
"Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you yourself know my service which I have served you."
And Laban said to him, "If, please, I have found favour in your eyes — I have divined that YHWH has blessed me on your account."
And he said, "Designate your wages upon me, and I will give it."
And he said to him, "You yourself know how I have served you, and how your livestock has fared with me."
"For the little you had before me has burst out into abundance, and YHWH has blessed you at my foot. And now, when shall I too work for my own house?"
