And he said, "What shall I give you?" And Jacob said, "You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will return, I will pasture your flock, I will keep it."

"Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted sheep, and every dark sheep among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and that shall be my wages."

"And my righteousness will testify for me on a later day, when you come concerning my wages before you: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and dark among the lambs, it is stolen, with me."
And Laban said, "Behold — if only it were according to your word."

And on that day he removed the striped and spotted male goats, and all the speckled and spotted female goats — every one that had white on it — and every dark one among the lambs, and he gave them into the hand of his sons.
And he set a journey of three days between himself and Jacob; and Jacob was pasturing the rest of Laban's flock.
And Jacob took for himself fresh rods of poplar and almond and plane, and he peeled white peelings in them, laying bare the white that was on the rods.
And he set the rods which he had peeled in the troughs, in the watering channels, where the flock came to drink, in front of the flock; and they went into heat when they came to drink.
And the flock went into heat at the rods, and the flock bore striped, speckled and spotted young.

And the lambs Jacob separated, and he set the faces of the flock toward the striped and every dark one in Laban's flock; and he made flocks for himself alone, and he did not put them with Laban's flock.
And it happened, whenever the sturdy of the flock went into heat, Jacob would set the rods before the eyes of the flock in the troughs, so that they would mate at the rods.
And when the flock were feeble he would not set them; so the feeble ones came to be Laban's, and the sturdy ones Jacob's.
And the man burst out very, very much, and he came to have many flocks, and maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.

genesis_31.t: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, "Jacob has taken all that was our father's, and from what was our father's he has made all this weight of wealth."
And Jacob saw the face of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as yesterday and the day before.
And YHWH said to Jacob, "Return to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you."
And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the open country, to his flock.
And he said to them, "I am seeing your father's face, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the day before; but the God of my father has been with me."
"And you yourselves know that with all my strength I have served your father."
"And your father has trifled with me and changed my wages ten times; but God did not permit him to do me harm."
"If he said thus, 'The speckled shall be your wages,' then all the flock bore speckled; and if he said thus, 'The striped shall be your wages,' then all the flock bore striped."
"So God took away your father's livestock and gave it to me."
"And it happened at the time the flock went into heat that I lifted my eyes and saw in a dream, and behold, the he-goats mounting the flock were striped, speckled and mottled."
"And the messenger of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob,' and I said, 'Here I am.'"
"And he said, 'Lift up, please, your eyes and see: all the he-goats mounting the flock are striped, speckled and mottled — for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.'"
"'I am the God of Beth-el, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to me. Now arise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your kindred.'"
And Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, "Have we still a share and an inheritance in our father's house?"
"Are we not accounted by him as foreign women? For he has sold us, and he has also consumed, consuming, our silver."
"For all the wealth which God has taken away from our father — it is ours and our children's. So now, all that God has said to you, do."
And Jacob arose and lifted his children and his wives onto the camels,

and he drove all his livestock and all his goods which he had accumulated, the livestock of his acquisition which he had accumulated in Paddan-aram, to come to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
And Laban had gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stole the teraphim that belonged to her father.
And Jacob stole the heart of Laban the Aramean, in not telling him that he was fleeing.
And he fled, he and all that was his; and he arose and crossed the River and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.
And it was told to Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.
And he took his kinsmen with him and pursued after him a journey of seven days, and he overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.
And God came to Laban the Aramean in the dream of the night and said to him, "Take heed to yourself, lest you speak with Jacob from good to bad."
And Laban overtook Jacob; and Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban pitched with his kinsmen in the hill country of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done, that you stole my heart and led away my daughters like captives of the sword?"
"Why did you hide yourself to flee, and steal me, and not tell me? — that I might have sent you off with gladness and with songs, with tambourine and with lyre."
"And you did not let me kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly in doing so."
"It is in the power of my hand to do you harm; but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, 'Take heed to yourself from speaking with Jacob from good to bad.'"
"And now, going you have gone, because longing you longed for your father's house. Why did you steal my gods?"
And Jacob answered and said to Laban, "Because I was afraid; for I said, lest you tear your daughters away from me."
"With whomever you find your gods, he shall not live. Before our kinsmen, identify for yourself what is with me, and take it for yourself." And Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.
And Laban went into Jacob's tent and into Leah's tent and into the tent of the two maidservants, and he did not find them; and he went out from Leah's tent and went into Rachel's tent.
And Rachel had taken the teraphim and put them in the camel's saddlebag and sat on them; and Laban felt through the whole tent and did not find them.
And she said to her father, "Let it not burn in my lord's eyes that I am not able to rise before you, for the way of women is upon me." And he searched and did not find the teraphim.
And it burned for Jacob, and he quarrelled with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban, "What is my transgression? What is my sin, that you have burned in pursuit after me?"
"For you have felt through all my things — what have you found of all your household things? Set it here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, and let them decide between the two of us."
"These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your she-goats have not miscarried, and the rams of your flock I have not eaten."
"A torn animal I did not bring to you; I myself bore its loss. From my hand you required it — the stolen of the day and the stolen of the night."
"I was — by day the heat consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes."
"This is twenty years for me in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times."

"If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been for me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. My affliction and the labour of my hands God has seen, and he decided last night."

And Laban answered and said to Jacob, "The daughters are my daughters, and the children are my children, and the flock is my flock, and all that you see is mine. But for my daughters — what shall I do for these today, or for their children whom they have borne?"
"And now, come, let us cut a covenant, I and you, and let it be a witness between me and you."
And Jacob took a stone and raised it up as a pillar.
And Jacob said to his kinsmen, "Gather stones." And they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.
And Laban called it Yegar Sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
And Laban said, "This heap is a witness between me and you today." Therefore its name was called Galeed,
and Mizpah, for he said, "May YHWH keep watch between me and you when we are hidden from each other,"
"if you mistreat my daughters, and if you take wives besides my daughters — no man is with us; see, God is witness between me and you."
And Laban said to Jacob, "Behold this heap, and behold the pillar which I have set up between me and you."
"This heap is a witness, and the pillar is a witness, that I will not pass beyond this heap to you, and that you will not pass beyond this heap and this pillar to me, for harm."
"The God of Abraham and the God of Nahor — may they judge between us, the God of their father." And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
And Jacob sacrificed a sacrifice in the hill country and called his kinsmen to eat bread; and they ate bread and stayed the night in the hill country.
And Laban rose early in the morning and kissed his sons and his daughters and blessed them; and Laban went and returned to his place.

genesis_32.t: And Jacob, he went to his way, and messengers of God met him.
And Jacob said, when he saw them, 'A camp of God is this,' and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, toward the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
And he commanded them, saying, 'Thus you shall say to my lord, to Esau: Thus says your servant Jacob: With Laban I have sojourned, and I have delayed until now.'
And there has come to be to me ox and donkey, flock and male servant and female servant; and I have sent to tell my lord, to find favour in your eyes.
And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, 'We came to your brother, to Esau, and also he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him.'
And Jacob feared exceedingly, and it was distress to him; and he divided the people who were with him, and the flock and the herd and the camels, into two camps.
And he said, 'If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the camp that remains shall be for an escaped remnant.'
And Jacob said, 'God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, YHWH who says to me, "Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will do good with you" —'
'I am too small for all the acts of steadfast love and for all the faithfulness that you have done with your servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
'Deliver me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I am fearing him, lest he come and strike me, mother upon children.
'And you, you said, "Doing good I will do good with you, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, which shall not be counted for multitude."'
And he stayed the night there in that night, and he took from what had come into his hand a gift for Esau his brother.
Female goats two hundred and male goats twenty, ewes two hundred and rams twenty,
nursing camels and their young thirty, cows forty and bulls ten, female donkeys twenty and donkey foals ten.
And he gave them into the hand of his servants, drove by drove by itself, and he said to his servants, 'Pass over before me, and a space you shall put between drove and drove.'
And he commanded the first, saying, 'When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying, "To whom do you belong, and where are you going, and to whom are these before you?" —
then you shall say, "To your servant, to Jacob; it is a gift sent to my lord, to Esau; and look, he also is behind us."'
And he commanded both the second and the third and all who were going behind the droves, saying, 'According to this word you shall speak to Esau when you find him;

and you shall say, "Also, look, your servant Jacob is behind us."' For he said, 'Let me cover his face with the gift that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will lift up my face.'
And the gift passed over upon his face, and he himself stayed the night in that night in the camp.
And he rose in that night, and he took his two wives and his two maidservants and his eleven children, and he passed over the ford of the Jabbok.
And he took them and sent them over the wadi, and he sent over what he had.
And Jacob was left, he alone, and a man wrestled with him until the coming up of the dawn.
And he saw that he did not prevail against him, and he touched the socket of his thigh, and the socket of Jacob's thigh was dislocated as he wrestled with him.
And he said, 'Let me go, for the dawn has come up.' And he said, 'I will not let you go unless you have blessed me.'
And he said to him, 'What is your name?' And he said, 'Jacob.'
And he said, 'Not Jacob shall your name be called any more, but Israel; for you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.'
And Jacob asked and said, 'Tell me, please, your name.' And he said, 'Why is this you ask for my name?' And he blessed him there.
And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel, 'For I have seen God face to face, and my life has been delivered.'
And the sun rose upon him as he passed over Penuel, and he was limping on his thigh.
Therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip that is on the socket of the thigh, until this day, because he touched the socket of Jacob's thigh, at the sinew of the hip.

genesis_33.t: And Jacob lifted up his eyes and saw, and look, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children upon Leah and upon Rachel and upon the two maidservants.
And he put the maidservants and their children first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph behind.
And he himself passed over before them, and he bowed down to the ground seven times, until his drawing near to his brother.
And Esau ran to meet him, and he embraced him, and he fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and he said, 'Who are these to you?' And he said, 'The children whom God has favoured your servant.'
And the maidservants approached, they and their children, and they bowed down.
And Leah also approached, and her children, and they bowed down; and after, Joseph approached, and Rachel, and they bowed down.
And he said, 'Who to you is all this camp that I have met?' And he said, 'To find favour in the eyes of my lord.'
And Esau said, 'There is to me much, my brother; let what is yours be yours.'

And Jacob said, 'No, please — if, please, I have found favour in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand; for therefore I have seen your face like the seeing of the face of God, and you have accepted me.'
'Take, please, my blessing that has been brought to you, for God has favoured me, and because there is to me everything.' And he urged him, and he took it.
And he said, 'Let us set out and let us go, and I will go alongside you.'
And he said to him, 'My lord knows that the children are tender, and the flock and the herd are nursing upon me; and if they drive them hard one day, all the flock will die.'
'Let my lord pass on before his servant, and I, I will lead on at my slowness, at the foot of the property that is before me and at the foot of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir.'
And Esau said, 'Let me place, please, with you some of the people who are with me.' And he said, 'Why this? Let me find favour in the eyes of my lord.'
And Esau returned on that day to his way, to Seir.
And Jacob set out to Succoth, and he built for himself a house, and for his livestock he made shelters; therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.
And Jacob came safe to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram, and he camped before the face of the city.
And he bought the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent, from the hand of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem, for a hundred pieces of money.
And he set up there an altar, and he called it El-Elohe-Israel.

genesis_34.t: And Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to look at the daughters of the land.
And Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the chief of the land, saw her, and he took her and lay with her and violated her.
And his self clung to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the girl, and he spoke to the heart of the girl.
And Shechem said to Hamor his father, saying, 'Get me this girl for a wife.'
And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter, and his sons were with his livestock in the field; and Jacob kept silent until they came.
And Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.

And the sons of Jacob came from the field when they heard, and the men were grieved, and it burned to them exceedingly, because he had done an outrage in Israel by lying with the daughter of Jacob — and so it is not done.
And Hamor spoke with them, saying, 'Shechem my son — his self loves your daughter. Give her, please, to him for a wife.
'And intermarry with us: your daughters you shall give to us, and our daughters you shall take for yourselves.
'And with us you shall dwell, and the land shall be before you; dwell and go about in it and take holdings in it.'
And Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, 'Let me find favour in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will give.
'Increase upon me exceedingly bride-price and gift, and I will give just as you say to me; and give me the girl for a wife.'
And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit, and they spoke — because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
And they said to them, 'We are not able to do this thing, to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin, for it is a reproach to us.
'Only in this will we agree to you: if you become like us, by every male of you being circumcised.
'And we will give our daughters to you, and your daughters we will take for ourselves, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
'And if you do not listen to us, to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and go.'
And their words were good in the eyes of Hamor and in the eyes of Shechem son of Hamor.
And the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in the daughter of Jacob; and he was honoured above all the household of his father.
And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and they spoke to the men of their city, saying,

'These men are at peace with us; let them dwell in the land and go about in it, and the land — look, it is broad of both hands before them. Their daughters we will take for ourselves as wives, and our daughters we will give to them.
'Only in this will the men agree to us, to dwell with us, to become one people: when every male of us has been circumcised, just as they are circumcised.
'Their livestock and their property and all their animals — will they not be ours? Only let us agree with them, and let them dwell with us.'
And all who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and to Shechem his son, and every male was circumcised — all who went out of the gate of his city.

And it was on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, took each his sword, and they came upon the city unopposed, and they killed every male.
And Hamor and Shechem his son they slew to the mouth of the sword, and they took Dinah from the house of Shechem and went out.
The sons of Jacob came upon the slain and plundered the city, which had defiled their sister.
Their flocks and their herds and their donkeys, and what was in the city and what was in the field, they took.
And all their wealth and all their little ones and their wives they took captive, and they plundered, and all that was in the house.

And Jacob said to Simeon and to Levi, 'You have troubled me, to make me stink among the inhabitant of the land, among the Canaanite and among the Perizzite; and I am men of number, and they will gather against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my household.'
And they said, 'Like a prostitute shall he treat our sister?'

genesis_35.t: And God said to Jacob, 'Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there, and make there an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from before Esau your brother.'
And Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, 'Remove the gods of foreignness that are in your midst, and cleanse yourselves, and change your clothes.
'And let us arise and go up to Bethel, and let me make there an altar to the God who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me on the way that I have gone.'
And they gave to Jacob all the gods of foreignness that were in their hand, and the rings that were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the terebinth that was near Shechem.
And they set out, and the terror of God was upon the cities that were around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
And Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan — that is Bethel — he and all the people who were with him.
And he built there an altar, and he called the place El-bethel, because there God revealed himself to him when he fled from before his brother.
And Deborah, the nurse of Rebekah, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and he called its name Allon Bacuth.
And God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and he blessed him.
And God said to him, 'Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be called Jacob any more, but Israel shall be your name.' And he called his name Israel.
And God said to him, 'I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and an assembly of nations shall be from you, and kings shall come out from your loins.
'And the land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, to you I will give it, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.'
And God went up from upon him, at the place where he had spoken with him.
And Jacob set up a pillar at the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured out on it a drink offering, and he poured on it oil.
And Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him there, Bethel.
And they set out from Bethel, and there was still a stretch of ground to come to Ephrath, and Rachel gave birth, and she had it hard in her giving birth.
And it was, when she had it hard in her giving birth, that the midwife said to her, 'Do not fear, for this one also is a son for you.'
And it was, as her life was going out — for she died — that she called his name Ben-oni; and his father called him Benjamin.
And Rachel died, and she was buried on the way to Ephrath — that is Bethlehem.
And Jacob set up a pillar over her grave; it is the pillar of Rachel's grave until this day.
And Israel set out, and he pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder.
And it was, when Israel was dwelling in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine, and Israel heard. — And the sons of Jacob were twelve.
The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant: Dan and Naphtali.
And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan Aram.
And Jacob came to Isaac his father, at Mamre, Kiriath-arba — that is Hebron — where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.
And the days of Isaac were a hundred years and eighty years.
And Isaac expired and died, and he was gathered to his peoples, old and satisfied of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

genesis_36.t: And these are the generations of Esau — that is Edom.
Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
and Basemath the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
And Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz, and Basemath bore Reuel.
And Oholibamah bore Jeush and Jalam and Korah. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

And Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters and all the people of his household, and his livestock and all his animals and all his possessions that he had accumulated in the land of Canaan, and he went to a land away from before Jacob his brother.
For their possessions were too much for dwelling together, and the land of their sojournings was not able to support them because of their livestock.
And Esau dwelt in the hill country of Seir. Esau — that is Edom.
And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in the hill country of Seir.
These are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz the son of Adah the wife of Esau, Reuel the son of Basemath the wife of Esau.
And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho and Gatam and Kenaz.
And Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz the son of Esau, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These are the sons of Adah the wife of Esau.
And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath the wife of Esau.
And these were the sons of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon, the wife of Esau: and she bore to Esau Jeush and Jalam and Korah.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

And these are the sons of Reuel the son of Esau: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath the wife of Esau.
And these are the sons of Oholibamah the wife of Esau: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the wife of Esau.
These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs — that is Edom.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan and Shobal and Zibeon and Anah,
and Dishon and Ezer and Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam; and the sister of Lotan was Timna.
And these are the sons of Shobal: Alvan and Manahath and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
And these are the sons of Zibeon: both Aiah and Anah. He is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness while he was pasturing the donkeys of Zibeon his father.
And these are the children of Anah: Dishon; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah.
And these are the sons of Dishan: Hemdan and Eshban and Ithran and Keran.
These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan and Zaavan and Akan.
These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the chiefs of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites, according to their chiefs, in the land of Seir.
And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned for the sons of Israel.
And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
And Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad reigned in his place, who defeated Midian in the region of Moab; and the name of his city was Avith.
And Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
And Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth of the River reigned in his place.
And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Pau; and the name of his wife was Mehetabel the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
And these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their clans, according to their places, by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their dwelling places in the land of their possession. That is Esau, the father of Edom.

genesis_37.t: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, a son of seventeen years, was shepherding with his brothers among the flock — and he a youth — with the sons of Bilhah and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father.
And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, for he was to him a son of old age; and he made for him a tunic of palms and soles.
And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and they were not able to speak to him for peace.
And Joseph dreamed a dream and told it to his brothers, and they added again to hate him.
And he said to them, 'Hear, please, this dream that I have dreamed.'
'And look, we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and look, my sheaf arose and also stood upright, and look, your sheaves gathered round and bowed down to my sheaf.'
And his brothers said to him, 'Reigning will you reign over us? Or ruling will you rule over us?' And they added again to hate him, over his dreams and over his words.
And he dreamed yet another dream, and he recounted it to his brothers, and he said, 'Look, I have dreamed a dream again, and look, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.'

And he recounted it to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said to him, 'What is this dream that you have dreamed? Coming, shall we come — I and your mother and your brothers — to bow down to you to the ground?'
And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter.
And his brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph, 'Are not your brothers pasturing at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.' And he said to him, 'Here I am.'
And he said to him, 'Go, please, see the peace of your brothers and the peace of the flock, and bring me back word.' And he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And a man found him, and look, he was wandering in the open country; and the man asked him, saying, 'What are you seeking?'
And he said, 'My brothers I am seeking. Tell me, please, where they are pasturing.'
And the man said, 'They have departed from here, for I heard them saying, "Let us go to Dothan."' And Joseph went after his brothers, and he found them at Dothan.
And they saw him from a distance, and before he drew near to them they dealt deceptively with him, to kill him.
And they said each to his brother, 'Look, this master of dreams is coming.'
'And now, come and let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say, "A wild animal has eaten him," and we shall see what his dreams will be.'
And Reuben heard, and he rescued him from their hand, and he said, 'Let us not strike him — a life.'

And Reuben said to them, 'Do not shed blood. Throw him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and do not stretch out a hand against him' — so as to rescue him from their hand, to bring him back to his father.
And it was, when Joseph came to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic of palms and soles that was on him,
and they took him and threw him toward the pit; and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

And they sat down to eat bread; and they lifted up their eyes and saw, and look, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, and their camels were carrying gum, balm and ladanum, going to bring them down to Egypt.
And Judah said to his brothers, 'What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
'Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let our hand not be against him, for he is our brother, our flesh.' And his brothers listened.
And Midianite men, traders, passed by, and they drew and brought Joseph up from the pit, and they sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty of silver; and they brought Joseph to Egypt.
And Reuben returned to the pit, and look, Joseph was not in the pit; and he tore his clothes.
And he returned to his brothers and said, 'The boy is not — and I, where am I to go?'
And they took Joseph's tunic, and they slaughtered a male goat, and they dipped the tunic in the blood.
And they sent the tunic of palms and soles, and they brought it to their father, and they said, 'This we have found. Recognise, please: is it your son's tunic, or not?'
And he recognised it and said, 'My son's tunic! A wild animal has eaten him. Torn, Joseph has been torn to pieces.'
And Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins, and he mourned over his son many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters arose to comfort him, and he refused to be comforted, and he said, 'For I will go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol.' And his father wept for him.
And the Medanites sold him into Egypt, to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the slaughterers.

genesis_38.t: And it was at that time that Judah went down from his brothers, and he turned aside to an Adullamite man, and his name was Hirah.
And Judah saw there a daughter of a Canaanite man, and his name was Shua; and he took her and went in to her.
And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
And she repeated again and bore a son, and she called his name Shelah; and he was at Kezib when she bore him.
And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
And Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH put him to death.
And Judah said to Onan, 'Go in to your brother's wife and act as brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.'
And Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; and so it was, whenever he went in to his brother's wife, that he ruined [it] toward the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
And what he did was evil in the eyes of YHWH, and he put him to death also.

And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, 'Dwell a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up' — for he said, 'Lest he die also, he like his brothers.' And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
And the days increased, and the daughter of Shua, Judah's wife, died. And Judah was comforted, and he went up to his sheepshearers, he and Hirah his friend the Adullamite, to Timnah.
And it was told to Tamar, saying, 'Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.'

And she removed the clothes of her widowhood from upon her, and she covered herself with the veil and wrapped herself up, and she sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah — for she had seen that Shelah had grown up and she had not been given to him for a wife.
And Judah saw her and considered her a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

And he turned aside to her by the road and said, 'Give me leave, please — let me go in to you' — for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, 'What will you give me, that you may come in to me?'
And he said, 'I will send a kid of the goats from the flock.' And she said, 'If you will give a pledge until your sending it.'

And he said, 'What is the pledge that I shall give you?' And she said, 'Your seal and your cord and your staff that is in your hand.' And he gave them to her, and he went in to her, and she conceived by him.
And she arose and went, and she removed her veil from upon her, and she put on the clothes of her widowhood.
And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to take the pledge from the woman's hand; and he did not find her.
And he asked the men of her place, saying, 'Where is the set-apart woman, the one at Enaim by the road?' And they said, 'There has been no set-apart woman in this place.'
And he returned to Judah and said, 'I did not find her; and also the men of the place said, "There has been no set-apart woman in this place."'
And Judah said, 'Let her take them for herself, lest we become a contempt. Look, I sent this kid, and you did not find her.'

And it was, about three months later, that it was told to Judah, saying, 'Tamar your daughter-in-law has acted as a prostitute, and moreover, look, she is pregnant by prostitution.' And Judah said, 'Bring her out, and let her be burned.'

She was being brought out, and she sent to her father-in-law, saying, 'By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant.' And she said, 'Recognise, please: whose are the seal and the cord and the staff, these?'
And Judah recognised them and said, 'She is more in the right than I, for indeed I did not give her to Shelah my son.' And he did not know her again.
And it was at the time of her giving birth, and look, twins were in her womb.
And it was, in her giving birth, that one put out a hand; and the midwife took and tied on his hand a scarlet thread, saying, 'This one came out first.'
And it was, as he was withdrawing his hand, that look, his brother came out; and she said, 'How you have broken out — a breach upon you!' And his name was called Perez.
And afterward his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread, and his name was called Zerah.

genesis_39.t: And Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the slaughterers, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
And YHWH was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master saw that YHWH was with him, and that all that he was doing YHWH was making successful in his hand.
And Joseph found favour in his eyes, and he served him; and he appointed him over his household, and all that he had he gave into his hand.

And it was, from the time he appointed him over his household and over all that he had, that YHWH blessed the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph; and the blessing of YHWH was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand, and he did not know anything with him except the food that he was eating. And Joseph was handsome of form and handsome of appearance.
And it was after these things that his master's wife lifted up her eyes to Joseph, and she said, 'Lie with me.'
And he refused, and he said to his master's wife, 'Look, my master does not know with me what is in the house, and all that he has he has given into my hand.
'He is not greater in this house than I, and he has not withheld from me anything except you, in that you are his wife. And how shall I do this great evil, and sin against God?'
And it was, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he did not listen to her, to lie beside her, to be with her.
And it was, about this day, that he came to the house to do his work; and there was no man of the men of the house there in the house.
And she seized him by his clothing, saying, 'Lie with me.' And he left his clothing in her hand, and he fled and went outside.
And it was, when she saw that he had left his clothing in her hand and had fled outside,
that she called out to the men of her household and said to them, saying, 'See — he has brought us a Hebrew man to mock us. He came to me to lie with me, and I called out with a loud voice.
'And it was, when he heard that I raised my voice and called out, that he left his clothing beside me and fled and went outside.'
And she placed his clothing beside her until his master came to his house.
And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, 'The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came to me to mock me.
'And it was, when I raised my voice and called out, that he left his clothing beside me and fled outside.'
And it was, when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, 'According to these things your servant did to me,' that his anger burned.
And Joseph's master took him and put him into the house of the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were imprisoned; and he was there in the house of the prison.
And YHWH was with Joseph, and he extended steadfast love to him, and he gave his favour in the eyes of the commander of the house of the prison.
And the commander of the house of the prison gave into Joseph's hand all the prisoners who were in the house of the prison; and all that they were doing there, he was the one doing it.
The commander of the house of the prison was not seeing anything at all in his hand, in that YHWH was with him; and what he was doing, YHWH was making successful.

genesis_40.t: And it was, after these things, [that] the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker sinned against their lord, the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh was angry at his two officials, at the chief of the cupbearers and at the chief of the bakers.
And he put them in the custody of the house of the commander of the guard, into the prison house, the place where Joseph was imprisoned there.
And the commander of the guard appointed Joseph with them, and he served them; and they were days in custody.

And they dreamed a dream, the two of them, each his own dream in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream — the cupbearer and the baker who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were imprisoned in the prison house.
And Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, and there they were, dejected.
And he asked the officials of Pharaoh who were with him in the custody of his lord's house, saying, Why are your faces bad today?
And they said to him, A dream we have dreamed, and there is no one interpreting it. And Joseph said to them, Do not interpretations belong to God? Recount it, please, to me.
And the chief of the cupbearers recounted his dream to Joseph, and he said to him, In my dream — and there! a vine was before me,
and on the vine three branches; and it, as it was budding, its blossom went up, its clusters ripened grapes.
And the cup of Pharaoh was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into the cup of Pharaoh, and I put the cup on the palm of Pharaoh.
And Joseph said to him, This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
In yet three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your post, and you will put the cup of Pharaoh into his hand according to the former custom, when you were his cupbearer.
Only remember me with you when it goes well for you, and do, please, loyalty with me, and bring me to remembrance before Pharaoh, and bring me out from this house.
For stolen I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and also here I have done nothing, that they should have put me in the pit.
And the chief of the bakers saw that he had interpreted well, and he said to Joseph, I too, in my dream — and there! three baskets of ḥori were on my head,
and in the uppermost basket some of all the food of Pharaoh, the work of a baker; and the birds were eating them from the basket from on my head.
And Joseph answered and said, This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
In yet three days Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.

And it was on the third day, the day of Pharaoh's being born, and he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief of the cupbearers and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants.
And he restored the chief of the cupbearers to his cupbearing, and he put the cup on the palm of Pharaoh.
And the chief of the bakers he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted for them.
And the chief of the cupbearers did not remember Joseph, and he forgot him.

genesis_41.t: And it was at the end of two years of days, and Pharaoh was dreaming, and there! he was standing by the Nile.
And there! from the Nile were coming up seven cows, good of appearance and fat of flesh, and they grazed in the reed grass.
And there! seven other cows coming up after them from the Nile, bad of appearance and thin of flesh, and they stood beside the cows on the bank of the Nile.
And the cows bad of appearance and thin of flesh ate the seven cows good of appearance and fat, and Pharaoh awoke.
And he slept and dreamed a second time, and there! seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, fat and good.
And there! seven ears of grain, thin and scorched by an east wind, springing up after them.
And the thin ears swallowed the seven fat and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and there! a dream.

And it was in the morning, and his spirit was troubled, and he sent and summoned all the ḥarṭummim of Egypt and all its wise men, and Pharaoh recounted to them his dream, and there was no one interpreting them for Pharaoh.
And the chief of the cupbearers spoke with Pharaoh, saying, My sins I am bringing to remembrance today.
Pharaoh was angry at his servants, and he put me in the custody of the house of the commander of the guard — me and the chief of the bakers.
And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; each according to the interpretation of his dream we dreamed.
And there with us was a Hebrew young man, a slave of the commander of the guard, and we recounted to him, and he interpreted for us our dreams; to each according to his dream he interpreted.
And it was, just as he interpreted for us, so it was: me he restored to my post, and him he hanged.
And Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph, and they hurried him from the pit; and he shaved and changed his clothes and came to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, A dream I have dreamed, and there is no one interpreting it. And I, I have heard concerning you, saying, You hear a dream to interpret it.
And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, Apart from me — God will answer the welfare of Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, In my dream, there I was, standing on the bank of the Nile.
And there! from the Nile were coming up seven cows, fat of flesh and good of form, and they grazed in the reed grass.
And there! seven other cows coming up after them, weak and very bad of form and lean of flesh; I have not seen their like in all the land of Egypt for badness.
And the lean and bad cows ate the seven former, fat cows.
And they went into their inward parts, and it was not known that they had gone into their inward parts; and their appearance was bad, just as at the beginning. And I awoke.
And I saw in my dream, and there! seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, full and good.
And there! seven ears of grain, ṣenumot, thin, scorched by an east wind, springing up after them.
And the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears. And I said it to the ḥarṭummim, and there was no one telling it to me.
And Joseph said to Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is doing he has told to Pharaoh.
The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; it is one dream.
And the seven lean and bad cows coming up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears scorched by the east wind — they will be seven years of famine.
That is the word which I spoke to Pharaoh: what God is doing he has shown Pharaoh.
There! seven years are coming — great plenty in all the land of Egypt.
And seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will finish off the land.
And the plenty will not be known in the land because of that famine afterward, for it will be very heavy.
And as for the dream being repeated to Pharaoh twice — because the matter is fixed from with God, and God is hurrying to do it.
And now let Pharaoh see a man discerning and wise, and let him set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh act, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take a fifth of the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty.
And let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and let them store up grain under the hand of Pharaoh, food in the cities, and let them keep it.
And the food will be a store for the land for the seven years of famine which will be in the land of Egypt, and the land will not be cut off by the famine.
And the word was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to his servants, Shall we find one like this, a man in whom is the spirit of God?
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, After God has made all this known to you, there is no one discerning and wise like you.
You will be over my house, and by your mouth all my people will be ruled; only in the throne will I be greater than you.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph's hand, and clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put the chain of gold on his neck.
And he made him ride in the second chariot that was his, and they called out before him, Abrek! And he set him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and apart from you no one will lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, for a wife. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
And Joseph was a son of thirty years when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from before Pharaoh and passed through all the land of Egypt.
And the land produced in the seven years of plenty by handfuls.
And he gathered all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and he put food in the cities; the food of the fields of a city which were around it he put inside it.
And Joseph stored up grain like the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for there was no counting.
And to Joseph two sons were born before the year of the famine came, whom Asenath the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, bore to him.
And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, for [he said], God has made me forget all my trouble and all my father's house.
And the name of the second he called Ephraim, for [he said], God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.
And the seven years of plenty which were in the land of Egypt came to an end.
And the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. And there was famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
And all the land of Egypt was hungry, and the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all Egypt, Go to Joseph; what he says to you, you will do.
And the famine was over all the face of the land, and Joseph opened all that was in them and sold grain to Egypt; and the famine grew strong in the land of Egypt.
And all the earth came to Egypt to buy grain, to Joseph, for the famine was strong in all the earth.

genesis_42.t: And Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, Why do you look at one another?
And he said, There! I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us from there, that we may live and not die.
And Joseph's brothers went down, ten of them, to buy grain from Egypt.
But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob did not send with his brothers, for he said, Lest harm should befall him.
And the sons of Israel came to buy grain among those who were coming, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
And Joseph — he was the ruler over the land, he was the one selling grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to him, faces to the ground.

And Joseph saw his brothers and recognised them, and he made himself a stranger to them and spoke harsh things with them. And he said to them, From where have you come? And they said, From the land of Canaan, to buy food.
And Joseph recognised his brothers, and they did not recognise him.
And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, You are spies! To see the nakedness of the land you have come.
And they said to him, No, my lord; and your servants have come to buy food.
All of us are the sons of one man. We are honest. Your servants have never been spies.
And he said to them, No — for the nakedness of the land you have come to see.
And they said, Twelve are your servants; we are brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. And there! the youngest is with our father today, and the one is not.
And Joseph said to them, That is what I said to you, saying, You are spies.
By this you will be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you will not go out from here unless your youngest brother comes here.
Send one from among you, and let him fetch your brother; and you, be imprisoned, and let your words be tested, whether the truth is with you. And if not — by the life of Pharaoh, you are spies.
And he gathered them into custody three days.
And Joseph said to them on the third day, Do this and live: I fear God.
If you are honest, let one of your brothers be imprisoned in your house of custody, and you, go, take grain for the hunger of your households,
and bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be confirmed and you will not die. And they did so.

And they said, each to his brother, Indeed we are guilty concerning our brother, whose distress of being we saw when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. That is why this distress has come to us.
And Reuben answered them, saying, Did I not say to you, saying, Do not sin against the boy? And you did not listen. And now, look, his blood is being required.
And they did not know that Joseph was listening, for the interpreter was between them.
And he turned away from them and wept. And he returned to them and spoke to them, and he took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.
And Joseph commanded, and they filled their vessels with grain, and to return their silver, each into his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And it was done for them so.
And they lifted their grain onto their donkeys and went from there.
And the one opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place, and he saw his silver, and there it was, in the mouth of his bag.
And he said to his brothers, My silver has been returned, and here it is, indeed, in my bag! And their heart went out, and they trembled, each to his brother, saying, What is this God has done to us?
And they came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and they told him all that had happened to them, saying,
The man, the lord of the land, spoke harsh things with us, and he took us for those spying out the land.
And we said to him, We are honest; we have never been spies.
We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. The one is not, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.
And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, By this I shall know that you are honest: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the hunger of your households and go,
and bring your youngest brother to me, and I shall know that you are not spies, that you are honest. I will give you your brother, and you may trade in the land.
And it was, as they were emptying their sacks, and there! each man's bundle of silver was in his sack. And they saw the bundles of their silver, they and their father, and they were afraid.
And Jacob their father said to them, Me you have bereaved! Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin you will take. Upon me all these have come.
And Reuben said to his father, saying, You may kill my two sons if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hand, and I will return him to you.
And he said, My son will not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he alone is left. If harm should befall him on the journey you go on, you will bring my grey hair down in sorrow to Sheol.

genesis_43.t: And the famine was heavy in the land.
And it was, when they had finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, Go back, buy us a little food.
And Judah said to him, saying, The man solemnly warned us, saying, You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.
If you are sending our brother with us, we will go down and buy you food.
And if you are not sending, we will not go down, for the man said to us, You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.
And Israel said, Why did you do harm to me, to tell the man that you still had a brother?

And they said, The man asked and asked about us and about our kindred, saying, Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother? And we told him according to the mouth of these words. Could we possibly have known that he would say, Bring your brother down?
And Judah said to Israel his father, Send the young man with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die — we too, and you too, and our little ones too.
I will stand surety for him; from my hand you will require him. If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, then I will have sinned against you all the days.
For if we had not delayed, by now we would have returned this twice.

And Israel their father said to them, If it must be so, then do this: take of the best products of the land in your vessels and take down to the man a gift — a little balm and a little honey, gum and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.
And take double silver in your hand, and the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks, take back in your hand; perhaps it was a mistake.
And take your brother, and arise, go back to the man.
And may God Almighty give you compassion before the man, and may he send away to you your other brother and Benjamin. And I — as I have been bereaved, I am bereaved.
And the men took this gift, and double silver they took in their hand, and Benjamin; and they arose and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
And Joseph saw Benjamin with them, and he said to the one over his house, Bring the men into the house, and slaughter a slaughter and prepare it, for the men will eat with me at noon.
And the man did as Joseph said, and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.

And the men were afraid because they had been brought into Joseph's house, and they said, It is over the matter of the silver returned in our sacks at the first that we are being brought in — to roll himself upon us and fall upon us and take us as slaves, and our donkeys.
And they approached the man who was over Joseph's house, and they spoke to him at the entrance of the house.
And they said, Pardon, my lord — we came down and came down at the first to buy food.
And it was, when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, and there! each man's silver was in the mouth of his sack — our silver in its full weight. And we have brought it back in our hand.
And other silver we have brought down in our hand to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.
And he said, Peace to you; do not fear. Your God and the God of your father gave you treasure in your sacks. Your silver came to me. And he brought Simeon out to them.
And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and he gave water and they washed their feet, and he gave fodder to their donkeys.
And they prepared the gift for Joseph's coming at noon, for they had heard that they would eat bread there.
And Joseph came into the house, and they brought him the gift that was in their hand, into the house, and they bowed down to him to the ground.
And he asked them of their welfare, and he said, Is your old father well, of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?
And they said, Your servant our father is well; he is still alive. And they bowed low and bowed down.
And he lifted his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother, and he said, Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me? And he said, God be gracious to you, my son.
And Joseph hurried, for his compassions grew hot toward his brother, and he sought to weep, and he came into the inner room and wept there.
And he washed his face and came out, and he restrained himself, and he said, Set out bread.

And they set out for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves; for the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to Egypt.
And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth; and the men looked at one another in astonishment.
And portions were carried to them from before him, and Benjamin's portion was greater than the portions of all of them, five hands. And they drank and became drunk with him.

genesis_44.t: And he commanded the one over his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they are able to carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
And my cup, the cup of silver, you will put in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and the silver of his grain. And he did according to the word of Joseph which he had spoken.
The morning grew light, and the men were sent off, they and their donkeys.

They had gone out of the city — they had not gone far — and Joseph said to the one over his house, Arise, pursue after the men, and you will overtake them, and you will say to them, Why have you repaid evil for good?
Is this not the one my lord drinks from, and he divines and divines by it? You have done evil in what you have done.
And he overtook them and spoke to them these words.
And they said to him, Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do a thing like this!
Look: silver which we found in the mouth of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. And how would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?
Whoever of your servants it is found with, let him die; and we also will be slaves to my lord.
And he said, Now also, according to your words, so let it be: the one it is found with will be my slave, and you will be innocent.
And they hurried and each man brought his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
And he searched: with the eldest he began, and with the youngest he finished. And the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
And they tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
And Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, and he was still there, and they fell before him to the ground.
And Joseph said to them, What is this deed you have done? Did you not know that a man such as I divines and divines?

And Judah said, What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? And how shall we justify ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants. Here we are, slaves to my lord — we, and also the one in whose hand the cup was found.
And he said, Far be it from me to do this. The man in whose hand the cup was found — he will be my slave; and you, go up in peace to your father.
And Judah drew near to him and said, Pardon, my lord — let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and let your anger not burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, saying, Do you have a father or a brother?
And we said to my lord, We have an old father, and a child of his old age, a young one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.
And you said to your servants, Bring him down to me, and let me set my eye upon him.
And we said to my lord, The young man is not able to leave his father; if he leaves his father, he will die.
And you said to your servants, If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you will not again see my face.
And it was, when we went up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
And our father said, Go back, buy us a little food.
And we said, We are not able to go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we are not able to see the man's face when our youngest brother is not with us.
And your servant my father said to us, You know that my wife bore me two.
And the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he has been torn to pieces, torn to pieces — and I have not seen him until now.
And if you take this one also from my presence, and harm befalls him, you will bring my grey hair down in calamity to Sheol.
And now, when I come to your servant my father and the young man is not with us — and his life is bound up with his life —
then it will be, when he sees that the young man is not there, he will die; and your servants will have brought the grey hair of your servant our father down in sorrow to Sheol.
For your servant stood surety for the young man with my father, saying, If I do not bring him to you, then I will have sinned against my father all the days.
And now, let your servant remain, please, in place of the young man as a slave to my lord, and let the young man go up with his brothers.
For how shall I go up to my father, and the young man is not with me? — lest I look on the evil that would find my father.

genesis_45.t: And Joseph was not able to restrain himself before all those standing over him, and he called out, Send every man out from me! And no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
And he gave his voice in weeping, and Egypt heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
And Joseph said to his brothers, I am Joseph. Is my father still alive? And his brothers were not able to answer him, for they were terrified before him.
And Joseph said to his brothers, Draw near to me, please. And they drew near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
And now, do not be grieved, and let it not burn in your eyes that you sold me here; for God sent me before you for the preserving of life.
For this is two years that the famine has been in the midst of the land, and there are yet five years in which there will be no ploughing and harvest.
And God sent me before you to place a remnant for you in the earth, and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.
And now, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and he made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler in all the land of Egypt.
Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not stand still.
And you will dwell in the land of Goshen and be near to me — you and your sons and your sons' sons, and your flocks and your herds and all that is yours.
And I will provide for you there, for there are yet five years of famine, lest you be impoverished, you and your household and all that is yours.
And there! your eyes are seeing, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth speaking to you.
And you will tell my father of all my honour in Egypt and of all that you have seen; and you will hurry and bring my father down here.
And he fell on the neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them; and after that his brothers spoke with him.
And the sound was heard in the house of Pharaoh, saying, Joseph's brothers have come. And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Say to your brothers, Do this: load your beasts and go, come to the land of Canaan,
and take your father and your households and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.
And you are commanded: Do this — take for yourselves carts from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and carry your father and come.
And let your eye not look with regret on your things, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.
And the sons of Israel did so, and Joseph gave them carts according to the mouth of Pharaoh, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
To all of them he gave, to each, changes of garments; and to Benjamin he gave three hundred of silver and five changes of garments.
And to his father he sent the like of this: ten donkeys carrying of the good of Egypt, and ten she-donkeys carrying grain and bread and food for his father for the journey.
And he sent his brothers off and they went, and he said to them, Do not quarrel on the way.
And they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
And they told him, saying, Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler in all the land of Egypt. And his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.
And they spoke to him all the words of Joseph which he had spoken to them; and he saw the carts which Joseph had sent to carry him, and the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
And Israel said, Enough! Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.

genesis_46.t: And Israel set out with all that was his, and he came to Beersheba, and he sacrificed sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
And God said to Israel in the visions of the night, and he said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here I am.
And he said, I am the God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid of going down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will bring you up, also bringing up; and Joseph will set his hand on your eyes.
And Jacob rose from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones and their wives, in the carts which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
And they took their livestock and their possessions which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt — Jacob and all his offspring with him,
his sons and his sons' sons with him, his daughters and his sons' daughters, and all his offspring he brought with him to Egypt.
And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt, Jacob and his sons: the firstborn of Jacob, Reuben.
And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch and Pallu and Hezron and Carmi.
And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jakin and Zohar, and Shaul the son of the Canaanite woman.
And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And the sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah and Perez and Zerah — and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
And the sons of Issachar: Tola and Puvah and Iob and Shimron.
And the sons of Zebulun: Sered and Elon and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, and Dinah his daughter. All the persons of his sons and his daughters: thirty-three.
And the sons of Gad: Ziphion and Haggi, Shuni and Ezbon, Eri and Arodi and Areli.
And the sons of Asher: Imnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob — sixteen persons.
The sons of Rachel the wife of Jacob: Joseph and Benjamin.
And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born those whom Asenath the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim.
And the sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Ashbel, Gera and Naaman, Ehi and Rosh, Muppim and Huppim and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob — all the persons, fourteen.
And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel and Guni and Jezer and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob — all the persons, seven.
All the persons coming with Jacob to Egypt, who came out of his thigh, apart from the wives of Jacob's sons — all the persons, sixty-six.
And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt: two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who came to Egypt: seventy.
And Judah he sent before him to Joseph, to give direction before him to Goshen. And they came to the land of Goshen.
And Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen; and he presented himself to him and fell on his neck and wept on his neck a long while.
And Israel said to Joseph, Let me die this time, after my seeing your face, that you are still alive.
And Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's house, I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and I will say to him, My brothers and my father's house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
And the men are shepherds of flocks, for they have been men of livestock; and their flocks and their herds and all that is theirs they have brought.
And it will be, when Pharaoh summons you and says, What is your occupation? —

then you will say, Your servants have been men of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers — so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd of flocks is an abomination to Egypt.

genesis_47.t: And Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and he said, My father and my brothers, and their flocks and their herds and all that is theirs, have come from the land of Canaan, and there they are in the land of Goshen.
And from among his brothers he took five men and presented them before Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to his brothers, What is your occupation? And they said to Pharaoh, Your servants are shepherds of flocks, both we and our fathers.

And they said to Pharaoh, To sojourn in the land we have come, for there is no pasture for the flocks that belong to your servants, for the famine is heavy in the land of Canaan. And now, let your servants please dwell in the land of Goshen.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, saying, Your father and your brothers have come to you.

The land of Egypt is before you; in the best of the land settle your father and your brothers. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. And if you know that there are men of ability among them, then set them as overseers of livestock over what is mine.
And Joseph brought Jacob his father and stood him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Jacob, How many are the days of the years of your life?

And Jacob said to Pharaoh, The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years. Few and bad have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the lives of my fathers in the days of their sojournings.
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from before Pharaoh.
And Joseph settled his father and his brothers, and he gave them a holding in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
And Joseph provided for his father and his brothers and all his father's house with bread, according to the mouth of the little ones.
And there was no bread in all the land, for the famine was very heavy, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.
And Joseph gathered up all the silver found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, for the grain that they were buying; and Joseph brought the silver into Pharaoh's house.
And the silver from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan came to an end, and all Egypt came to Joseph, saying, Give us bread! And why should we die before you? For the silver has run out.
And Joseph said, Give your livestock, and I will give you for your livestock, if the silver has run out.

And they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread for the horses and for the livestock of the flocks and for the livestock of the herds and for the donkeys; and he sustained them with bread for all their livestock in that year.

And that year came to an end, and they came to him in the second year and said to him, We will not hide from my lord that the silver is gone and the herds of cattle belong to my lord. There is nothing left before my lord except our bodies and our ground.

Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our ground? Buy us and our ground for bread, and we with our ground will be slaves to Pharaoh; and give seed, that we may live and not die, and that the ground may not be desolate.
And Joseph bought all the ground of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold each his field, because the famine was strong upon them; and the land became Pharaoh's.
And the people — he moved them into the cities, from one end of the territory of Egypt to its other end.
Only the ground of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had an allotment from Pharaoh, and they ate their allotment which Pharaoh gave them; therefore they did not sell their ground.
And Joseph said to the people, Look, I have bought you today, and your ground, for Pharaoh. Here is seed for you, and you will sow the ground.
And at the harvests you will give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four of the hands will be yours, for seed of the field and for your food and for those in your households and for your little ones to eat.
And they said, You have kept us alive. Let us find favour in the eyes of my lord, and we will be slaves to Pharaoh.
And Joseph established it as a statute to this day over the ground of Egypt: to Pharaoh, the fifth. Only the ground of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.
And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they took holdings in it, and they were fruitful and multiplied greatly.
And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years.

And the days of Israel drew near to die, and he called for his son Joseph and said to him, If I have found favour in your eyes, put your hand, please, under my thigh, and do with me loyalty and faithfulness: do not bury me, please, in Egypt.
And I will lie down with my fathers, and you will carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place. And he said, I will do according to your word.
And he said, Swear to me. And he swore to him. And Israel bowed down on the head of the bed.

genesis_48.t: And it was, after these things, that someone said to Joseph, Look, your father is ill. And he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
And someone told Jacob and said, Look, your son Joseph has come to you. And Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
And Jacob said to Joseph, God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and he blessed me,
and he said to me, Look, I am making you fruitful and will multiply you, and I will make you into a company of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you as a perpetual holding.
And now, your two sons born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt — they are mine. Ephraim and Manasseh, like Reuben and Simeon, will be mine.
And your offspring whom you father after them will be yours; by the name of their brothers they will be called in their inheritance.

And I — when I came from Paddan, Rachel died on me in the land of Canaan, on the way, with still some distance of land to come to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath, that is Bethlehem.
And Israel saw the sons of Joseph and said, Who are these?
And Joseph said to his father, They are my sons, whom God has given me in this place. And he said, Take them, please, to me, and I will bless them.
And the eyes of Israel were heavy from age; he was not able to see. And he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
And Israel said to Joseph, To see your face I had not reckoned, and look — God has shown me your offspring also.
And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed down with his face to the ground.
