And the man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city and called its name Luz — that is its name to this day.

And Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean and its daughters, and Taanach and its daughters, and the inhabitants of Dor and its daughters, and the inhabitants of Ibleam and its daughters, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its daughters; and the Canaanite was determined to dwell in this land.
And it was, when Israel became strong, that it put the Canaanite to forced labour; but dispossessing, it did not dispossess him.
And Ephraim did not dispossess the Canaanite dwelling in Gezer; and the Canaanite dwelt in his midst in Gezer.
Zebulun did not dispossess the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol; and the Canaanite dwelt in his midst, and they became forced labour.
Asher did not dispossess the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, or Ahlab or Achzib or Helbah or Aphik or Rehob.
And the Asherite dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite, the inhabitants of the land, for he did not dispossess him.

Naphtali did not dispossess the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-anath, and he dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite, the inhabitants of the land; and the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labour for them.
And the Amorite pressed the sons of Dan into the hill country, for he did not permit him to go down to the valley.
And the Amorite was determined to dwell in Mount Heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim; but the hand of the house of Joseph was heavy, and they became forced labour.
And the border of the Amorite was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

judges_2.t: And the messenger of YHWH went up from Gilgal to Bokim, and he said, "I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to your fathers, and I said, 'I will not break my covenant with you for ever.
"'And you — you shall not cut a covenant with the inhabitants of this land; their altars you shall pull down.' But you have not listened to my voice. What is this you have done?"
"And I also said, I will not drive them out from before you; and they shall become sides to you, and their gods shall become a snare to you."
And it was, when the messenger of YHWH spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice and wept.
And they called the name of that place Bokim, and they sacrificed there to YHWH.
And Joshua sent the people away, and the sons of Israel went, each man to his inheritance, to take possession of the land.
And the people served YHWH all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who prolonged days after Joshua, who had seen all the great work of YHWH that he did for Israel.
And Joshua son of Nun, the servant of YHWH, died, a son of a hundred and ten years.
And they buried him in the territory of his inheritance, in Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, to the north of Mount Gaash.
And also all that generation were gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know YHWH, and also not the work that he had done for Israel.
And the sons of Israel did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and they served the Baals.

And they forsook YHWH, the God of their fathers, who brought them out from the land of Egypt, and they went after other gods, from the gods of the peoples who were around them, and they bowed down to them, and they provoked YHWH to anger.
And they forsook YHWH and served the Baal and the Ashtaroth.

And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of plunderers, and they plundered them; and he sold them into the hand of their enemies round about, and they were no longer able to stand before their enemies.
In everything they went out to, the hand of YHWH was against them for harm, just as YHWH had spoken and just as YHWH had sworn to them; and they were distressed exceedingly.
And YHWH raised up judges, and they delivered them from the hand of those who plundered them.

And also to their judges they did not listen, for they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers had walked, to obey the commandments of YHWH; they did not do so.

And when YHWH raised up judges for them, YHWH was with the judge and delivered them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for YHWH was moved to compassion by their groaning because of those who oppressed them and crushed them.

And it was, when the judge died, they would turn back and act more corruptly than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They did not let drop any of their deeds or their stubborn way.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he said, "Because this nation has transgressed my covenant that I commanded their fathers, and has not listened to my voice,
"I also will no longer dispossess anyone from before them of the nations that Joshua left when he died."
so as to put Israel to the test by them, whether they will keep the way of YHWH, to walk in it as their fathers kept it, or not.
And YHWH left these nations, not dispossessing them quickly; and he did not give them into the hand of Joshua.

judges_3.t: And these are the nations that YHWH left, to put Israel to the test by them — all those who had not known all the wars of Canaan;
only so that the generations of the sons of Israel might know, to teach them war — only those who formerly had not known them.
the five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanite, and the Sidonian, and the Hivite dwelling in the mountain of the Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
And they were for putting Israel to the test by them, to know whether they would obey the commandments of YHWH that he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
And the sons of Israel dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite, the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.
And they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and their own daughters they gave to their sons, and they served their gods.
And the sons of Israel did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and they forgot YHWH their God, and they served the Baals and the Asheroth.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim; and the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
And the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH, and YHWH raised up a deliverer for the sons of Israel, and he delivered them — Othniel son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, the younger than he.
And the spirit of YHWH was upon him, and he judged Israel and went out to war; and YHWH gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
And the land had rest forty years; and Othniel son of Kenaz died.
And the sons of Israel again did the evil in the eyes of YHWH; and YHWH strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they did the evil in the eyes of YHWH.
And he gathered to himself the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the city of palms.
And the sons of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

And the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH, and YHWH raised up for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a man impeded in his right hand. And the sons of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
And Ehud made for himself a sword, and it had two mouths, a gomed in its length; and he girded it under his garments on his right thigh.
And he brought the tribute near to Eglon king of Moab; and Eglon was a very fat man.
And it was, when he had finished bringing near the tribute, that he sent away the people who bore the tribute.
But he himself turned back from the images that were by Gilgal, and he said, "A word of secrecy I have for you, O king." And he said, "Hush!" And all who stood by him went out from him.
And Ehud came to him, and he was sitting in the cool roof chamber that was his alone. And Ehud said, "A word of God I have for you." And he rose from upon the throne.
And Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the sword from upon his right thigh, and he thrust it into his belly.
And the hilt also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the dung went out.
And Ehud went out to the porch, and he shut the doors of the roof chamber behind him and locked them.
And he had gone out, and his servants came and looked, and there — the doors of the roof chamber were locked. And they said, "Surely he is covering his feet in the cool chamber."
And they writhed until they were ashamed; and there — he was not opening the doors of the roof chamber. And they took the key and opened them, and there — their lord had fallen to the ground, dead.
And Ehud escaped while they delayed; and he passed by the images and escaped to Seirah.
And it was, when he came, that he blew the ram's horn in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he was before them.

And he said to them, "Pursue after me, for YHWH has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand." And they went down after him, and they captured the fords of the Jordan toward Moab, and they did not allow anyone to pass over.
And they struck down Moab at that time, about ten thousand men, every stout one and every man of strength; and not a man escaped.
And Moab was subdued on that day under the hand of Israel; and the land had rest eighty years.
And after him was Shamgar son of Anath, and he struck down six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.

judges_4.t: And the sons of Israel again did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and Ehud was dead.
And YHWH sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and the commander of his army was Sisera, and he was dwelling in Harosheth-hagoyim.
And the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he oppressed the sons of Israel with force twenty years.
And Deborah, a woman, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth — she was judging Israel at that time.
And she was sitting under the palm of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went up to her for judgement.

And she sent and summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, "Has not YHWH the God of Israel commanded: Go, and you shall march to Mount Tabor, and you shall take with you ten thousand men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun?"
"And I will draw to you, to the wadi Kishon, Sisera commander of the army of Jabin, and his chariotry and his multitude; and I will give him into your hand."
And Barak said to her, "If you will go with me, then I will go; and if you will not go with me, I will not go."

And she said, "Going I will go with you; nevertheless it will not be your honour on the way that you are going, for into the hand of a woman YHWH will sell Sisera." And Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
And Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up at his feet; and Deborah went up with him.
And Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, from the sons of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses, and he had pitched his tent as far as the great tree in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh.
And they told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
And Sisera summoned all his chariotry, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the wadi Kishon.

And Deborah said to Barak, "Arise, for this is the day on which YHWH has given Sisera into your hand. Has not YHWH gone out before you?" And Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
And YHWH routed Sisera and all the chariotry and all the camp with the mouth of the sword before Barak; and Sisera got down from upon the chariot and fled on his feet.
And Barak pursued after the chariotry and after the camp as far as Harosheth-hagoyim; and all the camp of Sisera fell by the mouth of the sword — not even one was left.
And Sisera fled on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and she said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not be afraid." And he turned aside to her, into the tent, and she covered him with the rug.
And he said to her, "Give me a little water to drink, please, for I am thirsty." And she opened the skin of milk and gave him a drink, and she covered him.
And he said to her, "Stand at the opening of the tent; and it shall be, if anyone comes and asks you and says, 'Is there a man here?' then you shall say, 'No one.'"

And Jael the wife of Heber took a tent peg and put the hammer in her hand, and she came to him in secret and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground; and he was fast asleep and weary, and he died.

And there was Barak, pursuing Sisera; and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking." And he came to her, and there was Sisera, fallen dead, and the peg in his temple.
And God subdued on that day Jabin king of Canaan before the sons of Israel.
And the hand of the sons of Israel went, going and hard, against Jabin king of Canaan, until they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

judges_5.t: And Deborah sang, and Barak son of Abinoam, on that day, saying:
When the leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people offered themselves freely — bless YHWH!
Hear, O kings! Give ear, O rulers! I — to YHWH, I — I will sing, I will make music to YHWH, the God of Israel.
YHWH, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the field of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens also dripped, the clouds also dripped water.
The mountains flowed from before YHWH — this Sinai — from before YHWH, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, caravans ceased, and those who walked the paths walked twisting roads.
The villagers ceased in Israel, they ceased, until I arose, Deborah, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
It chose new gods; then — war at the gates. Was a shield seen, or a spear, among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart is toward the commanders of Israel, those offering themselves freely among the people — bless YHWH!
Riders of tawny she-asses, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk on the road — tell it out!

From the sound of those who parcel out the flocks between the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of YHWH, the righteous acts of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of YHWH went down to the gates.
Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, speak a song! Arise, Barak, and take captive your captives, son of Abinoam!
Then a survivor went down to the nobles; the people of YHWH went down for me among the mighty.
From Ephraim, their root in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples; from Machir commanders went down, and from Zebulun those who wield the staff of the muster-officer.
And my princes in Issachar were with Deborah; and Issachar, so Barak — into the valley he was sent at his feet. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great resolves of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistling for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Gilead dwelt beyond the Jordan; and Dan — why did he sojourn by the ships? Asher remained by the shore of the seas, and by his landings he dwelt.
Zebulun is a people that despised its life to death, and Naphtali, on the heights of the field.
Kings came, they fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. A profit of silver they did not take.
From heaven they fought; the stars from their highways fought with Sisera.
The wadi Kishon swept them away, an ancient wadi, the wadi Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!
Then the hooves of the horse hammered from the galloping, the galloping of his mighty ones.
"Curse Meroz," says the messenger of YHWH, "cursing, curse her inhabitants, for they did not come to the help of YHWH, to the help of YHWH among the mighty."
Blessed above women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; above women in the tent be she blessed.
Water he asked; milk she gave. In a bowl of nobles she brought near curds.
Her hand she stretched to the peg, and her right hand to the workmen's hammer; and she hammered Sisera, she shattered his head, and she smashed and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay; between her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell — destroyed.
Through the window she looked down and wailed, the mother of Sisera, through the lattice: "Why is his chariot delayed in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots tarry?"
The wise ones of her noble ladies answer her — indeed, she returns her own sayings to herself:

"Are they not finding, dividing spoil? — a womb, two wombs for the head of each man; spoil of dyed cloths for Sisera, spoil of dyed cloths, embroidered, a dyed cloth, two embroidered cloths, for the necks of the spoil."
So may all your enemies perish, YHWH; and may those who love him be like the going out of the sun in its strength. And the land had rest forty years.

judges_6.t: And the sons of Israel did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gave them into the hand of Midian seven years.
And the hand of Midian prevailed over Israel. Because of Midian the sons of Israel made for themselves the dens that are in the mountains, and the caves and the strongholds.
And it was, if Israel sowed, that Midian would come up, and Amalek and the people of the east, and they would come up against him.
And they would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as your coming to Gaza; and they would leave no sustenance in Israel, and no sheep or ox or donkey.
For they and their livestock would come up, and their tents, and they would come in like locusts for multitude — they and their camels without number — and they came into the land to destroy it.
And Israel became very low because of Midian; and the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH.
And it was, when the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH on account of Midian,
that YHWH sent a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel; and he said to them, "Thus says YHWH the God of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out from a house of slaves.
"And I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and I drove them out from before you and gave you their land.
"And I said to you, 'I am YHWH your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorite, in whose land you are dwelling.' But you have not listened to my voice."
And the messenger of YHWH came and sat under the oak that was in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite; and Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from Midian.
And the messenger of YHWH appeared to him and said to him, "YHWH is with you, mighty man of valour."

And Gideon said to him, "Pardon me, my lord — and is YHWH with us? Then why has all this found us? And where are all his wonders that our fathers recounted to us, saying, 'Did not YHWH bring us up from Egypt?' But now YHWH has abandoned us and given us into the palm of Midian."
And YHWH turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you shall deliver Israel from the palm of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
And he said to him, "Pardon me, my Lord — with what shall I deliver Israel? Behold, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
And YHWH said to him, "Because I will be with you, and you shall strike down Midian as one man."
And he said to him, "If now I have found favour in your eyes, then do for me a sign that it is you who are speaking with me.
"Do not depart from here, please, until I come to you and bring out my gift and set it before you." And he said, "I will remain until your returning."

And Gideon went and prepared a kid of the goats, and an ephah of flour as unleavened bread. The meat he put in a basket, and the broth he put in a pot, and he brought them out to him, under the oak, and presented them.
And the messenger of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread and set them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

And the messenger of YHWH stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread; and fire went up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. And the messenger of YHWH went from his eyes.
And Gideon saw that it was the messenger of YHWH; and Gideon said, "Alas, Lord YHWH! For I have seen the messenger of YHWH face to face."
And YHWH said to him, "Peace to you. Do not fear; you shall not die."
And Gideon built there an altar to YHWH and called it 'YHWH is peace'. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

And it was on that night that YHWH said to him, "Take the bull of the herd that belongs to your father, and the second bull of seven years; and tear down the altar of the Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it.

"And you shall build an altar to YHWH your God on the top of this stronghold, in the ordered arrangement; and you shall take the second bull and offer up a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you cut down."

And Gideon took ten men from his servants and did as YHWH had spoken to him; and it was, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city too much to do it by day, that he did it by night.

And the men of the city rose early in the morning, and there — the altar of the Baal was torn down, and the Asherah that was beside it was cut down, and the second bull had been offered up on the altar that had been built.
And they said each to his neighbour, "Who has done this thing?" And they investigated and searched and said, "Gideon son of Joash has done this thing."
And the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, and let him die, for he has torn down the altar of the Baal and cut down the Asherah that was beside it."

And Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for the Baal? Or will you deliver him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone has torn down his altar."
And on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, "Let the Baal contend against him, because he has torn down his altar."
And all Midian and Amalek and the people of the east gathered together, and they crossed over and encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
And the spirit of YHWH clothed Gideon, and he blew the ram's horn, and Abiezer was called out after him.
And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and it too was called out after him. And he sent messengers in Asher and in Zebulun and in Naphtali, and they went up to meet them.
And Gideon said to God, "If you are about to deliver Israel by my hand, as you have spoken —

"behold, I am setting the fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If dew is on the fleece alone, and on all the ground there is dryness, then I shall know that you will deliver Israel by my hand, as you have spoken."
And it was so. And he rose early the next day and squeezed the fleece, and he wrung dew from the fleece — a bowlful of water.

And Gideon said to God, "Let not your anger burn against me, and let me speak just this once. Let me test, please, just this once with the fleece: let there be dryness on the fleece alone, and on all the ground let there be dew."
And God did so on that night: there was dryness on the fleece alone, and on all the ground there was dew.

judges_7.t: And Jerubbaal — he is Gideon — rose early, and all the people who were with him, and they encamped at En-harod; and the camp of Midian was to the north of him, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
And YHWH said to Gideon, "The people who are with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel glorify itself over me, saying, 'My own hand has delivered me.'

"And now proclaim, please, in the ears of the people: Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead." And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

And YHWH said to Gideon, "Still the people are too many. Bring them down to the water, and I will refine them for you there. And it shall be, of whom I say to you, 'This one shall go with you' — he shall go with you; and every one of whom I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you' — he shall not go."

And he brought the people down to the water. And YHWH said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps with his tongue from the water, as the dog laps, set him apart; and everyone who bows down on his knees to drink."
And the number of those who lapped, with their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; and all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water.
And YHWH said to Gideon, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will deliver you, and I will give Midian into your hand; and all the people, let them go, each to his own place."

And they took the provisions of the people in their hand, and their ram's horns; and every man of Israel he sent away, each to his tents, and on the three hundred men he kept hold. And the camp of Midian was below him, in the valley.
And it was on that night that YHWH said to him, "Arise, go down into the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
"And if you are afraid to go down, go down, you and Purah your young man, to the camp,

"and you shall hear what they say; and afterwards your hands shall be strengthened, and you shall go down into the camp." And he went down, he and Purah his young man, to the edge of those arrayed for battle who were in the camp.

And Midian and Amalek and all the people of the east were lying in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number, like the sand that is on the shore of the sea for multitude.

And Gideon came, and there — a man was recounting a dream to his neighbour. And he said, "Behold, I have dreamed a dream, and behold, a round loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midian, and it came to the tent and struck it and it fell, and it turned it upside down, and the tent fell."
And his neighbour answered and said, "This is nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."

And it was, when Gideon heard the recounting of the dream and its interpretation, that he bowed down. And he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for YHWH has given the camp of Midian into your hand."
And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put ram's horns into the hand of all of them, and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.
And he said to them, "Look at me, and so shall you do. And behold, when I come to the edge of the camp, then as I do, so shall you do.
"And I will blow the ram's horn, I and all who are with me; and you also shall blow the ram's horns all around the whole camp, and you shall say, 'For YHWH and for Gideon!'"

And Gideon came, and the hundred men who were with him, to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, stationing, they had just stationed the watchmen; and they blew the ram's horns and smashed the jars that were in their hand.

And the three companies blew the ram's horns and broke the jars; and they held the torches in their left hand and the ram's horns in their right hand to blow; and they called out, "A sword for YHWH and for Gideon!"
And they stood, each in his place, all around the camp; and all the camp ran, and they shouted and fled.

And the three hundred blew the ram's horns, and YHWH set each man's sword against his neighbour, and against all the camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
And the man of Israel was called out from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.

And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian, and capture the waters before them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan." And every man of Ephraim was called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

And they captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at the winepress of Zeeb. And they pursued Midian, and the head of Oreb and Zeeb they brought to Gideon from across the Jordan.

judges_8.t: And the man of Ephraim said to him, "What is this thing you have done to us, not summoning us when you went to fight against Midian?" And they quarrelled with him with force.
And he said to them, "What have I now done compared with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
"Into your hand God has given the commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. And what have I been able to do compared with you?" Then their spirit relaxed from against him when he spoke this word.
And Gideon came to the Jordan, crossing over, he and the three hundred men who were with him — exhausted and pursuing.
And he said to the men of Succoth, "Give, please, round loaves of bread to the people who are at my feet, for they are exhausted; and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
And the officials of Succoth said, "Is the palm of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?"
And Gideon said, "Therefore, when YHWH gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with the briers."
And he went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
And he said also to the men of Penuel, "When I return in peace, I will tear down this tower."

And Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their camps with them, about fifteen thousand, all who remained of all the camp of the people of the east; and those who had fallen were a hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
And Gideon went up by the way of those who dwell in tents, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he struck the camp; and the camp was secure.
And Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued after them, and he captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna; and all the camp he routed.
And Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle, from the ascent of Heres.
And he captured a young man from the men of Succoth and enquired of him; and he wrote down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

And he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Is the palm of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your weary men?'"
And he took the elders of the city, and the thorns of the wilderness and the briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.
And the tower of Penuel he tore down, and he killed the men of the city.
And he said to Zebah and to Zalmunna, "Where are the men whom you killed at Tabor?" And they said, "As you, so they — each one like the form of the sons of a king."
And he said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As YHWH lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."
And he said to Jether his firstborn, "Arise, kill them." But the young man did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a young man.

And Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Rise yourself and fall upon us, for as the man is, so is his strength." And Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescents that were on the necks of their camels.
And the man of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us — you, and also your son, and also your son's son — for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian."
And Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. YHWH will rule over you."
And Gideon said to them, "Let me ask a request of you: give me, each of you, the earring of his plunder." For they had earrings of gold, because they were Ishmaelites.
And they said, "Giving, we will give." And they spread out the garment, and each threw there the earring of his plunder.

And the weight of the gold earrings that he asked for was a thousand seven hundred of gold, apart from the crescents and the pendants and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midian, and apart from the necklaces that were on the necks of their camels.
And Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, in Ophrah; and all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.
And Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not lift up their head again; and the land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.
And Jerubbaal son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
And to Gideon there were seventy sons who came out of his thigh, for he had many wives.
And his concubine who was in Shechem, she too bore him a son; and he set his name Abimelech.
And Gideon son of Joash died in a good old age, and he was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
And it was, when Gideon had died, that the sons of Israel turned back and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and they made Baal-berith their god.
And the sons of Israel did not remember YHWH their God, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies round about.
And they did not do loyalty with the house of Jerubbaal — Gideon — according to all the good that he had done with Israel.

judges_9.t: And Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers; and he spoke to them and to all the clan of his mother's father's house, saying,

"Speak, please, in the ears of all the lords of Shechem: 'What is good for you — that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you?' And remember that I am your bone and your flesh."
And his mother's brothers spoke concerning him in the ears of all the lords of Shechem all these words; and their heart turned after Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
And they gave him seventy of silver from the house of Baal-berith; and Abimelech hired with them empty and reckless men, and they went after him.

And he came to his father's house, to Ophrah, and he killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone. And Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, for he had hidden himself.
And all the lords of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered, and they went and made Abimelech king, by the great tree of the pillar that is in Shechem.
And they told Jotham, and he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim and lifted up his voice and called out; and he said to them, "Listen to me, lords of Shechem, and may God listen to you."
"Going, the trees went to anoint over them a king; and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
"And the olive tree said to them, 'Shall I cease my fatness, by which gods and men are honoured, and go to sway over the trees?'
"And the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, you, reign over us.'
"And the fig tree said to them, 'Shall I cease my sweetness and my good produce, and go to sway over the trees?'
"And the trees said to the vine, 'Come, you, reign over us.'
"And the vine said to them, 'Shall I cease my new wine, which gladdens gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
"And all the trees said to the bramble, 'Come, you, reign over us.'

"And the bramble said to the trees, 'If in faithfulness you are anointing me as king over you, come, take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire go out from the bramble and consume the cedars of Lebanon.'

"And now, if in faithfulness and in integrity you have acted in making Abimelech king, and if you have done good with Jerubbaal and with his house, and if you have done to him according to the dealing of his hands —
"— for my father fought for you and threw his life away in front, and he delivered you from the hand of Midian;

"and you have risen up against my father's house this day and killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and made Abimelech, the son of his female slave, king over the lords of Shechem, because he is your brother —
"if in faithfulness and in integrity you have acted with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.
"And if not, let fire go out from Abimelech and consume the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo; and let fire go out from the lords of Shechem and from Beth-millo, and consume Abimelech."
And Jotham fled and ran away and went to Beer, and he dwelt there because of Abimelech his brother.
And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,

so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
And the lords of Shechem set ambushers against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road; and it was told to Abimelech.
And Gaal son of Ebed came, and his brothers, and they passed through Shechem; and the lords of Shechem trusted in him.
And they went out into the field and gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trod them, and they held festivities; and they went into the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

And Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and Zebul his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! And why should we serve him?"
"And who would give this people into my hand, that I might remove Abimelech!" And he said of Abimelech, "Increase your army and come out!"
And Zebul the official of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, and his anger burned.
And he sent messengers to Abimelech in deceit, saying, "Behold, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers are coming to Shechem, and behold, they are closing the city against you.
"And now, arise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in wait in the field.

"And it shall be in the morning, when the sun rises, you shall rise early and make a raid on the city; and behold, he and the people who are with him will come out against you, and you shall do to him as your hand finds."
And Abimelech arose, and all the people who were with him, by night; and they lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
And Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city; and Abimelech rose, and the people who were with him, from the ambush.
And Gaal saw the people and said to Zebul, "Behold, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains." And Zebul said to him, "It is the shadow of the mountains that you are seeing, like men."
And Gaal spoke again and said, "Behold, people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the great tree of the soothsayers."
And Zebul said to him, "Where now is your mouth, you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is this not the people you rejected? Go out now and fight against him."
And Gaal went out before the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him; and many fell fatally wounded as far as the entrance of the gate.
And Abimelech dwelt at Arumah; and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers from dwelling in Shechem.
And it was on the next day that the people went out into the field; and they told Abimelech.

And he took the people and divided them into three companies and lay in wait in the field; and he looked, and there — the people were going out from the city. And he rose up against them and struck them down.
And Abimelech and the companies that were with him made a raid and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city; and the two companies made a raid on all who were in the field and struck them down.
And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and he captured the city and killed the people who were in it; and he pulled down the city and sowed it with salt.
And all the lords of the tower of Shechem heard, and they went into the stronghold of the house of El-berith.
And it was told to Abimelech that all the lords of the tower of Shechem had gathered together.

And Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took the axes in his hand and cut off a branch of the trees and lifted it and put it on his shoulder. And he said to the people who were with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry, do as I have done."

And all the people also cut off, each his own branch, and they went after Abimelech and put them on the stronghold, and they set the stronghold on fire over them; and all the people of the tower of Shechem also died, about a thousand men and women.
And Abimelech went to Thebez and encamped against Thebez and captured it.

And there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and the women and all the lords of the city fled there; and they shut the door behind them and went up onto the roof of the tower.
And Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it, and he drew near to the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
And one woman threw an upper millstone on Abimelech's head, and it crushed his skull.

And he called quickly to the young man who carried his armour and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" And his young man ran him through, and he died.
And the man of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, and they went, each to his own place.
And God repaid the evil of Abimelech that he had done to his father, in killing his seventy brothers;
and all the evil of the men of Shechem God repaid on their head; and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

judges_10.t: And after Abimelech there arose to deliver Israel Tola son of Puah son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he was dwelling in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
And he judged Israel twenty-three years; and he died and was buried in Shamir.
And after him there arose Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
And he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns; they call them Havvoth-jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

And the sons of Israel again did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and they served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram and the gods of Sidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the sons of Ammon and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook YHWH and did not serve him.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the sons of Ammon.
And they shattered and crushed the sons of Israel in that year — eighteen years — all the sons of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorite, which is in Gilead.
And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah and against Benjamin and against the house of Ephraim; and Israel was distressed exceedingly.
And the sons of Israel cried out to YHWH, saying, "We have sinned against you, and because we have forsaken our God and served the Baals."
And YHWH said to the sons of Israel, "Was it not from Egypt, and from the Amorite, and from the sons of Ammon, and from the Philistines,
"and the Sidonians and Amalek and Maon oppressed you, and you cried out to me, and I delivered you from their hand?
"But you have forsaken me and served other gods. Therefore I will not deliver you again.
"Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your distress."
And the sons of Israel said to YHWH, "We have sinned. Do to us according to all that is good in your eyes; only deliver us, please, this day."
And they removed the foreign gods from their midst and served YHWH; and his self was shortened at the trouble of Israel.
And the sons of Ammon were called out and encamped in Gilead; and the sons of Israel gathered and encamped at Mizpah.
And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said each to his neighbour, "Who is the man who will begin to fight against the sons of Ammon? He shall become chief over all the inhabitants of Gilead."

judges_11.t: And Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of a woman, a prostitute; and Gilead fathered Jephthah.

And the wife of Gilead bore him sons; and the sons of the wife grew up and drove Jephthah out, and they said to him, "You shall not inherit in our father's house, for you are the son of another woman."
And Jephthah fled from before his brothers and dwelt in the land of Tob; and empty men gathered themselves to Jephthah, and they went out with him.
And it was, after some days, that the sons of Ammon fought with Israel.
And it was, when the sons of Ammon fought with Israel, that the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah from the land of Tob.
And they said to Jephthah, "Come, and be for us a commander, and let us fight against the sons of Ammon."
And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Was it not you who hated me and drove me out from my father's house? And why have you come to me now, when you are in distress?"

And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That is why we have now returned to you: you shall come with us and fight against the sons of Ammon, and you shall become for us chief over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you are bringing me back to fight against the sons of Ammon and YHWH gives them before me — I will be your chief."
And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "YHWH will be the one who hears between us, if we do not do according to your word."
And Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them as chief and as commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before YHWH at Mizpah.
And Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, "What is between me and you, that you have come to me to fight in my land?"

And the king of the sons of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthah, "Because Israel took my land when it came up from Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and as far as the Jordan. And now restore them in peace."
And Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon,
and he said to him, "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the sons of Ammon.
"For when they came up from Egypt, Israel went in the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.

"And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Let me pass, please, through your land.' But the king of Edom did not listen. And it sent also to the king of Moab, and he was not willing; and Israel remained at Kadesh.

"And it went in the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and it came from the rising of the sun to the land of Moab, and they encamped beyond the Arnon; and they did not come into the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.
"And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him, 'Let us pass, please, through your land to my place.'
"But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; and Sihon gathered all his people and encamped at Jahaz and fought with Israel.
"And YHWH the God of Israel gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them; and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorite, the inhabitant of that land.
"And they took possession of all the territory of the Amorite, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok, and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
"And now YHWH the God of Israel has dispossessed the Amorite from before his people Israel — and you, would you take possession of it?
"Is it not so: what Chemosh your god gives you to possess, that you will possess; and all that YHWH our God has dispossessed from before us, that we will possess?
"And now, are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Quarrelling did he quarrel with Israel, or warring did he wage war against them?

"While Israel dwelt in Heshbon and its daughters, and in Aroer and its daughters, and in all the cities that are along the sides of the Arnon, three hundred years — why did you not recover them in that time?
"And I have not sinned against you, but you are doing evil to me by waging war against me. May YHWH the Judge judge this day between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon."
But the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen to the words of Jephthah that he sent to him.
And the spirit of YHWH was upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh; and he passed through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed on to the sons of Ammon.
And Jephthah vowed a vow to YHWH and said, "If giving you will give the sons of Ammon into my hand,
"then whatever comes out — that comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Ammon — shall be YHWH's, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering."
And Jephthah passed on to the sons of Ammon to fight against them, and YHWH gave them into his hand.
And he struck them from Aroer as far as your coming to Minnith — twenty cities — and as far as Abel-keramim, a very great defeat; and the sons of Ammon were subdued before the sons of Israel.
And Jephthah came to Mizpah, to his house — and there, his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and with dances! And she was an only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.

And it was, when he saw her, that he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, my daughter! Bringing low you have brought me low, and you are among those who trouble me. And I — I have opened my mouth to YHWH, and I cannot turn back."

And she said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to YHWH. Do to me according to what has come out of your mouth, after YHWH has done for you vengeance on your enemies, on the sons of Ammon."
And she said to her father, "Let this thing be done for me: let me alone for two months, and let me go and go down on the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions."
And he said, "Go." And he sent her away for two months; and she went, she and her companions, and wept over her virginity on the mountains.
And it was at the end of two months that she returned to her father, and he did to her his vow that he had vowed; and she had not known a man. And it became a custom in Israel,
that from days to days the daughters of Israel go to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in the year.

judges_12.t: And the man of Ephraim was called out and passed over to Zaphon; and they said to Jephthah, "Why did you pass over to fight against the sons of Ammon, and did not summon us to go with you? Your house we will burn over you with fire!"
And Jephthah said to them, "I was a man of great strife, I and my people, with the sons of Ammon; and I summoned you, and you did not deliver me from their hand.

"And I saw that you were no deliverer, and I put my life in my palm and passed over against the sons of Ammon; and YHWH gave them into my hand. So why have you come up against me this day to fight against me?"

And Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought with Ephraim; and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because they had said, "You are fugitives of Ephraim, Gilead, in the midst of Ephraim, in the midst of Manasseh."

And Gilead captured the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim; and it was, when the fugitives of Ephraim said, "Let me pass over," the men of Gilead said to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he said, "No."

then they would say to him, "Say, please, shibboleth," and he would say "sibboleth," and he could not manage to speak it rightly; and they would seize him and slaughter him at the fords of the Jordan. And there fell at that time of Ephraim forty-two thousand.
And Jephthah judged Israel six years; and Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in the cities of Gilead.
And after him Ibzan from Bethlehem judged Israel.
And he had thirty sons; and thirty daughters he sent outside, and thirty daughters he brought in for his sons from outside. And he judged Israel seven years.
And Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.
And Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
And after him Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
And he had forty sons and thirty sons of sons who rode on seventy donkeys; and he judged Israel eight years.
And Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekite.

judges_13.t: And the sons of Israel again did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gave them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
And there was one man from Zorah, from the clan of the Danite, and his name was Manoah; and his wife was barren and had not borne children.
And the messenger of YHWH appeared to the woman and said to her, "Behold now, you are barren and have not borne children; but you shall conceive and bear a son.
"And now take care, please, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

"For behold, you are pregnant and shall bear a son; and a razor shall not go up on his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb. And he shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."

And the woman came and said to her husband, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the messenger of God, very fearsome. And I did not ask him where he was from, and his name he did not tell me.

"And he said to me, 'Behold, you are pregnant and shall bear a son. And now do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any uncleanness, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.'"
And Manoah prayed to YHWH and said, "Pardon me, my Lord — let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, and let him teach us what we are to do for the boy who is to be born."
And God listened to the voice of Manoah; and the messenger of God came again to the woman, and she was sitting in the field, and Manoah her husband was not with her.
And the woman hurried and ran and told her husband, and she said to him, "Behold, the man has appeared to me, the one who came to me the other day."
And Manoah arose and went after his wife, and he came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I am."
And Manoah said, "Now, when your words come — what shall be the ruling for the boy, and his work?"
And the messenger of YHWH said to Manoah, "From all that I said to the woman she shall take care.
"From all that comes out of the vine of the wine she shall not eat, and wine and strong drink she shall not drink, and any uncleanness she shall not eat. All that I commanded her she shall keep."
And Manoah said to the messenger of YHWH, "Let us detain you, please, and prepare before you a kid of the goats."

And the messenger of YHWH said to Manoah, "If you detain me, I will not eat of your food; and if you make a burnt offering, offer it up to YHWH." For Manoah did not know that he was the messenger of YHWH.
And Manoah said to the messenger of YHWH, "What is your name, so that when your word comes we may honour you?"
And the messenger of YHWH said to him, "Why is this that you ask for my name? And it is wonderful."
And Manoah took the kid of the goats and the grain offering and offered it up on the rock to YHWH; and one doing an extraordinary thing — and Manoah and his wife were looking on.

And it was, when the flame went up from upon the altar toward the heavens, that the messenger of YHWH went up in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife were looking on, and they fell on their faces to the ground.
And the messenger of YHWH did not appear again to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the messenger of YHWH.
And Manoah said to his wife, "Dying we shall die, for we have seen God."

And his wife said to him, "If YHWH had desired to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hand, and he would not have shown us all these things, and at this time he would not have let us hear such a thing as this."
And the woman bore a son and called his name Samson; and the boy grew, and YHWH blessed him.
And the spirit of YHWH began to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

judges_14.t: And Samson went down to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines.
And he went up and told his father and his mother, and he said, "A woman I have seen in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. And now, get her for me as a wife."

And his father and his mother said to him, "Is there not among the daughters of your brothers, and among all my people, a woman, that you are going to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" And Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes."
And his father and his mother did not know that it was from YHWH, for he was seeking an occasion from the Philistines; and at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
And Samson went down, and his father and his mother, to Timnah; and they came as far as the vineyards of Timnah, and there — a young lion roaring to meet him!
And the spirit of YHWH rushed upon him, and he tore it apart as one tears apart a kid, and there was nothing in his hand; and he did not tell his father and his mother what he had done.
And he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
And he returned after some days to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion; and there — a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey!

And he scraped it out into his palms and went, going and eating; and he went to his father and to his mother and gave to them, and they ate. And he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey out of the body of the lion.
And his father went down to the woman; and Samson made a feast there, for so the young men used to do.
And it was, when they saw him, that they took thirty companions, and they were with him.

And Samson said to them, "Let me ask you a riddle, please. If telling you tell it to me within the seven days of the feast and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.
"But if you are not able to tell me, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." And they said to him, "Ask your riddle, and let us hear it."
And he said to them: "Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet." And they were not able to tell the riddle for three days.

And it was on the seventh day that they said to Samson's wife, "Entice your husband, that he may tell us the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire. Was it to impoverish us that you invited us? Was it not?"

And Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me and do not love me. You have asked a riddle to the sons of my people, and to me you have not told it." And he said to her, "Behold, to my father and my mother I have not told it — and shall I tell you?"
And she wept over him the seven days that their feast lasted; and it was on the seventh day that he told her, because she pressed him. And she told the riddle to the sons of her people.

And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before the sun went down: "What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them: "If you had not ploughed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle."

And the spirit of YHWH rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men of them and took their spoil, and gave the changes of clothes to those who told the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father's house.
And Samson's wife became his companion's, the one who had been a special friend to him.

judges_15.t: And it was after some days, in the days of the wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a kid of the goats. And he said, "Let me go in to my wife, into the chamber." But her father did not permit him to go in.
And her father said, "Saying I said that hating you hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Let her be yours, please, in her place."
And Samson said to them, "This time I shall be free of blame from the Philistines when I do them harm."
And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and he took torches and turned tail to tail, and he put one torch between the two tails, in the middle.
And he kindled fire on the torches and sent them into the standing grain of the Philistines, and he burned up from the stacked sheaves to the standing grain and to the vineyard of olive trees.

And the Philistines said, "Who has done this?" And they said, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." And the Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.
And Samson said to them, "If you act like this — then I will surely avenge myself on you, and afterwards I will cease."
And he struck them, leg upon thigh, a great defeat; and he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
And the Philistines went up and encamped in Judah, and they spread out at Lehi.
And the men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" And they said, "To bind Samson we have come up, to do to him as he did to us."

And three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines are ruling over us? What is this you have done to us?" And he said to them, "As they did to me, so I have done to them."
And they said to him, "To bind you we have come down, to give you into the hand of the Philistines." And Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you yourselves will not fall upon me."
And they said to him, "No — for binding we will bind you and give you into their hand, but killing we will not kill you." And they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.

He was coming to Lehi, and the Philistines shouted to meet him; and the spirit of YHWH rushed upon him, and the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that has been burned with fire, and his bonds dropped off from upon his hands.
And he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and he put out his hand and took it, and he struck down with it a thousand men.
And Samson said: "With the jawbone of the donkey, a heap, two heaps — with the jawbone of the donkey I struck down a thousand men."
And it was, when he finished speaking, that he threw the jawbone from his hand; and he called that place Ramath-lehi.

And he was very thirsty, and he called out to YHWH and said, "You yourself have given by the hand of your servant this great victory. And now, shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"
And God split open the hollow that is at Lehi, and water came out of it, and he drank; and his spirit returned and he revived. Therefore he called its name En-hakkore, which is at Lehi, to this day.
And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.

judges_16.t: And Samson went to Gaza, and he saw there a woman, a prostitute, and he went in to her.

To the Gazites, saying, "Samson has come here." And they surrounded and lay in wait for him all the night at the gate of the city; and they kept silent all the night, saying, "Until the light of morning — and we will kill him."

And Samson lay down until the middle of the night, and he rose in the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city and the two doorposts, and pulled them up with the bar, and put them on his shoulders and carried them up to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron.
And it was after this that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, and her name was Delilah.

And the lords of the Philistines went up to her and said to her, "Entice him and see in what his great strength lies, and by what we may prevail over him, so that we may bind him to humble him; and we ourselves will give you, each of us, eleven hundred of silver."
And Delilah said to Samson, "Tell me, please, in what your great strength lies, and by what you may be bound to humble you."
And Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh cords that have not been dried, then I shall become weak and be like one of humankind."
And the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh cords that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

And the ambusher was sitting for her in the chamber. And she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And he tore apart the cords as a thread of tow is torn apart when it smells fire; and his strength was not known.
And Delilah said to Samson, "Behold, you have deceived me and spoken lies to me. Now tell me, please, by what you may be bound."
And he said to her, "If binding they bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I shall become weak and be like one of humankind."

And Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" — and the ambusher was sitting in the chamber. And he tore them apart from upon his arms like a thread.
And Delilah said to Samson, "Until now you have deceived me and spoken lies to me. Tell me by what you may be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven plaits of my head with the web."
And she thrust with the pin, and she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom and the web.
And she said to him, "How can you say 'I love you' when your heart is not with me? These three times you have deceived me, and you have not told me in what your great strength lies."
And it was, because she pressed him with her words all the days and urged him, that his self was shortened to death.

And he told her all his heart and said to her, "A razor has not come up on my head, for I have been a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I were shaved, then my strength would depart from me, and I should become weak and be like all of humankind."

And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and summoned the lords of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this time, for he has told me all his heart." And the lords of the Philistines came up to her and brought up the silver in their hand.
And she made him sleep on her knees, and she summoned the man and shaved off the seven plaits of his head; and she began to humble him, and his strength departed from upon him.

And she said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as time after time and shake myself free." And he did not know that YHWH had departed from him.
And the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes, and they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters; and he was grinding in the prison house.
And the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
And the lords of the Philistines gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and for rejoicing; and they said, "Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."
And the people saw him and praised their god, for they said, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy, and the one who laid waste our land, and the one who multiplied our slain."

And it was, when their heart was merry, that they said, "Summon Samson, and let him make sport for us." And they summoned Samson from the prison house, and he made sport before them; and they set him between the pillars.
And Samson said to the young man who was holding his hand, "Let me alone, and let me feel the pillars on which the house is established, and let me lean on them."
And the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and on the roof were about three thousand men and women looking on while Samson made sport.

And Samson called out to YHWH and said, "Lord YHWH, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, O God, that I may avenge myself with one vengeance for my two eyes on the Philistines."
And Samson grasped the two middle pillars on which the house was established, and he braced himself on them, one with his right hand and one with his left.

And Samson said, "Let my life die with the Philistines." And he stretched out with strength, and the house fell on the lords and on all the people who were in it. And the dead whom he killed in his death were more than those whom he had killed in his life.
And his brothers and all his father's house went down and carried him up, and they buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he had judged Israel twenty years.

judges_17.t: And there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Micayehu.

And he said to his mother, "The eleven hundred of silver that was taken from you, and about which you uttered a curse and also spoke it in my ears — behold, the silver is with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by YHWH."

And he returned the eleven hundred of silver to his mother; and his mother said, "Consecrating, I consecrate the silver to YHWH from my hand, for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image. And now I will return it to you."

And he returned the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred of silver and gave it to the refiner, and he made it into a carved image and a cast image; and it was in the house of Micayehu.
And the man Micah — he had a house of God; and he made an ephod and teraphim, and he filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became a priest for him.
In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes.
And there was a young man from Bethlehem of Judah, from the clan of Judah; and he was a Levite, and he was sojourning there.
And the man went from the city, from Bethlehem of Judah, to sojourn wherever he might find; and he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, making his way.
And Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I may find."
And Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be for me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten of silver for the days, and an outfit of clothes, and your sustenance." And the Levite went.
And the Levite was willing to dwell with the man, and the young man was to him like one of his sons.
And Micah filled the hand of the Levite, and the young man became a priest for him; and he was in the house of Micah.
And Micah said, "Now I know that YHWH will do good to me, for the Levite has become a priest for me."

judges_18.t: In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danite was seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell in, for until that day nothing had fallen to it as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

And the sons of Dan sent from their clan five men from their whole number, men, sons of valour, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it; and they said to them, "Go, explore the land." And they came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and spent the night there.

They were near the house of Micah, and they recognised the voice of the young man, the Levite; and they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what is there for you here?"
And he said to them, "Thus and thus Micah has done for me, and he has hired me, and I have become a priest for him."
And they said to him, "Enquire, please, of God, that we may know whether our journey on which we are going will succeed."
And the priest said to them, "Go in peace. Your way on which you go is before YHWH."

And the five men went and came to Laish, and they saw the people who were in its midst dwelling in security, after the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; and there was no one putting to shame anything in the land, possessing restraint; and they were far from the Sidonians, and they had no dealings with anyone.
And they came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, "What of you?"
And they said, "Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good. And you are inactive! Do not hesitate to go, to enter, to take possession of the land.
"When you go, you will come to a secure people, and the land is broad on both hands, for God has given it into your hand — a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."
And there set out from there, of the clan of the Danite, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred men girded with weapons of war.
And they went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they call that place Mahaneh-dan to this day; behold, it is behind Kiriath-jearim.
And they passed through from there to the hill country of Ephraim, and they came to the house of Micah.

And the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish answered and said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there is an ephod, and teraphim, and a carved image, and a cast image? And now consider what you will do."
And they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite — the house of Micah — and asked him about his welfare.
And the six hundred men girded with their weapons of war, who were of the sons of Dan, were standing at the entrance of the gate.

And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up, came there, took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the cast image — and the priest was standing at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men girded with the weapons of war.
And these men came to the house of Micah and took the carved image, the ephod and the teraphim and the cast image; and the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

And they said to him, "Keep quiet. Put your hand over your mouth, and come with us, and be for us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one man, or to be a priest for a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
And the heart of the priest was glad, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the carved image, and he went in the midst of the people.
And they turned and went, and they put the little ones and the livestock and the valuables in front of them.
They had gone far from the house of Micah, and the men who were in the houses that were near the house of Micah were called together, and they overtook the sons of Dan.
And they called out to the sons of Dan; and they turned their faces round and said to Micah, "What is it to you, that you have been called together?"
And he said, "My gods that I made you have taken, and the priest, and you have gone. And what is left to me? And how is it that you say to me, 'What is it to you?'"
And the sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest bitter-tempered men fall upon you and you gather up your life and the life of your household."
And the sons of Dan went on their way; and Micah saw that they were too strong for him, and he turned and returned to his house.

And they took what Micah had made, and the priest who belonged to him, and they came upon Laish, upon a people quiet and secure, and struck them with the mouth of the sword; and the city they burned with fire.
And there was no deliverer, for it was far from Sidon, and they had no dealings with anyone; and it was in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. And they rebuilt the city and dwelt in it.
And they called the name of the city Dan, by the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; but Laish was the name of the city at the first.

And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image; and Jonathan son of Gershom son of Manasseh — he and his sons were priests for the tribe of the Danite until the day the land went into exile.
And they set up for themselves the carved image of Micah, which he had made, all the days that the house of God was at Shiloh.

judges_19.t: And it was in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a man, a Levite, sojourning in the remotest parts of the hill country of Ephraim; and he took for himself a woman, a concubine, from Bethlehem of Judah.
And his concubine prostituted herself against him, and she went from him to her father's house, to Bethlehem of Judah, and she was there days — four months.

And her husband rose and went after her, to speak to her heart, to bring her back; and his young man was with him, and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him to her father's house; and the father of the young woman saw him and was glad to meet him.
And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, took hold of him, and he stayed with him three days; and they ate and drank and spent the night there.

And it was on the fourth day that they rose early in the morning, and he rose to go; and the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "Sustain your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterwards you shall go."
And the two of them sat down and ate and drank together; and the father of the young woman said to the man, "Be willing, please, and spend the night, and let your heart be glad."
And the man rose to go; but his father-in-law urged him, and he turned back and spent the night there.
And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go, and the father of the young woman said, "Sustain your heart, please, and delay until the day declines." And the two of them ate.

And the man rose to go, he and his concubine and his young man; and his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, "Behold now, the day is sinking toward evening. Spend the night, please. Behold, the day is declining. Spend the night here and let your heart be glad; and tomorrow you shall rise early for your journey, and you shall go to your tent."
But the man was not willing to spend the night, and he rose and went, and he came opposite Jebus — that is Jerusalem; and with him were a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
They were near Jebus, and the day had gone far down; and the young man said to his master, "Come, please, let us turn aside to this city of the Jebusite and spend the night in it."
And his master said to him, "We will not turn aside to a foreign city, which is not of the sons of Israel; and we will pass on as far as Gibeah."
And he said to his young man, "Come, and let us draw near to one of the places, and we will spend the night in Gibeah or in Ramah."
And they passed on and went, and the sun went down on them beside Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
And they turned aside there to go in and spend the night in Gibeah; and he went in and sat down in the open square of the city, and there was no one taking them into a house to spend the night.
