And all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch, saying: The scroll from which you read in the ears of the people — take it in your hand and come. And Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him: Sit now and read it in our ears. And Baruch read it in their ears.
And it was, when they heard all the words, they were in dread, each toward his neighbour, and they said to Baruch: We must surely tell the king all these words.
And they asked Baruch, saying: Tell us now, how did you write all these words from his mouth?
And Baruch said to them: From his mouth he proclaimed all these words to me, and I was writing on the scroll with ink.
And the officials said to Baruch: Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.
And they went to the king, to the court, and the scroll they had deposited in the room of Elishama the scribe; and they told all the words in the ears of the king.

And the king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll, and he fetched it from the room of Elishama the scribe; and Jehudi read it in the ears of the king and in the ears of all the officials who were standing beside the king.
And the king was sitting in the winter house, in the ninth month, and the fire-pot before him was burning.

And it was, when Jehudi had read three or four columns, he would tear it with the scribe's knife and throw it into the fire that was in the fire-pot, until the whole scroll was consumed on the fire that was in the fire-pot.
And they were not afraid and did not tear their clothes — the king and all his servants who heard all these words.
And even Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made entreaty with the king not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.
And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but YHWH hid them.
And the word of YHWH came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying:
Take again for yourself another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were on the former scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say: Thus says YHWH: You yourself burned this scroll, saying: Why have you written on it, saying: The king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and cause human being and animal to cease from it?
Therefore thus says YHWH concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will not have anyone sitting on the throne of David; and his corpse will be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

And I will call him and his offspring and his servants to account for their iniquity; and I will bring on them and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and on the man of Judah all the disaster that I have spoken against them, but they did not listen.

And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the document that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many words like them were added to them besides.

jeremiah_37.t: And Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But he did not listen — he and his servants and the people of the land — to the words of YHWH that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: Pray now for us to YHWH our God.
And Jeremiah was coming and going in the midst of the people, and they had not put him in the house of imprisonment.
And the army of Pharaoh had come out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report of them and took themselves up from Jerusalem.
And the word of YHWH came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:

Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah, who is sending you to me to consult me: Look, the army of Pharaoh that was coming out to help you is about to return to its own land, Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city, and capture it and burn it with fire.
Thus says YHWH: Do not deceive yourselves, saying: The Chaldeans will surely go away from us — for they will not go.

For even if you struck down the whole army of the Chaldeans who are fighting with you, and there were left among them men pierced through, each in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.
And it was, when the army of the Chaldeans had taken itself up from Jerusalem because of the army of Pharaoh,
Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to receive a portion there in the midst of the people.

And he was at the Gate of Benjamin, and there was a captain of the guard whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah; and he arrested Jeremiah the prophet, saying: You are deserting to the Chaldeans!
And Jeremiah said: Falsehood! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans. But he did not listen to him, and Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
And the officials were angry at Jeremiah and struck him, and they put him in the house of fetters, the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into the house of imprisonment.
For Jeremiah went into the house of the cistern and into the cells, and Jeremiah remained there many days.

And King Zedekiah sent and took him, and the king asked him in his house, in secret, and said: Is there a word from YHWH? And Jeremiah said: There is. And he said: You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah: How have I sinned against you and against your servants and against this people, that you have put me in the house of imprisonment?
And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying: The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land?
And now, hear now, my lord the king: Let my supplication fall before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, that I may not die there.

And King Zedekiah commanded, and they deposited Jeremiah in the courtyard of the guard; and a round loaf of bread was given him daily from the street of the bakers, until all the bread in the city was gone. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

jeremiah_38.t: And Shephatiah son of Mattan, and Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying:

Thus says YHWH: The one who remains in this city will die by the sword, by famine and by pestilence; but the one who goes out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be his as plunder, and he will live.
Thus says YHWH: This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

And the officials said to the king: Let this man be put to death, for in this way he is weakening the hands of the men of war who remain in this city and the hands of all the people, by speaking such words to them; for this man is not seeking welfare for this people, but harm.
And King Zedekiah said: Look, he is in your hand; for the king can do nothing against you.

And they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard, and they let Jeremiah down with ropes. And in the cistern there was no water, only mud; and Jeremiah sank in the mud.
And Ebed-melech the Cushite, a man who was a court official, and he was in the house of the king, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern; and the king was sitting in the Gate of Benjamin.
And Ebed-melech went out from the house of the king and spoke to the king, saying:

My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the cistern; and he will die where he is because of the famine, for there is no more bread in the city.
And the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, saying: Take thirty men from here in your hand, and bring up Jeremiah the prophet from the cistern before he dies.

And Ebed-melech took the men in his hand and went to the house of the king, to a place under the storehouse, and took from there worn-out clothes and worn-out rags, and let them down to Jeremiah into the cistern with ropes.
And Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah: Put now the worn-out clothes and the rags under the joints of your arms, under the ropes. And Jeremiah did so.
And they drew Jeremiah out with the ropes and brought him up from the cistern; and Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

And King Zedekiah sent and brought Jeremiah the prophet to him, to the third entrance that was in the house of YHWH; and the king said to Jeremiah: I am asking you a matter; do not hide anything from me.
And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I counsel you, you will not listen to me.

And King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in secret, saying: As YHWH lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death, and I will not give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life.

And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: Thus says YHWH, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: If you will indeed go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then your life will live, and this city will not be burned with fire; and you will live, you and your household.

But if you do not go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire; and you yourself will not escape from their hand.
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: I dread the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hand and they deal wantonly with me.
And Jeremiah said: They will not give you. Listen now to the voice of YHWH, to what I am speaking to you, and it will go well for you, and your life will live.
But if you refuse to go out, this is the thing that YHWH has shown me:

And look, all the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah are being brought out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, and they are saying: They misled you and prevailed over you, the men of your peace; your feet are sunk in the mire, they have turned back.

And all your wives and your children they will bring out to the Chaldeans; and you yourself will not escape from their hand, for by the hand of the king of Babylon you will be captured, and this city will be burned with fire.
And Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: Let no one know of these words, and you will not die.

And if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you: Tell us now, what did you say to the king? Do not hide it from us, and we will not put you to death — and what did the king say to you? —
then you shall say to them: I was letting my supplication fall before the king, that he not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.
And all the officials came to Jeremiah and asked him, and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded; and they kept silent toward him, for the matter had not been heard.
And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured. And it was, when Jerusalem was captured —

jeremiah_39.t: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the city was broken into.

And all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebu, Sarsekim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.

And it was, when Zedekiah king of Judah and all the men of war saw them, that they fled and went out from the city by night, by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls; and he went out by way of the Arabah.

And the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and they took him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he spoke judgements with him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes; and all the nobles of Judah the king of Babylon slaughtered.
And the eyes of Zedekiah he blinded, and he bound him in bronze fetters to bring him to Babylon.
And the house of the king and the house of the people the Chaldeans burned with fire, and the walls of Jerusalem they pulled down.

And the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people who remained, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile to Babylon.
But some of the poor people, who had nothing, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards left in the land of Judah; and he gave them vineyards and fields on that day.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon gave command concerning Jeremiah, by the hand of Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards, saying:
Take him and set your eyes on him, and do him no harm at all; but just as he says to you, so do with him.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards sent, and Nebushazban the Rab-saris, and Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the chiefs of the king of Babylon;
and they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the guard, and gave him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to take him out to the house; and he remained in the midst of the people.
And to Jeremiah the word of YHWH had come while he was shut up in the courtyard of the guard, saying:

Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: Thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing my words against this city for harm and not for good; and they will happen before you on that day.
But I will deliver you on that day — the declaration of YHWH — and you will not be given into the hand of the men before whom you are afraid.
For I will surely rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword; and your life will be yours as plunder, because you trusted in me — the declaration of YHWH.

jeremiah_40.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from YHWH after Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had set him free from Ramah, when he took him — and he was bound in chains in the midst of all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile to Babylon.
And the chief of the bodyguards took Jeremiah and said to him: YHWH your God spoke this harm against this place,
and YHWH has brought it and done just as he said; for you sinned against YHWH and did not listen to his voice, and this thing has happened to you.

And now, look, I have set you free today from the chains that were on your hand. If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eye on you; but if it is displeasing in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, refrain. See, all the land is before you: to wherever is good and right in your eyes to go, go there.

And while he was still not turning back — Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him in the midst of the people; or go wherever it is right in your eyes to go. And the chief of the bodyguards gave him a food allowance and a present, and let him go.
And Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, to Mizpah, and dwelt with him in the midst of the people who remained in the land.

And all the commanders of the armies who were in the open country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had appointed with him men and women and little ones, and some of the poor of the land, from those who had not been taken into exile to Babylon.

And they came to Gedaliah, to Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite — they and their men.

And Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men, saying: Do not be afraid of serving the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you.

And I, look, I am dwelling at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us; and you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken hold of.

And also all the Judeans who were in Moab and among the sons of Ammon and in Edom, and who were in all the lands, heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.
And all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, to Mizpah; and they gathered wine and summer fruit in great abundance.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were in the open country came to Gedaliah, to Mizpah,
and said to him: Do you know for certain that Baalis king of the sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you, as to your life? But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

And Johanan son of Kareah said to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah: Let me go now and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he strike you, as to your life, and all Judah who have gathered to you be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish?
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah: You shall not do this thing, for you are speaking falsehood concerning Ishmael.

jeremiah_41.t: And it was in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal offspring and one of the chiefs of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah; and they were eating bread there together at Mizpah.

And Ishmael son of Nethaniah arose, and the ten men who were with him, and they struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword; and he killed him whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And all the Judeans who were with him — with Gedaliah — at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of war, Ishmael struck down.
And it was, on the second day after the killing of Gedaliah, and no one knew,

men came from Shechem, from Shiloh and from Samaria — eighty men, their beards shaven and their clothes torn and having cut themselves — with a grain offering and frankincense in their hand, to bring to the house of YHWH.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, going along and weeping; and it was, when he met them, he said to them: Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
And it was, when they came into the midst of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them into the midst of the cistern — he and the men who were with him.

But ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael: Do not kill us, for we have stores in the field — wheat and barley and oil and honey. And he refrained and did not kill them among their brothers.

And the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men whom he had struck down by the hand of Gedaliah — it was the one that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

And Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who were at Mizpah — the daughters of the king and all the people who remained at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and went to cross over to the sons of Ammon.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him heard all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
And they took all the men and went to do battle with Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him at the great waters that are in Gibeon.
And it was, when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him, they were glad.
And all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned round, and they turned back and went to Johanan son of Kareah.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped with eight men from before Johanan, and went to the sons of Ammon.

And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him took all the rest of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah — after he had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam — men, the men of war, and women and little ones and court officials, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And they went and stayed at Geruth Kimham, which is beside Bethlehem, to go on and come to Egypt,
because of the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

jeremiah_42.t: And all the commanders of the armies approached, and Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to Jeremiah the prophet: Let our supplication fall before you, and pray for us to YHWH your God, for all this remnant; for we are left a few out of many, as your eyes see us.
And let YHWH your God declare to us the way in which we should go and the thing we should do.

And Jeremiah the prophet said to them: I have heard. Look, I am praying to YHWH your God according to your words; and every word that YHWH answers you I will tell you — I will not withhold a word from you.
And they said to Jeremiah: May YHWH be a witness of faithfulness and faithful against us, if we do not act according to every word with which YHWH your God sends you to us.
Whether good or bad, to the voice of YHWH our God, to whom we are sending you, we will listen; so that it may go well for us, because we will listen to the voice of YHWH our God.
And it was, at the end of ten days, that the word of YHWH came to Jeremiah.
And he summoned Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to them: Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to make your supplication fall before him:
If you will indeed remain in this land, then I will build you and not overthrow you, and I will plant you and not pluck you up; for I relent concerning the harm that I have done to you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid of him — the declaration of YHWH — for I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
And I will give you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and restore you to your own ground.
But if you say: We will not remain in this land — so as not to listen to the voice of YHWH your God —
saying: No, but to the land of Egypt we will go, where we will not see warfare and will not hear the sound of the ram's horn and will not hunger for bread; and there we will dwell —
and now, therefore, hear the word of YHWH, remnant of Judah: Thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: If you indeed set your faces to go to Egypt, and you go to sojourn there,
then the sword that you are afraid of will overtake you there, in the land of Egypt; and the famine that you are anxious about will pursue closely after you there in Egypt, and there you will die.

And all the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to sojourn there will die by the sword, by famine and by pestilence; and they will have no survivor or escapee from before the disaster that I am bringing on them.

For thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: Just as my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt; and you will become a curse and a horror and a curse and a reproach, and you will not see this place again.
YHWH has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Know for certain that I have warned you today.

For you have gone astray at the cost of your lives; for you yourselves sent me to YHWH your God, saying: Pray for us to YHWH our God, and according to all that YHWH our God says, so tell us, and we will do it.
And I have told you today, but you have not listened to the voice of YHWH your God, or to anything with which he sent me to you.
And now, know for certain that by the sword, by famine and by pestilence you will die in the place where you desire to go to sojourn.

jeremiah_43.t: And it was, when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of YHWH their God, with which YHWH their God had sent him to them — all these words —

Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said, saying to Jeremiah: You are speaking falsehood! YHWH our God did not send you to say: You shall not go to Egypt to sojourn there.
For Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, so as to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put us to death and to take us into exile to Babylon.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies and all the people did not listen to the voice of YHWH, to remain in the land of Judah.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies took all the remnant of Judah, who had come back from all the nations where they had been driven, to sojourn in the land of Judah:

the men and the women and the little ones and the daughters of the king, and every person whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
And they went to the land of Egypt, for they did not listen to the voice of YHWH; and they came to Tahpanhes.
And the word of YHWH came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying:
Take large stones in your hand and hide them in the mortar, in the brick terrace that is at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of Judean men,

and say to them: Thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am sending and I will fetch Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden; and he will spread his canopy over them.
And he will come and strike the land of Egypt: those who are for death, to death; and those who are for captivity, to captivity; and those who are for the sword, to the sword.

And I will kindle fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and take them captive; and he will pick over the land of Egypt as a shepherd picks over his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.
And he will shatter the pillars of Beth-shemesh, which is in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of Egypt he will burn with fire.

jeremiah_44.t: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans who were dwelling in the land of Egypt — who were dwelling at Migdol and at Tahpanhes and at Memphis and in the land of Pathros — saying:

Thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: You yourselves have seen all the disaster that I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah; and look, they are a ruin this day, and there is no inhabitant in them,
because of their evil that they did, to provoke me to anger, by going to make smoke, to serve other gods whom they did not know — they, you, and your fathers.
And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, saying: Do not do this abominable thing, which I hate.
But they did not listen and did not incline their ear, to turn back from their evil, so as not to make smoke to other gods.
And my wrath and my anger poured forth and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin, a desolation, as at this day.

And now, thus says YHWH, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: Why are you doing great harm to your own lives, to cut off from you man and woman, child and suckling, from the midst of Judah, so as to leave yourselves no remnant —

provoking me to anger with the works of your hands, by making smoke to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have come to sojourn — so as to cut yourselves off, and so as to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers and the evils of the kings of Judah and the evils of his wives, and your own evils and the evils of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
They have not been crushed to this day, and they have not feared, and they have not walked in my law and in my statutes that I set before you and before your fathers.
Therefore thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am setting my face against you for harm, and to cut off all Judah.

And I will take away the remnant of Judah, who set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to sojourn there; and they will all meet their end in the land of Egypt. They will fall by the sword, by famine they will meet their end, from the least to the greatest; by the sword and by famine they will die, and they will become a curse, a horror, a curse and a reproach.
And I will call to account those who dwell in the land of Egypt, just as I called Jerusalem to account — by the sword, by famine and by pestilence.

And there will be no escapee or survivor for the remnant of Judah who went to sojourn there in the land of Egypt, to return to the land of Judah, to which they are lifting up their desire to return, to dwell there; for they will not return, except as fugitives.

And all the men who knew that their wives were making smoke to other gods, and all the women who were standing by, a great company, and all the people who were dwelling in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:
As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of YHWH — we are not going to listen to you.

For we will surely do everything that has gone out of our own mouth: to make smoke to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. And we were satisfied with bread and were well, and we saw no disaster.
But since we ceased to make smoke to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and by the sword and by famine we have met our end.

And when we were making smoke to the queen of the heavens and pouring out drink offerings to her — was it without our husbands that we made cakes for her, to form her image, and poured out drink offerings to her?
And Jeremiah said to all the people — to the men and to the women and to all the people who had answered him a word — saying:

Was it not the smoke offering that you made in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem — you and your fathers, your kings and your officials and the people of the land — that YHWH remembered, and that came up on his heart?

And YHWH could no longer endure it, because of the evil of your deeds, because of the abominations that you did; and your land has become a ruin and a waste and a curse, with no inhabitant, as at this day.

Because you made smoke, and because you sinned against YHWH and did not listen to the voice of YHWH, and did not walk in his law and in his statutes and in his testimonies — therefore this disaster has come upon you, as at this day.
And Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women: Hear the word of YHWH, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives — you have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying: We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to make smoke to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her. Then surely carry out your vows, and surely perform your vows!

Therefore hear the word of YHWH, all Judah who are dwelling in the land of Egypt: Look, I have sworn by my great name, says YHWH: My name will no longer be named in the mouth of any man of Judah, saying: As Lord YHWH lives! — in all the land of Egypt.
Look, I am watching over them for harm and not for good; and every man of Judah who is in the land of Egypt will meet his end by the sword and by famine, until they come to an end.

And escapees of the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah who went to the land of Egypt to sojourn there will know whose word stands — mine or theirs.
And this will be the sign for you — the declaration of YHWH — that I am about to call you to account in this place, so that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for harm:

Thus says YHWH: Look, I am giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.

jeremiah_45.t: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a scroll from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:
You said: Woe to me now, for YHWH has added sorrow to my pain! I am weary with my groaning, and I have found no rest.
Thus you shall say to him: Thus says YHWH: Look, what I have built I am overthrowing, and what I have planted I am plucking up — and that is the whole land.

And you — are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For look, I am bringing disaster on all flesh — the declaration of YHWH — but I will give you your life as plunder, in all the places where you go.

jeremiah_46.t: What came as the word of YHWH to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck down in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Set in order buckler and shield, and draw near for battle!
Harness the horses, and mount, you horsemen! Take your stand in helmets; polish the spears, put on the armour!
Why have I seen it? They are terrified, turning back; and their warriors are crushed. They have fled in flight and have not turned round — terror all around! — the declaration of YHWH.
Let not the swift flee, and let not the warrior escape! Northward, by the side of the river Euphrates, they have stumbled and fallen.
Who is this that rises like the Nile, whose waters surge like the rivers?
Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters surge like the rivers. And it said: I will rise, I will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and those who dwell in it.
Go up, you horses; drive madly, you chariots! And let the warriors go forth — Cush and Put, who wield the shield, and the Ludites, who wield and bend the bow.

And that day belongs to Lord YHWH of hosts, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. And the sword will devour and be satisfied, and take its fill of their blood; for Lord YHWH of hosts has a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt! In vain you have multiplied remedies; there is no new flesh for you.
The nations have heard your shame, and your outcry has filled the earth; for warrior has stumbled against warrior — the two of them have fallen together.
The word that YHWH spoke to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
Declare in Egypt, and proclaim in Migdol; proclaim in Memphis and in Tahpanhes! Say: Take your stand and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured all around you.
Why have your mighty ones been swept away? They did not stand, for YHWH pushed them down.
He has made many stumble; yes, each has fallen against his neighbour. And they said: Arise, and let us return to our own people and to the land of our birth, because of the sword of the oppressor.
They have called there: Pharaoh king of Egypt is a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.
As I live — the declaration of the King, whose name is YHWH of hosts — surely, like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea, he will come.
Make yourself baggage for exile, O inhabitant, daughter of Egypt! For Memphis will become a waste, and will be made desolate, with no inhabitant.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer; a gadfly from the north is coming, coming.

Also her hired soldiers in her midst are like calves of the stall; for they too have turned, they have fled together; they have not stood their ground. For the day of their doom has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound goes like the serpent's; for they come with an army, and with axes they come against her, like cutters of wood.
They have cut down her forest — the declaration of YHWH — for it cannot be searched; for they are more numerous than locusts, and they are without number.
The daughter of Egypt is put to shame; she is given into the hand of the people of the north.
YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am calling to account Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods, and her kings — Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

And I will give them into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of his servants. But afterwards it will be inhabited as in days of old — the declaration of YHWH.

And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, Israel; for look, I am saving you from far off, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. And Jacob will return and be undisturbed and at ease, with none to frighten him.

You, do not fear, my servant Jacob — the declaration of YHWH — for I am with you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. And I will discipline you for justice, and I will certainly not leave you unpunished.

jeremiah_47.t: What came as the word of YHWH to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Thus says YHWH: Look, waters are rising from the north, and they will become an overflowing torrent; and they will overflow the land and all that fills it, the city and those who dwell in it. And the people will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail

at the sound of the stamping of the hooves of his mighty ones, at the rattling of his chariotry, the din of his wheels. Fathers have not turned back to their children, because of the slackness of hands —

because of the day that is coming to devastate all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every surviving helper. For YHWH is devastating the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?
Alas, sword of YHWH! How long until you are quiet? Gather yourself into your sheath; rest, and be still.
How can you be quiet, when YHWH has given it a command? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast — there he has appointed it.

jeremiah_48.t: Concerning Moab. Thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame, it is captured; the stronghold is put to shame and shattered.
The praise of Moab is no more. In Heshbon they have planned calamity against her: Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation! You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will go after you.
A sound of a cry from Horonaim: devastation and great shattering!
Moab is shattered; her little ones have made a cry heard.
For the ascent of Luhith — with weeping one goes up weeping; for on the descent of Horonaim they have heard the distresses of the cry of shattering.
Flee! Save your lives, and be like a bush in the wilderness!
For because of your trusting in your works and in your treasures, you too will be captured; and Chemosh will go out into exile, his priests and his officials together.
And a devastator will come to every city, and no city will escape; and the valley will perish and the plain be destroyed, as YHWH has said.
Give a ṣiṣ to Moab, for she will surely go out in flight; and her cities will become a waste, with no inhabitant in them.
Cursed is the one who does the work of YHWH with slackness, and cursed is the one who withholds his sword from blood!

Moab has been at ease from his youth, and he has been undisturbed on his lees; and he has not been poured from vessel to vessel, and he has not gone into exile. Therefore his taste has stayed in him, and his aroma has not changed.
Therefore, look, days are coming — the declaration of YHWH — when I will send to him tippers, and they will tip him; and they will empty his vessels and smash their jars.
And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their trust.
How can you say: We are warriors, and men of strength for battle?
Moab is devastated, and her cities — he has gone up; and the choicest of his young men have gone down to the slaughter — the declaration of the King, whose name is YHWH of hosts.
The doom of Moab is near to coming, and his calamity hastens exceedingly.
Show sympathy for him, all you around him, and all who know his name! Say: How the staff of strength is shattered, the rod of splendour!
Come down from honour and sit in thirst, O inhabitant, daughter of Dibon! For the devastator of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your strongholds.
Stand by the road and watch, O inhabitant of Aroer! Ask the man who flees and the woman who escapes; say: What has happened?
Moab is put to shame, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare it at the Arnon that Moab is devastated.
And judgement has come to the land of the plain: to Holon, and to Jahzah, and against Mephaath,
and against Dibon, and against Nebo, and against Beth-diblathaim,
and against Kiriathaim, and against Beth-gamul, and against Beth-meon,
and against Kerioth, and against Bozrah, and against all the cities of the land of Moab, the far and the near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is shattered — the declaration of YHWH.
Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against YHWH; and Moab will splash down in his vomit, and he too will become a laughing-stock.
And was not Israel a laughing-stock to you? Was he found among thieves, that as often as your words were about him you shook your head?
Abandon the cities and dwell in the rock, O inhabitants of Moab! And be like a dove that nests on the sides of the mouth of a ravine.
We have heard of the pride of Moab — he is very proud — his haughtiness and his pride and his arrogance, and the loftiness of his heart.
I myself know — the declaration of YHWH — his fury, and it is not right; his empty boasts have not accomplished what is right.
Therefore I will wail over Moab, and for all Moab I will cry out; for the people of Kir-heres he groans.

More than the weeping of Jazer I will weep for you, O vine of Sibmah! Your tendrils crossed the sea; they reached as far as the sea of Jazer. On your summer fruit and on your vintage a devastator has fallen.
And joy and rejoicing are taken away from the garden-land and from the land of Moab; and I have made wine cease from the winepresses. No one will tread with the shout; the shout will be no shout.
From the cry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, they have given their voice; from Zoar as far as Horonaim, Eglath-shelishiyah. For the waters of Nimrim too will become wastes.
And I will put an end for Moab — the declaration of YHWH — to the one who offers up at a high place and the one who burns as smoke to his gods.
Therefore my heart groans for Moab like flutes, and my heart groans like flutes for the people of Kir-heres; therefore the wealth he acquired has perished.
For every head is baldness and every beard is clipped; on all hands are gashes, and on the loins, sackcloth.
On all the roofs of Moab and in her open places, all of it is wailing; for I have shattered Moab like a vessel no one delights in — the declaration of YHWH.
How it is shattered! They wail! How Moab has turned his neck in shame! And Moab has become a laughing-stock and an object of terror to all around him.
For thus says YHWH: Look, one will swoop like the eagle and spread his wings against Moab.
Kerioth is captured, and the strongholds are seized; and the heart of the warriors of Moab on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labour.
And Moab will be destroyed from being a people, for he magnified himself against YHWH.
Terror and pit and snare are upon you, O inhabitant of Moab — the declaration of YHWH.

The one who flees from before the terror will fall into the pit, and the one who climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the snare; for I will bring upon her, upon Moab, the year of their punishment — the declaration of YHWH.

In the shadow of Heshbon those who flee have stood, without strength; for a fire has gone out from Heshbon and a flame from between Sihon, and it has devoured the forehead of Moab and the crown of the head of the sons of uproar.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh has perished; for your sons have been taken into captivity and your daughters into captivity.
But I will turn back the captivity of Moab in the latter days — the declaration of YHWH. Thus far is the judgement of Moab.

jeremiah_49.t: Concerning the sons of Ammon. Thus says YHWH: Has Israel no sons? Or has he no heir? Why then has Milcom dispossessed Gad, and his people settled in its cities?

Therefore, look, days are coming — the declaration of YHWH — when I will sound the shout of battle against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon; and it will become a mound of desolation, and her daughter-towns will be kindled with fire. And Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed him, says YHWH.

Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Gird yourselves with sackcloth, mourn, and run to and fro among the walls; for Milcom will go into exile, his priests and his officials together.
Why do you boast in the valleys — your valley flowing away, O turning-away daughter, who trusts in her treasures: Who will come against me?
Look, I am bringing terror upon you — the declaration of Lord YHWH of hosts — from all who are around you; and you will be driven out, each one straight ahead, with no one to gather the fugitive.
But afterwards I will turn back the captivity of the sons of Ammon — the declaration of YHWH.
Concerning Edom. Thus says YHWH of hosts: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the discerning? Has their wisdom gone rotten?
Flee, turn back, go deep to dwell, O inhabitants of Dedan! For I have brought the doom of Esau upon him, the time when I called him to account.
If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, they would destroy only their fill.
For I myself have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding-places, and he cannot hide himself. His offspring is devastated, and his brothers and his neighbours, and he is no more.
Leave your fatherless; I myself will keep them alive. And let your widows trust in me.

For thus says YHWH: Look, those whose sentence was not to drink the cup will surely drink it — and you, are you the one who will be utterly exempt from punishment? You will not be exempt, for you will surely drink.
For by myself I swear — the declaration of YHWH — that Bozrah will become a waste, a reproach, a desolation and a curse; and all her cities will become everlasting ruins.
I have heard a report from YHWH, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: Gather yourselves and come against her, and rise up for battle!
For look, I have made you small among the nations, despised among humankind.

Your horror has deceived you, the presumption of your heart — you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest high as the eagle, from there I will bring you down — the declaration of YHWH.
And Edom will become a horror. Everyone who passes by her will be appalled and will hiss at all her wounds.
Like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbours, says YHWH, no one will dwell there, and no child of humankind will sojourn in her.

Look, like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan to the ever-flowing pasture; for in a moment I will drive him away from her, and whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. For who is like me, and who will summon me, and who is the shepherd who can stand before me?

Therefore hear the counsel of YHWH that he has counselled against Edom, and his purposes that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be made desolate over them.
At the sound of their fall the earth quakes; the outcry — at the Sea of Reeds its sound is heard.
Look, like the eagle he will go up and swoop, and spread his wings over Bozrah; and the heart of the warriors of Edom on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labour.
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard a bad report; they melt away. In the sea there is anxiety; it cannot be quiet.
Damascus has grown slack; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pains have taken hold of her, like a woman giving birth.
How is the city of praise not abandoned, the town of my joy?
Therefore her young men will fall in her open places, and all the men of war will be silenced on that day — the declaration of YHWH of hosts.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will devour the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus says YHWH: Arise, go up against Kedar, and devastate the sons of the east!
Their tents and their flocks will be taken; their tent-curtains and all their equipment and their camels they will carry off for themselves; and they will call out over them: Terror all around!

Flee, take flight far off, go deep to dwell, O inhabitants of Hazor — the declaration of YHWH! For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has counselled counsel against you and has purposed a purpose against you.
Arise, go up against a nation at ease, dwelling in security — the declaration of YHWH — with no gates and no bars; they dwell alone.

And their camels will become spoil, and the abundance of their livestock plunder; and I will scatter to every wind those who have their temples clipped, and from every side I will bring their doom — the declaration of YHWH.
And Hazor will become a lair of jackals, a desolation for ever; no one will dwell there, and no child of humankind will sojourn in her.
What came as the word of YHWH to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
Thus says YHWH of hosts: Look, I am breaking the bow of Elam, the first of their strength.
And I will bring against Elam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds; and there will be no nation where the outcasts of Elam do not come.

And I will shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life; and I will bring calamity upon them, the burning of my anger — the declaration of YHWH. And I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.
And I will set my throne in Elam, and I will destroy from there king and officials — the declaration of YHWH.
And it will be, in the latter days, that I will turn back the captivity of Elam — the declaration of YHWH.

jeremiah_50.t: The word that YHWH spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare among the nations and proclaim, and lift up a standard; proclaim, do not conceal it! Say: Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame, Marduk is shattered; her images are put to shame, her idols are shattered.
For a nation has come up against her from the north; it will make her land a waste, and there will be no inhabitant in her. From humankind to animal they have taken flight, they have gone.
In those days and at that time — the declaration of YHWH — the sons of Israel will come, they and the sons of Judah together; they will go, going and weeping, and they will seek YHWH their God.
They will ask the way to Zion, their faces set that way: Come, and let us join ourselves to YHWH in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.
Lost sheep have my people become; their shepherds have made them wander; on the mountains they have turned them away. From mountain to hill they have gone; they have forgotten their resting-place.
All who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said: We are not guilty — because they sinned against YHWH, the habitation of righteousness, and the hope of their fathers, YHWH.
Take flight from the midst of Babylon, and go out from the land of the Chaldeans; and be like he-goats before the flock.

For look, I am rousing and bringing up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north; and they will draw up against her — from there she will be captured. His arrows are like a skilled warrior's; he does not return empty.
And Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will be satisfied — the declaration of YHWH.
Because you rejoice, because you exult, O plunderers of my inheritance; because you skip about like a threshing heifer and neigh like stallions —
your mother is utterly put to shame; she who bore you is abashed. Look, the last of the nations: a wilderness, a parched land and a desert plain.
Because of the rage of YHWH she will not be inhabited, but will be a desolation, all of her. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and will hiss over all her wounds.
Draw up against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow! Shoot at her, do not spare an arrow, for she has sinned against YHWH.
Shout against her all around! She has given her hand; her towers have fallen, her walls are torn down. For this is the vengeance of YHWH: avenge yourselves on her; as she has done, do to her.
Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle in the time of harvest. Because of the sword of the oppressor, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
Israel is a scattered sheep that lions have driven away. The first devoured him — the king of Assyria; and this last one has gnawed his bones — Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
Therefore thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am calling to account the king of Babylon and his land, as I called to account the king of Assyria.
And I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; and on the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead his appetite will be satisfied.

In those days and at that time — the declaration of YHWH — the iniquity of Israel will be sought and there will be none, and the sins of Judah, and they will not be found; for I will forgive those whom I leave as a remnant.

Against the land of Merathaim — go up against her, and against the inhabitants of Pekod! Slay and devote to destruction after them — the declaration of YHWH — and do according to all that I have commanded you.
A sound of battle is in the land, and a great shattering.
How the hammer of all the earth is cut off and shattered! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
I set a snare for you, and you were also caught, Babylon, and you did not know it. You were found and also seized, because you engaged in strife with YHWH.
YHWH has opened his armoury and brought out the weapons of his indignation; for Lord YHWH of hosts has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest end; open her granaries; pile her up like heaps and devote her to destruction; let her have no remnant.
Slay all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter! Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
A sound of fugitives and escapees from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of YHWH our God, the vengeance of his temple!

Summon archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow! Encamp against her all around; let there be no escape for her. Repay her according to her deed; according to all that she has done, do to her. For she has been presumptuous against YHWH, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her young men will fall in her open places, and all her men of war will be silenced on that day — the declaration of YHWH.
Look, I am against you, O Arrogance — the declaration of Lord YHWH of hosts — for your day has come, the time when I call you to account.
And Arrogance will stumble and fall, with no one to raise him up; and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour all around him.
Thus says YHWH of hosts: The sons of Israel are oppressed, and the sons of Judah together; and all their captors have kept hold of them, they have refused to let them go.
Their Redeemer is strong; YHWH of hosts is his name. He will surely conduct their case, so as to give rest to the earth and to disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sword against the Chaldeans — the declaration of YHWH — and against the inhabitants of Babylon, and against her officials and against her wise men!
A sword against the empty talkers, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
A sword against his horses and against his chariotry, and against all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become women! A sword against her treasuries, and they will be plundered!
A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and over their dread things they act like madmen.
Therefore desert creatures will dwell there with hyenas, and daughters of the ostrich will dwell in her. And she will never again be inhabited, nor be settled from generation to generation.
Like the overthrow by God of Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbours — the declaration of YHWH — no one will dwell there, and no child of humankind will sojourn in her.
Look, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation and many kings will be roused from the remotest parts of the earth.
Bow and javelin they take hold of; cruel they are, and they show no mercy. Their sound roars like the sea, and on horses they ride, drawn up as a man for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands hang limp. Distress has taken hold of him, anguish like a woman giving birth.

Look, like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan to the ever-flowing pasture; for in a moment I will drive them away from her, and whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. For who is like me, and who will summon me, and who is the shepherd who can stand before me?

Therefore hear the counsel of YHWH that he has counselled against Babylon, and his purposes that he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely the pasture will be made desolate over them.
At the sound: Babylon is captured! — the earth quakes, and an outcry is heard among the nations.

jeremiah_51.t: Thus says YHWH: Look, I am rousing against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-qamai a destroying wind.
And I will send to Babylon winnowers, and they will winnow her and empty her land; for they will be against her from all around on the day of calamity.
Let not the one who bends bend his bow, and let him not rise up in his armour! And do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction.
And the slain will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and the pierced through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God, of YHWH of hosts — though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from the midst of Babylon; let each save his own life! Do not be destroyed in her iniquity; for this is a time of vengeance for YHWH — he is repaying her a recompense.
Babylon was a cup of gold in the hand of YHWH, making all the earth drunk. The nations drank of her wine; therefore the nations act like madmen.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered. Wail over her! Take balm for her pain; perhaps she may be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed. Leave her, and let us each go to his own land; for her judgement has reached to the heavens and has been lifted up to the clouds.
YHWH has brought forth our vindication. Come, and let us recount in Zion the work of YHWH our God!

Sharpen the arrows; fill the shields! YHWH has roused the spirit of the kings of Media, for his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her; for this is the vengeance of YHWH, the vengeance of his temple.
Against the walls of Babylon lift up a standard! Strengthen the watch; station watchmen; prepare the ambushes! For YHWH has both purposed and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who dwell by many waters, abundant in treasures: your end has come, the cubit of your cutting off.
YHWH of hosts has sworn by himself: Surely I will fill you with people like the locust, and they will raise the shout over you.
He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.

At the sound of his giving forth, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens; and he makes clouds rise from the end of the earth. He makes lightnings for the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Every human is stupid, without knowledge; every metalsmith is put to shame by the idol, for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are vapour, a work of mockery; at the time of their punishment they will perish.
Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for he is the one who formed everything; and the tribe of his inheritance — YHWH of hosts is his name.
You are my war-club, weapons of war; and with you I smash nations, and with you I destroy kingdoms.
And with you I smash horse and its rider, and with you I smash chariot and its rider;
and with you I smash man and woman, and with you I smash old man and young man, and with you I smash young man and virgin;
and with you I smash shepherd and his flock, and with you I smash farmer and his team, and with you I smash governors and officials.
And I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion before your eyes — the declaration of YHWH.

Look, I am against you, O destroying mountain — the declaration of YHWH — you who destroy all the earth! And I will stretch out my hand against you and roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain.
And they will not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for foundations, for you will be everlasting wastes — the declaration of YHWH.

Lift up a standard in the land; blow a horn among the nations! Consecrate nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz. Appoint a marshal against her; bring up horses like the bristling locust.
Consecrate nations against her: the kings of Media, her governors and all her officials, and all the land of his dominion.
And the land quakes and writhes, for the purposes of YHWH against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a waste, with no inhabitant.
The warriors of Babylon have ceased to fight; they sit in the strongholds. Their strength has dried up; they have become women. Her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are shattered.
Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is captured from end to end,
and that the fords are seized, and the reed-marshes burned with fire, and the men of war are terrified.
For thus says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden. Yet a little while, and the time of harvest will come for her.

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me, he has confused me; he has set me down an empty vessel. He has swallowed me like the sea-monster; he has filled his belly from my delicacies; he has rinsed me out.
The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon — she who dwells in Zion will say. And my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea — Jerusalem will say.
Therefore thus says YHWH: Look, I am conducting your case, and I will avenge your vengeance; and I will dry up her sea and make her spring dry.
And Babylon will become heaps of stones, a lair of jackals, a horror and a hissing, with no inhabitant.
Together they roar like young lions; they growl like lions' cubs.
When they are heated I will set out their drinking-feast, and I will make them drunk, so that they exult; and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake — the declaration of YHWH.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he-goats.
How Sheshach is captured, and the praise of all the earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has gone up over Babylon; she is covered by the tumult of its waves.
Her cities have become a waste, a parched land and a desert plain, a land where no one dwells and no child of humankind passes through.
And I will call Bel to account in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed; and the nations will no longer stream to him. Also the wall of Babylon has fallen.
Come out from her midst, my people, and let each save his own life from the burning of the anger of YHWH!

And do not let your heart be faint, and do not fear at the report that is heard in the land; for the report will come in one year, and after it the report in the next year, and violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.
Therefore, look, days are coming when I will call to account the carved images of Babylon; and all her land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
And heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon; for from the north the destroyers will come against her — the declaration of YHWH.
Babylon too must fall for the slain of Israel, just as for Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.
You who have escaped the sword, go; do not stand still! Remember YHWH from far off, and let Jerusalem come up on your heart.
We are put to shame, for we have heard reproach; ignominy has covered our faces, for strangers have come into the holy places of the house of YHWH.
Therefore, look, days are coming — the declaration of YHWH — when I will call to account her carved images; and in all her land the fatally wounded will groan.
Though Babylon should go up to the heavens, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, from me destroyers will come against her — the declaration of YHWH.
A sound of a cry from Babylon, and a great shattering from the land of the Chaldeans!
For YHWH is devastating Babylon and destroying from her the great voice; and their waves roar like many waters, the uproar of their voice is given out.
For a devastator has come against her, against Babylon, and her warriors are captured; their bows are shattered; for YHWH is a God of recompense — he will surely repay.

And I will make her officials and her wise men, her governors and her officers and her warriors drunk; and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake — the declaration of the King, whose name is YHWH of hosts.

Thus says YHWH of hosts: The broad walls of Babylon will be utterly demolished, and her high gates will be burned with fire; and peoples will labour for emptiness, and nations for fire — and they will grow weary.
The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And Seraiah was quartermaster.
And Jeremiah wrote all the calamity that would come upon Babylon in a single scroll — all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah: When you come to Babylon, then see that you read aloud all these words,
and say: YHWH, you yourself have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that there will be no inhabitant in it, from humankind to animal, but it will be everlasting desolations.
And when you have finished reading this scroll aloud, you shall tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
and say: Thus Babylon will sink and not rise, because of the calamity that I am bringing upon her — and they will grow weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

jeremiah_52.t: Zedekiah was a son of twenty-one years when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
For because of the anger of YHWH it came about in Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

And it was, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem; and they encamped against it and built a siege-wall against it all around.
And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine was severe in the city, and there was no food for the people of the land.

And the city was broken into; and all the men of war fled and went out from the city by night, by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden — and the Chaldeans were around the city — and they went by way of the Arabah.
And the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
And they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath; and he spoke judgements with him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; and also all the officials of Judah he slaughtered at Riblah.
And the eyes of Zedekiah he blinded, and he bound him in bronze fetters; and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the house of punishments until the day of his death.

And in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month — that was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of YHWH and the house of the king and all the houses of Jerusalem; and every great house he burned with fire.
And all the walls of Jerusalem all around, the whole army of the Chaldeans who were with the chief of the bodyguards broke down.

And some of the poorest of the people, and the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the artisans, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile.
And some of the poorest of the land Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards left behind, to be vinedressers and ploughmen.

And the pillars of bronze that belonged to the house of YHWH, and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of YHWH, the Chaldeans broke in pieces; and they carried all their bronze to Babylon.
And the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the basins and the pans, and all the vessels of bronze with which they served, they took away.

And the bowls and the fire-pans and the basins and the pots and the lampstands and the pans and the libation-bowls — what was gold as gold, and what was silver as silver — the chief of the bodyguards took away.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of YHWH — the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.
And as for the pillars: the height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a line of twelve cubits went round it; and its thickness was four fingers, hollow.

And a capital of bronze was upon it; and the height of the one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of bronze. And the second pillar had the like, and pomegranates.
And the pomegranates were ninety-six to a side; all the pomegranates were one hundred on the network all around.
And the chief of the bodyguards took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.

And from the city he took one court official who was an officer over the men of war, and seven men from those who saw the king's face, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its ground.
This is the people whom Nebuchadnezzar took into exile: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Judeans;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, from Jerusalem, eight hundred and thirty-two persons;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile seven hundred and forty-five Judean persons. All the persons were four thousand six hundred.

And it was, in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out from the prison-house.
And he spoke good things with him and set his seat above the seat of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed his prison clothes, and he ate food before him continually all the days of his life.
And as for his allowance, a continual allowance was given him from the king of Babylon, a day's portion in its day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

job_1.t: There was a man in the land of Uz, Job was his name; and that man was blameless and upright, and fearing God and turning aside from evil.
And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

And his livestock was seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels and five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household of servants; and that man was greater than all the people of the east.
And his sons would go and hold a feast, the house of each on his day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

And it would be, when the days of the feast had gone round, that Job would send and set them apart as holy, and rise early in the morning and offer up burnt offerings according to the number of them all; for Job said, "Perhaps my sons have sinned and blessed God in their heart." Thus Job did all the days.
And the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before YHWH, and the accuser also came among them.
And YHWH said to the accuser, "From where do you come?" And the accuser answered YHWH and said, "From roving about on the earth and from walking up and down on it."
And YHWH said to the accuser, "Have you set your heart on my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth — a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil."
And the accuser answered YHWH and said, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?
Have you not yourself put a hedge about him and about his house and about all that is his, round about? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has spread out in the land.
But stretch out your hand now and touch all that is his — if he will not bless you to your face!"
And YHWH said to the accuser, "Behold, all that is his is in your hand; only against him do not stretch out your hand." And the accuser went out from the presence of YHWH.
And the day came when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the firstborn.
And a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were ploughing and the female donkeys grazing beside them,
and Sabeans fell upon them and took them, and the servants they struck with the mouth of the sword; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."

This one was still speaking when another came and said, "The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned among the sheep and the servants and consumed them; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."

This one was still speaking when another came and said, "Chaldeans formed three companies and made a raid on the camels and took them, and the servants they struck with the mouth of the sword; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
While this one was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the firstborn,
and behold, a great wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young people and they died; and I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
And Job arose and tore his robe and shaved his head, and he fell to the earth and bowed down.
And he said, "Naked I came out from my mother's womb, and naked I shall return there. YHWH gave and YHWH has taken; may the name of YHWH be blessed."
In all this Job did not sin, and he did not ascribe unseemliness to God.

job_2.t: And the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before YHWH, and the accuser also came among them to present himself before YHWH.
And YHWH said to the accuser, "Where is it you come from?" And the accuser answered YHWH and said, "From roving about on the earth and from walking up and down on it."

And YHWH said to the accuser, "Have you set your heart on my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth — a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil; and still he holds fast to his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without cause."
And the accuser answered YHWH and said, "Skin for skin! And all that a man has he will give for his life.
But stretch out your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh — if he will not bless you to your face!"
And YHWH said to the accuser, "Behold, he is in your hand; only preserve his life."
And the accuser went out from the presence of YHWH, and he struck Job with bad boils, from the sole of his foot to his scalp.
And he took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he was sitting in the midst of the ashes.
And his wife said to him, "Are you still holding fast to your integrity? Bless God and die."
And he said to her, "You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we accept the good from God and not accept the evil?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

And the three friends of Job heard of all this evil that had come upon him, and they came each one from his place — Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite — and they met together by appointment to come to show him sympathy and to comfort him.

And they lifted up their eyes from a distance and did not recognise him, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and they tore each his robe, and they sprinkled dust on their heads toward the heavens.
