And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word to him, for they saw that the pain was very great.

job_3.t: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
And Job answered and said:
Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, "A man has been conceived."
That day — let it be darkness; let God above not seek it out, and let no daylight shine upon it.
Let darkness and deep darkness reclaim it; let a cloud settle upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
That night — let gloom take it; let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of the months.
Behold, that night — let it be barren; let no cry of joy come into it.
Let those who curse the day damn it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.
Let the stars of its twilight grow dark; let it hope for light, and there be none, and let it not look on the eyelids of dawn —
because it did not shut the doors of my womb and hide trouble from my eyes.
Why did I not die from the womb, come out from the belly and expire?
Why did knees receive me, and why breasts, that I should suck?
For now I would be lying down and at peace; I would have slept — then there would be rest for me,
with kings and counsellors of the earth who rebuilt ruins for themselves,
or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
Or like a hidden miscarriage I would not have been, like infants who never saw light.
There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary of strength are at rest.
Together the prisoners are at ease; they do not hear the voice of a taskmaster.
Small and great are there, and a slave is free from his masters.
Why does he give light to the sufferer, and life to the bitter of being —
who long for death and it is not, and dig for it more than for hidden treasures;
those who rejoice to exultation, who are glad when they find the grave.
to a man whose way is hidden, and whom God has hedged in.
For before my bread my groaning comes, and my roarings pour out like water.
For a fear I feared, and it has come upon me; and what I dreaded has come to me.
I am not at ease and I am not at peace and I am not at rest, and turmoil has come.

job_4.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
If one ventures a word to you, will you be weary? But who can hold back from words?
Behold, you have instructed many, and slack hands you have strengthened.
Your words have raised up the stumbling, and bending knees you have made firm.
But now it comes to you and you are weary; it touches you and you are dismayed.
Is not your fear your confidence, your hope, and the integrity of your ways?
Remember, please: who that was innocent ever perished? And where were the upright destroyed?
As I have seen: those who plough iniquity and sow trouble reap it.
By the breath of God they perish, and by the wind of his anger they come to an end.
The roaring of the lion and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken.
The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the whelps of the lioness are scattered.
And to me a word was brought by stealth, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
In disquieting thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people,
fear met me, and trembling, and it made the multitude of my bones tremble.
And a spirit passed over my face; it made the hair of my flesh bristle.
It stood still, and I did not recognise its appearance; a form was before my eyes. Silence — and I heard a voice:
"Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be clean before his Maker?"
Behold, in his servants he does not trust, and against his messengers he charges error;
how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before a moth!
From morning to evening they are shattered; with no one setting it to heart, they perish for ever.
Is not their tent-cord pulled up within them? They die, and not in wisdom.

job_5.t: Call now — is there one who answers you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?
For vexation kills the fool, and jealousy slays the simple.
I myself have seen a fool taking root, and suddenly I cursed his habitation.
His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate, and there is no deliverer.
Whose harvest the hungry eats, and takes it even from among thorns, and a snare pants after their wealth.
For hardship does not come out from the dust, and trouble does not spring up from the ground;
for a human is born to trouble, and the sons of flame fly high.
But as for me, I would seek God, and to God I would set my case.
who does great things and there is no searching them out, wonders until there is no number;
who gives rain on the face of the earth and sends water on the face of the open fields;
to set the lowly on high, and mourners are lifted to safety.
who frustrates the plans of the shrewd, so that their hands achieve no success.
who catches the wise in their shrewdness, and the counsel of the twisted is hurried away.
By day they meet darkness, and as in the night they grope at noon.
And he saves the needy from the sword from their mouth, and from the hand of the strong.
And there is hope for the poor, and injustice shuts its mouth.
Behold, how blessed is the mortal whom God reproves! And do not reject the discipline of the Almighty,
for he causes pain and he binds up; he shatters, and his hands heal.
In six troubles he will deliver you, and in seven no harm will touch you.
In famine he will ransom you from death, and in war from the hands of the sword.
In the whip of the tongue you will be hidden, and you will not fear destruction when it comes.
At destruction and at hunger you will laugh, and of the wild animals of the earth you need not be afraid.
For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the wild animal of the field will be at peace with you.
And you will know that your tent is at peace, and you will inspect your fold and miss nothing.
And you will know that your offspring are many, and your descendants like the vegetation of the earth.
You will come to the grave in full vigour, as a shock of grain goes up in its season.
Behold, this we have searched out; so it is. Hear it, and know it for yourself.

job_6.t: And Job answered and said:
If only my vexation were surely weighed, and my calamity lifted in the balances together!
For now it is heavier than the sand of the seas; therefore my words have been rash.
For the arrows of the Almighty are with me; my spirit drinks their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
Does the wild donkey bray over grass, or the ox low over its fodder?
Is tasteless food eaten without salt? Or is there taste in the white of an egg?
My being refuses to touch them; they are like the sickness of my food.
Who will grant that my petition come, and that God give my hope?
That God would be willing and crush me, that he would loose his hand and cut me off!
And it would still be my comfort — and I would exult in anguish that does not spare — that I have not concealed the sayings of the Holy One.
What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?
Is my help not in me, and sound wisdom driven from me?
To the despairing, kindness from his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have acted treacherously like a wadi, like the channel of wadis that pass away —
which are dark with ice, in which the snow hides itself;
At the time they grow warm they are silenced; in its heat they are extinguished from their place.
The paths of their way twist about; they go up into the waste and perish.
The caravans of Tema looked; the travellers of Sheba hoped for them.
They were ashamed because they had been confident; they came to it and were disappointed.
For now you have become nothing; you see a terror and you are afraid.
Is it because I said, "Give to me," or "From your wealth make a payment for me,"
or "Deliver me from the hand of an adversary, and from the hand of the ruthless ransom me"?
Teach me, and I will be silent; and make me understand where I have erred.
How painful are upright sayings! But what does reproof from you prove?
Do you plan to reprove words, and the sayings of a despairing man for wind?
Even over an orphan you would cast lots, and you would bargain over your friend.
And now, be willing: turn to me, and to your faces — if I lie!
Turn back, please, let there be no injustice; turn back again — my righteousness is in it.
Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern calamities?

job_7.t: Is there not hard service for a mortal on earth, and are not his days like the days of a hired labourer?
like a slave who pants for shade, and like a hired labourer who waits for his wages —
so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of trouble have been apportioned to me.
If I lie down, I say, "When shall I rise?" and the evening drags on, and I am surfeited with tossing until twilight.
My flesh is clothed with maggots and clods of dust; my skin hardens and runs.
My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
Remember that my life is a breath; my eye will not return to see good.
The eye of one who sees me will not behold me; your eyes are on me, and I am not.
A cloud is spent and goes; so the one who goes down to Sheol does not come up.
He does not return again to his house, and his place does not recognise him again.
Also I — I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the distress of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my being.
Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a guard over me?
When I say, "My couch will comfort me, my bed will carry away my complaint,"
then you dismay me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
so that my being chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
I reject it — I shall not live for ever. Cease from me, for my days are a breath.
What is a mortal, that you make him great, and that you set your heart on him,
and visit him every morning, test him every moment?
How long will you not look away from me, nor let me alone till I swallow my spittle?
I have sinned — what do I do to you, watcher of humankind? Why have you set me as your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?
And why do you not lift away my transgression and cause my iniquity to pass? For now I shall lie down in the dust, and you will seek me, and I am not.

job_8.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long will you speak these things, and the sayings of your mouth be a mighty wind?
Does God pervert judgement, or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
If your children sinned against him, then he sent them away into the hand of their transgression.
If you yourself will seek God and plead for favour from the Almighty,
if you are pure and upright, surely now he will rouse himself for you and restore the abode of your righteousness.
And your beginning will be small, and your latter end will grow very great.
For ask, please, of a former generation, and give attention to the searching of their fathers.
For we are of yesterday and know nothing, for our days on earth are a shadow.
Will they not teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their heart?
Does papyrus grow tall without a marsh? Does reed-grass grow without water?
While it is still in its greenness, not plucked, it dries up before any grass.
Such are the paths of all who forget God, and the hope of the godless perishes,
whose confidence is fragile, and whose trust is a spider's house.
He leans on his house, and it does not stand; he takes hold of it, and it does not endure.
He is a fresh plant before the sun, and over his garden his shoot goes out.
His roots are interwoven over a heap; he looks on a house of stones.
If one swallows him up from his place, then it denies him: "I have not seen you."
See, that is the joy of his way, and from the dust others spring up.
See, God does not reject a blameless man, and does not take hold of the hand of evildoers.
until he fills your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.

job_9.t: And Job answered and said:
Truly I know that it is so; but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
If one desired to contend with him, he could not answer him one time in a thousand.
Wise of heart and mighty in strength — who has hardened himself against him and remained whole?
who removes mountains and they do not know it, who overturns them in his anger;
who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars tremble;
who speaks to the sun and it does not rise, and who seals up the stars;
who alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the high places of the Sea;
who makes the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;
who does great things beyond searching out, and wonders beyond number.
See, he passes by me and I do not see him; he moves on and I do not perceive him.
See, he snatches away — who can turn him back? Who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
God does not turn back his anger; beneath him the helpers of Rahab lay prostrate.
How much less can I answer him, choose my words with him!
whom, though I were righteous, I could not answer; to my judge I would plead for favour.
If I called and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice —
he who crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He does not let me bring back my breath, but surfeits me with bitterness.
If it is a matter of strength — he is the mighty one! And if of judgement — who will summon me?
Though I were righteous, my own mouth would condemn me; blameless as I am, it would declare me perverse.
I am blameless. I do not know myself. I reject my life.
It is all one; therefore I say: the blameless and the wicked he brings to an end.
If a scourge kills suddenly, he mocks at the despair of the innocent.
A land is given into the hand of a wicked man; he covers the faces of its judges. If not — then who is it?
And my days are swifter than a runner; they flee, they have not seen good.
They have passed on with ships of reed, like an eagle swooping on food.
If I say, "I will forget my complaint, I will let go my face and be cheerful,"
I dread all my pains; I know that you will not hold me innocent.
I shall be counted guilty — why then should I labour in vain?
If I washed myself in snow water and cleansed my hands with lye,
then you would plunge me into the pit, and my own clothes would abhor me.
For he is not a man like me, that I should answer him, that we should come together into judgement.
There is no arbiter between us who might lay his hand on the two of us.
Let him remove his rod from upon me, and let his terror not dismay me.
Then I would speak and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.

job_10.t: My being loathes my life; I will let loose my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my being.
I will say to God: Do not condemn me; make known to me why you contend with me.
Is it good for you that you should oppress, that you should reject the labour of your hands and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
Are your days like the days of a mortal, or your years like the days of a man,
that you seek out my iniquity and search for my sin,
though you know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverer from your hand?
Your hands shaped me and made me, all around — and you swallow me up.
Remember, please, that you made me like clay — and will you return me to dust?
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knitted me together with bones and sinews.
Life and steadfast love you have done with me, and your care has kept my spirit.
Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was with you.
If I sinned, then you would watch me, and you would not acquit me of my iniquity.
If I am guilty — woe to me! And if I am in the right, I cannot lift my head, sated with shame and looking on my affliction.
And it rises up — like a lion you hunt me, and you turn back and show yourself marvellous against me.
You renew your witnesses before me and increase your vexation with me; changes and an army are with me.
And why did you bring me out from the womb? I would have expired, and no eye would have seen me.
As though I had not been, I would have been; from the womb I would have been carried to the grave.
Are not my days few? Then cease, and set yourself away from me, that I may be cheerful a little,
before I go and do not return, to the land of darkness and deep darkness,
a land of gloom like darkness, of deep darkness and without order, and it shines like darkness.

job_11.t: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Shall a multitude of words not be answered? And shall a man of lips be justified?
Shall your empty talk silence men? And shall you mock with no one to shame you?
For you have said, "My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes."
But who will grant that God would speak and open his lips with you!
and tell you the secrets of wisdom, for sound wisdom is double — and know that God causes some of your iniquity to be forgotten for you.
Can you find out the searching of God? Can you find out to the limit of the Almighty?
Heights of the heavens — what can you do? Deeper than Sheol — what can you know?
Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
If he passes by and shuts up and summons an assembly, who can turn him back?
For he knows men of falsehood; he sees iniquity and does not consider it.
And a hollow man will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born a human.
If you yourself have directed your heart and spread out your palms to him,
if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice dwell in your tents,
then you will lift up your face without blemish, and you will be firmly cast and not fear.
For you will forget trouble; like waters that have passed by you will remember it.
And your lifetime will rise higher than noon; though it be dark, it will be like the morning.
And you will be secure, for there is hope; and you will search about and lie down in safety.
And you will lie down with no one making you afraid, and many will entreat your face.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will perish from them, and their hope is the breathing out of life.

job_12.t: And Job answered and said:
Truly you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
I also have a heart like yours; I do not fall short of you; and with whom are things like these not?
A laughingstock to his friend I am — one who called on God and he answered him — a laughingstock, the righteous, the blameless.
Contempt for disaster, in the thought of one at ease; a push for those whose foot slips.
The tents of destroyers are at peace, and those who provoke God have security, to whoever brings a god in his hand.
But ask, please, the animals, and let them teach you, and the birds of the heavens, and let them tell you;
or complain to the earth, and let it teach you, and let the fish of the sea recount to you.
Who among all these does not know that the hand of YHWH has done this?
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all human flesh.
Does not the ear test words, and the palate taste food for itself?
With the aged is wisdom, and length of days is understanding.
With him are wisdom and might; to him belong counsel and understanding.
See, he tears down and it is not rebuilt; he shuts a man in and it is not opened.
See, he holds back the waters and they dry up; and he sends them out and they overturn the earth.
With him are strength and sound wisdom; to him belong the one who errs and the one who leads astray.
He leads counsellors away stripped, and judges he makes fools.
He loosens the bond of kings and binds a loincloth on their loins.
He leads priests away stripped, and the long-established he overthrows.
He removes the lip of the trusted, and takes away the discernment of elders.
He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the mighty.
He uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings deep darkness out to the light.
He makes nations great and destroys them; he spreads nations out and leads them away.
He removes the heart of the heads of the people of the earth, and makes them wander in a waste with no path.
They grope in darkness with no light, and he makes them wander like a drunkard.

job_13.t: See, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard and understood it.
As you know, I also know; I do not fall short of you.
But I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case with God.
But you are smearers of falsehood; you are all worthless physicians.
Who will grant that you would be altogether silent! And it would become wisdom for you.
Hear now my argument, and attend to the contentions of my lips.
Will you speak unrighteousness for God, and speak deceit for him?
Will you lift up his face? Will you contend for God?
Would it be good if he examined you? Or as one deceives a mortal, will you deceive him?
He will surely rebuke you if in secret you lift up faces.
Will not his majesty terrify you, and his dread fall upon you?
Your memorials are proverbs of ashes; your defences are defences of clay.
Be silent from me, and let me speak, and let come upon me what will.
Why do I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my palm?
See, he will kill me; in him I will hope — yet I will argue my ways to his face.
This also will be my deliverance, that a godless man will not come before him.
Listen carefully to my speech, and let my declaration be in your ears.
See now, I have set out my case; I know that I am the one in the right.
Who is he that will contend with me? For then I would be silent and expire.
Only two things do not do to me; then I will not hide from your face.
Put your hand far from upon me, and let your dread not terrify me.
Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and answer me.
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make known to me my transgression and my sin.
Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
Will you terrify a driven leaf and pursue dry chaff?
For you write bitter things against me and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
And you put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; on the roots of my feet you cut a mark.
And he wears out like something rotten, like a garment that a moth has eaten.

job_14.t: A human, born of a woman, is short of days and surfeited with turmoil.
Like a flower he comes out and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not stand.
Yet on such a one you open your eye, and you bring me into judgement with you.
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one.
If his days are determined, the number of his months is with you; you have made his limits, and he cannot pass.
look away from him and let him cease, until he takes pleasure in his day like a hired labourer.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoot will not fail.
Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the dust,
at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a plant.
But a man dies and lies powerless; a human expires — and where is he?
Waters disappear from the sea, and a river dries up and is parched;
so a man lies down and does not rise; till the heavens are no more they will not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.
Who will grant that you would hide me in Sheol, conceal me until your anger turns back, set me a limit and remember me!
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my service I would wait, until my relief should come.
You would call and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
For then you would count my steps; you would not watch over my sin.
My transgression would be sealed up in a bag, and you would smear over my iniquity.
But a falling mountain crumbles away, and a rock moves from its place;
waters wear away stones; their overflowings wash away the dust of the earth — and you destroy the hope of a mortal.
You overpower him for ever and he goes; you change his face and send him away.
His sons are honoured, and he does not know; they are brought low, and he does not perceive it of them.
Only his own flesh upon him is in pain, and his own being upon him mourns.

job_15.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Does a wise man answer with knowledge of wind and fill his belly with the east wind?
arguing with a word that is of no use, and with words by which he does not profit?
Indeed, you yourself annul the fear of God and diminish meditation before God.
For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the shrewd.
Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; and your own lips testify against you.
Were you born the first human? Were you brought forth before the hills?
Do you listen in the council of God and restrain wisdom to yourself?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us?
Both the grey-haired and the aged are among us, older in days than your father.
Are the consolations of God too little for you, and a word spoken gently with you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,
that you turn your spirit against God and bring out such words from your mouth?
What is a mortal, that he should be pure, and one born of a woman, that he should be in the right?
See, in his holy ones he does not trust, and the heavens are not pure in his eyes;
how much less one abhorrent and corrupt, a man who drinks unrighteousness like water!
I will declare to you — listen to me — and what I have seen I will recount:
what wise men have told and have not hidden, from their fathers,
to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them:
All the days of the wicked he writhes, and the number of years is stored up for the ruthless.
The sound of dreads is in his ears; in peace a destroyer comes upon him.
He does not believe he will return from darkness, and he is watched for by the sword.
He wanders for bread — where is it? He knows that a day of darkness is prepared at his hand.
Anxiety and distress terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle.
For he stretched out his hand against God and behaved proudly against the Almighty;
he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of his shields.
For he has covered his face with his fat and made a bulge upon his loins.
And he dwelt in destroyed cities, houses where no one lives, which are destined to become heaps.
He will not be rich, and his wealth will not endure, and their possessions will not stretch out to the earth.
He will not depart from darkness; a flame will dry up his shoot, and he will depart by the breath of his mouth.
Let him not trust in worthlessness — he is deceived; for worthlessness will be his recompense.
It will be completed before his day, and his palm branch will not be green.
He will shake off his unripe grapes like a vine, and cast off his blossom like an olive tree.
For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
They conceive trouble and give birth to iniquity, and their belly prepares deceit.

job_16.t: And Job answered and said:
I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.
Is there an end to words of wind? Or what provokes you that you answer?
I also could speak like you, if your being were in place of my being; I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.
I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the condolence of my lips would restrain your pain.
If I speak, my pain is not restrained; and if I cease, what goes from me?
Only now he has made me weary; you have devastated all my company.
And you have seized me — it has become a witness; and my leanness has risen up against me; it testifies to my face.
His anger has torn me and assailed me; he has gnashed his teeth at me; my adversary sharpens his eyes at me.
They have opened wide their mouth against me; in scorn they have struck my cheeks; together they mass themselves against me.
God delivers me up to an unjust one and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces; and he set me up as his target.
His archers surround me; he splits my kidneys and does not spare; he pours out my gall to the ground.
He breaks through me, breach upon breach; he runs at me like a warrior.
I have sewed sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn in the dust.
My face is reddened from weeping, and on my eyelids is deep darkness,
though there is no violence in my hands and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover my blood, and let there be no place for my outcry!
Even now, see — my witness is in the heavens, and the one who testifies for me is in the heights.
My friends scorn me; my eye pours out tears to God.
that he might argue for a man with God, and a son of humankind for his companion.
For years of number will come, and I shall go the way from which I do not return.

job_17.t: My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; graves are mine.
Surely mockeries are with me, and on their rebellion my eye must lodge.
Lay down a pledge for me with yourself! Who else is there that will strike hands with me?
For you have kept their heart from understanding; therefore you will not exalt them.
He who denounces his friends for a share — the eyes of his children will fail.
And he has set me as a byword of peoples, and I am one spat upon to the face.
And my eye has grown dim from vexation, and all my members are like a shadow.
Upright men are appalled at this, and the innocent rouses himself against the godless.
And the righteous holds to his way, and the clean of hands increases in strength.
But all of you — turn back and come now! And I shall not find a wise man among you.
My days have passed; my plans are torn apart, the possessions of my heart.
They make night into day; light is near, from before darkness.
If I hope for Sheol as my house, I have spread out my bed in the darkness;
to the pit I have called, "You are my father"; "My mother and my sister," to the maggot —
where then is my hope? And my hope — who will see it?
Will they go down to the bars of Sheol? Shall we descend together to the dust?

job_18.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long until you make an end of words? Understand, and afterwards we will speak.
Why are we counted as cattle, reckoned stupid in your eyes?
You who tear yourself in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake, and a rock move from its place?
Yes, the light of the wicked is extinguished, and the flame of his fire does not shine.
The light grows dark in his tent, and his lamp above him is extinguished.
The steps of his vigour are cramped, and his own counsel throws him down.
For he is sent into a net by his own feet, and he walks about on a mesh.
A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare takes hold on him.
His rope is hidden in the ground, and his trap on the path.
All around, sudden terrors terrify him and scatter him at his feet.
His strength is hungry, and disaster is ready for his stumbling.
It consumes the parts of his skin; the firstborn of death consumes his parts.
His trust is torn away from his tent, and it marches him to the king of terrors.
There dwells in his tent what is not his; sulphur is scattered over his habitation.
Beneath, his roots are dried up, and above, his branch withers.
His memory perishes from the earth, and he has no name on the face of the street.
They drive him from light into darkness and chase him from the world.
He has no offspring and no posterity among his people, and no survivor in his dwellings.
At his day those after are appalled, and those before take hold of a shudder.
Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous, and this is the place of one who does not know God.

job_19.t: And Job answered and said:
How long will you torment my being and crush me with words?
These ten times you have insulted me; you are not ashamed to wrong me.
And even if truly I have erred, my error lodges with me.
If truly you magnify yourselves against me and argue my disgrace against me,
know then that God has wronged me and has closed his net around me.
See, I cry out "Violence!" and am not answered; I cry for help, and there is no judgement.
He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and on my paths he puts darkness.
He has stripped my honour from me and removed the crown from my head.
He tears me down all around, and I am gone; and he has uprooted my hope like a tree.
And he has kindled his anger against me and counted me to him as his foes.
Together his troops come, and they cast up their way against me, and they encamp around my tent.
He has put my brothers far from me, and my acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.
My kindred have ceased, and those who knew me have forgotten me.
The guests of my house and my slave women count me a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
I call my servant and he does not answer; with my own mouth I must plead with him.
My breath is strange to my wife, and I am repulsive to the sons of my womb.
Even young boys despise me; I rise up and they speak against me.
All the men of my council abhor me, and those whom I loved have turned against me.
My bone clings to my skin and to my flesh, and I have escaped with the skin of my teeth.
Show me favour, show me favour, you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you pursue me like God and are not satisfied with my flesh?
Who will grant then that my words were written down! Who will grant that they were inscribed in a scroll!
with an iron stylus and lead, for ever engraved in the rock!
And I myself know that my redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the dust.
And after my skin — they have struck off this — yet from my flesh I shall see God,
whom I myself shall see for myself, and my own eyes shall see, and not a stranger. My kidneys are consumed within me.
If you say, "How shall we pursue him, and the root of the matter is found in me" —
be afraid for yourselves of the sword, for wrath brings the iniquities of the sword, so that you may know that there is a judgement.

job_20.t: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Therefore my disquieting thoughts make me answer, and because of my agitation within me.
I hear the correction of my insult, and a spirit out of my understanding answers me.
Do you know this from of old, from when humankind was set upon the earth,
that the exulting of the wicked is brief, and the gladness of the godless is for a moment?
Though his loftiness goes up to the heavens and his head reaches to the cloud,
like his own dung he perishes for ever; those who saw him will say, "Where is he?"
Like a dream he flies away and they do not find him; he is chased away like a vision of the night.
An eye caught sight of him and does so no more, and his place beholds him no longer.
His children will seek the favour of the poor, and his own hands will give back his wealth.
His bones were full of his youthful vigour, and it will lie down with him on the dust.
Though evil is sweet in his mouth, and he hides it under his tongue,
though he spares it and does not let it go, and holds it back in the midst of his palate,
his food is turned in his inward parts; it is the venom of cobras within him.
He swallows wealth and vomits it up; God drives it out of his belly.
He sucks the poison of cobras; the tongue of a viper kills him.
He will not look on the streams, the rivers, the wadis of honey and curds.
He gives back his gain and does not swallow it; according to the wealth of his trading, and he will not rejoice.
For he crushed and abandoned the poor; he seized a house he did not build.
For he knew no quiet in his belly; with what he desired he will not escape.
There is no survivor of his devouring; therefore his prosperity will not endure.
In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress will be his; every hand of the sufferer will come upon him.
Let it be, to fill his belly, that he sends against him the burning of his anger and rains it on him as his food.
He will flee from an iron weapon; a bronze bow will pierce him through.
He draws it out and it comes from his back, and the glittering point from his gall; terrors come upon him.
All darkness is hidden for his treasures; a fire not fanned will consume him; it will go badly for a survivor in his tent.
The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
The produce of his house will depart, things poured away on the day of his anger.
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance decreed for him from God.

job_21.t: And Job answered and said:
Listen carefully to my speech, and let this be your consolations.
Bear with me, and I myself will speak; and after I have spoken, you may mock.
Is my complaint to a human? And if so, why should my spirit not be short?
Turn to me and be appalled, and lay a hand on a mouth.
And when I remember, I am dismayed, and shuddering seizes my flesh.
Why do the wicked live, grow old, and also grow mighty in strength?
Their offspring is established before them, with them, and their descendants before their eyes.
Their houses are at peace, without fear, and the rod of God is not upon them.
His bull breeds and does not fail; his cow calves and does not miscarry.
They send out their young boys like a flock, and their children leap about.
They lift up voice with tambourine and lyre and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
They complete their days in prosperity, and in a moment they go down to Sheol.
And they say to God, "Depart from us; we do not desire the knowledge of your ways."
"What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what do we gain if we entreat him?"
See, their prosperity is not in their own hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, and their calamity comes upon them, and he apportions pains in his anger?
Are they like straw before a wind, and like chaff that a storm-wind has stolen?
"God stores up his wickedness for his children" — let him repay him, and let him know it!
Let his own eyes see his destruction, and let him drink from the rage of the Almighty.
For what is his pleasure in his household after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
Shall anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges those on high?
This one dies in the full strength of his completeness, wholly at ease and quiet.
His body is full of milk, and the marrow of his bones is watered.
And this one dies with a bitter being, and has not eaten of the good.
Together they lie down on the dust, and the maggot covers them.
See, I know your thoughts, and the schemes you do violence to me with.
For you say, "Where is the house of the noble, and where the tent, the dwellings of the wicked?"
Have you not asked those who pass along the road? And do you not recognise their signs —
that the evil man is spared in a day of calamity, that they are brought out in a day of wrath?
Who declares his way to his face? And what he has done — who repays him?
And he is borne to the graves, and over a tomb someone keeps watch.
The clods of the wadi are sweet to him; and after him every human draws on, and before him there is no number.
And how will you comfort me with vapour? And of your answers there remains treachery.

job_22.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Can a man be of use to God? Surely a wise man is of use to himself.
Is it a pleasure to the Almighty that you are in the right? Or is it gain that you make your ways blameless?
Is it for your fear of him that he reproves you and goes with you into judgement?
Is not your evil great, and is there no end to your iniquities?
For you have taken pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the garments of the naked.
You have given no water to the weary to drink, and from the hungry you have withheld bread.
And the man of the arm — the land is his, and the one lifted of face dwells in it.
You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless are crushed.
Therefore snares are all around you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of waters covers you.
Is not God the height of the heavens? And see the top of the stars, how high they are!
And you say, "What does God know? Can he judge through thick darkness?"
"Clouds are a hiding place for him and he does not see, and he walks about on the circle of the heavens."
Will you keep the ancient path that men of iniquity have trodden,
who were snatched away and it was not their time, whose foundation was poured away as a river?
who said to God, "Depart from us!" and "What can the Almighty do to them?"
Yet he filled their houses with good things — and the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
The righteous see it and rejoice, and the innocent mocks at them:
"Surely our adversary is destroyed, and fire has consumed what was left of them."
Be reconciled with him now and be at peace; by them good will come to you.
Accept law from his mouth, and put his sayings in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty you will be built up; you will put injustice far from your tent.
And lay gold on the dust, and the gold of Ophir among the rocks of the wadis,
and the Almighty will be your gold and silver in heaps for you.
For then you will take delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
You will pray to him and he will hear you, and you will pay your vows.
And you will decree a matter and it will be established for you, and on your ways light will shine.
When they are brought low, you will say, "Up!" and he saves the lowly of eyes.
He will deliver the one who is not innocent, and he will be delivered by the purity of your hands.

job_23.t: Even today my complaint is rebellion; my hand is heavy upon my groaning.
Who will grant that I knew where I might find him, that I might come to his dwelling place!
I would set my case in order before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would know the words he would answer me and understand what he would say to me.
Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No — surely he would give heed to me.
There an upright man would reason with him, and I would be delivered for ever from my judge.
See, I go forward and he is not there, and backward, and I do not perceive him;
on the left when he acts, and I do not see him; he turns to the right, and I do not see him.
For he knows the way with me; he has tested me — I shall come out like gold.
My foot has held to his step; I have kept his way and not turned aside.
From the commandment of his lips I have not departed; more than my portion I have treasured up the sayings of his mouth.
But he is at one, and who can turn him back? And what his being desires, he does.
For he performs what is decreed for me, and many such things are with him.
Therefore I am terrified before him; I consider, and I am in dread of him.
And God has made my heart faint, and the Almighty has terrified me;
for I have not been destroyed before the darkness, and he has covered thick gloom from my face.

job_24.t: Why are times not stored up by the Almighty, and why do those who know him not see his days?
They move boundaries; they seize a flock and pasture it.
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow's ox in pledge.
They thrust the needy off the road; the poor of the earth hide themselves together.
See, like wild donkeys in the wilderness they go out to their work, seeking for prey; the desert plain yields him food for the children.
In the field they harvest his fodder, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
Naked they spend the night, without clothing, and they have no covering in the cold.
From the rain of the mountains they are wet, and for lack of shelter they embrace the rock.
They tear the fatherless from the breast, and they take a pledge from the poor.
Naked they go about, without clothing, and hungry they carry the sheaf.
Between their walls they press out oil; they tread the winepresses and are thirsty.
From the city men groan, and the throat of the fatally wounded cries for help; and God does not set it down as unseemly.
They are among those who rebel against the light; they do not recognise its ways and do not dwell in its paths.
At the light the murderer rises; he kills the poor and the needy, and in the night he is like a thief.
And the eye of the adulterer watches for twilight, saying, "No eye will see me," and he puts a covering on his face.
He digs through houses in the darkness; by day they shut themselves up; they do not know the light.
For morning is together deep darkness to them; for he is acquainted with the terrors of deep darkness.
He is swift on the face of the waters; their portion in the land is cursed; he does not turn toward the way of the vineyards.
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; Sheol, those who have sinned.
The womb forgets him; the maggot feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.
He feeds on the barren woman who does not bear, and does no good to the widow.
And he drags off the mighty by his power; he rises, and no one trusts in life.
He gives him security, and he supports himself; and his eyes are on their ways.
They are exalted a little, and he is not; and they are brought low; like everyone they are gathered in, and like the head of an ear of grain they wither.
And if it is not so, who will prove me a liar and make my speech nothing?

job_25.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
Dominion and dread are with him; he makes peace in his heights.
Is there a number to his troops? And on whom does his light not rise?
And how can a mortal be in the right before God? And how can one born of a woman be pure?
See, even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes;
how much less a mortal, a maggot, and a son of humankind, a worm!

job_26.t: How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm without strength!
How you have counselled one without wisdom, and made known sound wisdom in abundance!
With whom have you told words, and whose breath has gone out from you?
The shades are made to writhe beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
Sheol is naked before him, and Abaddon has no covering.
He stretches out the north over emptiness; he hangs the earth on nothing.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud is not split open beneath them.
He covers the face of the throne; he spreads his cloud over it.
He has drawn a circle as a limit on the face of the waters, to the boundary of light with darkness.
The pillars of the heavens shake and are astonished at his rebuke.
By his power he stirred up the sea, and by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
By his wind the heavens were made fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
See, these are the ends of his ways, and what a whisper of a word we hear in him! And the thunder of his might — who can understand?

job_27.t: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
As God lives, who has taken away my judgement, and the Almighty, who has made my being bitter —
as long as my breath is in me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak injustice, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
Far be it from me that I should declare you in the right! Until I expire I will not put away my integrity from me.
I have kept hold of my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach any of my days.
May my enemy be as the wicked, and the one who rises against me as the unrighteous.
For what is the hope of the godless when he cuts him off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at every time?
I will instruct you concerning the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I will not hide.
See, all of you have seen it yourselves; and why then do you become utterly vain?
This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the ruthless, which they receive from the Almighty:
If his children increase, it is for the sword, and his descendants will not be satisfied with bread.
His survivors will be buried by the plague, and his widows will not weep.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and prepares clothing like clay,
he prepares it, and the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
He has built his house like a moth, and like a shelter that a watchman has made.
Rich he lies down, and he will not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and he is not.
Terrors overtake him like waters; by night a storm-wind steals him away.
The east wind lifts him up and he goes; it whirls him away from his place.
It hurls itself at him and does not spare; from its hand he flees headlong.
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its place.

job_28.t: For there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold that they purge.
Iron is taken from the dust, and stone is poured out as copper.
He puts an end to darkness, and to every limit he searches out the stone of gloom and deep darkness.
He breaks open a shaft away from where anyone sojourns, forgotten by the foot; they dangle far from human beings, they swing.
The earth — from it comes food, and beneath it, it is turned over as by fire.
Its stones are the place of sapphire, and it has dust of gold.
A path — no bird of prey knows it, and the eye of the falcon has not caught sight of it.
The proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it.
He puts out his hand against the flint; he overturns mountains from the root.
In the rocks he splits open channels, and his eye sees every precious thing.
He binds up the streams from weeping, and what is hidden he brings out to light.
But wisdom — from where will it be found? And where is this, the place of understanding?
A human does not know its valuation, and it is not found in the land of the living.
The deep says, "It is not in me," and the sea says, "It is not with me."
Fine gold cannot be given for it, and silver cannot be weighed out as its price.
It cannot be paid for with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or sapphire.
Gold and glass cannot be set beside it, and a vessel of pure gold is not its exchange.
Coral and crystal are not to be mentioned, and the price of wisdom is more than pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot be set beside it; it cannot be paid for with pure gold.
And wisdom — from where does it come? And where is this, the place of understanding?
It is concealed from the eyes of every living thing and hidden from the birds of the heavens.
Abaddon and Death say, "With our ears we have heard a report of it."
God understands its way, and he knows its place.
For he looks to the ends of the earth; he sees under all the heavens,
to make a weight for the wind and to measure out the waters by measure;
when he made a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt,
then he saw it and recounted it; he established it and also searched it out.
And he said to humankind: "See, the fear of the Lord — that is wisdom, and to turn from evil is understanding."

job_29.t: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
Who will grant me to be as in the months of long ago, as in the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
as I was in the days of my prime, when the intimacy of God was over my tent;
when the Almighty was still with me, my young men around me;
when my steps were bathed in curds, and the rock poured out streams of oil beside me;
when I went out to the gate at the town, when I prepared my seat in the public square;
the young men saw me and hid themselves, and the aged rose and stood;
chiefs restrained their words and laid a hand on their mouth;
the voice of nobles was hidden, and their tongue stuck to their palate;
for the ear heard and called me blessed, and the eye saw and bore witness to me;
for I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no helper.
The blessing of one about to perish came upon me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
I put on righteousness and it clothed me; my judgement was like a robe and a turban.
I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame I was.
I was a father to the needy, and the case of one I did not know I searched out.
And I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and made him drop the prey from his teeth.
And I said, "I shall expire with my nest, and I shall multiply days like the sand."
My root is open to the water, and dew lodges on my branch.
My honour is fresh with me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.
To me they listened and waited, and were silent for my counsel.
After my word they did not speak again, and my speech dropped upon them.
And they waited for me as for the rain, and opened their mouth wide as for the spring rain.
I laughed to them — they did not believe it — and the light of my face they did not cast down.
I chose their way and sat as chief, and I dwelt like a king among the troop, like one who comforts mourners.

job_30.t: But now they laugh at me, those younger than I in days, whose fathers I refused to set with the dogs of my flock.
Even the strength of their hands — what was it to me? Vigour had perished from them.
In want and hunger, barren, gnawing the dry ground, by night a waste and desolation;
who pluck mallow among the bushes, and the root of broom plants is their food.
They are driven out from the community; people shout after them as after a thief.
They dwell in the gullies of the wadis, in holes of the ground and of rocks.
Among the bushes they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.
Sons of a fool, and sons of no name, they were whipped out of the land.
And now I have become their taunt-song, and I am a byword to them.
They abhor me, they keep far from me, and from my face they have not withheld spittle.
For he has loosened my cord and afflicted me, and they have thrown off the bridle before me.
On the right hand a brood rises; they send away my feet and cast up against me their paths of disaster.
They have torn up my pathway; they profit from my destruction; no one helps them.
They come as through a wide breach; under the ruin they roll themselves on.
Terrors are turned upon me; my dignity is pursued like the wind, and my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
And now my being is poured out upon me; days of affliction have seized me.
By night my bones are pierced from upon me, and my gnawing pains do not rest.
With great strength my clothing is disfigured; it girds me like the collar of my tunic.
He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry for help to you, and you do not answer me; I stand, and you look hard at me.
You have turned cruel to me; with the might of your hand you are hostile to me.
You lift me up to the wind, you make me ride it, and you dissolve me in the storm.
For I know you will bring me back to death, and to the house of appointed meeting for all the living.
Surely one does not stretch out a hand against a ruin, or in his disaster is there a cry for help from them?
Did I not weep for the one whose day was hard? Was my being not grieved for the needy?
For I waited for good, and evil came; and I hoped for light, and darkness came.
My inward parts boil and are not still; days of affliction have confronted me.
I go about darkened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to daughters of the ostrich.
My skin has turned black upon me, and my bone burns from the heat.
And my lyre has become mourning, and my flute the sound of weepers.

job_31.t: I cut a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look closely at a virgin?
And what is the portion of God from above, and the inheritance of the Almighty from the heights?
Is it not calamity for the unrighteous, and misfortune for those who do iniquity?
Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?
If I have walked with falsehood and my foot has hurried to deceit —
let him weigh me in balances of righteousness, and let God acknowledge my integrity!
If my step has turned aside from the way, and my heart has walked after my eyes, and a blemish has stuck to my hands —
let me sow and another eat, and let my produce be rooted up!
If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbour's door —
let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her!
For that is depravity, and that is an iniquity for the judges;
for it is a fire that devours to Abaddon and would root up all my produce.
If I have rejected the cause of my male servant or my slave woman when they contended with me —
then what shall I do when God arises? And when he visits, what shall I answer him?
Did not the one who made me in the belly make him, and did not one prepare us in the womb?
If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or caused the eyes of a widow to fail,
or eaten my morsel alone and the fatherless has not eaten of it —
for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother's womb I guided her —
if I have seen one perishing for lack of clothing, and no covering for the needy,
if his loins have not blessed me, and he was not warmed with the fleece of my lambs —
if I have raised my hand against the fatherless because I saw my help in the gate —
let my shoulder fall from its socket, and let my arm be broken from its joint!
For the calamity of God was a dread to me, and before his majesty I could do nothing.
If I have made gold my confidence and said to pure gold, "My security" —
if I rejoiced because my wealth was great and because my hand had found much —
if I saw the light when it shone, or the moon moving in splendour,
and my heart was secretly enticed, and my hand kissed my mouth —
that too would be an iniquity calling for judgement, for I would have denied God above.
If I rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me and roused myself when calamity found him —
and I did not let my palate sin by asking for his life with a curse —
if the men of my tent have not said, "Who can find one not satisfied from his meat?" —
the sojourner did not spend the night in the street; I opened my doors to the road —
If I have covered my transgressions like humans, hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
because I feared a great multitude and the contempt of clans dismayed me, so that I was silent and did not go out of the door —
Who will grant me one who hears me! Here is my mark — let the Almighty answer me! — and the document my adversary at law has written.
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it on me as a crown.
I would tell him the number of my steps; like a prince I would approach him.
If my land has cried out against me, and its furrows have wept together,
if I have eaten its produce without payment and caused the life of its owners to breathe out —
let thorns come forth instead of wheat, and foul weeds instead of barley! The words of Job are finished.

job_32.t: And these three men ceased from answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
And the anger of Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned. Against Job his anger burned, because he justified himself rather than God.
And against his three friends his anger burned, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
And Elihu had waited for Job with words, because they were older than he in days.
And Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burned.
And Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite answered and said: I am young in days and you are aged; therefore I was anxious and afraid to tell you my knowledge.
I said, "Let days speak, and let many years make wisdom known."
But it is a spirit in a mortal, and the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.
It is not the many who are wise, nor the aged who understand judgement.
Therefore I say, "Listen to me; I too will tell my knowledge."
See, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your understandings while you searched out what to say.
And I gave you my attention, and see, there was no one to refute Job, none of you answering his sayings.
Lest you say, "We have found wisdom; God will drive him off, not a human" —
And he has not arranged words against me, and with your sayings I will not answer him.
They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have moved away from them.
And shall I wait, because they do not speak, because they have stood and answer no more?
I will answer, I too, my portion; I too will tell my knowledge.
For I am full of words; the spirit of my belly constrains me.
See, my belly is like wine that is not opened; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.
Let me speak, that it may be relieved for me; let me open my lips and answer.
Let me not lift up the face of anyone, and let me not flatter any human;
for I do not know how to flatter; in a little while my Maker would carry me away.

job_33.t: But now, Job, hear my speech, and give ear to all my words.
See now, I have opened my mouth; my tongue speaks in my palate.
My sayings are the uprightness of my heart, and my lips speak knowledge purely.
The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
If you can, answer me; set your case in order before me; take your stand.
See, I am toward God as your own mouth; I too was nipped off from clay.
See, my dread will not terrify you, and my pressure will not be heavy upon you.
Surely you have spoken in my ears, and I have heard the sound of your words:
"I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no iniquity in me.
See, he finds occasions against me; he considers me his enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths."
See, in this you are not in the right — I will answer you — for God is greater than a mortal.
Why have you contended against him, that he does not answer any of his words?
For God speaks in one way, and in two, though no one perceives it.
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people, in slumberings upon the bed,
then he uncovers the ear of people and seals their instruction,
to turn a human aside from his deed and to cover pride from a man;
he keeps back his being from the pit, and his life from passing away by the weapon.
And he is chastened with pain on his bed, and the multitude of his bones is constant;
and his life loathes bread, and his being the food of desire.
His flesh wastes away from sight, and his bones that were not seen are laid bare.
And his being draws near to the pit, and his life to those who bring death.
If there is beside him a messenger, a mediator, one of a thousand, to declare to a human what is right for him,
then he shows him favour and says, "Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom" —
let his flesh grow fresher than a boy's; let him return to the days of his youth.
He prays to God and he accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to a mortal his righteousness.
He looks upon people and says, "I have sinned and perverted what was upright, and it was not repaid to me."
He has ransomed my being from passing into the pit, and my life shall look on the light.
See, all these things God does, twice, three times, with a man,
to bring back his being from the pit, to be lighted with the light of the living.
Pay attention, Job; listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If there are words, answer me; speak, for I desire to declare you in the right.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

job_34.t: And Elihu answered and said:
Hear my words, you wise men, and give ear to me, you who know;
for the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
Let us choose judgement for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.
For Job has said, "I am in the right, and God has taken away my judgement."
"Concerning my judgement, should I lie? My arrow is incurable, without transgression."
What man is like Job, who drinks mockery like water,
and travels in company with doers of iniquity and walks with men of wickedness?
For he has said, "It profits a man nothing to delight himself with God."
Therefore, men of heart, hear me: far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do unrighteousness!
For the work of a human he repays to him, and according to a man's way he makes it find him.
Yes, truly, God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert judgement.
Who assigned the earth to him? And who appointed the whole world?
If he set his heart upon him, and gathered his spirit and his breath to himself,
all flesh would expire together, and humankind would return to dust.
And if there is understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.
Shall one who hates judgement govern? And will you condemn the Righteous Mighty One?
Does one say to a king, "Worthless one!" to nobles, "Wicked one!"?
who does not lift up the faces of princes and does not regard the rich before the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
In a moment they die, at midnight; a people is shaken and passes away, and the mighty are removed without a hand.
For his eyes are on the ways of a man, and he sees all his steps.
There is no darkness and no deep darkness where the doers of iniquity may hide themselves.
For he does not set a time for a man to go before God in judgement.
He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place.
Therefore he is acquainted with their deeds; he overturns them by night, and they are crushed.
He slaps them in the place of the wicked, in a place where people see,
because they turned aside from following him and did not consider any of his ways,
so as to bring to him the outcry of the poor, and he hears the outcry of the afflicted.
And when he is quiet, who can condemn? And when he hides his face, who can behold him? — over a nation and over a man alike,
so that a godless man should not reign, nor be a snare to a people.
For has anyone said to God, "I have borne it; I will not offend;
apart from what I see, teach me; if I have done unrighteousness, I will not do it again"?
Should he repay it on your terms, because you have refused? For you must choose, and not I; so what you know, speak.
Men of heart will say to me, and a wise man who listens to me:
"Job speaks without knowledge, and his words are without insight."
Would that Job were tested to the end, for answers among men of iniquity!
For he adds transgression to his sin; among us he claps, and multiplies his sayings against God.

job_35.t: Do you think this is judgement? You have said, "My righteousness is more than God's."
For you say, "What use is it to you? What do I profit more than from my sin?"
I will answer you with words, and your friends with you.
Look at the heavens and see; and behold the clouds, higher than you.
If you have sinned, what do you do to him? And if your transgressions are many, what do you do to him?
If you are in the right, what do you give him, or what does he receive from your hand?
Your wickedness is for a man like yourself, and your righteousness for a son of humankind.
From the multitude of oppressions people cry out; they cry for help from the arm of the great.
But no one says, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?"
There they cry out, and he does not answer, because of the pride of the wicked.
Surely God does not hear emptiness, and the Almighty does not behold it.
How much less when you say you do not behold him — the case is before him, and you must wait for him!
And now, because his anger has not punished, and he has not greatly regarded transgression,
Job opens his mouth in emptiness; without knowledge he multiplies words.

job_36.t: And Elihu went on and said:
Wait for me a little and I will show you, for there are still words for God.
I will bring my knowledge from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
For truly my words are not falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
See, God is mighty and does not reject; mighty in strength of heart.
He does not keep the wicked alive, and he gives judgement to the afflicted.
He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne he seats them for ever, and they are exalted.
And if they are bound in fetters, caught in cords of affliction,
then he declares to them their work and their transgressions, that they were behaving proudly.
And he uncovers their ear for correction and says that they should turn back from iniquity.
If they hear and serve him, they will complete their days in prosperity and their years in pleasant things.
And if they do not hear, they pass away by the weapon and expire without knowledge.
And the godless in heart lay up anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.
Their being dies in youth, and their life among the shrine prostitutes.
He rescues the afflicted by his affliction and uncovers their ear by oppression.
And also he has allured you from the mouth of distress to a broad place with no constraint beneath it, and the setting of your table was full of fatness.
But you are full of the judgement of the wicked; judgement and justice take hold of you.
For beware lest rage entice you into mockery, and let the greatness of the ransom not turn you aside.
Will your wealth set anything in order, that you be not in distress, or all the efforts of strength?
Do not long for the night, when peoples go up in their place.
Take heed; do not turn to iniquity, for this you have chosen rather than affliction.
See, God is exalted in his power; who is a teacher like him?
Who has assigned him his way? And who has said, "You have done unrighteousness"?
Remember to magnify his work, which people have sung.
All humankind has looked on it; a mortal beholds it from afar.
See, God is exalted, and we do not know him; the number of his years is beyond searching out.
For he draws up the drops of water; they distil rain for his mist,
which the clouds pour down; they drip on humankind abundantly.
Can anyone understand the spreadings of the cloud, the crashings of his pavilion?
See, he spreads his light upon it and covers the roots of the sea.
For by them he judges peoples; he gives food in abundance.
He covers his hands with light and commands it against an assailant.
His roar tells about him; the livestock also, about what rises.

job_37.t: At this also my heart trembles and leaps from its place.
Listen carefully to the raging of his voice and the rumbling that goes out from his mouth.
Under all the heavens he lets it loose, and his light to the corners of the earth.
After it a voice roars; he thunders with the voice of his majesty, and he does not hold them back when his voice is heard.
God thunders with his voice wondrously; he does great things that we do not know.
For to the snow he says, "Fall on the earth"; and to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
He seals up the hand of every human, so that all people may know his work.
And the wild animal goes into its lair and dwells in its dens.
From the chamber comes the storm-wind, and from the scattering winds the cold.
By the breath of God ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is in constraint.
He also loads the cloud with moisture; he scatters the cloud of his light.
And it turns round about by his guidance, to do all that he commands them on the face of the world, on the earth.
Whether for a rod, or for his earth, or for steadfast love, he makes it find its mark.
Give ear to this, Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
Do you know when God lays a charge upon them and makes the light of his cloud shine forth?
Do you know the balancings of the cloud, the wondrous works of one perfect in knowledge?
you whose garments are hot when the earth is still from the south?
Can you beat out with him the clouds, hard as a molten mirror?
Make known to us what we shall say to him; we cannot set anything in order because of darkness.
Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or has anyone said that he would be swallowed up?
And now people do not see the light; it is brilliant in the clouds, and a wind has passed and cleansed them.
Out of the north comes gold; upon God is awesome majesty.
The Almighty — we have not found him; he is exalted in power, and judgement and abundant righteousness he does not violate.
Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in heart.

job_38.t: And YHWH answered Job out of the tempest and said:
Who is this that darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
Gird up your loins like a man, and I will ask you, and you make it known to me.
Where were you when I founded the earth? Tell, if you know understanding.
Who fixed its measurements — for you know! — or who stretched the line upon it?
On what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
And who shut in the sea with doors when it burst forth, coming out from the womb,
when I made the cloud its clothing and thick darkness its swaddling band,
and I broke my boundary upon it and set a bar and doors,
and said, "This far you shall come and no further, and here shall be set a limit to the pride of your waves"?
Have you in your days commanded the morning, caused the dawn to know its place,
to take hold of the corners of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?
It is changed like clay under a seal, and they stand forth like a garment.
And their light is withheld from the wicked, and the uplifted arm is broken.
Have you gone to the springs of the sea or walked about in the recess of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you, and have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you given attention to the broad places of the earth? Tell, if you know it all.
Where is the way to where light dwells, and darkness — where is its place,
that you should take it to its territory and discern the paths to its house?
You know, for then you were born, and the number of your days is great!
Have you gone into the storehouses of snow, and have you seen the storehouses of hail,
which I have kept back for the time of distress, for the day of battle and war?
Where is the way by which light is distributed, by which the east wind is scattered over the earth?
Who has cut a channel for the torrent and a way for the thunderbolt,
to bring rain on a land where no one is, on a wilderness in which there is no human,
to satisfy the waste and desolation and to make the going forth of grass sprout?
Has the rain a father, or who fathered the drops of dew?
From whose womb did the ice come out, and the frost of heaven — who gave it birth?
The waters become hard like stone, and the surface of the deep freezes fast.
Can you bind the bonds of the Pleiades or loosen the cords of Orion?
Can you bring out the constellations in their season, or guide the Bear with her young?
Do you know the statutes of the heavens? Can you establish their rule over the earth?
Can you lift up your voice to the cloud, that an abundance of water may cover you?
Can you send forth lightnings, and they go and say to you, "Here we are"?
Who put wisdom in the inward parts, or who gave understanding to the mind?
Who can number the clouds by wisdom, and who can tip the waterskins of heaven,
when the dust runs into a mass and the clods stick together?
Can you hunt prey for the lioness and fill the life of the young lions,
when they crouch in their dens and sit in the thicket for a lair?
Who prepares food for the raven when its young cry to God for help and wander about for lack of food?

job_39.t: Do you know the time when the mountain goats of the rock give birth? Do you watch the writhing of the does?
Can you count the months they complete, and do you know the time when they give birth,
when they crouch, split open their young, and send forth their birth-pangs?
Their young grow strong; they grow up in the open; they go out and do not return to them.
Who let the wild donkey go free, and who loosed the fetters of the wild ass,
whose home I made the desert plain, and its dwelling-places the salt land?
It laughs at the tumult of the town; it does not hear the shouts of the driver.
It explores the mountains as its pasture and searches after every green thing.
Is the wild ox willing to serve you? Will it spend the night at your feeding trough?
Can you bind the wild ox with its rope in the furrow? Will it harrow the valleys behind you?
Will you trust it because its strength is great, and leave your labour to it?
Will you trust it to bring back your seed and gather it to your threshing floor?
The wing of the ostrich flaps joyously — is it the pinion and plumage of a stork?
For it abandons its eggs to the ground and lets them warm on the dust,
and it forgets that a foot may crush them and the wild animal of the field trample them.
It treats its young harshly, as not its own; its labour is in vain, without fear,
for God has made it forget wisdom and has given it no share in understanding.
When it lashes itself on high, it laughs at the horse and its rider.
Do you give the horse strength? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
Do you make him leap like a locust? The majesty of his snorting is terror.
They paw in the valley, and he rejoices in strength; he goes out to meet weaponry.
He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.
Upon him the quiver rattles, the blade of the spear and the javelin.
With shaking and raging he swallows the ground; he does not stand still when the horn sounds.
At every blast of the horn he says, "Aha!" and from afar he smells the battle, the thunder of the commanders and the war-cry.
Is it by your understanding that the falcon soars, spreading its wings toward the south?
Is it at your mouth that the eagle mounts up and sets its nest on high?
It dwells on the rock and lodges there, on the tooth of the rock and the stronghold.
From there it spies out food; its eyes look far off.
And its young ones lap up blood; and where the slain are, there it is.

job_40.t: And YHWH answered Job and said:
Shall a faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who reproves God answer it.
And Job answered YHWH and said:
See, I am small. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
Once I have spoken, and I will not answer; and twice, and I will not add.
And YHWH answered Job out of the tempest and said:
Gird up your loins like a man; I will ask you, and you make it known to me.
Will you even annul my judgement? Will you condemn me that you may be in the right?
Have you an arm like God? And can you thunder with a voice like his?
Deck yourself now with majesty and dignity; and clothe yourself with glory and honour.
Scatter the overflowings of your anger; and look on every proud one and bring him low.
Look on every proud one and humble him, and tread down the wicked where they stand.
Hide them in the dust together; bind up their faces in the hidden place.
Then I also will praise you, that your own right hand can save you.
See now Behemoth, which I made with you; he eats grass like the ox.
See now, his strength is in his loins, and his power in the muscles of his belly.
He stiffens his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are knit together.
His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs like a bar of iron.
He is the first of the ways of God; let the one who made him bring near his sword.
For the mountains bring him produce, and all the wild animals of the field play there.
