Under the lotus plants he lies down, in the covert of reeds and marsh.
The lotus plants cover him with their shade; the poplars of the wadi surround him.
See, if the river is violent, he is not alarmed; he is confident though the Jordan bursts against his mouth.
Can anyone take him by his eyes, or pierce his nose with snares?

job_41.t: Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish-hook or press down his tongue with a cord?
Can you put a rush-cord in his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
Will he multiply supplications to you? Will he speak soft words to you?
Will he cut a covenant with you, that you should take him as a perpetual slave?
Will you play with him as with a bird or tie him up for your girls?
Will partners bargain over him? Will they divide him among merchants?
Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fish-spears?
Lay your hand on him; remember the battle — you will not do it again!
See, one's hope of him is proved false; is one not cast down even at the sight of him?
No one is so fierce that he would rouse him. And who is he that can stand before me?
Who has confronted me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under all the heavens is mine.
I will not keep silence about his limbs, or the matter of his strength, or the grace of his frame.
Who has uncovered the face of his garment? Who can come into his double bridle?
Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
His pride is rows of shields, shut up with a tight seal.
One draws near to another, and no breath comes between them.
Each clings to its brother; they grasp one another and cannot be parted.
His sneezings flash forth light, and his eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.
From his mouth go torches; sparks of fire leap out.
From his nostrils goes out smoke, like a boiling pot and burning rushes.
His breath kindles coals, and a flame goes out from his mouth.
In his neck lodges strength, and before him dismay leaps.
The folds of his flesh cling together; they are cast hard upon him and do not move.
His heart is cast hard as stone, and cast hard as the lower millstone.
At his rising the mighty are afraid; at the crashing they are beside themselves.
The sword that reaches him does not hold, nor spear, dart, or javelin.
He counts iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood.
The arrow does not make him flee; sling-stones are turned to chaff for him.
A club is counted as chaff, and he laughs at the rattling of a javelin.
Beneath him are sharp potsherds; he spreads a threshing sledge on the mud.
He makes the deep boil like a pot; he makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
Behind him he lights up a path; one would think the deep to be grey-haired.
There is nothing on the dust like him, one made without fear.
He looks on everything that is high; he is king over all the sons of pride.

job_42.t: And Job answered YHWH and said:
I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose is withheld from you.
'Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge?' Therefore I have declared what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
'Hear now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you make it known to me.'
By the hearing of the ear I had heard of you, but now my eye has seen you.
Therefore I reject, and I am consoled, upon dust and ashes.

And it came about, after YHWH had spoken these words to Job, that YHWH said to Eliphaz the Temanite: My anger burns against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.

And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and my servant Job will pray for you; for I will lift up his face, so as not to do to you a disgrace — because you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.
And Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as YHWH had spoken to them; and YHWH lifted up the face of Job.
And YHWH turned back the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and YHWH added to all that Job had, to double.

And all his brothers and all his sisters and all who had known him before came to him and ate bread with him in his house; and they shook their heads over him and comforted him for all the trouble that YHWH had brought upon him. And each one gave him one piece of money and each one one ring of gold.
And YHWH blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and he had fourteen thousand sheep and six thousand camels and a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.
And he had seven sons and three daughters.
And he called the name of the first Jemimah, and the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-happuch.
And no women were found as beautiful as the daughters of Job in all the land; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
And Job lived after this a hundred and forty years, and he saw his sons and the sons of his sons, four generations.
And Job died, old and satisfied of days.

joel_1.t: The word of YHWH which came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Hear this, O elders, and give ear, all inhabitants of the land. Has this happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Recount it to your children, and your children to their children, and their children to another generation.

The remainder of the shearing locust the swarming locust has eaten, and the remainder of the swarming locust the licking locust has eaten, and the remainder of the licking locust the consuming locust has eaten.
Awake, O drunkards, and weep; and wail, all drinkers of wine, over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and without number. Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the fangs of a lioness.
It has made my vine a waste and splintered my fig tree. Stripping it bare, it has stripped it bare and thrown it down; its branches have turned white.
Wail like a virgin girded with sackcloth over the husband of her youth.
Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of YHWH. The priests mourn, the servants of YHWH.
The field is devastated, the ground mourns, for the grain is devastated, the new wine has dried up, the fresh oil withers.
Be ashamed, O farmers; wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and over the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig tree withers; pomegranate, palm and apple too — all the trees of the field have dried up. For joy has dried up from the sons of humankind.

Gird yourselves and lament, O priests; wail, O servants of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O servants of my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
Set apart a fast as holy, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders, all the inhabitants of the land, [to] the house of YHWH your God, and cry out to YHWH.
Alas for the day! For the day of YHWH is near, and like devastation from the Almighty it comes.
Has not food been cut off before our eyes, joy and rejoicing from the house of our God?
The seeds have shrivelled under their clods; the storehouses are desolate, the granaries torn down, for the grain has dried up.
How the livestock groans! The herds of cattle wander in confusion, for there is no pasture for them; the flocks of sheep also suffer.
To you, O YHWH, I call, for fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, and a flame has set ablaze all the trees of the field.
The animals of the field also pant for you, for the channels of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.

joel_2.t: Blow a ram's horn in Zion, and sound the alarm on my holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of YHWH is coming — for it is near:

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness. Like dawn spread over the mountains, a people numerous and mighty; its like has not been from of old, and after it there will be none again to the years of generation upon generation.
Before it fire consumes, and after it a flame sets ablaze. The land before it is like the garden of Eden, and after it a wilderness of desolation; and there is no escape from it, none.
Like the appearance of horses is its appearance, and like horsemen, so they run.
Like the sound of chariots on the tops of the mountains they leap, like the sound of a flame of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty people drawn up for battle.
Before it peoples are in anguish; all faces gather a glow.
Like warriors they run, like men of war they scale a wall. Each goes on his own ways, and they do not swerve from their paths.
They do not press one another; each goes on his own track. And through the weapons they fall, they are not stopped.
They rush upon the city, they run on the wall, they climb into the houses, through the windows they come like a thief.
Before it the earth trembles, the heavens shake. Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.
And YHWH has given forth his voice before his army, for his camp is very great, for mighty is the one who does his word. For great is the day of YHWH and very awesome — and who can endure it?
"Yet even now," the declaration of YHWH, "return to me with all your heart, and with fasting and with weeping and with wailing."
"And tear your heart and not your garments, and return to YHWH your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, long of nostrils and abundant in steadfast love, and relenting over harm."
Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him — a grain offering and a drink offering for YHWH your God.
Blow a ram's horn in Zion, set apart a fast as holy, call a solemn assembly.

Gather the people, set the assembly apart as holy, assemble the elders, gather the children and those who suckle at the breasts. Let the bridegroom come out from his room, and the bride from her chamber.

Between the porch and the altar let the priests weep, the servants of YHWH, and let them say: "Spare your people, YHWH, and do not give your inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
Then YHWH became jealous for his land, and he had compassion on his people.

And YHWH answered and said to his people: "Here I am, sending you the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and you will be satisfied with it; and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.

And the northerner I will remove far from you, and I will drive it into a land dry and desolate, its face toward the eastern sea and its rear toward the western sea. And its stench will go up, and its foul smell will go up, for it has done great things.
Do not fear, O ground; be glad and rejoice, for YHWH has done great things.
Do not fear, O animals of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have turned green; for the tree has borne its fruit, the fig tree and the vine have given their strength.
And children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in YHWH your God, for he has given you the early rain for righteousness; and he has sent down for you rain, early rain and spring rain, in the first [month].
And the threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and fresh oil.
"And I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust ate, the licking locust and the consuming locust and the shearing locust, my great army that I sent among you.
"And you will eat, eating and being satisfied, and you will praise the name of YHWH your God, who has dealt with you wondrously; and my people will never be ashamed.
"And you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am YHWH your God, and there is no other; and my people will never be ashamed."
"And it will be afterwards that I will pour out my spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
"And also on the male servants and on the female servants in those days I will pour out my spirit.
"And I will put wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
"The sun will be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the coming of the day of YHWH, the great and awesome day.

"And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of YHWH will escape; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, just as YHWH has said, and among the survivors whom YHWH is calling."

joel_3.t: "For look — in those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will enter into judgement with them there over my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations — and my land they divided up.
And for my people they cast a lot, and they gave a boy for a prostitute, and a girl they sold for wine — and drank.

"And also, what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia? Are you repaying me a recompense? And if you are making recompense against me, swiftly, speedily I will return your recompense on your head —
you who took my silver and my gold, and carried my good treasures into your temples;
and the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem you sold to the sons of the Greeks, to remove them far from their own territory.
"Here I am, rousing them from the place where you sold them, and I will return your recompense on your head.
And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a distant nation" — for YHWH has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Set apart a war as holy! Rouse the warriors! Let all the men of war draw near, let them come up!
Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning knives into spears. Let the weak say, "I am a warrior."
Hurry and come, all you nations from round about, and gather yourselves there. Bring down your warriors, O YHWH!
"Let the nations be roused and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations from round about.
Send out the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full, the vats overflow, for their evil is great."
Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of YHWH is near in the valley of decision.
Sun and moon have grown dark, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness.
And YHWH will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will give forth his voice, and the heavens and the earth will shake. But YHWH is a refuge for his people and a stronghold for the sons of Israel.
"And you will know that I am YHWH your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. And Jerusalem will be a holy place, and strangers will not pass through it again."

"And it will be on that day that the mountains will drip sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk, and all the ravines of Judah will flow with water. And a spring will go out from the house of YHWH and water the Wadi of the Acacias.
Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom will become a wilderness of desolation, because of the violence done to the sons of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
But Judah will remain for ever, and Jerusalem to generation and generation.
"And I will hold their blood innocent — that which I did not hold innocent." And YHWH is dwelling in Zion.

jonah_1.t: And the word of YHWH came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
'Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out against it, for their evil has come up before me.'

And Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish from before YHWH. And he went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish, and he gave its fare and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, from before YHWH.
And YHWH hurled a great wind at the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship thought itself about to be broken up.

And the sailors were afraid, and they cried out, each man to his gods, and they hurled the gear that was in the ship into the sea, to lighten it from upon them. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the vessel, and had lain down, and had fallen fast asleep.
And the chief helmsman drew near to him and said to him, 'What is this to you, sleeper? Arise, call to your god! Perhaps the god will give thought to us, and we will not perish.'
And they said, each to his neighbour, 'Come, let us cast lots, that we may know on whose account this evil is upon us.' And they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
And they said to him, 'Tell us, please, on whose account this evil is upon us. What is your occupation, and from where do you come? What is your land, and from which people are you?'
And he said to them, 'I am a Hebrew, and I fear YHWH, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry ground.'
And the men feared a great fear, and they said to him, 'What is this you have done?' — for the men knew that he was fleeing from before YHWH, because he had told them.
And they said to him, 'What shall we do to you, so that the sea may be calm for us?' — for the sea was going and storming.
And he said to them, 'Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will be calm for you — for I know that on my account this great storm is upon you.'
And the men rowed hard to return to the dry ground, and they were not able, for the sea was going and storming against them.
And they called out to YHWH and said, 'Please, O YHWH, let us not perish for the life of this man, and do not put innocent blood upon us — for you, O YHWH, have done as you pleased.'
And they picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped from its raging.
And the men feared YHWH — a great fear — and they sacrificed a sacrifice to YHWH and vowed vows.
And YHWH appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the inward parts of the fish three days and three nights.

jonah_2.t: And Jonah prayed to YHWH his God from the inward parts of the fish.
And he said: I called from my distress to YHWH, and he answered me; from the belly of Sheol I cried for help, you heard my voice.
And you cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and a river surrounded me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.
And I, I said, 'I have been driven away from before your eyes; nevertheless I will look again toward your holy temple.'
Waters encompassed me up to the throat; the deep surrounded me; reeds were wound about my head.
To the roots of the mountains I went down; the earth — its bars were behind me for ever; but you brought up my life from the pit, O YHWH my God.
When my life fainted away upon me, YHWH I remembered; and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
Those who keep worthless vanities forsake their steadfast love.
But I, with a voice of thanksgiving, I will sacrifice to you; what I have vowed I will fulfil. Deliverance belongs to YHWH.
And YHWH spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry ground.

jonah_3.t: And the word of YHWH came to Jonah a second time, saying,
'Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out to it the proclamation that I am speaking to you.'
And Jonah arose and went to Nineveh according to the word of YHWH. Now Nineveh was a city great to God, a journey of three days.
And Jonah began to go into the city, a journey of one day, and he proclaimed and said, 'Forty days more, and Nineveh is overthrown!'
And the people of Nineveh believed in God, and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their great to their small.
And the word reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne and took off his cloak from upon him and covered himself with sackcloth and sat on the ashes.

And he had it proclaimed and said in Nineveh, 'By decree of the king and his great ones: The people and the livestock, the cattle and the flocks, are not to taste anything; they are not to graze, and they are not to drink water.

And let them cover themselves with sackcloth — the people and the livestock — and let them call out to God with strength, and let them turn back, each from his evil way and from the violence that is in their palms.
Who knows? He may turn and God may relent, and turn back from the burning of his anger, and we will not perish.'
And God saw their deeds, that they had turned back from their evil way, and God relented concerning the evil that he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.

jonah_4.t: And it was evil to Jonah — a great evil — and it burned to him.

And he prayed to YHWH and said, 'Please, O YHWH — was this not my word while I was still on my own ground? That is why I went first to flee to Tarshish: for I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and one who relents concerning evil.'
'And now, O YHWH, take my life from me, please — for my death is better than my life.'
And YHWH said, 'Is it rightly that it burns to you?'
And Jonah went out from the city and sat down east of the city, and he made himself a booth there and sat under it in the shade, until he might see what would happen in the city.
And YHWH God appointed a plant, and it came up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his evil. And Jonah rejoiced over the plant with a great joy.
And God appointed a worm at the coming up of the dawn the next day, and it attacked the plant, and it withered.

And it was, when the sun rose, that God appointed a hot east wind, and the sun struck on Jonah's head, and he became faint. And he asked for his life to die, and he said, 'My death is better than my life.'
And God said to Jonah, 'Is it rightly that it burns to you over the plant?' And he said, 'Rightly it burns to me — to death.'
And YHWH said, 'You yourself had pity on the plant, for which you did not toil and which you did not make grow — which came to be a son of a night and perished a son of a night.
And I — shall I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than twelve myriads of people who do not know between their right hand and their left, and much livestock?'

joshua_1.t: And it was, after the death of Moses the servant of YHWH, that YHWH said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' attendant, saying,
"Moses my servant is dead. And now arise, cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to them, to the sons of Israel.
"Every place on which the sole of your foot treads I have given to you, just as I spoke to Moses.

"From the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates — all the land of the Hittites — and as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun shall be your territory.
"No one shall stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moses, I will be with you; I will not abandon you and I will not forsake you.
"Be strong and be bold, for you will cause this people to inherit the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.

"Only be strong and very bold, to take care to do according to all the law that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left, so that you may act wisely wherever you go.

"This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may take care to do according to all that is written in it; for then you will make your ways succeed, and then you will act wisely.
"Have I not commanded you? Be strong and be bold. Do not be terrified and do not be dismayed, for YHWH your God is with you wherever you go."
And Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying,

"Pass through the midst of the camp and command the people, saying, 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for in three days you are to cross this Jordan, to go in and take possession of the land that YHWH your God is giving you to possess.'"
And to the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said,
"Remember the word that Moses the servant of YHWH commanded you, saying, 'YHWH your God is giving you rest, and he will give you this land.'

"Your wives, your little ones and your livestock shall remain in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan; but you shall cross over armed for battle before your brothers, all the mighty men of valour, and you shall help them,

"until YHWH gives rest to your brothers as to you, and they also take possession of the land that YHWH your God is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession and take possession of it, which Moses the servant of YHWH gave you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun."
And they answered Joshua, saying, "All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
"Just as we listened to Moses in everything, so we will listen to you. Only may YHWH your God be with you, as he was with Moses.
"Anyone who rebels against your mouth and does not listen to your words, to all that you command him, shall be put to death. Only be strong and be bold."

joshua_2.t: And Joshua son of Nun sent two men as spies, secretly, from Shittim, saying, "Go, see the land, and Jericho." And they went and came to the house of a woman, a prostitute, and her name was Rahab; and they lay down there.
And it was told to the king of Jericho, "Behold, men have come here tonight from the sons of Israel to spy out the land."
And the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you, who came to your house, for they have come to spy out the whole land."
And the woman took the two men and hid him, and she said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
"And it was, when the gate was about to be shut, at dark, that the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue after them quickly, for you will overtake them."
And she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.
And the men pursued after them by the road of the Jordan, to the fords; and the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers had gone out after them.
And they had not yet lain down when she went up to them on the roof,
and she said to the men, "I know that YHWH has given you the land, and that dread of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land have melted away before you.

"For we have heard how YHWH dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
"And we heard, and our heart melted, and no spirit rose again in anyone because of you; for YHWH your God — he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.
"And now, swear to me, please, by YHWH, since I have done loyalty with you, that you also will do loyalty with my father's house; and give me a sign of faithfulness,
"and let my father and my mother and my brothers and my sisters and all who belong to them live, and deliver our lives from death."
And the men said to her, "Our life for yours, to die — if you do not tell this business of ours! And it shall be, when YHWH gives us the land, that we will do loyalty and faithfulness with you."
And she let them down by the rope through the window, for her house was in the wall of the city wall, and she was living in the city wall.
And she said to them, "Go to the hill country, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days until the pursuers return, and afterward you may go on your way."
And the men said to her, "We shall be free from this oath of yours that you have made us swear:

"Behold, when we come into the land, this cord of scarlet thread you shall bind in the window by which you let us down; and your father and your mother and your brothers and all your father's household you shall gather to yourself into the house.

"And it shall be that anyone who goes out from the doors of your house to the outside — his blood shall be on his own head, and we shall be free; and anyone who is with you in the house — his blood shall be on our head, if a hand is on him.
"And if you tell this business of ours, then we shall be free from your oath that you have made us swear."
And she said, "According to your words, so be it." And she sent them off and they went; and she bound the scarlet cord in the window.
And they went and came to the hill country and stayed there three days until the pursuers returned. And the pursuers searched all along the way and did not find them.
And the two men returned and came down from the hill country and crossed over and came to Joshua son of Nun, and they recounted to him all that had befallen them.
And they said to Joshua, "YHWH has given all the land into our hand; and also all the inhabitants of the land have melted away before us."

joshua_3.t: And Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the sons of Israel; and they stayed there before they crossed over.
And it was at the end of three days that the officers passed through the midst of the camp,
and they commanded the people, saying, "When you see the ark of the covenant of YHWH your God, and the priests, the Levites, carrying it, then you shall set out from your place and go after it.
"Only let there be a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you are to go, for you have not passed this way before."
And Joshua said to the people, "Set yourselves apart as holy, for tomorrow YHWH will do wonders in your midst."
And Joshua said to the priests, "Lift up the ark of the covenant and cross over before the people." And they lifted up the ark of the covenant and went before the people.
And YHWH said to Joshua, "This day I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that just as I was with Moses I will be with you.
"And you shall command the priests, the bearers of the ark of the covenant, saying, 'When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.'"
And Joshua said to the sons of Israel, "Draw near here and hear the words of YHWH your God."

And Joshua said, "By this you shall know that a living God is in your midst, and that he will surely dispossess before you the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Hivite and the Perizzite and the Girgashite and the Amorite and the Jebusite:
"behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is about to cross over before you into the Jordan.
"And now take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man, one man for each tribe.

"And it shall be, when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of YHWH, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan shall be cut off — the waters coming down from above — and they shall stand as one heap."
And it was, when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests, the bearers of the ark, the covenant, before the people,

and as the bearers of the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests, the bearers of the ark, were dipped in the edge of the waters — and the Jordan is full over all its banks all the days of harvest —

that the waters coming down from above stood still; they rose up as one heap very far off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those going down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. And the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

And the priests, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of YHWH, stood firm on the dry land in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over on the dry land, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.

joshua_4.t: And it was, when the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, that YHWH said to Joshua,
"Take for yourselves from the people twelve men, one man, one man from each tribe,

"and command them, saying, 'Take up for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the standing-place of the priests' feet, twelve stones set firm; and you shall carry them over with you and set them down at the lodging place where you stay tonight.'"
And Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the sons of Israel, one man, one man from each tribe.

And Joshua said to them, "Cross over before the ark of YHWH your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you lift up one stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel,
"so that this may be a sign in your midst. When your children ask tomorrow, saying, 'What are these stones to you?'

"then you shall say to them, 'Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of YHWH; when it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off.' And these stones shall be a memorial to the sons of Israel for ever."

And the sons of Israel did so, just as Joshua commanded, and they took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, just as YHWH had said to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.
And twelve stones Joshua set up in the middle of the Jordan, at the standing-place of the feet of the priests, the bearers of the ark of the covenant; and they have been there to this day.

And the priests, the bearers of the ark, stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was finished that YHWH had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people hurried and crossed over.
And it was, when all the people had finished crossing over, that the ark of YHWH crossed over, and the priests, before the people.
And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed for battle before the sons of Israel, just as Moses had spoken to them —
about forty thousand armed for war crossed over before YHWH for battle, to the plains of Jericho.
On that day YHWH made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him just as they had feared Moses all the days of his life.
And YHWH said to Joshua,
"Command the priests, the bearers of the ark of the testimony, that they come up from the Jordan."
And Joshua commanded the priests, saying, "Come up from the Jordan."

And it was, when the priests, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of YHWH, came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were drawn up onto the dry ground, that the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and went as before over all its banks.
And the people came up from the Jordan on the tenth of the first month, and they encamped at Gilgal, at the eastern edge of Jericho.
And those twelve stones that they had taken from the Jordan Joshua set up at Gilgal.
And he said to the sons of Israel, saying, "When your children ask their fathers tomorrow, saying, 'What are these stones?'
"then you shall make known to your children, saying, 'On dry ground Israel crossed this Jordan,'
"for YHWH your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as YHWH your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which he dried up before us until we had crossed over,
"so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of YHWH, that it is mighty, so that you may fear YHWH your God all the days."

joshua_5.t: And it was, when all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan to the west, and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea, heard that YHWH had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the sons of Israel until they had crossed over, that their heart melted, and there was no spirit in them any more because of the sons of Israel.
At that time YHWH said to Joshua, "Make for yourself knives of flint, and circumcise the sons of Israel again, a second time."
And Joshua made for himself knives of flint and circumcised the sons of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.
And this is the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way, when they came out of Egypt.
For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the wilderness on the way, when they came out of Egypt, had not been circumcised.

For forty years the sons of Israel walked in the wilderness, until the whole nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, was finished — those who had not listened to the voice of YHWH, to whom YHWH swore that he would not let them see the land that YHWH swore to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And their children he raised up in their place; these Joshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.
And it was, when the whole nation had finished being circumcised, that they stayed in their place in the camp until they were healed.
And YHWH said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from upon you." And the name of that place was called Gilgal, to this day.
And the sons of Israel encamped at Gilgal, and they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.
And they ate of the produce of the land on the day after the passover — unleavened bread and roasted grain — on that same day.
And the manna ceased on the day after, when they ate of the produce of the land; and the sons of Israel had manna no more, and they ate of the yield of the land of Canaan in that year.

And it was, when Joshua was at Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. And Joshua went to him and said to him, "Are you for us or for our foes?"
And he said, "No, for I am the commander of the army of YHWH. Now I have come." And Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and said to him, "What is my lord saying to his servant?"
And the commander of the army of YHWH said to Joshua, "Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place on which you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.

joshua_6.t: And Jericho was shutting and shut up because of the sons of Israel; no one went out and no one came in.
And YHWH said to Joshua, "See, I have given into your hand Jericho and its king, the mighty men of valour.
"And you shall go around the city, all the men of war, encircling the city once. So you shall do six days.
"And seven priests shall carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark. And on the seventh day you shall go around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.

"And it shall be, when they blow long on the horn of the ram, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, that all the people shall shout a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down where it stands, and the people shall go up, each straight ahead."
And Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of YHWH."
And he said to the people, "Pass on and go around the city, and let the armed men pass on before the ark of YHWH."

And it was, when Joshua had said this to the people, that the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before YHWH passed on and blew the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of YHWH went after them.
And the armed men went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rearguard went after the ark, going and blowing the trumpets.

And Joshua commanded the people, saying, "You shall not shout, and you shall not let your voice be heard, and no word shall go out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout."
And he caused the ark of YHWH to go around the city, encircling it once; and they came to the camp and stayed in the camp.
And Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of YHWH.

And the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of YHWH were going continually and blowing the trumpets; and the armed men went before them, and the rearguard went after the ark of YHWH, going and blowing the trumpets.
And they went around the city on the second day once, and returned to the camp. So they did six days.
And it was on the seventh day that they rose early, at the going up of the dawn, and went around the city in this manner seven times. Only on that day did they go around the city seven times.
And it was at the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, that Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For YHWH has given you the city.

"And the city shall be devoted to destruction, it and all that is in it, to YHWH. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.

"But you, keep away from what is devoted to destruction, lest you devote yourselves to destruction and take from what is devoted to destruction, and so make the camp of Israel devoted to destruction and bring trouble on it.
"And all silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron are holy to YHWH; they shall go into the treasury of YHWH."

And the people shouted, and they blew the trumpets. And it was, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, that the people shouted a great shout, and the wall fell down where it stood, and the people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and they captured the city.
And they devoted to destruction all that was in the city, from man to woman, from young to old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
And to the two men who had spied out the land Joshua said, "Go into the house of the woman, the prostitute, and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her, just as you swore to her."

And the young men who had spied out went in and brought out Rahab and her father and her mother and her brothers and all who belonged to her — all her clans they brought out — and they set them outside the camp of Israel.
And they burned the city with fire, and all that was in it. Only the silver and the gold and the articles of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of YHWH.

And Rahab the prostitute, and her father's household and all who belonged to her, Joshua let live; and she has dwelt in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

And Joshua administered an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed before YHWH be the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates."
And YHWH was with Joshua, and his report was in all the land.

joshua_7.t: But the sons of Israel acted unfaithfully, an unfaithfulness, in the matter of what was devoted to destruction: Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted to destruction. And the anger of YHWH burned against the sons of Israel.
And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, "Go up and spy out the land." And the men went up and spied out Ai.

And they returned to Joshua and said to him, "Let not all the people go up; let about two thousand men or about three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not make all the people toil there, for they are few."
And about three thousand men of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.

And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six men of them, and pursued them from before the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them down at the descent. And the heart of the people melted and became water.
And Joshua tore his garments and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of YHWH until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust on their heads.

And Joshua said, "Alas, Lord YHWH! Why have you brought this people right over the Jordan, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been willing and had stayed beyond the Jordan!
"Pardon me, Lord! What shall I say, after Israel has turned its neck before its enemies?
"And the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear and surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?"
And YHWH said to Joshua, "Get up! Why is it that you are falling on your face?

"Israel has sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant that I commanded them, and they have also taken some of what is devoted to destruction, and they have also stolen, and they have also deceived, and they have also put it among their own things.

"And the sons of Israel are not able to stand before their enemies; they turn a neck before their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any more unless you destroy what is devoted to destruction from your midst.

"Arise, set the people apart as holy, and say, 'Set yourselves apart as holy for tomorrow. For thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: There is something devoted to destruction in your midst, Israel. You will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove what is devoted to destruction from your midst.'

"And you shall be brought near in the morning by your tribes. And it shall be that the tribe that YHWH takes shall come near by families, and the family that YHWH takes shall come near by households, and the household that YHWH takes shall come near man by man.

"And the one taken with what is devoted to destruction shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of YHWH and because he has done an outrage in Israel."
And Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
And he brought near the family of Judah, and he took the family of the Zerahites; and he brought near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
And he brought near his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
And Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory, please, to YHWH the God of Israel, and give him confession; and tell me, please, what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
And Achan answered Joshua and said, "Truly I have sinned against YHWH, the God of Israel, and this and this is what I did.

"I saw among the spoil one good cloak of Shinar, and two hundred shekels of silver, and one wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels; and I coveted them and took them. And there they are, hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver under it."
And Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and there it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.
And they took them from inside the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the sons of Israel, and they poured them out before YHWH.

And Joshua took Achan son of Zerah, and the silver and the cloak and the wedge of gold, and his sons and his daughters and his ox and his donkey and his flock and his tent and all that belonged to him — and all Israel with him — and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
And Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? YHWH will bring trouble on you this day." And all Israel stoned him with stones; and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
And they raised over him a great heap of stones, to this day. And YHWH turned from the burning of his anger. Therefore the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor, to this day.

joshua_8.t: And YHWH said to Joshua, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the people of war, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai and his people and his city and his land.
"And you shall do to Ai and to its king just as you did to Jericho and to its king. Only its spoil and its livestock you shall plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city, behind it."
And Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up to Ai. And Joshua chose thirty thousand men, mighty men of valour, and sent them out by night.
And he commanded them, saying, "See, you are to lie in ambush for the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you be ready.
"And I and all the people who are with me will draw near to the city; and it shall be, when they come out to meet us as at the first, that we shall flee before them.
"And they will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are fleeing before us as at the first.' And we shall flee before them.
"And you shall rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, and YHWH your God will give it into your hand.
"And it shall be, when you have captured the city, that you shall set the city on fire. According to the word of YHWH you shall do. See, I have commanded you."
And Joshua sent them out, and they went to the ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. And Joshua stayed that night among the people.
And Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people; and he went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.
And all the people of war who were with him went up and drew near and came before the city, and they encamped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
And he took about five thousand men and set them as an ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.
And the people set the whole camp that was north of the city, with its rear guard west of the city. And Joshua went that night into the middle of the valley.

And it was, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hurried and rose early, and the men of the city went out to meet Israel for battle — he and all his people — at the appointed place before the Arabah. And he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
And Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten before them, and they fled by the way of the wilderness.
And all the people who were in Ai were called together to pursue after them, and they pursued after Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
And not a man remained in Ai and Bethel who did not go out after Israel; and they left the city open and pursued after Israel.
And YHWH said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." And Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
And the ambush rose quickly from its place, and they ran when he stretched out his hand; and they came into the city and captured it, and they hurried and set the city on fire.

And the men of Ai turned behind them and looked, and behold, the smoke of the city had gone up to the heavens; and there were no hands in them to flee this way or that. And the people who were fleeing to the wilderness turned back against the pursuer.
And Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city had gone up; and they turned back and struck the men of Ai.

And these came out of the city to meet them, and they were caught by Israel in the middle, these on one side and these on the other; and they struck them down until no survivor or fugitive was left to him.
And the king of Ai they captured alive and brought him near to Joshua.

And it was, when Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country, in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and all of them had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were finished, that all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
And all who fell that day, from man to woman, were twelve thousand — all the people of Ai.
And Joshua did not draw back his hand, which he had stretched out with the javelin, until he had devoted to destruction all the inhabitants of Ai.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel plundered for themselves, according to the word of YHWH that he had commanded Joshua.
And Joshua burned Ai and made it a perpetual mound, a desolation, to this day.

And the king of Ai he hanged on the tree until the time of evening; and at the going down of the sun Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised over it a great heap of stones, to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to YHWH, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

just as Moses the servant of YHWH commanded the sons of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones on which no one has wielded iron. And they offered up on it burnt offerings to YHWH, and sacrificed peace offerings.
And he wrote there on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written before the sons of Israel.

And all Israel — its elders and officers and its judges — were standing on this side and on that of the ark, before the priests, the Levites, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of YHWH, the sojourner as the native-born; half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, just as Moses the servant of YHWH had commanded, to bless the people Israel at the first.
And afterward he read aloud all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.
There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read aloud before all the assembly of Israel, and the women and the little ones and the sojourner who walked in their midst.

joshua_9.t: And it was, when all the kings who were beyond the Jordan — in the hill country and in the Shephelah and along all the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon: the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite — heard,
that they gathered together, all together, to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one mouth.
And the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
and they also acted with cunning: they went and prepared provisions, and took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and worn-out wineskins, split and mended,
and worn-out and patched sandals on their feet, and worn-out garments on themselves; and all the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbling.
And they went to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant land. And now cut a covenant with us."
And the men of Israel said to the Hivite, "Perhaps you are dwelling in my midst; and how can I cut a covenant with you?"
And they said to Joshua, "We are your servants." And Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
And they said to him, "From a very distant land your servants have come, for the name of YHWH your God; for we have heard the report of him, and all that he did in Egypt,
"and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.

"And our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, 'Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them, and say to them, We are your servants; and now cut a covenant with us.'
"This our bread — we took it warm as our provisions from our homes on the day we came out to go to you; and now, behold, it is dry and crumbling.
"And these wineskins that we filled were new, and behold, they have split. And these garments of ours and our sandals have worn out from the very great length of the journey."
And the men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask the mouth of YHWH.
And Joshua made peace with them and cut a covenant with them, to let them live; and the leaders of the congregation swore to them.
And it was at the end of three days, after they had cut a covenant with them, that they heard that they were near to them and that they were dwelling in their midst.
And the sons of Israel set out and came to their cities on the third day; and their cities were Gibeon and Kephirah and Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim.
And the sons of Israel did not strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by YHWH, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
And all the leaders said to the whole congregation, "We have sworn to them by YHWH, the God of Israel; and now we are not able to touch them.
"This we will do to them: let them live, so that there be no wrath upon us because of the oath that we swore to them."
And the leaders said to them, "Let them live." And they became cutters of wood and drawers of water for the whole congregation, just as the leaders had spoken to them.
And Joshua summoned them and spoke to them, saying, "Why did you deceive us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when you are dwelling in our midst?
"And now you are cursed, and none of you shall ever cease to be a slave — cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God."

And they answered Joshua and said, "Because it was surely told to your servants that YHWH your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. So we feared greatly for our lives because of you, and we did this thing.
"And now, behold, we are in your hand. As it is good and right in your eyes to do to us, do."
And he did so to them, and delivered them from the hand of the sons of Israel, and they did not kill them.
And Joshua made them on that day cutters of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of YHWH, to this day, at the place that he would choose.

joshua_10.t: And it was, when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction — as he had done to Jericho and to its king, so he had done to Ai and to its king — and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were in their midst,
that they feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
And Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron and to Piram king of Jarmuth and to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,
"Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the sons of Israel."

And the five kings of the Amorites — the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon — gathered and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped against Gibeon and fought against it.

And the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands drop from your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country have gathered against us."
And Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valour.
And YHWH said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not a man of them shall stand before you."
And Joshua came upon them suddenly; all the night he had gone up from Gilgal.
And YHWH routed them before Israel, and he struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and as far as Makkedah.

And it was, as they fled before Israel — they were at the descent of Beth-horon — that YHWH threw down great stones on them from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than those whom the sons of Israel killed with the sword.
Then Joshua spoke to YHWH, on the day YHWH gave the Amorites over before the sons of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel: "Sun, at Gibeon be still, and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon."

And the sun was still, and the moon stood, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Scroll of Jashar? And the sun stood in the middle of the heavens and did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.
And there has been no day like that one, before it or after it, when YHWH listened to the voice of a man; for YHWH was fighting for Israel.
And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
And those five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
And it was told to Joshua, saying, "The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah."
And Joshua said, "Roll great stones against the mouth of the cave, and appoint men over it to guard them.
"But you, do not stand still. Pursue after your enemies and attack their rear. Do not let them go into their cities, for YHWH your God has given them into your hand."
And it was, when Joshua and the sons of Israel had finished striking them with a very great defeat until they were finished, and the survivors who survived of them had gone into the fortified cities,
that all the people returned to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah, in peace. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the sons of Israel.
And Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring out to me those five kings from the cave."
And they did so, and brought out to him those five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon.

And it was, when they brought out those kings to Joshua, that Joshua summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near, put your feet on the necks of these kings." And they came near and put their feet on their necks.
And Joshua said to them, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Be strong and be bold, for thus YHWH will do to all your enemies whom you are fighting."
And afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees; and they were hanging on the trees until the evening.

And it was, at the time of the going down of the sun, that Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and put great stones over the mouth of the cave, which are there to this very day.

And Makkedah Joshua captured on that day, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king; he devoted them to destruction, and every person who was in it — he left no survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Makkedah to Libnah, and fought against Libnah.

And YHWH gave it also into the hand of Israel, and its king; and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who was in it — he left no survivor in it. And he did to its king just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Libnah to Lachish, and encamped against it and fought against it.

And YHWH gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who was in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he had left him no survivor.
And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Lachish to Eglon, and they encamped against it and fought against it.
And they captured it on that day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who was in it he devoted to destruction on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
And Joshua went up, and all Israel with him, from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.

And they captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and all its cities and every person who was in it — he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon; and he devoted it to destruction, and every person who was in it.
And Joshua turned back, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it.

And he captured it and its king and all its cities, and they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every person who was in it — he left no survivor. Just as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and to its king, and just as he had done to Libnah and to its king.

And Joshua struck all the land — the hill country and the Negev and the Shephelah and the slopes — and all their kings. He left no survivor, and every breathing thing he devoted to destruction, just as YHWH the God of Israel had commanded.
And Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea as far as Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, as far as Gibeon.
And all these kings and their land Joshua captured at one time, because YHWH the God of Israel was fighting for Israel.
And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

joshua_11.t: And it was, when Jabin king of Hazor heard, that he sent to Jobab king of Madon and to the king of Shimron and to the king of Acshaph,
and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country and in the Arabah south of Kinnereth and in the Shephelah and on the heights of Dor to the west,
to the Canaanite in the east and in the west, and the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
And they came out, they and all their armies with them, a people numerous as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude, and horses and chariots very many.
And all these kings met together, and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom to fight with Israel.

And YHWH said to Joshua, "Do not fear because of them, for tomorrow about this time I am giving all of them over, slain, before Israel. Their horses you shall hamstring and their chariots you shall burn with fire."
And Joshua came upon them, and all the people of war with him, at the waters of Merom suddenly, and they fell upon them.

And YHWH gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Greater Sidon and as far as Misrephoth-maim and as far as the Valley of Mizpeh eastward; and they struck them until he had left them no survivor.
And Joshua did to them just as YHWH had said to him: their horses he hamstrung and their chariots he burned with fire.
And Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor, and its king he struck with the sword; for Hazor was formerly the head of all these kingdoms.
And they struck every person who was in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction; not any breathing thing was left. And Hazor he burned with fire.
And all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, Joshua captured, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, just as Moses the servant of YHWH had commanded.
Only all the cities that stood on their mounds Israel did not burn — except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock the sons of Israel plundered for themselves; only every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them — they did not leave any breathing thing.
Just as YHWH had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that YHWH had commanded Moses.
And Joshua took all this land: the hill country and all the Negev and all the land of Goshen and the Shephelah and the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel and its Shephelah,
from Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. And all their kings he captured and struck and put to death.
For many days Joshua made war with all these kings.
There was not a city that made peace with the sons of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon; all of them they took in battle.

For it was from YHWH to harden their heart to meet Israel in battle, so that they might be devoted to destruction and have no favour, but that they might be destroyed, just as YHWH had commanded Moses.

And Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel; with their cities Joshua devoted them to destruction.
No Anakim were left in the land of the sons of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath and in Ashdod did they remain.

And Joshua took all the land, according to all that YHWH had spoken to Moses; and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions, by their tribes. And the land had rest from war.

joshua_12.t: And these are the kings of the land whom the sons of Israel struck, and whose land they took possession of beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the middle of the wadi, and half of Gilead, as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon;
and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Kinnereth eastward, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth-jeshimoth; and from the south, under the slopes of Pisgah;
and the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
and ruling over Mount Hermon and over Salecah and over all Bashan as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of YHWH and the sons of Israel struck them; and Moses the servant of YHWH gave it as a possession to the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

And these are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the sons of Israel struck beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon as far as Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir; and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession, according to their divisions:

in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Arabah and on the slopes and in the wilderness and in the Negev: the Hittite, the Amorite and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.
The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Acshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor, of the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goyim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. All the kings were thirty-one.

joshua_13.t: And Joshua was old, come into days; and YHWH said to him, "You are old, you have come into days, and very much of the land remains to be taken possession of.
"This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites,

"from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, as far as the border of Ekron to the north — it is reckoned to the Canaanite: the five rulers of the Philistines, the Gazite, the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite; and the Avvim,
"from the south: all the land of the Canaanite, and Mearah which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, as far as the border of the Amorite;
"and the land of the Gebalite, and all Lebanon toward the rising of the sun, from Baal-gad under Mount Hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.

"All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians — I myself will dispossess them before the sons of Israel. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, just as I commanded you.
"And now apportion this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
With it the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan eastward, just as Moses the servant of YHWH gave them:
from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the wadi, and all the plain of Medeba as far as Dibon,
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the sons of Ammon;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei — he was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. And Moses struck them and dispossessed them.
But the sons of Israel did not dispossess the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath have dwelt in the midst of Israel to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance: the food offerings of YHWH, the God of Israel — that is its inheritance, just as he spoke to it.
And Moses gave to the tribe of the sons of Reuben, by their clans;
and their territory was from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the wadi, and all the plain by Medeba;
Heshbon and all its cities that are in the plain: Dibon and Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,
and Jahaz and Kedemoth and Mephaath,
and Kiriathaim and Sibmah and Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
and Beth-peor and the slopes of Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck, with the leaders of Midian — Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who dwelt in the land.
And Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, the sons of Israel killed with the sword among their slain.
And the border of the sons of Reuben was the Jordan and its territory. This was the inheritance of the sons of Reuben by their clans, the cities and their villages.
And Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad, by their clans;
and their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the sons of Ammon, as far as Aroer which is before Rabbah;
and from Heshbon as far as Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim as far as the territory of Lo-debar;

and in the valley: Beth-haram and Beth-nimrah and Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and its territory, as far as the end of the Sea of Kinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward.
This was the inheritance of the sons of Gad by their clans, the cities and their villages.
And Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh; and it belonged to the half-tribe of the sons of Manasseh by their clans.
And their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;
and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, belonged to the sons of Machir son of Manasseh, to half of the sons of Machir by their clans.
These are the inheritances that Moses apportioned in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan of Jericho, eastward.
And to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: YHWH, the God of Israel — he is their inheritance, just as he spoke to them.

joshua_14.t: And these are what the sons of Israel inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the sons of Israel gave them as an inheritance,
by the lot of their inheritance, just as YHWH commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he gave no inheritance in their midst.

For the sons of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and they gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and for their property.
Just as YHWH commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did, and they apportioned the land.

And the sons of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know the word that YHWH spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh-barnea.
"I was a son of forty years when Moses the servant of YHWH sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him back word just as it was with my heart.
"But my brothers who went up with me melted the heart of the people, while I filled up after YHWH my God.
"And Moses swore on that day, saying, 'Surely the land on which your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance for you and for your children for ever, because you have filled up after YHWH my God.'

"And now, behold, YHWH has kept me alive, just as he spoke, these forty-five years since YHWH spoke this word to Moses, when Israel walked in the wilderness. And now, behold, I am today a son of eighty-five years.
"I am still today as strong as on the day Moses sent me; as my strength was then, so is my strength now, for war and for going out and for coming in.

"And now give me this hill country of which YHWH spoke on that day; for you yourself heard on that day that the Anakim were there and cities great and fortified. Perhaps YHWH will be with me, and I shall dispossess them, just as YHWH spoke."
And Joshua blessed him, and he gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he filled up after YHWH, the God of Israel.
And the name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-arba — he was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.

joshua_15.t: And the lot for the tribe of the sons of Judah, by their clans, was toward the border of Edom, the Wilderness of Zin, southward, from the far end of the south.
And their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces southward;
and it goes out south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and passes on to Zin, and goes up south of Kadesh-barnea and passes on to Hezron, and goes up to Addar and turns to Karka,
and passes on to Azmon and goes out at the Wadi of Egypt; and the extremities of the border are at the sea. This shall be your southern border.
And the eastern border is the Salt Sea as far as the end of the Jordan. And the border on the northern side is from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan;
and the border goes up to Beth-hoglah and passes north of Beth-arabah; and the border goes up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben;

and the border goes up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and northward it turns toward Gilgal, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, which is south of the wadi; and the border passes on to the waters of En-shemesh, and its extremities are at En-rogel;

and the border goes up the Valley of Ben-hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite — that is Jerusalem; and the border goes up to the top of the mountain that faces the Valley of Hinnom on the west, which is at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim;
and the border bends from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and goes out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border bends to Baalah — that is Kiriath-jearim;
and the border turns from Baalah westward to Mount Seir and passes on to the northern slope of Mount Jearim — that is Kesalon — and goes down to Beth-shemesh and passes on to Timnah;
and the border goes out to the northern slope of Ekron, and the border bends to Shikkeron and passes on to Mount Baalah and goes out at Jabneel; and the extremities of the border are at the sea.
