Or two days, or a month, or days — when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle to settle over it, the sons of Israel would encamp and would not set out; and when it was taken up they would set out.
At the mouth of YHWH they would encamp, and at the mouth of YHWH they would set out. The charge of YHWH they kept, at the mouth of YHWH by the hand of Moses.

numbers_10.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Make for yourself two trumpets of silver; of hammered work you shall make them. And they shall be for you for the convoking of the congregation and for the breaking of the camps.
And they shall blow on them, and all the congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And if they blow on one, the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather to you.
And when you blow an alarm, the camps encamping eastward shall set out.
And when you blow an alarm a second time, the camps encamping southward shall set out. An alarm they shall blow for their settings out.
And when the assembly is to be summoned, you shall blow, but you shall not sound an alarm.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and they shall be for you a statute of perpetuity for your generations.

And when you go to war in your land against the foe who presses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before YHWH your God, and you will be delivered from your enemies.

And on the day of your rejoicing, and at your appointed times, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be for you a memorial before your God. I am YHWH your God.
And it was, in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, that the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
And the sons of Israel set out on their journeyings from the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
And they set out for the first time at the mouth of YHWH by the hand of Moses.
And the standard of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first, by their hosts; and over its host was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, the bearers of the tabernacle, set out.
And the standard of the camp of Reuben set out, by their hosts; and over its host was Elizur son of Shedeur;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
And the Kohathites set out, the bearers of the sanctuary; and the tabernacle was set up before they came.
And the standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out, by their hosts; and over its host was Elishama son of Ammihud;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
And the standard of the camp of the sons of Dan set out, the rearguard of all the camps, by their hosts; and over its host was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
and over the host of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan;
These are the settings out of the sons of Israel by their hosts; and they set out.

And Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses: We are setting out to the place of which YHWH said, I will give it to you. Come with us and we will do good to you, for YHWH has spoken good concerning Israel.
And he said to him: I will not go, but to my own land and to my kindred I will go.
And he said: Do not, please, leave us; for you know our encamping in the wilderness, and you shall be for us as eyes.
And it shall be, if you go with us, that the same good with which YHWH does good to us, we will do good to you.
And they set out from the mountain of YHWH a journey of three days; and the ark of the covenant of YHWH set out before them a journey of three days, to search out for them a resting place.
And the cloud of YHWH was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
And it was, when the ark set out, that Moses said: Rise up, YHWH, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee from before you.
And when it rested, he said: Return, YHWH, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.

numbers_11.t: And the people were as those who complain of misfortune in the ears of YHWH; and YHWH heard, and his anger burned, and the fire of YHWH burned among them and consumed at the edge of the camp.
And the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to YHWH, and the fire died down.
And the name of that place was called Taberah, because the fire of YHWH had burned among them.
And the rabble that was in their midst craved a craving, and the sons of Israel also turned and wept and said: Who will feed us meat?
We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers and the melons and the leeks and the onions and the garlic.
And now our appetite is dry; there is nothing at all, except that our eyes are on the manna.
And the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.
The people would go about and gather it and grind it in hand-mills or pound it in a mortar, and boil it in a pot and make it into cakes; and its taste was like the taste of a rich cake of oil.
And when the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
And Moses heard the people weeping by their clans, each at the entrance of his tent; and the anger of YHWH burned exceedingly, and in the eyes of Moses it was bad.
And Moses said to YHWH: Why have you dealt badly with your servant, and why have I not found favour in your eyes, that you put the burden of all this people on me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you say to me, Carry them in your bosom as the foster-father carries the suckling child, to the land that you swore to their fathers?
From where do I have meat to give to all this people? For they weep to me, saying, Give us meat, that we may eat.
I am not able, I alone, to carry all this people, for it is too heavy for me.
And if this is how you are dealing with me, kill me, please, killing — if I have found favour in your eyes — and let me not look on my misery.

And YHWH said to Moses: Gather to me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people and its officials; and take them to the tent of meeting, and let them station themselves there with you.

And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them; and they shall carry with you in the burden of the people, and you shall not carry it, you alone.

And to the people you shall say: Set yourselves apart as holy for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, because you have wept in the ears of YHWH, saying, Who will feed us meat? For it was good for us in Egypt. And YHWH will give you meat, and you shall eat.
You shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,

until a month of days, until it comes out of your nose and becomes loathsome to you — because you have rejected YHWH who is in your midst and have wept before him, saying, Why did we ever come out of Egypt?
And Moses said: Six hundred thousand on foot are the people in whose midst I am, and you have said, I will give them meat, and they shall eat a month of days.
Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, and be enough for them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, and be enough for them?
And YHWH said to Moses: Is the hand of YHWH short? Now you will see whether my word will happen to you or not.
And Moses went out and spoke to the people the words of YHWH; and he gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

And YHWH came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy men, the elders. And when the spirit rested on them, they prophesied — and they did not do so again.

And two men had remained in the camp — the name of the one was Eldad and the name of the second Medad — and the spirit rested on them; and they were among those written down, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
And the young man ran and told Moses and said: Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.
And Joshua son of Nun, the attendant of Moses from his youth, answered and said: My lord Moses, restrain them!
And Moses said to him: Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the people of YHWH were prophets, that YHWH would put his spirit on them!
And Moses gathered himself back into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

And a wind set out from YHWH and drove quails in from the sea and let them fall by the camp, about a day's journey this way and a day's journey that way, around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the ground.
And the people rose all that day and all the night and all the next day and gathered the quail — the one who gathered least gathered ten homers — and they spread them out, spreading, around the camp.
The meat was still between their teeth, not yet chewed, when the anger of YHWH burned against the people, and YHWH struck the people with a very great blow.
And the name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out to Hazeroth, and they were at Hazeroth.

numbers_12.t: And Miriam spoke, and Aaron, against Moses on account of the Cushite woman he had taken — for he had taken a Cushite woman.
And they said: Has YHWH spoken only, only through Moses? Has he not also spoken through us? And YHWH heard.
And the man Moses was very humble, more than every human being who was on the face of the earth.
And YHWH said suddenly to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam: Go out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting. And the three of them went out.
And YHWH came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam; and the two of them went out.
And he said: Hear now my words: If there is a prophet of yours, YHWH, in a vision I make myself known to him, in a dream I speak with him.
Not so my servant Moses; in all my house he is faithful.
Mouth to mouth I speak with him, and in sight, and not in riddles; and the form of YHWH he beholds. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?
And the anger of YHWH burned against them, and he went.
And the cloud departed from over the tent, and there was Miriam, struck with leprosy, like snow. And Aaron turned to Miriam, and there — struck with leprosy.
And Aaron said to Moses: Pardon, my lord, do not, please, lay on us the sin in which we have acted foolishly and in which we have sinned.
Let her not, please, be like the dead one, who, when he comes out of his mother's womb, half his flesh is eaten away.
And Moses cried out to YHWH, saying: God, please, heal, please, her!

And YHWH said to Moses: And if her father had spat, spitting, in her face, would she not be shamed seven days? Let her be shut up seven days outside the camp, and afterwards she shall be gathered back.
And Miriam was shut up outside the camp seven days; and the people did not set out until Miriam was gathered back.
And afterwards the people set out from Hazeroth, and they encamped in the wilderness of Paran.

numbers_13.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:

Send for yourself men, that they may scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel. One man, one man for the tribe of his fathers you shall send, every one a leader among them.
And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the mouth of YHWH; all of them men who were heads of the sons of Israel.
And these are their names: for the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
for the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
for the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
for the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
for the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
for the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
for the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
for the tribe of Joseph, for the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
for the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
for the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
for the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
for the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Maki;
These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to scout out the land. And Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
And Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan, and said to them: Go up here into the Negev, and go up into the hill country.
And you shall see the land, what it is; and the people who dwell on it, whether they are strong or feeble, whether they are few or many;
and what the land is in which they dwell, whether it is good or bad; and what the cities are in which they dwell, whether in camps or in fortresses;

and what the land is, whether it is fat or lean, whether there are trees in it or not. And you shall strengthen yourselves and take some of the fruit of the land. And the days were the days of the first ripe grapes.
And they went up and scouted out the land, from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, at Lebo-hamath.
And they went up into the Negev, and he came to Hebron; and there were Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak. And Hebron was built seven years before Zoan of Egypt.
And they came to the Wadi Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and carried it on a pole between two of them; and some of the pomegranates and some of the figs.
That place was called the Wadi Eshcol, on account of the cluster that the sons of Israel cut down from there.
And they returned from scouting out the land at the end of forty days.

And they went and came to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
And they recounted to him and said: We went to the land where you sent us, and it does indeed flow with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Nevertheless, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large; and we also saw there the descendants of Anak.
Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev; and the Hittite and the Jebusite and the Amorite dwell in the hill country; and the Canaanite dwells by the sea and along the Jordan.
And Caleb silenced the people towards Moses and said: Going up, let us go up and take possession of it, for prevailing we shall prevail over it.
But the men who had gone up with him said: We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are.

And they brought out an evil report of the land that they had scouted out, to the sons of Israel, saying: The land through which we passed to scout it out is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw in it are men of great stature.
And there we saw the Nephilim — the sons of Anak are from the Nephilim — and we were in our own eyes like grasshoppers, and so we were in their eyes.

numbers_14.t: And all the congregation lifted up and gave forth their voice, and the people wept that night.
And all the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them: If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or in this wilderness, if only we had died!
And why is YHWH bringing us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to return to Egypt?
And they said, each to his brother: Let us appoint a head and return to Egypt.
And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the sons of Israel.
And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, of those who scouted out the land, tore their clothes.
And they said to all the congregation of the sons of Israel: The land through which we passed to scout it out — the land is very, very good.
If YHWH delights in us, then he will bring us into this land and give it to us — a land that flows with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against YHWH; and you, do not fear the people of the land, for they are our bread. Their shade has departed from over them, and YHWH is with us. Do not fear them.
And all the congregation said to stone them with stones. And the glory of YHWH appeared at the tent of meeting to all the sons of Israel.
And YHWH said to Moses: How long will this people spurn me? And how long will they not believe in me, with all the signs that I have done in their midst?
I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they.
And Moses said to YHWH: But the Egyptians will hear, for you brought up this people by your strength from among them,

and they will say to the inhabitants of this land — they have heard that you, YHWH, are in the midst of this people, you who are seen eye to eye, YHWH, with your cloud standing over them, and in a pillar of cloud you go before them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night —
and you put this people to death as one man, then the nations that have heard your report will say:
Because YHWH was not able to bring this people to the land that he swore to them, he slaughtered them in the wilderness.
And now, let the power of the Lord be great, please, as you have spoken, saying:

YHWH is long of nostrils and abundant in steadfast love, bearing iniquity and transgression; but clearing, he will not clear — visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, upon the third and upon the fourth.
Forgive, please, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, and as you have borne with this people from Egypt until now.
And YHWH said: I have forgiven, according to your word.
But as I live, and as all the earth is filled with the glory of YHWH —
for all the men who have seen my glory and my signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice —
if they see the land that I swore to their fathers! And all who have spurned me shall not see it.
But my servant Caleb — because another spirit was with him and he filled after me — I will bring him to the land where he went, and his offspring shall take possession of it.
And the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley. Tomorrow turn and set out for yourselves to the wilderness, by the way of the Sea of Reeds.
And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
How long for this evil congregation, which is grumbling against me? The grumblings of the sons of Israel, which they are grumbling against me, I have heard.
Say to them: As I live — the declaration of YHWH — if I do not do to you just as you have spoken in my ears!
In this wilderness your corpses shall fall, and all your enrolled, according to your whole number, from a son of twenty years and upward, who have grumbled against me.
If you come into the land that I lifted my hand to settle you in! — except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And your little ones, of whom you said they would become plunder — I will bring them in, and they shall know the land that you have rejected.
And your corpses, yours, shall fall in this wilderness.
And your sons shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your whoredoms until your corpses are finished in the wilderness.
By the number of the days in which you scouted out the land, forty days — a day for the year, a day for the year — you shall bear your iniquities forty years; and you shall know my opposition.
I, YHWH, have spoken: if I do not do this to all this evil congregation that has gathered against me! In this wilderness they shall meet their end, and there they shall die.
And the men whom Moses sent to scout out the land, who returned and made all the congregation grumble against him by bringing out an evil report of the land —
the men who brought out the evil report of the land died by the plague before YHWH.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive of those men who went to scout out the land.
And Moses spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
And they rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the hill country, saying: Here we are, and we will go up to the place of which YHWH spoke, for we have sinned.
And Moses said: Why is it that you are crossing the mouth of YHWH? And it will not succeed.
Do not go up, for YHWH is not in your midst, that you not be defeated before your enemies.
For the Amalekite and the Canaanite are there before you, and you will fall by the sword — because you have turned back from following YHWH, and YHWH will not be with you.
But they presumed to go up to the top of the hill country; and the ark of the covenant of YHWH and Moses did not depart from the midst of the camp.
And the Amalekite and the Canaanite who dwelt in that hill country came down and struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah.

numbers_15.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land of your dwellings, which I am giving you,

and you make a food offering to YHWH — a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfil a vow, or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed times — to make an odour of soothing to YHWH, from the herd or from the flock,
then the one who brings his offering near shall bring near to YHWH a grain offering: a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
And wine for the drink offering, a quarter of a hin, you shall offer with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.
Or for a ram you shall offer a grain offering: two tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil;
and wine for the drink offering, a third of a hin, you shall bring near as an odour of soothing to YHWH.
And when you offer a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfil a vow, or as peace offerings to YHWH,
then he shall bring near with the young bull a grain offering: three tenths of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil;
and wine you shall bring near for the drink offering, half a hin — a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH.
Thus it shall be done for each bull, or for each ram, or for the young of the flock, among the lambs or among the goats.
According to the number that you offer, so you shall do for each one, according to their number.
Every native shall do thus with these things, to bring near a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH.
And when a sojourner sojourns with you, or whoever is among you throughout your generations, and offers a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH — just as you do, so he shall do.
The assembly — one statute for you and for the sojourner who sojourns; a statute of perpetuity throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the sojourner be before YHWH.
One law and one ordinance shall be for you and for the sojourner who sojourns with you.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land to which I am bringing you,
then, when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall lift up a contribution to YHWH.
The first of your dough, a loaf, you shall lift up as a contribution; like the contribution of the threshing floor, so you shall lift it up.
From the first of your dough you shall give a contribution to YHWH, throughout your generations.
And when you err and do not do all these commandments that YHWH has spoken to Moses —
all that YHWH has commanded you by the hand of Moses, from the day that YHWH commanded and onward, throughout your generations —

then, if it was done inadvertently, away from the eyes of the congregation, all the congregation shall offer one young bull for a burnt offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the ordinance; and one male goat for a sin offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the sons of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them, because it was inadvertence and they have brought their offering, a food offering to YHWH, and their sin offering before YHWH for their inadvertence.
And it shall be forgiven to all the congregation of the sons of Israel and to the sojourner who sojourns among them, because it happened to all the people inadvertently.
And if one person sins inadvertently, then she shall bring near a female goat, a daughter of its year, for a sin offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for the person who has gone astray in sinning inadvertently, before YHWH, to make atonement for him; and it shall be forgiven him.
For the native among the sons of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns among them — one law shall be for you, for the one who acts inadvertently.
But the person who acts with a high hand, whether of the native or of the sojourner — he is reviling YHWH, and that person shall be cut off from among his kin.
For he has despised the word of YHWH and has broken his commandment; cutting off, that person shall be cut off — his iniquity is on him.
And the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, and they found a man gathering wood on the sabbath day.
And those who found him gathering wood brought him near to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation.
And they left him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
And YHWH said to Moses: The man shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.
And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, just as YHWH had commanded Moses.
And YHWH said to Moses, saying:

Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them that they shall make for themselves tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and shall put on the tassel of each corner a cord of violet.

And it shall be a tassel for you: you shall look at it and remember all the commandments of YHWH and do them, and not scout out after your own heart and after your own eyes, after which you are whoring;
so that you may remember and do all my commandments and be holy to your God.
I am YHWH your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt to be God to you. I am YHWH your God.

numbers_16.t: And Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi took — and Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben —
and they rose up before Moses, with men of the sons of Israel, two hundred and fifty, leaders of the congregation, called of the appointed meeting, men of name.

And they assembled against Moses and against Aaron and said to them: Enough for you! For all the congregation, all of them, are holy, and YHWH is in their midst. And why do you lift yourselves up over the assembly of YHWH?
And Moses heard, and fell on his face.

And he spoke to Korah and to all his company, saying: In the morning YHWH will make known who is his and who is holy, and will bring him near to himself; the one whom he chooses he will bring near to himself.
Do this: take for yourselves censers, Korah and all his company,
and put fire in them and set incense on them before YHWH tomorrow. And the man whom YHWH chooses, he is the holy one. Enough for you, sons of Levi!
And Moses said to Korah: Hear now, sons of Levi!

Is it too little for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself, to serve the service of the tabernacle of YHWH and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
And he brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you — and you seek priesthood too?
Therefore you and all your company are the ones gathered against YHWH. And Aaron — what is he, that you should grumble against him?
And Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab; and they said: We will not come up.
Is it too little that you have brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you should also make yourself a ruler, a ruler, over us?
Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of field and vineyard. Will you gouge out the eyes of those men? We will not come up.
And Moses was very angry, and said to YHWH: Do not turn to their grain offering. Not one donkey have I taken from them, and I have not done harm to one of them.
And Moses said to Korah: You and all your company, be before YHWH — you and they and Aaron — tomorrow.
And take each man his censer and put incense on them, and bring near before YHWH each man his censer — two hundred and fifty censers — and you and Aaron, each his censer.
And they took each man his censer and put fire on them and set incense on them, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting — and Moses and Aaron.
And Korah assembled against them all the congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting; and the glory of YHWH appeared to all the congregation.
And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
Separate yourselves from among this congregation, and I will consume them in a moment.
And they fell on their faces and said: God, God of the spirits of all flesh — one man sins, and will you be angry with all the congregation?
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the congregation, saying: Take yourselves up from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.
And Moses arose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel went after him.
And he spoke to the congregation, saying: Turn away now from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that belongs to them, lest you be swept away in all their sins.

And they took themselves up from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives and their sons and their little ones.
And Moses said: By this you shall know that YHWH has sent me to do all these works, and that it is not from my own heart:
If these men die like the death of every human, and the visitation of every human is visited upon them, then YHWH has not sent me.
But if YHWH creates a creation, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them, and they go down alive to Sheol, then you will know that these men have spurned YHWH.
And it was, as he finished speaking all these words, that the ground which was under them was split open.
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, and every person who belonged to Korah, and all the property.
And they went down, they and all that belonged to them, alive to Sheol, and the earth covered over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
And all Israel who were around them fled at their voice, for they said: Lest the earth swallow us!
And fire came forth from YHWH and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were bringing near the incense.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Say to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest that he take up the censers from among the burning, and scatter the fire far off; for they have become holy —

the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives. And they shall make them into beaten plates, an overlay for the altar, for they brought them near before YHWH and they became holy; and they shall be a sign for the sons of Israel.
And Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that those who were burned had brought near, and they beat them out as an overlay for the altar,

a reminder to the sons of Israel, so that no strange man who is not of the offspring of Aaron should draw near to turn incense to smoke before YHWH, and not be like Korah and like his company — just as YHWH had spoken by the hand of Moses concerning him.
And on the next day all the congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of YHWH.
And it was, when the congregation assembled against Moses and against Aaron, that they turned towards the tent of meeting, and behold, the cloud had covered it, and the glory of YHWH appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Get up from among this congregation, and I will make an end of them in a moment. And they fell on their faces.

And Moses said to Aaron: Take the censer and put fire on it from the altar and set incense on it, and go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them; for the wrath has gone out from before YHWH, the plague has begun.
And Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the midst of the assembly, and behold, the plague had begun among the people. And he put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was restrained.
And those who died by the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides those who died over the matter of Korah.
And Aaron returned to Moses, to the entrance of the tent of meeting; and the plague had been restrained.

numbers_17.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:

Speak to the sons of Israel and take from them a staff, a staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders by their ancestral houses — twelve staffs. Each man's name you shall write on his staff.
And Aaron's name you shall write on the staff of Levi, for there shall be one staff for the head of their ancestral house.
And you shall deposit them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
And it shall be that the man whom I choose, his staff will bud; and I will put an end to the grumblings of the sons of Israel from upon me, which they are grumbling against you.

And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders gave him a staff for each leader, a staff for each leader, by their ancestral houses — twelve staffs; and the staff of Aaron was among their staffs.
And Moses deposited the staffs before YHWH in the tent of the testimony.

And it was, on the next day, that Moses came into the tent of the testimony, and behold, the staff of Aaron of the house of Levi had budded: it had put forth a bud and blossomed a blossom and ripened almonds.
And Moses brought out all the staffs from before YHWH to all the sons of Israel; and they looked, and each man took his staff.

And YHWH said to Moses: Put back the staff of Aaron before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the sons of rebellion; and you shall put an end to their grumblings from upon me, so that they do not die.
And Moses did just as YHWH had commanded him; so he did.
And the sons of Israel said to Moses: Look, we are perishing, we are lost, all of us are lost!
Everyone who draws near, who draws near to the tabernacle of YHWH, will die. Are we to be finished off entirely, to perish?

numbers_18.t: And YHWH said to Aaron: You and your sons and your father's house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.

And also your brothers, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, bring near with you, and let them join themselves to you and minister to you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the tent of the testimony.
And they shall keep your charge and the charge of all the tent; only to the articles of the holy place and to the altar they shall not draw near, so that they do not die, neither they nor you.
And they shall join themselves to you and keep the charge of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the tent; and a stranger shall not draw near to you.
And you shall keep the charge of the holy place and the charge of the altar, so that there shall be no more wrath upon the sons of Israel.
And I, here, I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel; to you they are a gift, given to YHWH, to serve the service of the tent of meeting.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil, and you shall serve. As a service of gift I give your priesthood; and the stranger who draws near shall be put to death.

And YHWH spoke to Aaron: And I, here, I have given you the charge of my contributions. Of all the holy gifts of the sons of Israel I have given them to you as a portion, and to your sons, as a prescribed portion of perpetuity.

This shall be yours from the most holy things, from the fire: every offering of theirs — every grain offering of theirs and every sin offering of theirs and every guilt offering of theirs, which they give back to me — it is most holy for you and for your sons.
In the most holy place you shall eat it; every male shall eat it. It shall be holy for you.

And this is yours: the contribution of their gift, of all the wave offerings of the sons of Israel. To you I have given them, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a prescribed portion of perpetuity; everyone who is clean in your household may eat it.
All the best of the fresh oil, and all the best of the new wine and the grain — their first fruits, which they give to YHWH — to you I have given them.
The firstfruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to YHWH, shall be yours; everyone who is clean in your household may eat it.
Every devoted thing in Israel shall be yours.

Every firstborn of the womb, of all flesh, which they bring near to YHWH, whether human or animal, shall be yours; only you shall surely redeem the firstborn of humankind, and the firstborn of the unclean animal you shall redeem.
And its redemption price, from a month old, you shall redeem, at your valuation: silver, five shekels by the shekel of the holy place — twenty gerahs is that.

Only the firstborn of a cow or the firstborn of a sheep or the firstborn of a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. Their blood you shall dash on the altar, and their fat you shall turn to smoke, a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH.
And their meat shall be yours; like the breast of the wave offering and like the right thigh, it shall be yours.

All the contributions of the holy gifts that the sons of Israel lift up to YHWH I have given to you, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a prescribed portion of perpetuity. It is a covenant of salt for ever before YHWH, for you and for your offspring with you.
And YHWH said to Aaron: In their land you shall have no inheritance, and no share shall be yours among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
And to the sons of Levi, here, I have given every tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in return for their service that they serve, the service of the tent of meeting.
And the sons of Israel shall not draw near again to the tent of meeting, to bear sin and die.

And the Levite, he shall serve the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity. It is a statute of perpetuity throughout your generations; and among the sons of Israel they shall not inherit an inheritance.

For the tithe of the sons of Israel, which they lift up to YHWH as a contribution, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance; therefore I have said of them: Among the sons of Israel they shall not inherit an inheritance.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:

And to the Levites you shall speak and say to them: When you take from the sons of Israel the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, then you shall lift up from it a contribution to YHWH, a tithe of the tithe.
And your contribution shall be reckoned to you as the grain from the threshing floor and as the full yield from the winepress.
So you also shall lift up a contribution to YHWH from all your tithes that you take from the sons of Israel; and from it you shall give the contribution of YHWH to Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts you shall lift up every contribution of YHWH, from all the best of it, its holy part from it.
And you shall say to them: When you lift up the best of it from it, then it shall be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and as the produce of the winepress.
And you may eat it in any place, you and your household, for it is your wages in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
And you shall not bear sin over it when you lift up the best of it from it; and you shall not profane the holy gifts of the sons of Israel, so that you do not die.

numbers_19.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:

This is the statute of the law which YHWH has commanded, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them take to you a red heifer, unblemished, in which there is no blemish, upon which no yoke has gone up.
And you shall give her to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring her out to outside the camp, and one shall slaughter her before him.
And Eleazar the priest shall take some of her blood with his finger, and he shall sprinkle, toward the front of the face of the tent of meeting, some of her blood seven times.
And one shall burn the heifer before his eyes; her skin and her flesh and her blood, along with her offal, he shall burn.
And the priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet, and he shall throw them into the middle of the burning of the heifer.
And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp; and the priest shall be unclean until the evening.
And the one who burns her shall wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he shall be unclean until the evening.

And a clean man shall gather the ashes of the heifer and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place; and it shall be for the congregation of the sons of Israel as something kept, for water of impurity — it is a sin offering.

And the one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and he shall be unclean until the evening. And it shall be for the sons of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns among them a statute of perpetuity.
The one who touches a dead body, of any corpse of a human — he shall be unclean seven days.
He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day, then on the seventh day he shall not be clean.

Everyone who touches a dead body, the corpse of the human who dies, and does not purify himself — he has defiled the tabernacle of YHWH, and that person shall be cut off from Israel; because the water of impurity was not dashed on him he shall be unclean, his uncleanness is still on him.
This is the law: a human, when he dies in a tent — everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in the tent shall be unclean seven days.
And every open vessel which has no cover of a cord upon it — it is unclean.
And everyone who touches, on the face of the field, one slain of a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a human, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
And they shall take for the unclean one some of the dust of the burning of the sin offering, and he shall put living water upon it, into a vessel.

And a clean person shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and he shall sprinkle upon the tent and upon all the articles and upon the persons who were there, and upon the one who touched the bone, or the slain one, or the dead body, or the grave.

And the clean one shall sprinkle upon the unclean one on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall purify him from sin on the seventh day; and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be clean in the evening.

And a person who becomes unclean and does not purify himself — that person shall be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of YHWH; the water of impurity has not been dashed on him, he is unclean.

And it shall be for them a statute of perpetuity. And the one who sprinkles the water of impurity shall wash his clothes, and the one who touches the water of impurity shall be unclean until the evening.
And everything that the unclean one touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches shall be unclean until the evening.

numbers_20.t: And the sons of Israel came, the whole congregation, to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people settled in Kadesh. And Miriam died there, and she was buried there.
And there was no water for the congregation, and they assembled against Moses and against Aaron.
And the people quarrelled with Moses, and they said, saying: If only we had died when our brothers died before YHWH!
And why have you brought the assembly of YHWH into this wilderness, to die there, we and our livestock?
And why did you bring us up from Egypt, to bring us to this evil place? It is not a place of seed and fig and vine and pomegranate, and there is no water to drink.
And Moses and Aaron went from before the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and they fell on their faces; and the glory of YHWH appeared to them.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:

Take the staff and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and you shall speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water; and you shall bring out for them water from the rock, and you shall give the congregation and their livestock drink.
And Moses took the staff from before YHWH, just as he had commanded him.
And Moses and Aaron assembled the assembly before the face of the rock, and he said to them, Listen now, you rebels: from this rock shall we bring out water for you?
And Moses raised his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice, and much water came out, and the congregation drank, and their livestock.

And YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron: Because you did not believe in me, to treat me as holy before the eyes of the sons of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.
These are the waters of Meribah, where the sons of Israel quarrelled with YHWH, and he showed himself holy among them.
And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: Thus says your brother Israel, You know all the hardship that has come upon us,
and our fathers went down to Egypt, and we dwelt in Egypt many days, and Egypt did harm to us and to our fathers.
And we cried out to YHWH, and he heard our voice and sent a messenger and brought us out from Egypt. And here we are in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your territory.

Let us pass, please, through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, and we will not drink water of a well. We will go by the king's way; we will not turn aside right or left until we have passed through your territory.
And Edom said to him: You shall not pass through me, lest with the sword I come out to meet you.

And the sons of Israel said to him: We will go up by the highway, and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give their price. Only — it is no matter — let me pass through on my feet.
And he said: You shall not pass through. And Edom came out to meet him with a massive people and with a strong hand.
And Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory, and Israel turned aside from him.
And they set out from Kadesh, and the sons of Israel came, the whole congregation, to Hor the mountain.
And YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron at Hor the mountain, on the border of the land of Edom, saying:
Aaron shall be gathered to his peoples, for he shall not enter the land that I have given to the sons of Israel, because you rebelled against my mouth at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to Hor the mountain.
And strip Aaron of his garments and clothe Eleazar his son with them; and Aaron shall be gathered and shall die there.
And Moses did just as YHWH commanded, and they went up to Hor the mountain before the eyes of the whole congregation.
And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and clothed Eleazar his son with them; and Aaron died there at the top of the mountain. And Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
And the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, and they wept for Aaron thirty days, all the house of Israel.

numbers_21.t: And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim, and he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
And Israel vowed a vow to YHWH and said: If you will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction.
And YHWH listened to the voice of Israel and gave up the Canaanite; and he devoted them and their cities to destruction, and one called the name of the place Hormah.
And they set out from Hor the mountain by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom; and the self of the people grew short on the way.

And the people spoke against God and against Moses: Why did you bring us up from Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and there is no water, and our self loathes this worthless bread.
And YHWH sent among the people the fiery serpents, and they bit the people, and many people of Israel died.
And the people came to Moses and said: We have sinned, for we have spoken against YHWH and against you. Pray to YHWH, that he may remove the serpent from upon us. And Moses prayed for the people.
And YHWH said to Moses: Make for yourself a fiery serpent and put it on a standard; and it shall be that everyone who is bitten shall see it and live.
And Moses made a serpent of bronze and put it on the standard; and it was, if the serpent had bitten anyone, that he looked to the serpent of bronze and lived.
And the sons of Israel set out and encamped at Oboth.
And they set out from Oboth and encamped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness that is on the face of Moab, from the rising of the sun.
From there they set out and encamped in the wadi of Zered.
From there they set out and encamped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that comes out from the territory of the Amorite; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorite.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of YHWH: Waheb in Suphah, and the wadis, Arnon,
and the slope of the wadis that extends to the dwelling of Ar and leans upon the border of Moab.
And from there to Beer. That is the well of which YHWH said to Moses: Gather the people, and let me give them water.
Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
A well — princes dug it, the nobles of the people hollowed it out, with the ruler's staff, with their staffs. And from the wilderness, Mattanah,
and from Mattanah, Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel, Bamoth;
and from Bamoth, the valley that is in the region of Moab, the top of the Pisgah, which looks down over the face of the wasteland.
And Israel sent messengers to Sihon the king of the Amorite, saying:
Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard; we will not drink water of a well. By the king's way we will go, until we have passed through your territory.
And Sihon did not allow Israel to pass through his territory; and Sihon gathered all his people and went out to meet Israel in the wilderness, and he came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
And Israel struck him with the mouth of the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the sons of Ammon; for the border of the sons of Ammon was strong.
And Israel took all these cities, and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorite, in Heshbon and in all her daughters.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorite; and he had waged war against the former king of Moab and had taken all his land from his hand, as far as the Arnon.
Therefore those who speak in proverbs say: Come to Heshbon! Let it be built, let the city of Sihon be established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the town of Sihon; it consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh! He has made his sons fugitives and his daughters captives, to Sihon, king of the Amorite.
And we overthrew them; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon; and we laid waste as far as Nophah, which is as far as Medeba.
And Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorite.
And Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they captured her daughters, and he dispossessed the Amorite who was there.
And they turned and went up by the way of the Bashan; and Og the king of the Bashan came out to meet them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

And YHWH said to Moses: Do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land; and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon the king of the Amorite, who dwelt in Heshbon.
And they struck him and his sons and all his people, until there was no survivor left to him; and they took possession of his land.

numbers_22.t: And the sons of Israel set out and encamped in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan of Jericho.
And Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorite.
And Moab was very afraid because of the people, for it was numerous; and Moab felt dread because of the sons of Israel.
And Moab said to the elders of Midian: Now the company will lick up all our surroundings, as the ox licks up the greenery of the field. And Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

And he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, to Pethor which is by the River, the land of the sons of his people, to summon him, saying: Behold, a people has come out from Egypt; behold, it has covered the eye of the land, and it is settling opposite me.

And now, come, please, curse this people for me, for it is too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall be able to strike it and drive it out from the land; for I know that whom you bless is blessed, and whom you curse is cursed.
And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went, with divinations in their hand, and they came to Balaam and spoke to him the words of Balak.
And he said to them: Lodge here this night, and I will bring back word to you just as YHWH speaks to me. And the leaders of Moab stayed with Balaam.
And God came to Balaam and said: Who are these men with you?
And Balaam said to God: Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me:
Behold, the people that has come out from Egypt has covered the eye of the land. Now come, put a curse on it for me; perhaps I shall be able to fight against it and drive it out.
And God said to Balaam: You shall not go with them. You shall not curse the people, for it is blessed.
And Balaam rose in the morning and said to the leaders of Balak: Go to your land, for YHWH has refused to let me go with you.
And the leaders of Moab rose and came to Balak and said: Balaam has refused to come with us.
And Balak sent again — leaders more numerous and more honoured than these.
And they came to Balaam and said to him: Thus says Balak son of Zippor: Do not, please, let yourself be restrained from coming to me,
for I will indeed honour you exceedingly, and all that you say to me I will do. And come, please, put a curse on this people for me.

And Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak: If Balak were to give me the fullness of his house in silver and gold, I could not transgress the mouth of YHWH my God, to do a small thing or a great one.
And now, stay, please, here — you also — this night, so that I may know what YHWH will say further with me.
And God came to Balaam at night and said to him: If the men have come to summon you, rise, go with them; but only the word that I speak to you, that shall you do.
And Balaam rose in the morning and saddled his donkey and went with the leaders of Moab.
And the anger of God burned because he was going; and the messenger of YHWH stationed himself in the road as an opponent to him. And he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

And the donkey saw the messenger of YHWH stationed in the road, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turned aside from the road and went into the field. And Balaam struck the donkey, to turn her back to the road.
And the messenger of YHWH stood in the narrow way of the vineyards, a wall on this side and a wall on that side.
And the donkey saw the messenger of YHWH, and she pressed herself against the wall and pressed Balaam's foot against the wall; and he struck her again.
And the messenger of YHWH went on further and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn aside, right or left.
And the donkey saw the messenger of YHWH, and she lay down under Balaam; and Balaam's anger burned, and he struck the donkey with the stick.
And YHWH opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam: What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?
And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you have made a fool of me. If there were a sword in my hand, I would kill you now.
And the donkey said to Balaam: Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life until this day? Have I ever been in the habit of doing so to you? And he said: No.
And YHWH uncovered the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the messenger of YHWH stationed in the road, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed low and prostrated himself on his face.
And the messenger of YHWH said to him: For what have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I myself came out as an opponent, for the way is perverse before me.
And the donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from before me, surely now I would have killed you and let her live.
And Balaam said to the messenger of YHWH: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were stationed to meet me in the road. And now, if it is evil in your eyes, I will turn back for myself.
And the messenger of YHWH said to Balaam: Go with the men; but only the word that I speak to you, that shall you speak. And Balaam went with the leaders of Balak.
And Balak heard that Balaam had come, and he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, which is at the end of the territory.
And Balak said to Balaam: Did I not indeed send to you to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to honour you?
And Balaam said to Balak: Behold, I have come to you. Now — am I really able to speak anything at all? The word that God puts in my mouth, that I shall speak.
And Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
And Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent to Balaam and to the leaders who were with him.
And it was in the morning that Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal; and from there he saw the outskirts of the people.

numbers_23.t: And Balaam said to Balak: Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams.
And Balak did just as Balaam had spoken, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.
And Balaam said to Balak: Station yourself by your burnt offering, and let me go; perhaps YHWH will come to meet me, and whatever word he shows me I will tell you. And he went to a bare height.
And God met Balaam, and he said to him: The seven altars I have arranged, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.
And YHWH put a word in Balaam's mouth and said: Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.
And he returned to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, he and all the leaders of Moab.
And he lifted up his oracle and said: From Aram Balak led me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east: Come, curse Jacob for me, and come, denounce Israel.
How shall I put a curse on one whom God has not put a curse on, and how shall I denounce one whom YHWH has not denounced?
For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I observe him. Behold, a people that dwells alone, and among the nations does not reckon itself.
Who has counted the dust of Jacob, or numbered the fourth part of Israel? Let my self die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.
And Balak said to Balaam: What have you done to me? I took you to put a curse on my enemies, and behold, you have indeed blessed them.
And he answered and said: Is it not what YHWH puts in my mouth that I must take care to speak?
And Balak said to him: Come, please, with me to another place from which you will see him; only his outskirts you will see, and all of him you will not see; and put a curse on him for me from there.
And he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of the Pisgah, and he built seven altars and offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.
And he said to Balak: Station yourself here by your burnt offering, and I will meet [him] over there.
And YHWH met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said: Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.
And he came to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, and the leaders of Moab with him. And Balak said to him: What has YHWH spoken?
And he lifted up his oracle and said: Rise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of humankind, that he should change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or spoken, and will he not fulfil it?
Behold, I have received [a charge] to bless; and he has blessed, and I cannot turn it back.
He has not looked upon misfortune in Jacob, nor has he seen trouble in Israel. YHWH his God is with him, and the shout of a king is among him.
God is bringing them out from Egypt; he has, as it were, the horns of a wild ox.
For there is no enchantment against Jacob, and no divination against Israel. At this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel: What has God done!
Behold, a people rises like a lioness, and like a lion it lifts itself up. It will not lie down until it devours the prey and drinks the blood of the slain.
And Balak said to Balaam: Neither put a curse on them at all, nor bless them at all.
And Balaam answered and said to Balak: Did I not speak to you, saying, All that YHWH speaks, that I will do?
And Balak said to Balaam: Come, please, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will be right in the eyes of God, and you will put a curse on them for me from there.
And Balak took Balaam to the top of the Peor, which looks down over the face of the wasteland.
And Balaam said to Balak: Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams.
And Balak did just as Balaam had said, and he offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.

numbers_24.t: And Balaam saw that it was good in the eyes of YHWH to bless Israel, and he did not go, as time after time, to meet omens; but he set his face toward the wilderness.
And Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel dwelling by its tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him.
And he lifted up his declaration and said: The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, and the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
the declaration of one who hears the sayings of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and with eyes uncovered:
How good are your tents, Jacob, your dwelling places, Israel!
Like wadis stretched out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes that YHWH has planted, like cedars beside waters.
Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters. His king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be lifted up.
God is bringing him out from Egypt; he has, as it were, the horns of a wild ox. He shall devour the nations, his adversaries, and break their bones, and shatter his arrows.
He crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a lioness — who will rouse him? Blessed be those who bless you, and cursed be those who curse you.
And Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he clapped his hands. And Balak said to Balaam: To put a curse on my enemies I summoned you, and behold, you have indeed blessed them these three times.
And now, flee to your place. I said I would indeed honour you, and behold, YHWH has withheld you from honour.
And Balaam said to Balak: Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,
If Balak were to give me the fullness of his house in silver and gold, I could not transgress the mouth of YHWH, to do good or evil out of my own heart. What YHWH speaks, that I will speak.
And now, behold, I am going to my people. Come, let me advise you what this people will do to your people at the end of the days.
And he lifted up his declaration and said: The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, and the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
the declaration of one who hears the sayings of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and with eyes uncovered:

I see him, but not now; I observe him, but not near. A star has marched forth from Jacob, and a sceptre has risen from Israel; and it shall shatter the corners of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
And Edom shall become a possession, and Seir, his enemies, shall become a possession; and Israel shall do valiantly.
And one from Jacob shall rule, and he shall destroy the survivor from a city.
And he saw Amalek, and he lifted up his oracle and said: The first of the nations was Amalek, and his end shall be to destruction.
And he saw the Kenite, and he lifted up his oracle and said: Enduring is your dwelling, and set in the rock is your nest.
Yet Kain shall be for burning — how long until Asshur takes you captive?
And he lifted up his oracle and said: Woe! Who shall live when God does this?
And ships from the hand of Kittim, and they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber; and he also shall come to destruction.
And Balaam rose and went and returned to his place; and Balak also went on his way.

numbers_25.t: And Israel dwelt in Shittim, and the people began to whore with the daughters of Moab.
And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
And Israel joined itself to Baal Peor, and the anger of YHWH burned against Israel.
And YHWH said to Moses: Take all the heads of the people and impale them to YHWH before the sun, so that the burning of the anger of YHWH may turn away from Israel.
And Moses said to the judges of Israel: Kill, each man, his men who have joined themselves to Baal Peor.

And behold, a man from the sons of Israel came and brought near to his brothers the Midianite woman, before the eyes of Moses and before the eyes of all the congregation of the sons of Israel; and they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, and he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
And he went after the man of Israel into the chamber and pierced the two of them through — the man of Israel and the woman, into her belly. And the plague was held back from upon the sons of Israel.
And those who died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:

Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back my wrath from upon the sons of Israel by being zealous with my zeal among them, so that I did not make an end of the sons of Israel in my zeal.
Therefore say: Behold, I am giving to him my covenant, peace.
And it shall be for him and for his seed after him a covenant of perpetual priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.
And the name of the man of Israel who was struck down, who was struck down with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of a father's house of the Simeonites.
And the name of the woman who was struck down, the Midianite, was Cozbi daughter of Zur; he was head of the tribes of a father's house in Midian.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Be hostile to the Midianites, and you shall strike them down;

for they are hostile to you with their deceits, with which they deceived you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.

numbers_26.t: And it was after the plague that YHWH said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, saying:
Take the sum of all the congregation of the sons of Israel, from a son of twenty years and upward, by the house of their fathers, everyone going out to the host in Israel.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab at the Jordan of Jericho, saying:
From a son of twenty years and upward — just as YHWH commanded Moses and the sons of Israel who came out from the land of Egypt.
Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These are the clans of the Reubenites; and their enrolled were three and forty thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.

And the sons of Eliab: Nemuel and Dathan and Abiram. That is the Dathan and Abiram, the called of the congregation, who contended against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they contended against YHWH,
and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah, when that company died, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men; and they became a sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The sons of Simeon by their clans: of Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;
of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These are the clans of the Simeonites: two and twenty thousand and two hundred.
The sons of Gad by their clans: of Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; of Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;
of Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; of Eri, the clan of the Erites;
of Arod, the clan of the Arodites; of Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad, according to their enrolled: forty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Judah: Er and Onan. And Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Judah by their clans were: of Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; of Perez, the clan of the Perezites; of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
And the sons of Perez were: of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These are the clans of Judah, according to their enrolled: six and seventy thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Issachar by their clans: Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the clan of the Punites;
of Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These are the clans of Issachar, according to their enrolled: four and sixty thousand and three hundred.
The sons of Zebulun by their clans: of Sered, the clan of the Seredites; of Elon, the clan of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These are the clans of the Zebulunites, according to their enrolled: sixty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the clan of the Machirites; and Machir fathered Gilead; of Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; of Helek, the clan of the Helekites;
and Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; and Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites;
and Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; and Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
And Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, but only daughters; and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh; and their enrolled were two and fifty thousand and seven hundred.
These are the sons of Ephraim by their clans: of Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the clan of the Becherites; of Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
And these are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These are the clans of the sons of Ephraim, according to their enrolled: two and thirty thousand and five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph by their clans.
The sons of Benjamin by their clans: of Bela, the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
of Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
And the sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: the clan of the Ardites; of Naaman, the clan of the Naamanites.
These are the sons of Benjamin by their clans; and their enrolled were five and forty thousand and six hundred.
These are the sons of Dan by their clans: of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan by their clans.
All the clans of the Shuhamites, according to their enrolled: four and sixty thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Asher by their clans: of Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the clan of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
And the name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
These are the clans of the sons of Asher, according to their enrolled: three and fifty thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Naphtali by their clans: of Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
of Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These are the clans of Naphtali by their clans; and their enrolled were five and forty thousand and four hundred.
These are the enrolled of the sons of Israel: six hundred thousand and one thousand, seven hundred and thirty.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, by the number of names.
To the many you shall make his inheritance great, and to the few you shall make his inheritance small; each according to his enrolled shall his inheritance be given.
Only by lot shall the land be divided; by the names of the tribes of their fathers shall they inherit.
According to the lot shall his inheritance be divided, between the many and the few.
And these are the enrolled of the Levite by their clans: of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; of Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These are the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. And Kohath fathered Amram.
And the name of Amram's wife was Jochebed, daughter of Levi, whom she bore to Levi in Egypt; and she bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister.
And to Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And Nadab and Abihu died when they brought near strange fire before YHWH.

And their enrolled were three and twenty thousand, every male from a son of a month and upward; for they were not enrolled among the sons of Israel, because no inheritance was given to them among the sons of Israel.
These are the enrolled of Moses and Eleazar the priest, who enrolled the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab at the Jordan of Jericho.
And among these there was no man from the enrolled of Moses and Aaron the priest, who enrolled the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
For YHWH had said of them: They shall surely die in the wilderness. And not a man was left of them, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

numbers_27.t: And the daughters of Zelophehad drew near — son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. And these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the leaders and all the congregation, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, saying:
Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the company that gathered against YHWH in the company of Korah; for he died in his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be withdrawn from among his clan because he has no son? Give us a possession among the brothers of our father.
And Moses brought their case near before YHWH.
And YHWH said to Moses, saying:

Rightly do the daughters of Zelophehad speak. You shall surely give them a possession of an inheritance among the brothers of their father, and you shall cause the inheritance of their father to pass over to them.
And to the sons of Israel you shall speak, saying: A man, when he dies and has no son, you shall cause his inheritance to pass over to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
And if he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his relative who is nearest to him from his clan, and he shall take possession of it. And it shall be for the sons of Israel a statute of judgement, just as YHWH commanded Moses.
And YHWH said to Moses: Go up to this mountain of the Abarim and see the land that I have given to the sons of Israel.
And when you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your peoples, just as Aaron your brother was gathered,

since you rebelled against my mouth in the wilderness of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to treat me as holy at the waters before their eyes. Those are the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
And Moses spoke to YHWH, saying:
Let YHWH, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
who will go out before them and who will come in before them, who will lead them out and who will bring them in, so that the congregation of YHWH may not be like sheep that have no shepherd.
And YHWH said to Moses: Take for yourself Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is spirit, and lay your hand upon him.
And you shall make him stand before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, and you shall commission him before their eyes.
And you shall put some of your majesty upon him, so that all the congregation of the sons of Israel may hear.

And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and he shall enquire for him by the judgement of the Urim before YHWH. At his mouth they shall go out, and at his mouth they shall come in — he and all the sons of Israel with him, and all the congregation.
And Moses did just as YHWH commanded him, and he took Joshua and made him stand before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation.
And he laid his hands upon him and commissioned him, just as YHWH had spoken by the hand of Moses.

numbers_28.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Command the sons of Israel and say to them: My offering, my food, for my food offerings, my odour of soothing, you shall take care to bring near to me at its appointed time.
And you shall say to them: This is the food offering that you shall bring near to YHWH: lambs, sons of a year, unblemished, two a day, a continual burnt offering.
The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer between the evenings,
and a tenth of the ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil.
It is a continual burnt offering, the one instituted at Mount Sinai, for an odour of soothing, a food offering to YHWH.
And its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place pour out a drink offering of strong drink to YHWH.
