And the second lamb you shall offer between the evenings; like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you shall offer it, a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH.
And on the sabbath day: two lambs, sons of a year, unblemished, and two tenths of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
It is the burnt offering of the sabbath on its sabbath, besides the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
And at the beginnings of your months you shall bring near a burnt offering to YHWH: two bulls, sons of the herd, and one ram, seven lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and three tenths of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, for the one bull; and two tenths of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, for the one ram;
and a tenth, a tenth, of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, for the one lamb. It is a burnt offering, an odour of soothing, a food offering to YHWH.

And their drink offerings: half a hin of wine shall be for the bull, and a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for the lamb. This is the burnt offering of a month in its month, for the months of the year.
And one male goat of the goats for a sin offering to YHWH; besides the continual burnt offering it shall be offered, and its drink offering.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is a Passover to YHWH.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is a festival; seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On the first day is a convocation of holiness; any work of servitude you shall not do.
And you shall bring near a food offering, a burnt offering to YHWH: two bulls, sons of the herd, and one ram, and seven lambs, sons of a year — unblemished they shall be for you;
and their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil; three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram you shall offer.
A tenth, a tenth, you shall offer for the one lamb, for the seven lambs.
And one male goat of a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
Besides the burnt offering of the morning, which is for the continual burnt offering, you shall offer these.
Like these you shall offer daily, seven days, the food of a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH; besides the continual burnt offering it shall be offered, and its drink offering.
And on the seventh day there shall be for you a convocation of holiness; any work of servitude you shall not do.
And on the day of the firstfruits, when you bring near a new grain offering to YHWH at your Weeks, there shall be for you a convocation of holiness; any work of servitude you shall not do.
And you shall bring near a burnt offering for an odour of soothing to YHWH: two bulls, sons of the herd, one ram, seven lambs, sons of a year;
and their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil; three tenths for the one bull, two tenths for the one ram,
a tenth, a tenth, for the one lamb, for the seven lambs;
one male goat of the goats, to make atonement for you.
Besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering you shall offer them — unblemished they shall be for you — and their drink offerings.

numbers_29.t: And in the seventh month, on the first of the month, there shall be for you a convocation of holiness; any work of servitude you shall not do. It shall be for you a day of a loud blast.
And you shall offer a burnt offering for an odour of soothing to YHWH: one bull, a son of the herd, one ram, seven lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil; three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for the one lamb, for the seven lambs;
and one male goat of the goats, a sin offering, to make atonement for you;

besides the burnt offering of the new moon and its grain offering, and the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings according to their ordinance, for an odour of soothing, a food offering to YHWH.
And on the tenth of this seventh month there shall be for you a convocation of holiness, and you shall afflict your selves; any work you shall not do.
And you shall bring near a burnt offering to YHWH, an odour of soothing: one bull, a son of the herd, one ram, seven lambs, sons of a year — unblemished they shall be for you;
and their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil; three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
a tenth, a tenth, for the one lamb, for the seven lambs;
one male goat of the goats, a sin offering, besides the sin offering of the atonements and the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month there shall be for you a convocation of holiness; any work of servitude you shall not do. And you shall celebrate a festival to YHWH seven days.
And you shall bring near a burnt offering, a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH: thirteen bulls, sons of the herd, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year — unblemished they shall be;
and their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil; three tenths for the one bull, for the thirteen bulls; two tenths for the one ram, for the two rams;
and a tenth, a tenth, for the one lamb, for the fourteen lambs;
and one male goat of the goats, a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
And on the second day: twelve bulls, sons of the herd, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
and one male goat of the goats, a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
And on the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
and one male goat of a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
And on the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
and one male goat of the goats, a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
And on the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
and one male goat of a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
And on the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
and one male goat of a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offerings.
And on the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams and for the lambs, by their number, according to their ordinance;
and one male goat of a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the eighth day there shall be for you a solemn assembly; any work of servitude you shall not do.
And you shall bring near a burnt offering, a food offering, an odour of soothing to YHWH: one bull, one ram, seven lambs, sons of a year, unblemished;
their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance;
and one male goat of a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.

These you shall offer to YHWH at your appointed times, apart from your vows and your freewill offerings — for your burnt offerings and for your grain offerings and for your drink offerings and for your peace offerings.
And Moses said to the sons of Israel according to all that YHWH had commanded Moses.

numbers_30.t: And Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the sons of Israel, saying: This is the word that YHWH has commanded.
A man, when he vows a vow to YHWH or swears an oath to bind an obligation upon his self, shall not profane his word; according to all that goes out from his mouth he shall do.
And a woman, when she vows a vow to YHWH and binds an obligation in her father's house in her youth,

and her father hears her vow and her obligation that she has bound upon her self, and her father keeps silent toward her — then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation that she has bound upon her self shall stand.
But if her father forbids her on the day he hears, none of her vows or her obligations that she has bound upon her self shall stand; and YHWH will forgive her, because her father forbade her.
And if she indeed belongs to a husband, and her vows are upon her, or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound her self —
and her husband hears on the day he hears and keeps silent toward her — then her vows shall stand, and her obligations by which she has bound her self shall stand.
But if on the day her husband hears he forbids her and breaks her vow which is upon her and the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound her self, then YHWH will forgive her.
But the vow of a widow or a divorced woman — everything by which she has bound her self shall stand upon her.
And if in her husband's house she vowed, or bound an obligation upon her self by an oath,
and her husband heard and kept silent toward her, and did not forbid her — then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation that she bound upon her self shall stand.

But if her husband indeed breaks them on the day he hears, everything that has gone out of her lips, as to her vows and as to the obligation of her self, shall not stand; her husband has broken them, and YHWH will forgive her.
Every vow and every oath of obligation to afflict the self — her husband may confirm it, and her husband may break it.

But if her husband indeed keeps silent toward her from day to day, then he has confirmed all her vows or all her obligations that are upon her; he has confirmed them, because he kept silent toward her on the day he heard.
But if he indeed breaks them after he has heard, then he shall bear her iniquity.
These are the statutes that YHWH commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father's house.

numbers_31.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Avenge the vengeance of the sons of Israel from the Midianites; afterward you shall be gathered to your peoples.
And Moses spoke to the people, saying: Equip men from among you for the host, and let them be against Midian, to give the vengeance of YHWH on Midian.
A thousand for the tribe, a thousand for the tribe, for all the tribes of Israel you shall send out to the host.
And there were handed over from the thousands of Israel a thousand for the tribe: twelve thousand, armed for the host.
And Moses sent them, a thousand for the tribe, to the host — them and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the host, with the articles of the holy place and the trumpets of the blast in his hand.
And they waged war against Midian, just as YHWH commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
And the kings of Midian they killed along with their slain: Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian; and Balaam son of Beor they killed with the sword.
And the sons of Israel took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and all their cattle and all their livestock and all their wealth they plundered.
And all their cities in their dwelling places, and all their encampments, they burned with fire.
And they took all the spoil and all the booty, in humankind and in livestock.

And they brought to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to the congregation of the sons of Israel the captives and the booty and the spoil, to the camp, to the plains of Moab that are at the Jordan of Jericho.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them, to outside the camp.
And Moses was angry with the officers of the force, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who were coming from the campaign of the battle.
And Moses said to them: Have you let every female live?
Behold, these were the ones who, by the word of Balaam, caused the sons of Israel to hand over unfaithfulness against YHWH in the matter of Peor; and the plague was among the congregation of YHWH.
And now, kill every male among the little ones, and every woman who has known a man by lying with a male, kill.
But all the little ones among the women who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves.

And you, encamp outside the camp seven days. Everyone who has killed a person and everyone who has touched a slain one — you shall purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
And every garment and every article of hide and every product of goats' hair and every article of wood you shall purify.
And Eleazar the priest said to the men of the host who had gone to the battle: This is the statute of the law that YHWH commanded Moses.
Only the gold and the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin and the lead —

every thing that goes into the fire you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be purified with the water of impurity. And everything that does not go into the fire you shall pass through the water.
And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you shall be clean; and afterward you shall come into the camp.
And YHWH said to Moses, saying:
Take the sum of the booty that was captured, in humankind and in livestock — you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the fathers of the congregation.
And you shall halve the booty between those who took part in the battle, who went out to the host, and all the congregation.
And you shall raise a levy for YHWH from the men of war who went out to the host: one person out of five hundred, from the humankind and from the cattle and from the donkeys and from the sheep.
From their half you shall take it, and you shall give it to Eleazar the priest as a contribution of YHWH.

And from the half of the sons of Israel you shall take one drawn out of fifty, from the humankind, from the cattle, from the donkeys and from the sheep, from all the livestock; and you shall give them to the Levites who keep the charge of the tabernacle of YHWH.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest did just as YHWH commanded Moses.
And the booty, the remainder of the plunder that the people of the host had plundered, was: sheep, six hundred thousand and seventy thousand and five thousand;
and cattle, two and seventy thousand;
and donkeys, one and sixty thousand;
and persons of humankind, from the women who had not known lying with a male: every person, two and thirty thousand.
And the half, the portion of those who went out in the host, was: the number of the sheep, three hundred thousand and thirty thousand and seven thousand and five hundred;
and the levy for YHWH from the sheep was six hundred and seventy-five;
and the cattle were six and thirty thousand, and their levy for YHWH was two and seventy;
and the donkeys were thirty thousand and five hundred, and their levy for YHWH was one and sixty;
and the persons of humankind were sixteen thousand, and their levy for YHWH was two and thirty persons.
And Moses gave the levy, the contribution of YHWH, to Eleazar the priest, just as YHWH commanded Moses.
And from the half of the sons of Israel, which Moses divided from the men who went to war —
and the congregation's half was, from the sheep, three hundred thousand and thirty thousand, seven thousand and five hundred;
and cattle, six and thirty thousand;
and donkeys, thirty thousand and five hundred;
and persons of humankind, sixteen thousand.

And Moses took from the half of the sons of Israel the one drawn out of fifty, from the humankind and from the livestock, and gave them to the Levites who keep the charge of the tabernacle of YHWH, just as YHWH commanded Moses.
And the officers who were over the thousands of the host drew near to Moses — the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds —
and they said to Moses: Your servants have taken the sum of the men of war who were in our hand, and not a man of us is missing.

And we have brought near the offering of YHWH — each man what he found, an article of gold, an armlet and a bracelet, a signet ring, an earring and a necklace — to make atonement for our selves before YHWH.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, every article of workmanship.
And all the gold of the contribution that they raised for YHWH was sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels, from the commanders of thousands and from the commanders of hundreds.
The men of the host had plundered, each man for himself.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, a memorial for the sons of Israel before YHWH.

numbers_32.t: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad had much livestock, very numerous. And they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and behold, the place was a place for livestock.
And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben came and said to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation, saying:
Ataroth and Dibon and Jazer and Nimrah and Heshbon and Elealeh and Sebam and Nebo and Beon —
the land that YHWH struck down before the congregation of Israel — it is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.
And they said: If we have found favour in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants for a possession; do not make us cross the Jordan.
And Moses said to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Reuben: Shall your brothers go to the battle, and you sit here?
And why do you turn away the heart of the sons of Israel from crossing into the land that YHWH has given them?
Thus your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
And they went up as far as the wadi of Eshcol and saw the land, and they turned away the heart of the sons of Israel, so as not to go into the land that YHWH had given them.
And the anger of YHWH burned on that day, and he swore an oath, saying:
Surely the men who came up from Egypt, from a son of twenty years and upward, shall not see the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob — because they have not filled up after me.
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua son of Nun, for they have filled up after YHWH.
And the anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in the eyes of YHWH was finished.
And behold, you have risen up in place of your fathers, a brood of sinful men, to add still more to the burning of the anger of YHWH against Israel.
For if you turn back from after him, he will again leave them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.
And they drew near to him and said: We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones,

and we ourselves will equip ourselves in haste before the sons of Israel, until we have brought them to their place; and our little ones shall dwell in the fortified cities, because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our houses until the sons of Israel have inherited, each man his inheritance.
For we will not inherit with them beyond the Jordan and further on, because our inheritance has come to us beyond the Jordan, eastward.
And Moses said to them: If you do this thing, if you equip yourselves before YHWH for the battle,
and every equipped man of you crosses the Jordan before YHWH until he has dispossessed his enemies from before him,
and the land is subdued before YHWH, and afterward you return — then you shall be free of obligation toward YHWH and toward Israel, and this land shall be yours for a possession before YHWH.
But if you do not do so, behold, you have sinned against YHWH; and know your sin, that it will find you out.
Build for yourselves cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep; and what has gone out of your mouth you shall do.
And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben said to Moses, saying: Your servants will do just as my lord commands.
Our little ones, our wives, our livestock and all our cattle shall be there, in the cities of the Gilead.
And your servants will cross over, every man equipped for the host, before YHWH to the battle, just as my lord says.
And Moses commanded concerning them Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the sons of Israel.

And Moses said to them: If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, every man equipped for the battle before YHWH, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of the Gilead for a possession.
But if they do not cross over equipped with you, then they shall take possession among you in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben answered, saying: What YHWH has spoken to your servants, so we will do.
We ourselves will cross over equipped before YHWH into the land of Canaan, and with us shall be the possession of our inheritance beyond the Jordan.

And Moses gave to them — to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Reuben and to the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph — the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorite and the kingdom of Og king of the Bashan: the land with its cities within their borders, the cities of the land round about.
And the sons of Gad built Dibon and Ataroth and Aroer,
and Atroth-shophan and Jazer and Jogbehah,
and Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities and sheepfolds.
And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon and Elealeh and Kiriathaim,
and Nebo and Baal-meon — their names changed — and Sibmah; and they called by names the names of the cities that they built.
And the sons of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, and he dispossessed the Amorite who was in it.
And Moses gave the Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he dwelt in it.
And Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their tent-villages, and he called them Havvoth-jair.
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its daughters, and he called it Nobah, by his own name.

numbers_33.t: These are the stages of the sons of Israel, who came out from the land of Egypt by their hosts, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
And Moses wrote down their points of departure by their stages, at the mouth of YHWH; and these are their stages by their points of departure.
And they set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the sons of Israel went out with a high hand, before the eyes of all Egypt,
while Egypt were burying those whom YHWH had struck down among them, every firstborn; and on their gods YHWH had executed judgements.
And the sons of Israel set out from Rameses and encamped at Succoth.
And they set out from Succoth and encamped at Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
And they set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which is opposite Baal-zephon, and encamped before Migdol.
And they set out from before Hahiroth and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, and they went a journey of three days in the wilderness of Etham and encamped at Marah.
And they set out from Marah and came to Elim; and at Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they encamped there.
And they set out from Elim and encamped by the Sea of Reeds.
And they set out from the Sea of Reeds and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
And they set out from the wilderness of Sin and encamped at Dophkah.
And they set out from Dophkah and encamped at Alush.
And they set out from Alush and encamped at Rephidim; and there was no water there for the people to drink.
And they set out from Rephidim and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
And they set out from the wilderness of Sinai and encamped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
And they set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and encamped at Hazeroth.
And they set out from Hazeroth and encamped at Rithmah.
And they set out from Rithmah and encamped at Rimmon-perez.
And they set out from Rimmon-perez and encamped at Libnah.
And they set out from Libnah and encamped at Rissah.
And they set out from Rissah and encamped at Kehelathah.
And they set out from Kehelathah and encamped at Mount Shepher.
And they set out from Mount Shepher and encamped at Haradah.
And they set out from Haradah and encamped at Makheloth.
And they set out from Makheloth and encamped at Tahath.
And they set out from Tahath and encamped at Terah.
And they set out from Terah and encamped at Mithkah.
And they set out from Mithkah and encamped at Hashmonah.
And they set out from Hashmonah and encamped at Moseroth.
And they set out from Moseroth and encamped at Bene-jaakan.
And they set out from Bene-jaakan and encamped at Hor-haggidgad.
And they set out from Hor-haggidgad and encamped at Jotbathah.
And they set out from Jotbathah and encamped at Abronah.
And they set out from Abronah and encamped at Ezion-geber.
And they set out from Ezion-geber and encamped in the wilderness of Zin, that is Kadesh.
And they set out from Kadesh and encamped at Hor the mountain, on the border of the land of Edom.

And Aaron the priest went up to Hor the mountain at the mouth of YHWH and died there, in the fortieth year of the coming out of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first of the month.
And Aaron was a son of a hundred and twenty-three years when he died on Hor the mountain.
And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who was dwelling in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the sons of Israel.
And they set out from Hor the mountain and encamped at Zalmonah.
And they set out from Zalmonah and encamped at Punon.
And they set out from Punon and encamped at Oboth.
And they set out from Oboth and encamped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
And they set out from Iyim and encamped at Dibon-gad.
And they set out from Dibon-gad and encamped at Almon-diblathaim.
And they set out from Almon-diblathaim and encamped in the mountains of the Abarim, before Nebo.
And they set out from the mountains of the Abarim and encamped in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan of Jericho.
And they encamped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
And YHWH spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan of Jericho, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

then you shall dispossess all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and you shall destroy all their figured stones, and all their images of cast metal you shall destroy, and all their high places you shall demolish.
And you shall take possession of the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.

And you shall inherit the land by lot according to your clans: to the many you shall make his inheritance great, and to the few you shall make his inheritance small; wherever the lot falls for him, there it shall be his. By the tribes of your fathers you shall inherit.

But if you do not dispossess the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those of them whom you leave shall be as thorns in your eyes and as pricks in your sides, and they shall be hostile to you on the land in which you are dwelling.
And it shall be that as I intended to do to them, I will do to you.

numbers_34.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Command the sons of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land of Canaan — this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan by its borders.
And your southern side shall be from the wilderness of Zin along the hands of Edom; and your southern border shall be from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.

And the border shall turn for you from the south to the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass on toward Zin, and its extremities shall be south of Kadesh-barnea; and it shall go out to Hazar-addar and pass on toward Azmon.
And the border shall turn from Azmon toward the Wadi of Egypt, and its extremities shall be at the sea.
And the western border: the Great Sea shall be for you a border; this shall be for you the western border.
And this shall be for you the northern border: from the Great Sea you shall mark out for yourselves Hor the mountain.
From Hor the mountain you shall mark out to Lebo-hamath, and the extremities of the border shall be at Zedad.
And the border shall go out to Ziphron, and its extremities shall be at Hazar-enan. This shall be for you the northern border.
And you shall mark out for yourselves the eastern border, from Hazar-enan toward Shepham.
And the border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain; and the border shall go down and reach to the shoulder of the Sea of Kinnereth, eastward.
And the border shall go down to the Jordan, and its extremities shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land by its borders round about.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, which YHWH has commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

For the tribe of the sons of the Reubenite by their ancestral house, and the tribe of the sons of the Gadite by their ancestral house, have taken theirs; and the half-tribe of Manasseh have taken their inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have taken their inheritance beyond the Jordan of Jericho, eastward toward the sunrise.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
These are the names of the men who shall apportion the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
And one leader, one leader from each tribe, you shall take to apportion the land as an inheritance.
And these are the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
and of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
and of the tribe of the sons of Dan, a leader: Bukki son of Jogli;
of the sons of Joseph: of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, a leader: Hanniel son of Ephod;
and of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, a leader: Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
and of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, a leader: Elizaphan son of Parnach;
and of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, a leader: Paltiel son of Azzan;
and of the tribe of the sons of Asher, a leader: Ahihud son of Shelomi;
and of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, a leader: Pedahel son of Ammihud.
These are those whom YHWH commanded to apportion an inheritance to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.

numbers_35.t: And YHWH spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan of Jericho, saying:

Command the sons of Israel that they give to the Levites, out of the inheritance of their possession, cities to dwell in; and pasture land for the cities round about them you shall give to the Levites.
And the cities shall be theirs to dwell in, and their pasture lands shall be for their cattle and for their property and for all their living creatures.
And the pasture lands of the cities that you shall give to the Levites shall be from the wall of the city outward, a thousand cubits round about.

And you shall measure outside the city: the east side two thousand by the cubit, and the south side two thousand by the cubit, and the west side two thousand by the cubit, and the north side two thousand by the cubit, with the city in the middle. This shall be theirs, the pasture lands of the cities.
And the cities that you shall give to the Levites: the six cities of refuge, which you shall give for the killer to flee there; and besides them you shall give forty-two cities.
All the cities that you shall give to the Levites: forty-eight cities, them and their pasture lands.

And the cities that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel: from the many you shall take more, and from the few you shall take less; each according to the inheritance that they inherit shall give some of its cities to the Levites.
And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then you shall provide for yourselves cities: cities of refuge they shall be for you, and a killer who has struck down a person by inadvertence shall flee there.
And the cities shall be for you a refuge from the avenger, and the killer shall not die until he has stood before the congregation for judgement.
And the cities that you shall give: six cities of refuge they shall be for you.
Three cities you shall give beyond the Jordan, and three cities you shall give in the land of Canaan; cities of refuge they shall be.
For the sons of Israel and for the sojourner and for the resident alien among them these six cities shall be a refuge, for anyone who strikes down a person by inadvertence to flee there.
But if he struck him with an instrument of iron and he died, he is a killer; the killer shall surely be put to death.
And if he struck him with a stone in the hand by which one may die, and he died, he is a killer; the killer shall surely be put to death.
Or if he struck him with a wooden instrument in the hand by which one may die, and he died, he is a killer; the killer shall surely be put to death.
The avenger of the blood, he shall put the killer to death; when he meets him, he shall put him to death.
And if in hatred he pushed him, or threw something at him while lying in wait, and he died,
or in enmity struck him with his hand and he died, the one who struck shall surely be put to death; he is a killer. The avenger of the blood shall put the killer to death when he meets him.
But if he pushed him in an instant, without enmity, or threw any object at him without lying in wait,
or with any stone by which one may die, without seeing him, and he dropped it on him and he died — and he was not his enemy and was not seeking his harm —
then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck and the avenger of the blood, according to these judgements.

And the congregation shall deliver the killer from the hand of the avenger of the blood, and the congregation shall return him to his city of refuge where he had fled, and he shall dwell in it until the death of the great priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer ever goes out beyond the border of his city of refuge, where he flees,
and the avenger of the blood finds him outside the border of his city of refuge, and the avenger of the blood kills the killer, there is no blood-guilt for him.
For he must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the great priest; and after the death of the great priest the killer may return to the land of his possession.
And these shall be for you a statute of judgement throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.
Anyone who strikes down a person — at the mouth of witnesses one shall kill the killer; but one witness shall not testify against a person to bring death.
And you shall not take a ransom for the life of a killer who is guilty and deserves to die; for he shall surely be put to death.
And you shall not take a ransom for one who has fled to his city of refuge, to let him return to dwell in the land before the death of the priest.

And you shall not pollute the land in which you are, for the blood, it pollutes the land; and for the land no atonement can be made for the blood that was shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
And you shall not make unclean the land in which you are dwelling, in the midst of which I dwell; for I, YHWH, dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel.

numbers_36.t: And the heads of the fathers of the clan of the sons of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, from the clans of the sons of Joseph, drew near and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the fathers of the sons of Israel,

and they said: YHWH commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the sons of Israel; and my lord was commanded by YHWH to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

But if they become wives to one of the sons of the tribes of the sons of Israel, then their inheritance will be withdrawn from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they will belong; and from the lot of our inheritance it will be withdrawn.

And if the jubilee comes for the sons of Israel, then their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they will belong; and from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers their inheritance will be withdrawn.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel at the mouth of YHWH, saying: Rightly does the tribe of the sons of Joseph speak.

This is the word that YHWH has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying: To whoever is good in their eyes let them become wives — only, to the clan of the tribe of their father let them become wives.
And an inheritance of the sons of Israel shall not go round from tribe to tribe, for each of the sons of Israel shall cling to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

And every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the sons of Israel shall become a wife to one of the clan of the tribe of her father, so that the sons of Israel may each possess the inheritance of his fathers.
And an inheritance shall not go round from one tribe to another tribe, for the tribes of the sons of Israel shall each cling to its own inheritance.
Just as YHWH commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.
And Mahlah, Tirzah and Hoglah and Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, became wives to the sons of their uncles.
From the clans of the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph they became wives, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of the clan of their father.
These are the commandments and the judgements that YHWH commanded by the hand of Moses to the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan of Jericho.

obadiah_1.t: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says Lord YHWH concerning Edom: A report we have heard from YHWH, and an envoy among the nations has been sent: "Arise, and let us arise against her for battle!"
Look, small I have made you among the nations; you are despised exceedingly.
The presumption of your heart has deceived you, O dweller in the clefts of the rock, the height of his dwelling, who says in his heart, "Who will bring me down to the ground?"
If you make [yourself] high like the eagle, and if among the stars your nest is set, from there I will bring you down — the declaration of YHWH.
If thieves came to you, if destroyers of the night — how you have been destroyed! — would they not steal their sufficiency? If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?
How Esau has been searched out, his hidden treasures laid bare!

To the border they have sent you, all the men of your covenant; they have deceived you, they have prevailed over you, the men of your peace. Your bread — they set a snare under you. There is no understanding in him.
Will I not on that day — the declaration of YHWH — destroy the wise from Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
And your warriors will be dismayed, O Teman, so that everyone may be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
Because of the violence to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off for ever.
On the day of your standing aloof, on the day strangers took captive his wealth, and foreigners entered his gates and over Jerusalem they cast a lot — you too were like one of them.

And do not look on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune, and do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day of their perishing, and do not make your mouth big on the day of distress.
Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; do not look, you too, on his calamity on the day of his disaster; and do not reach out for his wealth on the day of his disaster.
And do not stand at the parting of the ways to cut off his fugitives, and do not deliver up his survivors on the day of distress.
For the day of YHWH is near upon all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will return on your own head.
For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, all the nations will drink continually; and they will drink and swallow, and they will be as though they had not been.
But on the mountain of Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be a holy place, and the house of Jacob will take possession of their possessions.

And the house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble; and they will burn among them and consume them, and there will be no survivor to the house of Esau — for YHWH has spoken.

And those of the Negev will take possession of the mountain of Esau, and those of the Shephelah, of the Philistines; and they will take possession of the region of Ephraim and the region of Samaria, and Benjamin, of the Gilead.

And the exiles of this rampart, of the people of Israel, who are among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad, will take possession of the cities of the Negev.
And deliverers will go up on the mountain of Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingship will belong to YHWH.

proverbs_1.t: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:
To know wisdom and discipline, to understand sayings of understanding;
to receive the discipline of insight, righteousness and justice and equity;
to give shrewdness to the naive, to a youth knowledge and discretion —
Let the wise hear and increase learning, and let the discerning acquire guidance —
to understand a proverb and a figure, the words of the wise and their riddles.
The fear of YHWH is the beginning of knowledge; wisdom and discipline fools despise.
Listen, my son, to the discipline of your father, and do not reject the law of your mother.
For they are a wreath of favour for your head, and necklaces for your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.
If they say, "Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us lurk for the innocent without cause;
let us swallow them alive, like Sheol, and whole, like those going down to the pit;
all precious wealth we shall find, we shall fill our houses with plunder;
cast your lot among us, one purse will belong to us all" —
My son, do not walk in the way with them; hold back your foot from their path.
For their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed blood.
For in vain is the net spread in the eyes of any owner of a wing.
And they lie in wait for their own blood, they lurk for their own lives.
Such are the ways of everyone who takes unjust gain: it takes the life of its owners.
Wisdom cries aloud in the street, in the open squares she gives her voice.
At the head of the noisy places she calls out; at the entrances of the gates in the city she speaks her sayings:
"How long, you naive ones, will you love naivety? And mockers have delighted in mockery, and dullards hate knowledge.
If you turn back at my reproof, here, I will pour out my spirit to you, I will make my words known to you.
Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one was paying attention,
and you let go of all my counsel, and my reproof you did not want —
I also will laugh at your calamity, I will mock when your dread comes,
when your dread comes like devastation, and your calamity arrives like a storm-wind, when trouble and distress come upon you.
Then they will call me and I will not answer; they will seek me earnestly and will not find me,
because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of YHWH.
They did not want my counsel; they spurned all my reproof.
So they will eat from the fruit of their way, and be sated with their own schemes.
For the turning away of the naive will kill them, and the complacency of dullards will destroy them.
But one who listens to me will dwell in security and be at ease, without dread of harm."

proverbs_2.t: My son, if you receive my sayings and treasure up my commandments with you,
making your ear attend to wisdom, inclining your heart to discernment;
for if you call out to understanding, to discernment give your voice;
if you seek her like silver and search for her like hidden treasures,
then you will discern the fear of YHWH and find the knowledge of God.
For YHWH gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and discernment.
He stores up sound sense for the upright, a shield for those who walk in integrity,
guarding the paths of justice and preserving the way of his godly ones.
Then you will understand righteousness and justice and equity — every good course.
For wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your being;
discretion will watch over you, discernment will preserve you,
to deliver you from an evil way, from anyone speaking perversity,
those leaving the paths of uprightness to walk in the ways of darkness,
those glad to do evil, who exult in the perversity of evil,
whose paths are twisted, and who are crooked in their tracks;
to deliver you from a strange woman, from a foreign woman who has made her sayings smooth,
who leaves the close companion of her youth and has forgotten the covenant of her God;
for her house sinks down to death, and her tracks to the shades.
None who go in to her return, and they do not reach the paths of life.
So that you may walk in the way of the good and keep the paths of the righteous.
For the upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will remain in it.
But the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous will be torn away from it.

proverbs_3.t: My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart keep my commandments;
for length of days and years of life and peace they will add to you.
Let steadfast love and faithfulness not leave you; bind them on your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
And find favour and good insight in the eyes of God and humankind.
Trust in YHWH with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways know him, and he will make your paths straight.
Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear YHWH and turn aside from evil.
Let it be healing to your navel and refreshment to your bones.
Honour YHWH from your wealth and from the first of all your produce,
and your storehouses will be filled with plenty, and your vats will burst open with new wine.
The discipline of YHWH, my son, do not reject, and do not loathe his reproof;
for whom YHWH loves he reproves, and like a father the son he is pleased with.
How blessed is the person who finds wisdom, and the person who obtains discernment!
For her profit is better than the profit of silver, and her gain than fine gold.
She is more precious than corals, and none of your delights compare with her.
Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, wealth and honour.
Her ways are ways of kindness, and all her pathways are peace.
She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and those who hold her fast are called blessed.
YHWH by wisdom founded the earth, established the heavens by discernment;
by his knowledge the deeps were split open, and the clouds drip dew.
My son, do not let them depart from your eyes; keep sound sense and discretion,
and they will be life to your being and favour to your neck.
Then you will walk your way in security, and your foot will not strike.
If you lie down, you will not be afraid; you will lie down, and your sleep will be pleasant.
Do not be afraid of sudden terror, or of the devastation of the wicked when it comes,
for YHWH will be your confidence and will keep your foot from capture.
Do not withhold good from its owners when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
Do not say to your neighbour, "Go, and come back, and tomorrow I will give it" — when it is with you.
Do not devise harm against your neighbour when he is dwelling in security with you.
Do not contend with a person without cause, if he has not dealt you evil.
Do not envy a person of violence, and do not choose any of his ways.
For the crooked is an abomination to YHWH, but his intimacy is with the upright.
The curse of YHWH is on the house of the wicked, but the dwelling of the righteous he blesses.
Though he mocks the mockers, yet to the humble he gives favour.
The wise will inherit honour, but dullards — disgrace lifts them up.

proverbs_4.t: Listen, children, to a father's discipline, and be attentive, to know understanding;
for I give you good learning; do not neglect my law.
For I was a son to my father, tender and an only one before my mother.
And he taught me and said to me: "Let your heart hold fast to my words; keep my commandments and live.
Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget, and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.
Do not abandon her, and she will keep you; love her, and she will guard you.
The beginning of wisdom is: acquire wisdom, and with all your acquiring, acquire understanding.
Esteem her, and she will exalt you; she will honour you when you embrace her.
She will set on your head a wreath of favour; a crown of beauty she will give you."
Listen, my son, and receive my sayings, and the years of your life will be many.
In the way of wisdom I have taught you; I have led you in tracks of uprightness.
When you walk, your step will not be hindered, and if you run, you will not stumble.
Take hold of discipline, do not let go; keep her, for she is your life.
Do not go in the path of the wicked, and do not advance in the way of the evil.
Avoid it, do not pass along it; turn aside from it and pass on.
For they do not sleep unless they do harm; and their sleep is taken away unless they make someone stumble.
For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, going on and shining brighter until the day is full.
The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know on what they stumble.
My son, be attentive to my words; to my sayings incline your ear.
Do not let them depart from your eyes; keep them in the midst of your heart.
For they are life to those who find them, and health to all his flesh.
More than all guarding, guard your heart, for from it are the sources of life.
Put away from yourself crookedness of mouth, and deviousness of lips put far from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and your eyelids look straight before you.
Make level the track of your foot, and let all your ways be steadfast.
Do not turn aside to the right or the left; turn your foot away from evil.

proverbs_5.t: My son, be attentive to my wisdom; to my discernment incline your ear,
to preserve discretion, and that your lips may observe knowledge.
For the lips of a strange woman drip honey, and her palate is smoother than oil;
but her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-mouthed sword.
Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold of Sheol.
The path of life — lest she should make it level; her tracks wander, she does not know.
And now, children, listen to me, and do not depart from the sayings of my mouth.
Keep your way far from her, and do not draw near to the entrance of her house,
lest you give your vigour to others, and your years to a cruel one;
lest strangers be sated with your strength, and your labours be in the house of a foreigner;
and you groan at your end, when your flesh and your body waste away,
and you say: "How I hated discipline, and my heart spurned reproof!
and I did not listen to the voice of my instructors, and to my teachers I did not incline my ear.
I was almost in every calamity in the midst of the assembly and the congregation."
Drink water from your own cistern, and streams from the midst of your own well.
Should your springs overflow outside, streams of water in the open squares?
Let them be yours, yours alone, and not for strangers with you.
Let your spring be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth,
a doe of loves and a goat of grace. Let her breasts satisfy you at every time; by her love may you be intoxicated continually.
And why should you go astray, my son, with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a foreign woman?
For a man's ways are before the eyes of YHWH, and he makes level all his tracks.
His iniquities will seize him — the wicked one — and by the cords of his sin he will be held.
He will die for lack of discipline, and in the greatness of his folly he will go astray.

proverbs_6.t: My son, if you have stood surety for your neighbour, have struck your palms for a stranger,
you have been ensnared by the sayings of your mouth, you have been caught by the sayings of your mouth.
Do this then, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into your neighbour's palm: go, humble yourself, and importune your neighbour.
Do not give sleep to your eyes, or slumber to your eyelids.
Deliver yourself like a gazelle from a hand, and like a bird from the hand of a fowler.
Go to the ant, sluggard; consider her ways and become wise.
which has no commander, officer or ruler,
yet she prepares her bread in the summer, gathers her food at the harvest.
How long, sluggard, will you lie down? When will you rise from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down —
and your poverty will come like a traveller, and your want like a man with a shield.
A worthless person, a man of wickedness, goes about with crookedness of mouth,
winking with his eyes, scraping with his feet, pointing with his fingers,
perversity in his heart, devising evil at every time, sending out contentions.
Therefore his disaster will come suddenly; in an instant he will be broken, and there will be no healing.
Six things there are that YHWH hates, and seven are the abomination of his being:
haughty eyes, a tongue of falsehood, and hands shedding innocent blood,
a heart devising plans of wickedness, feet hurrying to run to evil,
a false witness breathing out lies, and one sending out contentions between brothers.
Keep, my son, your father's commandment, and do not forsake your mother's law.
Bind them on your heart continually; tie them on your neck.
When you walk about, it will guide you; when you lie down, it will watch over you; and you will awake — it will speak with you.
For the commandment is a lamp and the law a light, and the reproofs of discipline are a way of life,
to keep you from an evil woman, from the smoothness of the tongue of a foreign woman.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her capture you with her eyelids.
For on account of a prostitute, [one comes] to a round loaf of bread, but a man's wife hunts a precious life.
Can a man scoop up fire in his bosom and his garments not be burned?
Or can a man walk on burning coals and his feet not be scorched?
So is the one who goes in to his neighbour's wife: no one who touches her will go unpunished.
People do not despise a thief if he steals to fill his appetite when he is hungry;
yet if he is found out he will repay sevenfold; all the wealth of his house he will give.
One who commits adultery with a woman lacks heart; he who does it destroys his own being.
A wound and disgrace he will find, and his reproach will not be wiped away.
For jealousy is a man's rage, and he will not spare on the day of vengeance.
He will not lift the face of any ransom, and he will not consent, though you make the bribe great.

proverbs_7.t: My son, keep my sayings, and treasure up my commandments with you.
Keep my commandments and live, and my law like the pupil of your eyes.
Bind them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding a kinswoman,
to keep you from a strange woman, from a foreign woman who has made her sayings smooth.
For at the window of my house, through my lattice I looked down,
and I saw among the naive, I observed among the sons a youth lacking heart,
passing along the street beside her corner, and he strode the way to her house,
at twilight, in the evening of the day, in the middle of the night and darkness.
And here, a woman to meet him, in the garment of a prostitute and guarded of heart.
She is boisterous and rebellious; her feet do not stay in her house.
Now in the street, now in the open squares, and beside every corner she lies in wait.
And she takes hold of him and kisses him; she makes her face bold and says to him:
"Sacrifices of peace offerings are upon me; today I have paid my vows.
Therefore I have come out to meet you, to seek your face, and I have found you.
Coverings I have spread on my couch, coloured fabrics, linen of Egypt.
I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning; let us delight ourselves with love.
For the man is not in his house; he has gone on a journey far off.
The bag of silver he took in his hand; at the day of the full moon he will come home."
She turns him aside with the greatness of her learning; with the smoothness of her lips she impels him.
He goes after her suddenly, like an ox that goes to the slaughter, and like an anklet to the discipline of a fool,
until an arrow pierces his liver; as a bird hurries into a trap, and he does not know that it is for his life.
And now, children, listen to me, and be attentive to the sayings of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her pathways.
For many are the slain she has brought down, and numerous are all those she has killed.
Her house is the ways of Sheol, going down to the chambers of death.

proverbs_8.t: Does not wisdom call out, and discernment give her voice?
At the top of the heights, beside the way, between the pathways she has stationed herself.
Beside the gates, at the mouth of the town, at the entrance of the doorways, they cry aloud:
"To you, O people, I call, and my voice is to the children of humankind.
Understand shrewdness, you naive; and you dullards, understand heart.
Listen, for I will speak princely things, and the opening of my lips will be equity.
For my palate will utter truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
All the sayings of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
All of them are straight to the one who discerns, and upright to those who find knowledge.
Take my discipline and not silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom is better than corals, and all delights do not compare with her.
I, wisdom, dwell with shrewdness, and I find the knowledge of discretion.
The fear of YHWH is to hate evil. Pride and arrogance and an evil way and a mouth of perversity I hate.
Counsel is mine, and sound sense; I am understanding, strength is mine.
By me kings reign, and rulers decree righteousness;
by me princes rule, and nobles — all who judge righteousness.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me earnestly find me.
Wealth and honour are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruit is better than gold, even than pure gold, and my gain than choice silver.
In the path of righteousness I walk, in the midst of the pathways of justice,
to give substance as an inheritance to those who love me, and I will fill their treasuries.
YHWH possessed me at the beginning of his way, before his works, from of old.
From of old I was installed, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth.
When there were no deeps I was brought forth, when there were no springs abounding with water.
Before the mountains were sunk into place, before the hills, I was brought forth,
while he had not yet made the earth and the open places, nor the first of the dusts of the world.
When he established the heavens, I was there; when he marked out a circle on the face of the deep,
when he made firm the clouds above, when the springs of the deep grew strong,
when he set for the sea its limit, so that the waters should not transgress his mouth, when he marked out the foundations of the earth —
then I was beside him, a master workman, and I was delights day by day, playing before him at every time,
playing in the world of his earth, and my delights were with the children of humankind.
And now, children, listen to me, and how blessed are those who keep my ways!
Listen to discipline and be wise, and do not let it go.
How blessed is the person who listens to me, watching at my doors day by day, keeping the doorposts of my doorways!
For one who finds me finds life and obtains favour from YHWH;
but one who misses me does violence to his own being; all who hate me love death."

proverbs_9.t: Wisdom has built her house; she has hewn out her seven pillars.
She has slaughtered her slaughter, she has mixed her wine, she has also set her table.
She has sent out her young women; she calls from the heights of the town:
"Whoever is naive, let him turn aside here!" To the one lacking heart she says:
"Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed.
Abandon the naive and live, and advance in the way of understanding."
One who admonishes a mocker takes disgrace for himself, and one who reproves a wicked person — his own defect.
Do not reprove a mocker, lest he hate you; reprove a wise one, and he will love you.
Give to a wise one, and he will be wiser still; make known to a righteous one, and he will increase in learning.
The start of wisdom is the fear of YHWH, and the knowledge of the holy ones is understanding.
For by me your days will increase, and years of life will be added to you.
If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; and if you mock, you alone will bear it.
A woman of dullness is boisterous — naivety, and she knows nothing at all.
And she sits at the doorway of her house, on a seat at the heights of the town,
to call to those passing by on the road, those making their paths straight:
"Whoever is naive, let him turn aside here!" And to the one lacking heart she says:
"Stolen waters are sweet, and bread of secret places is delightful."
And he does not know that the shades are there, that her invited ones are in the depths of Sheol.

proverbs_10.t: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a father glad, and a dull son is his mother's grief.
Treasures of wickedness do not profit, but righteousness delivers from death.
YHWH does not let the appetite of the righteous go hungry, but he thrusts aside the craving of the wicked.
A slack palm makes poor, but the hand of the diligent makes rich.
One who gathers in summer is a son who acts with insight; one who sleeps at harvest is a son who acts shamefully.
Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
The memory of the righteous is for a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
One wise of heart accepts commandments, but a fool of lips will be ruined.
One who walks in integrity walks in security, but one who makes his ways crooked will be found out.
One who winks an eye gives pain, but a fool of lips will be ruined.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Hatred stirs up contentions, but love covers over all transgressions.
On the lips of the discerning wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of one lacking heart.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is ruin close at hand.
The wealth of a rich man is his strong town; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
The wage of the righteous is to life; the yield of the wicked is to sin.
A path to life is one who keeps discipline, but one who abandons reproof leads astray.
One concealing hatred has lips of falsehood, and one who spreads slander — he is a dullard.
In a multitude of words transgression does not cease, but one who restrains his lips acts with insight.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous shepherd many, but fools die for lack of heart.
The blessing of YHWH — it makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it.
Doing depravity is like sport to a dullard, and so is wisdom to a person of discernment.
What the wicked dreads — it will come to him; but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
When a storm-wind passes, the wicked is no more, but the righteous is a perpetual foundation.
Like vinegar to the teeth and like smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.
The fear of YHWH adds days, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
The expectation of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will be lost.
The way of YHWH is a stronghold to integrity, but ruin to those who do wickedness.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous bears wisdom as fruit, but a tongue of perversity will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know favour, but the mouth of the wicked is perversity.

proverbs_11.t: Scales of deceit are an abomination to YHWH, but a perfect weight is his favour.
Insolence comes, and disgrace comes; but with the modest is wisdom.
The integrity of the upright guides them, but the distortion of the treacherous destroys them.
Wealth does not profit in the day of fury, but righteousness delivers from death.
The righteousness of the blameless makes his way straight, but by his own wickedness the wicked falls.
The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but by their own craving the treacherous are caught.
At the death of a wicked person hope is lost, and the expectation of strength perishes.
A righteous person is drawn out of distress, and a wicked person comes in his place.
By the mouth the godless ruins his neighbour, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.
In the good of the righteous a town rejoices, and when the wicked perish, a shout of joy.
By the blessing of the upright a town is exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
One who despises his neighbour lacks heart, but a person of discernment keeps quiet.
One who goes about as a talebearer reveals a confidence, but one faithful in spirit conceals a matter.
Where there is no guidance a people falls, but deliverance is in a multitude of counsellors.
He is surely harmed who stands surety for a stranger, but one who hates striking hands is secure.
A gracious woman lays hold of honour, and the ruthless lay hold of wealth.
A person of loyalty deals well with his own being, but a cruel one troubles his own body.
The wicked earns a wage of falsehood, but one who sows righteousness — a wage of truth.
Truly righteousness is to life, and one who pursues evil is to his own death.
Those perverse of heart are an abomination to YHWH, but those blameless in way are his favour.
Hand to hand, the evil will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
A ring of gold in a pig's snout — a beautiful woman who turns aside from discretion.
The desire of the righteous is only good; the hope of the wicked is fury.
There is one who scatters and is increased still, and one who withholds from what is right, only to want.
A being of blessing will be made fat, and one who waters — he also will be watered.
One who withholds grain — a people curse him, but a blessing is on the head of one who sells it.
One who seeks good earnestly seeks favour, but one who searches out evil — it will come to him.
One who trusts in his wealth — he will fall, but the righteous will bud like a leaf.
One who troubles his household will inherit wind, and a fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and one who takes lives is wise.
See, the righteous is repaid on the earth — how much more the wicked and the sinner!

proverbs_12.t: One who loves discipline loves knowledge, but one who hates reproof is a brute.
A good person obtains favour from YHWH, but a man of schemes he condemns.
A person is not established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous will not be moved.
A wife of ability is her husband's crown, but one who acts shamefully is like rot in his bones.
The plans of the righteous are justice; the counsel of the wicked is deceit.
The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright delivers them.
Overthrow the wicked and they are no more, but the house of the righteous will stand.
A person is praised according to his insight, but one perverted of heart will be held in contempt.
Better to be lightly esteemed and have a servant than to honour oneself and lack food.
A righteous person knows the life of his animal, but the compassion of the wicked is cruel.
One who works his ground will be satisfied with food, but one who pursues worthless things lacks heart.
The wicked desires the net of evil men, but the root of the righteous yields.
In the transgression of the lips is an evil snare, but the righteous comes out of trouble.
From the fruit of a person's mouth he is satisfied with good, and the dealing of a person's hands returns to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but one who listens to counsel is wise.
A fool — his vexation is known the same day, but one who conceals disgrace is shrewd.
One who breathes out faithfulness declares righteousness, but a witness of lies, deceit.
There is one who speaks rashly like the thrusts of a sword, but the tongue of the wise is healing.
A lip of truth is established for ever, but a tongue of falsehood only for a moment.
Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil, but for counsellors of peace there is joy.
No trouble befalls the righteous, but the wicked are full of distress.
Lips of falsehood are an abomination to YHWH, but those who deal in faithfulness are his favour.
A shrewd person conceals knowledge, but the heart of dullards proclaims folly.
The hand of the diligent will rule, but slackness will end in forced labour.
Anxiety in a person's heart bows it down, but a good word makes it glad.
The righteous searches out from his neighbour, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
Slackness does not roast its game, but the wealth of a person is precious — diligence.
In the path of righteousness is life, and the way of its pathway is no death.

proverbs_13.t: A wise son — a father's discipline; but a mocker does not listen to a rebuke.
From the fruit of a person's mouth he eats good, but the appetite of the treacherous is violence.
One who guards his mouth keeps his life; one who opens wide his lips — ruin is his.
The sluggard craves and gets nothing, but the appetite of the diligent is made fat.
A righteous person hates a word of falsehood, but a wicked one acts odiously and shamefully.
Righteousness guards integrity of way, but wickedness subverts sin.
There is one who makes himself rich and has nothing; one who makes himself poor, and has great wealth.
The ransom of a person's life is his wealth, but a poor person does not hear a threat.
The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be put out.
By insolence only comes contention, but with those who take counsel is wisdom.
Wealth from vapour dwindles, but one who gathers by hand increases it.
Expectation drawn out makes the heart sick, but a desire come is a tree of life.
One who despises a word will be held in pledge by it, but one who fears a commandment will be rewarded.
The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to turn aside from the snares of death.
Good insight gives favour, but the way of the treacherous is enduring.
Every shrewd person acts with knowledge, but a dullard spreads out folly.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy is healing.
Poverty and disgrace are for one who lets discipline go, but one who keeps reproof will be honoured.
A desire come to pass is pleasant to the being, but turning aside from evil is an abomination to dullards.
One who walks with the wise becomes wise, but one who associates with dullards will be harmed.
Calamity pursues sinners, but good repays the righteous.
A good person leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the wealth of a sinner is stored up for the righteous.
Much food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but there is what is swept away for want of justice.
One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him seeks him early with discipline.
A righteous person eats to the satisfying of his appetite, but the belly of the wicked will lack.

proverbs_14.t: The wisest of women builds her house, but folly tears it down with her own hands.
One who walks in his uprightness fears YHWH, but one crooked in his ways despises him.
In the mouth of a fool is a shoot of pride, but the lips of the wise preserve them.
Where there are no cattle the manger is clean, but much produce comes by the strength of an ox.
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
A mocker seeks wisdom and there is none, but knowledge is easy for the discerning.
Go from before a dull person, for you have not known lips of knowledge.
The wisdom of the shrewd is to understand his way, but the folly of dullards is deceit.
Fools — they scoff at the guilt offering, but among the upright is favour.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and a stranger does not share in its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
There is a way that is right before a person, but its end is the ways of death.
Even in laughter a heart is in pain, and the end of joy is grief.
One backslidden of heart will be sated from his own ways, and a good man from what is his.
A naive person believes every word, but a shrewd one understands his step.
A wise person fears and turns aside from evil, but a dullard rages on and is confident.
One short of nostrils does folly, and a man of schemes is hated.
The naive inherit folly, but the shrewd are crowned with knowledge.
The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
Even by his neighbour the poor is hated, but those who love the rich are many.
One who despises his neighbour sins, but how blessed is one who shows favour to the humble!
Do they not go astray who devise evil? But loyalty and faithfulness are for those who devise good.
In all hard labour there is profit, but a word of the lips leads only to want.
The crown of the wise is their wealth; the folly of dullards is folly.
A true witness delivers lives, but one who breathes out lies is deceit.
In the fear of YHWH is strong confidence, and for his children there will be a refuge.
The fear of YHWH is a fountain of life, to turn aside from the snares of death.
In a multitude of people is a king's glory, but in the absence of a people is a ruler's ruin.
One long of nostrils has great discernment, but one short of spirit exalts folly.
A heart of healing is the life of the flesh, but jealousy is rottenness of the bones.
One who oppresses the poor reproaches his Maker, but one who shows favour to the needy honours him.
In his own evil the wicked is thrust down, but the righteous seeks refuge in his death.
In the heart of the discerning wisdom rests, and in the midst of dullards it is made known.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but a disgrace to peoples is sin.
A king's favour is for a servant who acts with insight, but his fury is for one who acts shamefully.

proverbs_15.t: A soft answer turns away rage, but a word of hurt raises anger.
The tongue of the wise makes knowledge good, but the mouth of dullards pours out folly.
In every place are the eyes of YHWH, watching the evil and the good.
The healing of a tongue is a tree of life, but distortion in it is a breaking in the spirit.
A fool spurns his father's discipline, but one who keeps reproof is shrewd.
In the house of the righteous is great store, but in the income of the wicked is trouble.
The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the heart of dullards is not so.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to YHWH, but the prayer of the upright is his favour.
The way of the wicked is an abomination to YHWH, but he loves one who pursues righteousness.
Bad discipline is for one who forsakes the path; one who hates reproof will die.
Sheol and Abaddon are before YHWH — how much more the hearts of the children of humankind!
A mocker does not love being reproved; to the wise he will not go.
A joyful heart makes the face good, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is stricken.
A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of dullards feeds on folly.
All the days of the afflicted are bad, but one good of heart has a feast continually.
Better a little with the fear of YHWH than great treasure and turmoil with it.
Better a portion of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox and hatred with it.
A man of rage stirs up strife, but one long of nostrils quiets a dispute.
The way of the sluggard is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a raised road.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a dull person despises his mother.
Folly is a joy to one lacking heart, but a person of discernment makes his walking straight.
Plans are frustrated where there is no counsel, but with a multitude of counsellors they stand.
A person has joy in the answer of his mouth, and a word in its time — how good!
The path of life is upward for one of insight, so as to turn aside from Sheol beneath.
YHWH tears down the house of the proud, but he sets firm the boundary of a widow.
The plans of an evil person are an abomination to YHWH, but sayings of kindness are pure.
One who gains unjust gain troubles his own house, but one who hates gifts will live.
The heart of the righteous considers how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evils.
YHWH is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
The light of the eyes makes the heart glad; a good report makes the bones fat.
An ear that hears the reproof of life will lodge among the wise.
One who lets discipline go rejects his own being, but one who heeds reproof acquires heart.
The fear of YHWH is the discipline of wisdom, and before honour is humility.

proverbs_16.t: To a person belong the arrangements of the heart, but from YHWH comes the answer of the tongue.
All a person's ways are pure in his own eyes, but YHWH weighs the spirits.
Roll your works upon YHWH, and your plans will be established.
YHWH has made everything for its purpose, and even the wicked for a day of calamity.
Everyone haughty of heart is an abomination to YHWH; hand to hand, he will not go unpunished.
By loyalty and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of YHWH one turns aside from evil.
When YHWH is pleased with a person's ways, he makes even his enemies be at peace with him.
Better a little with righteousness than great gains without justice.
A person's heart plans his way, but YHWH directs his step.
Divination is on a king's lips; in judgement his mouth does not break faith.
A balance and scales of judgement are YHWH's; all the weights in the bag are his work.
Doing wickedness is an abomination to kings, for by righteousness a throne is established.
Lips of righteousness are kings' favour, and he loves one who speaks upright things.
A king's rage is messengers of death, but a wise person will cover it over.
In the light of a king's face is life, and his favour is like a cloud of spring rain.
