Trustworthy the word: for if we died together, also we will live together;
if we endure, also we will reign together; if we will deny, that one also will deny us;
if we lack trust, that one remains trustworthy; for to deny himself he is not able.
These things remind, solemnly witnessing before God not to word-fight, for nothing useful, upon overturning of those hearing.
Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a workman unashamed, cutting straight the word of the truth.
But the profane empty utterances stand away from; for they will progress upon more of ungodliness,
and their word will have pasture as gangrene; of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus,
who concerning the truth missed the mark, saying the resurrection to have already happened, and they overturn the trust of some.
Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: "The Lord knew the ones being his," and, "Let stand away from unrighteousness everyone naming the name of the Lord."
But in a great house there are not only gold and silver vessels but also wooden and earthen, and some unto honour, some unto dishonour.
If therefore anyone cleanses himself out from these, he will be a vessel unto honour, having been made holy and well-useful to the master, having been prepared for every good work.
But the youthful desires flee, and pursue righteousness, trust, love, peace with those calling upon the Lord out of a clean heart.
But the foolish and undisciplined disputes refuse, knowing that they beget battles;
and a servant of the Lord must not battle but be mild toward all, apt at teaching, bearing evil,
in gentleness disciplining those opposing, whether perhaps God may give them a change of mind unto full knowledge of truth,
and they may sober up out of the snare of the slanderer, having been caught alive by him unto the will of that one.

2 timothy_3.t: But know this, that in last days will stand in difficult seasons.
For the humans will be self-lovers, money-lovers, braggarts, haughty, blasphemers, to parents disobedient, ungrateful, unholy,
without natural affection, implacable, slanderers, without self-control, untamed, not lovers of good,
betrayers, headlong, having been puffed up, pleasure-lovers rather than God-lovers,
having a form of godliness but its power having denied; and these turn away from.
For out of these are those slipping into the houses and taking captive little women having been heaped with sins, being led by various desires,
always learning and never able to come unto full knowledge of truth.
And in the manner Jannes and Jambres stood against Moses, so also these stand against the truth, humans corrupted in the mind, unapproved concerning the trust.
But they will not progress upon more; for their folly will be very evident to all, as also that of those ones became.
But you followed closely my teaching, the conduct, the purpose, the trust, the long-suffering, the love, the endurance,
the persecutions, the sufferings, such as happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra; such persecutions I bore, and out of all the Lord rescued me.
And also all those wanting to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But wicked humans and sorcerers will progress unto the worse, deceiving and being deceived.
But you remain in what you learned and were assured of, knowing from whom you learned,
and that from a babe the sacred letters you have known, the ones able to make you wise unto salvation through the trust that is in Christ Jesus.
All writing God-breathed and useful toward teaching, toward reproof, toward correction, toward discipline that is in righteousness,
so that the human of God may be fitted, having been fully equipped toward every good work.

2 timothy_4.t: I solemnly witness therefore, I, before God and the Lord Christ Jesus, the one about to judge living ones and dead ones, and his appearing and his kingdom:
proclaim the word, stand ready in season, out of season, reprove, rebuke, exhort, in all long-suffering and teaching.
For there will be a season when the healthy teaching they will not bear, but according to their own desires they will heap up for themselves teachers, having itching hearing,
and from the truth the hearing they will turn away, and unto the myths they will be turned aside.
But you, be sober in all things, suffer evil, do a work of a good-news-announcer, fully carry out your service.
For I already am being poured out, and the season of my loosing-away has stood upon me.
The good struggle I have struggled, the course I have completed, the trust I have kept.
Henceforth is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord will give back to me in that day, the righteous judge; and not only to me but also to all those having loved his appearing.
Be diligent to come to me quickly.
For Demas deserted me, having loved the now age, and went into Thessalonica; Crescens into Galatia, Titus into Dalmatia.
Luke alone is with me. Mark having taken up bring with yourself, for he is well-useful to me for service.
But Tychicus I sent into Ephesus.
The cloak which I left behind in Troas with Carpus, coming bring, and the books, especially the parchments.
Alexander the coppersmith much evil showed to me; the Lord will give back to him according to his works;
whom also you guard against, for exceedingly he stood against our words.
In my first defence no one came alongside me, but all deserted me; may it not be counted to them.
But the Lord stood by me and empowered me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully carried out and all the nations might hear, and I was rescued out of a lion's mouth.
And the Lord will rescue me from every wicked work and will save unto his heavenly kingdom; to whom the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila and the house of Onesiphorus.
Erastus remained in Corinth; but Trophimus I left behind in Miletus ailing.
Be diligent to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers.
The Lord be with your spirit. The grace be with you all.

3 john_1.t: The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.
Beloved, concerning all things I pray you to be prospered and to be in health, just as is prospered of you the soul.
I rejoiced for exceedingly, coming brothers and witnessing of you to the truth, just as you in truth walk.
Greater than these things not I have joy, that I hear the my children in the truth walking.
Beloved, a faithful thing you do whatever you might work for the brothers and this strangers,
Who witnessed of you to the love before an assembly, whom well you will do having sent forward worthily of the God.
On behalf for of the name they went out nothing taking from the gentiles.
We therefore ought to take up the such ones, that co-workers we might become in the truth.
I wrote something to the assembly, but the one loving to be first of them, Diotrephes, not receives us.

On account of this, if I should come, I will bring to remembrance of him the works which he does, with words evil talking nonsense against us; and not being satisfied upon these, neither himself receives the brothers and the ones wanting he hinders and out of the assembly he throws.
Beloved, not imitate the bad but the good. The one doing good from the God is; the one doing bad not has seen the God.
To Demetrius it has been witnessed by all and by herself the truth; and we also witness, and you know that the witness of us true is.
Many things I had to write to you, but not I want through ink and reed to you to write.
I hope but immediately you to see, and mouth toward mouth we will speak.
Peace to you. Greet you the friends. Greet the friends by name.

acts_1.t: The first word I made concerning all things, O Theophilus, which Jesus began both to do and to teach,
until which day, having commanded through holy spirit the apostles whom he chose, he was taken up.
to whom also he presented himself living after he suffered, in many proofs, through forty days being seen by them and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of God.
And being assembled with them he charged them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to await the promise of the Father, "which you heard of me;
because John indeed baptised with water, but you in holy spirit will be baptised not after many these days."
Those therefore having come together were asking him, saying, "Lord, if in this time you are restoring the kingdom to Israel?"
But he said to them, "It is not yours to know times or seasons which the Father set in his own authority,
but you will receive power when the holy spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses both in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and as far as the last part of the earth."
And having said these things, while they were looking, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him up from their eyes.
And as they were gazing intently into the heaven while he was going, also look — two men had taken their stand beside them in white garments,
who also said, "Men, Galileans, why do you stand looking into the heaven? This Jesus, the one taken up from you into the heaven, thus will come in the manner you beheld him going into the heaven."
Then they returned into Jerusalem from a mountain called of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, having a Sabbath's journey.

And when they entered, into the upper room they went up, where they were remaining — both Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon the zealot and Judas of James.
These all were persevering with one accord in the prayer and the petition, with women and Mariam the mother of Jesus and with his brothers.
And in these days Peter, having stood up in the midst of the brothers, said — and there was a crowd of names in the same place, about a hundred and twenty —

"Men, brothers, it was necessary that this scripture be fulfilled which the holy spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David concerning Judas, the one having become guide to those who seized Jesus.
because he was numbered among us and obtained the lot of this service."
This one indeed therefore acquired a field out of the wage of unrighteousness, and having become headlong he burst in the middle and all his inward parts were poured out.
And it became known to all those inhabiting Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their own dialect Hakeldamach, that is, Field of Blood.
For it is written in the book of Psalms, 'Let his dwelling become desolate and let there not be the one dwelling in it,' and, 'His overseership let another take.'
It is necessary therefore, of the men having come together with us in all the time in which the Lord Jesus went in and went out upon us,
beginning from the baptism of John until the day in which he was taken up from us — one of these must become a witness of his resurrection with us."
And they set forth two, Joseph the one called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
And having prayed they said, "You, Lord, knower of hearts of all, show plainly whom you chose out of these two, one,
to take the place of this service and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place."
And they gave lots for them, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was voted in with the eleven apostles.

acts_2.t: And in the being fulfilled of the day of the Pentecost, they were all together at the same place.
And there came suddenly out of the heaven a sound as of a violent wind being borne along, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
And there appeared to them tongues being divided, as of fire, and it sat upon each one of them.
And they were all filled of holy spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the spirit was giving to them to utter.
And there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, reverent men from every nation of those under the heaven.
And this voice having occurred, the multitude came together and was confounded, because they were hearing each one in his own dialect them speaking.
And they were amazed and marvelled, saying to one another, "Behold, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
And how do we hear each in our own dialect in which we were born?
Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those inhabiting Mesopotamia, both Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
both Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya toward Cyrene, and the sojourning Romans,
Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs, we hear them speaking in our tongues the great things of God."
And all were amazed and were perplexed, another to another saying, "What does this want to be?"
But others, mocking, were saying that "They are filled with sweet wine."
But Peter, having stood with the eleven, lifted up his voice and uttered to them, "Men, Jews, and all those inhabiting Jerusalem, let this be known to you and give ear to my words.
For not, as you suppose, are these drunk, for it is the third hour of the day,
but this is that which has been spoken through the prophet Joel,

'And it will be in the last days, says God, I will pour out from my spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
And indeed upon my male servants and upon my female servants in those days I will pour out from my spirit, and they will prophesy.
And I will give wonders in the heaven above and signs upon the earth below, blood and fire and vapour of smoke.
The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the coming of the day of the Lord, the great and manifest one.
And it will be, everyone whoever calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.'
"Men, Israelites, hear these words. Jesus the Nazarene, a man demonstrated from God to you by powers and wonders and signs which God did through him in your midst, just as you yourselves know,
this one, by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God given over, through the hand of lawless ones having fastened up, you killed;
whom God raised up, having loosed the birth pangs of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.
For David says with reference to him, 'I was foreseeing the Lord before me through everything, because he is at my right so that I may not be shaken.
Because of this my heart was made glad and my tongue exulted; and still also my flesh will encamp upon hope,
because you will not abandon my soul into Hades, nor will you give your holy one to see corruption.
You made known to me ways of life; you will fill me with gladness with your face.'
"Men, brothers, it is permitted to speak with boldness to you concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us until this day.
Being therefore a prophet and knowing that with an oath God swore to him, out of the fruit of his loin to seat upon his throne,
having foreseen, he spoke concerning the resurrection of the Christ, that neither was he abandoned into Hades nor did his flesh see corruption.
This Jesus God raised up, of which we all are witnesses.
By the right hand of God therefore having been exalted, and the promise of the holy spirit having received from the Father, he poured out this which you both see and hear.
For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right,
until I place your enemies a footstool of your feet."'
Assuredly therefore let all the house of Israel know that God made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified."
And having heard, they were pierced in the heart, and said to Peter and the remaining apostles, "Men, brothers, what may we do?"
And Peter to them, "Change your minds," he says, "and let each of you be baptised upon the name of Jesus Christ unto release of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the holy spirit.
For to you is the promise and to your children and to all those at a distance, as many as the Lord our God may call to himself."
And with many other words he solemnly witnessed and was exhorting them, saying, "Be saved from this crooked generation."
Those indeed therefore having welcomed his word were baptised, and there were added in that day souls about three thousand.
And they were persevering in the teaching of the apostles and in the fellowship, in the breaking of the bread and in the prayers.
And fear was coming upon every soul, and many wonders and signs through the apostles were occurring.
And all those trusting were at the same place and had all things common,
and the possessions and the goods they were selling and were distributing them to all, according as anyone was having need.
And day by day persevering with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread according to house, they were partaking of food in gladness and simplicity of heart,
praising God and having favour toward the whole people. And the Lord was adding those being saved day by day at the same place.

acts_3.t: And at the same place Peter and John were going up into the temple at the hour of the prayer, the ninth.
And a certain man, lame from his mother's womb, was being carried, whom they used to set day by day at the door of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms from those entering into the temple.
who, seeing Peter and John about to enter into the temple, was asking to receive alms.
And Peter, having gazed intently at him with John, said, "Look at us."
And he was holding to them, expecting to receive something from them.
But Peter said, "Silver and gold does not belong to me; but what I have, this I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise up and walk."
And having seized him of the right hand he raised him. And instantly his feet and the ankle-bones were made firm,
and leaping up he stood and was walking, and entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
And they were recognising him, that he was the one sitting for the alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
And while he was holding fast to Peter and to John, all the people ran together to them at the portico called Solomon's, greatly amazed.
And Peter, having seen, answered to the people, "Men, Israelites, why do you marvel at this, or why do you gaze intently at us as if by our own power or piety having made him to walk?

The God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his child Jesus, whom you indeed handed over and denied before the face of Pilate, that one having judged to release him.
But you denied the holy and righteous one and asked for a man, a murderer, to be granted to you,
But the founder of the life you killed, whom God raised out of dead ones, of which we are witnesses.
And upon the trust of his name, this one whom you behold and know his name made firm, and the trust which is through him gave to him this wholeness before all of you.
And now, brothers, I know that according to ignorance you acted, just as also your rulers.
But God, the things which he announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he fulfilled thus.
Change your minds therefore and turn back, unto the wiping away of your sins,
so that seasons of refreshing may come from the face of the Lord, and he may send the one appointed beforehand for you, Christ Jesus,
whom it is necessary for heaven indeed to receive until times of restoration of all things, of which God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old.
Moses indeed said that 'A prophet for you will the Lord your God raise up out of your brothers, like me; him you shall hear according to all things whatever he may speak to you.
And it will be, every soul whoever does not hear that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.'
And also all the prophets from Samuel and those in order, as many as spoke, also announced these days.
You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God covenanted toward your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'And in your seed will be blessed all the families of the earth.'
To you first, God, having raised up his child, sent him blessing you in the turning away of each from your wickednesses.

acts_4.t: And while they were speaking to the people, the priests and the commander of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
being worn out because they were teaching the people and announcing in Jesus the resurrection out of dead ones,
And they laid hands on them and put them into keeping until the morrow, for it was already evening.
But many of those having heard the word trusted, and the number of the men became about five thousand.
And it happened upon the morrow that their rulers and the elders and the scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem,
and Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and as many as were of high-priestly descent,
And having stood them in the midst, they were inquiring, "By what power or in what name did you do this, you?"
Then Peter, having been filled of holy spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders,
if we today are being examined upon a good work of a weak man, by what this one has been saved,

let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised out of dead ones, in this one this man stands before you whole.
This is the stone, the one despised by you the builders, the one having become into head of the corner.
And there is not in another anyone the salvation, for neither is there another name under the heaven given among humans in which it is necessary for us to be saved."
And beholding the boldness of Peter and of John, and having grasped that they are unlettered humans and untrained, they were marvelling; and they were recognising them, that they were with Jesus.
And seeing the man standing with them, the one having been healed, they had nothing to say against.
And having ordered them to go away outside the council, they were conferring with one another,
saying, "What may we do to these humans? For that indeed a known sign has come through them is manifest to all those inhabiting Jerusalem, and we are not able to deny it.
But so that it may not be spread further to the people, let us threaten them with threatening to speak no longer upon this name to no one of humans."
And having called them, they charged them not at all to utter nor to teach upon the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John, answering, said to them, "If it is righteous before God to hear you rather than God, judge.
For we are not able, the things which we saw and heard, not to speak."
And they, having threatened further, released them, finding nothing as to how they might punish them, on account of the people, because all were glorifying God upon what had happened.
For the human was of more than forty years upon whom this sign of the healing had happened.
And having been released, they came to their own and reported as many things as the chief priests and the elders said to them.
And they, having heard, with one accord lifted a voice to God and said, "Master, you the God who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them,
the one who, of our father through holy spirit, of the mouth of David your child, said, 'Why did nations rage and peoples devise empty things?
The kings of the earth stood by and the rulers were gathered together at the same place against the Lord and against his Christ.'
For they were gathered together in truth in this city against your holy child Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate with nations and peoples of Israel,
to do as many things as your hand and your counsel predetermined to happen.
And now, Lord, look upon their threatenings and give to your servants with all boldness to speak your word,
in the stretching out of your hand for healing and signs and wonders to happen through the name of your holy child Jesus."
And when they had prayed, the place was shaken in which they were gathered together, and all were filled of the holy spirit and were speaking the word of God with boldness.
And of the multitude of those having trusted, the heart and the soul was one; and not even one was saying anything of the things belonging to him to be his own, but all things were to them common.
And with great power the apostles were giving back the witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon all of them.
For neither was anyone needy among them; for as many as were owners of fields or houses, selling, were bringing the prices of the things being sold
and were placing at the feet of the apostles; and it was distributed to each according as anyone was having need.
And Joseph, the one surnamed Barnabas by the apostles, which is being translated son of encouragement, a Levite, a Cypriot by descent,
a field belonging to him, having sold, brought the money and placed it at the feet of the apostles.

acts_5.t: But a certain man, Ananias by name, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
and kept back from the price, his wife also being aware, and having brought a certain part, placed it at the feet of the apostles.
But Peter said, "Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart for you to lie to the holy spirit and to keep back from the price of the field?
Remaining, did it not remain yours? And having been sold, was it not in your own authority? Why is it that you placed this deed in your heart? You did not lie to humans but to God."
And Ananias, hearing these words, having fallen, breathed out. And there came great fear upon all those hearing these things.
And the younger men, having risen, wrapped him and, having carried him out, buried him.
And there occurred about three hours' interval, and his wife, not knowing what had happened, entered.
And Peter answered to her, "Tell me, if you gave over the field for so much?" And she said, "Yes, for so much."
And Peter said to her, "Why is it that it was agreed by you to test the spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those having buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out."
And she fell instantly at his feet and breathed out. And the young men, having entered, found her dead and, having carried her out, buried her beside her husband.
And there came great fear upon the whole assembly and upon all those hearing these things.
And through the hands of the apostles there were occurring many signs and wonders among the people; and they were all with one accord in the portico of Solomon.
But of the rest no one was daring to join himself to them, but the people was magnifying them.
And more were being added, trusting the Lord, multitudes both of men and of women,
so as even into the streets to carry out the weak and to place them on small beds and mats, so that, Peter coming, even the shadow might overshadow some of them.
And there was coming together also the multitude of the cities around into Jerusalem, bringing weak ones and those being troubled by unclean spirits, who were being healed, all of them.
And the high priest having risen up, and all those with him, being the sect of the Sadducees, they were filled with zeal,
and they laid their hands upon the apostles and put them in public keeping.
But an angel of the Lord through the night, having opened the doors of the prison and having led them out, said,
"Go and, having stood, speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life."

And having heard, they entered at the dawn into the temple and were teaching. And the high priest having arrived, and those with him, they called together the council and all the elderhood of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison-house for them to be led out.
But the attendants having arrived did not find them in the prison; and having returned they reported,
saying that "The prison-house we found shut in all security and the guards standing at the doors; but having opened, inside we found no one."
And as they heard these words, both the priest and the commander of the temple and the chief priests, they were perplexed concerning them, whatever this might become.
And someone having arrived reported to them that "Behold, the men whom you put in the prison are in the temple standing and teaching the people."
Then the commander, having gone away with the attendants, was bringing them, not with violence, for they were fearing the people, lest they be stoned.
And having brought them, they stood them in the council. And the high priest questioned them,
saying, "With a charge we charged you not to teach upon this name, and behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring upon us the blood of this human."
And Peter, answering, and the apostles said, "It is necessary to obey God rather than humans.
The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you laid violent hands on, having hanged him upon a tree.
This one God exalted as founder and saviour by his right hand, to give a change of mind to Israel and release of sins.
And we are his witnesses of these words, and the holy spirit also, which God gave to those obeying him.
And they, having heard, were being cut through and were wanting to do away with them.
But a certain one in the council having stood up, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law honoured by all the people, ordered the humans to be put outside a short while,
and said to them, "Men, Israelites, take heed to yourselves concerning these humans, what you are about to do.

For before these days Theudas rose up, saying himself to be someone, to whom a number of men about four hundred was inclined; who was done away with, and all as many as were persuaded by him were dissolved and came to nothing.

After this one rose up Judas the Galilean in the days of the registration and drew away a considerable people after himself; and that one perished, and all as many as were persuaded by him were scattered.
And now I say to you, stand away from these humans and leave them alone; because if this counsel or this work is from humans, it will be overthrown;
but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them, lest also you be found God-fighters." And they were persuaded by him,
And having called the apostles, having flogged them, they charged them not to speak upon the name of Jesus and released them.
They indeed therefore were going from the face of the council rejoicing, because they were counted worthy on behalf of the name to be dishonoured;
and every day in the temple and according to house they were not ceasing teaching and proclaiming the good news, the Christ, Jesus.

acts_6.t: And in these days, the learners multiplying, there came a grumbling of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily service.
And the twelve, having called to themselves the multitude of the learners, said, "It is not pleasing for us, having left the word of God, to serve tables.
But look out, brothers and sisters, seven men from among you being well witnessed of, full of spirit and wisdom, whom we will appoint over this need;
but we will persevere in the prayer and in the service of the word."

And the word pleased before all the multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of trust and of holy spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch.
whom they set before the apostles, and having prayed they placed the hands upon them.
And the word of God was growing, and the number of the learners was being multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly, and a great crowd of the priests were obeying the trust.
And Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
But there rose up some of those from the synagogue called of Freedmen, and of Cyrenians and of Alexandrians and of those from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen;
and they were not strong enough to withstand the wisdom and the spirit by which he was speaking.
Then they suborned men saying that "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God."
And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and having come upon him they seized him together and led him into the council.
And they set up false witnesses saying, "This human does not cease speaking words against this holy place and the law;
for we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and will change the customs which Moses handed over to us."
And having gazed intently at him, all those sitting in the council saw his face as a face of an angel.

acts_7.t: And the high priest said, "If these things thus have it?"
And he said, "Men, brothers and fathers, hear. The God of the glory appeared to our father Abraham being in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran,
and said to him, 'Come out from your land and out of your kindred, and come here into the land which I shall show you.'
Then having come out from the land of Chaldeans he dwelt in Haran; and from there, after the dying of his father, he removed him into this land into which you now dwell.
And he did not give to him an inheritance in it, not even a foot's step, and he promised to give it to him for a holding and to his seed after him, there being no child to him.
And God spoke thus, that his seed will be a sojourner in a land belonging to another, and they will enslave it and mistreat it four hundred years.
'And the nation to which they shall be enslaved I will judge, I,' God said, 'and after these things they will come out and will serve me in this place.'
And he gave to him a covenant of circumcision; and thus he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
And the patriarchs, having been jealous of Joseph, gave him over into Egypt. And God was with him
and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave to him grace and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him leading one over Egypt and over his whole house.
But there came a famine upon the whole of Egypt and Canaan and great affliction, and our fathers were not finding fodder.
And Jacob, having heard there was grain in Egypt, sent out our fathers first.
And in the second Joseph was made known to his brothers, and the family of Joseph became manifest to Pharaoh.
And Joseph, having sent, called for Jacob his father and all his kindred in souls seventy-five.
And Jacob went down into Egypt, and he died, himself and our fathers,
and they were transferred into Shechem and were placed in the tomb which Abraham bought for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
But as the time of the promise was drawing near which God professed to Abraham, the people grew and was multiplied in Egypt,
until there rose up another king over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
This one, having dealt subtly with our race, mistreated the fathers, to make their babies exposed, so as not to be kept alive.
In which time Moses was born and was well-formed to God; who was nurtured three months in the house of the father.
And when he was exposed, the daughter of Pharaoh took him up and nurtured him for herself for a son.
And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of Egyptians; and he was powerful in his words and in his works.
And when a forty-year time was being fulfilled to him, it came up upon his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
And seeing a certain one being wronged, he defended and made vengeance for the one being worn down, having struck the Egyptian.
And he was supposing his brothers to understand that God through his hand was giving salvation to them; but they did not understand.
And on the following day he appeared to them as they were fighting, and was reconciling them into peace, saying, 'Men, you are brothers; why do you wrong one another?'
But the one wronging his neighbour pushed him away, saying, 'Who appointed you a ruler and a judge over us?
You do not want to do away with me in the manner you did away with the Egyptian yesterday?'
And Moses fled at this word and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
And forty years having been fulfilled, there appeared to him in the wilderness of the mountain Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire of a bramble bush.
And Moses, having seen, was marvelling at the vision; and as he was coming near to observe, there came a voice of the Lord,
'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob.' And Moses, having become trembling, was not daring to observe.
And the Lord said to him, 'Loose the sandal of your feet, for the place upon which you stand is holy earth.
Seeing I have seen the mistreatment of my people in Egypt and of their groaning I heard, and I came down to deliver them; and now come, I will send you into Egypt.'
This Moses whom they denied, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge?' — this one God has sent both as ruler and redeemer with the hand of the angel appearing to him in the bramble bush.
This one led them out, having done wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and in the Red Sea and in the wilderness forty years.
This is the Moses having said to the sons of Israel, 'A prophet for you will God raise up out of your brothers like me.'
This is the one having been in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel speaking to him in the mountain Sinai and with our fathers, who received living oracles to give to us.
to whom our fathers did not want to become obedient, but pushed him away and turned back in their hearts into Egypt,
saying to Aaron, 'Make for us gods who will go before us; for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what happened to him.'
And they made a calf in those days and brought up a sacrifice to the idol, and were being made glad in the works of their hands.

But God turned and gave them over to serve the host of the heaven, just as it has been written in a book of the prophets, 'Did you bring to me slain beasts and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
And you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god of you, Rephan, the figures which you made to bow before them; and I will remove you beyond Babylon.'
The tabernacle of the testimony was among our fathers in the wilderness, just as the one speaking to Moses arranged to make it according to the pattern which he had seen.
which also, having received in succession, our fathers brought in with Joshua in the dispossession of the nations whom God drove out from the face of our fathers until the days of David,
who found grace before God and asked to find a tent for the house of Jacob.
But Solomon built for him a house.
But the Most High does not dwell in handmade things, just as the prophet says,
'The heaven for me a throne, and the earth a footstool of my feet; what sort of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what place of my rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?'
"Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in the hearts and in the ears, you always fall against the holy spirit; as your fathers, also you.

Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those having announced beforehand concerning the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you now have become betrayers and murderers,
who received the law unto ordinances of angels, and did not keep it."
And hearing these things, they were being cut through in their hearts and were gnashing the teeth at him.
But being full of holy spirit, having gazed intently into the heaven, he saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right of God,
and he said, "Behold, I see the heavens having been opened and the Son of Man standing at the right of God."
And having cried out with a great voice, they held together their ears and rushed with one accord upon him.
And having cast him outside the city, they were stoning him. And the witnesses laid aside their garments beside the feet of a young man called Saul.
And they were stoning Stephen, calling upon and saying, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
And having placed the knees, he cried with a great voice, "Lord, do not set this sin against them." And having said this, he fell asleep.

acts_8.t: And Saul was consenting to his doing away with. And there came on that day a great persecution upon the assembly in Jerusalem; and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
And reverent men carried Stephen together and made a great beating of the breast over him.
But Saul was devastating the assembly, entering according to the houses, dragging both men and women, he was handing them over into prison.
Those indeed therefore having been scattered went through, announcing the good news of the word.
And Philip, having gone down into the city of Samaria, was heralding to them the Christ.
And the crowds were giving heed with one accord to the things being said by Philip, in their hearing and seeing the signs which he was doing.
For of many of those having unclean spirits, crying with a great voice, they were coming out; and many having been paralysed and lame were healed.
And there was much joy in that city.
But a certain man, Simon by name, was previously in the city practising magic and amazing the nation of Samaria, saying himself to be someone great.
to whom all were giving heed from small to great, saying, "This one is the power of God, the one called Great."
And they were giving heed to him because for a considerable time with the magic arts he had amazed them.
But when they trusted Philip announcing the good news concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were being baptised, both men and women.
And Simon himself also trusted, and having been baptised he was persevering with Philip; and beholding signs and great powers occurring, he was amazed.
And the apostles in Jerusalem, having heard that Samaria has received the word of God, sent to them Peter and John.
who, having gone down, prayed concerning them so that they might receive holy spirit;
for not yet was it having fallen upon any one of them, but only they had been baptised into the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then they were placing the hands upon them, and they were receiving holy spirit.
And Simon, having seen that through the laying on of the hands of the apostles the spirit is given, brought to them money,
saying, "Give also to me this authority, so that on whomever I place the hands he may receive holy spirit."
But Peter said to him, "Your silver with you be into destruction, because you supposed the gift of God to be acquired through money.
There is not to you a part nor a lot in this word, for your heart is not straight before God.
Change your mind therefore from this your evil and petition the Lord, if then the design of your heart will be released to you.
For into gall of bitterness and a bond of unrighteousness I see you being."
And Simon, answering, said, "You petition on my behalf toward the Lord, so that nothing may come upon me of the things you have spoken."
They indeed therefore, having solemnly witnessed and spoken the word of the Lord, were returning to Jerusalem, and to many villages of the Samaritans they were announcing the good news.
And an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Rise up and go according to midday upon the road going down from Jerusalem into Gaza; this is desert."
And having risen he went. And behold, a man, an Ethiopian, a eunuch, a potentate of Candace queen of Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come worshipping into Jerusalem,
and he was returning and sitting upon his chariot and was reading aloud the prophet Isaiah.
And the spirit said to Philip, "Approach and be joined to this chariot."
And Philip, having run up, heard him reading aloud Isaiah the prophet and said, "Then do you know what you are reading?"
And he said, "For how might I be able, unless someone shall guide me?" And he invited Philip, having come up, to sit with him.
And the passage of the scripture which he was reading aloud was this: 'As a sheep to slaughter he was led, and as a lamb before the one shearing him is voiceless, thus he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his judgment was taken away; his generation, who will describe it? For his life is taken from the earth.'
And the eunuch, answering, said to Philip, "I beg of you, concerning whom does the prophet say this? Concerning himself or concerning some other?"
And Philip, having opened his mouth and having begun from this scripture, announced the good news to him — Jesus.
And as they were going along the road, they came upon a certain water, and the eunuch says, "Behold, water; what prevents me to be baptised?"
[And Philip said, "If you trust out of the whole heart, it is permitted." And answering he said, "I trust the Son of God to be Jesus Christ."]
And he commanded the chariot to stand, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptised him.
And when they came up out of the water, spirit of the Lord seized Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him any longer; for he was going his way rejoicing.
But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he was announcing the good news to all the cities until his coming into Caesarea.

acts_9.t: But Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the learners of the Lord, having come to the high priest,
asked from him letters into Damascus to the synagogues, so that if he found any being of the Way, both men and women, having been bound he might lead them into Jerusalem.
And in the going, it happened that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly there flashed around him a light out of the heaven;
and having fallen upon the earth he heard a voice saying to him, "Saoul, Saoul, why do you persecute me?"
And he said: Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said: I am Jesus whom you are persecuting; [hard for you to kick against goads.]
[And trembling and astonished he said: Lord, what do you will me to do? And the Lord toward him:] But rise up and enter into the city, and it will be spoken to you what you must do.
And the men travelling with him had stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice but beholding no one.
And Saul was raised from the earth, and his eyes having been opened he was seeing nothing; and leading him by the hand they brought him into Damascus.
And he was three days not seeing, and did not eat nor drink.
And there was a certain learner in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias." And he said, "Behold I, Lord."
And the Lord to him, "Having risen, go upon the lane called Straight and seek in the house of Judas one named Saul, a Tarsian; for behold, he is praying,
and he saw a man named Ananias in a vision entering and placing hands upon him, so that he might see again."
But Ananias answered, "Lord, I heard from many concerning this man, how many evils he did to your holy ones in Jerusalem;
and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all those calling upon your name."
But the Lord said to him, "Go, because a vessel of choice is this one to me, to bear my name before nations and both kings and sons of Israel.
For I will show to him how many things it is necessary for him to suffer on behalf of my name."

And Ananias went away and entered into the house, and having placed upon him the hands he said, "Saoul, brother, the Lord has sent me — Jesus, the one having appeared to you in the way by which you were coming — so that you may see again and be filled of holy spirit."
And immediately there fell away from his eyes as scales, and he saw again, and having risen he was baptised,
and having taken food he was strengthened. And Saul was with the learners in Damascus some days;
and immediately in the synagogues he was heralding Jesus, that this one is the Son of God.

And all those hearing were amazed and were saying, "Is not this the one having ravaged in Jerusalem those calling upon this name, and here for this had come, so that having bound them he might lead them to the chief priests?"
But Saul was being empowered more and was confounding the Jews dwelling in Damascus, proving together that this one is the Christ.
And when considerable days were being fulfilled, the Jews took counsel together to do away with him.
But their plot was made known to Saul. And they were watching closely also the gates both day and night, so that they might do away with him;
but the learners of him, having taken him by night, through the wall let him down, having lowered him in a basket.
And having arrived into Jerusalem he was attempting to join himself to the learners; and all were fearing him, not trusting that he is a learner.

But Barnabas, having taken hold of him, led him to the apostles and described to them how in the way he saw the Lord and that he spoke to him, and how in Damascus he spoke boldly in the name of Jesus.
And he was with them going in and going out in Jerusalem, and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus,
and he was speaking and disputing toward the Hellenists; but they were setting their hand to do away with him.
And the brothers, having recognised it, brought him down into Caesarea and sent him away into Tarsus.

The assembly indeed therefore throughout the whole of Judea and Galilee and Samaria was having peace, being built up and going on in the fear of the Lord, and in the encouragement of the holy spirit it was being multiplied.
And it happened that Peter, going through all, came down also to the holy ones inhabiting Lydda.
And he found there a certain human named Aeneas, out of eight years lying upon a mat, who was paralysed.
And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus the Christ heals you; rise up and spread for yourself." And immediately he rose up.
And all those inhabiting Lydda and the Sharon saw him, who turned to the Lord.
And in Joppa there was a certain woman learner named Tabitha, which being translated is called Dorcas; she was full of good works and of acts of mercy which she was doing.
And it happened in those days that she, having become weak, died; and having washed her they placed her in an upper room.
And Lydda being near to Joppa, the learners, having heard that Peter is in it, sent two men to him, exhorting, "Do not delay to come through to us."

And Peter, having risen, went with them; whom having arrived they led up into the upper room, and all the widows stood beside him weeping and showing tunics and garments, as many as Dorcas was making while being with them.
And Peter, having put all outside and having placed the knees, prayed; and having turned toward the body he said, "Tabitha, rise up." And she opened her eyes, and having seen Peter she sat up.
And having given to her a hand, he raised her up; and having called the holy ones and the widows, he presented her living.
And it became known throughout the whole of Joppa, and many trusted upon the Lord.
And it happened that he remained considerable days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.

acts_10.t: Now a certain man was in Caesarea, by name Cornelius, a centurion out of the cohort called Italian,
reverent and fearing God with all his house, doing many acts of mercy for the people and petitioning God through all,
He saw in a vision plainly, about the ninth hour of the day, a messenger of God coming in toward him and saying to him: Cornelius.
And he, staring at him and becoming full of fear, said: What is it, Lord? And he said to him: Your prayers and your acts of mercy went up for a memorial before God.
And now send men to Joppa and send for a certain Simon who is surnamed Peter;
This one is being hosted by a certain Simon, a tanner, to whom is a house beside the sea; this one will speak to you what you must do.
And as the messenger speaking to him went away, calling two of his house-slaves and a reverent soldier of those attending closely on him,
and having narrated all things to them, he sent them off to Joppa.
And on the next day, as those were journeying and drawing near to the city, Peter went up onto the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour.
And he became very hungry and was wanting to taste; but while they were preparing, a standing-outside came upon him,
and he beholds the heaven having been opened and a certain vessel coming down upon him like a great linen cloth, bound by four beginnings, and being lowered onto the earth;
in which were existing all the four-footed things and the wild beasts and the creeping things of the earth and the winged things of the heaven.
And a voice came toward him: Rising up, Peter, sacrifice and eat.
But Peter said: By no means, Lord; because I never ate anything common and unclean.
And a voice again out of a second time toward him: What things God cleansed, you do not make common.
And this happened up to three times, and immediately the vessel was taken up into the heaven.

And as Peter was thoroughly perplexed in himself what the vision which he saw might be, behold, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having asked through for the house of Simon, stood at the gateway;
and having called out they were inquiring whether Simon, the one surnamed Peter, is being hosted here.
And while Peter was pondering through about the vision, the Spirit said to him: Behold, three men seeking you;
But rising up go down and travel with them, judging nothing between, because I myself have sent them.
And Peter, going down toward the men who had been sent from Cornelius to him, said: Behold, I am he whom you seek; what is the cause on account of which you are present?

And they said: Cornelius a centurion, a just man and fearing God, and being witnessed to by the whole nation of the Jews, was divinely instructed by a holy messenger to send for you into his house and to hear words from you.
So having called them in he hosted them. And on the next day, rising up, Peter went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa came together with him.
And on the next day he entered into Caesarea; and Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his kinsmen and his necessary friends.
And as it happened that Peter entered, Cornelius, meeting him, falling at his feet, did obeisance.
But Peter raised him, saying: Stand up; I myself also am a human.
And conversing with him he entered and finds many having come together,
And he said to them: You yourselves know how it is unlawful for a Jewish man to be joined to or to come toward one of another tribe; and to me God showed to call no human common or unclean.
Therefore also without contradiction I came, having been sent for. I inquire therefore, for what account did you send for me?
And Cornelius said: From the fourth day until this hour I was fasting and praying the ninth hour in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in shining clothing
and says: Cornelius, your prayer was heard and your acts of mercy were remembered before God.
Send therefore to Joppa and call over Simon who is surnamed Peter; this one is being hosted in the house of Simon a tanner beside the sea, who having arrived will speak to you.
At once therefore I sent to you, and you did well having arrived. Now therefore we all are present before God to hear all the things having been ordered to you by the Lord.
And Peter, opening the mouth, said: In truth I grasp that God is not a face-receiver,
but in every nation the one fearing him and working righteousness is acceptable to him.
The word which he sent to the sons of Israel, announcing peace through Jesus Christ — this one is Lord of all —
you yourselves know the word that came about throughout the whole of Judea, having begun from Galilee after the baptism which John proclaimed,
Jesus the one from Nazareth, how God anointed him with holy Spirit and power, who went through doing good and healing all those being oppressed by the slanderer, because God was with him;
And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; whom also they killed, hanging him upon a tree.
This one God raised on the third day and gave him to become manifest,
not to all the people but to witnesses having been hand-picked beforehand by God, to us, who ate together and drank together with him after his rising out of dead ones;
And he charged us to proclaim to the people and to witness fully that this is the one having been marked out by God as judge of living and dead.
To this one all the prophets witness, that everyone trusting into him receive release of sins through his name.
While Peter was still speaking these words, the holy Spirit fell upon all those hearing the word.
And the faithful ones out of circumcision, as many as came together with Peter, were astounded, because also upon the nations the gift of the holy Spirit has been poured out;
for they were hearing them speaking with tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered:
Can anyone forbid the water, that these not be baptised, who received the holy Spirit as also we?
And he ordered them to be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ of the Lord. Then they asked him to remain on some days.

acts_11.t: And the apostles and the brothers who were throughout Judea heard that also the nations received the word of God.
And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those out of circumcision were separating themselves against him,
saying that: You entered toward men having uncircumcision, and you ate together with them.
And Peter, beginning, was setting it out to them in order, saying:

I was in the city of Joppa praying, and I saw in a standing-outside a vision, a certain vessel coming down like a great linen cloth, by four beginnings being lowered out of the heaven, and it came as far as me;
into which, staring, I was observing and saw the four-footed things of the earth and the wild beasts and the creeping things and the winged things of the heaven.
And I heard also a voice saying to me: Rising up, Peter, sacrifice and eat.
But I said: By no means, Lord; because everything common or unclean never entered into my mouth.
But a voice out of a second time answered me out of the heaven: What things God cleansed, you do not make common.
And this happened up to three times, and all was drawn up again into the heaven.
And behold, at once three men stood at the house in which we were, having been sent from Caesarea toward me.
And the Spirit said to me to go together with them, judging nothing between. And these six brothers came with me, and we entered into the house of the man.
And he reported to us how he saw the messenger in his house having stood and saying to him: Send to Joppa men and send for Simon the one surnamed Peter,
who will speak words toward you in which you will be saved, you and all your house.
And in my beginning to speak, the holy Spirit fell upon them, just as also upon us in the beginning.
And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he was saying: John indeed baptised with water, but you will be baptised in holy Spirit.
If therefore God gave the equal gift to them as also to us, having trusted upon the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, able to forbid God?
And having heard these things they became quiet and glorified God, saying: So then also to the nations God gave the change of mind unto life.
So then those having been scattered from the pressure that came about over Stephen went through as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except only to Jews.
But some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, coming into Antioch, were speaking also to the Hellenists, announcing the good news of the Lord Jesus.
And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number, the one having trusted, turned upon the Lord.
And the word was heard into the ears of the assembly that was in Jerusalem concerning them, and they sent out Barnabas to go through as far as Antioch;
who, having arrived and having seen the grace that is of God, rejoiced and was encouraging all with the purpose of the heart to remain toward in the Lord;
because he was a good man and full of holy Spirit and of trust. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.
And Barnabas went out to Tarsus to search up Saul,

and having found him he led him to Antioch. And it happened to them also a whole year to be gathered together in the assembly and to teach a considerable crowd, and to be styled first in Antioch, the disciples, Christians.
And in these days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch;
And one out of them, by name Agabus, standing up, signified through the Spirit a great famine to be about to be upon the whole inhabited world, which also came about upon Claudius Caesar.
And of the disciples, according as anyone was prospering, they determined, each of them, to send for service to the brothers dwelling in Judea;
which also they did, having sent to the elders through the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

acts_12.t: And down at that season Herod the king threw on the hands to mistreat some of those from the assembly.
And he did away with James the brother of John with a sword.
And having seen that it is pleasing to the Jews, he added to seize Peter also — and these were the days of the unleavened things —
whom also having arrested he placed into prison, having handed over to four quaternions of soldiers to guard him, intending after the Passover to lead him up to the people.
So then Peter was being kept in the prison; but prayer was being made stretched-out by the assembly toward God concerning him.
And when Herod was about to lead him forward, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, having been bound with two chains, and guards before the door were guarding the prison.
And behold, a messenger of the Lord stood by and a light shone in the dwelling; and having struck the side of Peter he raised him, saying: Stand up in speed. And his chains fell out from the hands.
And the messenger said toward him: Gird yourself and bind on your sandals. And he did so. And he says to him: Throw around your outer garment and follow me.
And having gone out he was following, and he did not know that it is true, the thing happening through the messenger, but was supposing to see a vision.

And having gone through a first guard and a second they came upon the iron gate leading into the city, which of itself was opened to them, and having gone out they went forward one alley, and immediately the messenger stood away from him.
And Peter, having come to be in himself, said: Now I know truly that the Lord sent out his messenger and took me out from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
And having seen it together he came upon the house of Mary the mother of John the one surnamed Mark, where considerable ones were having been gathered together and praying.
And when he knocked at the door of the gateway, a young female slave came toward to listen, by name Rhoda;
and having recognised the voice of Peter, from the joy she did not open the gateway, but having run in she announced Peter to have stood before the gateway.
And they said toward her: You are raving. But she was insisting strongly to have it so. And they were saying: It is his messenger.
But Peter was remaining knocking; and having opened they saw him and were astounded.

And having waved down to them with the hand to be silent, he narrated to them how the Lord led him out from the prison; and he said: Report these things to James and to the brothers. And having gone out he travelled into another place.
And day having come, there was not a little disturbance among the soldiers, what then Peter became.
And Herod, having sought him out and not having found, having examined the guards, ordered them to be led away; and having gone down from Judea to Caesarea he was spending time.

And he was fighting in rage with Tyrians and Sidonians; and with one passion they were present toward him and, having persuaded Blastus the one over the bedchamber of the king, they were asking for peace, because of their country being fed from the royal one.
And on an appointed day Herod, having put on royal clothing and having sat upon the judgment seat, was addressing the people to them.
And the populace was shouting on: A god's voice and not a human's.
And instantly a messenger of the Lord struck him, in return for which he did not give the glory to God, and having become worm-eaten he expired.
But the word of God was growing and being multiplied.
And Barnabas and Saul returned into Jerusalem, having fulfilled the service, having taken along also John the one surnamed Mark.

acts_13.t: And there were in Antioch, throughout the assembly that was there, prophets and teachers, both Barnabas and Simeon the one called Niger and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen a foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
And while they were performing public service to the Lord and fasting, the holy Spirit said: Set apart indeed to me both Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.
Then having fasted and having prayed and having laid the hands on them, they released.
They indeed therefore, having been sent out by the holy Spirit, came down to Seleucia, and from there sailed away to Cyprus.
And having come to be in Salamis they were proclaiming the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; and they had also John as an attendant.
And having gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, to whom the name was Bar-Jesus,
who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an understanding man. This one, having called toward Barnabas and Saul, sought to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the magician withstood them, for so his name is translated, seeking to turn aside the proconsul from the trust.
But Saul, the one also Paul, having been filled with holy Spirit and having stared into him,
said: O full of all guile and all recklessness, son of the slanderer, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease twisting the straight ways of the Lord?

And now behold, a hand of the Lord upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun until a season. And instantly there fell upon him a mist and darkness, and going about he was seeking hand-leaders.
Then the proconsul, having seen the thing having happened, trusted, being struck out at the teaching of the Lord.
And having put out from Paphos, those around Paul came to Perga of Pamphylia; but John, having departed from them, returned to Jerusalem.
And they, having gone through from Perga, arrived at Antioch the Pisidian, and having entered into the synagogue on the day of the sabbaths they sat down.
And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the synagogue rulers sent toward them saying: Men, brothers, if there is among you any word of encouragement toward the people, speak.
And Paul, having stood up and having waved down with the hand, said: Men, Israelites, and those fearing God, hear.
The God of this people Israel chose out our fathers and exalted the people in the sojourning in a land of Egypt, and with a high arm he led them out from it;
And about a forty-year time he bore with their ways in the wilderness,
and having taken down seven nations in a land of Canaan he gave their land as an inheritance,
as with four hundred and fifty years; and after these things he gave judges until Samuel the prophet.
And from there they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul son of Kish, a man out of a tribe of Benjamin, forty years;
and having removed him he raised up David to them for a king, to whom also he said, witnessing: I found David the one of Jesse, a man according to my heart, who will do all my wishes.
Of this one God, from the seed according to promise, led to Israel a saviour, Jesus,
John having proclaimed beforehand, before the face of his entrance, a baptism of change of mind to all the people of Israel.
And as John was fulfilling the course he was saying: What do you suppose me to be? I am not; but behold, one comes after me of whom I am not worthy to loose the sandal of the feet.
Men, brothers, sons of a race of Abraham and those among you fearing God, to us the word of this salvation was sent out.
For those dwelling in Jerusalem and their rulers, not having known this one and the voices of the prophets which are read according to every sabbath, having judged, fulfilled them;
And having found not one cause of death, they asked Pilate for him to be done away with.
And as they completed all the things written about him, having taken him down from the tree they placed him into a tomb.
But God raised him out of dead ones,
who was seen for more days by those having gone up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who now are his witnesses toward the people.
And we announce good news to you, the promise having come about toward the fathers,
that this God has fulfilled out to their children, to us, having raised up Jesus, as also in the psalm it has been written, the second: You are my son, I today have begotten you.
And that he raised him out of dead ones, no longer being about to return into corruption, thus he has said that: I will give to you the holy things of David, the faithful ones.
Therefore also in another place he says: You will not give your holy one to see corruption.
For David indeed, having served the counsel of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was added toward his fathers and saw corruption;
But he whom God raised did not see corruption.
Known therefore let it be to you, men, brothers, that through this one release of sins is proclaimed to you;
and from all things from which you were not able in the law of Moses to be freed, in this one everyone trusting is freed.
See therefore lest that come upon you which has been spoken in the prophets:
See, the despisers, and marvel and be made to vanish, because a work I am working, I, in your days, a work which you will by no means trust if anyone narrates it out to you.
And as they were going out from the synagogue of the Jews, the nations were urging that on the sabbath between these words be spoken to them.
And the synagogue having been loosed, many of the Jews and of the reverent proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking toward them, were persuading them to remain toward in the grace of God.
And on the coming sabbath nearly all the city was gathered together to hear the word of the Lord.
But the Jews, having seen the crowds, were filled with zeal and were speaking against the things being spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.

And having spoken with all openness, Paul and Barnabas said: To you it was necessary that the word of God be spoken first; since you thrust it away and do not judge yourselves worthy of the eternal life, behold, we turn to the nations.
For thus the Lord has commanded us: I have set you for a light of nations, for you to be for salvation as far as an extremity of the earth.
And the nations, hearing, were rejoicing and were glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as were having been appointed unto eternal life trusted.
And the word of the Lord was being carried through the whole country.
But the Jews urged on the reverent women and the well-formed ones and the first men of the city, and they roused up a persecution upon Paul and Barnabas and threw them out from their boundaries.
And they, having shaken out the dust of their feet against them, came to Iconium.
And the learners were being filled with joy and with holy Spirit.

acts_14.t: And it happened in Iconium, according to the same, that they entered into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke thus, so that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks trusted.
But the Jews having disbelieved roused up and made evil the souls of the nations against the brothers.
A considerable time therefore they spent speaking openly upon the Lord, the one witnessing upon the word of his grace, and giving signs and wonders to happen through their hands.
And the multitude of the city was split, and some were with the Jews, but others with the apostles.
And as there came about an impulse of both the nations and Jews with their rulers to insult and to stone them,
having seen it together they fled down into the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding country,
and there they were announcing good news.
And a certain man, powerless in the feet, was sitting in Lystra, being lame from his mother's belly, who never walked about.
This one heard Paul speaking, who, having stared at him and having seen that he has trust to be saved,
said with a great voice: Stand up upon your feet upright. And he leaped and was walking about.
And the crowds, having seen what Paul did, lifted up their voice, saying in Lycaonian: The gods, having been made like humans, came down toward us;
And they were calling Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, since he was the one leading the word.
And the priest of the Zeus being before the city, having brought bulls and garlands to the gateways, was wanting to sacrifice with the crowds.
But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having heard, having torn their garments, sprang out into the crowd, crying out

and saying: Men, why do you do these things? We also are humans of like feeling with you, announcing good news to you to turn from these vain things to a living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them,
who in the generations having gone by let all the nations travel in their own ways;
although he did not leave himself unwitnessed, doing good, giving to you rains from heaven and fruit-bearing seasons, filling full of food and gladness your hearts.
And saying these things they scarcely stopped the crowds from sacrificing to them.
But there came upon them from Antioch and Iconium Jews, and having persuaded the crowds and having stoned Paul, they were dragging him outside the city, supposing him to have died.
But the learners having encircled him, rising up he entered into the city; and on the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
And having announced good news to that city and having made learners of a considerable number, they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch,
strengthening upon the souls of the learners, encouraging to remain in the trust, and that through many pressures it is necessary for us to enter into the kingdom of God.
And having stretched out the hand for them, elders in each assembly, having prayed with fastings, they committed them to the Lord into whom they had trusted.
And having gone through Pisidia they came to Pamphylia,
and having spoken in Perga the word, they went down to Attalia;
and from there they sailed away to Antioch, from where they had been handed over to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.
And having arrived and having gathered together the assembly they were announcing as much as God did with them, and that he opened to the nations a door of trust.
And they spent there not a little time with the learners.

acts_15.t: And certain ones having come down from Judea were teaching the brothers that: Unless you are circumcised in the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.

And there having come about no little standing-apart and questioning by Paul and Barnabas toward them, they arranged for Paul and Barnabas and certain others out of them to go up to the apostles and elders into Jerusalem about this question.

They indeed therefore, having been sent forward by the assembly, were going through both Phoenicia and Samaria, narrating out the turning of the nations, and they were making great joy for all the brothers.
And having arrived into Jerusalem they were received from the assembly and the apostles and the elders, and they announced as much as God did with them.
But there stood up some of those from the sect of the Pharisees who had trusted, saying that it is necessary to circumcise them and to charge them to keep the law of Moses.
And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this word.

And much questioning having come about, Peter, having stood up, said toward them: Men, brothers, you yourselves know that from ancient days God chose among you, through my mouth, for the nations to hear the word of the good news and to trust.
And the heart-knower God witnessed to them, having given the holy Spirit to them just as also to us,
and he judged nothing between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by the trust.
Now therefore why do you test God, to place a yoke upon the neck of the learners which neither our fathers nor we were strong enough to bear?
But through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we trust to be saved, according to which manner also those ones.
And all the multitude was silent, and they were hearing Barnabas and Paul narrating as much as God did, signs and wonders, among the nations through them.
And after their being silent James answered, saying: Men, brothers, hear me.
Simeon narrated how first God visited to take out of the nations a people for his name.
And with this the words of the prophets agree, as it has been written:
After these things I will turn back and rebuild the tent of David that has fallen, and its things having been dug down I will rebuild and I will set it straight again,
so that the rest of the humans may seek out the Lord, and all the nations upon whom my name has been called upon them, says the Lord doing these things,
known from an age are to God all his works.
Therefore I judge not to trouble further those from the nations turning to God,
but to write to them to hold off from the pollutions of the idols and from sexual immorality and from what is strangled and from blood.
For Moses from ancient generations has in each city those proclaiming him, being read in the synagogues according to every sabbath.

Then it seemed good to the apostles and to the elders with the whole assembly, having chosen out men from among them, to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas the one called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men among the brothers,
having written through their hand these things: The apostles and the elders and the brothers, to the brothers throughout Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, those from nations: to rejoice.
Since we heard that certain ones from among us, having gone out, troubled you with words, dismantling your souls, to whom we gave no orders,
it seemed good to us, having become of one passion, having chosen out men, to send to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
humans having handed over their souls for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, and they themselves through word announcing the same things.
For it seemed good to the holy Spirit and to us to place upon you no greater burden except these necessary things:
to hold off from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from strangled things and from sexual immorality; from which keeping yourselves thoroughly you will do well. Be strong.
They indeed therefore, having been released, came down to Antioch, and having gathered together the multitude they handed over the letter.
And having read it they rejoiced at the encouragement.
And Judas and Silas, being themselves also prophets, through much word encouraged the brothers and strengthened them.
And having made a time they were released with peace from the brothers toward those having sent them.
[But it seemed good to Silas to remain there.]
And Paul and Barnabas were spending time in Antioch, teaching and announcing good news, with also many others, of the word of the Lord.
And after some days Paul said toward Barnabas: Having turned back, let us indeed visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, how they have it.
And Barnabas was wishing to take along also John the one called Mark;
