But Paul was deeming it right, the one having stood away from them from Pamphylia and not having come together with them to the work, not to take along this one.
And there came about a sharp provocation, so that they separated from one another, and Barnabas, having taken Mark, sailed away to Cyprus.
And Paul, having chosen Silas, went out, having been handed over to the grace of the Lord by the brothers.
And he was going through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.

acts_16.t: And he arrived also at Derbe and at Lystra. And behold, a certain learner was there, by name Timothy, son of a certain Jewish woman, a faithful one, but of a Greek father.
who was being witnessed to by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.
This one Paul wished to go out with him, and having taken him he circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places; for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
And as they were travelling through the cities, they were handing over to them to guard the decrees that had been judged by the apostles and the elders who were in Jerusalem.
The assemblies indeed therefore were being made firm in the trust and were abounding in number according to each day.
And they went through the Phrygian and Galatian country, having been forbidden by the holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia,
and having come down along Mysia they were attempting to travel into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not permit them.
And having passed by Mysia they came down to Troas.
And a vision through the night was seen by Paul: a certain Macedonian man was standing and urging him and saying: Having crossed over into Macedonia, help us.
And as he saw the vision, immediately we sought to go out into Macedonia, concluding together that God has called us to announce good news to them.
Having put out therefore from Troas we ran straight to Samothrace, and on the following day to Neapolis,
and from there to Philippi, which is a city of a first part of Macedonia, a colony. And we were in this city spending some days.
And on the day of the sabbaths we went outside the gate beside a river, where we were supposing there to be a prayer, and having sat down we were speaking to the women having come together.
And a certain woman by name Lydia, a purple-seller of the city of Thyatira, revering God, was hearing, whose heart the Lord opened up to attend to the things being spoken by Paul.
And as she was baptised, and her house, she urged, saying: If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, having entered into my house, remain. And she constrained us.
And it happened, as we were travelling to the prayer, a certain young female slave having a python spirit met us, who was providing much work-profit for her lords by divining.
This one, following after Paul and us, was crying out, saying: These humans are servants of the Most High God, who announce to you a way of salvation.

And this she was doing over many days. And Paul, having been worn out, and having turned to the spirit, said: I charge you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out from her. And it came out in that hour.
And her lords, having seen that the hope of their work-profit went out, having laid hold of Paul and Silas, dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers,
and having led them forward to the magistrates they said: These humans are thoroughly disturbing our city, being Jews,
and they proclaim customs which is not lawful for us to receive nor to do, being Romans.
And the crowd stood together against them, and the magistrates, having torn off their garments, were ordering to beat with rods.
And having laid many blows on them they threw them into prison, having charged the jailer to keep them securely;
who, having received such a charge, threw them into the inner prison and secured their feet into the wood.
And down about the midnight Paul and Silas, praying, were hymning God; and the prisoners were listening in to them.
And suddenly a great earthquake happened, so that the foundations of the prison-house were shaken; and instantly all the doors were opened, and the bonds of all were loosed.
And the jailer, having become awake and having seen the doors of the prison having been opened, having drawn the sword, was about to do away with himself, supposing the prisoners to have escaped.
But Paul called with a great voice, saying: Do nothing bad to yourself, for we are all here.
And having asked for lights he sprang in, and having become trembling he fell before Paul and Silas,
and having led them forward outside he said: Lords, what must I do that I may be saved?
And they said: Trust upon the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your house.
And they spoke to him the word of the Lord with all those in his house.
And having taken them along in that hour of the night he washed from the blows, and he was baptised, he and all those of his, instantly.
And having led them up into his house he set a table beside, and he exulted with his whole house, having trusted in God.
And day having come, the magistrates sent the rod-bearers, saying: Release those humans.
And the jailer announced these words toward Paul, that: The magistrates have sent so that you may be released; now therefore, having gone out, travel in peace.

But Paul said toward them: Having flogged us publicly uncondemned, humans being Romans, they threw us into prison, and now secretly they throw us out? No indeed, but having come themselves let them lead us out.
And the rod-bearers announced these words to the magistrates; and they were afraid, having heard that they are Romans.
And having come they urged them, and having led them out they were asking them to go away from the city.
And having gone out from the prison they entered toward Lydia, and having seen the brothers they encouraged them and went out.

acts_17.t: And having journeyed through Amphipolis and Apollonia they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
And according to the thing having been customary to Paul, he entered toward them, and upon three sabbaths he reasoned with them from the writings,
opening up and setting before that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise out of dead ones, and that this is the Christ, the Jesus whom I proclaim to you.
And some out of them were persuaded and were allotted to Paul and to Silas, both of the reverent Greeks a great multitude and of the first women not a few.

But the Jews, having become zealous, and having taken along some wicked men of the market-loungers and having made a crowd, were making an uproar in the city; and having stood upon the house of Jason, they were seeking to lead them forward to the populace.
And not having found them, they were dragging Jason and some brothers upon the city-rulers, shouting that: These, the ones having stirred up the inhabited world, are present here also,
whom Jason has received; and these all act opposite to the decrees of Caesar, saying another to be king, Jesus.
And they troubled the crowd and the city-rulers hearing these things,
and having taken the sufficient thing from Jason and the rest, they released them.
And the brothers immediately through the night sent out both Paul and Silas to Berea, who, having arrived, were going into the synagogue of the Jews.
And these were more well-born than those in Thessalonica, who received the word with all eagerness, according to each day examining up the writings whether these things might have it thus.
Many indeed therefore out of them trusted, and of the Greek women, the well-formed ones, and men, not a few.
And as the Jews from Thessalonica knew that also in Berea the word of God was proclaimed by Paul, they came there also, shaking and troubling the crowds.
And immediately then the brothers sent Paul out to travel as far as upon the sea; and both Silas and Timothy remained there.
And those conducting Paul led him as far as Athens, and having received a command toward Silas and Timothy that as quickly as possible they should come toward him, they were going out.
And in Athens, while Paul was waiting for them, his spirit was being provoked in him, observing the city being full of idols.
He was reasoning therefore in the synagogue with the Jews and with those revering, and in the marketplace according to every day with those happening to be present.

And some also of the Epicurean and of the Stoic philosophers were engaging with him; and some were saying: What might this seed-picker wish to say? And others: He seems to be an announcer of foreign divinities — because he was announcing the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
And having taken hold of him they led him upon the Areopagus, saying: Are we able to know what is this new teaching being spoken by you?
For you bring in some strange things to our hearings; we wish therefore to know what these things might wish to be.
And all Athenians and the foreigners sojourning there were having leisure for nothing else than to say something or to hear something newer.
And Paul, having stood in the middle of the Areopagus, said: Men, Athenians, according to all things I observe you as rather god-fearing.
For going through and observing up your objects of reverence, I found also an altar on which had been inscribed: To an unknown god. What therefore not knowing you revere, this I proclaim to you.
The God having made the world and all the things in it, this one, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in hand-made shrines,
nor is he served by human hands as needing anything in addition, himself giving to all life and breath and all things,
And he made out of one [man] every nation of humans to dwell upon all the face of the earth, having marked out appointed seasons and the boundary-settings of their dwelling,
to seek God, if perhaps indeed they might feel after him and find, and yet he is not far from one each of us.
For in him we live and are moved and are, as also some of the poets according to you have said: For of him also we are offspring.
Being therefore offspring of God, we ought not to suppose the divine to be like to gold or silver or stone, an engraving of skill and of reflection of a human.
The times indeed therefore of the ignorance God, having overlooked, now charges the humans, all everywhere, to change the mind,
because he set a day in which he is about to judge the inhabited world in righteousness by a man whom he marked out, having offered trust to all, having raised him out of dead ones.
And having heard a resurrection of dead ones, some were mocking, but others said: We will hear you about this also again.
And thus Paul went out from the midst of them.
But some men, having been joined to him, trusted, among whom also Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman by name Damaris and others with them.

acts_18.t: And after these things, having separated from Athens, Paul came to Corinth.

And having found a certain Jew by name Aquila, a Pontian by race, recently having come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife, because of Claudius having arranged all the Jews to be separated from Rome, he came toward them.
And because of being of the same trade he was remaining with them and was working; for they were tentmakers by the trade.
And he was reasoning in the synagogue according to every sabbath, and was persuading both Jews and Greeks.
And as both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was being held together by the word, witnessing fully to the Jews the Christ to be Jesus.
And they setting themselves in array against and blaspheming, having shaken out the garments he said toward them: Your blood upon your head; I am clean; from now I will travel to the nations.
And having crossed over from there he entered into a house of a certain one by name Titius Justus, revering God, of whom the house was bordering on the synagogue.
And Crispus the synagogue ruler trusted the Lord with his whole house, and many of the Corinthians hearing were trusting and being baptised.
And the Lord said in a night through a vision to Paul: Do not fear, but speak and do not be silent,
because I am with you, and no one will lay upon you to mistreat you; because a people is to me, much, in this city.
And he sat a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
And Gallio being proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up with one passion against Paul and led him upon the judgment seat,
saying that: Contrary to the law this one persuades the humans to revere God.
And Paul being about to open the mouth, Gallio said toward the Jews: If indeed therefore it were some wrongdoing or wicked recklessness, O Jews, according to reason I would have borne with you;
But if it is questions about a word and names and law according to you, you yourselves will see; a judge of these things I do not wish to be.
And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
And all, having laid hold of Sosthenes the synagogue ruler, were beating him before the judgment seat; and none of these things was a care to Gallio.

And Paul, having remained on still considerable days, having taken leave of the brothers, was sailing away into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having sheared the head in Cenchreae; for he was having a vow.
And they arrived at Ephesus, and those ones he left there; but he himself, having entered into the synagogue, reasoned with the Jews.
And they asking him to remain upon a longer time, he did not nod assent;
but having taken leave and having said: It is necessary for me by all means to make the coming feast in Jerusalem; and again I will come back toward you, God willing. And he put out from Ephesus.
And having come down to Caesarea, having gone up and having greeted the assembly, he went down to Antioch;
and having made some time he went out, going through in order the Galatian country and Phrygia, strengthening all the learners.
And a certain Jew, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by race, a man of words, arrived at Ephesus, being powerful in the writings.
This one had been catechised in the way of the Lord, and boiling in the spirit he was speaking and teaching accurately the things about Jesus, understanding only the baptism of John.
And this one began to speak openly in the synagogue; and Priscilla and Aquila, having heard him, took him to themselves and more accurately set forth to him the way of God.
And he wishing to go through into Achaia, the brothers, having urged him on, wrote to the learners to receive him; who, having arrived, contributed much to those having trusted through the grace;
for vigorously he was thoroughly confuting the Jews publicly, demonstrating through the writings the Christ to be Jesus.

acts_19.t: And it happened, in Apollos being in Corinth, Paul, having gone through the upper parts, to come down to Ephesus and to find some learners,
and he said toward them: Did you receive holy Spirit having trusted? And they said toward him: But neither whether there is a holy Spirit did we hear.
And he said: Into what then were you baptised? And they said: Into the baptism of John.
And Paul said: John baptised a baptism of change of mind, saying to the people to trust into the one coming after him, that is, into the Christ Jesus.
And having heard they were baptised into the name of the Lord Jesus;
and Paul having laid on them the hands, the holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking with tongues and prophesying.
And all the men were about twelve.
And having entered into the synagogue he was speaking openly over three months, reasoning and persuading the things about the kingdom of God.

And as some were being hardened and were disbelieving, speaking evil of the way before the multitude, having stood away from them he separated the learners, according to each day reasoning in the school of a certain Tyrannus.
And this happened over two years, so that all those dwelling in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
And powers not the ones happening by chance God was doing through the hands of Paul,
so that even upon those being weak were carried away from his skin sweat-cloths or work-aprons, and the diseases were released from them, and the evil spirits went out.
And some also of the Jews going about, exorcists, undertook to name over those having the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying: I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims.
And there were of a certain Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, seven, the sons, doing this.
And answering, the evil spirit said to them: The Jesus indeed I know, and the Paul I am acquainted with; but you, who are you?
And having leapt upon them, the human in whom was the evil spirit, and having mastered both, he was strong against them, so that naked and having been wounded they fled out from that house.
And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, those dwelling in Ephesus, and fear fell upon all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
And many of those having trusted were coming, confessing out and announcing up their practices.

And considerable ones of those having practised the curious arts, having brought together the books, were burning them before all; and they counted together their prices and found silver, five myriads.
Thus according to might the word of the Lord was growing and was being strong.

And as these things were fulfilled, Paul placed in the spirit, having gone through Macedonia and Achaia, to travel into Jerusalem, having said that: After my coming to be there, it is necessary for me also to see Rome.
And having sent into Macedonia two of those serving him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself held on a time in Asia.
And there came about down at that season a disturbance not a little concerning the way.
For a certain one by name Demetrius, a silversmith making silver shrines of Artemis, was providing to the craftsmen not a little work-profit;
whom having gathered together, and the workers concerning such things, he said: Men, you understand that from this work-profit is our well-being,
and you observe and hear that not only of Ephesus but of nearly all Asia this Paul, having persuaded, removed a considerable crowd, saying that they are not gods, the ones coming to be through hands.

And not only this is in danger for us, the part, to come into refutation, but also the sanctuary of the great goddess Artemis to be reckoned as nothing, and to be about also to be taken down from her magnificence, whom the whole of Asia and the inhabited world reveres.
And having heard and having become full of rage, they were crying out, saying: Great is the Artemis of Ephesians.
And the city was filled with the confusion; and they rushed with one passion into the theatre, having seized together Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, fellow travellers of Paul.
And Paul wishing to enter into the populace, the learners were not permitting him;
And also some of the Asiarchs, being friends to him, having sent toward him, were urging him not to give himself into the theatre.
Others indeed therefore were crying out another thing; for the assembly was having been confused, and the majority did not know for what cause they had come together.
And out of the crowd they instructed together Alexander, the Jews having thrust him forward; and Alexander, having waved down the hand, was wishing to defend himself to the populace.
And having recognised that he is a Jew, one voice came about out of all, for about two hours crying: Great is the Artemis of Ephesians.

And the scribe, having settled down the crowd, says: Men, Ephesians, for what human is there who does not know the city of the Ephesians to be temple-keeper of the great Artemis and of the sky-fallen thing?
These things therefore being not to be spoken against, it is necessary for you to be having been settled down and to do nothing headlong.
For you led these men, neither temple-robbers nor blaspheming our goddess.
If indeed therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a word against anyone, court days are brought and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.
And if you seek anything beyond, in the lawful assembly it will be resolved.
For also we are in danger of being accused of faction concerning today, no cause existing concerning which we will not be able to render an account concerning this coiling-together.
And these things having said, he dismissed the assembly.

acts_20.t: And after the uproar ceased, Paul, having sent for the disciples and having encouraged them, having embraced them, went out to journey into Macedonia.
And having gone through those parts and having encouraged them with much speech, he came into Greece.
And having made three months, a plot having come about against him by the Jews as he was about to put out to sea for Syria, he became of a mind to return through Macedonia.
And there accompanied him as far as Asia Sopater of Pyrrhus, a Beroean, and of Thessalonians Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius a Derbean, and Timothy, and Asians Tychicus and Trophimus,
And these, having gone ahead, were waiting for us in Troas;
And we sailed out after the days of the unleavened bread from Philippi and came to them in Troas within five days, where we spent seven days.
And on the first of the sabbaths, we having been gathered together to break bread, Paul was discoursing to them, being about to depart on the next day, and he prolonged the word until midnight;
And there were sufficient lamps in the upper room where we were gathered together.

And a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting on the window, being carried down by deep sleep, Paul discoursing at greater length, having been carried down from the sleep, fell from the third storey below and was picked up dead.
And Paul, having gone down, fell upon him and, having embraced him, said, "Do not be making an uproar, for his soul is in him."
And having gone up and having broken the bread and having tasted, and having conversed a considerable while until dawn, so he departed.
And they brought the boy living, and were comforted not moderately.
But we, having gone ahead to the ship, put out for Assos, from there intending to take Paul aboard; for so he had arranged it, intending himself to go on foot.
And as he met with us at Assos, having taken him aboard we came to Mitylene;
And having sailed from there, on the following day we arrived opposite Chios, and on the next we put in at Samos and, having remained at Trogyllium, on the day after we came to Miletus.
For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that it might not happen to him to spend time in Asia; for he was hurrying, if it might be possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
And from Miletus, having sent to Ephesus, he summoned the elders of the assembly.
And when they came to him he said to them, "You yourselves know from the first day on which I set foot in Asia how I was with you the whole time,
slaving for the Lord with all lowliness of mind and many tears and trials that befell me in the plots of the Jews;
how I kept back nothing of the things profitable, so as not to announce to you and to teach you publicly and from house to house,
witnessing thoroughly to Jews and also to Greeks the change of mind toward God and trust into our Lord Jesus Christ.
And now behold, I, bound in the spirit, am going to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will meet me in it,
except that the Holy Spirit witnesses thoroughly to me city by city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.

But of no account do I make my soul, nor do I hold it precious to myself, so as to finish my course with joy and the service which I received from the Lord Jesus, to witness thoroughly the good news of the grace of God.
And now behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom of God, will no longer see my face.
Therefore I witness to you on this day that I am clean from the blood of all.
For I did not keep back so as not to announce to you all the counsel of God.
Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the Holy Spirit set you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of God, which he acquired through his own blood.
For I myself know this, that after my departure grievous wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock,
and from among your own selves men will rise up speaking things having been distorted, to draw away the disciples after themselves.
Therefore be watchful, remembering that for three years night and day I did not cease admonishing each one with tears.
And now I commit you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those having been made holy.
Of silver or of gold or of clothing of no one did I covet.
But you yourselves know that to my needs and to those being with me these hands served.

In all things I showed you that thus labouring it is necessary to take hold of those being weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, "It is more blessed to give than to receive."
And having said these things, having placed his knees with them all, he prayed.
And considerable weeping of all came about, and having fallen upon Paul's neck they were kissing him fervently,
grieving most of all over the word which he had spoken, that they were no longer about to behold his face. And they were escorting him to the ship.

acts_21.t: And when it came about that we put out to sea, having been torn away from them, running a straight course we came to Cos, and on the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
And having found a ship crossing over into Phoenicia, having embarked we put out to sea.
And having sighted Cyprus and having left it on the left, we were sailing to Syria and came down to Tyre; for there the ship was unloading the cargo.
And having found the disciples, we remained there seven days; and these were telling Paul through the Spirit not to embark for Jerusalem.

And when it came about that we had completed the days, having gone out we were journeying, all of them with wives and children escorting us as far as outside the city, and having placed our knees on the shore, having prayed
we took leave of one another and embarked on the ship, and those went back to their own things.
And we, having completed the voyage from Tyre, arrived at Ptolemais, and having greeted the brothers we remained one day with them.
And on the next day, having gone out, those around Paul, we came to Caesarea, and having entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, being of the seven, we remained with him.
And to this man there were four daughters, virgins, prophesying.
And while we were remaining more days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea,

and having come to us and having taken up Paul's belt, having bound his own feet and hands, he said, "These things says the Holy Spirit: the man whose belt this is, so will the Jews in Jerusalem bind, and they will hand him over into the hands of the nations."
And as we heard these things, we ourselves and the local people were begging him not to go up to Jerusalem.
Then Paul answered, "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart in pieces? For I am ready not only to be bound but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
And as he was not persuaded we became quiet, saying, "Let the will of the Lord come about."
And after these days, having packed up, we were going up to Jerusalem.
And there came together also some of the disciples from Caesarea with us, bringing us to the one with whom we should be lodged, a certain Mnason a Cypriot, an early disciple.
And when we came to Jerusalem the brothers received us gladly.
And on the following day Paul was going in with us to James, and all the elders came to be present.
And having greeted them, he was relating one by one each of the things which God did among the nations through his service.
And having heard, they were glorifying God, and they said to him, "You behold, brother, how many myriads there are among the Jews of those having trusted, and all are zealots of the law.
And they were informed about you that you teach apostasy from Moses to all the Jews throughout the nations, saying that they should not circumcise their children nor walk in the customs.
What then is it? Certainly a multitude must come together; for they will hear that you have come.
Therefore do this which we say to you: there are with us four men having a vow upon themselves.

Taking these, be purified with them and spend on them so that they may shave the head, and all will know that of the things they have been informed about you there is nothing, but that you yourself also walk in line, guarding the law.

And concerning the nations having trusted, we ourselves sent a letter, having judged that they should keep none of such things, except that they should guard themselves both from what is sacrificed to idols and blood and what is strangled and sexual immorality.

Then Paul, having taken the men, on the following day having been purified with them, was going into the temple, announcing the fulfilment of the days of the purification, until the offering was offered for each one of them.
And as the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia, having seen him in the temple, were throwing all the crowd into confusion and laid their hands on him,

crying out, "Men, Israelites, help! This is the man who teaches all everywhere against the people and the law and this place; and further he has even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place."
For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they were supposing that Paul brought into the temple.
And the whole city was moved and there came about a running together of the people, and having taken hold of Paul they were dragging him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
And while they were seeking to kill him, a report went up to the tribune of the cohort that all Jerusalem is being poured into confusion.
who at once, having taken soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them; and they, having seen the tribune and the soldiers, ceased beating Paul.
Then the tribune, having drawn near, took hold of him and ordered him to be bound with two chains, and was inquiring who he might be and what he has done.
And others were calling out one thing, others another, in the crowd. And since he was not able to know what was certain because of the uproar, he ordered him to be brought into the barracks.
And when he came upon the steps, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
for the multitude of the people was following, crying out, "Away with him!"
And being about to be led into the barracks, Paul says to the tribune, "Is it permitted for me to say something to you?" And he said, "Do you know Greek?
Are you not then the Egyptian who before these days raised a revolt and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?"
And Paul said, "I am a man, a Jew, a Tarsian of Cilicia, a citizen of no unmarked city; and I beg you, permit me to speak to the people."
And when he had given permission, Paul, standing on the steps, motioned with the hand to the people, and much silence having come about, he addressed them in the Hebrew language, saying:

acts_22.t: "Men, brothers and fathers, hear my defence now made to you."
And having heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they provided the more quiet. And he says:

"I am a man, a Jew, having been born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but having been brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel having been trained according to the exactness of the ancestral law, being a zealot for God just as you all are today,
who persecuted this Way as far as death, binding and handing over into prisons both men and women,

as also the high priest witnesses for me and all the body of elders, from whom also, having received letters to the brothers, I was journeying to Damascus to bring also those being there, bound, to Jerusalem, in order that they might be punished.
And it came about to me, journeying and drawing near to Damascus about midday, suddenly out of heaven a great light flashed around me;
and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?'
And I answered, 'Who are you, Lord?' And he said to me, 'I am Jesus the Nazorean, whom you are persecuting.'
And those being with me on the one hand gazed at the light, but the voice of the one speaking to me they did not hear.
And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' And the Lord said to me, 'Having risen, journey into Damascus, and there it will be spoken to you concerning all things which have been appointed for you to do.'
And as I was not seeing because of the glory of that light, being led by the hand by those being with me, I came into Damascus.
And a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, being witnessed to by all the Jews dwelling there,
having come to me and having stood over me, said to me, 'Saul, brother, look up.' And I in that very hour looked up at him.
And he said, 'The God of our fathers appointed you beforehand to know his will and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice out of his mouth,
because you will be a witness for him to all humans of what you have seen and heard.
And now, why do you delay? Having risen, be baptised and wash away your sins, having called upon his name.'
And it came about to me, having returned to Jerusalem and while I was praying in the temple, that I came to be in a trance
and saw him saying to me, 'Make haste and go out quickly from Jerusalem, because they will not receive your witness concerning me.'
And I said, 'Lord, they themselves understand that I was imprisoning and flogging throughout the synagogues those trusting upon you,
and when the blood of Stephen your witness was being poured out, I myself also was standing by and consenting and guarding the garments of those doing away with him.'
And he said to me, 'Go, because I will send you out far away to the nations.'"
And they were hearing him as far as this word, and they lifted up their voice, saying, "Away from the earth with such a one; for it was not fitting for him to live."
And as they were screaming and tossing their garments and throwing dust into the air,
the tribune ordered him to be brought into the barracks, having said that he was to be examined with lashes, so that he might know thoroughly for what cause they were calling out against him thus.
And as they stretched him forward with the thongs, Paul said to the centurion standing by, "Is it permitted to you to flog a man, a Roman, and uncondemned?"
And the centurion, having heard, having come to the tribune, reported, saying, "See what you are about to do; for this man is a Roman."
And the tribune, having come, said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?" And he said, "Yes."
And the tribune answered, "I acquired this citizenship for a large sum." And Paul said, "But I have even been born so."
Immediately therefore those being about to examine him stood away from him; and the tribune also was afraid, having recognised that he is a Roman and that he was the one who had bound him.

And on the next day, wishing to know the certainty, what he is accused of by the Jews, he loosed him from the bonds and ordered the chief priests and all their council to come together, and having brought Paul down, he stood him among them.

acts_23.t: And Paul, having looked intently at the council, said, "Men, brothers, I have conducted myself as a citizen to God in all good conscience until this day."
And the high priest Ananias ordered those standing beside him to strike his mouth.
Then Paul said to him, "God is about to strike you, whitewashed wall; and you sit judging me according to the law, and transgressing the law you order me to be struck?"
And those standing by said, "Do you revile the high priest of God?"
And Paul said, "I did not know, brothers, that he is high priest; for it has been written that 'A ruler of your people you shall not speak of badly.'"

And Paul, having known that the one part is of Sadducees and the other of Pharisees, was crying out in the council, "Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; concerning hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged."
And when he had said this, there came about a faction of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the multitude was split.
For Sadducees say there is not a resurrection, nor angel nor spirit; but Pharisees confess them both.

And there came about a great outcry, and some of the scribes of the part of the Pharisees, having stood up, were contending fiercely, saying, "We find nothing evil in this man; and if a spirit spoke to him, or an angel — let us not fight against God."

And much faction coming about, the tribune, having feared lest Paul be torn apart by them, ordered the detachment, having gone down, to seize him out of their midst and to bring him into the barracks.
And on the following night the Lord, having stood over him, said, "Take courage, Paul; for as you witnessed thoroughly the things concerning me at Jerusalem, so you must also witness at Rome."
And day having come, the Jews, having made a conspiracy, put themselves under a curse, saying neither to eat nor to drink until they should kill Paul.
And there were more than forty who had made this sworn conspiracy;
who, having come to the chief priests and the elders, said, "With a curse we have cursed ourselves to taste nothing until we kill Paul.

Now therefore do you make it clear to the tribune, with the council, so that he might bring him down to you tomorrow as though about to determine more exactly the things concerning him; and we, before he draws near, are ready to do away with him."
But the son of Paul's sister, having heard of the ambush, having come and having entered into the barracks, reported to Paul.
And Paul, having called to himself one of the centurions, said, "Lead this young man away to the tribune, for he has something to report to him."
So he, having taken him, led him to the tribune and says, "The prisoner Paul, having called me to himself, asked me to bring this young man to you, having something to speak to you."
And the tribune, having taken hold of his hand and having withdrawn privately, was inquiring, "What is it which you have to report to me?"
And he said that "The Jews have agreed to ask you that tomorrow you bring Paul down into the council, as though about to inquire something more exactly concerning him.

Therefore do not be persuaded by them; for more than forty men of them are lying in ambush for him, who put themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they do away with him, and now they are ready, awaiting the promise from you."
So the tribune sent away the young man, having charged him to tell no one that "you disclosed these things to me."

And having called to himself two certain of the centurions, he said, "Prepare two hundred soldiers so that they may journey as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, from the third hour of the night,"
and to provide beasts, so that having mounted Paul they might bring him through safely to Felix the governor.
having written a letter having this form:
Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix, greeting.
This man, having been seized by the Jews and being about to be done away with by them, having come upon them with the detachment, I rescued, having learned that he is a Roman.
And wishing to know thoroughly the cause for which they were accusing him, I brought him down into their council;
whom I found being accused concerning questions of their law, but having no accusation worthy of death or of bonds.
And a plot against the man having been disclosed to me, being about to be, I sent him at once to you, having charged the accusers also to speak the things against him before you. Farewell.
So the soldiers, according to what had been ordered them, having taken up Paul, brought him through the night to Antipatris.
And on the next day, having allowed the horsemen to go away with him, they returned to the barracks;
who, having entered into Caesarea and having handed over the letter to the governor, presented also Paul to him.
And having read it, and having asked from what sort of province he is, and having learned that he is from Cilicia,
"I will hear you thoroughly," he said, "when also your accusers arrive." And having ordered him to be guarded in the praetorium of Herod.

acts_24.t: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator Tertullus, who made a formal statement to the governor against Paul.
And when he had been called, Tertullus began to accuse, saying, "Obtaining much peace through you, and reforms coming about for this nation through your forethought,
in every way and everywhere we welcome it, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
But so that I may not hinder you further, I beg you to hear us briefly in your forbearance.
For having found this man a pestilence and moving factions among all the Jews throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazoreans —
who also attempted to profane the temple, whom also we seized and according to our law we wished to judge.
[But Lysias the tribune, having come along, with much violence led him away out of our hands,]
having ordered his accusers to come to you; from whom you will be able yourself, having examined him, to know thoroughly concerning all these things of which we accuse him."
And the Jews also joined in the attack, asserting these things to be so.
And Paul answered, the governor having nodded to him to speak: "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge to this nation, I defend the things concerning myself with good courage,
you being able to know thoroughly that there are not more than twelve days for me from when I went up to worship in Jerusalem;
and neither in the temple did they find me disputing with anyone or making a gathering of a crowd, nor in the synagogues nor throughout the city;
nor are they able to present to you concerning the things of which they now accuse me.

But I confess this to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the ancestral God, trusting all the things according to the law and the things having been written in the prophets,
having a hope toward God, which these men themselves also await, that there is about to be a resurrection of both just and unjust.
In this I myself also train to have a conscience without stumbling toward God and humans through everything.
And after more years I came, about to make alms to my nation, and offerings.
in which they found me having been purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with an uproar;
but some Jews from Asia, whom it was necessary to be present before you and to accuse, if they should have anything against me.
Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,
than concerning this one voice which I cried out standing among them, that 'Concerning resurrection of the dead I am being judged today before you.'"
And having heard these things, Felix put them off, knowing more exactly the things concerning the Way, having said, "When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will determine the things concerning you."
having ordered the centurion for him to be kept, and to have relief, and to hinder none of his own people from serving him or coming to him.
And after some days, Felix, having arrived with Drusilla his own wife, being a Jewess, sent for Paul and heard him concerning the trust into Christ Jesus.

And as he discoursed concerning righteousness and self-control and the judgment about to be, Felix, having become afraid, answered, "For the present go; and having got an opportunity I will call you back."
At the same time also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul, so that he might loose him; therefore also, sending for him more frequently, he was conversing with him.
And two years having been fulfilled, Felix received a successor, Porcius Festus; and wishing to lay up a favour with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.

acts_25.t: Festus therefore, having set foot in the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea,
and the chief priests and the first men of the Jews made a formal statement to him against Paul, and were urging him,
asking a favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, making an ambush to do away with him along the road.
Festus therefore answered that Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to go out shortly.
"Therefore let those among you," he says, "who are able, having gone down together, accuse him, if there is anything out of place in the man."
And having spent among them not more than eight or ten days, having gone down to Caesarea, on the next day, having sat on the judgment seat, he ordered Paul to be brought.
And when he had arrived, the Jews having come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing down many and weighty charges against Paul, which they were not able to prove,
Paul defending himself: "Neither against the law of the Jews nor against the temple nor against Caesar have I sinned in anything."
But Festus, wishing to lay up a favour with the Jews, answering Paul said, "Are you willing, having gone up to Jerusalem, there to be judged concerning these things before me?"
And Paul said, "I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I must be judged. To Jews I have done no wrong, as you also very well know.

If therefore I am doing wrong and have done anything worthy of death, I do not beg off from dying; but if there is nothing of the things of which these accuse me, no one is able to grant me to them as a favour. I call upon Caesar."
Then Festus, having spoken together with the council, answered, "You have called upon Caesar; to Caesar you will go."
And some days having passed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, having greeted Festus.
And as they were spending more days there, Festus laid before the king the things concerning Paul, saying, "There is a certain man left behind by Felix, a prisoner,
concerning whom, when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews made a formal statement, asking a judgment against him;

to whom I answered that it is not a custom for Romans to grant any human as a favour before the one being accused should have the accusers face to face and receive a place of defence concerning the accusation.
Therefore they having come together here, having made no delay, on the next day, having sat on the judgment seat, I ordered the man to be brought;
concerning whom the accusers, having stood up, were bringing no charge of the evil things which I was suspecting;
but they had certain questions against him concerning their own religion and concerning a certain Jesus who had died, whom Paul was asserting to be alive.
And being at a loss about the inquiry concerning these things, I was saying whether he might be willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these things.
But Paul, having appealed to be kept for the decision of the Augustus, I ordered him to be kept until I might send him up to Caesar."
And Agrippa said to Festus, "I was wishing also myself to hear the man." "Tomorrow," he says, "you will hear him."

Therefore on the next day, Agrippa having come and Bernice, with much display, and having entered into the audience hall together with both the tribunes and the men of eminence of the city, and Festus having given the order, Paul was brought.

And Festus says, "King Agrippa and all the men present with us, you behold this man, concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me both in Jerusalem and here, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
But I myself grasped that he had done nothing worthy of death; and this one himself having appealed to the Augustus, I decided to send him,

concerning whom I have nothing certain to write to the lord; therefore I brought him forward before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that the examination having taken place, I may have something I might write.
For it seems to me unreasonable, sending a prisoner, not also to signify the charges against him."

acts_26.t: And Agrippa said to Paul, "It is permitted to you to speak concerning yourself." Then Paul, having stretched out the hand, was making his defence:
"Concerning all the things of which I am accused by Jews, King Agrippa, I have considered myself blessed, being about today to defend myself before you,
especially you being an expert of all the customs and questions among Jews; therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
Therefore my manner of life from youth, which from the beginning came about among my nation and in Jerusalem, all the Jews know,
knowing me beforehand from the first, if they should be willing to witness, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
And now for hope of the promise having come about by God to our fathers I stand being judged,
to which our twelve-tribe body, serving in earnestness night and day, hopes to arrive; concerning which hope I am accused, Agrippa, by the Jews, O king.
Why is it judged unbelievable among you if God raises dead ones?
I myself therefore thought to myself that it was necessary to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus the Nazorean,

which also I did in Jerusalem, and many of the holy ones I myself shut up in prisons, having received the authority from the chief priests, and when they were being done away with I cast down a pebble.
and throughout all the synagogues, often punishing them, I was compelling them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly enraged at them I was persecuting them even as far as the outside cities.
In which things also, journeying to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
at midday along the road I saw, O king, from heaven, beyond the brightness of the sun, a light shining around me and those journeying with me.
And all of us having fallen down to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me and saying in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.'
And I said, 'Who are you, Lord?' And the Lord said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
But rise up and stand on your feet; for to this end I was seen by you, to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things in which you saw me and of the things in which I will be seen by you,
delivering you from the people and from the nations, to whom I am sending you

to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the authority of Satan to God, that they may receive release of sins and an inheritance among those having been made holy by trust into me.'
Whence, King Agrippa, I did not become disobedient to the heavenly vision,

but to those in Damascus first and also in Jerusalem, and to all the country of Judea, and to the nations, I was announcing to change the mind and to turn to God, doing works worthy of the change of mind.
On account of these things the Jews, having seized me being in the temple, were attempting to lay hands on me.

Having therefore obtained the help from God, until this day I stand witnessing to both small and great, saying nothing outside of the things which both the prophets said were about to come about, and Moses,
if the Christ is subject to suffering, if first from resurrection of the dead he is about to proclaim light both to the people and to the nations."
And as he was defending these things, Festus says with a great voice, "You are raving, Paul; the many letters are turning you around into madness."
But Paul, "I am not raving," he says, "most excellent Festus, but I utter words of truth and sound-mindedness.

For the king understands concerning these things, to whom also, speaking boldly, I speak; for I am not persuaded that any of these things escapes him, none of it; for this has not been done in a corner.
Do you trust the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you trust."
And Agrippa said to Paul, "In little you persuade me to make a Christian."
And Paul said, "I would pray to God, both in little and in great, not only you but also all those hearing me today to become such as I also am, apart from these bonds."
And when he had said these things, the king stood up and the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them,
and having withdrawn they were speaking to one another, saying that "This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds."
And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man was able to have been released, if he had not called upon Caesar."

acts_27.t: And when it was decided for us to sail away to Italy, they were handing over both Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
And having embarked on a ship of Adramyttium, being about to sail to the places along Asia, we put out to sea, Aristarchus a Macedonian, a Thessalonian, being with us.
And on the next day we put in at Sidon, and Julius, having treated Paul humanely, permitted him, having gone to the friends, to obtain care.
And having put out from there, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary,
and having sailed across the open sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came down to Myra of Lycia.
And there the centurion, having found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy, put us into it.
And in a considerable number of days sailing slowly and with difficulty having come off Cnidus, the wind not permitting us further, we sailed under Crete off Salmone,
and with difficulty coasting along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was a city, Lasea.
And considerable time having passed, and the voyage being already unsafe because the Fast also had already gone by, Paul was advising,
saying to them, "Men, I perceive that with violence and much loss, not only of the cargo and of the ship but also of our souls, the voyage is about to be."
But the centurion was persuaded more by the helmsman and the shipmaster than by the things being said by Paul.

And the harbour being unsuitable for wintering, the greater number set a plan to put out from there, if somehow they might be able, having arrived at Phoenix, to winter — a harbour of Crete looking down the southwest wind and down the northwest wind.
And a south wind having blown gently, having supposed that they had got hold of their purpose, having weighed anchor they were coasting along Crete closer in.
But after not much, there beat down from it a typhonic wind, the one called Euraquilo.
And the ship having been seized and not being able to look the wind in the eye, having given way we were being carried along.
And having run under a certain small island called Cauda, we were with difficulty able to become masters of the ship's boat,
which having hoisted up, they were using supports, undergirding the ship; and fearing lest they fall onto the Syrtis, having lowered the gear, so they were being carried along.
And we being violently storm-tossed, on the next day they were making a jettison;
and on the third day with their own hands they threw off the ship's tackle.
And neither sun nor stars appearing over more days, and no small storm lying upon us, from then on all hope of our being saved was being taken away.

And much abstinence from food being present, then Paul, having stood in their midst, said, "It was necessary indeed, O men, having obeyed me, not to put out to sea from Crete, and to have gained this violence and loss.
And now I advise you to be of good cheer; for there will be no loss of soul from among you, except of the ship.
For there stood beside me this night an angel of the God whose I am, whom also I serve,
saying, 'Do not fear, Paul; you must stand before Caesar, and behold, God has granted to you all those sailing with you.'
Therefore be of good cheer, men; for I trust God that so it will be according to the manner in which it has been spoken to me.
But onto a certain island we must fall."
And when the fourteenth night came, we being carried across in the Adriatic, about the middle of the night the sailors were suspecting that some land was drawing near to them.
And having sounded they found twenty fathoms; and having stood off a little and having sounded again, they found fifteen fathoms.
And fearing lest somewhere we should fall on rough places, having thrown four anchors from the stern, they were praying for day to come.
And the sailors seeking to flee from the ship and having lowered the ship's boat into the sea, with the pretext as though about to lay out anchors from the prow,
Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, "Unless these remain in the ship, you are not able to be saved."
Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the ship's boat and let it fall away.
And until day was about to come about, Paul was urging them all to partake of food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day you continue waiting, without food, having taken on nothing.
Therefore I urge you to partake of food; for this is for your salvation; for not a hair from the head of any of you will perish."
And having said these things and having taken bread, he gave thanks to God before all, and having broken it he began to eat.
And all having become cheerful, they themselves also took food.
And we were, all the souls in the ship, two hundred and seventy-six.
And having been satisfied with food, they were lightening the ship, throwing out the grain into the sea.
And when day came, they were not recognising the land, but they were observing a certain bay having a beach, onto which they were deliberating, if they were able, to drive out the ship.

And having cut away the anchors, they were letting them go into the sea, at the same time having loosened the bindings of the steering-oars, and having hoisted the foresail to the blowing wind, they were holding course for the beach.
But having fallen upon a place between two seas, they ran the ship aground; and the prow, having stuck fast, remained unmoved, but the stern was being broken up by the violence of the waves.
And of the soldiers a plan came about that they should kill the prisoners, lest any, having swum out, should escape.
But the centurion, wishing to bring Paul through safely, prevented them from the plan, and ordered those able to swim, having thrown themselves off, to go out first onto the land,
and the rest, some on planks and some on some of the things from the ship. And so it came about that all were brought safely through onto the land.

acts_28.t: And having been brought safely through, then we recognised that the island is called Malta.
And the barbarians were showing us no ordinary humanity; for having kindled a fire they welcomed us all, because of the rain that had set in and because of the cold.
And Paul having gathered together a certain quantity of sticks and having put them on the fire, a viper, having come out from the heat, fastened on his hand.

And as the barbarians saw the beast hanging from his hand, they were saying to one another, "Certainly this man is a murderer, whom, having been brought safely through from the sea, Justice did not permit to live."
So he, having shaken off the beast into the fire, suffered nothing bad.

But they were expecting him to be about to swell up or suddenly to fall down dead; but over much time, while they were expecting and observing nothing out of place coming about in him, having changed their minds they were saying him to be a god.
And in the parts about that place there were lands belonging to the first man of the island, named Publius, who, having received us, lodged us in a friendly way three days.
And it came about that the father of Publius was lying down, held by fevers and dysentery, to whom Paul, having entered and having prayed, having laid the hands on him, healed him.
And this having come about, also the rest, those in the island having weaknesses, were coming and were being healed.
who also honoured us with many honours, and, as we were putting out to sea, they put on board the things for our needs.
And after three months we put out to sea in a ship having wintered at the island, an Alexandrian, marked with the Dioscuri.
And having put in at Syracuse, we remained three days,
from where, having cast off, we arrived at Rhegium; and after one day a south wind having come up, on the second day we came to Puteoli,
where, having found brothers, we were urged to remain with them seven days; and so we came to Rome.

And from there the brothers, having heard the things concerning us, came for a meeting with us as far as Appius's Forum and Three Taverns, whom having seen, Paul, having given thanks to God, took courage.
And when we entered into Rome, the centurion handed over the prisoners to the camp commander; but to Paul it was permitted to remain by himself with the soldier guarding him.

And it came about after three days that he called together those being the first men of the Jews; and they having come together, he was saying to them, "I, men, brothers, having done nothing contrary to the people or to the ancestral customs, was handed over a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
who, having examined me, were wishing to release me, because of there being no cause of death in me.
But the Jews speaking against it, I was compelled to call upon Caesar, not as having anything of which to accuse my nation.
For this cause therefore I called for you, to see and to speak with you; for on account of the hope of Israel I have this chain lying around me."
And they said to him, "We neither received letters concerning you from Judea, nor did any of the brothers, having arrived, report or speak anything evil concerning you.
But we think it right to hear from you what things you think; for concerning this sect it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against."

And having appointed a day for him, more of them came to him at the lodging, to whom he was setting it out, witnessing thoroughly to the kingdom of God and persuading them the things concerning Jesus, from both the law of Moses and the prophets, from morning until evening.
And some were being persuaded by the things being said, but others were disbelieving.
And being in disagreement with one another they were being dismissed, Paul having said one word, that "Rightly did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
saying, 'Go to this people and say: With hearing you will hear and by no means understand, and looking you will look and by no means see.

For the heart of this people was thickened, and with the ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they closed; lest they should see with the eyes and hear with the ears and understand with the heart and turn about, and I will heal them.'
Therefore let it be known to you that to the nations this salvation of God was sent; they also will hear."
[And he having said these things, the Jews went away, having much disputation among themselves.]
And he remained two whole years in his own hired dwelling, and was welcoming all those coming in to him,
proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, unhinderedly.

colossians_1.t: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through will of God, and Timothy the brother,
to the in Colossae holy ones and faithful brothers in Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ always praying about you,
having heard of your trust in Christ Jesus and the love which you have toward all the holy ones,
because of the hope laid away for you in the heavens, which you heard beforehand in the word of the truth of the good news,
the one being present to you, just as also in all the world, and it is bearing fruit and growing, just as also among you, from which day you heard and fully knew the grace of God in truth;
just as you learned from Epaphras our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful servant of the Christ on your behalf,
the one also having made clear to us your love in spirit.
Because of this we also, from which day we heard, do not cease praying on your behalf and asking that you may be filled with the full knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
for you to walk worthily of the Lord for all pleasing, in every good work bearing fruit and growing in the full knowledge of God,
in all power being empowered according to the might of his glory for all endurance and long-suffering; with joy
giving thanks to the Father, the one having made you sufficient for the share of the lot of the holy ones in the light,
who rescued us out of the authority of the darkness and transferred into the kingdom of the son of his love,
in whom we have the redemption, the release of the sins;
who is image of the invisible God, firstborn of all creation;

because in him were created all things, the ones in the heavens and the ones on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; the all things through him and for him have been created;
And he is before all things, and the all things in him have held together.
And he is the head of the body, of the assembly, who is the beginning, firstborn out of the dead ones, so that he might become in all things himself holding first place;
because in him was pleased all the fullness to dwell,
and through him to reconcile the all things to him, having made peace through the blood of his cross, through him whether the things upon the earth or the things in the heavens;
And you once being alienated and enemies in the mind in the evil works,
but now he reconciled in the body of his flesh through the death, to present you holy and unblemished and unaccusable before him —

if indeed you remain on in the trust, having been founded and settled and not being moved away from the hope of the good news which you heard, the one having been proclaimed in all the creation under the heaven, of which I, Paul, became a servant.
Now I rejoice in the sufferings on your behalf, and I fill up in turn the lacks of the afflictions of the Christ in my flesh on behalf of his body, which is the assembly,
of which I became a servant according to the stewardship of God, the one given to me toward you, to fill up the word of God,
the mystery the one having been hidden from the ages and from the generations, but now it was manifested to his holy ones,
to whom God willed to make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the nations, which is Christ in you, the hope of the glory;
whom we announce, admonishing every human and teaching every human in all wisdom, so that we may present every human complete in Christ Jesus,
for which also I labour, contending according to his working, the one working in me in power.

colossians_2.t: For I want you to know how great a contest I have on behalf of you and the ones in Laodicea and as many as have not seen my face in flesh,

so that their hearts may be encouraged, having been joined together in love and to all the riches of the full assurance of the understanding, to full knowledge of the mystery of God and Father and of the Christ,
in whom are all the treasures of the wisdom and the knowledge hidden;
And this I say so that no one may reason you aside in plausible speech;
For if also in the flesh I am absent, yet in the spirit I am with you, rejoicing and seeing your order and the firmness of your trust toward Christ.
As therefore you received the Christ Jesus the Lord, in him walk,
having been rooted and being built up in him and being confirmed in the trust just as you were taught, abounding in it in thanksgiving.

Look, lest anyone will be the one carrying you off as spoil through the philosophy and empty deceit according to the tradition of the humans, according to the elements of the world and not according to Christ;
because in him dwells all the fullness of the deity bodily,
and you are in him having been filled, who is the head of every rule and authority;
in whom also you were circumcised with a circumcision not hand-made in the stripping-off of the body of the sins of the flesh, in the circumcision of the Christ,
having been buried together with him in the baptism, in which also you were raised together through the trust of the working of God, the one having raised him out of the dead ones.
And you being dead in the trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive together with him, having graciously forgiven us all the trespasses;
having wiped out the against-us handwriting in the decrees, which was contrary to us, and he has taken it out of the midst, having nailed it to the cross;
having stripped off the rulers and the authorities, he exposed them in boldness, having triumphed over them in him.
Therefore let no one judge you in eating and in drinking or in respect of a festival or of a new moon or of sabbaths,
which things are a shadow of the coming things, but the body of the Christ.
Let no one disqualify you, willing in lowliness of mind and worship of the angels, entering into what he has seen, being vainly puffed up by the mind of his flesh,
and not holding the head, out of whom all the body through the joints and bonds being supplied and being joined together grows the growth of God.
If you died with the Christ from the elements of the world, why as living in a world are you being decreed at —
do not handle, nor taste, nor touch —
which things are all for decay in the using up, according to the commandments and teachings of the humans;
which things are having indeed a word of wisdom in self-chosen worship and lowliness of mind and unsparingness of body, not in any honour toward satisfaction of the flesh.

colossians_3.t: If therefore you were raised together with the Christ, seek the things above, where the Christ is, at God's right hand seated;
Think the things above, not the things upon the earth.
For you died, and your life has been hidden together with the Christ in God;
Whenever the Christ may be manifested, your life, then also you together with him will be manifested in glory.
Put to death therefore your members the ones upon the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, passion, evil desire, and the greed which is idolatry,
because of which things comes the wrath of God upon the sons of the disobedience;
in which also you once walked, when you were living in these things.
But now put away also you the all things: wrath, anger, badness, blasphemy, shameful speech out of your mouth.
Do not lie to one another, having stripped off the old human with its practices
and having put on the new, the one being renewed to full knowledge according to image of the one having created it;
where there is not Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free, but the all things and in all Christ.
Put on therefore, as chosen of God holy and having been loved, inward parts of compassion, kindness, lowliness of mind, meekness, long-suffering,
bearing with one another and graciously forgiving yourselves, if anyone toward anyone has a complaint; just as also the Lord graciously forgave you, thus also you;
And upon all these things, the love, which is a bond of the completeness.
And let the peace of the Christ arbitrate in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and become thankful.
Let the word of the Christ dwell in you richly, in all wisdom teaching and admonishing yourselves with psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, in the grace singing in your hearts to God;
And everything whatever you may do in word or in work, all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to the God and Father through him.
The wives, be subject to your own husbands, as was fitting in the Lord.
The husbands, love the wives and do not be embittered toward them.
The children, obey the parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing in the Lord.
The fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they may not become disheartened.
The slaves, obey in all things the according-to-flesh masters, not in eye-service as human-pleasers but in singleness of heart, fearing the Lord.
And everything whatever you may do, work from soul as to the Lord and not to humans,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive back the repayment of the inheritance; for the Lord Christ you slave for.
For the one doing wrong will receive back what he did wrong, and there is no receiving-of-faces.

colossians_4.t: The masters, provide to the slaves the just thing and the fairness, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.
To the prayer be devoted, keeping awake in it in thanksgiving,
praying at the same time also about us, that God may open to us a door of the word, to speak the mystery of the Christ, because of which also I have been bound,
so that I may manifest it as it is necessary for me to speak.
In wisdom walk toward the ones outside, buying out the season.
Your word always in grace, having been seasoned with salt, to know how it is necessary for you to answer each one.
All the things concerning me Tychicus will make known to you, the beloved brother and faithful servant and fellow slave in the Lord,
whom I sent to you for this very thing, so that you may know the things about us and he may encourage your hearts,
with Onesimus the faithful and beloved brother, who is out of you; all the things here they will make known to you.
Aristarchus my fellow prisoner-of-war greets you, and Mark the cousin of Barnabas, about whom you received commands — if he comes to you, receive him —
and Jesus the one called Justus — the ones being of circumcision, these only co-workers for the kingdom of God, who became to me a consolation.

Epaphras greets you, the one out of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, always contending on your behalf in the prayers, so that you may stand complete and having been fully assured in all the will of God.
For I witness for him that he has much toil on behalf of you and the ones in Laodicea and the ones in Hierapolis.
Luke the physician the beloved greets you, and Demas.
Greet the brothers in Laodicea and Nympha and the assembly according to her house.
And whenever the letter may be read among you, do so that also in the assembly of Laodiceans it may be read, and the one out of Laodicea, that you also may read.
And say to Archippus: look at the service which you received in the Lord, so that you may fulfil it.
The greeting by my hand, of Paul. Remember my chains. The grace with you. Amen. [To Colossians it was written from Rome through Tychicus and Onesimus.]

ephesians_1.t: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the holy ones being [in Ephesus] and faithful in Christ Jesus:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the one having blessed us in every spiritual blessing in the heavenlies in Christ,
just as he chose us in him before the founding of the world, for us to be holy and unblemished before him in love,
having marked out beforehand us for placement as a son through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,
into praise of glory of his grace, in which he graced us in the beloved one,
in whom we have the redemption through his blood, the release of the trespasses, according to the wealth of his grace,
which he made abound toward us in all wisdom and insight,
having made known to us the mystery of his will according to his good pleasure which he purposed in him,
into a stewardship of the fullness of the times, to head up all things in the Christ, the things upon the heavens and the things upon the earth, in him,
in whom also we were allotted, having been marked out beforehand according to purpose of the one working all things according to the counsel of his will,
for us to be into praise of his glory, the ones having hoped beforehand in the Christ;
in whom also you, having heard the word of the truth, the good news of your salvation, in whom also having trusted you were sealed with the Spirit of the promise, the holy one,
which is a deposit of our inheritance, into redemption of the acquisition, into praise of his glory.
Because of this I also, having heard of the trust among you in the Lord Jesus and the love toward all the holy ones,
do not cease giving thanks on behalf of you, making mention of you at my prayers,
so that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of the glory, might give to you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in full knowledge of him,
the eyes of your heart having been enlightened, for you to know what is the hope of his calling, what the wealth of the glory of his inheritance in the holy ones,
and what the surpassing greatness of his power toward us the ones trusting, according to the working of the strength of his might,
which he worked in the Christ, having raised him out of the dead ones and having seated him at his right in the heavenlies,
above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name being named, not only in this age but also in the coming one,
and all things he subjected under his feet and him he gave as head over all things to the assembly,
which is his body, the fullness of the one filling the all things in all.

ephesians_2.t: And you, being dead in the trespasses and your sins,
in which once you walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit now working in the sons of the disobedience,
among whom also we all were conducted once in the desires of our flesh, doing the wants of the flesh and of the thoughts, and we were children by nature of wrath as also the rest.
But God, being rich in mercy, because of his much love with which he loved us,
and us being dead in the trespasses he made alive together with the Christ — by grace you are having been saved —
and raised together and seated together in the heavenlies in Christ Jesus,
so that he might show forth in the ages coming on the surpassing wealth of his grace in kindness upon us in Christ Jesus.
For by the grace you are having been saved through the trust, and this not out of you, of God the gift,
not out of works, so that no one may boast.
For of him we are a making, created in Christ Jesus upon good works, which God prepared beforehand so that in them we might walk.
Therefore remember that once you the nations in flesh, the ones called uncircumcision by the one called circumcision in flesh made by hand,
that you were in that season apart from Christ, having been alienated from the citizenship of Israel and strangers of the covenants of the promise, not having hope and godless in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus you the ones once being far off became near in the blood of the Christ.
For he is our peace, the one having made the both one and having loosed the middle wall of the fence, the hostility, in his flesh,
the law of the commandments in decrees having nullified, so that the two he might create in himself into one new human, making peace,
and might reconcile the both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility in him.
And having come he proclaimed peace as good news to you the ones far off and peace to the ones near;
because through him we have the access, the both, in one spirit toward the Father.
So then no longer are you strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens of the holy ones and household members of God,
having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, being himself extreme-corner, Christ Jesus,
in whom all the building being fitted together grows into a holy shrine in the Lord,
