in whom also you are being built together into a dwelling of God in spirit.

ephesians_3.t: For the sake of this I Paul, the prisoner of the Christ Jesus on behalf of you the nations —
if indeed you heard of the stewardship of the grace of God given to me for you,
that according to revelation was made known to me the mystery, just as I wrote beforehand in brief,
toward which you are able, reading, to understand my insight in the mystery of the Christ,
which in other generations was not made known to the sons of the humans as now it was revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in spirit,
the nations to be joint-heirs and joint-bodied and joint-sharers of his promise in Christ Jesus through the good news,
of which I became a servant according to the gift of the grace of God given to me according to the working of his power.
To me the leaster of all the holy ones was given this grace, among the nations to proclaim as good news the untrackable wealth of the Christ,
and to enlighten all what is the stewardship of the mystery having been hidden from the ages in God the one having created all things,
so that might be made known now to the rules and to the authorities in the heavenlies through the assembly the many-coloured wisdom of God,
according to a purpose of the ages which he made in the Christ Jesus our Lord,
in whom we have the boldness and the access in confidence through the faith in him.
Therefore I ask not to lose heart in my afflictions on behalf of you, which is your glory.
For the sake of this I bend my knees toward the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
out of whom every fatherhood in heavens and upon earth is named,
so that he might give to you according to the wealth of his glory with power to be strengthened through his spirit into the inner human,
for the Christ to dwell through the trust in your hearts, in love having been rooted and having been founded,
so that you might be fully able to grasp together with all the holy ones what the breadth and length and height and depth,
and to know the surpassing-of-knowledge love of the Christ, so that you might be filled into all the fullness of God.
But to the one being able above all things to do beyond-out-of-abundantly what we ask or think according to the power working in us,
to him the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus into all the generations of the age of the ages, amen.

ephesians_4.t: I exhort therefore you, I the prisoner in the Lord, worthily to walk of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness of mind and gentleness, with long-suffering, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the oneness of the spirit in the bond of the peace.
One body and one spirit, just as also you were called in one hope of your calling;
one Lord, one trust, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, the one over all and through all and in all of you.
But to one each of us was given the grace according to the measure of the gift of the Christ.
Therefore it says: 'Having ascended into height he captured captivity, he gave gifts to the humans.'
But the 'he ascended', what is it except that also he descended into the lower parts of the earth?
The one having descended, he himself is also the one having ascended above all the heavens, so that he might fill the all things.
And he himself gave the ones apostles, and the ones prophets, and the ones proclaimers of good news, and the ones shepherds and teachers,
toward the fitting-out of the holy ones into work of service, into building up of the body of the Christ,
until we all attain into the oneness of the trust and of the full knowledge of the Son of God, into a complete man, into a measure of stature of the fullness of the Christ,
so that we may be no longer infants, being wave-tossed and carried around by every wind of the teaching in the dice-play of the humans, in craftiness toward the scheming of the deceit,
but truthing in love let us grow into him the all things, who is the head, the Christ,

out of whom all the body being fitted together and being joined together through every joint of the supply according to working in measure of one each part the growth of the body makes toward building up of itself in love.
This therefore I say and witness in the Lord, no longer for you to walk just as also the rest of the nations walk in futility of their mind,
having been darkened in the understanding, having been alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance being in them, because of the hardening of their heart,
who having become past-feeling gave themselves over to the licentiousness, into a working of all uncleanness in greediness.
But you not thus learned the Christ,
if indeed him you heard and in him you were taught, just as truth is in the Jesus,
for you to put off according to the former conduct the old human, the one being corrupted according to the desires of the deceit,
and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
and to put on the new human, the one according to God having been created in righteousness and holiness of the truth.
Therefore having put off the lie speak truth each with his neighbour, because we are of one another members.
Be angry and do not sin; the sun let it not set upon your provocation,
nor give a place to the devil.
The one stealing let him steal no longer, but rather let him labour working with his own hands the good, so that he may have to share with the one having need.
Every rotten word out of your mouth let it not go forth, but if any good toward building up of the need, so that it might give grace to the ones hearing.
And do not grieve the Spirit the holy of God, in whom you were sealed into a day of redemption.
All bitterness and rage and anger and clamour and blasphemy let it be removed from you with all malice.
But become toward one another kind, tender-hearted, graciously forgiving yourselves, just as also God in Christ graciously forgave you.

ephesians_5.t: Become therefore imitators of God as beloved children,
and walk in love just as also the Christ loved us and gave himself over on behalf of us, an offering and sacrifice to God into an odour of sweet smell.
But sexual immorality and all uncleanness or greediness let it not even be named among you, just as is fitting for holy ones;
and shamefulness and foolish talk or coarse wit, which were not fitting, but rather thanksgiving.
For this know, knowing, that every sexually immoral one or unclean one or greedy one, who is an idolater, does not have an inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and of God.
Let no one you deceive with empty words; for because of these things comes the wrath of God upon the sons of the disobedience.
Do not therefore become joint-sharers with them.
For you were once darkness, but now light in the Lord; as children of light walk,
for the fruit of the light in all goodness and righteousness and truth,
testing what is well-pleasing to the Lord.
And do not share together in the works the unfruitful ones of the darkness, but rather even expose them,
For the things being done in secret by them it is shameful even to speak of.
But all the things being exposed by the light are made manifest,
for everything being manifested is light. Therefore it says: 'Rise, the one sleeping, and stand up out of the dead ones, and the Christ will shine upon you.'
See therefore carefully how you walk, not as unwise but as wise,
buying out the season, because the days are evil.
Because of this do not become senseless, but understand what the will of the Lord.
And do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissoluteness, but be filled in spirit,
speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and playing in your heart to the Lord,
giving thanks always on behalf of all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to the God and Father,
submitting yourselves to one another in fear of Christ.
The wives, to their own husbands [submit] as to the Lord,
because a man is head of the woman as also the Christ is head of the assembly, he himself being saviour of the body.
But as the assembly submits itself to the Christ, so also the wives to their own husbands in everything.
The men, love your own women just as also the Christ loved the assembly and gave himself over on behalf of her,
so that her he might make holy, having cleansed by the washing of the water in a word,
so that he might present to himself glorious the assembly, not having spot or wrinkle or any of such things, but so that she might be holy and unblemished.
Thus ought also the men to love their own women as their own bodies. The one loving his own woman loves himself.
for no one ever his own flesh hated, but nourishes and warms it, just as also the Christ the assembly,
because members we are of his body, [out of his flesh and out of his bones].
'Because of this a human will leave his father and the mother and will be joined toward his woman, and the two will be into one flesh.'
This mystery is great; but I speak toward Christ and toward the assembly.
Nevertheless also you the ones according to one, each his own woman so let him love as himself, and the woman that she may fear the husband.

ephesians_6.t: The children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is righteous.
'Honour your father and the mother', which is a first commandment in promise,
'so that well for you it may be and you will be long-lived upon the earth.'
And the fathers, do not provoke to anger your children, but nourish them in discipline and admonition of the Lord.
The slaves, obey the according-to-flesh masters with fear and trembling in singleness of your heart as to the Christ,
not according to eye-slavery as human-pleasers but as servants of Christ doing the will of God out of soul,
with goodwill serving as slaves as to the Lord and not to humans,
knowing that each whatever good he may do, this he will receive from the Lord, whether slave or free.
And the masters, the same things do toward them, giving up the threat, knowing that also of them and of you the Master is in heavens, and partiality is not with him.
For the rest, my brothers, be empowered in the Lord and in the strength of his might.
Put on the full-armour of God for you to be able to stand against the schemings of the devil;

because the wrestling is not to us against blood and flesh but against the rules, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of the darkness of this age, against the spiritual things of the evil in the heavenlies.
Because of this take up the full-armour of God, so that you may be able to withstand in the evil day and, having worked out all things, to stand.
Stand therefore, having girded your loin in truth and having put on the breastplate of the righteousness,
and having shod the feet in readiness of the good news of the peace,
in all things having taken up the large-shield of the trust, in which you will be able all the arrows of the evil one, the ones having been set on fire, to quench;
and the helmet of the salvation receive, and the sword of the spirit, which is a spoken word of God,
through every prayer and petition praying in every season in spirit, and unto this same thing keeping awake in all perseverance and petition concerning all the holy ones,
and on behalf of me, so that to me may be given a word in an opening of my mouth in boldness to make known the mystery of the good news,
on behalf of which I am an ambassador in a chain, so that in it I may speak boldly as it is necessary for me to speak.
But so that you also may know the things concerning me, what I am doing, all things will make known to you Tychicus the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord,
whom I sent to you unto this same thing, so that you might know the things concerning us and he might encourage your hearts.
Peace to the brothers and love with trust from God the Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
The grace with all the ones loving our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption. Amen. [Written to the Ephesians from Rome, through Tychicus.]

galatians_1.t: Paul, apostle not from humans nor through a human but through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from dead ones,
and all the brothers with me, to the assemblies of Galatia:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ,
the one having given himself on behalf of our sins, so that he might take us out from the present evil age according to the will of our God and Father,
to whom the glory into the ages of the ages, amen.
I marvel that so quickly you are being shifted away from the one having called you in Christ's grace into a different good news —
which is not another, except that there are some troubling you and wanting to turn about the good news of Christ.
But even if we or a messenger out of heaven should proclaim good news to you contrary to what we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.
As we have said before, and now again I say, if anyone proclaims good news to you contrary to what you received, let him be accursed.
For now am I persuading humans or God? Or am I seeking to please humans? If I were still pleasing humans, I would not be Christ's servant.
For I make known to you, brothers and sisters, the good news proclaimed by me, that it is not according to a human;
for neither did I receive it from a human nor was I taught it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
For you heard of my former conduct once in Judaism, that beyond measure I was persecuting the assembly of God and was ravaging it,
and I was advancing in Judaism beyond many contemporaries in my race, being more exceedingly a zealot of my ancestral traditions.
But when God, the one having set me apart from my mother's womb and having called through his grace, was pleased
to reveal his Son in me, so that I might proclaim him as good news among the nations, immediately I did not consult with flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia and again returned to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas, and I remained with him fifteen days.
But another of the apostles I did not see, except James the brother of the Lord.
Now what I write to you, look, before God, that I do not lie.
Then I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia,
and I was being unknown by face to the assemblies of Judea, the ones in Christ,
but only hearing they were, that 'the one persecuting us formerly now proclaims as good news the faith which he formerly ravaged,'
and they were glorifying God in me.

galatians_2.t: Then through fourteen years again I went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking along also Titus;

But I went up according to a revelation and I laid before them the good news which I proclaim among the nations, but privately to the ones seeming to be, lest somehow I am running or ran into emptiness.
But neither Titus the one with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised;
But because of the smuggled-in false brothers, who came in alongside to spy out our freedom which we have in Christ Jesus, so that they will enslave us —
to whom not even for an hour did we yield in submission, so that the truth of the good news might remain with you.
But from the ones seeming to be something — whatever sort they once were makes no difference to me; God does not receive a human's face — for to me the ones seeming added nothing.
but on the contrary, having seen that I have been entrusted with the good news of the uncircumcision just as Peter of the circumcision,
for the one having worked in Peter for apostleship of the circumcision worked also in me for the nations,

and having known the grace given to me, James and Cephas and John, the ones seeming to be pillars, gave right hands of fellowship to me and Barnabas, so that we to the nations, but they to the circumcision,
only that we should remember the poor, which very thing I was eager to do.
But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to the face, because he was condemned.
For before the coming of certain ones from James he was eating with the nations; but when they came, he was withdrawing and separating himself, fearing the ones out of circumcision;
and the rest of the Jews also joined in hypocrisy with him, so that even Barnabas was led away with them by their hypocrisy.

But when I saw that they are not walking straight toward the truth of the good news, I said to Cephas before all: 'If you, being a Jew, live gentile-wise and not Jewish-wise, how do you compel the nations to judaise?'
We by nature Jews and not out of the nations sinners —

but knowing that a human is not justified out of works of law except through faith in Jesus Christ, we also trusted into Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified out of faith in Christ and not out of works of law, because out of works of law all flesh will not be justified.
But if, seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were found also sinners, then is Christ a servant of sin? Let it not be!
For if what I tore down, these things again I build, I present myself a transgressor;
For I through law to law died, so that to God I might live. With Christ I have been crucified;
and I live no longer, but Christ lives in me; and what I now live in flesh, I live in the faith in the Son of God, the one having loved me and having given himself over for me.
I do not set aside the grace of God; for if through law righteousness, then Christ died for nothing.

galatians_3.t: O senseless Galatians, who bewitched you not to be persuaded by the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was written up beforehand as crucified?
This only I want to learn from you: out of works of law did you receive the Spirit, or out of hearing of trust?
Are you so senseless? Having begun in spirit, now in flesh are you being completed?
So much you suffered in vain? If indeed also in vain.
So the one supplying to you the Spirit and working powers among you — out of works of law, or out of hearing of trust?
Just as Abraham trusted God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness.
Know then that the ones out of trust, these are sons of Abraham.
And the Scripture, having foreseen that out of trust God justifies the nations, proclaimed good news beforehand to Abraham: 'All the nations will be blessed in you.'
So that the ones out of trust are blessed together with the trusting Abraham.
For as many as are out of works of law are under a curse; for it is written that 'Cursed is everyone who does not remain in all the things written in the book of the law, to do them.'
And that in law no one is justified before God is clear, because 'the righteous out of trust will live.'
But the law is not out of trust, but 'the one having done them, the human, will live in them.'
Christ redeemed us out of the curse of the law, having become on our behalf a curse, because it is written: 'Cursed is everyone hanging on wood',
so that into the nations the blessing of Abraham might come in Christ Jesus, so that the promise of the Spirit we might receive through the trust.
Brothers and sisters, according to a human I speak: even so, a human covenant having been ratified no one sets aside or adds provisions to.
But to Abraham were spoken the promises and to his seed. It does not say 'and to the seeds' as upon many, but as upon one, 'and to your seed', who is Christ.
But this I say: a covenant previously ratified by God [toward Christ], the law having come after four hundred and thirty years does not invalidate, so as to nullify the promise.
For if out of law the inheritance, no longer out of promise; but to Abraham through promise God has given it freely.
What then the law? Because of the transgressions it was added, until the seed should come to whom it has been promised, having been ordained through messengers in a mediator's hand.
But the mediator is not of one, but God is one.
Is then the law against the promises of God? Let it not be! For if a law had been given able to make alive, truly out of law would have been the righteousness;
But the Scripture shut up all things under sin, so that the promise out of faith in Jesus Christ might be given to the ones trusting.
But before the coming of the trust, under law we were being guarded, being shut up toward the trust about to be revealed.
So that the law has become our child-minder toward Christ, so that out of trust we might be justified.
But the trust having come, no longer under a child-minder are we.
For all of you are sons of God through the trust in Christ Jesus.
For as many as into Christ were baptised, Christ you put on.
There is not Jew nor Greek, there is not slave nor free, there is not male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
And if you of Christ, then of Abraham seed you are, and according to promise heirs.

galatians_4.t: But I say, for as long a time as the heir is an infant, he differs nothing from a slave, being lord of all;
but he is under guardians and household managers until the appointed day of the father.
So also we, when we were infants, under the elements of the world we were having been enslaved;
But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, having become out of a woman, having become under law,
so that those under law he might redeem, so that the placement as a son we might receive.
And because you are sons, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying 'Abba, the Father.'
So that no longer are you a slave but a son; and if a son, also an heir through God.
But then indeed, not knowing God, you served as slaves to the ones by nature not being gods;
but now, having known God, or rather having been known by God, how do you turn back again to the weak and poor elements, to which again from the start you want to serve as slaves?
Days you observe closely, and months and seasons and years.
I fear for you, lest somehow in vain I have laboured for you.
Become as I, because I also as you. Brothers and sisters, I beg you: nothing me you wronged.
But you know that through weakness of the flesh I proclaimed good news to you the former time,
and the trial of you in my flesh you did not despise nor spit out, but as a messenger of God you received me, as Christ Jesus.
Where then was your blessedness? For I witness to you that, if possible, your eyes having gouged out you would have given to me.
So have I become your enemy telling you truth?
They are zealous for you not well, but to shut you out they want, so that for them you may be zealous.
But it is good to be zealously sought in good always, and not only in my being present with you,
my children, whom again I am in labour with until Christ should be formed in you,
But I was wishing to be present with you now and to change my voice, because I am perplexed in you.
Tell me, the ones wanting to be under law, the law do you not hear?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one out of the slave girl and one out of the free woman.
But the one out of the slave girl according to flesh has been born, and the one out of the free woman through the promise.
Which things are being allegorised; for these are two covenants, one indeed from Mount Sinai, into slavery bearing, which is Hagar.
But the Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and it corresponds to the now Jerusalem, for she serves as a slave with her children.
But the above Jerusalem is free, who is mother of us all.
For it is written: 'Be glad, barren one not bearing; break forth and cry out, the one not in labour, because many are the children of the desolate more than of the one having the husband.'
But you, brothers and sisters, according to Isaac are children of promise.
But just as then the one having been born according to flesh was persecuting the one according to spirit, so also now.
But what says the Scripture? 'Cast out the slave girl and her son, for by no means will the son of the slave girl inherit with the son of the free woman.'
Therefore, brothers and sisters, we are not children of a slave girl but of the free woman.

galatians_5.t: For the freedom Christ freed us; stand then and do not again in a yoke of slavery be held.
See, I Paul say to you that if you be circumcised, Christ will benefit you nothing.
And I testify again to every human being circumcised that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
You were nullified away from Christ, whoever in law are being justified; out of the grace you fell.
For we by spirit out of trust the hope of righteousness eagerly await.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision has any strength nor uncircumcision, but trust through love working.
You were running well; who hindered you not to be persuaded by the truth?
The persuasion is not out of the one calling you.
A little leaven leavens the whole lump.
I have been persuaded toward you in the Lord that nothing other you will think; but the one troubling you will bear the judgement, whoever he may be.
But I, brothers and sisters, if circumcision still I proclaim, why still am I persecuted? Then the stumbling-block of the cross has been nullified.
Would that they will even cut themselves off, the ones upsetting you.
For you were called upon freedom, brothers and sisters; only not the freedom into an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another as slaves.
For the whole law in one word has been fulfilled, in the 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself.'
But if one another you bite and eat up, watch lest by one another you be consumed.
But I say, by spirit walk, and desire of flesh you will certainly not complete.
For the flesh desires against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh; for these to one another are opposed, so that not whatever things you may want, these you do.
But if by spirit you are led, you are not under law.
But manifest are the works of the flesh, which are adultery, sexual immorality, uncleanness, licentiousness,
idolatry, drug-sorcery, enmities, strife, jealousy, rages, rivalries, dissensions, factions,
envyings, murders, drunkennesses, revels, and the things like these, which I tell you beforehand as also I said before, that the ones practising such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, long-suffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, self-mastery; against such things there is not a law.
But the ones of Christ Jesus crucified the flesh with the passions and the desires.
If we live by spirit, by spirit also let us walk in line.
Let us not become vainglorious, one another provoking, one another envying.

galatians_6.t: Brothers and sisters, if also a human be caught beforehand in some trespass, you the spiritual ones restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself lest also you be tested.
One another's weights carry, and thus fill up the law of Christ.
For if anyone thinks to be something being nothing, he deceives his own mind.
But let each test his own work, and then into himself alone the boast he will have and not into the other;
For each his own burden will carry.
But let the one being instructed in the word share with the one instructing in all good things.
Do not be led astray, God is not sneered at; for whatever a human sows, this also he will reap.
Because the one sowing into his own flesh out of the flesh will reap corruption, but the one sowing into the spirit out of the spirit will reap eternal life.
But doing the good let us not lose heart, for in its own season we will reap not fainting.
So then, as we have season, let us work the good toward all, and especially toward the household members of the faith.
See with what large letters I wrote to you with my own hand.
As many as want to look good in flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that for the cross of Christ they may not be persecuted.
For neither do the ones being circumcised themselves guard law, but they want you to be circumcised so that in your flesh they may boast.
But for me may it not be to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom to me the world has been crucified and I to the world.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision is anything nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
And as many as by this rule will keep in line, peace upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
For the rest let no one furnish troubles to me; for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers and sisters. Amen. [Written to the Galatians from Rome.]

hebrews_1.t: In many portions and in many ways, long ago, God having spoken to the fathers in the prophets,
at the last of these days spoke to us in a Son, whom he set as heir of all things, through whom also he made the ages,

who being radiance of the glory and exact impress of his substance, and carrying all things by the word of his power, through himself having made cleansing of sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
having become by so much better than the angels as he has inherited a name more excellent than theirs.
For to which of the angels did he ever say: 'You are my Son, I today have begotten you'? and again: 'I will be to him for a father, and he will be to me for a son'?
But when again he brings in the firstborn into the inhabited world he says: 'And let all God's angels bow down to him.'
And to the angels on the one hand he says: 'The one making his angels winds and his ministers a flame of fire';
but to the Son: 'Your throne, O God, is to the age of the age, and the staff of uprightness is the staff of your kingdom.'
'You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; because of this God, your God, anointed you with oil of gladness beyond your companions.'
And: 'You at the beginnings, Lord, founded the earth, and the heavens are works of your hands;
'they themselves will perish, but you remain; and all will be made old like a garment,
'and like a cloak you will roll them up, like a garment, and they will be changed; but you are the same, and your years will not fail.'
But to which of the angels has he ever said: 'Sit at my right hand until I set your enemies as a footstool of your feet'?
Are they not all ministering spirits being sent out for service on account of those about to inherit salvation?

hebrews_2.t: On account of this it is necessary for us to give heed more abundantly to the things heard, lest ever we drift away.
For if the word spoken through angels became firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
how will we escape, having neglected so great a salvation? — which, having taken its beginning to be spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,
God witnessing along with them by signs and both wonders and various powers and distributions of holy spirit according to his will.
For not to angels did he subject the coming inhabited world, concerning which we are speaking.
But someone somewhere witnessed, saying: 'What is a human, that you remember him, or a son of a human, that you visit him?
'You made him a little lower than angels; with glory and honour you crowned him, and you appointed him over the works of your hands;
'all things you subjected under his feet.' For in the subjecting to him of all things, he left nothing unsubjected to him. But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
But we see him having been made a little lower than angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honour, so that by God's grace he might taste death on behalf of everyone.
For it was fitting for him, on account of whom are all things and through whom are all things, in leading many sons to glory, to complete the originator of their salvation through sufferings.
For both the one sanctifying and those being sanctified are all from one; for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
saying: 'I will announce your name to my brothers, in the midst of an assembly I will sing your praise.'
And again: 'I will be trusting upon him.' And again: 'Behold, I and the children whom God gave me.'

Since therefore the children have shared in blood and flesh, he also himself in like manner partook of the same, so that through death he might render idle the one having the power of death, that is, the devil,
and might release these, as many as by fear of death through all of living were held liable to slavery.
For surely not of angels does he take hold, but of Abraham's seed he takes hold.

Whence he was obliged in all things to be made like the brothers, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the things toward God, for the making of propitiation for the sins of the people.
For in that he himself has suffered, having been tested, he is able to help those being tested.

hebrews_3.t: Whence, holy brothers and sisters, sharers of a heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus,
being faithful to the one having made him, as also Moses in all his house.
For of more glory than Moses this one has been counted worthy, by as much as more honour than the house has the one having built it.
For every house is built by someone, but the one having built all things is God.
And Moses on the one hand was faithful in all his house as an attendant, for a testimony of the things that would be spoken,
but Christ as a son over his house; whose house we are, if indeed we hold fast the boldness and the boast of the hope firm to the end.
Wherefore, just as the Holy Spirit says: 'Today, if you hear his voice,
'do not harden your hearts as in the embittering, according to the day of the testing in the wilderness,
'where your fathers tested me in a testing and saw my works
forty years; wherefore I was provoked with this generation and said: They always wander in the heart; and they themselves did not know my ways;
'as I swore in my anger: If they shall enter into my rest.'
See, brothers and sisters, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unfaithfulness in falling away from a living God;
but encourage yourselves each day, as long as it is called 'Today', so that none from among you be hardened by sin's deceit;
For we have become sharers of Christ, if indeed we hold the beginning of the substance firm to the end,
in the saying: 'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the embittering.'
For who, having heard, embittered? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?
And with whom was he provoked forty years? Was it not with those having sinned, whose limbs fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did he swear that they would not enter into his rest, except to those having disobeyed?
And we see that they were not able to enter because of lack of trust.

hebrews_4.t: Let us fear therefore, lest, a promise being left of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to have come short.
For indeed we are ones having had good news announced, just as they also; but the word of hearing did not benefit those, not having been mixed with trust in those who heard.
For we who trusted are entering into the rest, just as he has said: 'As I swore in my anger: If they shall enter into my rest' — and yet the works had come to be from the founding of the world.
For he has said somewhere concerning the seventh thus: 'And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.'
And in this again: 'If they shall enter into my rest.'
Since therefore it is left for some to enter into it, and those formerly having had the good news announced did not enter because of disobedience,
again he marks out a certain day, 'Today', in David saying after so long a time, just as it has been said before: 'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.'
For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not afterwards have spoken about another day.
So then there remains a sabbath-keeping for the people of God.
For the one having entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his own.
Let us be eager therefore to enter into that rest, so that no one fall in the same pattern of disobedience.

For living is the word of God and active and sharper than any two-edged sword and piercing as far as division of both soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and able to judge thoughts and intentions of the heart;
and there is no creature unmanifest before him, but all things are naked and laid bare to his eyes, toward whom is our word.
Having therefore a great high priest having passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast the confession.
For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathise with our weaknesses, but one having been tested in all things according to likeness, apart from sin.
Let us come near therefore with boldness to the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.

hebrews_5.t: For every high priest taken from among humans is appointed on behalf of humans in the things toward God, so that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
being able to feel measuredly toward the ignorant and the wandering, since he himself also is surrounded by weakness;
and because of it he is obliged, as concerning the people so also concerning himself, to offer for sins.
And not to himself does anyone take the honour, but being called by God, just as also Aaron was.
So also Christ did not glorify himself to become a high priest, but the one having spoken to him: 'You are my Son, I today have begotten you';
just as also in another place he says: 'You are a priest to the age according to the order of Melchizedek.'
who in the days of his flesh, having offered up both petitions and supplications with strong crying and tears to the one able to save him from death, and having been heard because of his reverence,
though being a son, he learned obedience from the things he suffered,
and having been completed he became to all those obeying him a cause of eternal salvation,
having been addressed by God as high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
Concerning whom the word is long for us and hard to interpret in the saying, since you have become sluggish in your hearings.

For indeed, owing to be teachers because of the time, you again have need of someone to teach you what are the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have become ones having need of milk and not of solid food.
For everyone partaking of milk is inexperienced in a word of righteousness; for he is an infant;
But solid food is of the complete, of those who because of habit have their faculties trained for discernment of both good and evil.

hebrews_6.t: Wherefore, having left the word of the beginning of Christ, let us be carried on to completeness, not again laying a foundation of change of mind from dead works and of trust toward God,
of teaching of washings, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgement.
And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
For it is impossible, those once having been enlightened, and having tasted of the heavenly gift and having become sharers of holy spirit
and having tasted a good word of God and powers of a coming age,
and having fallen away, again to renew to change of mind, crucifying again for themselves the Son of God and holding him up to public shame.
For land having drunk the rain coming often upon it and bearing vegetation fit for those on account of whom it is also farmed, partakes of blessing from God;
but bringing forth thorns and thistles, it is worthless and near a curse, whose end is for burning.
But we have been persuaded concerning you, beloved, of better things and things holding to salvation, even if we speak thus.
For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and the labour of the love that you showed toward his name, having served the holy ones and serving them.
But we desire each of you to show the same eagerness toward the full assurance of the hope until the end,
so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those through trust and long-suffering inheriting the promises.
For to Abraham, having promised, God, since he had no one greater to swear by, swore by himself,
saying: 'Surely blessing I will bless you and multiplying I will multiply you';
and thus, having been long-suffering, he obtained the promise.
For humans swear by the greater, and for them the oath is an end of all dispute, for confirmation.
In which God, wishing more abundantly to show to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of his purpose, mediated with an oath,
so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we might have strong encouragement, we who have fled for refuge to seize the hope lying before us;
which we have as an anchor of the soul, both safe and firm, and entering into the inner side of the curtain,
where as forerunner on our behalf Jesus entered, having become a high priest to the age according to the order of Melchizedek.

hebrews_7.t: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of the Most High God, the one having met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and having blessed him,
to whom also Abraham apportioned a tenth from all things — being first interpreted 'king of righteousness' and then also 'king of Salem', which is 'king of peace',
fatherless, motherless, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but having been made like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.
But see how great this one was, to whom even Abraham gave a tenth from the choicest spoils, the patriarch.
And those from among the sons of Levi receiving the priesthood have a commandment to tithe the people according to the law, that is, their brothers, though they have come out of the loin of Abraham.
But the one not tracing genealogy from them has tithed Abraham and has blessed the one having the promises.
And apart from all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the better.
And here dying humans receive tithes, but there one being witnessed that he lives.
And so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, the one receiving tithes, has been tithed;
for he was still in the loin of the father when Melchizedek met him.

If therefore completion was through the Levitical priesthood — for on the basis of it the people has been given the law — what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For the priesthood being changed, of necessity a change of law also comes about.
For the one concerning whom these things are said has shared in another tribe, from which no one has attended at the altar.
For it is plain beforehand that our Lord has risen out of Judah, concerning which tribe Moses said nothing about priests.
And it is still more abundantly clear, if according to the likeness of Melchizedek another priest arises,
who has become so not according to a law of fleshly commandment but according to a power of indestructible life;
for it is witnessed that 'You are a priest to the age according to the order of Melchizedek.'
For a setting aside of a preceding commandment comes about because of its weakness and uselessness
— for the law completed nothing — but a bringing in besides of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And inasmuch as it was not apart from an oath-taking — for those on the one hand without an oath-taking are having become priests,
but he with an oath-taking, through the one saying to him: 'The Lord swore and will not regret it: You are a priest to the age according to the order of Melchizedek' —
by so much also of a better covenant has Jesus become guarantor.
And they on the one hand have become many priests, because they were hindered by death from continuing;
but he, because he remains to the age, holds his priesthood untransferable.
Whence also he is able to save to the uttermost those coming to God through him, always living to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was also fitting for us: holy, guileless, undefiled, having been separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens;
who does not have need daily, as the high priests, first on behalf of his own sins to offer up sacrifices, then those of the people; for this he did once for all, having offered up himself.
For the law appoints humans as high priests having weakness, but the word of the oath-taking that is after the law, a Son completed to the age.

hebrews_8.t: Now a main point upon the things being said: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
a minister of the holy things and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, not a human.
For every high priest is appointed for the offering of both gifts and sacrifices; whence it is necessary for this one also to have something that he may offer.
If then he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, there being those offering the gifts according to the law;

who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when about to complete the tent: 'See,' he says, 'that you make all things according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain';
But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as also he is mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted upon better promises.
For if that first one were faultless, a place would not be sought for a second.
For finding fault with them he says: 'Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will complete upon the house of Israel and upon the house of Judah a new covenant,

'not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day of my taking hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.'

'For this is the covenant that I will covenant with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: giving my laws into their mind, and upon their hearts I will write them; and I will be to them for a God, and they themselves will be to me for a people.'
'And they shall not teach, each his fellow citizen and each his brother, saying: Know the Lord, because all will know me, from the small of them to the great of them;
'because I will be merciful to their unrighteous acts, and their sins I will remember no more.'
In the saying 'new' he has made the first old; and the thing being made old and growing aged is near vanishing.

hebrews_9.t: Now then the first tent also had regulations of service, and the worldly holy place.
For a tent was prepared, the first one, in which were both the lampstand and the table and the setting out of the loaves, which is called Holy.
And after the second curtain, a tent called Holy of Holies,

having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which were a golden jar holding the manna and the staff of Aaron that had budded and the tablets of the covenant;
and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the place of mercy; concerning which things it is not now the time to speak in detail.
And these things having been thus prepared, into the first tent the priests go continually, completing the services;
but into the second, once of the year, the high priest alone, not apart from blood, which he offers on behalf of himself and of the ignorances of the people;
the Holy Spirit showing this, that the way of the holy places has not yet been made manifest while the first tent still has standing;
which is a parable for the time that has come, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that are unable, as to conscience, to complete the one serving,
only upon foods and drinks and various washings, regulations of flesh imposed until a time of setting right.
But Christ having arrived as high priest of the good things that have come, through the greater and more complete tent not made by hands, that is, not of this creation,
nor through blood of goats and calves but through his own blood, he entered once for all into the holy places, having found eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls and ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled sanctifies toward the purity of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through eternal spirit offered himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works for the serving of a living God?

And on account of this he is mediator of a new covenant, so that, a death having occurred for redemption from the transgressions under the first covenant, those having been called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
For where a covenant is, the death of the one having covenanted must be borne;
for a covenant is firm over dead ones, since it never has force when the one having covenanted lives.
Whence not even the first has been inaugurated apart from blood.

For every commandment according to the law having been spoken by Moses to all the people, taking the blood of the calves and of the goats with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
saying: 'This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded toward you.'
And the tent also and all the vessels of the service he likewise sprinkled with the blood.
And nearly all things are cleansed with blood according to the law, and apart from bloodshedding no forgiveness comes about.
It was necessary therefore for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
For not into holy places made by hands did Christ enter, copies of the true ones, but into heaven itself, now to be made manifest before the face of God on our behalf;
nor that he might offer himself often, just as the high priest enters into the holy places yearly with blood not his own;

since it would have been necessary for him to suffer often from the founding of the world; but now once at the completion of the ages he has been made manifest for the setting aside of sin through his sacrifice.
And inasmuch as it is laid up for humans once to die, and after this judgement,
so also Christ, having been offered once to bear up the sins of many, will be seen a second time apart from sin by those eagerly awaiting him, for salvation.

hebrews_10.t: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the image itself of the things, can never with the same sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, complete those coming near;
since would they not have ceased being offered, because those serving, once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year;
for it is impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Wherefore, coming into the world he says: 'Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you fitted for me;
'whole burnt offerings and offerings concerning sin you did not take pleasure in.'
'Then I said: Behold, I have come — in the roll of a book it is written concerning me — to do, O God, your will.'
Saying above that 'sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings concerning sin you did not desire nor take pleasure in' — which are offered according to the law —
then he has said: 'Behold, I have come to do, O God, your will.' He takes away the first so that he may set up the second;
by which will we are ones having been made holy, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands day by day serving and offering often the same sacrifices, which are never able to take away sins;
but this one, having offered one sacrifice on behalf of sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until his enemies are set as a footstool of his feet.
For by one offering he has completed for all time those being made holy.
And the Holy Spirit also witnesses to us; for after having said:
'This is the covenant that I will covenant toward them after those days, says the Lord: giving my laws upon their hearts, and upon their mind I will write them';
and 'their sins and their lawless acts I will remember no more.'
And where forgiveness of these is, there is no longer an offering concerning sin.
Having therefore, brothers and sisters, boldness for the entrance of the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
which he inaugurated for us, a way fresh and living, through the curtain, that is, his flesh,
and having a great priest over the house of God,
let us come near with a true heart in full assurance of trust, having had the hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and having had the body washed with clean water.
Let us hold fast the confession of the hope unbending, for faithful is the one having promised;
and let us consider one another for a provoking of love and good works,
not forsaking the gathering together of ourselves, as is the custom with some, but encouraging, and by so much more as you see the Day drawing near.
For if we sin willingly after receiving the full knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice concerning sins,
but a certain fearful expectation of judgement and a zeal of fire about to consume the adversaries.
Anyone having set aside Moses' law dies without mercies on the word of two or three witnesses;

how much worse punishment, do you think, will he be counted worthy of who trampled the Son of God and considered common the blood of the covenant by which he was made holy, and outraged the Spirit of grace?
For we know the one having said: 'Vengeance is mine, I will repay,' says the Lord; and again: 'The Lord will judge his people.'
Fearful is the falling into the hands of a living God.
But remember the former days, in which, having been enlightened, you endured a great contest of sufferings,
partly being made a spectacle by reproaches and afflictions, and partly having become sharers of those so treated;
For you both suffered along with the prisoners and accepted with joy the seizure of your possessions, knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession in the heavens, and abiding.
Do not therefore throw away your boldness, which has great recompense.
For you have need of endurance, so that having done the will of God you may receive back the promise.
For yet a little, how very little, 'the coming one will come and will not delay';
'But my righteous one will live from trust; and if he shrinks back, my soul does not take pleasure in him.'
But we are not of shrinking back to destruction, but of trust to the preserving of soul.

hebrews_11.t: Now trust is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
For in this the elders were witnessed to.
By trust we understand the ages to have been framed by a word of God, so that not out of things appearing has what is seen come to be.
By trust Abel offered to God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he was witnessed to be righteous, God witnessing over his gifts; and through it, having died, he still speaks.
By trust Enoch was transferred so as not to see death, and he was not found because God transferred him; for before his transfer he had been witnessed to have pleased God.
And apart from trust it is impossible to please; for the one coming to God must trust that he is and that to those seeking him out he becomes a rewarder.

By trust Noah, having been warned about the things not yet seen, having taken care, prepared an ark for the salvation of his household, through which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness according to trust.
By trust the one being called, Abraham, obeyed to go out to a place that he was about to receive for an inheritance, and he went out not knowing where he is going.
By trust he sojourned in the land of the promise as in a foreign land, having settled in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the co-heirs of the same promise;
for he was waiting for the city having the foundations, whose craftsman and maker is God.
By trust also Sarah herself, barren, received power for a laying down of seed and beyond the season of age, since she considered faithful the one having promised.
Therefore also from one, and these things from one having been deadened, were born as the stars of heaven in multitude and as the sand beside the shore of the sea, innumerable.
According to trust these all died, not having received the promises but having seen them from afar and greeted them, and having confessed that they are strangers and sojourners upon the earth.
For those saying such things make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.
And if indeed they had been remembering that one from which they had gone out, they would have had opportunity to return;
but now they reach out for a better, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God; for he prepared for them a city.
By trust Abraham has offered up Isaac, being tested, and the one having received the promises was offering up the only-begotten,
to whom it was said that 'In Isaac seed will be called for you';
reckoning that God is able to raise even from the dead, from where he also received him back in a parable.
By trust also concerning things to come Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau.
By trust Jacob, dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and bowed down upon the top of his staff.
By trust Joseph, coming to his end, remembered concerning the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave command concerning his bones.
By trust Moses, having been born, was hidden three months by his fathers, because they saw the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the decree of the king.
By trust Moses, having become great, refused to be called son of Pharaoh's daughter,
having chosen rather to be ill-treated together with the people of God than to have a temporary enjoyment of sin,
having considered the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he was looking away to the recompense.
By trust he left Egypt, not having feared the anger of the king; for he persevered as seeing the invisible one.
By trust he has made the Passover and the pouring of the blood, so that the one destroying the firstborn might not touch them.
By trust they crossed the Red Sea as through dry land, of which the Egyptians, taking trial, were swallowed up.
By trust the walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled for seven days.
By trust Rahab the prostitute did not perish together with those having disobeyed, having received the spies with peace.
And what more shall I say? For the time will fail me recounting about Gideon, Barak and Samson and Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets;
who through trust conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, shut mouths of lions,
quenched the power of fire, escaped mouths of the sword, were made powerful from weakness, became strong in war, turned back the camps of foreigners.
Women received their dead from resurrection; but others were broken on the wheel, not accepting the release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection;
And others received trial of mockings and floggings, and further of chains and imprisonment;
they were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were tested, they died by murder of the sword; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, lacking, afflicted, ill-treated,
of whom the world was not worthy — wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and the holes of the earth.
And these all, having been witnessed to through the trust, did not receive the promise,
God having foreseen something better concerning us, so that not apart from us might they be completed.

hebrews_12.t: Therefore we also, having so great a cloud of witnesses lying around us, having laid aside every weight and the easily-entangling sin, let us run with endurance the contest lying before us,
looking away to the originator and completer of the trust, Jesus, who for the joy lying before him endured a cross, having despised shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For consider the one having endured such contradiction from sinners against himself, so that you may not grow weary, fainting in your souls.
Not yet unto blood have you resisted, struggling against sin;
and you have forgotten the encouragement which reasons with you as with sons: 'My son, do not think little of the Lord's training, nor faint when reproved by him;
'for whom the Lord loves he trains, and he flogs every son whom he receives.'
For training you endure; as with sons God deals with you. For what son is there whom a father does not train?
But if you are apart from training, of which all have become sharers, then you are illegitimate and not sons.
Then we had the fathers of our flesh as trainers and we respected them; shall we not much more be subjected to the Father of the spirits and live?
For they for a few days trained according to what seemed good to them, but he for what is profitable, for the sharing of his holiness.
And all training for the present does not seem to be of joy but of grief; but later it gives back a peaceful fruit of righteousness to those having been trained through it.
Therefore straighten up the drooping hands and the paralysed knees,
and make straight tracks for your feet, so that the lame may not be turned aside but rather be healed.
Pursue peace with all and the holiness apart from which no one will see the Lord;
overseeing lest anyone be falling short from the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness growing up cause trouble, and through it the many be defiled;
lest anyone be a fornicator or profane, as Esau, who for one meal gave away his own birthright.
For you know that also afterwards, wanting to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place of change of mind, though having sought it with tears.
For you have not come to a thing being touched and burning with fire, and to gloom and darkness and storm,
and to a trumpet's sound and to a voice of words, of which those who heard begged that no word be added to them;
for they could not bear what was being commanded: 'Even if a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or shot through with a dart';
and so fearful was what appeared, Moses said: 'I am terrified and trembling';
but you have come to Zion, a mountain, and to a city of a living God, a heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels, a festal gathering,
and to an assembly of firstborn ones enrolled in the heavens, and to a judge, God of all, and to spirits of righteous ones having been completed,
and to a mediator of a new covenant, Jesus, and to blood of sprinkling speaking better than Abel.
See that you do not refuse the one speaking; for if those did not escape, having refused the one warning on earth, much more we, who turn away from the one from the heavens,
whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying: 'Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.'
And the 'yet once more' makes clear the removal of the things being shaken, as of things having been made, so that the things not being shaken may remain.
Therefore, receiving an unshakeable kingdom, let us have grace, through which let us serve God acceptably with reverence and awe;
for indeed our God is a consuming fire.

hebrews_13.t: Let brotherly love remain.
Do not forget hospitality; for through this some, without knowing it, entertained angels.
Remember the prisoners as bound with them, those being ill-treated as also yourselves being in a body.
Marriage honourable among all, and the bed undefiled; but fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
The manner of life without love of money; being content with the things present; for he himself has said: 'I will not leave you, nor will I ever forsake you';
so that we, being confident, may say: 'The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear; what will a human do to me?'
Remember your leaders, who spoke to you the word of God; considering closely the outcome of their way of life, imitate the trust.
Jesus Christ, yesterday and today the same, and to the ages.
Do not be carried away by various and strange teachings; for it is good for the heart to be confirmed by grace, not by foods, in which those walking were not benefited.
We have an altar from which those serving the tent have no authority to eat.
For of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy places concerning sin through the high priest, of these the bodies are burned outside the camp.
Therefore Jesus also, so that he might make the people holy through his own blood, suffered outside the gate.
Therefore let us go out to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.
For we do not have here an abiding city, but we seek the coming one.
Through him therefore let us offer up a sacrifice of praise continually to God, that is, fruit of lips confessing his name.
And do not forget the doing of good and fellowship; for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

Be persuaded by your leaders and yield; for they keep watch over your souls as ones who will give an account, so that they may do this with joy and not groaning; for this would be unprofitable for you.
Pray concerning us; for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, wanting in all things to conduct ourselves well.
And I urge you more abundantly to do this, so that I may be restored to you the more quickly.
Now the God of peace, the one having brought up from the dead the shepherd of the sheep, the great one, by blood of an eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
equip you in every good work for the doing of his will, doing in us what is well pleasing before him through Jesus Christ; to whom be the glory to the ages of the ages, amen.
And I urge you, brothers and sisters, bear with the word of the encouragement; for indeed through few words I have written to you.
Know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom, if he comes soon, I will see you.
Greet all your leaders and all the holy ones. Those from Italy greet you.
The grace be with all of you. Amen. [To the Hebrews it was written from Italy through Timothy.]

james_1.t: James, of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ a servant, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: Rejoice.
All joy consider it, my brothers and sisters, whenever you fall among various trials,
knowing that the tested-genuineness of your trust works out endurance.
And let the endurance have a complete work, so that you may be complete and entire, lacking in nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from the God who gives to all simply and does not reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in trust, doubting nothing; for the one doubting is like a surge of sea, wind-driven and tossed.
For let not that person suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord —
a double-souled man, unstable in all his ways.
But let the lowly brother boast in his height,
but the rich one in his humiliation, because like a flower of the grass he will pass away.
For the sun rose with the burning heat and withered the grass, and its flower fell off, and the beauty of its appearance perished; so also the rich one in his goings will be withered.
Blessed is a man who endures trial, because having become tested he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to those loving him.
Let no one being tried say that 'From God I am being tried'; for God is untried by evils, and he himself tries no one.
But each is tried by his own desire, being drawn out and lured.
Then the desire, having conceived, bears sin; and the sin, having been brought to completion, gives birth to death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers and sisters.
Every good giving and every complete gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the lights, with whom there is not a change or a shadowing of turning.
Having willed it, he gave us birth by a word of truth, for us to be a certain firstfruits of his creatures.
Know this, my beloved brothers and sisters; but let every human be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
For anger of a man does not work righteousness of God.
Therefore, having put away all filthiness and abundance of evil, receive in meekness the implanted word, the one able to save your souls.
But become doers of word and not only hearers, deceiving yourselves by false reckoning.
Because if anyone is a hearer of word and not a doer, this one is like a man observing the face of his birth in a mirror;
For he observed himself and has gone away and immediately forgot what sort he was.

But the one having stooped into a complete law, the one of freedom, and having remained — this one, not having become a hearer of forgetfulness but a doer of work — this one will be blessed in his doing.
If anyone seems to be religious, not bridling his tongue but deceiving his heart, of this one the religion is empty.
Religion clean and undefiled before the God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, to keep oneself unspotted from the world.

james_2.t: My brothers and sisters, do not, in acts of face-receiving, hold the faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, of the glory.
For if there enters into your synagogue a gold-ringed man in bright clothing, and there enters also a poor man in filthy clothing,
and you look upon the one wearing the bright clothing and say to him, 'You sit here well,' and to the poor you say, 'You stand there, or sit under my footstool' —
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges of evil reasonings?
Listen, my beloved brothers and sisters: did not God choose the poor to the world to be rich in trust and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to those loving him?
But you dishonoured the poor. Do not the rich oppress you, and they themselves drag you into courts?
Do not they blaspheme the good name called upon you?
If indeed you complete a royal law according to the scripture, 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself,' you do well.
But if you receive faces, you work sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one, has become guilty of all.
For the one having said, 'Do not commit adultery,' said also, 'Do not murder.' But if you do not commit adultery but you do murder, you have become a transgressor of law.
So speak and so act as those about to be judged through a law of freedom.
For the judgement is merciless to the one not having done mercy; mercy boasts against judgement.
What is the benefit, my brothers and sisters, if someone says he has trust but does not have works? The trust is not able to save him, is it?
But if a brother or sister is naked and lacking the daily food,
and someone of you says to them, 'Go in peace, be warmed and be filled,' but you do not give them the necessities of the body, what is the benefit?
So also the trust, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.
But someone will say, 'You have trust and I have works.' Show me your trust apart from the works, and I will show you out of my works the trust.
You trust that God is one; you do well. The demons also trust, and they shudder.
But do you wish to know, O empty man, that the trust apart from the works is idle?
Was not Abraham our father justified out of works, having offered up Isaac his son upon the altar?
You see that the trust was working together with his works, and out of the works the trust was completed,
And the scripture was fulfilled which says, 'And Abraham trusted God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness'; and he was called friend of God.
You see, then, that out of works a human is justified and not out of trust only.
And likewise also Rahab the prostitute — was she not justified out of works, having received the messengers and having thrown them out by another way?
For just as the body apart from spirit is dead, so also the trust apart from works is dead.

james_3.t: Do not become many teachers, my brothers and sisters, knowing that we will receive greater judgement.
For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a complete man, able to bridle also the whole body.
But if we throw the bridles of the horses into their mouths for them to obey us, we also steer their whole body.
Behold also the ships, being so great and driven by hard winds, are steered by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wills.
So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Behold, how small a fire sets alight how great a forest;
And the tongue is a fire, the world of unrighteousness; the tongue is set among our members, the one staining the whole body and setting on fire the wheel of birth, and being set on fire by Gehenna.
For every nature of beasts and of birds, of reptiles and of sea creatures, is tamed and has been tamed by the human nature;
but the tongue no one of humans is able to tame; an unstable evil, full of death-bearing venom.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse the humans who have come to be according to the likeness of God.
Out of the same mouth comes out blessing and curse. It ought not, my brothers and sisters, these things so to be.
The spring does not from the same opening gush the sweet and the bitter, does it?
A fig tree is not able, my brothers and sisters, to make olives, or a vine figs? Neither salt to make sweet water.
Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show out of the good conduct his works in meekness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.
This is not the wisdom coming down from above, but earthly, soulish, demonic.
For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is instability and every worthless deed.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, easily persuaded, full of mercy and of good fruits, undivided, unhypocritical.
And fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those making peace.

james_4.t: From where are wars and from where battles among you? Is it not from here, out of your pleasures campaigning in your members?
You desire and do not have; you murder and you are jealous and are not able to obtain; you battle and you wage war; but you do not have because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive, because you ask badly, in order that you may spend it in your pleasures.
Adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that the friendship of the world is enmity of God? Therefore whoever wills to be a friend of the world is constituted an enemy of God.
Or do you suppose that the scripture speaks emptily? Toward envy he longs for the spirit which he settled in us;
But he gives greater grace; therefore it says, 'God opposes the arrogant, but to the lowly he gives grace.'
Be subjected therefore to God; but stand against the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse hands, sinners, and purify hearts, double-souled.
Be miserable and mourn and weep; let your laughter be turned into mourning, and the joy into dejection.
Be humbled before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

Do not speak against one another, brothers and sisters. The one speaking against a brother or judging his brother speaks against law and judges law; but if you judge law, you are not a doer of law but a judge.
One is the lawgiver and judge, the one able to save and to destroy; but you, who are you, the one judging the neighbour?
Come now, those saying, 'Today or tomorrow we will travel into this city and will spend there one year and will trade and will make a profit' —
who do not know the thing of tomorrow — what your life is. For you are a vapour, appearing for a little and then also vanishing;
Instead of your saying, 'If the Lord wills, we will both live and will do this or that.'
But now you boast in your arrogances; all such boasting is evil.
Therefore to the one knowing to do good and not doing it, to him it is sin.

james_5.t: Come now, the rich, weep, wailing over your miseries coming upon you.
Your riches have rotted and your garments have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and the silver have been corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You stored up treasure in last days.
Behold, the wage of the workers who mowed your fields, which has been withheld from you, cries out, and the cries of those who harvested have entered into the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.
You lived luxuriously on the earth and were self-indulgent; you fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
You condemned, you murdered the righteous one; he does not oppose you.

Be long-tempered therefore, brothers and sisters, until the arrival of the Lord. Behold, the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, being long-tempered over it until it receives early and late rain.
Be long-tempered also yourselves; strengthen your hearts, because the arrival of the Lord has drawn near.
Do not groan against one another, brothers and sisters, in order that you may not be judged; behold, the judge stands before the doors.
Take an example, my brothers and sisters, of the suffering of evil and of long-temper: the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Behold, we call blessed those who endured. You heard of the endurance of Job and saw the end of the Lord, because the Lord is very compassionate and merciful.

But before all things, my brothers and sisters, do not swear, neither by the heaven nor by the earth nor any other oath; but let your yes be yes and the no no, so that you may not fall under judgement.
Does anyone among you suffer evil? Let him pray. Is anyone in good spirits? Let him sing praise.
Is anyone among you sick? Let him call to himself the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the vow of trust will save the one being weary, and the Lord will raise him; and if he should be one having done sins, it will be forgiven him.
Therefore confess to one another the sins and pray on behalf of one another, so that you may be healed. A petition of a righteous one is very strong, being at work.
Elijah was a human of like feeling with us, and with prayer he prayed for it not to rain, and it did not rain upon the earth three years and six months.
And again he prayed, and the heaven gave rain and the earth sprouted its fruit.
My brothers and sisters, if anyone among you is led astray from the truth and someone turns him,
let him know that the one having turned a sinner from the wandering of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

john_1.t: In beginning was the Word, and the Word was toward God, and God was the Word.
This one was in beginning toward God.
All things through him came to be, and apart from him came to be not even one thing which has come to be.
In him life was, and the life was the light of the humans.
And the light in the darkness shines, and the darkness it did not grasp/overcome.
Came to be a human sent from beside God, name to him John.
This one came for witness, that he might witness concerning the light, that all might trust through him.
Not was that one the light, but that he might witness concerning the light.
Was the light the true, which enlightens every human, coming into the world.
In the world he was, and the world through him came to be, and the world him did not know.
To the own things he came, and the own ones him did not receive.
But as many as received him, he gave to them authority children of God to become, to the ones trusting into his name,
who not out of bloods nor out of will of flesh nor out of will of a man but out of God were begotten.
And the Word flesh became and pitched his tent among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of an only-born from a father, full of grace and truth.
John witnesses concerning him and has cried out saying: This was he of whom I said, The one behind me coming ahead of me has come to be, because first of me he was.
