Because out of his fullness we all received, and grace in place of grace.
Because the law through Moses was given, the grace and the truth through Jesus Christ came to be.
God no one has seen ever; the only-born God, the one being in the bosom of the father, that one explained him.
And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent to him out of Jerusalem priests and Levites, that they might ask him: You, who are you?
And he confessed and did not deny, and he confessed that: I am not the Christ.
And they asked him: What then? Elijah are you? And he says: I am not. The prophet are you? And he answered: No.
They said therefore to him: Who are you? that an answer we may give to the ones having sent us; what do you say concerning yourself?
He said: I a voice of one crying in the wilderness: Straighten the way of the Lord, as said Isaiah the prophet.
And the ones having been sent were out of the Pharisees.
And they asked him and said to him: Why then do you baptise if you are not the Christ nor Elijah nor the prophet?
Answered them John saying: I baptise in water; in the middle of you has stood one whom you do not know,
he the one behind me coming, of whom not am I worthy that I should loose of him the strap of the sandal.
These things in Bethany came to be across the Jordan, where was John baptising.
On the next day he sees Jesus coming toward him and says: See, the lamb of God, the one taking away the sin of the world.
This one is concerning whom I said: Behind me comes a man who ahead of me has come to be, because first of me he was.
And I did not know him, but that he might be revealed to Israel, on account of this came I in the water baptising.
And witnessed John saying that: I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of heaven, and it remained upon him.

And I did not know him, but the one having sent me to baptise in water, that one to me said: Upon whomever you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, this one is the one baptising in Spirit Holy.
And I have seen and have witnessed that this one is the Chosen One of God.
On the next day again had stood John and out of his disciples two.
And having looked at Jesus walking he says: See, the lamb of God.
And heard the two disciples of him speaking and they followed Jesus.
And having turned Jesus and having beheld them following says to them: What do you seek? And they said to him: Rabbi — which is said, being translated, Teacher — where are you remaining?
He says to them: Come and you will see. They came therefore and saw where he remains, and beside him they remained that day; hour it was about tenth.
Was Andrew the brother of Simon Peter one out of the two of the ones having heard from beside John and having followed him.
Finds this one first the brother the own Simon and says to him: We have found the Messiah — which is, being translated, Christ.
He led him toward Jesus. Having looked at him Jesus said: You are Simon the son of John; you will be called Cephas — which is interpreted Peter.
On the next day he willed to go out into Galilee and finds Philip, and says to him Jesus: Follow me.
Was now Philip from Bethsaida, out of the city of Andrew and Peter.
Finds Philip Nathanael and says to him: Whom wrote Moses in the law and the prophets, we have found — Jesus son of Joseph the one from Nazareth.
And said to him Nathanael: Out of Nazareth can any good thing be? Says to him Philip: Come and see.
Saw Jesus Nathanael coming toward him and says concerning him: See truly an Israelite in whom deceit is not.
Says to him Nathanael: From where me do you know? Answered Jesus and said to him: Before the you Philip to call, being under the fig tree, I saw you.
Answered him Nathanael and says: Rabbi, you are the Son of God, you the king are of Israel.
Answered Jesus and said to him: Because I said to you that I saw you underneath the fig tree, do you trust? Greater things than these you will see.
And he says to him: Amen amen I say to you, you will see the heaven having been opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.

john_2.t: And on the day the third a wedding came to be in Cana of Galilee, and was the mother of Jesus there.
Was called now also Jesus and his disciples into the wedding.
And wine having failed says the mother of Jesus toward him: Wine they do not have.
And says to her Jesus: What to me and to you, woman? Not yet has come my hour.
Says his mother to the servants: Whatever he might say to you, do.
Were now there stone water-jars six according to the cleansing of the Jews lying, holding up to measures two or three.
Says to them Jesus: Fill the water-jars of water. And they filled them until above.
And he says to them: Draw now and carry to the head-of-the-table. And they carried.
As now tasted the head-of-the-table the water wine having become and did not know from where it is, but the servants knew the ones having drawn the water, calls the bridegroom the head-of-the-table
and says to him: Every human first the good wine sets out, and whenever they may be drunk, the lesser; you have kept the good wine until now.
This did the beginning of the signs Jesus in Cana of Galilee and revealed his glory, and trusted into him his disciples.
After this he went down into Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples, and there they remained not many days.
And near was the Passover of the Jews, and went up into Jerusalem Jesus.
And he found in the temple the ones selling oxen and sheep and doves and the coin-dealers sitting.
And having made a whip out of cords, all he drove out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen, and of the money-changers he poured out the coin and the tables he overturned.
And to the ones the doves selling he said: Take these things from here, do not make the house of my Father a house of merchandise.
Remembered now his disciples that written it is: The zeal of your house will devour me.
Answered therefore the Jews and said to him: What sign do you show to us that these things you do?
Answered Jesus and said to them: Loose this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it.
Said therefore the Jews: In forty and six years was built this sanctuary, and you in three days will raise it?
But that one was speaking concerning the sanctuary of his body.
When therefore he was raised out of dead ones, remembered his disciples that this he was saying, and they trusted the scripture and the word which said Jesus.
And as he was in Jerusalem in the Passover in the feast, many trusted into his name, beholding of him the signs which he was doing.
But he himself Jesus was not entrusting himself to them on account of the him to know all,
and because need he did not have that anyone should witness concerning the human; for he himself was knowing what was in the human.

john_3.t: Was now a human out of the Pharisees, Nicodemus name to him, a ruler of the Jews.
This one came toward him by night and said to him: Rabbi, we know that from God you have come a teacher; for no one can these signs do which you do, unless God be with him.
Answered Jesus and said to him: Amen amen I say to you, unless someone be begotten from above/again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
Says toward him Nicodemus: How can a human be begotten being old? Not can he into the belly of his mother a second time enter and be begotten?
Answered Jesus: Amen amen I say to you, unless someone be begotten out of water and Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
The thing having been begotten out of the flesh flesh is, and the thing having been begotten out of the Spirit spirit is.
Do not marvel that I said to you: It is necessary for you all to be begotten from above/again.
The wind/Spirit where it wills blows, and its voice you hear, but you do not know from where it comes and where it goes; so is everyone having been begotten out of the Spirit.
Answered Nicodemus and said to him: How can these things come to be?
Answered Jesus and said to him: You are the teacher of Israel and these things you do not know?
Amen amen I say to you that what we know we speak and what we have seen we witness, and our witness you do not receive.
If the earthly things I said to you and you do not trust, how if I say to you the heavenly things will you trust?
And no one has ascended into the heaven except the one out of the heaven having descended, the Son of Man [who is in the heaven].
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must be lifted up the Son of Man,
that everyone trusting in him may have life eternal.
For thus loved God the world, so that the Son of him the only-born he gave, that everyone trusting into him might not perish but have life eternal.
For God did not send the Son into the world that he might judge the world, but that might be saved the world through him.
The one trusting into him is not judged; the one now not trusting already has been judged, because he has not trusted into the name of the only-born Son of God.
And this is the judgment, that the light has come into the world and loved the humans rather the darkness than the light; for evil was of them the works.
For everyone the worthless things practising hates the light and does not come toward the light, that may not be exposed his works.
But the one doing the truth comes toward the light, that may be revealed of him the works, that in God they are having been worked.
After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the Judean land, and there he was spending time with them and was baptising.
Was now also John baptising in Aenon near the Salim, because waters many were there, and they were arriving and were being baptised.
For not yet was having been thrown into the prison John.
Came to be therefore a questioning out of the disciples of John with a Jew concerning cleansing.
And they came toward John and said to him: Rabbi, he who was with you across the Jordan, to whom you have witnessed, see, this one baptises and all are coming toward him.
Answered John and said: Cannot a human receive not even one thing unless it be having been given to him out of the heaven.
You yourselves to me witness that I said that: I am not the Christ, but that having been sent I am before that one.

The one having the bride a bridegroom is; but the friend of the bridegroom, the one having stood and hearing him, with joy rejoices on account of the voice of the bridegroom. This therefore the joy the mine has been fulfilled.
That one must increase, but I must decrease.
The one from above coming above all is; the one being out of the earth out of the earth is and out of the earth speaks. The one out of the heaven coming above all is.
What he has seen and heard, this he witnesses, and his witness no one receives.
The one having received his witness has sealed that God true is.
For whom God sent the words of God speaks; for not out of measure he gives the Spirit.
The Father loves the Son and all things has given in his hand.
The one trusting into the Son has life eternal; but the one disobeying the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.

john_4.t: When therefore knew Jesus that heard the Pharisees that Jesus more disciples makes and baptises than John,
although indeed Jesus himself was not baptising but his disciples,
he left Judea and went away again into Galilee.
And it was necessary for him to pass through Samaria.
He comes therefore into a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the piece of land which gave Jacob to Joseph his son.
And was there a spring of Jacob. Jesus therefore having grown weary from the journeying was sitting thus upon the spring; hour it was about sixth.
Comes a woman out of Samaria to draw water. Says to her Jesus: Give me to drink.
For his disciples had gone away into the city that food they might buy.
Says therefore to him the woman the Samaritan: How you a Jew being from me to drink do ask, being a woman a Samaritan? For not do use together Jews with Samaritans.
Answered Jesus and said to her: If you had known the gift of God and who is the one saying to you: Give me to drink, you would have asked him and he would have given to you water living.
Says to him the woman: Lord/Sir, neither a drawing-vessel do you have and the well is deep; from where therefore do you have the water the living?
Not you greater are than the father of us Jacob, who gave to us the well, and he himself out of it drank and the sons of him and the cattle of him?
Answered Jesus and said to her: Everyone drinking out of this water will thirst again;

but whoever might drink out of the water which I will give to him, not shall he thirst into the age, but the water which I will give to him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into life eternal.
Says toward him the woman: Lord/Sir, give to me this water, that not I may thirst nor come through here to draw.
He says to her: Go, call your husband and come here.
Answered the woman and said to him: Not I have a husband. Says to her Jesus: Well you said that: A husband not I have;
For five husbands you had, and now whom you have is not of you a husband; this truly you have said.
Says to him the woman: Lord/Sir, I perceive that a prophet are you.
The fathers of us on this mountain worshipped, and you all say that in Jerusalem is the place where to worship it is necessary.
Says to her Jesus: Trust me, woman, that comes an hour when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you all worship the Father.
You all worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because the salvation out of the Jews is.
But comes an hour and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for indeed the Father such ones seeks the ones worshipping him.
Spirit the God, and the ones worshipping him in spirit and truth must worship.
Says to him the woman: I know that Messiah comes, the one called Christ; whenever comes that one, he will announce to us all things.
Says to her Jesus: I am, the one speaking to you.
And upon this came his disciples and they were marvelling that with a woman he was speaking; no one however said: What do you seek? or: Why do you speak with her?
Left therefore the water-jar of her the woman and went away into the city and says to the humans:
Come, see a human who said to me all things whatever I did; not this one is the Christ?
They went out out of the city and were coming toward him.
In the meanwhile were asking him the disciples saying: Rabbi, eat.
But he said to them: I food have to eat which you do not know.
Were saying therefore the disciples toward one another: Not anyone brought to him to eat?
Says to them Jesus: My food is that I should do the will of the one having sent me and should complete of him the work.
Not you say that yet four-months it is and the harvest comes? Behold I say to you: Lift up the eyes of you and behold the fields, that white they are toward harvest already.
And the one reaping wages receives and gathers fruit into life eternal, that the one sowing together may rejoice and the one reaping.
For in this the word is the true, that another is the one sowing and another the one reaping.
I sent you to reap what not you have laboured for; others have laboured, and you into the labour of them have entered.
Out of that city now many trusted into him of the Samaritans on account of the word of the woman witnessing that: He said to me all things which I did.
As therefore came toward him the Samaritans, they were asking him to remain beside them; and he remained there two days.
And by much more trusted on account of the word of him,
and to the woman they were saying that: No longer on account of your talk do we trust; for we ourselves have heard and we know that this one is truly the saviour of the world.
And after the two days he went out from there into Galilee.
For he himself Jesus witnessed that a prophet in the own homeland honour does not have.
When therefore he came into Galilee, received him the Galileans, all things having seen whatever he did in Jerusalem in the feast; for also they came into the feast.
He came therefore again into the Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And was a certain royal one of whom the son was sick in Capernaum.
This one having heard that Jesus has come out of Judea into Galilee, went away toward him and was asking that he might come down and might heal of him the son; for he was about to die.
Said therefore Jesus toward him: Unless signs and wonders you all see, not at all will you trust.
Says toward him the royal one: Lord/Sir, come down before to die the little child of me.
Says to him Jesus: Go, the son of you lives. Trusted the human the word which said to him Jesus, and he was going.
Already now of him going down the slaves of him met him and reported saying that the boy of him lives.
He enquired therefore the hour from them in which better he got. They said therefore to him that: Yesterday hour seventh left him the fever.
Knew therefore the father that in that the hour in which said to him Jesus that: The son of you lives, and he trusted himself and the household of him whole.
This now again second sign did Jesus having come out of Judea into Galilee.

john_5.t: After these things was a feast of the Jews, and went up Jesus into Jerusalem.
And there is in Jerusalem at the sheep-place a pool, the one being called in Hebrew Bethzatha, five porticoes having.
In these was lying a multitude much of the ones being sick, blind, lame, withered, waiting for the of the water moving.

[For an angel according to season was going down in the pool and was troubling the water; the one therefore first having stepped in after the troubling of the water healthy was becoming, by whatever disease he was being held.]
And was a certain human there thirty and eight years having in the sickness of him.
This one having seen Jesus lying, and having known that much already time he has, says to him: Do you wish healthy to become?

Answered to him the one being sick: Lord/Sir, a human I do not have that whenever might be troubled the water he might throw me into the pool; but in which I am coming myself, another before me goes down.
Says to him Jesus: Rise, take up the mat of you and walk.
And immediately became healthy the human and took up the mat of him and was walking. And it was sabbath on that the day.
Were saying therefore the Jews to the one having been healed: Sabbath it is, and not is it lawful for you to take up the mat of you.
But he answered to them: The one having made me healthy, that one to me said: Take up the mat of you and walk.
They asked him: Who is the human the one having said to you: Take up and walk?
But the one having been healed did not know who it is; for Jesus turned aside, a crowd being in the place.
After these things finds him Jesus in the temple and said to him: See, healthy you have become; no longer sin, that not something worse to you might happen.
Went away the human and reported to the Jews that Jesus is the one having made him healthy.
And on account of this were persecuting the Jews Jesus, because these things he was doing on sabbath.
But Jesus answered to them: The Father of me until now works, and I work.
On account of this therefore rather were seeking him the Jews to kill, because not only was he loosing the sabbath but also father his own was calling God, equal himself making with God.

Answered therefore Jesus and was saying to them: Amen amen I say to you, cannot the Son do from himself not one thing, unless something he might see the Father doing; for whatever things that one does, these things also the Son likewise does.
For the Father loves the Son and all things shows to him which he himself does, and greater than these he will show to him works, that you may marvel.
For just as the Father raises the dead ones and makes alive, thus also the Son whom he wills makes alive.
For neither does the Father judge anyone, but the judgment all he has given to the Son,
that all may honour the Son just as they honour the Father. The one not honouring the Son does not honour the Father the one having sent him.
Amen amen I say to you that the one the word of me hearing and trusting the one having sent me has life eternal, and into judgment does not come, but has crossed over out of the death into the life.
Amen amen I say to you that comes an hour and now is when the dead ones will hear the voice of the Son of God and the ones having heard will live.
For just as the Father has life in himself, thus also to the Son he gave life to have in himself.
And authority he gave to him and judgment to do, because son of man he is.
Do not marvel at this, because comes an hour in which all the ones in the tombs will hear the voice of him
and will come out, the ones the good things having done into a resurrection of life, the ones now the worthless things having practised into a resurrection of judgment.
Cannot I do from myself not one thing; just as I hear I judge, and the judgment the mine just is, because I do not seek the will the mine but the will of the one having sent me.
If I witness concerning myself, the witness of me is not true.
Another is the one witnessing concerning me, and I know that true is the witness which he witnesses concerning me.
You have sent toward John, and he has witnessed to the truth.
But I not from a human the witness receive, but these things I say that you may be saved.
That one was the lamp the one burning and shining, and you willed to exult for an hour in the light of him.
But I have the witness greater than of John; for the works which has given to me the Father that I might complete them, these the works which I do, witness concerning me that the Father me has sent.
And the one having sent me Father, that one has witnessed concerning me. Neither voice of him ever have you heard nor form of him have you seen,
and the word of him you do not have in you remaining, because whom sent that one, in this one you do not trust.
You search the scriptures, because you think in them life eternal to have; and those are the ones witnessing concerning me,
And you do not will to come toward me that life you may have.
Glory from humans I do not receive,
but I have known you, that the love of God you do not have in yourselves.
I have come in the name of the Father of me, and you do not receive me; if another might come in the name the own, that one you will receive.
How can you trust, glory from one another receiving, and the glory the one from the only God you do not seek?
Do not think that I will accuse you toward the Father; there is the one accusing you, Moses, into whom you have hoped.
For if you were trusting Moses, you would be trusting me; for concerning me that one wrote.
But if the of that one writings you do not trust, how the my sayings will you trust?

john_6.t: After these things went away Jesus across the sea of Galilee, of Tiberias.
And was following him a crowd much, because they were beholding of him the signs which he was doing upon the ones being sick.
Went up now into the mountain Jesus and there was sitting with the disciples of him.
And near was the Passover, the feast of the Jews.
Having lifted up therefore the eyes Jesus and having beheld that a much crowd comes toward him, he says toward Philip: From where might we buy loaves that these might eat?
But this he was saying testing him; for he himself knew what he was about to do.
Answered to him Philip: Of two hundred denarii loaves are not sufficient for them that each a little something might receive.
Says to him one out of the disciples of him, Andrew the brother of Simon Peter:
There is a little boy one here who has five loaves of barley and two little fish; but these things what are they for so many?
Said now Jesus: Make the humans recline. And was grass much in the place. Reclined therefore the men the number about five thousand.
Took therefore the loaves Jesus and having given thanks he distributed to the ones reclining, likewise also out of the little fish as much as they were willing.
As now they were filled he says to the disciples of him: Gather together the having-abounded fragments, that not anything might be lost.
They gathered together therefore and filled twelve baskets of fragments out of the five loaves the barley which abounded to the ones having eaten.
The therefore humans having seen what he did a sign were saying that: This one is truly the prophet the one coming into the world.
Jesus therefore having known that they are about to come and to seize him that they might make him king, withdrew again into the mountain he himself alone.
As now evening came to be, went down the disciples of him upon the sea,
and having embarked into the boat they were coming across the sea into Capernaum. And darkness already had come to be and not yet had come toward them Jesus,
and the sea, a wind great blowing, was being roused.
Having rowed therefore about stadia twenty-five or thirty, they behold Jesus walking upon the sea and near the boat becoming, and they were afraid.
But he says to them: I am; do not fear.
They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat, and immediately came to be the boat upon the land into which they were going.

On the next day the crowd the one having stood across the sea saw that a little boat other was not there except one, and that not did go in together with the disciples of him Jesus into the boat but alone the disciples of him went away.
But other little boats came out of Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread, the Lord having given thanks.
When therefore saw the crowd that Jesus is not there nor the disciples of him, they embarked themselves into the little boats and came into Capernaum seeking Jesus.
And having found him across the sea they said to him: Rabbi, when here have you come to be?
Answered to them Jesus and said: Amen amen I say to you, you seek me not because you saw signs but because you ate out of the loaves and were fed full.
Work not for the food the perishing but for the food the remaining into life eternal, which the Son of Man to you will give; for this one the Father sealed, God.
They said therefore toward him: What might we do that we might work the works of God?
Answered Jesus and said to them: This is the work of God, that you might trust into whom sent that one.
They said therefore to him: What therefore do you do a sign that we might see and might trust you? What do you work?
The fathers of us the manna ate in the wilderness, just as it is written: Bread out of the heaven he gave to them to eat.
Said therefore to them Jesus: Amen amen I say to you, not Moses has given to you the bread out of the heaven, but the Father of me gives to you the bread out of the heaven the true.
For the bread of God is the one coming down out of the heaven and life giving to the world.
They said therefore toward him: Lord/Sir, always give to us this the bread.
Said to them Jesus: I am the bread of the life; the one coming toward me shall not hunger, and the one trusting into me shall not thirst ever.
But I said to you that also you have seen me and you do not trust.
All which gives to me the Father toward me will come, and the one coming toward me not at all shall I cast out outside.
Because I have come down from the heaven not that I might do the will the mine but the will of the one having sent me.
And this is the will of the one having sent me Father, that all which he has given to me I should not lose out of it, but I should raise it up on the last day.
For this is the will of the Father of me, that everyone beholding the Son and trusting into him might have life eternal, and will raise up him I on the last day.
Were murmuring therefore the Jews concerning him because he said: I am the bread the one having come down out of the heaven,
and they were saying: Not this one is Jesus the son of Joseph, of whom we know the father and the mother? How now says this one that: Out of the heaven I have come down?
Answered Jesus and said to them: Do not murmur with one another.
No one can come toward me unless the Father the one having sent me might draw him, and I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: And they shall be all taught of God. Everyone the one having heard from beside the Father and having learned comes toward me.
Not that the Father anyone has seen except the one being from beside God, this one has seen the Father.
Amen amen I say to you, the one trusting into me has life eternal.
I am the bread of the life.
The fathers of you ate in the wilderness the manna and they died;
this is the bread the one out of the heaven coming down, that anyone out of it might eat and not die.

I am the bread the living the one out of the heaven having come down; if anyone might eat out of this the bread, he will live into the age. And the bread now which I will give the flesh of me is, for the of the world life.
Were fighting therefore with one another the Jews saying: How can this one give to us the flesh to eat?
Said therefore to them Jesus: Amen amen I say to you, unless you might eat the flesh of the Son of Man and might drink of him the blood, you do not have life in yourselves.
The one gnawing of me the flesh and drinking of me the blood has life eternal, and I will raise up him on the last day.
For the flesh of me true is food, and the blood of me true is drink.
The one gnawing of me the flesh and drinking of me the blood in me remains and I in him.
Just as sent me the living Father and I live on account of the Father, also the one gnawing me, that one also will live on account of me.
This is the bread the one out of heaven having come down, not just as ate the fathers and died; the one gnawing this the bread will live into the age.
These things he said in a synagogue teaching in Capernaum.
Many therefore having heard out of the disciples of him said: Hard is this the word; who can it hear?
Knowing but Jesus in himself that are murmuring concerning this the disciples of him said to them: This you does it scandalise?
If therefore you might behold the Son of Man ascending where he was the former?
The Spirit is the one making alive, the flesh does not profit anything; the sayings which I have spoken to you spirit are and life are.
But there are out of you some who do not trust. For knew from beginning Jesus who are the ones not trusting and who is the one who will hand him over.
And he was saying: On account of this I have said to you that no one can come toward me unless it be having been given to him out of the Father.
Out of this many out of the disciples of him went away into the things behind and no longer with him were walking.
Said therefore Jesus to the twelve: Not also you do you wish to go away?
Answered to him Simon Peter: Lord, toward whom shall we go away? Sayings of life eternal you have,
and we have trusted and have known that you are the Holy One of God.
Answered to them Jesus: Not I you the twelve chose? And out of you one a devil is.
But he was saying the Judas of Simon Iscariot; for this one was about to hand him over, one being out of the twelve.

john_7.t: And after these things was walking Jesus in Galilee; for he was not willing in Judea to walk, because were seeking him the Jews to kill.
And near was the feast of the Jews, the Tabernacling.
Said therefore toward him the brothers of him: Move on from here and go into Judea, that also the disciples of you will behold of you the works which you do;
For no one anything in secret does and seeks himself in openness to be. If these things you do, reveal yourself to the world.
For not even the brothers of him were trusting into him.
Says therefore to them Jesus: The time the mine not yet is present, but the time the yours always is ready.
Cannot the world hate you, me but it hates, because I witness concerning it that the works of it evil are.
You go up into the feast this; I do not go up into this the feast, because the my time not yet has been fulfilled.
These things now having said, he himself remained in Galilee.
As but went up the brothers of him into the feast, then also he himself went up, not openly but as in secret.
The therefore Jews were seeking him in the feast and were saying: Where is that one?
And murmuring concerning him was much in the crowds; some were saying that: Good he is; others but were saying: No, but he deceives the crowd.
No one however openly was speaking concerning him on account of the fear of the Jews.
Already now of the feast being in the middle went up Jesus into the temple and was teaching.
And were marvelling therefore the Jews saying: How this one letters knows not having learned?
Answered therefore to them Jesus and said: The my teaching is not mine but of the one having sent me;
If anyone might will the will of him to do, he will know concerning the teaching, whether out of God it is or I from myself speak.
The one from himself speaking the glory the own seeks; the one but seeking the glory of the one having sent him, this one true is and unrighteousness in him is not.
Not Moses has given to you the law? And no one out of you does the law. Why me do you seek to kill?
Answered the crowd: A demon you have; who you seeks to kill?
Answered Jesus and said to them: One work I did and all you marvel.
On account of this Moses has given to you the circumcision, not that out of the Moses it is but out of the fathers, and on sabbath you circumcise a human.
If circumcision receives a human on sabbath that not might be loosed the law of Moses, with me are you bitter because whole a human healthy I made on sabbath?
Do not judge according to sight, but the righteous judgment judge.
Were saying therefore some out of the Jerusalemites: Not this one is whom they seek to kill?
And see openly he speaks and nothing to him they say. Not perhaps truly knew the rulers that this one is truly the Christ?
But this one we know from where he is; the but Christ whenever he might come, no one knows from where he is.
Cried out therefore in the temple teaching Jesus and saying: Both me you know and you know from where I am; and from myself I have not come, but is true the one having sent me, whom you do not know.
I know him, because from beside him I am and that one me sent.
They were seeking therefore him to seize, and no one laid upon him the hand, because not yet had come the hour of him.
Out of the crowd but many trusted into him and were saying that: The Christ whenever he might come, not more signs will he do than which this one did?
Heard the Pharisees the crowd murmuring concerning him these things, and sent the chief priests and the Pharisees officers that they might seize him.
Said therefore Jesus: Yet a time little with you I am and I go away toward the one having sent me.
You will seek me and you will not find me, and where am I, you cannot come.
Said therefore the Jews toward themselves: Where this one is about to go that we will not find him? Not into the dispersion of the Greeks is he about to go and to teach the Greeks?
What is the word this which he said: You will seek me and you will not find me, and where am I, you cannot come?
On the but last day the great of the feast had stood Jesus and cried out saying: If anyone thirsts, let him come toward me and let him drink.
The one trusting into me, just as said the scripture, rivers out of the belly of him will flow of water living.
This but he said concerning the Spirit which were about to receive the ones having trusted into him; not yet for was Spirit Holy given, because Jesus not yet was glorified.
Out of the crowd therefore having heard the words these were saying that: This one is truly the prophet.
Others were saying: This one is the Christ; the ones but were saying: Not for out of the Galilee the Christ comes?
Not the scripture said that out of the seed of David and from Bethlehem the village where was David comes the Christ?
A division therefore came to be in the crowd on account of him.
Some but were willing out of them to seize him, but no one laid upon him the hands.
Came therefore the officers toward the chief priests and Pharisees, and said to them those: On account of what did you not lead him?
Answered the officers: Never spoke thus a human as this the human.
Answered therefore to them the Pharisees: Not also you have been deceived?
Not anyone out of the rulers trusted into him or out of the Pharisees?
But the crowd this the one not knowing the law accursed are they.
Says Nicodemus toward them, the one having come toward him previously, one being out of them:
Not the law of us judges the human unless it might hear first from beside him and might know what he does?
They answered and said to him: Not also you out of the Galilee are? Search and see that out of the Galilee a prophet is not raised.
[[And went each into the house of him,

john_8.t: But Jesus went to the mountain of the olive trees.
And at dawn again he arrived into the temple, and all the people were coming, and having sat he was teaching them.
And bring the scribes and the Pharisees toward him a woman in adultery having been caught, and having stood her in the middle
they say to him, testing: Teacher, this the woman has been caught in the very act committing adultery;
and in the law to us Moses commanded such ones to be stoned; you therefore what do you say?
But this they were saying testing him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus down having stooped with the finger was writing into the earth, not taking notice.
And as they were persisting asking him, having straightened up he said toward them: The sinless one of you, first upon her let him throw a stone.
And again having stooped down he was writing into the earth.
And they having heard and by the conscience being convicted were going out one by one, having begun from the elders; and he was left alone, Jesus, and the woman being in the middle.
And having straightened up Jesus and no one having beheld except the woman he said to her: Where are they, those accusers of you? No one you condemned?
And she said: No one, Lord/Sir. And said Jesus: Neither I you judge; go, and no longer sin.]]
Again therefore to them spoke Jesus saying: I am the light of the world; the one following me shall not walk in the darkness but will have the light of the life.
Said therefore to him the Pharisees: You concerning yourself witness; the witness of you is not true.
Answered Jesus and said to them: Even if I witness concerning myself, true is the witness of me, because I know from where I came and where I go; you but do not know from where I come or where I go.
You according to the flesh judge; I do not judge anyone.
And if I judge but I, the judgment the mine true is, because alone I am not, but I and the one having sent me Father.
And in the law but the yours it has been written that of two humans the witness true is.
I am the one witnessing concerning myself, and witnesses concerning me the one having sent me Father.
They were saying therefore to him: Where is the father of you? Answered Jesus: Neither me do you know nor the Father of me; if me you had known, also the Father of me would you have known.
These the sayings he spoke in the treasury teaching in the temple; and no one seized him, because not yet had come the hour of him.
He said therefore again to them: I go away, and you will seek me, and in the sin of you you will die; where I go away you cannot come.
Were saying therefore the Jews: Not will he kill himself, because he says: Where I go away you cannot come?
And he was saying to them: You out of the things below are, I out of the things above am; you out of this the world are, I am not out of this the world.
I said therefore to you that you will die in the sins of you; for unless you trust that I am, you will die in the sins of you.
They were saying therefore to him: You, who are you? Said to them Jesus: What from the beginning I also say to you.
Many things I have concerning you to speak and to judge; but the one having sent me true is, and I what I heard from beside him, these things I speak into the world.
They did not know that the Father to them he was speaking.
Said therefore to them Jesus: Whenever you might lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and from myself I do not one thing, but just as taught me the Father, these things I speak.
And the one having sent me with me is; he did not leave me alone, because I the pleasing things to him do always.
These things of him speaking many trusted into him.
Was saying therefore Jesus toward the ones having trusted him Jews: If you might remain in the word the mine, truly disciples of me you are,
and you will know the truth, and the truth will free you.
They answered toward him: Seed of Abraham we are and to no one have we been enslaved ever; how you say that: Free you will become?
Answered to them Jesus: Amen amen I say to you that everyone doing the sin a slave is of the sin.
And the slave does not remain in the house into the age; the son remains into the age.
If therefore the Son you might free, really free you will be.
I know that seed of Abraham you are; but you seek me to kill, because the word the mine does not have room in you.
What I have seen from beside the Father I speak; and you therefore what you heard from beside the father of you do.
They answered and said to him: The father of us Abraham is. Says to them Jesus: If children of Abraham you are, the works of the Abraham you would be doing;
Now but you seek me to kill, a human who the truth to you has spoken which I heard from beside the God; this Abraham did not do.
You do the works of the father of you. They said to him: We out of sexual immorality were not born; one father we have, the God.
Said to them Jesus: If the God father of you was, you would be loving me; for I out of the God went out and have come; for neither from myself have I come, but that one me sent.
On account of what the talk the mine do you not know? Because you cannot hear the word the mine.

You out of the father the devil are, and the desires of the father of you you will to do. That one a man-killer was from beginning and in the truth has not stood, because truth is not in him. Whenever he might speak the lie, out of the own things he speaks, because a liar he is and the father of it.
I but because the truth I say, you do not trust me.
Who out of you convicts me concerning sin? If truth I say, on account of what you do not trust me?
The one being out of the God the sayings of the God hears; on account of this you do not hear, because out of the God you are not.
Answered the Jews and said to him: Not well do we say we that a Samaritan are you and a demon you have?
Answered Jesus: I a demon do not have, but I honour the Father of me, and you dishonour me.
I but do not seek the glory of me; there is the one seeking and judging.
Amen amen I say to you, if anyone the my word might keep, death shall he not behold into the age.
Said to him the Jews: Now we have known that a demon you have. Abraham died and the prophets, and you say: If anyone the word of me might keep, shall he not taste of death into the age.
Not you greater are than the father of us Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Whom yourself do you make?
Answered Jesus: If I might glorify myself, the glory of me nothing is; it is the Father of me the one glorifying me, whom you say that God of us he is,
and you have not known him, I but know him. And if I might say that I do not know him, I will be like you a liar; but I know him and the word of him I keep.
Abraham the father of you exulted that he might see the day the mine, and he saw and rejoiced.
Said therefore the Jews toward him: Fifty years not yet do you have, and Abraham have you seen?
Said to them Jesus: Amen amen I say to you, before Abraham to come to be, I am.
They took up therefore stones that they might throw upon him; Jesus but was hidden and went out out of the temple, having passed through the middle of them, and was passing by thus.

john_9.t: And passing by he saw a human blind from birth.
And his disciples asked him saying: Rabbi, who sinned, this one or his parents, that blind he should be born?
Jesus answered: Neither this one sinned nor his parents, but so that the works of God might be made manifest in him.
Us it is necessary to work the works of the one having sent me while day it is; night comes, when no one is able to work.
Whenever in the world I may be, light I am of the world.
These things having said, he spat on the ground and made clay out of the spittle and smeared on him the clay upon the eyes of the blind man.
and said to him: Go, wash into the pool of Siloam — which is interpreted 'Having-been-sent'. He went away therefore and washed and came seeing.
The neighbours therefore and those seeing him formerly, that a beggar he was, were saying: Is not this one the one sitting and begging?
Others were saying, 'This one is he'; others were saying, 'No, but he is like him.' That one was saying, 'I am.'
They were saying therefore to him: How then were opened your eyes?

That one answered and said: The human, the one called Jesus, made clay and smeared of me the eyes and said to me that: Go into the pool of Siloam and wash. Having gone away therefore and having washed, I saw again/looked up.
And they said to him: Where is that one? He says: I do not know.
They lead him to the Pharisees — the once-blind one.
Now it was Sabbath on which day Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
Again therefore were asking him also the Pharisees how he saw again. And he said to them: Clay he put upon my eyes, and I washed, and I see.

Some therefore of the Pharisees were saying: This is not from God, the human, because the Sabbath he does not keep. But others were saying: How is able a human, a sinner, such signs to do? And a split was among them.
They say therefore to the blind man again: What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes? And he said that: A prophet he is.
The Jews did not trust therefore concerning him that he was blind and saw again, until they called the parents of him, of the one having seen again.
and they asked them saying: Is this your son, whom you say that blind he was born? How then does he see now?
His parents therefore answered them and said: We know that this is our son and that blind he was born.
But how now he sees we do not know, or who opened his eyes we do not know; him ask, he himself has the age; he himself concerning himself will speak.
These things his parents said, because they were fearing the Jews; for already the Jews had agreed together that if anyone should confess him Christ, he should become put-out-of-the-synagogue.
On account of this his parents said that: He has the age, question him.
They called therefore the human out of a second time, who was blind, and said to him: Give glory to God; we know that this human a sinner is.
That one therefore answered and said: If a sinner he is I do not know; one thing I know, that being blind, now I see.
They said therefore to him again: What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?
He answered them: I told you already, and you did not hear. Why again do you want to hear? Surely you also do not want his disciples to become?
And they reviled him and said: You are a disciple of that one, but we of Moses are disciples.
We know that to Moses God has spoken, but this one we do not know from where he is.
The human answered and said to them: For in this the marvellous thing is, that you do not know from where he is, and he opened my eyes.
But we know that of sinners God does not hear, but if anyone God-revering may be and his will may do, of this one he hears.
Out of the age it was not heard that anyone opened eyes of one having-been-born blind.
If this one were not from God, he was not able to do nothing.
They answered and said to him: In sins you were born, wholly, and you teach us? And they cast him out, outside.
Jesus heard that they cast him out, outside, and having found him said: Do you trust into the Son of the Human?
That one answered and said: And who is he, Lord/Sir, that I may trust into him?
Jesus said to him: Both you have seen him, and the one speaking with you, that one is.
[And he said: I trust, Lord; and he worshipped/prostrated himself to him.]
And Jesus said: For judgement I into this world came, so that those not seeing may see and those seeing blind may become.
And some of the Pharisees heard these things, those being with him, and said to him: Surely we also are not blind?
Jesus said to them: If blind you were, you would not have sin; but now you say that: We see — your sin therefore remains.

john_10.t: Amen amen I say to you: the one not entering through the door into the courtyard of the sheep but climbing up from elsewhere, that one is a thief and a bandit.
But the one entering through the door is shepherd of the sheep.
To this one the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep of his voice hear, and his own sheep he calls by name and leads them out.
And whenever his own, all of them, he may cast out, before them he goes, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
But a stranger they will certainly not follow but will flee from him, because they do not know of strangers the voice.
This the figure Jesus said to them; but those did not know what things they were which he was speaking to them.
Jesus therefore said again to them: Amen amen I say to you that I am the door of the sheep.
All, as many as came before me, thieves are and bandits; but the sheep did not hear them.
I am the door; through me if anyone should enter, he will be saved and will enter in and will go out and pasture will find.
The thief does not come except so that he may steal and may slaughter/sacrifice and may destroy; I came so that life they may have and abundance they may have.
I am the shepherd, the good one; the shepherd, the good one, his soul/life lays down on behalf of the sheep.
But the hired hand — also not being a shepherd, whose the sheep are not his own — sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them and scatters the sheep.
But the hired hand flees because a hired hand he is and it is not a care to him concerning the sheep.
I am the shepherd, the good one, and I know the ones that are mine, and the ones that are mine know me,
just as knows me the Father and I also know the Father; and my soul/life I lay down on behalf of the sheep.
And other sheep I have, which are not out of this courtyard; and those it is necessary for me to lead, and of my voice they will hear, and they will become one flock, one shepherd.
On account of this me the Father loves, because I lay down my soul/life, so that again I may take it.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down from myself. Authority I have to lay it down, and authority I have again to take it. This the commandment I received from my Father.
A split therefore again came to be among the Jews on account of these words.
And many of them were saying: A demon he has and he is raving; why of him do you hear?
But others were saying: These the words are not of one being demonised; a demon is not able blind people's eyes to open, is it?
There came to be then the Dedication in Jerusalem; and it was winter,
and Jesus was walking about in the temple, in the colonnade of Solomon.
The Jews therefore encircled him and were saying to him: Until when our soul/life do you take away? If you are the Christ, tell us with openness.
Jesus answered them: I told you, and you do not trust. The works which I do in the name of my Father, these witness concerning me;
But you do not trust, because you are not out of the sheep, the ones that are mine, just as I said to you.
The sheep, the ones that are mine, of my voice hear, and I also know them, and they follow me,
and I also give to them life eternal, and they will certainly not perish into the age, and not will anyone snatch them out of my hand.
My Father — what he has given to me — greater than all is, and no one is able to snatch out of the hand of my Father.
I and the Father one thing are.
The Jews carried again stones, so that they might stone him.
Jesus answered them: Many works, good ones, I showed you out of my Father; on account of what kind of work of them me do you stone?
The Jews answered him saying: Concerning a good work we do not stone you but concerning blasphemy, and because you, a human being, make yourself God.
Jesus answered them: Is it not written in your law that: I said, gods you are?
If those he called gods, to whom the Word of God came to be, and the writing is not able to be loosed,
the one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, you say that: You blaspheme, because I said: Son of God I am?
If I do not do the works of my Father, do not trust me;
But if I do, even if me you do not trust, the works trust, so that you may know and may be knowing that in me the Father and I in the Father.
They were seeking therefore him again to arrest; and he went out out of the hand of them.
And he went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was at the first baptising, and he remained there.
And many came to him and were saying that: John indeed did no sign, but all things, as many as John said concerning this one, were true.
And many trusted into him there.

john_11.t: Now there was a certain one being ill, Lazarus from Bethany, out of the village of Mary and Martha her sister.
Now Mary was the one having anointed the Lord with ointment and having wiped off his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was ailing.
The sisters therefore sent to him saying: Lord, see — the one whom you love is ailing.
But having heard, Jesus said: This illness is not toward death but for the sake of the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.
Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
When therefore he heard that he is ailing, then indeed he remained in the place in which he was two days.
Then after this he says to the disciples: Let us go into Judea again.
The disciples say to him: Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and again you are going there?
Jesus answered: Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.
These things he said, and after this he says to them: Lazarus our friend has fallen asleep; but I am going so that I may wake him.
The disciples therefore said to him: Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will be saved.
But Jesus had spoken concerning his death; but those ones supposed that he speaks concerning the repose of sleep.
Then therefore Jesus said to them plainly: Lazarus died.
And I rejoice for your sake, so that you may trust, that I was not there; but let us go to him.
Thomas therefore, the one called Twin, said to the fellow-disciples: Let us go also we, so that we may die with him.
Having come therefore, Jesus found him already having four days in the tomb.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia off.
And many of the Jews had come to those around Martha and Mary so that they might console them concerning their brother.
Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus is coming, met him; but Mary was sitting in the house.
Martha therefore said toward Jesus: Lord, if you were here, my brother would not have died.
But even now I know that as many things as you may ask God, God will give you.
Jesus says to her: Your brother will rise.
Martha says to him: I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.
Jesus said to her: I am the resurrection and the life. The one trusting into me, even if he dies, shall live,
and everyone living and trusting into me shall not by any means die forever. Do you trust this?
She says to him: Yes, Lord. I have trusted that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.
And having said this she went away and called Mary her sister secretly, saying: The teacher is present and calls you.
But that one, when she heard, was raised quickly and was coming to him.
But Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha met him.

The Jews therefore, the ones being with her in the house and consoling her, having seen Mary that she rose quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she is going to the tomb so that she might wail there.
Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was, having seen him, fell of him at the feet, saying to him: Lord, if you were here, my brother would not have died.
Jesus therefore, when he saw her wailing and the Jews having come with her wailing, snorted with indignation in the spirit and troubled himself,
and said: Where have you put him? They say to him: Lord, come and see.
Jesus shed tears.
The Jews therefore were saying: See how he loved him.
But some out of them said: Was this one not able, the one having opened the eyes of the blind man, to do so that this one also might not die?
Jesus therefore, again snorting with indignation in himself, comes to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone was lying upon it.
Jesus says: Lift the stone. The sister of the one having come to his end, Martha, says to him: Lord, already he smells; for he is a fourth-day man.
Jesus says to her: Did I not say to you that if you should trust you will see the glory of God?
They lifted therefore the stone. But Jesus lifted the eyes upward and said: Father, I thank you that you heard me.
But I knew that always you hear me; but on account of the crowd standing around I said it, so that they may trust that you sent me.
And having said these things, with a great voice he cried out: Lazarus, here — outside!
And the one having died came out, bound the feet and the hands with strips, and his face had been bound about with a face-cloth. Jesus says to them: Loose him and let him go.
Many therefore out of the Jews, the ones having come to Mary and having beheld what he did, trusted into him.
But some out of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus did.
The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council and were saying: What are we doing, because this human does many signs?
If we leave him thus, all will trust into him, and the Romans will come and will take away from us both the place and the nation.
But a certain one out of them, Caiaphas, being high priest of that year, said to them: You know nothing,
nor do you reckon that it is advantageous for you that one human die on behalf of the people, and not the whole nation perish.
But this he did not say from himself, but being high priest of that year he prophesied that Jesus was about to die on behalf of the nation,
and not on behalf of the nation only, but so that also the children of God, the ones having been scattered, he might gather together into one.
From that day therefore they took counsel so that they might kill him.
Jesus therefore no longer was walking openly among the Jews, but went away from there into the country near the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there he remained with his disciples.
Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up into Jerusalem out of the country before the Passover so that they might purify themselves.
They were seeking Jesus therefore and were saying with one another, standing in the temple: What does it seem to you? That he will not by any means come to the feast?
But the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone should know where he is, he should report it, so that they might seize him.

john_12.t: Jesus therefore, six days before the Passover, came into Bethany, where Lazarus was, the one having died, whom Jesus raised out of dead ones.
They made therefore for him a supper there, and Martha was serving; but Lazarus was one out of the ones reclining with him.

Mary therefore, having taken a litra of ointment of pistic nard, very costly, anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped off with her hair his feet; and the house was filled out of the smell of the ointment.
But Judas of Simon the Iscariot says, one out of his disciples, the one being about to hand him over:
Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to poor ones?
But he said this not because it mattered to him concerning the poor ones, but because he was a thief and, having the money box, he was carrying/carrying off what was put in.
Jesus said therefore: Leave her, so that for the day of my burial-preparation she may keep it.
For the poor ones you have always with yourselves, but me you do not always have.
The great crowd out of the Jews knew therefore that he is there, and they came not on account of Jesus only but so that also they might see Lazarus, whom he raised out of dead ones.
But the chief priests took counsel so that they might kill Lazarus also,
because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and were trusting into Jesus.
On the next day the great crowd, the one having come to the feast, having heard that Jesus is coming into Jerusalem,
took the palm-branches of the palm trees and went out to a meeting with him and were crying out: Hosanna, blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord, and the King of Israel.
But Jesus, having found a little donkey, sat upon it, just as it is written:
Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your king comes, sitting upon a colt of a donkey.
But these things his disciples did not know at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written concerning him and these things they did to him.
The crowd therefore was witnessing, the one being with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him out of dead ones.
On account of this also the crowd met him, because they heard that he had done this sign.
The Pharisees therefore said toward themselves: Do you see that you gain nothing? Behold, the world whole has gone away after him.
Now there were certain Greeks out of the ones going up so that they might worship at the feast.
These therefore came to Philip, the one from Bethsaida of Galilee, and were asking him, saying: Sir, we wish to see Jesus.
Philip comes and says to Andrew; Andrew comes and Philip, and they say to Jesus.
But Jesus answers them saying: The hour has come so that the Son of Man may be glorified.
Amen amen I say to you: unless the grain of the wheat, having fallen into the earth, dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
The one loving his soul/life destroys it, and the one hating his soul/life in this world will guard it into life eternal.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also my servant will be. And if anyone serves me, the Father will honour him.
Now my soul/life has been troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me out of this hour? But on account of this I came into this hour.
Father, glorify your name. There came therefore a voice out of heaven: I both glorified and again will glorify.
The crowd therefore, the one standing and having heard, was saying thunder to have happened. Others were saying: A messenger/angel has spoken to him.
Jesus answered and said: Not on account of me has this voice happened but on account of you.
Now is judgement of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast outside.
And I, if I am lifted up/exalted out of the earth, will drag all to myself.
But this he was saying signifying by what kind of death he was about to die.
The crowd therefore answered him: We heard out of the law that the Christ remains forever, and how do you say that it is necessary for the Son of Man to be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?

Jesus said therefore to them: Yet a little time the light is in/among you. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness may not overtake/grasp you; and the one walking in the darkness does not know where he goes.
While you have the light, trust into the light, so that sons of light you may become. These things Jesus spoke, and having gone away he was hidden from them.
But so many signs of his having been done before them, they were not trusting into him,
so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled which he said: Lord, who trusted our hearing? And the arm of the Lord, to whom was it revealed?
On account of this they were not able to trust, because again Isaiah said:
He has blinded of them the eyes and hardened of them the heart, so that they might not see with the eyes and understand with the heart and turn, and I will heal them.
These things Isaiah said because he saw his glory, and he spoke concerning him.
Nevertheless however even out of the rulers many trusted into him, but on account of the Pharisees they were not confessing, so that they might not become put-out-of-the-synagogue.
For they loved the glory of the humans more than the glory of God.
But Jesus cried out and said: The one trusting into me does not trust into me but into the one having sent me,
and the one beholding me beholds the one having sent me.
I, a light, have come into the world, so that everyone trusting into me may not remain in the darkness.
And if anyone hears my sayings and does not guard them, I do not judge him; for I did not come so that I might judge the world but so that I might save the world.
The one setting me aside and not receiving my sayings has the one judging him: the word which I spoke, that one will judge him on the last day.
Because I out of myself did not speak, but the Father who sent me, he himself has given me a commandment what I should say and what I should speak.
And I know that his commandment is life eternal. What things therefore I speak, just as the Father has said to me, thus I speak.

john_13.t: Now before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, having known that his hour had come that he should cross over out of this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, to the end he loved them.
And supper coming to be, the devil having already thrown into the heart that Judas of Simon Iscariot should hand him over,
Jesus, having known that the Father had given all things to him into the hands, and that from God he came out and to God he is going,
He rises from the supper and lays aside the garments, and having taken a towel he girded himself.
Then he throws water into the basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples and to wipe them with the towel with which he had been girded.
He comes then to Simon Peter; and that one says to him: Lord, you — my feet you wash?
Jesus answered and said to him: What I am doing, you do not know now, but you will know after these things.
Peter says to him: You shall never wash my feet, into the age. Jesus answered him: Unless I wash you, you have no part with me.
Simon Peter says to him: Lord, not my feet only but also the hands and the head.
Jesus says to him: The one having been bathed has no need except to wash the feet, but is wholly clean; and you are clean, but not all.
For he had known the one handing him over; on account of this he said that 'Not all of you are clean.'
When therefore he had washed their feet and taken his garments and reclined again, he said to them: Do you know what I have done to you?
You call me 'The Teacher' and 'The Lord', and you speak well, for I am.
If then I washed your feet, the Lord and the Teacher, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
For an example I gave to you, so that just as I did to you, you also should do.
Amen amen I say to you, a slave is not greater than his lord, nor is one sent greater than the one having sent him.
If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
Not concerning all of you do I speak; I know which ones I chose; but so that the scripture may be fulfilled: 'The one gnawing my bread lifted up against me his heel.'
From now I tell you before it comes to be, so that you may trust when it comes to be that I am.
Amen amen I say to you, the one receiving whomever I may send receives me; and the one receiving me receives the one having sent me.
These things having said, Jesus was troubled in the spirit and witnessed and said: Amen amen I say to you that one of you will hand me over.
The disciples then were looking at one another, being at a loss concerning whom he speaks.
Now there was reclining one of his disciples in the bosom of Jesus, whom Jesus loved.
Simon Peter therefore nods to this one and says to him to inquire who it might be concerning whom he speaks.
That one, having leaned back just so upon the chest of Jesus, says to him: Lord, who is it?
Jesus therefore answers: That one it is for whom I shall dip the morsel and give it to him. Having dipped therefore the morsel, he takes and gives it to Judas of Simon Iscariot.
And after the morsel, then Satan entered into that one. Jesus therefore says to him: What you are doing, do more quickly.
But this no one of those reclining knew, for what he said it to him.
For some were supposing, since Judas had the money-box, that Jesus says to him: Buy what things we have need of for the feast, or that he should give something to the poor.
Having taken therefore the morsel, that one went out immediately; and it was night.
When therefore he had gone out, Jesus says: Now was glorified the Son of Man, and God was glorified in him.
[If God was glorified in him,] God also will glorify him in himself, and immediately he will glorify him.
Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You will seek me, and just as I said to the Jews, 'Where I go, you are not able to come', I say also to you now.
A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; just as I loved you, that you also love one another.
By this all will know that to me disciples you are, if you have love among one another.
Simon Peter says to him: Lord, where are you going? Jesus answered him: Where I go you are not able to follow me now, but you will follow later.
Peter says to him: Lord, why am I not able to follow you now? My life/soul I will lay down for you.
Jesus answers him: Your life/soul for me you will lay down? Amen amen I say to you, a cock will certainly not crow until you deny me three times.

john_14.t: Let not be troubled your heart; trust into God, and into me trust.
In the house of my Father there are many remaining-places; and if not, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you?
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will take you along to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.
And where I go you know, and the way you know.
Thomas says to him: Lord, we do not know where you are going; and how are we able to know the way?
Jesus says to him: I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
If you have known me, you will know my Father also; and from now you know him and have seen him.
Philip says to him: Lord, show us the Father, and it suffices us.
Jesus says to him: So long a time with you I am, and you have not known me, Philip? The one having seen me has seen the Father; and how do you say: Show us the Father?
Do you not trust that I am in the Father and the Father in me is? The words that I say to you from myself I do not speak; but the Father remaining in me, he does his works.
Trust me that I am in the Father and the Father in me; and if not, on account of the works themselves trust me.
Amen amen I say to you, the one trusting into me, the works that I do that one also will do, and greater than these he will do, because I to my Father go.
And whatever you may ask in my name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.
If you love me, my own commandments you will keep.
And I will ask the Father, and another one called alongside he will give to you, so that with you into the age he may be —
the Spirit of the truth, which the world is not able to receive, because it neither beholds it nor knows it; but you know it, because alongside you it remains and in you it will be.
I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.
Yet a little while and the world no longer beholds me, but you behold me; because I live, you also will live.
In that day you will know, you, that I am in my Father and you in me and I in you.
The one having my commandments and keeping them, that one is the one loving me; and the one loving me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will manifest myself to him.
Judas says to him — not the Iscariot: Lord, and what has come to be that to us you are about to manifest yourself and not to the world?
Jesus answered and said to him: If anyone loves me, my word he will keep, and my Father will love him, and to him we will come and a remaining-place alongside him we will make.
The one not loving me does not keep my words; and the word that you hear is not mine but of the Father who sent me.
These things I have spoken to you while remaining alongside you.
But the one called alongside, the Holy Spirit whom the Father will send in my name, that one will teach you all things and will remind you of all things that I said to you.
Peace I leave to you, peace that is mine I give to you; not just as the world gives do I give to you. Let not be troubled your heart, nor let it be afraid.
You heard that I said to you: I go away and I am coming to you. If you loved me, you would have rejoiced that I said, I go to the Father, because the Father greater than me is.
And now I have told you before it comes to be, so that when it comes to be, you may trust.
No longer will I speak many things with you; for the ruler of this world is coming, and in me he has nothing.
but so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father commanded me, so I do. Rise up, let us go from here.

john_15.t: I am the vine, the true one, and my Father is the farmer.
Every branch in me not bearing fruit, he takes it away, and every one bearing the fruit, he cleans it so that it may bear more fruit.
Already you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.
Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch is not able to bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither you unless in me you remain.
I am the vine, you the branches. The one remaining in me and I in him, this one bears much fruit; because apart from me you are able to do nothing.
If anyone does not remain in me, he was thrown outside like the branch and was dried up, and they gather them and into the fire they throw, and it burns.
If you remain in me and my words in you remain, whatever you wish, ask, and it will come to be for you.
In this was my Father glorified, that you bear much fruit and become disciples to me.
Just as the Father loved me, I also loved you; remain in the love that is mine.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I the commandments of my Father have kept and remain in his love.
These things I have spoken to you so that the joy that is mine may be in you and your joy may be filled full.
This is the commandment that is mine, that you love one another just as I loved you.
Greater than this love no one has, that someone should lay down his life/soul for his friends.
You are friends of mine if you do what things I command you.
No longer do I call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his lord is doing; but you I have called friends, because all things that I heard from my Father I made known to you.
Not you chose me, but I chose you and placed you so that you should go and bear fruit, and your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give to you.
These things I command you, that you love one another.
If the world hates you, you know that me it has hated before you.
If out of the world you were, the world would love its own; but because out of the world you are not, but I chose you out of the world, on account of this the world hates you.
Remember the word that I said to you: a slave is not greater than his lord. If they persecuted me, you also they will persecute; if my word they kept, yours also they will keep.
But all these things they will do to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one having sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, sin they would not have; but now excuse they have not concerning their sin.
The one hating me hates my Father also.
If the works I had not done among them that no one else did, sin they would not have; but now they have both seen and have hated both me and my Father.
But so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: 'They hated me as a gift / without cause.'
But when the one called alongside comes, whom I will send to you from alongside the Father, the Spirit of the truth who goes out from alongside the Father, that one will witness concerning me.
And you also witness, because from the beginning with me you are.

john_16.t: These things I have spoken to you, so that you may not be made to stumble.
Put-out-of-the-synagogue they will make you; but an hour is coming so that everyone having killed you will suppose to be offering service to God.
And these things they will do to you, because they knew not the Father nor me.

But these things I have spoken to you, so that whenever their hour comes, you may remember them — that I myself said them to you. But these things to you from the beginning I said not, because with you I was.
But now I go away to the one having sent me, and no one out of you asks me, 'Where do you go away?'
But because these things I have spoken to you, the grief has filled your heart.
But I the truth say to you: it is to your advantage that I go away. For if I do not go away, the one called alongside will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
And having come, that one will convict/expose the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment.
Concerning sin on the one hand, because they trust not into me.
And concerning righteousness, because to the Father of mine I go away, and no longer do you behold me.
And concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
Still many things I have to say to you, but you are not able to bear them just now.

But whenever that one comes, the Spirit of the truth, he will guide you in the truth, all of it. For he will not speak from himself, but as much as he will hear he will speak, and the things coming he will announce to you.
That one will glorify me, because out of that which is mine he will receive and will announce to you.
All things, as many as the Father has, mine are. Because of this I said that out of that which is mine he receives and will announce to you.
A little, and no longer do you behold me; and again a little, and you will see me, because I go away to the Father.

Some therefore out of his disciples said to one another, 'What is this that he says to us: a little, and you do not behold me, and again a little, and you will see me? and: because I go away to the Father?'
They were saying therefore, 'What is this that he says, the "a little"? We have not known what he speaks.'

Jesus knew therefore that they were wanting to ask him, and he said to them, 'Concerning this you seek with one another, that I said: a little, and you do not behold me, and again a little, and you will see me?'
Amen amen I say to you that you yourselves will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you yourselves will be grieved, but your grief into joy will come to be.

The woman, whenever she gives birth, grief has, because her hour came; but whenever she has borne the child, no longer does she remember the affliction, because of the joy that a human was born into the world.
And you therefore now on the one hand grief have, but again I will see you and your heart will rejoice, and your joy no one takes from you.
