And in that day me you will ask nothing. Amen amen I say to you, whatever you may request of the Father in my name he will give to you.
Until just now you have requested nothing in my name; request, and you will receive, so that your joy may be having been filled full.
These things in veiled sayings I have spoken to you; an hour is coming when no longer in veiled sayings will I speak to you, but with openness concerning the Father I will report to you.
In that day in my name you will request; and I do not say to you that I myself will ask the Father concerning you;
for he himself, the Father, loves you, because you yourselves have loved me and have trusted that I from alongside God came out.
I came out from alongside the Father and have come into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father.
His disciples say to him, 'See, now with openness you speak and not one veiled saying do you say.'
Now we have known that you have known all things and have no need that anyone should ask you. In this we trust that from God you came out.
Jesus answered them, 'Just now you trust?'
Behold, an hour is coming and has now come that you may be scattered each to his own things, and me alone you may leave; and I am not alone, because the Father with me is.
These things I have spoken to you so that in me peace you may have. In the world affliction you have; but take courage, I myself have conquered the world.

john_17.t: These things Jesus spoke, and having lifted his eyes to the heaven he said: 'Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, so that the Son of yours may glorify you,
just as you gave to him authority of all flesh, so that all that you have given to him, he might give to them life eternal.
And this is the eternal life, that they may be knowing you, the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
I glorified you upon the earth, the work having completed which you have given to me so that I might do it.
and now glorify me, you yourself, Father, alongside yourself with the glory which I was having before the world was, alongside you.
I made manifest your name to the humans whom you gave me out of the world. Yours they were and to me them you gave, and your word they have kept.
Now they have known that all things, as many as you have given me, from alongside you are;
because the utterances which you gave to me I have given to them, and they themselves received and knew truly that from alongside you I came out, and they trusted that you sent me.
I myself concerning them ask; not concerning the world do I ask, but concerning those whom you have given me, because yours they are;
and the things mine all are yours and the things yours mine; and I have been glorified in them.
and no longer am I in the world, and they themselves are in the world, and I to you come. Holy Father, keep them in your name which you have given to me, so that they may be one just as we also.

When I was with them in the world, I myself was keeping them in your name which you have given to me, and I guarded, and not one out of them perished except the son of the destruction, so that the writing might be fulfilled.
But now to you I come, and these things I speak in the world, so that they may have the joy, the mine, having been filled full in themselves.
I myself have given to them your word, and the world hated them, because they are not out of the world just as I am not out of the world.
I do not ask that you take them out of the world but that you keep them out of the evil one.
Out of the world they are not, just as I am not out of the world.
Make them holy in your truth; the word, the one that is yours, is truth.
Just as me you sent into the world, I also sent them into the world.
And on behalf of them I myself make myself holy, so that they also may be having been made holy in truth.
Not concerning these do I ask only, but also concerning those trusting through their word into me;
so that all may be one, just as you, Father, in me and I in you, so that they also in us one may be; so that the world may trust that you sent me.
And I, the glory which you have given to me, I have given to them, so that they may be one just as we are one;
I in them and you in me, so that they may be having been completed into one, and so that the world may be knowing that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.

Father, that which you have given me — I want that where I am, I myself, those also may be with me, so that they may behold the glory, the mine, which you have given to me, because you loved me before the founding of the world.
Righteous Father, and the world knew you not, but I myself knew you, and these knew that you sent me;
And I made known to them your name and I will make known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.

john_18.t: These things having said, Jesus went out with his disciples across the winter-torrent of the Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he entered, he and his disciples.
And Judas also, the one handing him over, had known the place, because often Jesus was gathered there with his disciples.
Judas therefore, having taken the cohort and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
Jesus therefore, knowing all the things coming upon him, went out and says to them: Whom do you seek?
They answered him: Jesus the Nazorean. Jesus says to them: I am. And Judas also, the one handing him over, had been standing with them.
When therefore he said to them that: I am, they went away to the rear and fell to the ground.
Again therefore he asked them: Whom do you seek? And they said: Jesus the Nazorean.
Jesus answered: I told you that I am. If therefore me you seek, let these go.
so that the word might be fulfilled which he said that: Those whom you have given me, I lost not one of them.
Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear-lobe. And the name to the slave was Malchus.
Jesus therefore said to Peter: Throw the sword of you into the sheath. The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not by any means drink it?
The cohort therefore and the tribune and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him
and led him to Annas first; for he was father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest of that year.
And Caiaphas was the one having counselled the Jews that it is expedient for one human to die on behalf of the people.
And Simon Peter was following Jesus, and the other disciple. And that disciple was known to the high priest and entered together with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
But Peter had been standing at the door outside. The other disciple therefore, the one known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Peter in.
The servant girl, the doorkeeper, says therefore to Peter: You are not also from the disciples of this human, are you? That one says: I am not.
And the slaves and the officers had been standing, having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. And Peter also was with them standing and warming himself.
The high priest therefore questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Jesus answered him: I openly have spoken to the world. I always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews come together, and in secret I spoke nothing.
Why do you question me? Question those having heard what I spoke to them. Look, these know the things which I said.
And when he had said these things, one of the officers standing by gave a blow to Jesus, having said: Do you answer the high priest like this?
Jesus answered him: If badly I spoke, witness concerning the bad; but if well, why do you flay me?
Annas therefore sent him, having been bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
And Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore to him: You are not also from his disciples, are you? That one denied therefore and said: I am not.
One of the slaves of the high priest, being a relative of the one whose ear Peter cut off, says: Did I not see you in the garden with him?
Again therefore Peter denied, and immediately a rooster crowed.

They lead Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the praetorium; and it was early. And they themselves did not enter into the praetorium, so that they might not be defiled but that they might eat the Passover.
Pilate therefore went outside out to them and says: What accusation do you bring against this human?
They answered and said to him: If this one were not doing evil, we would not have handed him over to you.
Pilate therefore said to them: Take him yourselves and according to the law of you judge him. The Jews therefore said to him: For us it is not permitted to kill anyone.
so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he said, signifying by what kind of death he was about to die.
Pilate therefore entered again into the praetorium and called Jesus and said to him: You are the king of the Jews?
Jesus answered him: From yourself do you say this, or did others tell you about me?
Pilate answered: I am not a Jew, am I? The nation, the one of you, and the chief priests handed you over to me. What did you do?

Jesus answered: The kingdom, the one that is mine, is not out of this world. If out of this world the kingdom that is mine were, the officers, the ones that are mine, would be contending so that I might not be handed over to the Jews; but now the kingdom that is mine is not from here.

Pilate therefore said to him: So then a king you are? Jesus answered: You say that a king I am. I for this have been born and for this I have come into the world, that I might witness to the truth. Everyone who is out of the truth hears my voice.
Pilate says to him: What is truth? And this having said, again he went out to the Jews and says to them: I find not one charge in him.
But there is a custom for you that one I release to you at the Passover; do you wish therefore that I release to you the king of the Jews?
They shouted therefore again, all of them, saying: Not this one but Barabbas. And Barabbas was a bandit.

john_19.t: Then therefore Pilate took Jesus and flogged.
And the soldiers, having plaited a wreath out of thorns, placed it on his head, and a purple garment they threw around him
and they were coming to him and were saying: Hail, the king of the Jews. And they were giving him blows.
And Pilate went out again outside and says to them: Look, I bring him to you outside, so that you may know that not one charge do I find in him.
Jesus therefore came outside, wearing the thorny wreath and the purple garment. And he says to them: Look — the human.
When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out saying: Crucify, crucify him. Pilate says to them: Take him yourselves and crucify; for I do not find in him a charge.
The Jews answered him: We have a law, and according to the law of us he ought to die, because Son of God himself he made.
When therefore Pilate heard this word, he was the more afraid
and he entered into the praetorium again and says to Jesus: From where are you? But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate says therefore to him: To me you do not speak? Do you not know that authority I have to release you and authority I have to crucify you?
Jesus answered him: You would not be having authority against me, not any, if it were not given to you from above; because of this, the one having handed me over to you has greater sin.
Out of this Pilate was seeking to release him. But the Jews cried out saying: If this one you release, you are not a friend of Caesar. Everyone making himself a king speaks against Caesar.
Pilate therefore, having heard these words, led Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called Stone-Pavement, and in Hebrew Gabbatha.
And it was Preparation of the Passover, the hour was about the sixth. And he says to the Jews: Look, the king of you.
Those ones therefore cried out: Take away, take away, crucify him. Pilate says to them: The king of you shall I crucify? The chief priests answered: We have no king except Caesar.
Then therefore he handed him over to them so that he might be crucified. They took over Jesus therefore and led him away.
and bearing for himself the cross he went out to the place called Skull-place, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha,
where they crucified him, and with him others two, on this side and on that side, and in the middle Jesus.
And Pilate wrote also a title and put it on the cross. And it was written: Jesus the Nazorean the king of the Jews.
This title therefore many of the Jews read, because near was the place of the city where Jesus was crucified; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, in Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews said therefore to Pilate: Do not write, The king of the Jews, but that that one said, King I am of the Jews.
Pilate answered: What I have written, I have written.

The soldiers therefore, when they crucified Jesus, took the garments of him and made four parts, to each soldier a part, and the tunic. And the tunic was seamless, out of the upper parts woven through the whole.

They said therefore to one another: Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots concerning it, whose it shall be; so that the scripture might be fulfilled, the one saying: They divided my garments among themselves and upon my clothing they cast a lot. The soldiers indeed therefore did these things,
And there had been standing beside the cross of Jesus the mother of him and the sister of the mother of him, Mary the one of Clopas and Mary the Magdalene.
Jesus therefore, having seen the mother and the disciple standing by whom he loved, says to the mother of him: Woman, look, your son.
Then he says to the disciple: Look, your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her into his own things.
After this, Jesus knowing that already all things have been completed, so that the scripture might be brought to completion, says: I thirst.
A vessel was lying there full of sour wine. Having therefore put around hyssop a sponge full of the sour wine, they brought it to the mouth of him.
When therefore he took the sour wine, Jesus said: It has been completed. And having bowed the head he handed over the spirit/Spirit.

The Jews therefore, since it was Preparation, so that the bodies might not remain on the cross on the sabbath — for great was the day of that sabbath — asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and they might be taken away.
The soldiers therefore came and of the first broke the legs and of the other, the one crucified with him.
But having come upon Jesus, when they saw him already having died, they did not break his legs.
but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and immediately came out blood and water.
And the one having seen has witnessed, and true is his witness, and that one knows that he speaks true things, so that you also may trust.
For these things came to be so that the scripture might be fulfilled: A bone of him shall not be crushed.
And again another scripture says: They shall look on the one whom they pierced through.

And after these things Joseph, the one from Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus but having been hidden because of the fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus. And Pilate permitted. He came therefore and took away his body.
And Nicodemus also came, the one having come to him by night at the first, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred litrai.
They took therefore the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, just as it is custom for the Jews to bury.
And there was in the place where he was crucified a garden, and in the garden a tomb, new, in which not yet no one had been laid.
There therefore, because of the Preparation of the Jews, since the tomb was near, they laid Jesus.

john_20.t: And on the one of the sabbaths Mary the Magdalene comes early, darkness still being, into the tomb and sees the stone having been taken away out of the tomb.

She runs therefore and comes toward Simon Peter and toward the other disciple whom Jesus was befriending, and says to them: They took the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they placed him.
Went out therefore Peter and the other disciple and were coming into the tomb.
And were running the two together; and the other disciple ran ahead more quickly than Peter and came first into the tomb.
And having stooped to look he sees lying the linen cloths, not however did he enter.
Comes therefore also Simon Peter following him and he entered into the tomb, and he beholds the linen cloths lying,
and the face-cloth which was upon the head of him, not with the linen cloths lying but apart having been wrapped up into one place.
Then therefore entered also the other disciple the one having come first into the tomb, and he saw and he trusted.
For not yet did they know the scripture that it is necessary for him out of dead ones to rise.
They went away therefore again toward themselves the disciples.
But Mary had stood toward the tomb outside weeping. As therefore she was weeping, she stooped to look into the tomb,
and she beholds two angels in white ones sitting, one toward the head and one toward the feet, where was lying the body of Jesus.
And they say to her, those ones: Woman, why do you weep? She says to them: Because they took the Lord of me, and I do not know where they placed him.
These things having said she turned into the things behind and beholds Jesus standing, and she did not know that Jesus it is.

Says to her Jesus: Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek? That one supposing that the gardener he is says to him: Lord/Sir, if you carried him, tell me where you placed him, and I him will take away.
Says to her Jesus: Mariam. Having turned that one says to him in Hebrew: Rabbouni — which is said, Teacher.

Says to her Jesus: Do not touch me, for not yet have I ascended toward the Father; but go toward the brothers of me and say to them: I ascend toward the Father of me and Father of you and God of me and God of you.
Comes Mariam the Magdalene announcing to the disciples that: I have seen the Lord, and these things he said to her.

Evening therefore being on that the day, the one of the sabbaths, and the doors having been shut where were the disciples gathered on account of the fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood into the middle and says to them: Peace to you.
And this having said he showed both the hands and the side to them. Rejoiced therefore the disciples having seen the Lord.
Said therefore to them Jesus again: Peace to you; just as has sent me the Father, I also send you.
And this having said he breathed in and says to them: Receive Spirit Holy.
If of any you might release the sins, they have been released to them; if of any you might hold fast, they have been held fast.
Thomas but one out of the twelve, the one called Twin, was not with them when came Jesus.

Were saying therefore to him the other disciples: We have seen the Lord. But he said to them: Unless I might see in the hands of him the mark of the nails and might thrust the finger of me into the mark of the nails and might thrust of me the hand into the side of him, not at all will I trust.
And after days eight again were inside the disciples of him and Thomas with them. Comes Jesus, the doors having been shut, and stood into the middle and said: Peace to you.
Then he says to the Thomas: Bring the finger of you here and see the hands of me, and bring the hand of you and thrust into the side of me, and do not become unbelieving but believing.
And answered Thomas and said to him: The Lord of me and the God of me.
Says to him Jesus: Because you have seen me you have trusted; blessed the ones not having seen and having trusted.
Many indeed therefore also other signs did Jesus before the disciples of him which are not having been written in this book.
These but have been written that you might trust that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, and that trusting life you might have in the name of him.

john_21.t: After these things revealed himself again Jesus to the disciples upon the sea of Tiberias; he revealed but thus.
Were together Simon Peter and Thomas the one called Twin and Nathanael the one from Cana of Galilee and the ones of Zebedee and others out of the disciples of him two.
Says to them Simon Peter: I go away to fish. They say to him: We come also we with you. They went out and embarked into the boat, and in that the night they caught not one thing.
And morning already having come to be stood Jesus upon the shore; not however did the disciples know that Jesus it is.
Says therefore to them Jesus: Little children, not anything to eat with do you have? They answered to him: No.
But he said to them: Cast into the right parts of the boat the net, and you will find. They cast therefore, and no longer it to draw were they strong from the multitude of the fishes.

Says therefore the disciple that one whom Jesus was loving to Peter: The Lord it is. Simon therefore Peter having heard that the Lord it is, the outer garment girded around, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea.
The but other disciples in the little boat came, for not were they far from the land but about from cubits two hundred, dragging the net of the fishes.
As therefore they went out upon the land they see a charcoal fire lying and small fish lying upon and bread.
Says to them Jesus: Bring from the small fish which you caught now.
Went up therefore Simon Peter and drew the net into the land full of fishes great, a hundred fifty three; and so many being, not was torn the net.
Says to them Jesus: Come, breakfast. No one but dared of the disciples to examine him: You, who are you? knowing that the Lord it is.
Comes Jesus and takes the bread and gives to them, and the small fish likewise.
This already third was revealed Jesus to the disciples having been raised out of dead ones.

When therefore they had breakfasted, says to the Simon Peter Jesus: Simon of John, do you love me more than these? He says to him: Yes Lord, you know that I befriend you. He says to him: Feed the lambs of me.
Says to him again a second time: Simon of John, do you love me? He says to him: Yes Lord, you know that I befriend you. He says to him: Shepherd the sheep of me.

He says to him the third time: Simon of John, do you befriend me? Was grieved the Peter because he said to him the third time: Do you befriend me? And he says to him: Lord, all things you know, you know that I befriend you. Says to him Jesus: Feed the sheep of me.

Amen amen I say to you, when you were younger you were girding yourself and were walking where you were willing; whenever but you might grow old, you will stretch out the hands of you, and another you will gird and will carry where you do not will.
This but he said signifying by what death he will glorify God. And this having said he says to him: Follow me.
Having turned the Peter sees the disciple whom Jesus was loving following, who also leaned back in the supper upon the breast of him and said: Lord, who is the one handing you over?
This one therefore having seen the Peter says to Jesus: Lord, this one but what?
Says to him Jesus: If him I will to remain until I come, what toward you? You me follow.

Went out therefore this the word into the brothers that the disciple that one does not die; and not said but to him Jesus that he does not die, but: If him I will to remain until I come, what toward you?
This is the disciple the one witnessing concerning these things and the one having written these things, and we know that true of him the witness is.
There are but also other things many which did Jesus, which if they might be written each one, not even itself I suppose the world to contain the being-written books.

jude_1.t: Jude of Jesus Christ a servant, brother but of James, to the ones in God the Father having been loved and to Jesus Christ having been kept, called:
Mercy to you and peace and love may it be multiplied.
Beloved, all diligence making to write to you concerning the common of us salvation, necessity I had to write to you urging to contend for the once having been handed over to the holy ones trust.

Slipped in for certain humans, the ones long ago having been written before into this the judgement, irreverent, the of the God of us grace transferring into licentiousness and the only Master and Lord of us Jesus Christ denying.
To remind but you I want, knowing you once all things, that Jesus a people out of land of Egypt having saved, the second time the ones not having trusted destroyed.
Angels and the ones not having kept the of themselves rule but having left behind the own dwelling place, for judgement of great day in bonds everlasting under gloom he has kept;

As Sodom and Gomorrah and the around them cities, the like manner to these having committed sexual immorality and having gone away after flesh other, are set forth an example of fire eternal penalty undergoing.
Likewise nevertheless also these dreaming, flesh on the one hand defile, lordship and set aside, glories and blaspheme.
The but Michael the archangel, when with the devil disputing he was arguing concerning the of Moses body, not he dared a judgement to bring on of blasphemy but said: May rebuke you the Lord.
These but as much as on the one hand not they know they blaspheme; as much as and naturally as the unreasoning animals they understand, in these things they are corrupted.
Woe to them, because in the way of Cain they went and in the error of Balaam of pay they were poured out and in the contradiction of Korah they perished.

These are the ones in the love feasts of you reefs, feasting together, fearlessly themselves shepherding; clouds waterless by winds being carried past; trees autumnal fruitless, twice having died, having been uprooted;
Waves wild of sea foaming up the of themselves shames; stars wandering, for whom the gloom of the darkness into age has been kept.
Prophesied but also to these seventh from Adam Enoch saying: Behold came the Lord in holy myriads of him,

To do judgement against all and to convict all the irreverent concerning all the works of irreverence of them which they were irreverent in, and concerning all the harsh things which spoke against him sinners irreverent.
These are grumblers, blamers-of-their-lot, according to the desires of them going, and the mouth of them speaks over-swollen things, marvelling at faces for the sake of advantage.
You but, beloved, remember the words the ones having been spoken before by the apostles of the Lord of us Jesus Christ,
That they were saying to you: upon last of time will be mockers according to the of themselves desires going of the irreverences.
These are the ones making divisions, soulish, spirit not having.
You but, beloved, building up yourselves in the most holy of you trust, in Spirit Holy praying,
Yourselves in love of God keep, awaiting the mercy of the Lord of us Jesus Christ into life eternal.
And whom on the one hand have mercy on, wavering;
Whom but save out of fire snatching, whom but have mercy on in fear, hating also the from the flesh having been stained tunic.
To the one but being able to guard you unstumbling and to set before the glory of him blameless in exultation,
To only God Saviour of us, through Jesus Christ the Lord of us, glory, majesty, might and authority, before all the age and now and into all the ages. Amen.

luke_1.t: Inasmuch as many have set their hand to draw up in order a narrative concerning the matters brought to fullness among us,
just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and became servants of the word handed them down to us,
it seemed good to me also, having followed all things accurately from the first, to write for you in orderly sequence, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you might know fully, concerning the accounts in which you were instructed, the certainty.
It came to pass in the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest by name Zechariah, of the division of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
And both were righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord, blameless.
And there was no child to them, inasmuch as Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.
Now it came to pass, in his serving as priest in the order of his division before God,
according to the custom of the priesthood he obtained by lot to burn incense, having entered into the sanctuary of the Lord;
And all the multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the incense.
And there appeared to him an angel of the Lord standing at the right of the altar of the incense;
And Zechariah was troubled at seeing, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel said to him: Do not fear, Zechariah, because your petition was heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
And there will be joy to you and exultation, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before the Lord, and wine and strong drink he shall never drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
And many of the sons of Israel he will turn to the Lord their God,

and he himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn hearts of fathers to children and disobedient ones in the prudence of righteous ones, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.
And Zechariah said to the angel: By what shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her days.
And answering, the angel said to him: I am Gabriel, the one who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and to announce good news to you of these things.
And behold, you shall be silent and not able to speak until the day these things come to pass, in return for which you did not believe my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season.
And the people were expecting Zechariah, and they were marvelling at his delaying in the sanctuary.
And having come out he was not able to speak to them, and they recognised that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. And he himself was making signs to them, and he remained mute.
And it came to pass, as the days of his service were fulfilled, he went away to his house.
And after these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself five months, saying
that thus the Lord has done to me in days in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among humans.
Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee to which the name was Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man to whom the name was Joseph, of the house of David, and the name of the virgin was Mary.
And having come in to her, the angel said: Rejoice, you who have been graced; the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.
But she, having seen, was greatly troubled at his word, and was reasoning what sort this greeting might be.
And the angel said to her: Do not fear, Mary, for you found favour beside God.
And behold, you will conceive in the womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.
This one will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob into the ages, and of his kingdom there will be no end.
But Mary said to the angel: How shall this be, since I do not know a man?
And answering, the angel said to her: A Holy Spirit will come upon you, and power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore also the one being born holy will be called Son of God.
And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman, she also has conceived a son in her old age, and this month is the sixth for her, the one called barren;
because not a single word will be impossible with God.
But Mary said: Behold the servant of the Lord; may it come to pass to me according to your word. And the angel went away from her.
And having risen up, Mary in these days went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
and she entered into the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
And it came to pass, as Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the babe leapt in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit,
and she cried out with a great cry and said: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
And whence to me this, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For behold, as the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the babe leapt in exultation in my womb.
And blessed is she who trusted that there will be a completion to the things spoken to her from the Lord.
And Mary said: My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit exulted in God my Saviour,
because he looked upon the lowliness of his servant. For behold, from now on all the generations will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One did great things to me, and holy is his name,
and his mercy is to generations and generations to those fearing him.
He did a mighty deed with his arm; he scattered the proud in the thought of their heart;
he pulled down rulers from thrones and raised up lowly ones;
hungering ones he filled with good things, and being-rich ones he sent away empty;
he took hold of Israel his child, to remember mercy,
just as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed, into the age.
And Mary remained with her about three months, and returned to her house.
Now for Elizabeth the time was fulfilled for her to bear, and she bore a son.
And her neighbours and her kinsfolk heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy with her, and they were rejoicing with her.
And it came to pass, on the eighth day they came to circumcise the little child, and they were calling it by the name of his father, Zechariah.
And answering, his mother said: No, but he shall be called John.
And they said to her that no one is out of your kindred who is called by this name.
And they were making signs to his father, the what he might wish it to be called.
And having asked for a writing-tablet, he wrote, saying: John is his name. And they all marvelled.
And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue, and he was speaking, blessing God.
And fear came upon all those dwelling around them, and in the whole hill country of Judea all these words were being talked over,
and all those hearing laid them in their heart, saying: What then will this little child be? For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.
And Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because he visited and made redemption for his people,
and raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his child,
just as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from the age,
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all those hating us,
to do mercy with our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,
an oath which he swore to Abraham our father, to give to us
that without fear, having been delivered out of the hand of our enemies, we might serve him
in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.
And you also, little child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give knowledge of salvation to his people in release of their sins,
through the inward parts of mercy of our God, in which a rising from on high will visit us,
to appear to those sitting in darkness and shadow of death, to direct our feet into a way of peace.
And the little child was growing and being strengthened in spirit, and he was in the deserts until the day of his showing to Israel.

luke_2.t: Now it came to pass in those days, there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus for all the inhabited world to be registered.
This registration first came to pass while Quirinius was governing Syria.
And all were going to be registered, each into his own city.
And Joseph also went up from Galilee out of the city of Nazareth into Judea, into the city of David which is called Bethlehem, because of his being out of the house and family of David,
to register himself with Mary, the one betrothed to him as wife, being pregnant.
Now it came to pass, in their being there, the days were fulfilled for her to bear,
and she bore her son, the firstborn, and wrapped him in swaddling-cloths and laid him down in the manger, because there was not a place for them in the lodging-place.
And there were shepherds in the same country, living in the fields and keeping the watches of the night over their flock.
And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared a great fear.
And the angel said to them: Do not fear; for behold, I announce good news to you of great joy which will be to all the people,
because there was born to you today a Saviour, who is Christ, Lord, in the city of David.
And this is the sign to you: you will find a babe wrapped in swaddling-cloths and lying in a manger.
And suddenly there came to be with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God and saying:
Glory in highest places to God, and upon earth peace among humans of good pleasure.

And it came to pass, as the angels went away from them into heaven, the men, the shepherds, were speaking to one another: Let us go through indeed as far as Bethlehem and let us see this word that has come to pass, which the Lord made known to us.
And they came hurrying and found both Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in the manger.
And having seen, they made known concerning the word spoken to them about this little child.
And all those hearing marvelled concerning the things spoken to them by the shepherds.
But Mary was keeping together all these words, pondering them in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things which they heard and saw, just as it was spoken to them.
And when eight days were fulfilled for circumcising him, his name was also called Jesus, the name called by the angel before his being conceived in the womb.
And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up into Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
just as it has been written in the law of the Lord that every male opening a womb shall be called holy to the Lord,
and to give a sacrifice according to the thing said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtle-doves or two young of pigeons.
And behold, there was a human in Jerusalem to whom the name was Simeon, and this human was righteous and reverent, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and a Holy Spirit was upon him.
And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit not to see death before he should see the Christ of the Lord.
And he came in the Spirit into the temple; and in the parents' bringing in the little child Jesus, for them to do according to the thing customary of the law concerning him,
and he himself received it into his arms and blessed God and said:
Now you release your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace,
because my eyes saw your salvation,
which you prepared before the face of all the peoples,
a light for revelation of nations and glory of your people Israel.
And his father and the mother were marvelling at the things being spoken concerning him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: Behold, this one is set for a falling and a rising of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against,
and of you yourself a sword will go through the soul, so that reasonings out of many hearts may be uncovered.
And there was Anna a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher; she was advanced in many days, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
and she a widow until eighty-four years, who did not depart from the temple, serving with fastings and petitions night and day.
And she at that same hour, having stood by, was confessing to God and was speaking concerning him to all those waiting for redemption in Jerusalem.
And as they completed all the things according to the law of the Lord, they turned back into Galilee into their own city Nazareth.
And the little child was growing and being strengthened, being filled with wisdom, and grace of God was upon him.
And his parents were going every year into Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover.
And when he became twelve years, they going up into Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast,
and having completed the days, in their returning, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and his parents, Joseph and his mother, did not know.
But supposing him to be in the company, they went a day's journey and were seeking him among the kinsfolk and among the acquaintances.
And not having found him, they returned into Jerusalem seeking him.
And it came to pass after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers and hearing them and questioning them.
And all those hearing him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
And having seen him they were struck out, and his mother said to him: Child, why did you do to us thus? Behold, your father and I, being pained, were seeking you.
And he said to them: Why is it that you were seeking me? Did you not know that in the things of my Father I must be?
And they did not understand the word which he spoke to them.
And he went down with them and came into Nazareth and was being subject to them. And his mother was keeping through all these words in her heart.
And Jesus was progressing in the wisdom and stature and grace beside God and humans.

luke_3.t: Now in the fifteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate governing Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother being tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias being tetrarch of Abilene,
in the high-priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, a word of God came upon John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
And he came into all the region around the Jordan proclaiming a baptism of change of mind for release of sins,
as it has been written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet saying: A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight his paths.
Every ravine shall be filled and every mountain and hill shall be brought low, and the crooked things shall be into a straight thing and the rough ways into smooth roads,
and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
Therefore he was saying to the crowds going out to be baptised by him: Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

Therefore make fruits worthy of the change of mind, and do not begin to say in yourselves: We have Abraham as father. For I say to you that God is able out of these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
And already also the axe lies toward the root of the trees; therefore every tree not making good fruit is cut out and thrown into fire.
And the crowds were questioning him saying: What then shall we do?
And answering he was saying to them: The one having two tunics, let him share with the one not having, and the one having foods, let him do likewise.
And tax-farmers also came to be baptised, and they said to him: Teacher, what shall we do?
And he said to them: Exact nothing more beside the thing appointed to you.
And soldiers also were questioning him saying: And we — what shall we do? And he said to them: Extort from no one, nor accuse falsely, and be satisfied with your wages.
Now the people expecting and all reasoning in their hearts concerning John whether perhaps he himself might be the Christ,

John answered, saying to all: I indeed baptise you with water; but there comes the one stronger than me, of whom I am not sufficient to loose the strap of his sandals. He himself will baptise you in Holy Spirit and fire.
Of whom the winnowing-shovel is in his hand, both to cleanse through his threshing-floor and to gather together the wheat into his storehouse; but the chaff he will burn down with unquenchable fire.
Therefore, with many other things also, exhorting, he was announcing good news to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him concerning Herodias the wife of Philip his brother and concerning all the evil things which Herod did,
added also this upon all: and he shut up John in the prison.
Now it came to pass, in all the people being baptised, and Jesus having been baptised and praying, the heaven was opened
and the Holy Spirit came down in bodily form as a dove upon him, and a voice came to be out of heaven saying: You are my Son, the beloved; in you I took delight.
And Jesus himself was beginning, being about thirty years, being a son — as was supposed — of Joseph, of Heli,
of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Jannai, of Joseph,
of Mattathias, of Amos, of Nahum, of Esli, of Naggai,
of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, of Josech, of Joda,
of Joanan, of Rhesa, of Zerubbabel, of Shealtiel, of Neri,
of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
of Joshua, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonam, of Eliakim,
of Melea, of Menna, of Mattatha, of Nathan, of David,
of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Sala, of Nahshon,
of Amminadab, of Admin, of Arni, of Hezron, of Perez, of Judah,
of Jacob, of Isaac, of Abraham, of Terah, of Nahor,
of Serug, of Reu, of Peleg, of Eber, of Shelah,
of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,
of Methuselah, of Enoch, of Jared, of Mahalalel, of Cainan,
of Enosh, of Seth, of Adam, of God.

luke_4.t: And Jesus, full of Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was being led in the Spirit in the wilderness
forty days being tested by the devil. And he ate nothing in those days, and they having been completed, afterward he hungered.
And the devil said to him: If you are Son of God, speak to this stone that it become bread.
And Jesus answered to him saying: It has been written that not on bread alone shall the human live, but on every word of God.
And having led him up, the devil showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in a point of time
and said to him: To you I will give this authority, all of it, and their glory, because to me it has been handed over, and to whomever I wish I give it.
You therefore, if you will bow down before me, it shall all be yours.
And answering, Jesus said to him: Go behind me, Satan; for it has been written: You shall bow down before the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.
And he led him into Jerusalem and stood him upon the wing of the temple and said to him: If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here;
For it has been written that to his angels he will give charge concerning you, to guard you through,
and that upon hands they will lift you, lest ever you strike your foot against a stone.
And answering, Jesus said to him that it has been said: You shall not put to the test the Lord your God.
And having completed every testing, the devil departed from him until a season.
And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and a report went out through the whole region round about concerning him.
And he himself was teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
And he came into Nazara, where he was brought up, and entered according to his custom on the day of the sabbaths into the synagogue, and stood up to read.
And there was given over to him a scroll of the prophet Isaiah, and having unrolled the scroll he found the place where it was written:

A Spirit of the Lord is upon me, on account of which he anointed me to announce good news to poor ones; he has sent me to heal the ones crushed in heart, to proclaim to captives release and to blind ones recovery of sight, to send away the ones broken in release,
to proclaim an acceptable year of the Lord.
And having rolled up the scroll, having given it back to the attendant, he sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were gazing at him.
And he began to say to them that today this writing has been fulfilled in your ears.
And all were witnessing to him and marvelling at the words of grace proceeding out of his mouth, and they were saying: Is this not a son of Joseph?
And he said to them: Doubtless you will say to me this parable: Physician, heal yourself; as many things as we heard happening in Capernaum, do also here in your fatherland.
And he said: Amen I say to you that no prophet is acceptable in his fatherland.
But upon truth I say to you, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up for three years and six months, as a great famine came upon all the land;
and to none of them was Elijah sent except into Zarephath of Sidonia to a woman, a widow.
And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.
And all in the synagogue were filled with rage, hearing these things.
And having risen up, they threw him out outside the city and led him as far as the brow of the mountain upon which their city had been built, so as to throw him down headlong.
But he himself, having gone through the midst of them, was going on.
And he came down into Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the sabbaths.
And they were struck out at his teaching, because his word was in authority.
And in the synagogue there was a human having a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a great voice
saying: Ha, what to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene? Did you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are: the Holy One of God.
And Jesus rebuked it saying: Be muzzled and come out from him. And the demon, having thrown him into the midst, came out from him, having harmed him nothing.
And amazement came upon all, and they were talking together with one another saying: What is this word, that in authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out?
And a sound concerning him was going out into every place of the region round about.
And having risen up from the synagogue he entered into the house of Simon. And the mother-in-law of Simon was being gripped by a great fever, and they asked him concerning her.
And having stood over her he rebuked the fever, and it left her; and immediately having risen up she was serving them.
And the sun setting, all as many as had ones being weak with various diseases led them to him; and he, laying the hands upon each one of them, was healing them.
And demons also were coming out from many, crying out and saying that you are the Son of God. And rebuking them he was not permitting them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.
And day having come, having gone out he went into a desert place; and the crowds were seeking for him and came as far as him and were holding him fast so that he would not go from them.
But he said to them that also to the other cities it is necessary for me to announce the good news of the kingdom of God, because for this I was sent.
And he was proclaiming in the synagogues of Judea.

luke_5.t: Now it came to pass, in the crowd pressing upon him and hearing the word of God, and he himself was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,
and he saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fishermen, having got out from them, were washing the nets.
And having embarked into one of the boats, which was Simon's, he asked him to put out from the land a little; and having sat down, he was teaching the crowds out of the boat.
And as he ceased speaking, he said to Simon: Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.
And answering, Simon said to him: Master, through the whole night having laboured we took nothing; but upon your word I will let down the nets.
And having done this, they enclosed together a great multitude of fishes; and their nets were being torn through.
And they signalled to the partners in the other boat, that having come they should take hold together with them; and they came and filled both the boats so that they were sinking.
And having seen, Simon Peter fell at the knees of Jesus, saying: Go out from me, because I am a sinful man, Lord.
For amazement gripped him and all those with him at the catch of the fishes which they took together,
and likewise also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon: Do not fear; from now on you will be taking humans alive.
And having brought down the boats onto the land, having left all things, they followed him.

And it came to pass, in his being in one of the cities, and behold a man full of leprosy; and having seen Jesus, having fallen upon his face, he begged him saying: Lord, if you are willing, you are able to cleanse me.
And having stretched out the hand he touched him saying: I am willing, be cleansed. And immediately the leprosy went away from him.
And he himself charged him to tell no one, but: Having gone away, show yourself to the priest and offer concerning your cleansing just as Moses appointed, for a witness to them.
But the word concerning him was going through more, and many crowds were coming together to hear and to be healed by him from their weaknesses.
But he himself was withdrawing in the deserts and praying.

And it came to pass on one of the days, and he himself was teaching; and there were sitting Pharisees and law-teachers who were come out of every village of Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem, and power of the Lord was for the healing.
And behold, men carrying upon a pallet a human who had been paralysed, and they were seeking to bring him in and to place him before him.

And not having found by what sort of way they might bring him in on account of the crowd, having gone up upon the roof-terrace, through the tiles they let him down with the little pallet into the midst before Jesus.
And having seen their trust he said to him: Human, your sins have been released to you.
And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who is able to release sins except God alone?
But Jesus, having recognised their reasonings, answering said to them: Why do you reason in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say: Your sins have been released to you, or to say: Rise and walk?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority upon the earth to release sins — he said to the paralysed one: To you I say, rise and having taken up your little pallet go into your house.
And immediately having risen up before them, having taken up that upon which he was lying, he went away into his house glorifying God.
And ecstasy took hold of all, and they were glorifying God and were filled with fear, saying that we saw unexpected things today.
And after these things he went out and beheld a tax-farmer by name Levi sitting at the tax-office, and he said to him: Follow me.
And having left behind all things, having risen up, he was following him.
And Levi made a great reception for him in his house, and there was a great crowd of tax-farmers and others who were reclining with them.
And the Pharisees and their scribes were murmuring to his learners, saying: Why do you eat and drink with the tax-farmers and sinners?
And answering, Jesus said to them: The ones being healthy have no need of a physician, but the ones having badly.
I have not come to call righteous ones but sinners into change of mind.
But they said to him: The learners of John fast frequently and make petitions, likewise also those of the Pharisees; but yours eat and drink.
But Jesus said to them: You are not able to make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them, are you?
But days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days.

And he was telling also a parable to them, that no one, having torn a patch from a new garment, puts it upon an old garment; but if otherwise, he will both tear the new, and the patch from the new will not agree with the old.
And no one throws new wine into old wineskins; but if otherwise, the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it itself will be poured out and the wineskins will be destroyed.
But new wine must be thrown into fresh wineskins.
And no one having drunk old immediately wants new; for he says: The old is good.

luke_6.t: Now it came to pass on a [second-first] sabbath that he was going through the grainfields, and his learners were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing them with the hands.
But some of the Pharisees said: Why do you do what is not permitted to do on the sabbaths?
And answering them, Jesus said: Did you not read even this, what David did when he hungered, he himself and those being with him,
how he entered into the house of God and, having taken the loaves of the presentation, he ate and gave also to those with him, which it is not permitted to eat except the priests alone?
And he was saying to them that the Son of Man is lord also of the sabbath.
Now it came to pass also on another sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught; and there was a human there, and his right hand was withered.
And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching him closely, whether on the sabbath he heals, so that they might find to accuse him.
But he himself knew their reasonings. And he said to the man having the withered hand: Rise and stand into the midst. And having risen up, he stood.
And Jesus said to them: I question you whether it is permitted on the sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a soul or to destroy it.
And having looked round on them all, he said to him: Stretch out your hand. And he did so, and his hand was restored sound as the other.
But they themselves were filled with mindlessness and were talking with one another what they might do to Jesus.
Now it came to pass in these days that he went out into the mountain to pray, and he was spending the whole night through in the prayer of God.
And when day came, he called to himself his learners, and having chosen from them twelve, whom also he named apostles:
Simon whom also he named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John and Philip and Bartholomew,
and Matthew and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon the one called Zealot,
and Judas of James, and Judas Iscariot who also became a betrayer.
And having come down with them, he stood upon a level place, and a great crowd of his learners and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon,
and those being troubled by unclean spirits, and they were being healed.
And all the crowd were seeking to touch him, because power was going out from him and he was healing all.
And he himself, having lifted up his eyes to his learners, was saying: Blessed are the poor, because yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are those hungering now, because you will be fed full. Blessed are those weeping now, because you will laugh.
Blessed are you when humans hate you, and when they separate you off and reproach you and cast out your name as evil on account of the Son of Man.
Rejoice in that day and leap, for behold, your reward is much in heaven; for according to the same things their fathers were doing to the prophets.
But woe to you the rich ones, because you are having in full your consolation.
Woe to you, the ones having been filled full now, because you will hunger. Woe, the ones laughing now, because you will mourn and weep.
Woe when all the humans speak well of you; for according to the same things their fathers were doing to the false prophets.
But to you I say, to those hearing: love your enemies, do well to those hating you,
bless those cursing you, pray concerning those insulting you.
To the one striking you upon the cheek, offer also the other; and from the one taking away your outer garment, do not forbid also the tunic.
And to everyone asking you, give; and from the one taking away the things that are yours, do not demand back.
And just as you wish that humans should do to you, do to them likewise.
And if you love those loving you, what sort of grace is it to you? For even the sinners love those loving them.
For even if you do good to those doing good to you, what sort of grace is it to you? Even the sinners do the same.
And if you lend from those from whom you hope to receive, what sort of grace is it to you? For even sinners lend to sinners so that they may receive back the equal things.
But love your enemies and do good and lend, despairing of nothing; and your reward will be much, and you will be sons of the Most High, because he himself is kind toward the ungrateful and evil.
Become compassionate, just as also your Father is compassionate.
And do not judge, and you shall never be judged; and do not condemn, and you shall never be condemned. Release, and you will be released.

Give, and it will be given to you; a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, overflowing, they will give into your lap; for with the same measure with which you measure, it will be measured back to you.
And he told also a parable to them: A blind one is not able to lead a blind one, is he? Will not both fall into a pit?
A learner is not above his teacher; but everyone having been fully equipped will be as his teacher.
And why do you look at the speck in the eye of your brother, but the beam in your own eye you do not consider?

Or how are you able to say to your brother: Brother, let me cast out the speck in your eye, yourself not looking at the beam in your eye? Hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of your eye, and then you will see through clearly to cast out the speck in the eye of your brother.
For there is not a good tree making rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree making good fruit;
for each tree is known out of its own fruit; for they do not gather figs out of thorns, nor do they harvest a grape-cluster from a bramble.
The good human out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth the good, and the evil human out of the evil brings forth the evil; for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.
And why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do the things which I say?
Everyone coming to me and hearing my words and doing them, I will show you to whom he is like.

He is like a human building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation upon the rock; and a flood having come, the river broke against that house, and it was not strong enough to shake it, because of its having been built well upon the rock.

But the one having heard and not having done is like a human having built a house upon the earth without a foundation, against which the river broke, and immediately it fell together, and the breaking of that house became great.

luke_7.t: When he fulfilled all his words into the ears of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
And a certain centurion's slave, having badly, was about to die, who was valuable to him.
And having heard concerning Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him that having come he might bring safely through his slave.
And they, having come to Jesus, were urging him earnestly, saying that he is worthy to whom you will grant this;
for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us.

And Jesus was going with them. And already, he being not far distant from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him: Lord, do not be troubled, for I am not sufficient that you should come under my roof;
wherefore neither did I count myself worthy to come to you; but say with a word, and let my boy be healed.
For I also am a human being placed under authority, having under myself soldiers, and I say to this one: Go, and he goes; and to another: Come, and he comes; and to my slave: Do this, and he does it.
And having heard these things, Jesus marvelled at him, and having turned to the crowd following him he said: I say to you, not even in Israel did I find such trust.
And those having been sent, having returned into the house, found the slave being healthy.
And it came to pass in the next, he went into a city called Nain, and his learners were going with him, a considerable number, and a great crowd.

And as he drew near to the gate of the city, and behold, one who had died was being carried out, an only-born son to his mother, and she herself was a widow; and a considerable crowd of the city was with her.
And having seen her, the Lord was moved in the guts toward her and said to her: Do not weep.
And having come to it he touched the bier, and those bearing it stood still; and he said: Young man, to you I say, be raised.
And the dead one sat up and began to speak; and he gave him to his mother.
And fear took hold of all, and they were glorifying God, saying that a great prophet was raised up among us, and that God visited his people.
And this word went out in the whole of Judea concerning him, and in all the region round about.
And his learners reported to John concerning all these things. And having summoned two certain of his learners, John
He sent to the Lord, saying: Are you the coming one, or are we to expect another?
And the men, having arrived to him, said: John the Baptist sent us to you saying: Are you the coming one, or are we to expect another?
In that hour he healed many from diseases and scourges and evil spirits, and to many blind ones he granted to see.

And answering he said to them: Having gone, report to John what you saw and heard: blind ones see again, lame ones walk about, lepers are cleansed, and deaf ones hear, dead ones are raised, poor ones have good news announced,
And blessed is whoever is not scandalised in me.
And John's messengers having gone away, he began to say to the crowds concerning John: What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed being shaken by wind?
But what did you go out to see? A human clothed in soft garments? Behold, those in glorious clothing and existing in luxury are in the royal palaces.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more abundant than a prophet.
This is he concerning whom it has been written: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.
For I say to you, among ones born of women no prophet is greater than John; but the lesser one in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
And all the people, having heard, and the tax-farmers, declared God to be just, having been baptised with the baptism of John;
but the Pharisees and the lawyers set aside the counsel of God for themselves, not having been baptised by him.
To what therefore shall I liken the humans of this generation, and to what are they like?
They are like little children sitting in a marketplace and calling to one another, which says: We piped to you and you did not dance; we sang a dirge and you did not weep.
For John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say: He has a demon.
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say: Behold a human, a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax-farmers and sinners.
And wisdom was vindicated from all her children.
And a certain one of the Pharisees was asking him that he might eat with him; and having entered into the house of the Pharisee, he reclined.
And behold, a woman who was in the city, a sinner, and having recognised that he reclines in the house of the Pharisee, having brought an alabaster jar of ointment

and having stood behind beside his feet, weeping, with the tears she began to wet his feet and with the hairs of her head she was wiping them off, and she was kissing his feet fervently and anointing them with the ointment.
And having seen, the Pharisee who called him spoke in himself, saying: This one, if he were the prophet, would know who and what sort the woman is who touches him, that she is a sinner.
And answering, Jesus said to him: Simon, I have something to say to you. And he says: Teacher, speak.
Two debtors were to a certain moneylender; the one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
They not having anything to give back, he freely forgave both. Which therefore of them will love him more?
And answering, Simon said: I take it that it is the one to whom he freely forgave the more. And he said to him: You judged rightly.

And having turned to the woman, he said to Simon: Do you see this woman? I entered into your house; water for my feet you did not give, but she wet my feet with the tears and wiped them off with her hairs.
A kiss you did not give me, but she from when I entered has not left off kissing my feet fervently.
With oil my head you did not anoint, but she anointed my feet with ointment.
For which reason I say to you, her many sins have been released, because she loved much; but to whom little is released, he loves little.
And he said to her: Your sins have been released.
And those reclining together began to say in themselves: Who is this who even releases sins?
And he said to the woman: Your trust has saved you; go into peace.

luke_8.t: And it came to pass in the next, that he himself was journeying through according to city and village, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God, and the twelve with him,
and certain women who had been healed from evil spirits and weaknesses, Mary the one called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna wife of Chuza a steward of Herod, and Susanna, and many others, who were serving them out of the things belonging to them.
And a great crowd coming together, and those from city by city journeying to him, he spoke through a parable:
The one sowing went out to sow his seed; and in his sowing, some fell beside the way and was trodden down, and the birds of the heaven ate it down.
And other fell down upon the rock, and having grown it was dried up because of not having moisture.
And other fell in the midst of the thorns, and the thorns having grown up together choked it off.
And other fell into the good earth, and having grown it made fruit a hundredfold. Saying these things he was calling out: The one having ears to hear, let him hear.
And his learners were questioning him what this parable might be.
And he said: To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; but to the rest in parables, so that seeing they may not see and hearing they may not understand.
And this is the parable: the seed is the word of God.
And those beside the way are those having heard; then comes the devil and takes away the word from their heart, so that they may not, having trusted, be saved.
And those upon the rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, who for a season trust, and in a season of testing they withdraw.
And the thing that fell into the thorns, these are those having heard, and being carried along by anxieties and riches and pleasures of life, they are choked together and do not bear to completion.
And the thing in the good earth, these are those who in a good and noble heart, having heard the word, hold it fast and bear fruit in endurance.
And no one having lit a lamp covers it with a vessel or puts it underneath a bed, but he puts it upon a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.
For there is not a hidden thing which will not become manifest, nor a concealed thing which shall never be known and come into the open.
Look therefore how you hear; for whoever may have, it will be given to him, and whoever may not have, even what he seems to have will be taken away from him.
And his mother and his brothers came to him, and they were not able to meet with him on account of the crowd.
And it was reported to him by ones saying: Your mother and your brothers stand outside wishing to see you.
But he answering said to them: My mother and my brothers are these, the ones hearing the word of God and doing it.
And it came to pass on one of the days, and he himself embarked into a boat, and his learners, and he said to them: Let us go through into the other side of the lake. And they put out to sea.
And they sailing, he fell asleep. And a whirlwind of wind came down into the lake, and they were being filled up and were in danger.

And having come to him they thoroughly roused him, saying: Master, Master, we are perishing. And he having been roused rebuked the wind and the surge of the water, and they ceased, and there came to be a calm.
And he said to them: Where is your trust? And having been afraid they marvelled, saying to one another: Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?
And they sailed down into the country of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.

And to him having come out upon the land, there met him a certain man out of the city having demons; and for a considerable time he did not put on a garment, and in a house he was not remaining but among the tombs.
And having seen Jesus and having cried out, he fell before him and with a great voice said: What to me and to you, Jesus, Son of God the Most High? I beg you, do not torment me.

For he had charged the unclean spirit to come out from the human; for many times it had seized him together, and he was being bound with chains and fetters, being guarded, and breaking through the bonds he was being driven by the demon into the deserts.
And Jesus questioned him saying: What is a name to you? And he said: Legion, because many demons entered into him.
And they were begging him that he would not command them to go away into the abyss.
And there was there a considerable herd of pigs feeding on the mountain; and they begged him that he would permit them to enter into those. And he permitted them.
And the demons having come out from the human entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the cliff into the lake and was drowned.
And those feeding them, having seen the thing that had happened, fled and having gone away reported it into the city and into the fields.

And they went out to see the thing that had happened, and they came to Jesus and found the human from whom the demons had gone out sitting, clothed and being sound-minded, beside the feet of Jesus; and they were afraid.
And those having seen reported to them how the one who had been demonised was saved.

And all the multitude of the region round about of the Gerasenes asked him to go away from them, because they were gripped together with a great fear. And he himself, having embarked into the boat, returned.
And the man from whom the demons had gone out was begging him to be with him. But Jesus released him, saying:
Return to your house and relate through as much as God did for you. And he went away through the whole city proclaiming as much as Jesus did for him.
And it came to pass, in Jesus returning, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all expecting him.
And behold, there came a man to whom the name was Jairus, and this one was existing a ruler of the synagogue; and having fallen beside the feet of Jesus he was begging him to enter into his house,
because an only-born daughter was to him, about twelve years, and she was dying. And in his going, the crowds were choking him.
And a woman being in a flow of blood from twelve years, who having spent her whole living upon physicians was not strong enough to be healed by any,
having come to him behind, she touched the fringe of his garment, and instantly the flow of her blood stood still.

And Jesus said: Who is the one having touched me? And all denying, Peter said, and those with him: Master, the crowds hold you together and press upon you, and you say: Who is the one having touched me?
But Jesus said: Someone touched me; for I myself knew power having gone out from me.

And the woman, having seen that she had not escaped notice, came trembling, and having fallen before him she reported before all the people for what cause she touched him, and how she was healed instantly.
And he said to her: Take courage, daughter, your trust has saved you; go into peace.
While he was still speaking, someone comes from the synagogue-ruler saying to him that your daughter has died; trouble the teacher no longer.
But Jesus, having heard, answered him saying: Do not fear; only trust, and she will be saved.
And having come into the house he did not permit anyone to enter with him except Peter and John and James, and the father of the child and the mother.
And all were weeping and beating themselves for her. But he said: Do not weep, for she did not die but is sleeping.
And they were laughing him down, knowing that she died.
But he himself, having put them all outside and having taken hold of her hand, called out saying: The child, rise.
And her spirit returned, and she rose up instantly, and he directed that there be given to her to eat.
And her parents were amazed; but he charged them to tell no one the thing that had happened.

luke_9.t: And having called together his twelve disciples, he gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to heal diseases,
and he sent them to herald the kingdom of God and to heal the weak.
And he said to them: Take nothing for the road, neither staff nor bag nor bread nor silver, nor to have two tunics apiece.
And into whatever house you enter, remain there, and from there go out.
And as many as do not receive you, going out from that city shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
And going out they were going through the villages, proclaiming good news and healing everywhere.
And Herod the tetrarch heard all the things happening by him, and he was thoroughly perplexed because of its being said by some that John had been raised from the dead,
and by some that Elijah appeared, and by others that some prophet of the ancients rose up.
And Herod said: John I beheaded. But who is this about whom I hear such things? And he was seeking to see him.
And the apostles, having returned, recounted to him whatever they did. And taking them along he withdrew privately to a deserted place, a city called Bethsaida.
But the crowds, having known, followed him. And having welcomed them he was speaking to them about the kingdom of God, and those having need of healing he was curing.

And the day began to decline. And the twelve, having come forward, said to him: Release the crowd, so that going into the villages round about and the fields they may lodge and find provisions, because here we are in a deserted place.
But he said to them: You give them to eat. And they said: There are not to us more than five loaves and two fish, unless going ourselves we should buy food for all this people.
For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples: Make them recline in reclining-groups of about fifty each.
And they did so and made them all recline.
And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up into the heaven he blessed them and broke them down and was giving to the disciples to set before the crowd.
And they ate and were all satisfied, and there was taken up the surplus to them of fragments, twelve baskets.
And it happened, in his being praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he questioned them saying: Who do the crowds say me to be?
And answering they said: John the Baptist, but others Elijah, and others that some prophet of the ancients rose up.
And he said to them: But you, who do you say me to be? And Peter answering said: The Christ of God.
But he, having rebuked them, charged them to say this to no one,
saying that it is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer many things and to be rejected from the elders and chief priests and scribes and to be killed and on the third day to be raised.
And he was saying to all: If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and let him follow me.
