For whoever wishes to save his soul will destroy it, but whoever destroys his soul for my sake, this one will save it.
For what is a human benefited, having gained the whole world but having destroyed or forfeited himself?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, of this one the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and of the Father and of the holy angels.
But I say to you truly, there are some of those standing here who will by no means taste of death until they see the kingdom of God.
And it happened about eight days after these words, and taking along Peter and John and James he went up into the mountain to pray.
And it happened, in his praying, the appearance of his face was other, and his clothing white, flashing out like lightning.
And look, two men were speaking with him, who were Moses and Elijah.
who, having been seen in glory, were speaking of his exodus, which he was about to fulfil in Jerusalem.
But Peter and those with him were burdened with sleep. But having become fully awake they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

And it happened, in their being parted from him, Peter said to Jesus: Master, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah, not knowing what he says.
But while he was saying these things a cloud came and was overshadowing them. And they were afraid in their entering into the cloud.
And a voice came out of the cloud saying: This is my Son, the chosen one; hear him.
And in the voice's coming, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silence and reported to no one in those days anything of what they had seen.
And it happened on the next day, they having come down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
And look, a man from the crowd cried out saying: Teacher, I beg of you to look upon my son, because he is an only-born to me.
And look, a spirit takes him and suddenly he cries out, and it convulses him with foaming, and it withdraws from him with difficulty, crushing him.
And I begged your disciples that they might cast it out, and they were not able.
And answering, Jesus said: O generation without trust and having been distorted, until when will I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.
And while he was still coming forward the demon tore him and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him back to his father.
And all were struck out at the magnificence of God. But with all marvelling at all the things which he was doing, he said to his disciples:
You, put into your ears these words: for the Son of Man is about to be delivered over into hands of humans.
But they did not know this saying, and it was having been veiled from them so that they might not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
But a reasoning entered among them, the which of them might be greater.
But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their heart, having taken hold of a child stood it beside himself,
and said to them: Whoever receives this child upon my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one having sent me. For the one being smaller among you all, this one is great.
And answering, John said: Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we were preventing him, because he does not follow with us.
And Jesus said to him: Do not prevent. For whoever is not against you is for you.
And it happened, in the days of his taking-up being fulfilled, and he himself set his face to go into Jerusalem.
And he sent messengers before his face. And going, they entered into a village of Samaritans so as to prepare for him.
And they did not receive him, because his face was going into Jerusalem.
And seeing it, his disciples James and John said: Lord, do you wish we should say fire to come down from the heaven and consume them, as also Elijah did?
But turning, he rebuked them, and said: [You do not know of what sort of spirit you are.]
[For the Son of Man did not come to destroy souls of humans, but to save.] And they went into another village.
And it happened, as they were going in the road, someone said to him: I will follow you wherever you go, Lord.
And Jesus said to him: The foxes have dens, and the birds of the heaven roosting-places, but the Son of Man does not have where he may lay the head.
And he said to another: Follow me. But he said: Lord, permit me, having gone away, first to bury my father.
But Jesus said to him: Leave the dead to bury their own dead. But you, having gone away, announce thoroughly the kingdom of God.
And another also said: I will follow you, Lord; but first permit me to take leave of those in my house.
And Jesus said to him: No one having put his hand upon a plough and looking into the things behind is well-placed for the kingdom of God.

luke_10.t: And after these things the Lord designated seventy-two others also, and sent them two by two before his face into every city and place where he himself was about to come.
And he was saying to them: The harvest indeed is much, but the workers few. Beg therefore the lord of the harvest that he might cast out workers into his harvest.
Go. Look, I send you as lambs in the midst of wolves.
Do not carry a money-bag, nor a bag, nor sandals, and greet no one along the road.
And into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace to this house.
And if indeed there is a son of peace there, your peace will rest upon him; but if not, it will bend back upon you.
And in that same house remain, eating and drinking the things from them, for the worker is worthy of his wage. Do not move across from house into house.
And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you
and heal the weak in it and say to them: The kingdom of God has drawn near upon you.
But into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, having gone out into its wide streets say:
Even the dust having stuck to us from your city onto the feet we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God has drawn near.
I say to you that for Sodom in that day it will be more bearable than for that city.
Woe to you, Chorazin, woe to you, Bethsaida, because if in Tyre and Sidon there had happened the powers having happened among you, long ago sitting in sackcloth and ashes they changed their minds.
Nevertheless for Tyre and Sidon it will be more bearable in the judgement than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you not be lifted up as far as heaven? As far as Hades you will come down.
The one hearing you hears me, and the one setting you aside sets me aside; but the one setting me aside sets aside the one having sent me.
And the seventy-two returned with joy saying: Lord, even the demons are subjected to us in your name.
And he said to them: I was watching the Satan as lightning out of the heaven having fallen.
Look, I have given you the authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy, and nothing will by any means injure you.
Nevertheless in this do not rejoice, that the spirits are subjected to you; but rejoice rather that your names have been inscribed in the heavens.

In that same hour he exulted in the Holy Spirit and said: I confess out to you, Father, Lord of the heaven and of the earth, because you hid these things from wise and understanding ones and revealed them to infants. Yes, the Father, because thus good pleasure came to be before you.

And having turned toward the disciples he said: All things were delivered over to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son and to whomever the Son wishes to reveal.
And having turned toward the disciples privately he said: Blessed the eyes seeing what you see.
For I say to you that many prophets and kings wished to see what you see and did not see, and to hear what you hear and did not hear.
And look, a certain lawyer stood up testing him out and saying: Teacher, having done what will I inherit eternal life?
And he said to him: In the law what has been written? How do you read?
And answering he said: You shall love the Lord your God out of your whole heart and in your whole soul and in your whole strength and in your whole understanding, and your neighbour as yourself.
And he said to him: You answered rightly; do this and you will live.
But he, wishing to justify himself, said to Jesus: And who is my neighbour?

Taking it up, Jesus said: A certain human was going down from Jerusalem into Jericho and fell among robbers, who both having stripped him and having laid on blows went away, leaving him being half dead.
And by coincidence a certain priest was going down on that road, and having seen him he passed by on the opposite side.
And likewise also a Levite, having come down to the place and having seen, passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan travelling came down upon him, and having seen him was moved in the guts,
and having come to him he bound up his wounds, pouring on olive oil and wine; and having mounted him upon his own animal he led him into an inn and took care of him.

And upon the next day, having gone out, having thrown out he gave two denarii to the innkeeper and said to him: Take care of him, and whatever you may spend in addition, I on my coming back will give back to you.
Which of these three seems to you to have become neighbour of the one having fallen among the robbers?
And he said: The one having done the mercy with him. And Jesus said to him: Go, and you do likewise.
And it happened in their going, and he himself entered into a certain village. And a certain woman by name Martha received him under into her house.
And to this one there was a sister called Mariam, who also having sat beside at the feet of the Lord was hearing his word.

But Martha was being dragged around about much service. And having stood over him she said: Lord, is it no care to you that my sister left me down alone to serve? Speak therefore to her that she might take hold along with me.
But answering, the Lord said to her: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.
but of one thing there is need. For Mariam chose out the good part, which will not be taken away from her.

luke_11.t: And it happened, in his being in a certain place praying, as he ceased, one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.
And he said to them: When you pray, say: Father [of us, the one in the heavens], let your name be made holy; let your kingdom come; [let your will come to be, as in heaven, also upon the earth;]
Our epiousios bread give us daily.
And release for us our sins, for we ourselves also release everyone owing to us; and do not bring us into testing. [But rescue us from the evil one.]
And he said to them: Which of you will have a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him: Friend, lend me three loaves,
since a friend of mine came along out of a road to me, and I do not have what I shall set before him,
And that one from within answering should say: Do not hand me troubles; already the door has been shut and my children are with me in the bed; I am not able, having risen, to give to you.
I say to you, even if he will not give to him, having risen, because of being his friend, yet because of his shamelessness, having been roused, he will give him as much as he needs.
And I say to you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone asking receives, and the one seeking finds, and to the one knocking it will be opened.
But which father of you will the son ask for [bread, will he hand him a stone; or also] a fish, and instead of a fish will he hand him a serpent?
Or also if he asks an egg, will he hand him a scorpion?
If therefore you, being evil, know to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give Holy Spirit to those asking him.
And he was casting out a demon, and it was mute. And it happened, the demon having gone out, the mute one spoke, and the crowds marvelled.
But some of them said: By Beelzeboul the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.
But others, testing, were seeking from him a sign out of heaven.
But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them: Every kingdom having been divided against itself is made desolate, and a house falls upon a house.
But if also the Satan was divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because you say by Beelzeboul I cast out the demons.
But if I by Beelzeboul cast out the demons, your sons by whom do they cast out? Because of this they themselves will be your judges.
But if by a finger of God I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God came upon you.
Whenever the strong one, having been fully armed, guards his own courtyard, in peace are his belongings.
But when the one stronger than he, having come upon him, conquers him, he takes his full armour upon which he had trusted, and distributes his plunder.
The one not being with me is against me, and the one not gathering with me scatters.
Whenever the unclean spirit goes out from the human, it goes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding, then it says: I will return into my house from where I came out.
And having come it finds it standing empty, having been swept and having been put in order.
Then it goes and takes along seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having entered they dwell there, and the last things of that human become worse than the first.
And it happened, in his saying these things, a certain woman having lifted up a voice out of the crowd said to him: Blessed the belly having borne you and breasts which you sucked.
But he said: Rather blessed are those hearing the word of God and guarding it.
And the crowds gathering thickly upon him, he began to say: This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, thus also will be the Son of Man to this generation.

A queen of the south will be raised in the judgement with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came out of the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, more than Solomon here.
Men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because they changed their minds at the heralding of Jonah, and look, more than Jonah here.
No one having lit a lamp puts it into a hidden place nor under the measuring-basket, but upon the lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.
The lamp of the body is your eye. Whenever therefore your eye is single, also your whole body is light-filled; but when it is evil, also your body is dark.
Look out therefore lest the light in you is darkness.
If therefore your whole body is light-filled, not having any part dark, it will be light-filled whole, as whenever the lamp with the lightning-flash gives light to you.
And in his speaking, a certain Pharisee asks him so that he might breakfast with him. And having entered he reclined.
But the Pharisee having seen marvelled that he was not first washed before the breakfast.
But the Lord said to him: Now you the Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the plate, but the inside of you is full of plunder and evil.
Fools, did not the one having made the outside also make the inside?
Nevertheless the things being within give as almsgiving, and look, all things are clean to you.

But woe to you the Pharisees, because you tithe the mint and the rue and every garden herb, and you pass by the judgement and the love of God; but these things it was necessary to do, and not to leave those aside.
Woe to you the Pharisees, because you love the first seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like the unseen tombs, and the people walking above do not know.
And answering, a certain one of the lawyers says to him: Teacher, saying these things you also outrage us.
But he said: And to you the lawyers, woe, because you load the people with loads hard to bear, and you yourselves with one of your fingers do not touch the loads.
Woe to you, because you build the memorials of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
So then you are witnesses and you consent together to the works of your fathers, because they indeed killed them, but you build their memorials.
Because of this also the wisdom of God said: I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and will pursue,
so that the blood of all the prophets having been poured out from the foundation of the world might be sought out from this generation,
from the blood of Abel until the blood of Zechariah, the one having perished between the sacrificial altar and the house. Yes, I say to you, it will be sought out from this generation.
Woe to you the lawyers, because you took away the key of knowledge; you yourselves did not enter, and those entering you prevented.
And from there, he having gone out, the scribes and the Pharisees began terribly to hold against him and to question him closely about many things,
lying in ambush for him, seeking to hunt something out of his mouth so that they might accuse him.

luke_12.t: In which things, the ten-thousands of the crowd having been gathered together so as to trample one another down, he began to say to his disciples first: Take heed to yourselves from the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
But nothing has been covered together which will not be uncovered, and hidden which will not be known.
In return for which, whatever you said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you spoke toward the ear in the storerooms will be heralded upon the housetops.
But I say to you, my friends, do not be frightened from those killing the body and after these things not having anything more excessive to do.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one having authority, after the killing, to throw into the Gehenna. Yes, I say to you, fear this one.
Are not five sparrows sold for two assarion-coins? And one of them is not having been forgotten before God.
But even the hairs of your head all have been numbered. Do not fear; you differ from many sparrows.
And I say to you, everyone whoever confesses in me before the people, also the Son of Man will confess in him before the angels of God.
But the one having denied me in the presence of the people will be denied in the presence of the angels of God.
And everyone who will say a word into the Son of Man, it will be released to him; but to the one having blasphemed into the Holy Spirit it will not be released.
But whenever they bring you in upon the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious how or what you might defend or what you might say;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what things it is necessary to say.
And someone out of the crowd said to him: Teacher, speak to my brother to divide with me the inheritance.
But he said to him: Human, who set me a judge or a divider over you?
And he said to them: See and guard yourselves from all greed, because not in the abounding to someone is his life out of the things belonging to him.
And he spoke a parable to them saying: Of a certain rich human the land bore well.
And he was reasoning within himself saying: What shall I do, because I do not have where I shall gather my fruits?
And he said: This I will do: I will take down my storehouses and I will build greater ones, and I will gather together there all the grain and my good things,
and I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many good things lying up for many years; rest, eat, drink, be merry.
But God said to him: Fool, this night they are demanding back your soul from you; but the things you prepared, to whom will they be?
Thus the one treasuring up for himself and not being rich toward God.
And he said to his disciples: Because of this I say to you, do not be anxious for the soul what you might eat, nor for the body what you might put on.
For the soul is more than the food, and the body than the clothing.
Consider the ravens, that they do not sow nor reap, to which there is not a storeroom nor a storehouse, and God feeds them. By how much more do you differ from the birds.
But which of you, being anxious, is able to add upon his age one forearm-length?
If therefore you are not able even for the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how it grows: it does not labour nor spin. But I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed around as one of these.
But if the grass in the field, being today and tomorrow being thrown into an oven, God thus clothes around, by how much more you, little-trusters.
And you, do not seek what you might eat and what you might drink, and do not be raised aloft.
For all these things the nations of the world seek after; but your Father knows that you need these things.
Nevertheless seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
Do not fear, the little flock, because your Father took pleasure to give you the kingdom.
Sell the things belonging to you and give almsgiving; make for yourselves money-bags not being made old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where a thief does not draw near nor a moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there also your heart will be.
Let your loins be having been girded and the lamps burning,
and you like people awaiting their own lord, when he may return from the wedding feasts, so that having come and having knocked they might open to him immediately.
Blessed those slaves whom the lord having come will find watching. Amen I say to you that he will gird himself and will make them recline, and having come alongside he will serve them.
And if he comes in the second watch and if in the third watch he comes and finds thus, blessed are those slaves.
But know this, that if the housemaster had known in what hour the thief comes, he would have watched and would not have let his house be dug through.
And you therefore become ready, because in the hour you do not suppose the Son of Man comes.
And Peter said to him: Lord, toward us are you speaking this parable, or also toward all?
And the lord said: Who then is the trustworthy manager, the prudent one, whom the lord will set over his body of attendants to give in season the grain-measure?
Blessed that slave whom his lord having come will find doing thus.
Truly I say to you that over all his belongings he will set him.
But if that slave says in his heart: My lord delays to come, and begins to strike the boys and the girls and both to eat and to drink and to be drunk,
the lord of that slave will arrive in a day in which he does not expect and in an hour which he does not know, and will cut him in two, and his part he will set with the untrusting.
But that slave, the one having known the will of his lord and not having prepared or done toward his will, will be flogged many.

But the one not having known, but having done things worthy of blows, will be flogged few. And to everyone to whom much was given, much will be sought from him; and to whom they entrusted much, more excessive they will ask of him.
Fire I came to throw upon the earth, and what do I wish if it was already kindled.
But I have a baptism to be baptised, and how I am held together until it is finished.
Do you suppose that I arrived to give peace in the earth? Not at all, I say to you, but rather division.
For there will be from now five in one house having been divided, three against two and two against three.
They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against the daughter and daughter against the mother, mother-in-law against her bride and bride against the mother-in-law.
And he was saying also to the crowds: Whenever you see the cloud rising up upon the west, immediately you say that a rainstorm comes, and it happens thus.
And whenever a south wind blowing, you say that there will be burning heat, and it happens.
Hypocrites, the face of the earth and of the heaven you know to test out, but this season how do you not know to test out?
And why also from yourselves do you not judge the right thing?

For as you go with your opponent-at-law before a ruler, in the road give work to be released from him, lest he drag you down toward the judge, and the judge will hand you over to the bailiff, and the bailiff will throw you into prison.
I say to you, you will by no means come out from there until you give back even the last lepton.

luke_13.t: And there were present some at that same season reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices.
And answering he said to them: Do you suppose that these Galileans became sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered these things?
Not at all, I say to you, but unless you change your mind, all of you will likewise be destroyed.
Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them, do you suppose that they became debtors beyond all the people dwelling in Jerusalem?
Not at all, I say to you, but unless you change your mind, all of you will likewise be destroyed.
And he was speaking this parable: A certain one had a fig tree having been planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and did not find.
And he said to the vinedresser: Look, three years from when I come seeking fruit on this fig tree and I do not find; cut it out therefore. Why also does it make the ground useless?
But answering he says to him: Lord, leave it also this year, until I dig around it and throw manures;
and if indeed it should make fruit for the coming; but if not, you will cut it out.
And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbaths.
And look, a woman having a spirit of weakness eighteen years, and she was bent together and not able to unbend fully.
And seeing her, Jesus called to her and said to her: Woman, you have been released from your weakness.
And he laid on her the hands, and instantly she was made straight again and was glorifying God.

But answering, the ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because on the sabbath Jesus healed, was saying to the crowd that there are six days in which it is necessary to work; in them therefore coming be healed, and not on the day of the sabbath.
But the Lord answered him and said: Hypocrites, does not each of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his donkey from the feeding-trough and, having led it away, give it drink?
But this one, being a daughter of Abraham whom the Satan bound, look, ten and eight years, was it not necessary to be loosed from this bond on the day of the sabbath?
And as he was saying these things, all those opposing him were being put to shame, and all the crowd was rejoicing at all the glorious things happening by him.
Therefore he was saying: To what is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I liken it?
It is like a grain of mustard which a human, having taken, threw into his own garden, and it grew and became into a great tree, and the birds of the heaven nested in its branches.
And again he said: To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven which a woman, having taken, hid into three measures of wheat flour until the whole was leavened.
And he was going through according to cities and villages, teaching and making a journey into Jerusalem.
And someone said to him: Lord, if few are the ones being saved. And he said toward them:
Struggle to enter in through the narrow door, because many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be strong enough.

From when the housemaster may be raised up and may shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock the door saying: Lord, Lord, open to us; and answering he will say to you: I do not know you, from where you are.
Then you will begin to say: We ate before you and drank, and in our wide streets you taught.
And he will say, saying to you: I do not know you, from where you are; stand off from me, all workers of unrighteousness.
There will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you being cast outside.
And they will come from risings and settings and from north and south and will recline in the kingdom of God.
And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
In that same hour some Pharisees came forward saying to him: Come out and go from here, because Herod wishes to kill you.
And he said to them: Going, say to this fox: Look, I cast out demons and I complete healings today and tomorrow, and on the third I am finished.
Nevertheless it is necessary for me today and tomorrow and on the following to go, because it is not admissible for a prophet to be destroyed outside Jerusalem.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one killing the prophets and stoning those having been sent to her, how many times I wished to gather together your children in the manner a bird her own brood under the wings, and you did not wish.
Look, your house is left to you. But Amen I say to you that you will by no means see me until it will come when you say: Having been blessed the one coming in the name of the Lord.

luke_14.t: And it happened, in his coming into a house of a certain one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a sabbath to eat bread, and they themselves were watching him closely.
And look, a certain human was dropsical before him.
And answering, Jesus said toward the lawyers and Pharisees saying: Is it lawful on the sabbath to heal, or not?
But they kept quiet. And having taken hold, he healed him and released him.
And answering toward them he said: Of which of you a son or an ox will fall into a well, and he will not immediately draw him up on the day of the sabbath?
And they were not strong enough to answer back to him toward these things.
And he was speaking toward those having been invited a parable, holding on how they were choosing out the first couches, saying toward them:
Whenever you are invited by someone into wedding feasts, do not recline into the first couch, lest someone more honoured than you has been invited by him,
and having come, the one having invited you and him will say to you: Give place to this one, and then you will begin with shame to hold down the last place.

But whenever you are invited, having gone, recline into the last place, so that whenever the one having invited you comes, he will say to you: Friend, come up higher; then there will be glory to you before all those reclining together with you.
Because everyone lifting himself up will be humbled, and the one humbling himself will be lifted up.

And he was saying also to the one having invited him: Whenever you make a breakfast or a supper, do not call your friends nor your brothers nor your relatives nor rich neighbours, lest they also invite you in return and there be a repayment to you.
But whenever you make a reception, call poor ones, maimed ones, lame ones, blind ones.
And blessed you will be, because they do not have to repay you; for it will be repaid to you in the resurrection of the just.
And having heard these things, a certain one of those reclining together said to him: Blessed whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God.
But he said to him: A certain human was making a great supper and invited many.
And he sent his slave at the hour of the supper to say to those having been invited: Come, because already it is prepared, all things.
And they began from one all to beg off. The first said to him: I bought a field and I have necessity, having gone out, to see it; I ask you, have me having been excused.
And another said: I bought five yokes of oxen and I go to test them out; I ask you, have me having been excused.
And another said: I married a wife, and because of this I am not able to come.

And having arrived, that slave reported these things to his lord. Then having become angry, the housemaster said to his slave: Go out quickly into the wide streets and narrow lanes of the city, and the poor and maimed and blind and lame lead in here.
And the slave said: Lord, it has happened what you commanded, and still there is place.
And the lord said toward the slave: Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.
For I say to you that not one of those men, those having been invited, will taste of my supper. [For many are called, but few chosen.]
And great crowds were going together with him, and having turned he said toward them:

If anyone comes toward me and does not hate his own father and the mother and the wife and the children and the brothers and the sisters, and still also his own soul, he is not able to be my disciple.
And whoever does not carry his own cross and come behind me is not able to be my disciple.
For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first, having sat down, count up the expense, whether he has the things for completion?
So that lest, he having laid a foundation and not being strong enough to finish out, all those looking on begin to mock him,
saying that this human began to build and was not strong enough to finish out.
Or what king going to engage another king into war will not, having sat down first, take counsel whether he is able with ten thousands to meet the one coming with twenty thousands against him?
But if not, while he is still far off, having sent an embassy he asks the things toward peace.
Thus therefore everyone of you who does not take leave of all his own belongings is not able to be my disciple.
Therefore the salt is good; but if also the salt is made foolish, with what will it be seasoned?
Neither for soil nor for a dung-heap is it well-placed; they throw it outside. The one having ears to hear, let him hear.

luke_15.t: And all the tax-farmers and the sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
And both the Pharisees and the scribes were muttering through, saying that this one receives sinners and eats together with them.
And he spoke toward them this parable saying:
What human of you having a hundred sheep and having lost one out of them does not leave down the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one having been lost until he finds it?
And having found it he lays it upon his shoulders rejoicing,
and having come into the house he calls together the friends and the neighbours saying to them: Rejoice together with me, because I found my sheep, the one having been lost.
I say to you that thus there will be joy in the heaven over one sinner changing his mind, than over ninety-nine just ones who do not have need of a change of mind.
Or what woman having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek carefully until she finds?
And having found she calls together the women friends and the women neighbours saying: Rejoice together with me, because I found the drachma which I lost.
Thus, I say to you, there comes to be joy before the angels of God over one sinner changing his mind.
And he said: A certain human had two sons.
And the younger of them said to the father: Father, give me the falling-to share of the substance. And he divided to them the living.
And after not many days, having gathered together all things, the younger son went abroad into a far country, and there he scattered abroad his substance, living unsavingly.
And he having spent all things, there came a strong famine throughout that country, and he himself began to be in want.
And having gone he glued himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
And he was desiring to be filled the belly out of the carob-pods which the pigs were eating, and no one was giving to him.
But having come into himself he said: How many hired workers of my father have an abundance of loaves, and I here am perishing by famine.
Having risen I will go toward my father and I will say to him: Father, I sinned into the heaven and before you.
No longer am I worthy to be called your son; make me as one of your hired workers.
And having risen he came toward his own father. But while he was still holding far off, his father saw him and was moved in the guts, and having run he fell upon his neck and kissed him down.
And the son said to him: Father, I sinned into the heaven and before you; no longer am I worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired workers.
But the father said toward his slaves: Quickly bring out the first robe and clothe him, and give a ring into his hand and sandals into the feet.
And bring the calf, the fattened one, sacrifice it, and having eaten let us be merry,
because this son of mine was dead and came alive again, and was having been lost and was found. And they began to be merry.
But his son, the older one, was in a field. And as, coming, he drew near to the house, he heard a symphony and dancing choruses,
and having called to himself one of the boys he was inquiring what these things might be.
And he said to him that your brother has arrived, and your father sacrificed the fattened calf, because he received him back being healthy.
But he was angered and was not willing to enter. And his father, having come out, was calling him alongside.

But answering he said to his father: Look, so many years I slave for you and never did I pass by a command of yours, and to me never did you give a young goat so that with my friends I might be merry.
But when this son of yours, the one having devoured your living with prostitutes, came, you sacrificed for him the fattened calf.
But he said to him: Child, you are always with me, and all the things that are mine are yours.
But to be merry and to rejoice it was necessary, because this brother of yours was dead and lived, and was having been lost and was found.

luke_16.t: And he was saying also toward his disciples: There was a certain rich human who had a manager, and this one was accused to him as scattering abroad his belongings.
And having called him he said to him: What is this I hear about you? Give back the account of your management, for you are not able any longer to manage.
And the manager said within himself: What shall I do, because my lord takes away the management from me? To dig I am not strong enough, to beg I am ashamed.
I knew what I shall do, so that whenever I am removed out of the management, they may receive me into their houses.
And having called to himself each one of the debtors of his own lord, he was saying to the first: How much do you owe to my lord?
And he said: A hundred baths of olive oil. And he said to him: Take back your writings and having sat down quickly write fifty.
Thereupon to another he said: But you, how much do you owe? And he said: A hundred kors of wheat. He says to him: Take back your writings and write eighty.
And the lord praised the manager of the injustice because he acted prudently, because the sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of the light toward their own generation.
And I say to you, make for yourselves friends out of the mamonas of the injustice, so that whenever it fails they may receive you into the eternal tents.
The trustworthy one in the least is also trustworthy in much, and the one in the least unjust is also unjust in much.
If therefore in the unjust mamonas you did not become trustworthy, the true thing, who will entrust to you?
And if in the belonging-to-another you did not become trustworthy, the yours, who will give to you?

No house-slave is able to slave for two lords; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or of one he will hold fast and the other he will despise. You are not able to slave for God and mamonas.
And the Pharisees, being lovers of silver, were hearing all these things, and they were turning up their noses at him.
And he said to them: You are those justifying yourselves before the people, but God knows your hearts, because the high thing among humans is an abomination before God.
The law and the prophets until John; from then the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone into it forces.
But it is easier for the heaven and the earth to pass by than for one horn of the law to fall.
Everyone releasing his wife and marrying another commits adultery, and everyone marrying her having been released from a husband commits adultery.
But a certain human was rich, and he was clothing himself in purple and fine linen, being merry day by day splendidly.
And a certain poor one by name Lazarus had been thrown toward his gate, having been ulcerated,
and desiring to be filled from the things falling from the table of the rich one; but even the dogs, coming, were licking his ulcers.
And it happened for the poor one to die and for him to be carried away by the angels into the bosom of Abraham; and the rich one also died and was buried.
And in Hades having lifted up his eyes, being in torments, he sees Abraham from far off and Lazarus in his bosom.
And he, having called, said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger of water and cool down my tongue, because I am in anguish in this flame.
But Abraham said: Child, remember that you received back your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise the bad things; but now here he is called alongside, and you are in anguish.
And in all these things, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those wishing to cross over from here toward you are not able, nor may they cross over from there toward us.
And he said: I ask you therefore, father, that you might send him into the house of my father,
for I have five brothers, so that he may testify thoroughly to them, so that they also may not come into this place of the torment.
But Abraham says to him: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
But he said: Not so, father Abraham, but if someone from dead ones goes toward them, they will change their mind.
But he said to him: If Moses and the prophets they do not hear, neither if someone rises out of dead ones will they be persuaded.

luke_17.t: And he said toward his learners: It is inadmissible that the stumbling-traps not come, yet woe through whom it comes.
It is more profitable for him if a mill-stone lies around his neck and he has been thrown into the sea, than that he trip up one of these little ones.
Hold to yourselves. And if your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he changes his mind, release him.
And if seven times of the day he sins against you and seven times of the day he turns back toward you saying, I am changing my mind — you will release him.
And the sent-ones said to the Lord: Add to us trust.
And the Lord said: If you have trust as a grain of mustard, you would be saying to this mulberry: Be uprooted and be planted in the sea — and it would have obeyed you.
But which of you, having a slave ploughing or shepherding, who to him coming in out of the field will say: At once, having come by, recline?
But will he not say to him: Prepare what I may dine on, and having girded yourself serve me until I eat and drink, and after these things you shall eat and drink?
He does not have gratitude to that slave because he did the things ordered to him? I do not think so.
So also you, whenever you do all the things ordered to you, say that: Useless slaves we are; because what we were obliged to do we have done.
And it came to be, in the going of him into Jerusalem, and he was passing through through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And of him entering into a certain village, there met him ten leprous men, who stood far off.
And they lifted a voice saying: Jesus, Overseer, have mercy on us.
And having seen he said to them: Having gone, show yourselves to the priests. And it came to be, in the going away of them, they were cleansed.
But one out of them, having seen that he was healed, returned with a great voice glorifying God.
And he fell upon face beside his feet giving thanks to him — and he was a Samaritan.
And answering, Jesus said: Were not the ten cleansed? But the nine, where?
Were they not found returning to give glory to God except this other-born one?
And he said to him: Having stood up, go; your trust has saved you.
And having been questioned by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God comes, he answered them and said: The kingdom of God does not come with observation,
Nor will they say: Behold here, or, Behold there. For behold, the kingdom of God is among you.
And he said toward the learners: Days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see.
And they will say to you: Behold there, or, Behold here. Do not go away nor pursue.
For just as the lightning, the flashing one, out of the under-heaven into the under-heaven shines, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
But first it is necessary for him to suffer many things and to be rejected from this generation.
And just as it came to be in the days of Noah, so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.
They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed all.
Likewise just as it came to be in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building.
But on which day Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulphur from heaven and destroyed all.
According to the same things it will be on which day the Son of Man is revealed.
In that day, whoever will be upon the housetop and his vessels in the house, let him not come down to take them; and the one in the field likewise, let him not turn back to the things behind.
Remember the wife of Lot.
Whoever seeks to preserve his soul will destroy it, and whoever destroys it will bring it forth alive.
I say to you: on this night there will be two upon one couch; the one will be taken along and the other will be released.
There will be two grinding upon the same place; the one will be taken along, but the other will be released.
[Two in a field; one will be taken along and the other will be released.]
And answering they say to him: Where, Lord? And he said to them: Where the body is, there also the eagles will be gathered together.

luke_18.t: And he was telling also a parable to them toward the necessity for them always to pray and not to grow weary,
saying: A certain judge was in a certain city, not fearing God and not being ashamed before a human.
And a widow was in that city, and she was coming toward him saying: Vindicate me from my opponent-at-law.
And he was not willing for a time. But after these things he said in himself: If also God I do not fear nor am ashamed before a human,
yet because this widow provides trouble for me, I will vindicate her, so that she may not, coming to the end, give me a black eye.
And the Lord said: Hear what the judge of unrighteousness says.
And will God by no means do the vindication of his chosen ones, the ones crying toward him day and night — and is he long-suffering over them?
I say to you that he will do their vindication in speed. Nevertheless the Son of Man, having come — will he then find the trust upon the earth?
And he said also toward certain ones who had trusted upon themselves that they are righteous and were treating the rest as nothing, this parable.
Two humans went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax-farmer.

The Pharisee, having stood, was praying these things toward himself: The God, I give thanks to you that I am not just as the rest of the humans — rapacious, unrighteous, adulterers — or also as this tax-farmer.
I fast twice of the sabbath; I tithe all things, as much as I acquire.
But the tax-farmer, standing far off, was not willing even to lift the eyes into the heaven, but was striking into his chest saying: The God, be propitiated to me the sinner.

I say to you: this one went down into his house having been justified rather than that one. Because everyone lifting himself high will be brought low, but the one bringing himself low will be lifted high.
And they were bringing to him also the infants, so that he might touch them; but the learners, having seen, were rebuking them.
But Jesus called them toward himself saying: Let the little children come toward me and do not hinder them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
Amen I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, may by no means enter into it.
And a certain ruler questioned him saying: Good teacher, having done what shall I inherit eternal life?
And Jesus said to him: Why do you say me good? No one is good except one — the God.
The commandments you know: You may not commit adultery, you may not murder, you may not steal, you may not bear false witness, honour your father and your mother.
And he said: These things all I guarded from my youth.

And having heard these things, Jesus said to him: Still one thing to you is lacking; all things as much as you have, sell and distribute to poor ones, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come here, follow me.
But he, having heard these things, became very grieved; for he was exceedingly rich.
And Jesus, having seen him having become very grieved, said: How with difficulty do the ones having the goods journey into the kingdom of God.
For it is easier for a camel to enter through a hole of a needle than for a rich one to enter into the kingdom of God.
And the ones having heard said: And who is able to be saved?
And he said: The impossible things beside humans are possible beside the God.
And Peter said: Behold, we, having left the own things, followed you.
And he said to them: Amen I say to you that there is no one who left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
who shall not by all means receive back many times more in this season, and in the age that is coming, eternal life.
And having taken along the twelve, he said toward them: Behold, we are going up into Jerusalem, and all the things having been written through the prophets to the Son of Man will be completed.
For he will be handed over to the nations and will be mocked and will be outraged and will be spat upon,
and having scourged him they will kill him, and on the third day he will stand up.
And they understood nothing of these things, and this word was having been hidden from them, and they were not knowing the things being said.
And it came to be, in the drawing near of him into Jericho, a certain blind one was sitting beside the way begging.
And having heard a crowd passing through, he was inquiring what this might be.
And they reported to him that Jesus the Nazorean is passing by.
And he cried out saying: Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me.
And the ones going before were rebuking him that he might be silent; but he much more was crying: Son of David, have mercy on me.
And Jesus, having stood, ordered him to be led toward him. And of him having drawn near, he questioned him,
saying: What do you wish I may do for you? And he said: Lord, that I may look up again.
And Jesus said to him: Look up again; your trust has saved you.
And instantly he looked up again and was following him, glorifying God. And all the people, having seen, gave praise to the God.

luke_19.t: And having entered, he was passing through the Jericho.
And behold, a man called by name Zacchaeus — and he was a chief tax-farmer, and he was rich.
And he was seeking to see the Jesus, who he is, and he was not able from the crowd, because in stature he was small.
And having run ahead into the front, he went up upon a sycamore-fig so that he might see him, because through that one he was about to pass through.
And as he came upon the place, having looked up, the Jesus saw him and said toward him: Zacchaeus, having hurried, come down; for today in your house it is necessary for me to remain.
And having hurried, he came down and received him rejoicing.
And having seen, all were grumbling through, saying that: Beside a sinful man he entered in to lodge.
And Zacchaeus, having stood, said toward the Lord: Behold, the halves of my belongings, Lord, to poor ones I give; and if of anyone anything I defrauded, I give back fourfold.
And Jesus said toward him that: Today salvation came to be to this house, according as also he is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the thing having been lost.
And of them hearing these things, having added he spoke a parable, because of him being near Jerusalem and of them supposing that instantly the kingdom of God is about to appear.
He said therefore: A certain well-born human journeyed into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.
And having called ten slaves of his own, he gave to them ten minas and said toward them: Do business in which until I come.
But his citizens were hating him, and they sent an embassy after him saying: We do not wish this one to reign over us.
And it came to be, in the coming back of him having received the kingdom, and he said to be called to him these slaves to whom he had given the silver, so that he might know what each had traded.
And the first came alongside saying: Lord, your mina worked in addition ten minas.
And he said to him: Well, good slave — because in a least thing you became trustworthy, be having authority over ten cities.
And the second came saying: Your mina, lord, made five minas.
And he said also to this one: And you, be over five cities.
And the other came saying: Lord, behold your mina, which I was having laid away in a face-cloth.
For I was fearing you, because a severe human you are; you take what you did not lay down and you reap what you did not sow.
He says to him: Out of your mouth I will judge you, evil slave. You knew that I a severe human am, taking what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow.
And through what did you not give my silver upon the table, and I, having come, would have exacted it with interest?
And to the ones having stood beside he said: Take the mina from him and give to the one having the ten minas.
And they said to him: Lord, he has ten minas.
I say to you that to everyone having it will be given, but from the one not having, even what he has will be taken away from him.
Nevertheless these enemies of mine, the ones not having wished me to reign over them, lead here and slaughter them before me.
And having said these things, he was journeying in front, going up into Jerusalem.
And it came to be as he drew near into Bethphage and Bethany toward the mountain called of Olives, he sent two of his learners,
saying: Go away into the village opposite, in which entering you will find a colt having been bound, upon which no one ever yet of humans sat; and having loosed it, lead it.
And if anyone asks you: Through what do you loose it? — thus you will say to him that: Its lord has need.
And having gone away, the ones having been sent found just as he said to them.
And of them loosing the colt, its lords said toward them: Why do you loose the colt?
And they said that: Its lord has need.
And they led it toward the Jesus, and having thrown their garments upon the colt, they mounted Jesus.
And of him journeying, they were spreading under their garments in the way.

And of him drawing near already toward the descent of the mountain of the olives, the whole multitude of the learners began, rejoicing, to praise the God with a great voice concerning all the powers which they saw,
saying: Blessed is the coming one, the king, in the name of the Lord; in heaven peace, and glory in the highest places.
And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said toward him: Teacher, rebuke your learners.
And answering he said: I say to you that if these will be silent, the stones will cry out.
And as he drew near, having seen the city he wept over it,
saying that: If you knew, even in this your day, also you, the things toward your peace — but now it was hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you, and your enemies will throw around you a palisade and will encircle you and will hem you in from all sides,
and they will dash you to the ground and your children in you, and they will not leave stone upon stone in you, in return for which you did not know the season of your visitation.
And having entered into the temple, he began to throw out the ones selling in it and buying,
saying to them: It has been written, And my house shall be a house of prayer; but you made it a cave of robbers.
And he was teaching according to the day in the temple; but the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy him, and the first ones of the people,
and they were not finding the what they might do; for all the people was hanging upon him, hearing.

luke_20.t: And it came to be on one of those days, of him teaching the people in the temple and announcing good news, the chief priests and the scribes stood upon him together with the elders,
and they said, saying toward him: Tell us by what sort of authority you do these things, or who is the one having given you this authority?
And answering he said toward them: I will question you also one word, and tell me:
The baptism of John — was it out of heaven or out of humans?
And they reckoned together toward themselves saying that: If we say Out of heaven, he will say: Through what then did you not trust him?
But if we say Out of humans, the people, all of it, will stone us down; for it has been persuaded that John is a prophet.
And they answered not to know from where.
And the Jesus said to them: Neither do I say to you by what sort of authority I do these things.
And he began toward the people to say this parable: A certain human planted a vineyard and gave it out to farmers, and he went abroad for considerable times.
And in season he sent toward the farmers a slave, so that from the fruit of the vineyard they will give to him. But the farmers sent him out having flayed him, empty.
And he added to send another slave; but they, having flayed and dishonoured that one also, sent him out empty.
And he added to send a third; but they, having wounded also this one, threw him out.
And the lord of the vineyard said: What shall I do? I will send my son, the beloved; perhaps this one, having seen, they will be ashamed before.
But having seen him, the farmers were reckoning toward one another saying: This one is the heir; come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.
And having thrown him outside of the vineyard, they killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and will destroy these farmers and will give the vineyard to others. And having heard, they said: May it not come to be.
And he, having looked into them, said: What therefore is this having been written: A stone which the ones building rejected as unfit, this one became into a head of a corner?
Everyone having fallen upon that stone will be dashed together; but upon whomever it falls, it will winnow him.
And the scribes and the chief priests sought to throw the hands upon him in that very hour, and they feared the people; for they knew that toward them he said this parable.

And having watched closely, they sent men set in place, pretending themselves to be righteous, so that they might take hold of him in a word, so as to hand him over to the rule and to the authority of the governor.
And they questioned him saying: Teacher, we know that rightly you speak and teach, and you do not receive a face but upon truth you teach the way of God.
Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar or not?
But having perceived their craftiness, he said toward them: Why do you test me?
Show me a denarius. Of whom does it have an image and an inscription? And they said: Of Caesar.
And he said toward them: Accordingly, give back the things of Caesar to Caesar and the things of the God to the God.
And they were not strong enough to take hold of his word before the people, and having marvelled at his answer they were silent.
And some of the Sadducees having come toward him, the ones speaking against there being a resurrection, questioned him,
saying: Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if anyone's brother dies having a wife, and this one is childless, that his brother should take the wife and raise up seed to his brother.
Seven brothers therefore were; and the first, having taken a wife, died childless.
And the second took the wife, and this one died childless.
And the third took her likewise; and likewise also the seven did not leave down children, and they died.
And later of all, also the woman died.
The woman therefore in the resurrection, of which of them does she become wife? For the seven had her as wife.
And answering, the Jesus said to them: The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,
but the ones having been counted worthy to obtain that age and the resurrection, the one out of dead ones, neither marry nor are given in marriage;
For neither are they able to die still, for they are equal-to-angels, and they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
But that the dead ones are raised, also Moses disclosed at the bramble-bush, as he says: Lord the God of Abraham and God of Isaac and God of Jacob.
But God he is not of dead ones but of living ones; for all live to him.
And answering, some of the scribes said: Teacher, well you spoke.
For no longer were they daring to question him anything.
And he said toward them: How do they say the Christ to be son of David?
For David himself says in a book of psalms: Said the Lord to my lord, Sit out of my right hand parts,
until I place your enemies a footstool of your feet.
David therefore calls him lord, and how is he his son?
And of all the people hearing, he said to his learners:
Hold away from the scribes, the ones wishing to walk about in robes and loving greetings in the marketplaces and first seats in the synagogues and first couches in the dinners,
who devour down the houses of the widows and for a pretence pray at length; these will receive more abundant judgement.

luke_21.t: And having looked up, he saw the ones throwing into the treasury their gifts — rich ones.
And he saw also a certain needy widow throwing there two lepta.
And he said: Truly I say to you that this widow, the destitute one, threw in more than all;
For all these out of the abounding to them threw into the gifts of God; but she out of her lack threw in all the living which she had.
And of some speaking concerning the temple, that with beautiful stones and votive gifts it has been adorned, he said:
These things which you behold — days will come in which not will be left a stone upon a stone here which will not be loosed down.
And they questioned him saying: Teacher, when therefore will these things be, and what the sign whenever these things are about to come to be?
And he said: See that you are not led astray; for many will come upon my name saying that I am, and, The season has drawn near. Do not go away behind them.
And whenever you hear wars and instabilities, do not be terrified; for it is necessary for these things to come to be first, but not immediately the end.
Then he was saying to them: Nation will be raised against nation and kingdom against kingdom,
And great earthquakes and according to places famines and pestilences will be, and fearful things and from heaven great signs will be.
But before all these things, they will throw upon you their hands and will persecute, handing over into the synagogues and prisons, being led away upon kings and governors for the sake of my name.
It will turn out to you into a witness.
Place therefore in your hearts not to premeditate to make a defence;
for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all the ones lying against you will not be able to stand against or to speak against.
And you will be handed over also by parents and brothers and kinsmen and friends, and they will put to death out of you.
And you will be being hated by all through my name.
And a hair out of your head may by no means be destroyed.
In your endurance acquire your souls.
But whenever you see Jerusalem being encircled by encamped armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
Then let the ones in the Judea flee into the mountains, and let the ones in the midst of her depart out, and let the ones in the countrysides not enter into her.
Because days of vindication these are, for all the things having been written to be filled full.
But woe to the ones having in womb and to the ones giving suck in those days; for there will be great necessity upon the earth and wrath in this people,
and they will fall by mouth of sword and will be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be being trampled by nations until which the times of nations should be fulfilled.
And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth pressing-together of nations in perplexity of roaring of sea and of tossing,
of humans expiring from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and much glory.
And of these things beginning to come to be, bend yourselves up and lift your heads, because your release-by-ransom is drawing near.
And he said a parable to them: See the fig tree and all the trees;
Whenever they put forth already, seeing from yourselves you know that already near the summer is.
So also you, whenever you see these things coming to be, know that near is the kingdom of God.
Amen I say to you that this generation may by no means pass away until all things should come to be.
The heaven and the earth will pass away, but my words may by no means pass away.
But hold to yourselves, lest ever your hearts be weighed down in hangover and drunkenness and cares of daily life, and that day stand upon you sudden
as a snare; for it will come in upon all the ones sitting upon face of all the earth.
But be sleepless in every season, begging that you may prevail to flee out these things, all the ones about to come to be, and to stand before the Son of Man.
And he was in the days in the temple teaching; but the nights, going out, he was lodging in the open into the mountain called of Olives.
And all the people was rising early toward him in the temple to hear him.

luke_22.t: And the feast of the unleavened things was drawing near, the one called Passover;
and the chief priests and the scribes were seeking the how they might take him up; for they were fearing the people.
And Satan entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, being out of the number of the twelve.
And having gone away, he spoke together with the chief priests and the commanders about the how he might hand him over to them.
And they rejoiced and covenanted to give him silver.
And he confessed out, and he was seeking a good season to hand him over to them apart from a crowd.
And the day of the unleavened things came, in which it was necessary to be sacrificed the Passover.
And he sent Peter and John having said: Having gone, prepare for us the Passover so that we may eat.
And they said to him: Where do you wish we should prepare?
And he said to them: Behold, of you having entered into the city, there will meet you a human carrying an earthen vessel of water; follow him into the house into which he goes,
and you will say to the house-master of the house: The teacher says to you, Where is the lodging-place where the Passover with my learners I may eat?
And that one will show you an upper room, great, having been spread; there prepare.
And having gone away, they found just as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when the hour came to be, he reclined, and the sent-ones with him.
And he said toward them: With desire I desired this Passover to eat with you before the me to suffer.
For I say to you that no longer may I by no means eat of it until which it should be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
And having received a cup, having given thanks, he said: Take this and divide it into yourselves.
For I say to you that I may by no means drink from now from the produce of the vine until which the kingdom of God should come.
And having taken bread, having given thanks, he broke and gave to them saying: This is my body, [the one being given for you; this do into the my remembrance.
And the cup likewise after the dining, saying: This cup is the new covenant in my blood, the one being poured out for you.]
Nevertheless behold, the hand of the one handing me over is with me upon the table.
Because the Son of Man according to the thing having been marked out journeys; nevertheless woe to that human through whom he is handed over.
And they began to seek together toward themselves the who then it might be out of them, the one about to do this.
And there came to be also a love-of-strife among them, the which of them seems to be greater.
And he said to them: The kings of the nations exercise lordship over them, and the ones having authority over them are called benefactors.
But you not so; rather let the greater among you become as the younger, and the one leading as the one serving.
For who is greater, the one reclining or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am in your midst as the one serving.
But you are the ones having remained through with me in my testings.
And I covenant to you, just as my Father covenanted to me, a kingdom,
so that you may eat and may drink at my table in my kingdom, and you will sit upon thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, behold, Satan demanded you for himself, to sift you as the wheat.
But I begged concerning you, that your trust may not fail out. And you, when once having turned back, establish your brothers.
And he said to him: Lord, with you ready I am both into prison and into death to journey.
And he said: I say to you, Peter, a cock will not sound today until three times you will deny to know me.
And he said to them: When I sent you apart from purse and wallet and sandals, did you lack anything? And they said: Nothing.
And he said to them: But now, the one having a purse, let him take it, likewise also a wallet; and the one not having, let him sell his garment and let him buy a sword.
For I say to you that still this thing having been written it is necessary to be completed in me, the: And with lawless ones he was reckoned. For indeed the thing concerning me has an end.
And they said: Lord, behold, swords here two. And he said to them: It is sufficient.
And having gone out, he journeyed according to the custom into the mountain of the olives; and the learners also followed him.
And having come to be upon the place, he said to them: Pray not to enter into testing.
And he himself was drawn away from them about a stone's throw, and having placed the knees he was praying,
saying: Father, if you will, carry aside this cup from me; nevertheless let not my will but the your come to be.
And there was seen by him an angel from heaven strengthening him.
And having come to be in agony, more stretched-out he was praying; and his sweat became as clots of blood coming down upon the earth.
And having stood up from the prayer, having come toward the learners, he found them sleeping from the grief,
and he said to them: Why do you sleep? Having stood up, pray, so that you may not enter into testing.
While he was yet speaking, behold a crowd, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them; and he drew near to the Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus said to him: Judas, with a kiss the Son of Man do you hand over?
And the ones around him, having seen the thing about to be, said to him: Lord, shall we strike with a sword?
And a certain one out of them struck the slave of the chief priest and took away his right ear, the right one.
But answering, the Jesus said: Allow until this. And having touched the little ear, he healed him.
And the Jesus said toward the ones having come out upon him — chief priests and commanders of the temple and elders: As upon a robber did you come out with swords and wooden clubs?
According to the day, of me being with you in the temple, you did not stretch out the hands upon me; but this is your hour and the authority of the darkness.
And having seized him, they led and brought him into the house of the chief priest; but the Peter was following far off.
And of them having kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and having sat down together, Peter was sitting in the midst of them.
And a certain young female slave, having seen him sitting toward the light and having gazed intently at him, said: Also this one was with him.
But he denied him saying: I do not know him, woman.
And after a short while, another having seen him declared: Also you are out of them. But the Peter declared: Human, I am not.
And about one hour having stood apart, a certain other was strongly insisting saying: Upon truth also this one was with him; for indeed he is a Galilean.
But the Peter said: Human, I do not know what you say. And instantly, while he was yet speaking, a cock sounded.
And having turned, the Lord looked into the Peter; and the Peter was reminded of the word of the Lord, as he said to him that: Before a cock to sound today, you will deny me three times.
And having gone outside, the Peter wept bitterly.
And the men, the ones holding him together, were mocking him, flaying him.
And having covered him around, they were questioning him saying: Prophesy, who is the one having struck you?
And many other things, blaspheming, they were saying against him.
And as day came to be, the eldership of the people was gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away into their council,
saying: If you are the Christ, tell us. And he said to them: If to you I should say, you may by no means trust;
and if I should question, you may by no means answer me, or release.
But from the now there will be the Son of Man sitting out of right hand parts of the power of the God.
And they all said: You therefore are the Son of the God? And he toward them declared: You say that I am.
And they said: What still do we have need of witness? For we ourselves heard from his mouth.

luke_23.t: And having stood up, the whole multitude of them led him upon the Pilate.
And they began to accuse him saying: This one we found perverting our nation and hindering to give tributes to Caesar and saying himself to be Christ, a king.
And the Pilate questioned him saying: You are the king of the Jews? And he, answering him, declared: You say.
And the Pilate said toward the chief priests and the crowds: Nothing I find causative in this human.
But they were growing strong saying that: He stirs up the people, teaching down the whole of the Judea and having begun from the Galilee until here.
And Pilate, having heard, questioned if the human is a Galilean;
and having come to know that he is out of the authority of Herod, he sent him up toward the Herod, being also himself in Jerusalem in these days.

And the Herod, having seen the Jesus, rejoiced greatly; for he was for considerable times wishing to see him, through the hearing many things concerning him, and he was hoping some sign to see coming to be by him.
And he was questioning him in considerable words; but he answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and the scribes had stood, intensely accusing him.
And having treated him as nothing, also the Herod together with his troops, and having mocked, having thrown around him bright clothing, he sent him back to the Pilate.
And there came to be friends both the Herod and the Pilate on that very day with one another; for they were previously being in enmity toward themselves.
And Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
said toward them: You brought to me this human as turning away the people; and behold I, before you having examined, found nothing in this human causative of the things which you accuse against him;
but neither Herod; for he sent him back toward us; and behold, nothing worthy of death is having been done by him.
Having disciplined him therefore, I will release.
[And he was having necessity to release to them according to feast one.]
But they cried out all-together saying: Take away this one, but release to us the Barabbas.
who was, through a certain insurrection having come to be in the city and murder, having been thrown in the prison.
And again the Pilate called toward them, wishing to release the Jesus.
But they were calling upon, saying: Crucify, crucify him.
And he, a third time, said toward them: For what evil did this one do? Nothing causative of death I found in him; having disciplined him therefore, I will release.
But they were lying upon with great voices, asking for him to be crucified, and their voices were prevailing, and of the chief priests.
And Pilate judged upon their request to come to be.
And he released the one having been thrown into the prison through insurrection and murder, whom they were asking for; but the Jesus he handed over to their will.
And as they led him away, having taken hold of Simon, a certain Cyrenian coming from a field, they placed upon him the cross to carry behind the Jesus.
And there was following him a great multitude of the people and of women who were also beating themselves and lamenting him.
And having turned toward them, the Jesus said: Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep upon me; nevertheless upon yourselves weep and upon your children.
Because behold, days are coming in which they will say: Blessed the barren ones and the wombs which did not bear and breasts which did not nourish.
Then they will begin to say to the mountains: Fall upon us; and to the hills: Cover us.
Because if in the moist wood these things they do, in the dry what may come to be?
And there were being led also others, criminals two, together with him to be taken up.
And when they came upon the place, the one called Skull, there they crucified him and the criminals, the one out of right hand parts and the one out of left hand parts.
And the Jesus was saying: Father, release to them, for they do not know what they do. And dividing up his garments, they threw lots.
And the people had stood beholding. But the rulers also were sneering out, saying: Others he saved; let him save himself, if this one is the Christ of the God, the chosen one.
And there mocked him also the soldiers coming toward, and bringing to him vinegar-wine,
and saying: If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.
And there was also an inscription having been written upon him in Greek and Roman and Hebrew letters: This is the king of the Jews.
And one of the criminals having been hanged was blaspheming him saying: Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us.
But answering, the other, rebuking him, declared: Do you not even fear the God, because in the same judgement you are?
And we indeed justly, for things worthy of what we did we are receiving back; but this one nothing out of place did.
And he was saying: To the Jesus, remember me, Lord, whenever you should come into your kingdom.
And Jesus said to him: Amen to you I say, today with me you will be in the paradise.
And it was already about hour sixth, and darkness came to be upon whole the earth until hour ninth,
of the sun having failed. And there was torn the curtain of the temple-shrine in the middle.
And having called with a great voice, the Jesus said: Father, into your hands I place alongside my spirit. And this having said, he breathed out.
And having seen the thing having come to be, the centurion was glorifying the God saying: Really this human was righteous.
