And all the crowds having come together upon this spectacle, having beheld the things having come to be, beating their own chests were returning.
And there had stood all the ones known to him from far off, and women, the ones following together with him from the Galilee, seeing these things.
And behold, a man by name Joseph, being a councillor, and a man good and righteous —
this one was not having consented together with the plan and the action of them — from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who was also himself awaiting the kingdom of God.
This one, having come toward the Pilate, asked for himself the body of the Jesus.
And having taken it down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth and placed him in a tomb hewn in rock, where no one was yet lying.
And a day it was of Preparation, and sabbath was dawning upon.
And having followed down, also the women, such as were having come together with him out of the Galilee, beheld the tomb and how his body was placed.
And having returned, they prepared spices and ointments; and on the one hand the sabbath they kept quiet according to the commandment.

luke_24.t: But on the one of the sabbaths, of deep dawn, upon the tomb they came bearing the spices which they prepared, and certain ones together with them.
But they found the stone having been rolled away from the tomb.
And having entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And it came to be, in the being perplexed of them concerning this, and behold, two men stood by them in flashing clothing.
And of them having become in fear and bending the faces into the earth, they said toward them: Why do you seek the living one with the dead ones?
He is not here, but he was raised. Remember how he spoke to you, being still in the Galilee,
saying the Son of Man that it is necessary to be handed over into hands of sinful humans and to be crucified and on the third day to stand up.
And they were reminded of his words.
And having returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
And they were the Magdalene Mary and Joanna and Mary the of James, and the rest with them; they were saying toward the sent-ones these things,
And these words appeared before them as if raving, and they were disbelieving them.
But the Peter, having stood up, ran upon the tomb, and having stooped alongside, he sees the linen strips alone; and he went away toward himself marvelling at the thing having come to be.
And behold, two out of them on that same day were journeying into a village standing away sixty stadia from Jerusalem, to which the name Emmaus,
and they themselves were conversing toward one another concerning all these things having come together.
And it came to be, in the conversing of them and discussing together, and he himself, Jesus, having drawn near, was journeying together with them;
but their eyes were being held of the not to recognise him.
And he said toward them: What are these words which you throw back and forth toward one another walking about? And they stood still, gloomy-faced.
And answering, the one out of them, to whom by name Cleopas, said toward him: You alone dwell as a stranger in Jerusalem and did not know the things having come to be in her in these days?
And he said to them: What sort of things? And they said to him: The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who became a man, a prophet powerful in work and word before the God and all the people,
how both handed him over the chief priests and our rulers into a judgement of death, and crucified him.
But we were hoping that he himself is the one about to ransom the Israel; but indeed also together with all these things, this third day it leads today from which these things came to be.
But also certain women out of us astounded us, having come to be at daybreak upon the tomb,
and not having found his body, they came saying also a sight of angels to have seen, who say him to live.
And there went away certain of the ones together with us upon the tomb, and they found thus just as also the women said; but him they did not see.
And he himself said toward them: O unperceiving ones and slow in the heart of the to trust upon all which the prophets spoke;
Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?
And having begun from Moses and from all the prophets, he thoroughly interpreted to them in all the writings the things concerning himself.
And they drew near into the village where they were journeying, and he himself made a show of journeying farther.
And they constrained him saying: Remain with us, because toward evening it is and the day has already declined. And he entered in to remain together with them.
And it came to be, in the reclining of him with them, having taken the bread he blessed, and having broken he was giving over to them.
And of them the eyes were thoroughly opened, and they recognised him; and he himself became unseen from them.
And they said toward one another: Was not our heart burning in us as he was speaking to us in the way, as he was opening thoroughly to us the writings?
And having stood up in that very hour, they returned into Jerusalem, and they found having been gathered together the eleven and the ones together with them,
saying that: Really the Lord was raised and was seen by Simon.
And they themselves were leading out the things in the way and how he was known to them in the breaking of the bread.
And these things of them speaking, he himself stood in the midst of them and says to them: Peace to you.
But having been terrified and having become in fear, they were supposing to behold a spirit.
And he said to them: Why having been troubled are you, and through what do reasonings go up in your heart?
See my hands and my feet, that I myself am he; handle me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones just as you behold me having.
And this having said, he showed them the hands and the feet.
And still of them disbelieving from the joy and marvelling, he said to them: Do you have anything edible here?
And they gave over to him a part of a broiled fish [and from a bee's honeycomb].
And having taken it, before them he ate.

And he said toward them: These are my words which I spoke toward you being still together with you, that it is necessary to be fulfilled all the things having been written in the law of Moses and the prophets and psalms concerning me.
Then he opened thoroughly their mind of the to understand the writings.
And he said to them that: Thus it has been written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to stand up out of dead ones on the third day,
and to be heralded upon his name a change of mind into release of sins into all the nations, having begun from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And behold, I send out the promise of my Father upon you; but you, sit in the city until which you should be clothed with power out of height.
And he led them out outside until toward Bethany, and having lifted up his hands he blessed them.
And it came to be, in the blessing of him them, he stood apart from them and was borne up into the heaven.
And they, having worshipped him, returned into Jerusalem with great joy,
and they were through everything in the temple praising and blessing the God. [Amen]

matthew_1.t: Book of the genesis of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham begot Isaac; and Isaac begot Jacob; and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers;
and Judah begot Perez and Zerah out of Tamar; and Perez begot Hezron; and Hezron begot Ram;
and Ram begot Amminadab; and Amminadab begot Nahshon; and Nahshon begot Salmon;
and Salmon begot Boaz out of Rahab; and Boaz begot Obed out of Ruth; and Obed begot Jesse;
and Jesse begot David the king; and David the king begot Solomon out of the [wife] of Uriah;
and Solomon begot Rehoboam; and Rehoboam begot Abijah; and Abijah begot Asaph;
and Asaph begot Jehoshaphat; and Jehoshaphat begot Joram; and Joram begot Uzziah;
and Uzziah begot Jotham; and Jotham begot Ahaz; and Ahaz begot Hezekiah;
and Hezekiah begot Manasseh; and Manasseh begot Amos; and Amos begot Josiah;
and Josiah begot Jechoniah and his brothers, at the removal-of-dwelling of Babylon.
And after the removal-of-dwelling of Babylon, Jechoniah begot Shealtiel; and Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel;
and Zerubbabel begot Abiud; and Abiud begot Eliakim; and Eliakim begot Azor;
and Azor begot Zadok; and Zadok begot Achim; and Achim begot Eliud;
and Eliud begot Eleazar; and Eleazar begot Matthan; and Matthan begot Jacob;
and Jacob begot Joseph the man of Mary, out of whom was born Jesus, the one called Christ.

All the generations therefore from Abraham until David [are] fourteen generations, and from David until the removal-of-dwelling of Babylon fourteen generations, and from the removal-of-dwelling of Babylon until the Christ fourteen generations.
Now of Jesus Christ the genesis was thus: his mother Mary having been betrothed to Joseph, before their coming together she was found having [a child] in the belly out of holy spirit.
And Joseph her man, being righteous and not willing to expose her, purposed to release her secretly.

But as he was pondering these things, behold, a messenger of [the] Lord appeared to him according to a dream, saying: Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take alongside Mary your woman; for the [thing] begotten in her is out of holy spirit.
And she will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus; for he will save his people from their sins.
Now this whole [thing] has happened so that there might be fulfilled the [word] spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying:
Behold, the virgin will have [a child] in the belly and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel — which is, being translated, God with us.
And Joseph, having been raised from the sleep, did as the messenger of [the] Lord ordered him, and took alongside his woman,
and he was not knowing her until she bore her son, the firstborn; and he called his name Jesus.

matthew_2.t: Now Jesus having been born in Bethlehem of Judea in [the] days of Herod the king, behold, magi from [the] risings came to Jerusalem,
saying: Where is the one born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the rising, and we came to prostrate ourselves to him.
And King Herod having heard was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him,
and having gathered together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he was inquiring from them where the Christ is born.
And they said to him: In Bethlehem of Judea; for thus it has been written through the prophet:
And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the leaders of Judah; for out of you will come forth one leading, who will shepherd my people Israel.
Then Herod, having secretly called the magi, ascertained exactly from them the time of the appearing star,

and having sent them to Bethlehem he said: Having gone, search out exactly concerning the little child; and when you find [him], report back to me, so that I also, having come, may prostrate myself to him.
And they, having heard the king, went. And behold, the star which they saw in the rising was going before them, until having come it stood over where the little child was.
And having seen the star they rejoiced [with] joy great exceedingly.

And having come into the house they saw the little child with Mary his mother, and having fallen they prostrated themselves to him; and having opened their treasures they brought to him gifts: gold and frankincense and myrrh.
And having been divinely instructed according to a dream not to return to Herod, through another road they withdrew into their own country.

And they having withdrawn, behold, a messenger of [the] Lord appears according to a dream to Joseph, saying: Having been raised, take alongside the little child and his mother and flee into Egypt, and be there until I tell you; for Herod is about to seek the little child to destroy it.
And he, having been raised, took alongside the little child and his mother by night and withdrew into Egypt,
and was there until the end of Herod, so that there might be fulfilled the [word] spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt I called my son.

Then Herod, having seen that he was mocked by the magi, was greatly enraged, and having sent he took up all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its borders, from two years and under, according to the time which he ascertained exactly from the magi.
Then was fulfilled the [word] spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
A voice in Ramah was heard, lamentation and weeping and much mourning, Rachel weeping [for] her children, and she was not willing to be comforted, because they are not.
But Herod having come to his end, behold, a messenger of [the] Lord appears according to a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
saying: Having been raised, take alongside the little child and his mother and go into [the] land of Israel; for those seeking the life of the little child have died.
And he, having been raised, took alongside the little child and his mother and entered into [the] land of Israel.

But having heard that Archelaus reigns over Judea instead of his father Herod, he feared to go away there; and having been divinely instructed according to a dream he withdrew into the parts of Galilee,
and having come he dwelt in a city called Nazareth, so that there might be fulfilled the [word] spoken through the prophets that he will be called a Nazorean.

matthew_3.t: Now in those days arrives John the Baptist, heralding in the wilderness of Judea
and saying: Be changing [your] mind, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying: A voice of one shouting in the wilderness: Prepare the road of [the] Lord, make straight his paths.
And John himself had his garment from hairs of a camel and a leather belt around his loin; and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then was going out to him Jerusalem and all Judea and all the surrounding country of the Jordan,
and were being baptised in the Jordan river by him, confessing out their sins.
But having seen many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them: Broods of vipers, who showed you to flee from the coming wrath?
Make therefore fruit worthy of the change of mind.
And do not think to say in yourselves: We have Abraham [as] father. For I say to you that God is able out of these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
And already also the axe lies toward the root of the trees; every tree therefore not making good fruit is cut out and into fire is thrown.
I indeed baptise you in water into a change of mind; but the one coming after me is stronger than I, of whom I am not sufficient to bear the sandals; he will baptise you in holy spirit and fire.

Whose winnowing-shovel [is] in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing-floor and will gather together his wheat into the storehouse; but the chaff he will burn down with unquenchable fire.
Then arrives Jesus from Galilee at the Jordan to John, to be baptised by him.
But John was hindering him, saying: I have need to be baptised by you, and you come to me?
But Jesus answering said to him: Permit [it] now; for thus it is fitting for us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he permits him.
And Jesus, having been baptised, immediately went up from the water; and behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the spirit of God descending as a dove and coming upon him.
And behold, a voice out of the heavens saying: This is my son, the beloved, in whom I was well pleased.

matthew_4.t: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the spirit, to be tested by the devil.
And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward he hungered.
And the one testing, having come, said to him: If you are son of God, speak that these stones may become loaves.
But he answering said: It has been written: Not on bread alone will the human live, but on every word going out through [the] mouth of God.
Then the devil takes him alongside into the holy city, and stood him on the little wing of the temple

and says to him: If you are son of God, throw yourself down; for it has been written that to his messengers he will give charge concerning you, and on hands they will lift you up, lest ever you strike against a stone your foot.
Jesus said to him: Again it has been written: You shall not test out [the] Lord your God.
Again the devil takes him alongside into a mountain exceedingly high, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
and said to him: All these things to you I will give, if having fallen you prostrate yourself to me.
Then Jesus says to him: Go away behind me, Satan; for it has been written: [The] Lord your God you shall worship, and him only shall you render service.
Then the devil leaves him, and behold, messengers came and were ministering to him.
But Jesus, having heard that John was handed over, withdrew into Galilee.
And having left behind Nazara, having come he dwelt in Capernaum beside the sea, in [the] borders of Zebulun and Naphtali,
so that there might be fulfilled the [word] spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying:
Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, way of [the] sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations,
the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and to those sitting in [the] country and shadow of death, a light rose upon them.
From then Jesus began to herald and to say: Be changing [your] mind, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
And walking beside the sea of Galilee he saw two brothers, Simon the one called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a casting-net into the sea; for they were fishers.
And he says to them: Come here after me, and I will make you fishers of humans.
And they immediately, having left the nets, followed him.
And having gone on from there he saw other two brothers, Jacob the [son] of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, putting in order their nets, and he called them.
And they immediately, having left the boat and their father, followed him.
And Jesus was going about in the whole of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and heralding the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

And the report of him went away into the whole of Syria; and they brought to him all those having [it] badly, held together by various diseases and tortures, and demonised and moonstruck and paralytics; and he healed them.
And there followed him many crowds from Galilee and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea and beyond the Jordan.

matthew_5.t: And having seen the crowds he went up into the mountain, and he having sat, his disciples came to him.
And having opened his mouth he was teaching them, saying:
Fortunate the poor in the spirit, because theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Fortunate those mourning, because they themselves will be comforted.
Fortunate the meek, because they themselves will inherit the land.
Fortunate those hungering and thirsting [for] righteousness, because they themselves will be satisfied.
Fortunate the merciful, because they themselves will be shown mercy.
Fortunate the clean in the heart, because they themselves will see God.
Fortunate the peace-makers, because they themselves will be called sons of God.
Fortunate those having been persecuted on account of righteousness, because theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Fortunate are you whenever they reproach you and persecute [you] and say every evil word against you, lying, on account of me.
Rejoice and exult, because your wage [is] much in the heavens; for thus they persecuted the prophets before you.
You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt is made foolish, with what will it be salted? It is strong for nothing still except, having been thrown outside, to be trampled down by the humans.
You are the light of the world; a city is not able to be hidden lying upon a mountain;
nor do they burn a lamp and place it under the measuring-basket, but upon the lampstand, and it shines for all those in the house.
Thus let your light shine before the humans, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father, the [one] in the heavens.
Do not suppose that I came to loose down the law or the prophets; I did not come to loose down but to fulfil.
For Amen I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away, one iota or one horn shall not pass away from the law until all things happen.

Whoever therefore looses one of these least commandments and teaches the humans thus, least will he be called in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches [them], this one great will be called in the kingdom of the heavens.
For I say to you that unless your righteousness exceeds more than [that] of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
You heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not murder; and whoever murders will be liable to the judgement.

But I say to you that everyone being angry with his brother [without cause] will be liable to the judgement; and whoever says to his brother: Raka — will be liable to the Sanhedrin; and whoever says: Moron — will be liable into the Gehenna of the fire.
If therefore you bring your gift upon the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave there your gift before the altar, and go away, first be reconciled to your brother, and then having come bring your gift.

Be well-minded toward your opponent-at-law quickly, while you are with him on the road, lest ever the opponent hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the attendant, and into prison you be thrown.
Amen I say to you, you shall not come out from there until you pay back the last quadrans.
You heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not commit adultery.
But I say to you that everyone looking at a woman toward the desiring of her has already committed adultery [with] her in his heart.
And if your right eye scandalises you, tear it out and throw [it] from you; for it profits you that one of your members perish and not your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand scandalises you, cut it off and throw [it] from you; for it profits you that one of your members perish and not your whole body go away into Gehenna.
And it was said that whoever releases his wife, let him give her a document-of-standing-apart.
But I say to you that everyone releasing his wife apart from a word of porneia makes her to be adulterated; and whoever marries a released woman commits adultery.
Again you heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not swear falsely, but you shall pay back to the Lord your oaths.
But I say to you not to swear at all: neither by the heaven, because it is God's throne,
neither by the earth, because it is a footstool of his feet; neither toward Jerusalem, because it is a city of the great king;
neither by your head shall you swear, because you are not able [to] make one hair white or black.
But let your word be Yes yes, No no; and the excess of these is out of the evil one.
You heard that it was said: An eye instead of an eye, and a tooth instead of a tooth.
But I say to you not to stand against the evil one. But whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him also the other.
And to the one willing to be judged with you and to take your tunic, leave to him also the outer garment.
And whoever will requisition you one mile, go with him two.
To the one asking you give, and the one willing to borrow from you do not turn away from.
You heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.
But I say to you: love your enemies, bless those cursing you, do well to those hating you, and pray on behalf of those insulting you and persecuting you,
so that you may become sons of your Father, the [one] in the heavens, because his sun he raises upon evil and good, and he rains upon righteous and unrighteous.
For if you love those loving you, what wage have you? Do not also the tax-farmers do the same?
And if you greet your brothers only, what excess do you do? Do not also the gentiles do the same?
You shall be therefore complete, as your heavenly Father is complete.

matthew_6.t: But take heed not to do your righteousness before the humans toward being seen by them; otherwise you have no wage with your Father, the [one] in the heavens.

Whenever therefore you do mercy-giving, do not trumpet before you, just as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the lanes, so that they may be glorified by the humans. Amen I say to you, they have received in full their wage.
But you doing mercy-giving, let not your left hand know what your right hand does,
so that your mercy-giving may be in the hidden; and your Father, the one seeing in the hidden, he himself will give back to you in the open.

And whenever you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, because they love in the synagogues and in the corners of the wide streets standing to pray, so that they may appear to the humans. Amen I say to you, they have received in full their wage.

But you, whenever you pray, enter into your inner-room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father, the [one] in the hidden; and your Father, the one seeing in the hidden, will give back to you in the open.
And praying, do not batter-words as the gentiles [do]; for they suppose that in their much-speaking they will be heard.
Do not therefore be made like to them; for God your Father knows of what things you have need before your asking him.
Thus therefore pray you: Our Father, the [one] in the heavens, let your name be made holy;
Let your kingdom come; let your will be brought about, as in heaven also upon the earth.
Our bread, the daily [one], give us today;
and release to us our debts, as also we released to our debtors;
and do not bring us into testing, but rescue us from the evil one. [Because yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory into the ages. Amen.]
For if you release to the humans their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also release to you;
But if you do not release to the humans their trespasses, neither will your Father release your trespasses.

And whenever you fast, do not become as the hypocrites, sullen-faced; for they make invisible their faces so that they may appear to the humans fasting. Amen I say to you, they have received in full their wage.
But you, fasting, anoint your head and wash your face,
so that you may not appear to the humans fasting but to your Father, the [one] in the concealed; and your Father, the one seeing in the concealed, will give back to you in the open.
Do not treasure up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and eating make invisible, and where thieves dig through and steal;
But treasure up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor eating makes invisible, and where thieves do not dig through nor steal.
For where your treasure is, there also will be your heart.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is single, your whole body will be luminous.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. If therefore the light in you is darkness, the darkness — how great!
No one is able to slave for two lords; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to one and despise the other. You are not able to slave for God and mammon.

On account of this I say to you, do not be anxious for your soul, what you may eat or what you may drink, nor for your body, what you may put on. Is not the soul more than the food, and the body [more] than the clothing?
Look into the birds of the heaven, that they do not sow nor reap nor gather together into storehouses, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Do you not rather differ from them?
And who out of you by being anxious is able to add upon his stature one cubit?
And concerning clothing, why are you anxious? Learn thoroughly the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not toil nor spin.
But I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed as one of these.
And if the grass of the field, being today and tomorrow being thrown into an oven, God thus clothes, [will he] not much more you, [you] of little faith?
Do not therefore be anxious, saying: What may we eat? or: What may we drink? or: What may we put on?
For all these things the nations seek after; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not therefore be anxious for the tomorrow, for the tomorrow will be anxious [for] itself. Sufficient for the day [is] its own badness.

matthew_7.t: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged;
For with what judgement you judge, you will be judged; and with what measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
And why do you look at the chip in the eye of your brother, but the beam in your own eye you do not perceive?
Or how will you say to your brother: Let me cast out the chip from your eye — and behold, the beam [is] in your eye?
Hypocrite, cast out first from your eye the beam, and then you will see through to cast out the chip from the eye of your brother.
Do not give the holy [thing] to the dogs, nor throw your pearls before the swine, lest they trample them down with their feet and, having turned, tear you.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone asking receives, and the one seeking finds, and to the one knocking it will be opened.
Or what human is there of you who, if his son asks [for] bread — he will not hand him a stone?
Or also if he asks [for] a fish — he will not hand him a serpent?
If therefore you, being evil, know [how] to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father, the [one] in the heavens, give good things to those asking him.
All things therefore, as many as you wish that the humans should do to you, thus also you do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate, because wide [is] the gate and spacious the road leading away into the destruction, and many are those entering through it.
How narrow [is] the gate and having-been-pressed the road leading away into the life, and few are those finding it.
But beware of the false prophets, who come to you in garments of sheep, but inside are rapacious wolves.
From their fruits you will recognise them. Surely they do not gather from thorns grapes, or from thistles figs?
Thus every good tree makes good fruits, but the rotten tree makes evil fruits.
A good tree is not able to make evil fruits, nor a rotten tree to make good fruits.
Every tree not making good fruit is cut out and into fire is thrown.
So then from their fruits you will recognise them.
Not everyone saying to me: Lord, Lord — will enter into the kingdom of the heavens, but the one doing the will of my Father, the [one] in the heavens.
Many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many powers?
And then I will confess to them that: Never did I know you; depart from me, those working the lawlessness.
Everyone therefore who hears these my words and does them will be likened to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
And everyone hearing these my words and not doing them will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and struck against that house, and it fell, and its fall was great.
And it happened, when Jesus finished these words, the crowds were astounded at his teaching;
For he was teaching them as having authority, and not as their scribes.

matthew_8.t: And he having come down from the mountain, many crowds followed him.
And behold, a leper having come was prostrating himself to him, saying: Lord, if you are willing, you are able to cleanse me.
And having stretched out the hand, Jesus touched him, saying: I am willing, be cleansed. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
And Jesus says to him: See [that] you tell no one, but go away, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift which Moses ordered, for a witness to them.
And he having entered into Capernaum, there came to him a centurion, calling upon him
and saying: Lord, my boy has been laid in the house, paralysed, terribly tormented.
And he says to him: I, having come, will heal him.
And the centurion answering said: Lord, I am not sufficient that you should enter under my roof; but only speak with a word, and my boy will be healed.

For I also am a human under authority, being appointed, having under myself soldiers; and I say to this one: Go — and he goes; and to another: Come — and he comes; and to my slave: Do this — and he does [it].
And Jesus having heard was amazed, and said to those following: Amen I say to you, from no one so great faith in Israel have I found.
But I say to you that many from risings and settings will come and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens,
But the sons of the kingdom will be cast out into the darkness, the outer; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
And Jesus said to the centurion: Go, and as you believed let it be brought about for you. And his boy was healed in that hour.
And Jesus having come into the house of Peter saw his mother-in-law having been laid and burning with fever;
And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she was raised and was serving him.
And evening having come, they brought to him many demonised; and he cast out the spirits with a word, and all those having [it] badly he healed,
so that there might be fulfilled the [word] spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying: He himself took our weaknesses and bore the diseases.
And Jesus having seen many a crowd around him, ordered to go away to the other side.
And one scribe having come said to him: Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go away.
And Jesus says to him: The foxes have holes and the birds of the heaven nests, but the Son of Man has not where he may lay the head.
And another of his disciples said to him: Lord, permit me first to go away and bury my father.
But Jesus says to him: Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.
And he having embarked into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And behold, a great shaking happened in the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but he was sleeping.
And having come, his disciples raised him, saying: Lord, save us, we are perishing.
And he says to them: Why are you cowardly, [you] of little faith? Then having been raised he rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
And the humans were amazed, saying: What sort is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?

And he having come to the other side into the country of the Gadarenes, there met him two demonised coming out from the tombs, exceedingly harsh, so that no one was strong [enough] to pass by through that road.
And behold, they cried out saying: What to us and to you, Jesus son of God? Did you come here before [the] season to torment us?
But there was far from them a herd of many swine feeding.
And the demons were calling upon him, saying: If you cast us out, permit — send us into the herd of the swine.
And he said to them: Go. And they having come out went away into the herd of the swine; and behold, the whole herd of the swine rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they died in the waters.
And those feeding [them] fled, and having gone away into the city they reported all things, and the things of the demonised.
And behold, all the city came out to a meeting with Jesus, and having seen him they called upon him so that he might depart from their borders.

matthew_9.t: And having embarked into the boat he crossed over and came into his own city.
And behold, they were bringing to him a paralytic laid upon a bed. And Jesus having seen their faith said to the paralytic: Take courage, child, your sins are released.
And behold, some of the scribes said in themselves: This one blasphemes.
And Jesus having seen their thoughts said: Why do you think evil things in your hearts?
For which is easier: to say, Your sins are released — or to say, Rise and walk?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority upon the earth to release sins — then he says to the paralytic: Having been raised, take up your bed and go away into your house.
And having been raised he went away into his house.
And the crowds having seen were afraid, and glorified God, the one having given such authority to the humans.
And Jesus passing along from there saw a human sitting at the tax-office, called Matthew, and he says to him: Follow me. And having stood up he followed him.
And it happened, he reclining in the house, and behold, many tax-farmers and sinners having come were reclining with Jesus and his disciples.
And the Pharisees having seen said to his disciples: Why with the tax-farmers and sinners does your teacher eat?
But he having heard said to them: Those being strong have no need of a physician, but those having [it] badly.
But having gone, learn what it is: Mercy I desire and not sacrifice; for I did not come to call righteous [ones] but sinners into a change of mind.
Then come to him the disciples of John, saying: Why do we and the Pharisees fast much, but your disciples do not fast?

And Jesus said to them: Are the sons of the bridechamber able to mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days will come whenever the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
But no one puts a patch of unfulled rag upon an old garment; for its fullness takes away from the garment, and a worse split happens.

Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins are burst, and the wine is poured out, and the wineskins perish. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are kept together.

These things he speaking to them, behold, one ruler having come was prostrating himself to him, saying that: My daughter just now came to her end; but having come lay your hand upon her, and she will live.
And Jesus having been raised followed him, and his disciples.
And behold, a woman hemorrhaging twelve years, having come from behind, touched the fringe of his garment.
For she was saying in herself: If only I touch his garment, I will be saved.
But Jesus having turned and having seen her said: Take courage, daughter, your faith has saved you. And the woman was saved from that hour.
And Jesus having come into the house of the ruler, and having seen the flute-players and the crowd being in an uproar,
he was saying: Withdraw, for the little girl did not die but sleeps. And they were laughing down at him.
But when the crowd was cast out, having entered he took hold of her hand, and the little girl was raised.
And this report went out into that whole land.
And Jesus passing along from there, there followed him two blind [men] crying out and saying: Have mercy on us, son of David.
And he having come into the house, the blind [men] came to him, and Jesus says to them: Do you believe that I am able to do this? They say to him: Yes, Lord.
Then he touched their eyes, saying: According to your faith let it be brought about for you.
And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly charged them, saying: See, let no one know.
But they having gone out spread the report of him in that whole land.
And they going out, behold, they brought to him a mute human, demonised.
And the demon having been cast out, the mute spoke. And the crowds were amazed, saying that: Never was it seen thus in Israel.
But the Pharisees were saying: By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.
And Jesus was going about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and heralding the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
And having seen the crowds he was moved in the guts concerning them, because they were harassed and cast down like sheep not having a shepherd.
Then he says to his disciples: The harvest indeed [is] much, but the workers few.
Beg therefore the Lord of the harvest that he may cast out workers into his harvest.

matthew_10.t: And having called to himself his twelve learners, he gave them authority of unclean spirits, so as to throw them out and to heal every disease and every weakness.
Now of the twelve sent-ones the names are these: first Simon, the one called Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James the son of Zebedee and John his brother,
Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthaios the tax-farmer, James the son of Alphaeus and Lebbaios the one surnamed Thaddaeus,
Simon the Cananaean and Judas the Iscariot, the one who also handed him over.
These twelve Jesus sent out, charging them, saying: Into a road of nations do not go away, and into a city of Samaritans do not enter;
But go rather to the sheep, the ones having been lost, of the house of Israel.
And going, proclaim, saying that the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
Heal weak ones, raise dead ones, cleanse lepers, throw out demons. Freely you received, freely give.
Do not acquire gold nor silver nor copper for your belts,
no travelling-bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for worthy is the worker of his food.
And into whatever city or village you enter, search out who in it is worthy, and there remain until you go out.
And entering into the house, greet it.
And if on the one hand the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace be turned back to you.
And whoever does not receive you nor hear your words, going out outside that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Amen I say to you, more bearable will it be for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in a day of judgement than for that city.
Behold, I myself send you as sheep in the midst of wolves; become therefore prudent as the serpents and unmixed as the doves.
But beware of the humans; for they will hand you over into councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;
and before governors and also kings you will be led on account of me, for a witness to them and to the nations.
But whenever they hand you over, do not be anxious how or what you might speak; for it will be given to you in that hour what you shall speak;
For you are not the ones speaking but the Spirit of your Father, the one speaking in you.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and father child; and children will rise up against parents and will put them to death.
And you will be being hated by all on account of my name; but the one having endured to the end, this one will be saved.
But whenever they persecute you in this city, flee into the other; for amen I say to you, you will certainly not complete the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.
A learner is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his lord.
Sufficient for the learner that he become as his teacher, and the slave as his lord. If the house-master they surnamed Beelzeboul, how much more his house-members?
Therefore do not fear them; for nothing is having been covered which will not be uncovered, and hidden which will not be known.
What I say to you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what into the ear you hear, proclaim upon the housetops.
And do not fear from the ones killing the body but not being able to kill the soul; but fear rather the one being able both soul and body to destroy in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? And one of them will not fall upon the earth without your Father.
But of you even the hairs of the head all have been numbered.
Therefore do not fear; you differ from many sparrows.
Everyone therefore who will confess in me before the humans, I also will confess in him before my Father, the one in the heavens.
But whoever denies me before the humans, I also will deny him before my Father, the one in the heavens.
Do not consider that I came to throw peace upon the earth; I did not come to throw peace but a sword.
For I came to divide a human against his father and a daughter against her mother and a bride against her mother-in-law,
and the enemies of the human are his house-members.
The one loving father or mother above me is not worthy of me, and the one loving son or daughter above me is not worthy of me;
and whoever does not take his cross and follow behind me is not worthy of me.
The one having found his soul will destroy it, and the one having destroyed his soul on account of me will find it.
The one receiving you receives me, and the one receiving me receives the one having sent me.
The one receiving a prophet in the name of a prophet will take a prophet's wage, and the one receiving a righteous one in the name of a righteous one will take a righteous one's wage.
And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold to drink in the name of a learner, amen I say to you, he will certainly not destroy his wage.

matthew_11.t: And it happened, when Jesus finished ordering his twelve learners, he went over from there to teach and to proclaim in their cities.
But John, having heard in the prison the works of the Christ, having sent through his learners
said to him: Are you the coming one, or another do we expect?
And answering Jesus said to them: Going, report to John what you hear and see:
Blind ones see again, and lame ones walk about, lepers are cleansed, and deaf ones hear, and dead ones are raised, and poor ones are given good news.
And blessed is whoever is not made to stumble in me.
But as these were going, Jesus began to say to the crowds concerning John: What did you go out into the wilderness to gaze at? A reed being shaken by wind?
But what did you go out to see? A human clothed in soft garments? Behold, the ones wearing the soft things are in the houses of the kings.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more excessive than a prophet.
For this is he concerning whom it has been written: Behold, I myself send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your road before you.
Amen I say to you, there has not been raised among ones born of women a greater than John the Baptist; but the lesser one in the kingdom of the heavens is greater than he.
But from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of the heavens is forced, and forcers snatch it.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to receive it, he himself is Elijah, the one about to come.
The one having ears, let him hear.
But to what shall I liken this generation? It is like little children sitting in the marketplaces who, calling to the others,
say: We piped to you and you did not dance; we mourned and you did not beat yourselves.
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: He has a demon.
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: Behold, a human, a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax-farmers and of sinners. And wisdom was vindicated from her works.
Then he began to reproach the cities in which happened the most of his powers, because they did not change their minds.

Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; because if in Tyre and Sidon had happened the powers, the ones having happened in you, long ago in sackcloth and ashes they would have changed their minds.
Nevertheless I say to you, for Tyre and for Sidon more bearable will it be in a day of judgement than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? Unto Hades you will go down; because if in Sodom had happened the powers, the ones having happened in you, it would have remained until today.
Nevertheless I say to you that for the land of Sodom more bearable will it be in a day of judgement than for you.
In that time Jesus answering said: I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and of the earth, because you hid these things from wise and understanding ones and revealed them to infants.
Yes, the Father, because thus good pleasure came to be before you.
All things were handed over to me by my Father, and no one fully knows the Son except the Father, nor the Father does anyone fully know except the Son and to whomever the Son wills to reveal.
Come to me all the ones toiling and having been burdened, and I will rest you.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am meek and lowly in the heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is serviceable and my burden is light.

matthew_12.t: In that time Jesus went on the sabbaths through the sown fields; and his learners were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
But the Pharisees having seen said to him: Behold, your learners do what is not permitted to do on a sabbath.
But he said to them: Did you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him?
How he entered into the house of God and they ate the loaves of the setting-out, which was not permitted for him to eat nor for the ones with him, except for the priests alone?
Or did you not read in the law that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are guiltless?
But I say to you that greater than the temple is here.
But if you had known what is: Mercy I want and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless ones.
For lord is even of the sabbath the Son of Man.
And having gone over from there he came into their synagogue.
And behold, a human was there having the hand withered; and they questioned him saying: Is it permitted on the sabbaths to heal? — so that they might accuse him.
But he said to them: What human will there be of you who will have one sheep, and if this falls on the sabbaths into a pit, will he not take hold of it and raise it?
By how much then does a human differ from a sheep! So it is permitted on the sabbaths to do well.
Then he says to the human: Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and it was restored healthy as the other.
But the Pharisees having gone out took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
But Jesus having known withdrew from there; and many crowds followed him, and he healed them all,
and he rebuked them so that they might not make him manifest,
so that might be fulfilled the thing spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying:
Behold my child, whom I chose, my beloved in whom my soul was well pleased. I will place my Spirit upon him, and judgement to the nations he will announce.
He will not wrangle nor cry out, nor will anyone hear in the broad ways his voice.
A reed having been crushed he will not break, and a flax-wick smoking he will not quench, until he throws out judgement into victory.
And in his name nations will hope.
Then was brought to him one demonised, blind and mute, and he healed him, so that the mute and blind one both spoke and saw.
And all the crowds were amazed and said: This one is not the Son of David, is he?
But the Pharisees having heard said: This one does not throw out the demons except by Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons.
But knowing their reasonings he said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is made desolate, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
And if the Satan throws out the Satan, upon himself he was divided; how then will his kingdom stand?
And if I by Beelzeboul throw out the demons, your sons by whom do they throw out? On account of this they themselves will be your judges.
But if by the Spirit of God I throw out the demons, then the kingdom of God came upon you.
Or how is anyone able to enter into the house of the strong one and to snatch his vessels, unless first he binds the strong one? And then he will plunder his house.
The one not being with me is against me, and the one not gathering with me scatters.
On account of this I say to you: every sin and blasphemy will be released for the humans, but the blasphemy of the Spirit will not be released.
And whoever says a word against the Son of Man, it will be released for him; but whoever says against the Holy Spirit, it will not be released for him, neither in this now age nor in the coming one.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for from the fruit the tree is known.
Broods of vipers, how are you able good things to speak, being evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
The good human out of the good treasure of the heart throws out good things, and the evil human out of the evil treasure throws out evil things.
But I say to you that every idle word which the humans will speak, they will give back concerning it an account in a day of judgement.
For out of your words you will be justified, and out of your words you will be condemned.
Then answered him some of the scribes and Pharisees, saying: Teacher, we want from you a sign to see.
But he answering said to them: An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster three days and three nights, so will be the Son of Man in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
Ninevite men will stand up in the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because they changed their minds at the proclamation of Jonah, and behold, more than Jonah here.

A queen of the south will be raised in the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, more than Solomon here.
But whenever the unclean spirit goes out from the human, it goes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find.
Then it says: Into my house I will return from where I came out. And having come it finds it unoccupied and having been swept and having been put in order.

Then it goes and takes along with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having entered it dwells there; and the last things of that human become worse than the first. Thus will it be also for this evil generation.
But while he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, the mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
But someone said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.
But he answering said to the one telling him: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
And having stretched out his hand over his learners he said: Behold my mother and my brothers.
For whoever does the will of my Father, the one in heavens, he is my brother and sister and mother.

matthew_13.t: In that day Jesus, having gone out of the house, was sitting beside the sea.
And there were gathered to him many crowds, so that he, having embarked into the boat, was sitting, and all the crowd on the beach had stood.
And he spoke to them many things in parables, saying: Behold, the sower went out to sow.
And in his sowing, some on the one hand fell beside the road, and the birds having come devoured them.
But other fell upon the rocky places where it did not have much earth, and immediately it sprang up on account of not having depth of earth.
But the sun having risen it was scorched, and on account of not having root it was dried up.
But other fell upon the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.
But other fell upon the earth, the good one, and was giving fruit, this one a hundred, this one sixty, this one thirty.
The one having ears to hear, let him hear.
And the learners having come said to him: Why in parables do you speak to them?
But he answering said to them: Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to those it has not been given.
For whoever has, it will be given to him and he will be made to abound; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
On account of this in parables to them I speak, because seeing they do not see and hearing they do not hear nor understand.
And is filled up upon them the prophecy of Isaiah, the one saying: With hearing you will hear and shall certainly not understand, and seeing you will see and shall certainly not perceive.

For the heart of this people was made fat, and with the ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they closed; lest ever they should see with the eyes and with the ears should hear and with the heart should understand and should turn, and I will heal them.
But of you blessed are the eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.
For amen I say to you that many prophets and righteous ones desired to see what you see and did not see, and to hear what you hear and did not hear.
You therefore hear the parable of the one having sown:
Of everyone hearing the word of the kingdom and not understanding, there comes the evil one and snatches what has been sown in his heart; this is the one sown beside the road.
But the one upon the rocky places sown, this is the one hearing the word and immediately with joy receiving it;
but he does not have root in himself but is temporary; and when tribulation or persecution happens on account of the word, immediately he is made to stumble.
But the one into the thorns sown, this is the one hearing the word, and the anxiety of this age and the deceit of the riches chokes the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
But the one upon the good earth sown, this is the one hearing the word and understanding, who indeed bears fruit and makes, this one a hundred, this one sixty, this one thirty.
Another parable he set before them, saying: The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a human having sowed good seed in his field.
But in the sleeping of the humans, his enemy came and sowed over darnel in the midst of the wheat, and went away.
But when the grass sprouted and made fruit, then appeared also the darnel.
And the slaves of the house-master having come said to him: Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where then does it have the darnel?
But he said to them: An enemy human did this. But the slaves say to him: Do you want then, having gone away, we should gather them?
But he says: No, lest ever gathering the darnel you should uproot together with them the wheat.

Leave both to grow together until the harvest; and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather first the darnel and bind them into bundles for the burning of them, but the wheat gather together into my storehouse.
Another parable he set before them, saying: Like is the kingdom of the heavens to a grain of mustard, which a human having taken sowed in his field.
Which is smaller on the one hand than all the seeds, but whenever it is grown it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the heaven come and encamp in its branches.
Another parable he spoke to them: Like is the kingdom of the heavens to leaven, which a woman having taken hid into three measures of meal until the whole was leavened.
These things all Jesus spoke in parables to the crowds, and without a parable he was speaking nothing to them,
so that might be fulfilled the thing spoken through the prophet, saying: I will open in parables my mouth, I will belch out things having been hidden from the foundation of the world.
Then having left the crowds Jesus came into the house. And there came to him his learners, saying: Make clear to us the parable of the darnel of the field.
But he answering said to them: The one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man.
And the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the darnel are the sons of the evil one;
and the enemy, the one having sown them, is the devil; and the harvest is the completion of the age; and the reapers are messengers.
Just as therefore is gathered the darnel and with fire is burned up, thus will it be in the completion of this age.
The Son of Man will send out his messengers, and they will gather out of his kingdom all the stumbling-traps and the ones doing lawlessness,
and will throw them into the furnace of the fire; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth.
Then the righteous ones will shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. The one having ears, let him hear.
Like is the kingdom of the heavens to treasure having been hidden in the field, which a human having found hid; and from his joy he goes and sells all as much as he has and buys that field.
Again like is the kingdom of the heavens to a human, a merchant, seeking good pearls.
Who having found one very valuable pearl, having gone away has sold all as much as he had and bought it.
Again like is the kingdom of the heavens to a dragnet thrown into the sea and having gathered from every kind;
which when it was filled, having drawn it up upon the beach and having sat down, they gathered the good into vessels, but the rotten they threw outside.
Thus will it be in the completion of the age: the messengers will go out and will mark off the evil ones from the midst of the righteous ones,
and will throw them into the furnace of the fire; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth.
Jesus says to them: Did you understand these things all? They say to him: Yes, lord.

But he said to them: On account of this every scribe having been made a learner for the kingdom of the heavens is like a human, a house-master, who throws out of his treasure new things and old things.
And it happened, when Jesus finished these parables, he departed from there;
and having come into his fatherland he was teaching them in their synagogue, so as to astonish them and to say: From where to this one this wisdom and the powers?
Is not this one the son of the craftsman? Is not his mother called Mariam, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And his sisters, are they not all with us? From where then to this one all these things?
And they were being made to stumble in him. But Jesus said to them: A prophet is not dishonoured except in his fatherland and in his house.
And he did not do there many powers on account of their untrustingness.

matthew_14.t: In that time Herod the tetrarch heard the hearing of Jesus
and said to his servants: This one is John the Baptist; he himself was raised from the dead, and on account of this the powers work in him.
For Herod having seized John bound him and put him away in the prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother.
For John was saying to him: It is not permitted for you to have her.
And wanting to kill him he feared the crowd, because as a prophet they were holding him.
But birthday celebrations having come to be of Herod, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst and pleased Herod;
from where with an oath he confessed to give to her whatever she should ask.
But she, having been pushed forward by her mother: Give me, she says, here upon a platter the head of John the Baptist.
And having been grieved, the king, but on account of the oaths and the ones reclining together, ordered it to be given;
And having sent he beheaded John in the prison.
And his head was brought upon a platter and was given to the little girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And having come, his learners took the corpse and buried it, and having come they reported to Jesus.
And Jesus having heard withdrew from there in a boat into a deserted place by himself; and the crowds having heard followed him on foot from the cities.
And having gone out he saw a great crowd and was moved in the guts over them and healed their sick ones.

But evening having come there came to him the learners, saying: Deserted is the place and the hour already has gone by; release the crowds so that having gone away into the villages they may buy for themselves food.
But Jesus said to them: They have no need to go away; you yourselves give to them to eat.
But they say to him: We do not have here except five loaves and two fish.
But he said: Bring them to me here.

And having ordered the crowds to recline upon the grass, having taken the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up into the heaven he blessed, and having broken he gave to the learners the loaves, and the learners to the crowds.
And all ate and were satisfied, and they took up the abounding of the fragments, twelve hand-baskets full.
But the ones eating were men about five thousand, apart from women and children.
And immediately he compelled the learners to embark into the boat and to go before him into the other side, until he should release the crowds.
And having released the crowds he went up into the mountain by himself to pray. And evening having come, alone he was there.
But the boat already many stadia from the land was holding off, being tormented by the waves; for the wind was contrary.
But in the fourth watch of the night he came to them walking upon the sea.
But the learners having seen him upon the sea walking were troubled, saying that it is a phantom, and from the fear they cried out.
But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying: Take courage, I am; do not fear.
And Peter answering him said: Lord, if you are, order me to come to you upon the waters.
But he said: Come. And having come down from the boat Peter walked upon the waters and came towards Jesus.
But seeing the wind strong he was afraid, and having begun to be sunk he cried out, saying: Lord, save me.
And immediately Jesus having stretched out the hand took hold of him and says to him: Little-truster, into what did you doubt?
And they having gone up into the boat, the wind grew weary.
But the ones in the boat, having come, prostrated themselves before him, saying: Truly of God you are Son.
And having crossed over they came upon the land into Gennesaret.
And having recognised him, the men of that place sent into that whole surrounding country and brought to him all the ones having badly,
and they were calling upon him that only they might touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched were carried safely through.

matthew_15.t: Then there come to Jesus the ones from Jerusalem, Pharisees and scribes, saying:
Why do your learners step over the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands whenever they eat bread.
But he answering said to them: Why do also you yourselves step over the commandment of God on account of your tradition?
For God said, saying: Honour the father and the mother, and: The one speaking badly of father or mother, by death let him come to an end.
But you yourselves say: Whoever says to the father or to the mother: A gift, whatever from me you might be benefited —
and he shall certainly not honour his father of him or his mother of him; and you invalidated the word of God on account of your tradition.
Hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy concerning you, saying:
This people draws near to me with their mouth, and with the lips honours me, but their heart far off holds away from me.
But in vain they revere me, teaching teachings, commandments of humans.
And having called to himself the crowd he said to them: Hear and understand;
Not the thing entering into the mouth makes the human common, but the thing going out from the mouth, this makes the human common.
Then having come the learners say to him: Do you know that the Pharisees having heard the word were made to stumble?
But he answering said: Every planting which my Father, the heavenly one, did not plant will be rooted up.
Leave them; blind ones they are, guides of blind ones. But a blind one if he guides a blind one, both into a pit will fall.
And Peter answering said to him: Declare to us this parable.
But he said: Even now are you yourselves also without understanding?
Do you not perceive that everything travelling into the mouth into the belly goes and into a latrine is thrown out?
But the things going out from the mouth out of the heart come out, and those things make the human common.
For out of the heart come out evil reasonings, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false witnessings, blasphemies.
These things are the ones making the human common; but the eating with unwashed hands does not make the human common.
And having gone out from there Jesus withdrew into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.
And behold, a Canaanite woman from those borders having come out was crying out to him, saying: Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter badly is demonised.
But he did not answer her a word. And having come to him his learners were asking him, saying: Release her, because she cries out behind us.
But he answering said: I was not sent except to the sheep, the ones having been lost, of the house of Israel.
But she having come was prostrating herself before him, saying: Lord, help me.
But he answering said: It is not good to take the bread of the children and to throw it to the little dogs.
But she said: Yes, lord; for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs, the ones falling from the table of their lords.
Then answering, Jesus said to her: O woman, great is your trust; let it come to be for you as you want. And her daughter was healed from that hour.
And having gone over from there Jesus came beside the sea of Galilee, and having gone up into the mountain he was sitting there.
And there came to him many crowds having with themselves lame ones, blind ones, maimed ones, mute ones, and many others, and they flung them beside his feet; and he healed them,
so as for the crowd to marvel, seeing mute ones speaking, maimed ones whole, and lame ones walking about, and blind ones seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.

But Jesus, having called to himself his learners, said: I am moved in the guts over the crowd, because already three days they remain with me and do not have what they might eat; and to release them fasting I do not want, lest ever they be unstrung on the road.
And his learners say to him: From where to us in a desolate place loaves so many as to satisfy a crowd so great?
And Jesus says to them: How many loaves do you have? And they said: Seven, and a few little fish.
And having charged the crowd to fall back upon the ground,
and he took the seven loaves and the fish, and having given thanks he broke and was giving to his learners, and the learners to the crowds.
And all ate and were satisfied, and the abounding of the fragments they took up, seven large baskets full.
But the ones eating were four thousand men, apart from women and children.
And having released the crowds he embarked into the boat and came into the borders of Magadan.

matthew_16.t: And having come, the Pharisees and Sadducees, testing, questioned him to display to them a sign out of the heaven.
But he answering said to them: Evening having come you say: Fair weather, for the heaven is fiery red.
And at dawn: Today a storm, for the heaven is fiery red, being gloomy. Hypocrites, the face of the heaven on the one hand you know to discern, but the signs of the times you are not able?
An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. And having left them behind he went away.
And the learners having come into the other side forgot to take loaves.
But Jesus said to them: See and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
But they were reasoning among themselves, saying that loaves we did not take.
But Jesus having known said to them: Why do you reason among yourselves, little-trusters, that loaves you do not have?
Do you not yet perceive, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand and how many hand-baskets you took?
Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand and how many large baskets you took?
How do you not perceive that not concerning loaves I said to you? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Then they understood that he did not say to beware of the leaven of the loaves, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
But having come, Jesus into the parts of Caesarea of Philip was asking his learners, saying: Whom do the humans say the Son of Man to be?
And they said: Some on the one hand John the Baptist, but others Elijah, and different ones Jeremiah or one of the prophets.
He says to them: But you yourselves, whom do you say me to be?
And Simon Peter answering said: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
And Jesus answering said to him: Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal it to you but my Father, the one in the heavens.
And I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my assembly, and gates of Hades will not prevail against it.

And I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens; and whatever you should bind upon the earth will be having been bound in the heavens, and whatever you should loose upon the earth will be having been loosed in the heavens.
Then he charged the learners that to no one should they say that he himself is Jesus the Christ.

From then began Jesus Christ to show to his learners that it is necessary for him into Jerusalem to go away and many things to suffer from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and to be killed, and on the third day to be raised.
And having taken him aside, Peter began to rebuke him, saying: Merciful to you, Lord; this shall certainly not be for you.
But he having turned said to Peter: Go behind me, Satan; a stumbling-trap you are of me, because you do not mind the things of God but the things of the humans.
Then Jesus said to his learners: If anyone wants behind me to come, let him deny himself and let him take his cross and let him follow me.
For whoever wants his soul to save will destroy it; but whoever destroys his soul on account of me will find it.
For what will a human be benefited if the whole world he should gain but his soul he should be fined? Or what will a human give as an exchange for his soul?
For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his messengers, and then he will give back to each according to his practice.
Amen I say to you that there are some of the ones standing here who shall certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.

matthew_17.t: And after six days Jesus takes along Peter and James and John his brother and brings them up into a high mountain by themselves.
And he was transformed before them, and his face shone as the sun, and his garments became white as the light.
And behold, there was seen by them Moses and Elijah talking together with him.
And Peter answering said to Jesus: Lord, good it is for us here to be; if you want, I will make here three tents, for you one and for Moses one and for Elijah one.
While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my Son, the beloved one, in whom I was well pleased; hear him.
And the learners having heard fell upon their face and were exceedingly afraid.
And Jesus came and having touched them said: Be raised and do not fear.
But having lifted up their eyes they saw no one except him, Jesus alone.
And as they were coming down out of the mountain Jesus commanded them, saying: To no one tell the vision until the Son of Man out of dead ones is raised.
And the learners questioned him, saying: Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
But Jesus answering said to them: Elijah on the one hand comes first and will restore all things;
But I say to you that Elijah already came, and they did not recognise him but did in him as much as they wanted; thus also the Son of Man is about to suffer by them.
Then the learners understood that concerning John the Baptist he spoke to them.
And they having come to the crowd, there came to him a human kneeling before him
Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is moonstruck and badly suffers; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.
And I brought him to your learners, and they were not able to heal him.
And Jesus answering said: O generation untrusting and having been perverted, until when with you shall I be? Until when shall I bear with you? Bring him to me here.
And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out from him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Then having come, the learners to Jesus privately said: Why were we not able to throw it out?

But he says to them: On account of your little-trust. For amen I say to you, if you have trust as a grain of mustard, you will say to this mountain: Move over from here to there, and it will move over; and nothing will be impossible for you.
[But this kind does not go out except in prayer and fasting.]
And as they were gathering together in Galilee Jesus said to them: The Son of Man is about to be handed over into hands of humans,
and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised. And they were exceedingly grieved.
And they having come into Capernaum, there came the ones taking the two-drachmas to Peter and said: Your teacher does not pay the two-drachmas?

He says: Yes. And when he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: What does it seem to you, Simon? The kings of the earth, from whom do they take customs or census-tax? From their sons or from the strangers?
And he having said: From the strangers, Jesus said to him: Then indeed free are the sons.

But so that we might not make them stumble, having gone to the sea throw a hook, and the first fish coming up take, and having opened its mouth you will find a stater; that one having taken give to them for me and you.

matthew_18.t: In that hour there came the learners to Jesus, saying: Who then is greater in the kingdom of the heavens?
And having called to himself a little child, he stood it in the midst of them
and said: Amen I say to you, unless you turn and become as the little children, you shall certainly not enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
Whoever therefore will humble himself as this little child, this one is the greater in the kingdom of the heavens.
And whoever receives one such little child upon my name receives me.
But whoever makes to stumble one of these little ones, the ones trusting into me, it is advantageous for him that a donkey-millstone be hung around his neck and he be sunk in the open sea.
Woe to the world from the stumbling-traps; for it is necessary that the stumbling-traps come, nevertheless woe to that human through whom the stumbling-trap comes.

But if your hand or your foot makes you stumble, cut it off and throw it from you; good for you it is to enter into the life maimed or lame than having two hands or two feet to be thrown into the fire, the eternal one.
And if your eye makes you stumble, take it out and throw it from you; good for you it is one-eyed into the life to enter than having two eyes to be thrown into the Gehenna of the fire.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their messengers in heavens through all continually see the face of my Father, the one in heavens.
[For the Son of Man came to save the thing having been lost.]

What does it seem to you? If there should come to be to a certain human a hundred sheep and one of them should be led astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine upon the mountains and having gone seek the one being led astray?
And if it comes about to find it, amen I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine, the ones not having been led astray.
Thus it is not a will before your Father, the one in heavens, that one of these little ones should perish.
But if your brother sins against you, go and expose him between you and him alone; if he hears you, you gained your brother.
