But if he does not hear, take along with you still one or two, so that upon the mouth of two witnesses or three every word may be stood.
But if he disregards them, tell it to the assembly; but if also the assembly he disregards, let him be to you just as the outsider and the tax-farmer.

Amen I say to you, as many things as you should bind upon the earth will be having been bound in the heaven, and as many things as you should loose upon the earth will be having been loosed in the heaven.
Again amen I say to you that if two of you should agree upon the earth concerning every matter, whatever they should ask, it will come to be for them from my Father, the one in heavens.
For where two or three are having been gathered into my name, there I am in the midst of them.
Then having come, Peter said to him: Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I will release him? Until seven times?
Jesus says to him: I do not say to you until seven times but until seventy times seven.
On account of this the kingdom of the heavens was likened to a human, a king, who wanted to take up accounts with his slaves.
And of him having begun to take up, there was brought to him one debtor of ten thousand talents.
But he not having to give back, the lord ordered him to be sold, and the wife and the children and all as much as he has, and it to be given back.
Having fallen therefore, the slave was prostrating before him, saying: Lord, be long-tempered over me, and all I will give back to you.
And having been moved in the guts, the lord of that slave released him and the loan he released for him.
But having gone out, that slave found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and having seized him he was choking him, saying: Give back if you owe anything.
Having fallen therefore, his fellow slave at his feet was calling upon him, saying: Be long-tempered over me, and I will give back to you.
But he was not willing, but having gone away he threw him into prison until he should give back the thing owed.
Having seen therefore his fellow slaves the things having happened, they were exceedingly grieved, and having come they made thoroughly clear to their lord all the things having happened.
Then having called him to himself, his lord says to him: Evil slave, all that debt I released for you, since you called upon me;
Was it not necessary also for you to have mercy on your fellow slave, as I also had mercy on you?
And having been enraged, his lord handed him over to the torturers until he should give back all the thing owed to him.
Thus also my Father, the heavenly one, will do to you if you do not release, each one his brother, from your hearts, their trespasses.

matthew_19.t: And it happened, when Jesus finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
And large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
And the Pharisees came to him testing him and saying to him, "Is it permitted for a human to release his wife for every cause?"
And answering he said to them, "Have you not read that the one who created from the beginning made them male and female,
and said, 'For this reason a human will leave the father and the mother and will be glued to his wife, and the two will be into one flesh' —
so that they are no longer two but one flesh. What therefore God yoked together, let a human not separate."
They say to him, "Why then did Moses command to give a scroll of divorce and to release her?"
He says to them that "Moses, toward the hardness of your heart, permitted you to release your wives; but from the beginning it has not happened so.
And I say to you that whoever releases his wife, except upon sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and the one who marries her who has been released commits adultery."
His learners say to him, "If the case of the human with the wife is like this, it is not advantageous to marry."
But he said to them, "Not all make room for this word, but those to whom it has been given.

For there are eunuchs who were begotten thus from a mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by humans, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs on account of the kingdom of the heavens. The one able to make room, let him make room."
Then children were brought to him so that he might lay the hands on them and pray; but the learners rebuked them.
But Jesus said, "Leave the children and do not hinder them from coming to me, for of such is the kingdom of the heavens."
And having laid the hands on them he went from there.
And behold, one coming to him said, "Good teacher, what good shall I do so that I may have eternal life?"
But he said to him, "Why do you ask me concerning the good? One is the good. But if you wish to enter into the life, keep the commandments."
He says to him, "Which?" And Jesus said, "The: you shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness,
honour the father and the mother, and you shall love your neighbour as yourself."
The young man says to him, "All these I guarded from my youth; what do I still lack?"
Jesus said to him, "If you wish to be complete, go, sell your belongings and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heavens, and come, follow me."
But hearing this word the young man went away grieving, for he was having many possessions.
And Jesus said to his learners, "Amen I say to you that a rich person will enter into the kingdom of the heavens with difficulty.
And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to go through a hole of a needle than for a rich person to enter into the kingdom of God."
And hearing, his learners were exceedingly struck out, saying, "Who then is able to be saved?"
And looking at them Jesus said to them, "With humans this is impossible, but with God all things are possible."
Then answering, Peter said to him, "Behold, we left all and followed you; what then will be for us?"

And Jesus said to them, "Amen I say to you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits upon a throne of his glory, you also will sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields on account of my name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
But many will be first last, and last first.

matthew_20.t: For the kingdom of the heavens is like a human, a master of a house, who went out together with early morning to hire workers into his vineyard.
And having agreed with the workers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
And going out about the third hour he saw others standing in the marketplace idle,
and to those he said, "Go, you also, into the vineyard, and whatever may be just I will give you."
And they went away. And again going out about the sixth and ninth hour he did likewise.
And about the eleventh hour, going out, he found others standing idle, and he says to them, "Why have you stood here the whole day idle?"
They say to him that "No one hired us." He says to them, "Go, you also, into the vineyard, and whatever may be just you will receive."
And evening having come, the lord of the vineyard says to his steward, "Call the workers and give back to them the wage, beginning from the last until the first."
And coming, those about the eleventh hour received each a denarius.
And coming, the first supposed that they would receive more; and they also received each a denarius.
And receiving it they were grumbling against the master of the house,
saying that "These last did one hour, and you made them equal to us, who bore the weight of the day and the burning heat."
But answering to one of them he said, "Companion, I do not wrong you; did you not agree with me for a denarius?
Take what is yours and go; but I wish to give to this last one as also to you.
Or is it not permitted for me to do what I wish with my own things? Or is your eye evil because I am good?"
Thus will the last be first and the first last; for many are called, but few chosen.
And Jesus, being about to go up to Jerusalem, took aside the twelve learners privately, and on the road he said to them,
"Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
and they will hand him over to the nations for mocking and flogging and crucifying; and on the third day he will be raised."
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, bowing down and asking something from him.
And he said to her, "What do you wish?" She says to him, "Say that these my two sons may sit one at your right hand and one at your left in your kingdom."

And answering Jesus said, "You do not know what you ask for. Are you able to drink the cup which I am about to drink, and to be baptised with the baptism with which I am baptised?" They say to him, "We are able."

And he says to them, "My cup indeed you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptised you will be baptised; but to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give, but to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
And hearing, the ten were indignant concerning the two brothers.
But Jesus, calling them to himself, said, "You know that the rulers of the nations lord it down over them, and the great ones exercise authority down over them.
But it shall not be so among you; but whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant,
and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave;
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom in place of many."
And as they were going out from Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
And behold, two blind men sitting beside the road, hearing that Jesus is passing by, cried out saying, "Have mercy on us, Lord Jesus, Son of David."
But the crowd rebuked them that they should be silent; but they cried out the more, saying, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David."
And standing still, Jesus called them and said, "What do you wish I should do for you?"
They say to him, "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
And moved in the guts, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they saw again, and they followed him.

matthew_21.t: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came into Bethphage to the Mount of the Olives, then Jesus sent two learners,
saying to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied and a colt with her; loosing them, lead them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, you shall say that 'The Lord has need of them'; and immediately he will send them."
But this whole thing has happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
"Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, meek and mounted upon a donkey and upon a colt, son of a beast of burden."
And the learners, going and doing just as Jesus arranged for them,
led the donkey and the colt and put upon them their garments, and he sat upon them.
And the very great crowd spread their own garments in the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them in the road.
And the crowds going before him and those following were crying out saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest."
And when he entered into Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, "Who is this?"
And the crowds were saying, "This is the prophet Jesus, the one from Nazareth of Galilee."
And Jesus entered into the temple of God and threw out all those selling and buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling the doves,
and he says to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer'; but you make it a cave of robbers."
And blind and lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
But the chief priests and the scribes, seeing the wonders which he did and the children crying out in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David," were indignant,
and said to him, "Do you hear what these say?" And Jesus says to them, "Yes. Did you never read that 'Out of the mouth of infants and nursing ones you prepared praise'?"
And leaving them behind he went outside the city into Bethany, and lodged there.
And early, returning to the city, he hungered.

And seeing one fig tree by the road he came upon it and found nothing on it except leaves only, and he says to it, "May fruit no longer come from you for ever." And immediately the fig tree was dried up.
And seeing it the learners marvelled, saying, "How immediately was the fig tree dried up?"

And answering, Jesus said to them, "Amen I say to you, if you have trust and are not divided, not only will you do the thing of the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted and be thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
And all things, whatever you may ask in prayer, trusting, you will receive."
And when he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him teaching, saying, "By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?"
And answering, Jesus said to them, "I also will ask you one word, which if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John — from where was it? From heaven or from humans?" And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why then did you not trust him?'
But if we say, 'From humans,' we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet."
And answering Jesus they said, "We do not know." He also said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
But what does it seem to you? A human had two children, and coming to the first he said, 'Child, go today, work in the vineyard.'
And answering he said, 'I do not wish'; but later, having changed his mind, he went.
And coming to the other he said likewise. And answering he said, 'I, lord,' and did not go.
Which of the two did the will of the father?" They say to him, "The first." Jesus says to them, "Amen I say to you that the tax-farmers and the prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of God.
For John came to you in a way of righteousness, and you did not trust him; but the tax-farmers and the prostitutes trusted him. And you, seeing it, did not even change your minds later, to trust him.
Hear another parable. There was a human, a master of a house, who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug in it a winepress and built a tower, and let it out to farmers and went abroad.
And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the farmers to receive his fruits.
And the farmers, taking his slaves, one they beat, one they killed, one they stoned.
Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did to them likewise.
And later he sent to them his son, saying, 'They will be put to shame before my son.'
But the farmers, seeing the son, said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.'
And taking him they threw him outside the vineyard and killed him.
When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?"
They say to him, "Bad ones, badly he will destroy them, and he will let out the vineyard to other farmers, who will give back to him the fruits in their seasons."
Jesus says to them, "Did you never read in the scriptures: 'A stone which the builders rejected, this became into a head of a corner; from the Lord this came about, and it is marvellous in our eyes'?
Because of this I say to you that the kingdom of God will be taken from you and will be given to a nation producing its fruits.
And the one falling upon this stone will be shattered together; but on whomever it may fall, it will winnow him.
And hearing his parables, the chief priests and the Pharisees knew that he speaks about them.
And seeking to seize him they feared the crowds, since they held him as a prophet.

matthew_22.t: And answering, Jesus again spoke to them in parables, saying:
"The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a human, a king, who made a wedding for his son.
And he sent his slaves to call those who had been called to the wedding, and they were not willing to come.

Again he sent other slaves, saying, 'Say to those who have been called: Behold, my dinner I have prepared, my bulls and the fattened animals have been sacrificed, and all things are ready; come into the wedding.'
But they, having no care, went off, one to his own field, another to his trading.
And the rest, seizing his slaves, insulted and killed them.
And hearing, that king was angered, and sending his armies he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he says to his slaves, 'The wedding indeed is ready, but those who had been called were not worthy.
Go therefore onto the crossings of the roads, and as many as you may find, call into the wedding.'
And going out into the roads, those slaves gathered together all whom they found, both evil and good; and the wedding was filled with those reclining.
And the king, entering to view those reclining, saw there a human not clothed with a garment of wedding,
and he says to him, 'Companion, how did you enter here not having a garment of wedding?' And he was muzzled.
Then the king said to the servants, 'Binding his feet and hands, take and throw him out into the outer darkness; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth.'
For many are called, but few chosen."
Then the Pharisees, going, took counsel how they might trap him in a word.

And they send to him their learners with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that you are true and teach the way of God in truth, and it is not a care to you concerning anyone, for you do not look into the face of humans.
Say therefore to us, what does it seem to you? Is it permitted to give a poll-tax to Caesar or not?"
But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said, "Why do you test me, hypocrites?
Show me the coin of the poll-tax." And they brought to him a denarius.
And he says to them, "Whose is this image and the inscription?"
They say to him, "Caesar's." Then he says to them, "Give back therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God."
And hearing, they marvelled, and leaving him they went away.
In that day Sadducees came to him, those saying there is no resurrection, and they questioned him,
saying, "Teacher, Moses said, 'If someone dies not having children, his brother shall marry as next of kin his wife and shall raise up seed for his brother.'
Now there were with us seven brothers, and the first, having married, died, and not having seed he left his wife to his brother;
likewise also the second and the third, up to the seven.
And last of all the woman died.
In the resurrection therefore, of which of the seven will she be wife? For all had her."
And answering, Jesus said to them, "You are led astray, not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are as angels of God in heaven.
But concerning the resurrection of the dead, did you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying:
'I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'? God is not God of dead ones but of living ones."
And hearing, the crowds were struck out at his teaching.
But the Pharisees, hearing that he muzzled the Sadducees, were gathered together upon the same place.
And one of them, a lawyer, questioned him, testing him and saying,
"Teacher, what kind of commandment is great in the law?"
And he said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God in your whole heart and in your whole soul and in your whole mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And a second like it: 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself.'
In these two commandments the whole law hangs, and the prophets."
And the Pharisees having been gathered, Jesus questioned them,
saying, "What does it seem to you concerning the Christ? Whose son is he?" They say to him, "David's."
He says to them, "How then does David in spirit call him Lord, saying:
'The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies underneath your feet'?
If therefore David calls him Lord, how is he his son?"
And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day to question him any longer.

matthew_23.t: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his learners,
saying, "Upon the seat of Moses sat the scribes and the Pharisees.
All things therefore, whatever they tell you, do and keep; but according to their works do not do, for they say and do not do.
And they bind heavy and hard-to-bear burdens and place them upon the shoulders of humans; but they themselves with their finger do not wish to move them.
But all their works they do toward being seen by humans; for they widen their phylacteries and enlarge the fringes of their garments.
And they love the first couch at the dinners and the first seats in the synagogues,
and the greetings in the marketplaces and to be called by humans, 'Rabbi, Rabbi.'
But you, do not be called Rabbi; for one is your teacher, and you all are brothers.
And do not call your father upon the earth, for one is your Father, the heavenly one.
Neither be called guides, because your guide is one, the Christ.
But the greater of you shall be your servant.
And whoever will exalt himself will be humbled, and whoever will humble himself will be exalted.
But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of the heavens before humans; for you do not enter, nor do you allow those entering to enter.
[Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour the houses of the widows, and for a pretext praying at length; because of this you will receive a heavier judgement.]
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you go around the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as you.
Woe to you, blind guides, those saying, 'Whoever swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the sanctuary is obligated.'
Fools and blind, for which is greater, the gold or the sanctuary that sanctified the gold?
And, 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift upon it is obligated.'
Blind ones, for which is greater, the gift or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
The one therefore having sworn by the altar swears by it and by all the things upon it;
and the one having sworn by the sanctuary swears by it and by the one dwelling in it;
and the one having sworn by the heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one sitting upon it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe the mint and the dill and the cumin, and you left the weightier things of the law: the judgement and the mercy and the trust. But these it was necessary to do, and not to leave those aside.
Blind guides, those straining out the gnat but gulping down the camel.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you cleanse the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside they are full from plunder and lack of self-control.
Blind Pharisee, cleanse first the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that also the outside of it may become clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitened tombs, which outside indeed appear beautiful, but inside are full of bones of dead ones and of all uncleanness.
Thus also you outside indeed appear righteous to humans, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
and you say, 'If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets.'
So that you witness to yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
And you, fill up the measure of your fathers.
Serpents, offspring of vipers, how may you flee from the judgement of Gehenna?

Because of this, behold, I send to you prophets and wise ones and scribes; and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and will persecute from city to city,

so that upon you may come all righteous blood poured out upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous until the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Amen I say to you that all these things will come upon this generation.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one killing the prophets and stoning those sent to her, how often I wished to gather together your children, in the manner a bird gathers together her young under the wings — and you were not willing.
Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
For I say to you, you will certainly not see me from now until you say, 'Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord.'"

matthew_24.t: And Jesus, going out from the temple, was going away, and his learners came to show him the buildings of the temple.
And answering he said to them, "Do you not see all these things? Amen I say to you, there will certainly not be left here stone upon stone which will not be thrown down."

And as he was sitting upon the Mount of the Olives, the learners came to him privately, saying, "Tell us, when will these things be, and what is the sign of your coming and of the completion of the age?"
And answering, Jesus said to them, "See that no one leads you astray.
For many will come upon my name saying, 'I am the Christ,' and will lead many astray.
But you will be about to hear wars and hearings of wars; see, do not be disturbed; for it is necessary for all to happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will be raised against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in places.
But all these things are a beginning of birth-pangs.
Then they will hand you over into affliction and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of my name.
And then many will be scandalised and will hand over one another and will hate one another.
And many false prophets will be raised and will lead many astray.
And because of the lawlessness being multiplied, the love of the many will grow cold.
But the one having endured to the end, this one will be saved.
And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.
When therefore you see the abomination of the desolation, the thing spoken through Daniel the prophet, standing in a holy place — let the one reading understand —
then let those in Judea flee into the mountains;
let the one upon the housetop not go down to take the things out of his house;
and let the one in the field not turn back to take his garment.
But woe to those having in the womb and to those nursing in those days.
But pray that your flight may not happen in winter nor on a sabbath.
For there will be then great affliction, such as has not happened from a beginning of a world until now, nor ever will happen.
And unless those days were shortened, no flesh would be saved; but on account of the chosen ones those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Christ' or 'Here,' do not trust it.
For false christs and false prophets will be raised and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
Behold, I have told you beforehand.
If therefore they say to you, 'Behold, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Behold, in the inner chambers,' do not trust it.
For just as the lightning comes out from risings and appears until settings, so will be also the coming of the Son of Man.
For wherever the fallen body may be, there will the eagles be gathered together.

But immediately after the affliction of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give her radiance, and the stars will fall from the heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

And then will appear the sign of the Son of Man in the heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will beat themselves, and they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of the heaven with power and much glory.
And he will send his angels with a trumpet of a great sound, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the extremities of the heavens until their extremities.
But from the fig tree learn the parable: when already its branch becomes tender and puts out the leaves, you know that the summer is near.
Thus also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at doors.
Amen I say to you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
The heaven and the earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels of the heavens nor the Son, except my Father alone.
For just as the days of Noah, so will be also the coming of the Son of Man.
For as they were in those days, the ones before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered into the ark,
and they did not know until the flood came and took all away, so will be also the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two will be in the field; the one is taken along and the one is left.
Two grinding at the mill; one is taken along and one is left.
Watch therefore, because you do not know on what day your Lord comes.
But know that, if the master of the house had known in which watch the thief comes, he would have watched and would not have allowed his house to be dug through.
Because of this you also become ready, because in an hour which you do not suppose the Son of Man comes.
Who then is the faithful and prudent slave whom his lord set over his household to give to them the food in season?
Blessed is that slave whom his lord, having come, will find doing thus.
Amen I say to you that over all his belongings he will set him.
But if that evil slave says in his heart, 'My lord delays to come,'
and begins to beat his fellow slaves, and eats and drinks with the drunken,
the lord of that slave will come on a day which he does not expect and in an hour which he does not know,
and will cut him in two, and will place his part with the hypocrites; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth.

matthew_25.t: Then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins, who, taking their lamps, went out to a meeting of the bridegroom.
But five of them were foolish and the five prudent.
For the foolish, taking their lamps, did not take with themselves oil;
but the prudent took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
But the bridegroom delaying, they all became drowsy and were sleeping.
But in the middle of the night a cry has happened: "Behold, the bridegroom comes; go out to a meeting of him."
Then all those virgins were raised and set in order their lamps.
And the foolish said to the prudent, "Give us from your oil, because our lamps are being quenched."
But the prudent answered, saying, "Lest there not be enough for us and for you; go rather to those selling and buy for yourselves."
But while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and the ready ones entered with him into the wedding, and the door was shut.
But later the remaining virgins also come, saying, "Lord, lord, open to us."
But answering he said, "Amen I say to you, I do not know you."
Watch therefore, because you do not know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man comes.
For just as a human going abroad called his own slaves and handed over to them his belongings,
and to one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability, and he went abroad. Immediately
the one having received the five talents, going, worked with them and gained another five talents.
Likewise also the one with the two gained another two.
But the one having received the one, going away, dug in the ground and hid the silver of his lord.
But after much time the lord of those slaves comes and settles a reckoning with them.
And coming, the one having received the five talents brought another five talents, saying, "Lord, five talents you handed over to me; see, another five talents I gained upon them."
And his lord said to him, "Well, good and faithful slave; over a few things you were faithful, over many I will set you; enter into the joy of your lord."
And coming also the one having received the two talents said, "Lord, two talents you handed over to me; see, another two talents I gained upon them."
His lord said to him, "Well, good and faithful slave; over a few things you were faithful, over many I will set you; enter into the joy of your lord."
But coming also the one having received the one talent said, "Lord, I knew you, that you are a hard human, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter,
and being afraid, going away, I hid your talent in the ground; see, you have what is yours."
But answering, his lord said to him, "Evil and shrinking slave, you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?
It was necessary therefore for you to throw my silver to the bankers, and coming, I would have received back what was mine with interest.
Take therefore from him the talent and give to the one having the ten talents.
For to everyone having it will be given, and he will abound; but from the one not having, even what he has will be taken from him.
And the useless slave, throw out into the outer darkness; there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth."
But when the Son of Man comes in his glory and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit upon a throne of his glory,
and all the nations will be gathered together before him, and he will separate them from one another just as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
and he will stand the sheep indeed at his right hand, but the young goats at the left.
Then the king will say to those at his right hand, "Come, the blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from a founding of a world.
For I hungered and you gave me to eat; I thirsted and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you gathered me in;
naked and you clothed me; I was weak and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me."
Then the righteous will answer him, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungering and we fed you, or thirsting and we gave drink?
And when did we see you a stranger and we gathered you in, or naked and we clothed you?
And when did we see you weak or in prison and we came to you?"
And answering, the king will say to them, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of these my brothers, the least, to me you did it."
Then he will say also to those at the left, "Go from me, the cursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I hungered and you did not give me to eat; and I thirsted and you did not give me drink;
I was a stranger and you did not gather me in; naked and you did not clothe me; weak and in prison and you did not visit me."
Then they also will answer, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungering or thirsting or a stranger or naked or weak or in prison, and did not serve you?"
Then he will answer them, saying, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of these least ones, neither to me did you do it."
And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

matthew_26.t: And it happened when Jesus finished all these words, he said to his learners,
"You know that after two days the Passover happens, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."
Then were gathered together the chief priests and the scribes and the elders of the people into the court of the high priest, the one called Caiaphas,
and they took counsel together so that they might seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
But they were saying, "Not in the feast, so that a tumult may not happen among the people."
And Jesus having come to be in Bethany in a house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very valuable ointment and poured it down upon his head as he reclined.
But seeing it, his learners were indignant, saying, "For what this destruction?"
"For this could have been sold for much and given to poor ones."
But knowing it, Jesus said to them, "Why do you cause troubles for the woman? For a good work she worked toward me.
For always the poor you have with yourselves, but me you do not always have.
For she, casting this ointment upon my body, did it toward preparing me for burial.
Amen I say to you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken for a memorial of her."
Then one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, going to the chief priests,
said, "What do you wish to give me, and I will hand him over to you?" And they set for him thirty silver pieces.
And from then he was seeking a good opportunity that he might hand him over.
And on the first of the Unleavened the learners came to Jesus, saying to him, "Where do you wish we should prepare for you to eat the Passover?"
But he said, "Go into the city to such a one and say to him, 'The teacher says: My season is near; with you I make the Passover with my learners.'"
And the learners did as Jesus arranged for them, and they prepared the Passover.
And evening having come, he was reclining with the twelve learners.
And as they were eating he said, "Amen I say to you that one of you will hand me over."
And being exceedingly grieved they began to say to him, each one of them, "Surely it is not I, Lord?"
But answering he said, "The one having dipped with me the hand in the dish, this one will hand me over.
The Son of Man indeed goes just as it has been written concerning him; but woe to that human through whom the Son of Man is handed over; good was it for him if that human had not been begotten."
And answering, Judas, the one handing him over, said, "Surely it is not I, Rabbi?" He says to him, "You said."
And as they were eating, Jesus, taking the bread and having blessed, broke, and giving to the learners he said, "Take, eat; this is my body."
And taking a cup and having given thanks he gave to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you;
for this is my blood, that of the new covenant, which is poured out concerning many for release of sins.
And I say to you that I will certainly not drink from now from this offspring of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father."
And having sung a hymn they went out to the Mount of the Olives.
Then Jesus says to them, "All you will be scandalised in me in this night; for it has been written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
But after my being raised I will go before you into Galilee."
But answering, Peter said to him, "If even all will be scandalised in you, I will never be scandalised."
Jesus said to him, "Amen I say to you that in this night, before a cock to crow, three times you will deny me."
Peter says to him, "Even if it is necessary for me to die with you, I will certainly not deny you." And likewise also all the learners said.
Then Jesus comes with them into a place called Gethsemane, and he says to the learners, "Sit here while, going away, I pray there."
And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee he began to be grieved and to be in distress.
Then he says to them, "My soul is deeply grieved until death; remain here and watch with me."
And going forward a little he fell upon his face praying and saying, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless not as I wish but as you."
And he comes to the learners and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter, "So you were not strong enough to watch one hour with me?
Watch and pray, so that you may not enter into testing; the spirit indeed is eager, but the flesh is weak."
Again, from a second time, going away he prayed, saying, "My Father, if this cup cannot pass from me unless I drink it, let your will happen."
And coming again he found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down.
And leaving them, going away again he prayed a third time, saying the same word again.
Then he comes to his learners and says to them, "Sleep the remaining time and rest; behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is handed over into hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go; behold, the one handing me over has drawn near."
And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.
And the one handing him over gave them a sign, saying, "Whomever I may kiss, he it is; seize him."
And immediately coming to Jesus he said, "Hail, Rabbi," and kissed him down.
But Jesus said to him, "Companion, for what are you here." Then, coming forward, they laid the hands upon Jesus and seized him.
And behold, one of those with Jesus, stretching out the hand, drew out his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest took off his ear.
Then Jesus says to him, "Turn back your sword into its place; for all those having taken a sword will perish by a sword.
Or do you suppose that I am not able to call upon my Father, and he will place beside me now more than twelve legions of angels?
How then may the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it is necessary to happen?"

In that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "As against a robber did you come out with swords and clubs to take me together? Daily toward you in the temple I was sitting teaching, and you did not seize me.
But this whole thing has happened so that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then the learners all, leaving him, fled.
And those having seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
But Peter was following him from far off, as far as the court of the high priest, and entering inside he was sitting with the attendants to see the end.
And the chief priests and the elders and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false witness against Jesus so that they might put him to death,
and they did not find it, though many false witnesses came forward, they did not find it. But later, two false witnesses coming forward
said, "This one said, 'I am able to destroy the sanctuary of God and through three days to build it.'"
And standing up, the high priest said to him, "Do you answer nothing? What do these witness against you?"
But Jesus was silent. And answering, the high priest said to him, "I adjure you by the living God that you tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Jesus says to him, "You said. Nevertheless I say to you, from now you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming upon the clouds of the heaven."
Then the high priest tore his garments, saying that "He blasphemed; what further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now you heard his blasphemy.
What does it seem to you?" And answering they said, "He is liable to death."
Then they spat into his face and beat him with fists; and others struck him with open hands,
saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ, who is the one having struck you?"
But Peter was sitting outside in the court; and one servant girl came to him, saying, "And you were with Jesus the Galilean."
But he denied before them all, saying, "I do not know what you say."
And as he was going out into the gateway, another saw him and says to those there, "This one was with Jesus the Nazorean."
And again he denied with an oath that "I do not know the human."
And after a little, those standing there, coming forward, said to Peter, "Truly you also are of them, for even your speech makes you evident."
Then he began to curse and to swear that "I do not know the human." And immediately a cock crowed.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said to him that "Before a cock to crow three times you will deny me." And going outside he wept bitterly.

matthew_27.t: And morning having come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus so as to put him to death;
and binding him they led him away and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, the one having handed him over, seeing that he was condemned, having changed his mind, returned the thirty silver pieces to the chief priests and the elders,
saying, "I sinned, having handed over innocent blood." But they said, "What is that toward us? You will see."
And throwing the silver pieces into the sanctuary he withdrew, and going away he hanged himself.
And the chief priests, taking the silver pieces, said, "It is not permitted to throw them into the offering-treasury, since it is a price of blood."
And taking counsel they bought with them the field of the potter for a burial place for strangers.
Therefore that field was called a field of blood until today.
Then was fulfilled the thing spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying: "And they took the thirty silver pieces, the price of the one having been priced, whom they priced from sons of Israel,
and they gave them for the field of the potter, as the Lord arranged for me."
And Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor questioned him, saying, "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him, "You say."
And in his being accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate says to him, "Do you not hear how many things they witness against you?"
And he did not answer him toward even one word, so that the governor marvelled exceedingly.
But at a feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the crowd, whom they wished.
And they had then a notable prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.
Therefore they having been gathered together, Pilate said to them, "Whom do you wish I release to you? Jesus Barabbas or Jesus the one called Christ?"
For he knew that because of envy they handed him over.
And as he was sitting upon the judgement seat, his wife sent to him, saying, "Nothing to you and to that righteous one; for many things I suffered today in a dream because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
And answering, the governor said to them, "Which from the two do you wish I release to you?" And they said, "Barabbas."
Pilate says to them, "What then shall I do with Jesus, the one called Christ?" They all say, "Let him be crucified."
And the governor said, "For what evil did he do?" But they were crying out exceedingly, saying, "Let him be crucified."

And Pilate, seeing that it profits nothing but rather a tumult is happening, taking water, washed off the hands opposite the crowd, saying, "I am innocent of the blood of this righteous one; you will see."
And answering, all the people said, "His blood upon us and upon our children."
Then he released to them Barabbas; but Jesus, having flogged him, he handed over so that he might be crucified.
Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus along into the praetorium, gathered together against him the whole cohort,
and stripping him they put around him a scarlet military cloak,
and plaiting a crown out of thorns they placed it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand, and kneeling before him they mocked him, saying, "Hail, king of the Jews."
And spitting on him they took the reed and were striking into his head.
And when they mocked him, they stripped off him the cloak and put on him his garments, and led him away for the crucifying.
And going out they found a human, a Cyrenian, by name Simon; this one they compelled into service that he might take up his cross.
And coming into a place called Golgotha, which is called a place of a skull,
they gave him to drink wine mixed with gall, and having tasted it he did not wish to drink.

And having crucified him they divided his garments, casting a lot, so that might be fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet: "They divided my garments among themselves and upon my clothing they cast a lot."
and sitting down they were keeping watch over him there.
And they placed above his head his charge, written: "This is Jesus, the king of the Jews."
Then are crucified with him two robbers, one at the right hand and one at the left.
And those passing by were blaspheming him, shaking their heads
and saying, "The one destroying the sanctuary and in three days building it, save yourself; if you are Son of God, come down from the cross."
And likewise also the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders and Pharisees, were saying,
"Others he saved, himself he is not able to save; if he is king of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will trust upon him.
He has trusted upon God; let him rescue him now if he wants him; for he said that 'I am God's son.'"
And the same thing also the robbers crucified together with him were reproaching him.
And from the sixth hour darkness happened upon the whole land until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" — that is, "My God, my God, for what did you forsake me?"
And some of those standing there, hearing, were saying that "This one calls Elijah."
And immediately one of them, running and taking a sponge and having filled it with sour wine and putting it around a reed, was giving him to drink.
But the rest were saying, "Leave him; let us see if Elijah comes saving him."
And Jesus, crying again with a loud voice, released the spirit.
And behold, the curtain of the sanctuary was torn from above until below into two, and the earth was shaken and the rocks were split,
and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the fallen-asleep holy ones were raised,
and coming out from the tombs after his rising they entered into the holy city and were made visible to many.
But the centurion and those with him keeping watch over Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that happened, feared exceedingly, saying, "Truly this was God's son."
And there were there many women watching from far off, who followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him;
among whom was Mary the Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
And evening having come, there came a rich human from Arimathea, by name Joseph, who himself also was discipled to Jesus.
This one, coming to Pilate, asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given back.
And taking the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth
and placed it in his new tomb which he had hewn in the rock, and having rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb he went away.
And there was there Mariam the Magdalene and the other Mary, sitting opposite the grave.
And on the next day, which is after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
saying, "Lord, we remembered that that deceiver said while still living, 'After three days I am raised.'

Order therefore the grave to be made secure until the third day, lest his learners, coming by night, steal him and say to the people, 'He was raised from the dead'; and the last deception will be worse than the first."
And Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go, make it secure as you know."
And they, going, made the grave secure, sealing the stone with the guard.

matthew_28.t: And late of sabbaths, at the dawning into one of sabbaths, came Mariam the Magdalene and the other Mary to view the grave.
And behold, a great shaking happened; for an angel of the Lord, descending from heaven and coming, rolled away the stone from the door and was sitting upon it.
And his appearance was as lightning and his clothing white as snow.
And from the fear of him those keeping watch were shaken and became as dead ones.
And answering, the angel said to the women, "Do not fear, you; for I know that you seek Jesus the crucified one.
He is not here, for he was raised just as he said; come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
And going quickly say to his learners that he was raised from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, I told you."
And going away quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to announce to his learners.
And as they were going to announce to his learners, behold, Jesus met them, saying, "Rejoice." And they, coming to him, took hold of his feet and bowed down to him.
Then Jesus says to them, "Do not fear; go, announce to my brothers that they should go away into Galilee, and there they will see me."
And as they were going, behold, some of the guard, coming into the city, announced to the chief priests all the things that happened.
And having been gathered together with the elders and having taken counsel, they gave sufficient silver pieces to the soldiers,
saying, "Say that 'His learners, coming by night, stole him while we were sleeping.'
And if this is heard before the governor, we will persuade him and will make you without care."
And they, taking the silver pieces, did as they were taught. And this word was spread abroad among Jews until today's day.
And the eleven learners went into Galilee, into the mountain where Jesus arranged for them.
And seeing him they bowed down to him; but they doubted.
And coming, Jesus spoke to them, saying, "All authority was given to me in heaven and upon the earth.
Going therefore, disciple all the nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to keep all things whatever I commanded you; and behold, I am with you all the days until the completion of the age." Amen

mark_1.t: Beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, son of God —
Just as it has been written in Isaiah the prophet: Behold, I send off my messenger before your face, who will build your road ahead of you.
A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the road of the Lord, make his tracks straight.
John came to be, the one baptising in the wilderness and heralding a baptism of a change of mind into release of sins.
And all the Judean country was going out to him and all the Jerusalemites, and they were being baptised by him in the Jordan river, confessing out their sins.
And John was clothed in camel hairs and a leather belt around his loin, and eating locusts and wild honey.
And he was heralding, saying: There comes the one stronger than me after me, of whom I am not competent, stooping, to loosen the strap of his sandals.
I baptised you in water, but he will baptise you in holy spirit.
And it came to be in those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptised into the Jordan by John.
And immediately, coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens being split and the spirit as a dove coming down into him.
And a voice came to be out of the heavens: You are my son, the beloved; in you I was well pleased.
And immediately the spirit throws him out into the wilderness.
And he was there in the wilderness forty days, being tested by the Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the messengers were serving him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee heralding the good news of the kingdom of God
and saying that: The season has been filled full and the kingdom of God has drawn near; change your minds and trust in the good news.
And passing along beside the sea of Galilee he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net around in the sea; for they were fishers.
And Jesus said to them: Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of humans.
And immediately, leaving their nets, they followed him.
And going forward from there a little he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, and them in the boat repairing the nets,
And immediately he called them. And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men they went off after him.
And they go into Capernaum. And immediately on the sabbaths, entering into the synagogue, he was teaching.
And they were being struck out of themselves at his teaching; for he was teaching them as having authority and not as the scribes.
And immediately there was in their synagogue a human in an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
saying: Ha! What to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene? Did you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are — the holy one of God.
And Jesus rebuked it, saying: Be muzzled and come out of him.
And the unclean spirit, tearing him and shouting with a great voice, came out of him.
And all were astounded so as to debate with each other, saying: What is this? What is this new teaching — that with authority he even orders the unclean spirits, and they obey him?
And his report went out immediately everywhere into the whole surrounding country of Galilee.
And immediately, coming out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.
But the mother-in-law of Simon was lying down burning with fever, and immediately they say to him about her.
And coming to her he raised her, taking hold of her hand; and the fever left her immediately, and she was serving them.
But evening having come to be, when the sun set, they were carrying to him all those having it badly and the demonised.
And the whole city was gathered together at the door.
And he healed many having it badly with various diseases and he threw out many demons and he was not permitting the demons to speak, because they knew him to be Christ.
And early, while very much night, rising he went out and went away into a deserted place, and there he was praying.
And Simon and those with him hunted him down;
and they found him and they say to him that: All are seeking you.
And he says to them: Let us go elsewhere, into the neighbouring towns, so that there also I may herald; for it was for this that I came out.
And he came heralding into their synagogues into the whole of Galilee and throwing out the demons.
And there comes to him a leper urging him and kneeling to him and saying to him that: If you want, you are able to cleanse me.
And moved in the guts, stretching out his hand he touched him and says to him: I want; be cleansed.
And when he said it, immediately the leprosy went away from him, and he was cleansed.
And snorting at him, immediately he threw him out,
and he says to him: See, say nothing to no one; but go, show yourself to the priest and bring near concerning your cleansing what Moses ordered, for a witness to them.

But he, going out, began to herald much and to spread the word abroad, so that he was no longer able openly to enter into a city, but was outside in deserted places. And they were coming to him from everywhere.

mark_2.t: And entering again into Capernaum after days, and it was heard that he is in a house.
And immediately many were gathered together so that there was no longer room, not even the places at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
And they come carrying to him a paralytic lifted by four.
And not being able to bring him near to him because of the crowd, they unroofed the roof where he was and, digging it out, they lower the pallet where the paralytic was lying down.
And Jesus, seeing their trust, says to the paralytic: Child, your sins are released for you.
But there were some of the scribes sitting there and reckoning in their hearts:
Why does this one speak thus? He blasphemes. Who is able to release sins except one, God?
And immediately Jesus, recognising in his spirit that they are reckoning thus in themselves, says to them: Why do you reckon these things in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say to the paralytic: Your sins are released, or to say: Rise and lift your pallet and walk about?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority to release sins upon the earth — he says to the paralytic:
To you I say: Rise, and lift your pallet and go away into your house.
And he rose and immediately, lifting the pallet, he went out in front of all, so that all were standing outside themselves and glorifying God, saying that: Never did we see it thus.
And he went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.
And passing along he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax-office, and he says to him: Follow me. And rising he followed him.
And it comes to be, in his reclining in his house, and many tax-farmers and sinners were reclining together with Jesus and his learners; for there were many, and they were following him.
And the scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that he eats with the sinners and tax-farmers, were saying to his learners: Why is it that with the tax-farmers and sinners he eats and drinks?
And Jesus, hearing, says to them that: The strong have no need of a physician but those having it badly; I did not come to call righteous ones but sinners into a change of mind.
And John's learners and those of the Pharisees were fasting, and they come and say to him: Through what do the learners of John and the learners of the Pharisees fast, but your learners do not fast?

And Jesus said to them: The sons of the bridal chamber are not able to fast while the bridegroom is with them, are they? As long a time as they have the bridegroom with them they are not able to fast.
But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
And no one sews a patch of unfulled rag upon an old garment; but if not, the filling lifts away from it, the new from the old, and a worse split comes to be.
And no one throws young wine into old skins; but if not, the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is destroyed and the skins; but young wine into new skins.
And it came to be that he on the sabbaths was passing along through the sown fields, and his learners began to make a road, plucking the heads.
And the Pharisees were saying to him: See, why do they do on the sabbaths what is not allowed?
And he himself says to them: Did you never read what David did when he had need and hungered, he himself and those with him?

how he entered into the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of the setting-out, which it is not allowed to eat except the priests, and he gave also to those being with him?
And he was saying to them: The sabbath came to be because of the human, and not the human because of the sabbath.
So that the Son of Man is lord also of the sabbath.

mark_3.t: And he entered again into the synagogue, and there was there a human having a dried-up hand.
And they were watching him closely, whether on the sabbaths he will heal him, so that they might accuse him.
And he says to the human having the dry hand: Rise into the middle.
And he says to them: Is it allowed on the sabbaths to do good or to do bad, to save a life or to kill? But they were being silent.

And looking around at them with anger, grieving together at the hardening of their heart, he says to the human: Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, sound as the other.
And the Pharisees, going out, immediately with the Herodians were giving counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
And Jesus with his learners withdrew to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judea
and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan and those around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing as much as he was doing, came to him.
And he said to his learners that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they might not press him.
For he healed many, so that they fell upon him so as to touch him, as many as had scourges.
And the unclean spirits, whenever they were watching him, were falling before him and were crying out, saying that: You are the son of God.
And much he was rebuking them, so that they might not make him manifest.
And he goes up into the mountain and calls toward himself whom he himself wanted, and they went away to him.
And he made twelve, whom also he named sent-ones, so that they might be with him and so that he might send them off to herald,
and to have authority to heal the diseases and to throw out the demons.
And he made the twelve, and he placed on Simon a name, Rock;
and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and he placed on them names, Boanerges, which is: sons of thunder;
and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.
And the crowd comes together again, so that they were not able even to eat bread.
And those from beside him, hearing, went out to take hold of him; for they were saying that he is out of his mind.
And the scribes who came down from Jerusalem were saying that he has Beelzebul and that by the ruler of the demons he throws out the demons.
And calling them toward himself, in parables he was saying to them: How is Satan able to throw out Satan?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom is not able to be made to stand;
and if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand;
and if Satan rose against himself and was divided, he is not able to stand but has an end.
But no one is able, entering into the house of the strong one, to plunder his vessels, unless first he binds the strong one, and then he will plunder his house.
Amen I say to you that all will be released for the sons of humans, the sins and the blasphemies, as much as they may blaspheme;
but whoever blasphemes into the holy spirit does not have release into the age, but is liable to an eternal sin —
because they were saying: He has an unclean spirit.
And there comes his mother and his brothers, and standing outside they sent off to him, calling him.
And a crowd was sitting around him, and they say to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers and your sisters outside are seeking you.
And answering them he says: Who is my mother and my brothers?
And looking around at those sitting around him in a circle, he says: See, my mother and my brothers.
For whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and sister and mother.

mark_4.t: And again he began to teach beside the sea. And there gathers to him a very great crowd, so that he, embarking into a boat, sat on the sea, and all the crowd were toward the sea upon the land.
And he was teaching them in parables many things and he was saying to them in his teaching:
Hear. Behold, the sower went out to sow.
And it came to be in the sowing, one fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
And other fell upon the rocky ground where it did not have much earth, and immediately it sprang up because of not having depth of earth.
And when the sun rose it was burnt, and because of not having a root it was dried up.
And other fell into the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it together, and it gave no fruit.
And others fell into the earth, the good one, and it was giving fruit coming up and growing, and it was bearing one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred.
And he was saying to them: Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And when he came to be alone, those around him together with the twelve were asking him the parables.
And he was saying to them: To you has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those outside, everything comes to be in parables,
so that seeing they may see and not see, and hearing they may hear and not put together, lest they should turn back and it be released for them.
And he says to them: Do you not know this parable? And how will you know all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
And these are those beside the road where the word is sown, and whenever they hear, immediately Satan comes and lifts the word that has been sown into them.
And these are likewise those sown upon the rocky places, who, whenever they hear the word, immediately with joy receive it,
and they do not have a root in themselves but are for a season; then, when pressure or persecution comes to be because of the word, immediately they are made to stumble.
And others are those sown into the thorns; these are those who heard the word,
and the anxieties of this age and the deceit of wealth and the desires concerning the rest, coming in, choke the word together, and it comes to be fruitless.
And those are those sown upon the earth, the good one, who hear the word and receive it alongside and bear fruit, one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred.
And he was saying to them that: Does the lamp come so that it may be placed under the measuring basket or under the couch? Is it not so that it may be placed upon the lampstand?
For nothing is hidden except so that it may be made manifest, nor did anything come to be concealed but so that it might come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.
And he was saying to them: See what you hear. In what measure you measure it will be measured to you, and it will be added to you who hear.
For whoever has, it will be given to him; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be lifted from him.
And he was saying: Thus is the kingdom of God, as if a human should throw the seed upon the earth
and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed sprouts and lengthens, how he himself does not know.
For of itself the earth bears fruit — first grass, then a head, then full grain in the head.
But whenever the fruit hands itself over, immediately he sends off the sickle, because the harvest has stood ready.
And he was saying: How may we liken the kingdom of God, or in what parable may we place it?
As with a grain of mustard, which whenever it is sown upon the earth, being smaller than all the seeds that are upon the earth —
and whenever it is sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all the garden herbs and makes great branches, so that the birds of the heaven are able to nest under its shade.
And with many such parables he was speaking the word to them, just as they were able to hear.
But without a parable he was not speaking to them; but privately to his own learners he was loosing everything.
And he says to them in that day, evening having come to be: Let us go through to the other side.
And leaving the crowd they take him along as he was in the boat, and other boats were with him.
And there comes a great whirlwind of wind, and the waves were throwing themselves into the boat, so that the boat was already being filled.
And he himself was in the stern upon the headrest, sleeping. And they raise him and say to him: Teacher, is it no care to you that we are being destroyed?
And being roused he rebuked the wind and said to the sea: Be silent, be muzzled. And the wind grew weary, and there came to be a great calm.
And he said to them: Why are you cowardly? Do you not yet have trust?
And they feared a great fear and were saying to one another: Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

mark_5.t: And they came into the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
And on his coming out of the boat, immediately there met him out of the tombs a human in an unclean spirit,
who had his dwelling in the tombs. And not even with a chain was anyone any longer able to bind him,
because of his having often been bound with fetters and chains, and the chains having been pulled apart by him and the fetters having been shattered, and no one was strong enough to tame him.
And through all, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself down with stones.
And seeing Jesus from far off he ran and bowed down to him,
and crying with a great voice he says: What to me and to you, Jesus, son of the God the Most High? I bind you by oath by God, do not torment me.
For he was saying to him: Come out, the unclean spirit, out of the human.
And he was questioning him: What name to you? And he answers, he says to him: Legion is name to me, because we are many.
And he was urging him much so that he might not send them off outside the country.
And there was there toward the mountain a great herd of pigs feeding.
And they urged him, all the demons, saying: Send us into the pigs, so that into them we may enter.

And immediately Jesus permitted them. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the cliff into the sea — and they were about two thousand — and they were being choked in the sea.
And those feeding them fled and reported into the city and into the fields. And they came to see what it is that has happened.
And they come to Jesus and they watch the demonised one sitting and clothed and being sound-minded, the one having had the legion, and they were afraid.
And those who saw described to them how it happened to the demonised one, and concerning the pigs.
And they began to urge him to go away from their borders.
And on his embarking into the boat, the one who had been demonised was urging him so that he might be with him.
And he did not permit him, but says to him: Go away into your house to your own, and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and had mercy on you.
And he went away and began to herald in the Decapolis how much Jesus did for him, and all were marvelling.
And on Jesus crossing over in the boat again into the other side, a great crowd was gathered together to him, and he was beside the sea.
And behold, there comes one of the synagogue-rulers, by name Jairus, and seeing him he falls toward his feet
and urges him much, saying that: My little daughter is at the last; that coming you may place the hands on her so that she may be saved and may live.
And he went away with him. And a great crowd was following him and they were crushing him together.
And a certain woman being in a flow of blood twelve years
and having suffered many things under many physicians and having spent all things from herself and having been helped nothing but rather having come into the worse,
having heard the things about Jesus, coming in the crowd from behind she touched his garment;
for she was saying that: If I touch even his garments, I will be saved.
And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up, and she knew in the body that she has been healed from the scourge.
And immediately Jesus, recognising in himself the power gone out from him, turning about in the crowd was saying: Who touched my garments?
And his learners were saying to him: You see the crowd crushing you together, and you say: Who touched me?
And he was looking around to see the one, feminine, who did this.
But the woman, having feared and trembling, knowing what has happened to her, came and fell before him and told him all the truth.
But he said to her: Daughter, your trust has saved you. Go away into peace and be sound from your scourge.
While he is still speaking, there come from the synagogue-ruler saying that: Your daughter died. Why still trouble the teacher?
But Jesus, immediately overhearing the word being spoken, says to the synagogue-ruler: Do not fear, only trust.
And he did not permit anyone to follow together with him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
And they come into the house of the synagogue-ruler, and he watches an uproar and people weeping and wailing much,
and entering he says to them: Why are you in uproar and weeping? The little child did not die but is sleeping.
And they were laughing him down. But he himself, throwing out all, takes along the father of the little child and the mother and those with him and goes in where the little child was lying.
And taking hold of the hand of the little child he says to her: Talitha koum — which is, being translated: The little girl, to you I say, rise.
And immediately the little girl rose and was walking about; for she was of twelve years. And immediately they were standing outside themselves with a great standing-outside.
And he ordered them much so that no one might know this, and he said to give to her to eat.

mark_6.t: And he went out from there and comes into his fatherland, and his learners follow him.

And the sabbath having come to be, he began to teach in the synagogue; and the many, hearing, were being struck out of themselves, saying: From where to this one these things, and what is the wisdom given to this one, that even such powers come to be through his hands?
Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us? And they were being made to stumble in him.
And Jesus was saying to them that: A prophet is not dishonoured except in his fatherland and among his relatives and in his house.
And he was not able there to do any power, except that, placing the hands on a few sick ones, he healed.
And he was marvelling because of their untrust. And he was going around the villages in a circle, teaching.
And he calls toward himself the twelve and began to send them off two by two, and he was giving them authority of the unclean spirits.
And he commanded them that they should lift nothing into the road except a staff only, no bread, no wallet, no copper into the belt,
but having been shod with sandals, and: Do not put on two tunics.
And he was saying to them: Wherever you enter into a house, there remain until you go out from there.

And whatever place will not receive you nor hear you, going out from there shake off the dust underneath your feet for a witness to them. [Amen I say to you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah in a day of judgement than for that city.]
And going out they heralded so that they might change their minds,
and they were throwing out many demons and they were anointing with oil many sick ones and they were healing.
And king Herod heard, for his name became manifest, and they were saying that John the baptising one has been raised out of the dead, and because of this the powers work in him.
But others were saying that he is Elijah; but others were saying that he is a prophet, as one of the prophets.
But Herod, hearing, was saying that: Whom I beheaded, John, this one is; he was raised.
For Herod himself, sending, seized John and bound him in the prison because of Herodias the wife of Philip his brother, because he married her.
For John was saying to Herod that: It is not allowed for you to have the wife of your brother.
But Herodias was holding it in against him and was wanting to kill him, and was not able;
for Herod was fearing John, knowing him a righteous and holy man, and he was keeping him safe. And hearing him he was much at a loss, and he was hearing him gladly.
And a well-timed day having come to be, when Herod on his birthday made a dinner for his great ones and the commanders of thousands and the first ones of Galilee.
And the daughter of Herodias herself having entered and having danced, and she pleased Herod and those reclining together, the king said to the girl: Ask me whatever you want, and I will give to you.
And he swore to her much: Whatever you ask me I will give to you, up to half of my kingdom.
And she, going out, said to her mother: What may I ask? But she said: The head of John the baptising one.
And entering immediately with haste to the king she asked, saying: I want that at once you give me upon a platter the head of John the Baptist.
And the king, having become deeply grieved, because of the oaths and those reclining did not want to set her aside.
And immediately the king, sending off an executioner, commanded to bring his head. And going away he beheaded him in the prison
