and brought his head upon a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And his learners, hearing, came and lifted his corpse and placed it in a tomb.
And the sent-ones gather together to Jesus and reported to him all things, as much as they did and as much as they taught.
And he says to them: Come, you yourselves, privately into a deserted place and rest a little. For those coming and those going were many, and they were not even finding time to eat.
And they went away in the boat into a deserted place privately.
And they saw them going away, and many recognised him, and on foot from all the cities they ran together there and came before them and came together to him.
And coming out he saw a great crowd and was moved in the guts over them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
And already much hour having come to be, his learners, coming to him, were saying that: The place is deserted, and already much hour;
Release them, so that going away into the surrounding fields and villages they may buy for themselves what they may eat.
But he, answering, said to them: You yourselves give them to eat. And they say to him: Going away, should we buy two hundred denarii of loaves and give them to eat?
But he says to them: How many loaves do you have? Go, see. And knowing, they say: Five, and two fish.
And he commanded them to make all recline, drinking-party by drinking-party, upon the green grass.
And they fell back garden-plot by garden-plot, by hundreds and by fifties.

And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up into the heaven he blessed and broke down the loaves and was giving to his learners so that they might set them before them, and the two fish he divided to all.
And all ate and were fed full,
and they lifted fragments, twelve baskets full, and from the fish.
And those who ate the loaves were about five thousand males.
And immediately he compelled his learners to embark into the boat and to go before into the other side toward Bethsaida, while he himself releases the crowd.
And having taken leave of them he went away into the mountain to pray.
And evening having come to be, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he alone upon the land.
And seeing them being tormented in the rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he comes to them walking upon the sea, and he was wanting to pass alongside them.
But they, seeing him upon the sea walking about, thought that it is a phantom, and they cried out;
for all saw him and were stirred up. But he immediately spoke with them and says to them: Take courage, I am; do not fear.
And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind grew weary. And exceedingly, beyond measure, in themselves they were standing outside themselves and marvelling;
for they did not put together upon the loaves, but their heart was having been hardened.
And having crossed over onto the land they came into Gennesaret and were moored.
And on their coming out of the boat, immediately recognising him,
they ran around that whole country and began upon the pallets to carry around those having it badly, wherever they were hearing that he is.

And wherever he was entering, into villages or into cities or into fields, in the marketplaces they were placing the weak ones and were urging him so that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were being saved.

mark_7.t: And there gather together to him the Pharisees and some of the scribes, having come from Jerusalem.
And seeing some of his learners that with common hands, that is, unwashed, they eat the loaves —
For the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless they wash the hands with a fist, do not eat, holding fast the tradition of the elders;
and coming from the marketplace, unless they wash, they do not eat; and there are many other things which they received to hold fast — washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and couches.
And the Pharisees and the scribes question him: Through what do your learners not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but with common hands eat the bread?

But he, answering, said to them that: Well did Isaiah prophesy concerning you, the play-actors, as it has been written that: This people honours me with the lips, but their heart holds far away from me;
But in vain they revere me, teaching teachings, commandments of humans.
Leaving the commandment of God, you hold fast the tradition of the humans; washings of pitchers and cups and many other such similar things you do.
And he was saying to them: Well do you set aside the commandment of God so that you may make your tradition stand.
For Moses said: Honour your father and your mother; and: The one speaking badly of father or mother, let him end in death.
But you yourselves say: If a human says to the father or to the mother: Korban — which is: a gift — whatever from me you might have been benefited by,
you no longer let him do anything for his father or his mother,
invalidating the word of God by your tradition which you handed over; and many such similar things you do.
And calling toward himself again the crowd, he was saying to them: Hear me, all of you, and put it together.
There is nothing outside the human, entering into him, which is able to make him common; but the things coming out from the human, those are the things making the human common.
[If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.]
And when he entered into a house from the crowd, his learners were questioning him about the parable.
And he says to them: Thus are you also without understanding? Do you not perceive that everything from outside entering into the human is not able to make him common,
because it does not enter into his heart but into the belly, and goes out into the latrine, cleansing all the foods.
But he was saying that: The thing coming out from the human, that makes the human common.
For from within, out of the heart of the humans, the bad reckonings come out: sexual immoralities, thefts, murders,
adulteries, greedinesses, evils, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, arrogance, senselessness.
All these bad things come out from within and make the human common.
And rising from there he went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. And entering into the house he wanted no one to know, and he was not able to escape notice.
But immediately a woman, hearing about him, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, coming, fell toward his feet.
And the woman was a Greek, Syrophoenician by race, and she was asking him so that he might throw the demon out of her daughter.
And he was saying to her: Let the children first be fed full; for it is not good to take the bread of the children and to throw it to the little dogs.
But she answered and says to him: Yes, Lord; even the little dogs underneath the table eat from the crumbs of the children.
And he said to her: Because of this word, go away; the demon has come out from your daughter.
And going away into her house she found the little child thrown upon the couch and the demon having come out.
And again going out from the borders of Tyre he came through Sidon into the sea of Galilee up through the middle of the borders of Decapolis.
And they bring to him a deaf one and hardly-speaking, and they urge him so that he might place the hand on him.
And taking him away from the crowd privately he threw his fingers into his ears, and spitting he touched his tongue,
and looking up into the heaven he groaned and says to him: Ephphatha — which is: Be opened.
And immediately his hearings were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking rightly.
And he ordered them so that they might tell no one; but as much as he was ordering them, they much more abundantly were heralding.
And beyond all measure they were being struck out of themselves, saying: Well has he done all things; he even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.

mark_8.t: In those days again, a great crowd being and not having what they may eat, calling toward himself the learners he says to them:
I am moved in the guts over the crowd, because already three days they remain with me and they do not have what they may eat.
And if I release them fasting into their house, they will be undone in the road; and some of them have come from far off.
And his learners answered him that: From where will anyone be able here to feed these full with loaves in a desolate place?
And he was asking them: How many loaves do you have? But they said: Seven.

And he commands the crowd to fall back upon the earth, and taking the seven loaves, giving thanks, he broke and was giving to his learners so that they might set them before, and they set them before the crowd.
And they had a few little fishes; and blessing them he said also to set these before them.
And they ate and were fed full, and they lifted leftovers of fragments, seven hampers.
And there were those who ate about four thousand; and he released them.
And immediately, embarking into the boat with his learners, he came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to debate with him, seeking from him a sign from the heaven, testing him.
And groaning up in his spirit he says: Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen I say to you, if a sign will be given to this generation —
And leaving them, embarking again, he went away into the other side.
And they forgot to take loaves, and except one loaf they did not have any with themselves in the boat.
And he was ordering them, saying: See, look away from the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.
And they were reckoning toward one another that they do not have loaves.
And knowing, he says to them: Why do you reckon that you do not have loaves? Do you not yet perceive nor put it together? Do you have your heart having been hardened?
Having eyes do you not see, and having ears do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves into the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you lift? They say to him: Twelve.
And when the seven into the four thousand, of how many hampers fullnesses of fragments did you lift? And they say to him: Seven.
And he was saying to them: Do you not yet put it together?
And they come into Bethsaida, and they bring to him a blind one and urge him so that he might touch him.
And taking hold of the hand of the blind one he brought him outside the village, and spitting into his eyes, placing the hands on him, he was questioning him: Do you see anything?
And looking up he was saying: I see the humans, because as trees I see them walking about.
Then again he placed the hands upon his eyes, and he saw through and was restored and was looking at all things far-shiningly.
And he sent him off into his house, saying: Do not even enter into the village.
And Jesus went out, and his learners, into the villages of Caesarea of Philip. And in the road he was questioning his learners, saying to them: Whom do the humans say me to be?
But they said to him, saying that: John the Baptist, and others Elijah, but others that one of the prophets.
And he himself was questioning them: But you, whom do you say me to be? And Peter, answering, says to him: You are the Christ.
And he rebuked them so that they might tell no one about him.

And he began to teach them that it is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer many things and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes and to be killed and after three days to rise up.
And with openness he was speaking the word. And Peter, taking him alongside, began to rebuke him.
But he, turning about and seeing his learners, rebuked Peter and says: Go away behind me, Satan, because you do not mind the things of God but the things of the humans.
And calling toward himself the crowd together with his learners he said to them: If anyone wants to follow after me, let him deny himself and lift his cross and let him follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will destroy it; but whoever will destroy his life for the sake of me and of the good news, this one will save it.
For what does it profit the human to gain the whole world and to be fined his life?
For what might a human give in exchange for his life?

For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him whenever he comes in the glory of his father with the holy messengers.

mark_9.t: And he was saying to them: Amen I say to you that there are some here of those standing who will certainly not taste of death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power.
And after six days Jesus takes along Peter and James and John and brings them up into a high mountain by themselves alone. And he was transformed before them,
and his garments became glistening, exceedingly white as snow, such as a fuller on the earth is not able so to whiten.
And Elijah was seen by them with Moses, and they were talking together with Jesus.
And answering Peter says to Jesus: Rabbi, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah —
for he did not know what he should answer, for they became terrified.
And there came a cloud overshadowing them, and there came a voice out of the cloud saying: This is my son, the beloved; listen to him.
And suddenly, having looked around, they no longer saw anyone but Jesus alone with themselves.
And as they were coming down out of the mountain he ordered them that they should relate to no one the things they had seen, except when the Son of Man should rise out of the dead.
And they kept hold of the word among themselves, debating what the rising out of the dead is.
And they were asking him saying: Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
And he answering said to them: Elijah indeed coming first restores all things; and how has it been written upon the Son of Man that he should suffer many things and be counted as nothing?
But I say to you that Elijah also has come, and they did to him as much as they wanted, just as it has been written upon him.
And coming to the disciples they saw a large crowd around them and scribes debating with them.
And immediately all the crowd, seeing him, were utterly astounded, and running to him they were greeting him.
And he asked them, scribes: What are you debating with them?
And one out of the crowd answered him, said: Teacher, I brought my son to you, having a speechless spirit.
And wherever it seizes him, it tears him down; and he foams and grinds his teeth and becomes dry. And I told your disciples that they should cast it out, and they were not strong enough.
And he answering them says: O generation without trust, how long will I be with you? how long will I bear with you? Bring him to me.
And they brought him to him. And the spirit, seeing him, immediately convulsed him, and falling upon the ground he was rolling, foaming.
And he asked his father: How much time is it since this has happened to him? And he said: From childhood.
And often it has thrown him both into the fire and into waters so that it might destroy him; but if you are able anything, help us, moved in the guts over us.
And Jesus said to him: The 'if you are able' — all things are possible to the one trusting.
Immediately crying out the father of the child with tears was saying: I trust, Lord; come to the help of my untrust.
And Jesus, seeing that a crowd is running together, rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it: The speechless and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him, and no longer enter into him.
And crying out and convulsing him much it came out, and he became as if dead, so that the many were saying that he died.
But Jesus, having taken hold of his hand, raised him, and he stood up.
And when he had entered into a house his disciples privately were asking him: Why were we not able to cast it out?
And he said to them: This kind is able to come out by nothing except by prayer [and fasting].
And going out from there they were passing along through Galilee, and he was not wanting that anyone should know;

for he was teaching his disciples and was saying to them that the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of humans, and they will kill him, and having been killed, after three days he will rise.
But they were not knowing the saying and were afraid to ask him.
And they came into Capernaum. And having come to be in the house he was asking them: What on the road were you discussing among yourselves?
But they were silent; for on the road they had argued with one another who is greater.
And having sat down he called the twelve and says to them: If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.
And taking a child he stood it in their midst, and taking it in his arms he said to them:
Whoever receives one of such children upon my name receives me; and whoever receives me does not receive me but the one who sent me.
John said to him saying: Teacher, we saw someone in your name casting out demons who does not follow us, and we were preventing him because he was not following us.
But Jesus said: Do not prevent him; for there is no one who will do a work of power upon my name and will be able quickly to speak evil of me.
For whoever is not against us is for us.
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in the name that you are of Christ, Amen I say to you that he will certainly not lose his reward.
And whoever trips up one of these little ones who trust into me, it is good for him rather if a donkey-millstone is placed around his neck and he has been thrown into the sea.
And if your hand trips you up, cut it off; it is good for you to enter into life maimed than having the two hands to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
[where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched]
And if your foot trips you up, cut it off; it is good for you to enter into life lame than having the two feet to be thrown into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
[where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.]
And if your eye trips you up, throw it out; it is good for you one-eyed to enter into the kingdom of God than having two eyes to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire,
where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is good; but if the salt becomes saltless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.

mark_10.t: And rising up from there he comes into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds come together to him again, and as he had been accustomed he was teaching them again.
And Pharisees coming forward were asking him if it is permitted for a man to dismiss a wife, testing him.
And he answering said to them: What did Moses command you?
And they said: Moses permitted to write a scroll of severance and to dismiss.
And answering Jesus said to them: Toward the hardness of your heart he wrote you this commandment;
But from the beginning of creation male and female he made them, God;
On account of this a human will leave behind his father and the mother and will be glued to his wife,
and the two will be into one flesh; so that they are no longer two but one flesh.
What therefore God yoked together, let a human not separate.
And into the house again the disciples were asking him about this.
And he says to them: Whoever dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery upon her.
And if she, having dismissed her husband, marries another, she commits adultery.
And they were bringing to him children so that he might touch them; but the disciples rebuked them, those bringing them.
But Jesus, seeing, was indignant and said to them: Let the children come to me, do not prevent them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
Amen I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will certainly not enter into it.
And taking them in his arms he was fervently blessing them, placing his hands upon them.
And as he was going out into a road, one running up and kneeling to him was asking him: Good teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
And Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except one — God.
The commandments you know: Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honour your father and your mother.
And he answering said to him: Teacher, all these I have guarded from my youth.

And Jesus, having looked into him, loved him and said to him: One thing you lack; go, whatever you have sell and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. And come, follow me, taking up the cross.
But he, gloomy at the word, went away being grieved; for he was one having many possessions.
And having looked around Jesus says to his disciples: How difficultly will those having riches enter into the kingdom of God.
But the disciples were astounded at his words. But Jesus again answering says to them: Children, how difficult it is for those who have trusted upon riches to enter into the kingdom of God.
It is easier for a camel to go through the hole of the needle than for a rich person to enter into the kingdom of God.
But they were exceedingly astonished, saying to themselves: And who is able to be saved?
Having looked into them Jesus says: With humans impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.
Peter began to say to him: Look, we ourselves have left all things and have followed you.
Jesus answering said: Amen I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or wife or children or fields for the sake of me and for the sake of the gospel,
who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age that is coming eternal life.
But many first will be last and the last first.

And they were on the road going up into Jerusalem, and Jesus was going before them, and they were astounded; and those following were afraid. And taking along again the twelve he began to tell them the things about to happen to him,
that Look, we are going up into Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will hand him over to the nations
and they will mock him and will spit at him and will scourge him and will kill him, and after three days he will rise.
And James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, come to him, saying to him: Teacher, we want that whatever we ask you, you would do for us.
But he said to them: What do you want me to do for you?
But they said to him: Give to us that one at your right and one at your left we may sit in your glory.
But Jesus said to them: You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink or to be baptised with the baptism that I am baptised with?
But they said to him: We are able. But Jesus said to them: The cup that I drink you will drink, and the baptism that I am baptised with you will be baptised with;
But to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.
And hearing, the ten began to be indignant about James and John.
And calling them to himself Jesus says to them: You know that those reputed to rule the nations lord it down over them, and their great ones exercise authority down upon them.
But it is not so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant;
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom in exchange for many.
And they come into Jericho. And as he was going out from Jericho and his disciples and a considerable crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, the blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
And hearing that it is Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and to say: Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me.
And many were rebuking him that he should be silent. But he was crying out much more: Son of David, have mercy on me.
And Jesus, having stood still, said: Call him. And they call the blind man, saying to him: Take courage, rise, he is calling you.
And he, throwing away his outer garment, springing up, came to Jesus.
And answering him Jesus said: What do you want me to do for you? And the blind man said to him: Rabbouni, that I may see again.
And Jesus said to him: Go, your trust has saved you. And immediately he saw again and was following him on the road.

mark_11.t: And when they draw near into Jerusalem, into Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mount of the olives, he sends two of his disciples
and says to them: Go into the village opposite you, and immediately entering into it you will find a colt tied on which no one of humans has yet sat; untie it and bring it.
And if anyone says to you: Why are you doing this? say: The Lord has need of it, and immediately he sends it again here.
And they went away and found the colt tied toward a door outside upon the open street, and they untie it.
And some of those standing there were saying to them: What are you doing, untying the colt?
And they said to them just as Jesus said, and they let them go.
And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw upon it their garments, and he sat upon it.
And many spread their garments into the road, and others, having cut branches out of the fields, were spreading them into the road.
And those going before and those following were crying out saying: Hosanna, blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord,
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David; Hosanna in the highest places.
And he entered into Jerusalem into the temple, and having looked around at all things, the hour being already late, he went out into Bethany with the twelve.
And on the next day, they having gone out from Bethany, he hungered.
And seeing a fig tree from afar having leaves he came, if then he will find anything on it. And coming upon it he found nothing except leaves; for it was not the season of figs.
And answering he said to it: No longer for ever may anyone eat fruit out of you. And his disciples were hearing.

And they come into Jerusalem. And entering into the temple he began to cast out those selling and those buying in the temple, and the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling the doves he overturned,
and he was not permitting that anyone should carry a vessel through the temple.
And he was teaching and saying to them: Has it not been written that My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations? But you have made it a cave of bandits.
And the chief priests and the scribes heard, and they were seeking how they might destroy him; for they were afraid of him, for all the crowd was astounded at his teaching.
And whenever it became late, they were going out outside the city.
And passing along early they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
And having remembered, Peter says to him: Rabbi, look, the fig tree that you cursed has been dried up.
And answering Jesus says to them: Have trust in God.
For Amen I say to you that whoever says to this mountain: Be lifted up and be thrown into the sea, and does not waver in his heart but trusts that what he speaks comes about — it will be for him.
On account of this I say to you: all things whatever you pray and ask, trust that you received, and it will be for you.
And whenever you stand praying, release if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in the heavens may also release for you your trespasses.
[But if you yourselves do not release, neither will your Father who is in the heavens release your trespasses.]
And they come again into Jerusalem. And as he was walking about in the temple the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him
and were saying to him: By what kind of authority are you doing these things, or who gave you this authority that you should do these things?
But Jesus said to them: I will ask you also one word, and answer me, and I will tell you by what kind of authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, was it out of heaven or out of humans? Answer me.
And they were reasoning among themselves saying: What shall we say? If we say Out of heaven, he will say: Why then did you not trust him?
But if we say Out of humans — they were fearing the crowd; for all held John really that he was a prophet.
And answering Jesus they say: We do not know. And Jesus answering says to them: Neither do I tell you by what kind of authority I do these things.

mark_12.t: And he began to speak to them in parables: A vineyard a human planted and put around it a fence and dug a wine-vat and built a tower, and let it out to farmers and went away abroad.
And he sent to the farmers at the season a slave that from the farmers he might receive from the fruits of the vineyard.
And taking him they flayed him and sent him away empty.
And again he sent to them another slave; and that one they struck on the head and sent away, having dishonoured him.
And again another he sent; and that one they killed, and many others, some indeed flaying, but others killing.
Still one he had, a beloved son; he sent him also, last, to them saying that They will be turned about before my son.
But those farmers said to themselves that This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and ours will be the inheritance.
And taking him they killed him and cast him outside the vineyard.
What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers and will give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this writing: A stone which those building rejected, this one became into the head of the corner;
from the Lord this came about, and it is marvellous in our eyes?
And they were seeking to seize him, and they feared the crowd; for they knew that against them he spoke the parable. And leaving him they went away.
And they send to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians so that they might catch him in a word.

And coming they say to him: Teacher, we know that you are true and it is not a care to you about anyone; for you do not look into the face of humans but upon truth you teach the way of God. Is it permitted to give the census-tax to Caesar or not?
Should we give or should we not give?' But he, knowing their play-acting, said to them: Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius that I may see.
And they brought. And he says to them: Whose is this image and the inscription? And they said to him: Caesar's.
And Jesus answering said to them: The things of Caesar give back to Caesar and the things of God to God. And they were utterly astonished at him.
And Sadducees come to him, who say there is not a resurrection, and they were asking him saying:
Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if anyone's brother dies and leaves behind a wife and does not leave a child, that his brother should take his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
Seven brothers there were; and the first took a wife and dying left no seed.
And the second took her and died, not himself having left behind seed; and the third likewise.
And the seven left no seed. Last of all the woman also died.
In the resurrection therefore, when they rise, of which of them will she be wife? For the seven had her as wife.
Jesus said to them: Is it not on account of this that you are led astray, not knowing the writings nor the power of God?
For when out of the dead they rise, neither do they marry nor are they given in marriage, but they are as angels in the heavens.
But concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him saying: I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?
He is not God of dead ones but of living ones; you yourselves are much led astray.
And one of the scribes coming forward, having heard them debating, seeing that he answered them well, asked him: Which commandment is first of all?
Jesus answered him that First is: Hear, Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord;
and you shall love the Lord your God out of your whole heart and out of your whole soul and out of your whole understanding and out of your whole strength. This is the first commandment.
Second is this: You shall love your neighbour as yourself. Greater than these another commandment there is not.
And the scribe said to him: Well, teacher, upon truth you said that he is one and there is not another besides him;

and to love him out of the whole heart and out of the whole understanding and out of the whole soul and out of the whole strength, and to love the neighbour as oneself, is more than all the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices.
And Jesus, seeing him, that he answered with a mind, said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one any longer was daring to question him.
And answering Jesus was saying, teaching in the temple: How do the scribes say that the Christ is son of David?
David himself said in the Holy Spirit: The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right until I place your enemies underneath your feet.
David himself therefore calls him lord, and from where is he his son? And the large crowd was hearing him gladly.
And in his teaching he was saying: Watch out from the scribes, those wanting to walk about in robes and greetings in the marketplaces
and first seats in the synagogues and first couches at the dinners,
those devouring the houses of the widows and for a pretext praying long prayers, these will receive a more abundant judgement.
And having sat down opposite the treasury he was watching how the crowd throws copper into the treasury; and many rich were throwing in much.
And one poor widow coming threw in two lepta, which is a quadrans.
And calling to himself his disciples he said to them: Amen I say to you that this widow, the poor one, has thrown in more than all those throwing into the treasury;
for all out of what abounds to them threw in, but she out of her lack threw in all as much as she had, her whole living.

mark_13.t: And as he was going out of the temple one of his disciples says to him: Teacher, look, what sort of stones and what sort of buildings.
And Jesus answering said to him: Do you see these great buildings? There will certainly not be left here stone upon stone which will certainly not be thrown down.
And as he was sitting on the mount of the olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking him privately:
Tell us, when will these things be, and what is the sign when all these things are about to be completed?
But Jesus began to say to them: Watch out lest anyone lead you astray.
Many will come upon my name saying that I am, and they will lead many astray.
But when you hear wars and hearings of wars, do not be disturbed; it must come about, but not yet the end.
For nation will be raised against nation and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in places; there will be famines and disturbances. A beginning of birth-pangs these things.
But watch out for yourselves; for they will hand you over into councils, and into synagogues you will be flayed, and before governors and kings you will be stood for my sake, for a witness to them.
And into all the nations first the gospel must be proclaimed.

And when they lead you handing you over, do not worry beforehand what you should speak, nor rehearse; but whatever is given to you in that hour, this speak; for you are not the ones speaking but the Holy Spirit.
And brother will hand over brother into death and a father a child, and children will rise up against parents and will put them to death.
And you will be being hated by all on account of my name. But the one having endured into the end, this one will be saved.
But when you see the abomination of the desolation standing where it must not, let the one reading understand, then let those in Judea flee into the mountains.
Let the one upon the housetop not come down nor enter to take anything out of his house;
and let the one being in the field not turn back into the things behind to take his outer garment.
But woe to those having in the womb and to those giving suck in those days.
But pray that it may not come about in winter.
For those days will be tribulation such as has not come about of such a kind from the beginning of creation which God created until now, and certainly will not come about.
And unless the Lord shortened the days, not any flesh would be saved; but on account of the chosen whom he chose he shortened the days.
And then if anyone says to you: Look, here is the Christ, or Look, there, do not trust.
For false-christs and false-prophets will be raised up and will give signs and portents toward leading astray, if possible, the chosen.
But you yourselves watch out; look, I have told you all things beforehand.
But in those days after that tribulation the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its brightness,
and the stars will be falling out of the heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with much power and glory.
And then he will send the messengers and will gather together his chosen out of the four winds from the extremity of earth to the extremity of heaven.
But from the fig tree learn the parable: whenever its branch has already become tender and puts out the leaves, you know that the summer is near.
So also you yourselves, whenever you see these things coming about, know that it is near, at the doors.
Amen I say to you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things come about.
The heaven and the earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But concerning that day or the hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, except the Father.
Watch out, keep awake; for you do not know when the time is.
As a person away abroad, having left his house and having given to his slaves the authority, to each his work, and to the doorkeeper he commanded that he should keep awake.
Keep awake therefore; for you do not know when the lord of the house comes, either late or midnight or cock-crowing or early,
lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
But what I say to you, I say to all: keep awake.

mark_14.t: Now it was the Passover and the unleavened bread after two days, and the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how, having seized him by deceit, they might kill him;
for they were saying: Not in the feast, lest there will be an uproar of the people.

And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, while he was reclining, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of nard, genuine, very costly; and having shattered the alabaster jar she poured it down over his head.
But there were some being indignant among themselves and saying: For what has this destruction of the ointment come about?
For this ointment was able to be sold for more than three hundred denarii and to be given to the poor. And they were snorting at her.
But Jesus said: Let her be; why do you cause troubles for her? A good work she worked in me.
For always the poor you have with yourselves, and whenever you want you are able to do good for them; but me you do not always have.
What she had she did; she took beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.
But Amen I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed into the whole world, also what she did will be spoken for a memorial of her.
And Judas Iscariot, the one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests that he might hand him over to them.
And they hearing rejoiced and promised to give him silver; and he was seeking how conveniently he might hand him over.
And on the first day of the unleavened bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover, his disciples say to him: Where do you want that going away we should prepare that you may eat the Passover?
And he sends two of his disciples and says to them: Go into the city, and there will meet you a person carrying a jar of water; follow him.
And wherever he enters, say to the master of the house that The teacher says: Where is my guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
And he himself will show you a large upper room furnished, ready; and there prepare for us.
And his disciples went out and came into the city and found just as he said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
And evening having come he comes with the twelve.
And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said: Amen I say to you that one of you will hand me over, the one eating with me.
They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one: Surely not I? and another: Surely not I?
But he answering said to them: One of the twelve, the one dipping in with me into the one bowl.
Because the Son of Man goes just as it has been written concerning him, but woe to that person through whom the Son of Man is handed over; good was it for him if that person had not been born.
And as they were eating, having taken bread, having blessed, he broke and gave to them and said: Take[, eat]; this is my body.
And having taken a cup, having given thanks, he gave to them, and they all drank out of it.
And he said to them: This is my blood, that of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
Amen I say to you that no longer will I certainly not drink out of the produce of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
And having sung a hymn they went out into the mount of the olives.
And Jesus says to them that All of you will be tripped up, because it has been written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.
But after my being raised I will go before you into Galilee.
But Peter said to him: Even if all will be tripped up, yet not I.
And Jesus says to him: Amen I say to you that you yourself today, on this night, before a cock crows twice, three times will deny me.
But he was speaking excessively the more: If it is necessary for me to die together with you, I will certainly not deny you. And likewise also all were saying.
And they come into a piece of ground of which the name was Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples: Sit here while I pray.
And he takes along Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be utterly astounded and to be in anguish.
And he says to them: Deeply grieved is my soul unto death; remain here and keep awake.
And going forward a little he was falling upon the ground and was praying that if it is possible the hour might pass away from him.
And he was saying: Abba, the Father, all things are possible for you; carry away this cup from me; but not what I want but what you.
And he comes and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter: Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not strong enough to keep awake one hour?
Keep awake and pray that you may not come into testing; the spirit indeed is eager, but the flesh is weak.
And again going away he prayed, saying the same word.
And again coming he found them sleeping, for their eyes were being weighed down, and they did not know what they should answer him.
And he comes the third time and says to them: Sleep the rest and rest yourselves; it is enough, the hour came; look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of the sinners.
Rise, let us go; look, the one handing me over has drawn near.

And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas arrives, the Iscariot, being one of the twelve, and with him a crowd with swords and wooden clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
Now the one handing him over had given a pre-arranged signal to them saying: Whomever I kiss, he it is; seize him and lead him away securely.
And coming, immediately going up to him he says to him: Rabbi, and he kissed him fervently.
But they laid their hands upon him and seized him.
But one certain of those standing by, having drawn the sword, struck the slave of the high priest and took off his little ear.
And answering Jesus said to them: As against a bandit did you come out with swords and wooden clubs to take me together?
Daily I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me; but that the writings might be fulfilled.
And leaving him they all fled.
And one young man was following him together, having been clothed with a linen cloth upon his nakedness, and they seize him.
But he, having left behind the linen cloth, fled naked from them.
And they led away Jesus to the high priest, and there come together with him all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.
And Peter from afar followed him as far as inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting together with the attendants and warming himself toward the light.
But the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they were not finding it.
For many were bearing false witness against him, and the testimonies were not equal.
And some rising up were bearing false witness against him saying
that We heard him saying that I will destroy this sanctuary made with hands and through three days another not made with hands I will build.
And not even so was their testimony equal.
And the high priest, standing up into the midst, questioned Jesus saying: Do you answer nothing? What are these testifying against you?
But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest was questioning him and says to him: Are you the Christ, the son of the Blessed?
And Jesus said: I am, and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.
But the high priest, having torn apart his tunics, says: Why still do we have need of witnesses?
You heard the blasphemy; what does it appear to you? And they all condemned him to be liable to death.
And some began to spit at him and to cover around his face and to strike him with fists and to say to him: Prophesy, and the attendants received him with blows.
And Peter being below in the courtyard, there comes one of the servant girls of the high priest,
and seeing Peter warming himself, having looked into him she says: You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus.
But he denied saying: Neither do I know nor understand, you, what you say. And he went outside into the porch, and a cock crowed.
And the servant girl, seeing him, began again to say to those standing by that This one is of them.
But he again was denying. And after a little again those standing by were saying to Peter: Truly you are of them, for you are also a Galilean [and your speech is like theirs].
But he began to put himself under a curse and to swear that I do not know this person whom you speak of.

And immediately a second time a cock crowed. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus said to him that Before a cock crows twice, three times you will deny me. And having thrown himself upon it he was weeping.

mark_15.t: And immediately upon the early morning, the chief priests having made a council with the elders and scribes and the whole council, having bound Jesus they carried him away and handed him over to Pilate.
And Pilate questioned him: Are you the king of the Jews? And he answering him says: You say.
And the chief priests were accusing him of many things.
But Pilate again was questioning him saying: Do you answer nothing? See how many things they accuse you of.
But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate marvelled.
But at a feast he was releasing to them one prisoner whom they were requesting.
And there was the one called Barabbas, bound with the rebels who in the uprising had done murder.
And the crowd going up began to request just as he was always doing for them.
But Pilate answered them saying: Do you want that I should release to you the king of the Jews?
For he was knowing that on account of envy the chief priests had handed him over.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd that rather he should release Barabbas to them.
But Pilate again answering was saying to them: What therefore do you want I should do with the one you call the king of the Jews?
But they again cried out: Crucify him.
But Pilate was saying to them: For what has he done evil? But they cried out exceedingly: Crucify him.
But Pilate, wishing to do the sufficient thing for the crowd, released to them Barabbas, and handed over Jesus, having flogged him, that he might be crucified.
But the soldiers led him away inside the courtyard, which is the praetorium, and they call together the whole cohort.
And they clothe him in purple and place around him, having plaited it, a thorny crown.
And they began to greet him: Hail, the king of the Jews.
And they were striking his head with a reed and were spitting at him, and placing the knees they were bowing down to him.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped off him the purple and clothed him with his own garments. And they lead him out that they might crucify him.
And they press into service one passing by, Simon a Cyrenian coming from a field, the father of Alexander and Rufus, that he might take up his cross.
And they bring him upon the Golgotha place, which is being translated, Skull's place.
And they were giving him myrrhed wine to drink; but he did not take it.
And they crucify him and divide his garments, casting a lot upon them, who should take what.
Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
And the inscription of his charge had been inscribed: The king of the Jews.
And with him they crucify two bandits, one at his right and one at his left.
[And the writing was fulfilled that says: And with lawless ones he was reckoned.]
And those passing along were blaspheming him, shaking their heads and saying: Aha, the one destroying the sanctuary and building it in three days,
save yourself, having come down from the cross.
Likewise also the chief priests, mocking among one another with the scribes, were saying: Others he saved, himself he is not able to save.
The Christ, the king of Israel — let him come down now from the cross, that we may see and trust. And those crucified together with him were reproaching him.
And the sixth hour having come, darkness came upon the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a great voice: Eloi Eloi, lema sabachthani? which is being translated: My God my God, for what did you abandon me?
And some of those standing by, hearing, were saying: Look, he calls Elijah.
But someone running and having filled a sponge with sour wine, having placed it around a reed, was giving him to drink, saying: Let be; let us see if Elijah comes to take him down.
But Jesus, having let go a great voice, breathed out.
And the curtain of the sanctuary was split into two from above until below.
And the centurion standing by opposite him, seeing that thus he breathed out, said: Truly this human was Son of God.
And there were also women from afar looking on, among whom also was Mary the Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the small and of Joses, and Salome,
who also, when he was in Galilee, were following him and were serving him, and many others who had come up together with him into Jerusalem.
And already evening having come, since it was preparation, which is before-sabbath,
Joseph from Arimathea came, a well-formed councillor, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, having dared he entered to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus.
But Pilate marvelled if he had already died, and having summoned the centurion he questioned him if he died long ago.
And having known from the centurion he granted the corpse to Joseph.
And having bought a linen cloth, having taken him down, he wrapped him in the linen cloth and placed him in a tomb which had been hewn out of rock, and he rolled a stone upon the door of the tomb.
But Mary the Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he has been placed.

mark_16.t: And the sabbath having passed, Mary the Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices so that coming they might anoint him.
And very early on the first of the sabbaths they come upon the tomb, the sun having risen.
And they were saying to themselves: Who will roll away for us the stone out of the door of the tomb?
And having looked up they observe that the stone has been rolled away; for it was exceedingly great.
And having entered into the tomb they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were utterly astounded.
But he says to them: Do not be utterly astounded. Jesus you seek, the Nazarene, the crucified one; he was raised, he is not here; see the place where they placed him.
But go, say to his disciples and to Peter that he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him, just as he said to you.

And having gone out they fled from the tomb, for trembling and bewilderment were holding them; and to no one did they say nothing, for they were afraid — for [[But all the things commanded they reported briefly to those around Peter. And after these things Jesus himself also sent out through them, from east and as far as west, the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.]]
[[But having risen early on the first of the sabbath he appeared first to Mary the Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
That one, having gone, reported to those who had come to be with him, as they were mourning and weeping.
And those, hearing that he lives and was seen by her, did not trust.
But after these things to two of them walking he was manifested in a different form as they were going into a field.
And those, having gone away, reported to the rest; neither those did they trust.
But afterward, to them, the eleven, as they were reclining, he was manifested, and he reproached their untrust and hardness of heart, because those who had seen him raised they did not trust.
And he said to them: Having gone into all the world, proclaim the gospel to all the creation.
The one having trusted and having been baptised will be saved; but the one having not trusted will be condemned.
But these signs will follow along with those having trusted: in my name they will cast out demons, they will speak in new tongues,
they will take up serpents, and if they drink anything deadly it will certainly not harm them; upon the sick they will place hands and they will be well.
So then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into the heaven and sat at the right of God.
But those, having gone out, proclaimed everywhere, the Lord working together with them and confirming the word through the signs following along.]]

philippians_1.t: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the holy ones in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with overseers and deacons:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to my God at every remembrance of you,
always in every petition of mine on behalf of all of you, with joy making the petition,
on your sharing toward the good news from the first day until now,
having been persuaded of this very thing, that the one having begun in you a good work will complete it until the day of Christ Jesus;

just as it is right for me to think this over all of you, because of my having you in the heart, both in my chains and in the defence and confirmation of the good news, all of you being co-sharers with me of the grace.
For God is my witness how I yearn for all of you in the inward parts of Christ Jesus.
And this I pray, that your love may yet more and more abound in full knowledge and all discernment,
for you to test the things that differ, so that you may be unmixed and without stumbling for the day of Christ,
having been filled with fruit of righteousness, the one through Jesus Christ, to glory and praise of God.
And I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that the things concerning me have come rather to the advance of the good news,
so that my chains have become manifest in Christ in the whole praetorium and to all the rest,
and the majority of the brothers in the Lord, having become confident by my chains, more abundantly to dare to speak the word of God fearlessly.
Some indeed even because of envy and strife, but some also because of goodwill, are proclaiming the Christ.
The ones on the one hand out of love, knowing that for defence of the gospel I am set;
The ones on the other hand out of rivalry proclaim the Christ, not purely, supposing affliction to raise for my chains.
For what? Only that in every manner, whether in pretext or in truth, Christ is being announced, and in this I rejoice — but also I will rejoice.
For I know that this will turn out to me for deliverance through your petition and supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
according to my eager watching and hope that in nothing I will be shamed, but in all boldness, as always also now, Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
For to me, to live — Christ; and to die — gain.
But if to live in flesh — this to me is fruit of work; and what I will choose I do not make known.
But I am held together out of the two, having the desire for the loosing-away and to be with Christ, for it is by much rather better;
but to remain on in the flesh is more necessary because of you.
And having been persuaded of this, I know that I will remain and remain alongside all of you for your advance and joy of the trust,
so that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my arrival again to you.

Only live as citizens worthily of the good news of the Christ, so that whether coming and seeing you or being absent I may hear the things about you, that you stand in one spirit, with one soul striving together for the trust of the good news,
and not being startled in anything by those opposing, which is to them a demonstration of destruction, but of your salvation — and this from God;
because to you it was graciously given, the thing on behalf of Christ, not only to trust into him but also to suffer on his behalf,
having the same contest such as you saw in me and now hear in me.

philippians_2.t: If therefore any encouragement in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any sharing of spirit, if any inward parts and compassions,
fill up my joy, that you may think the same, having the same love, joined in soul, thinking the one thing,
nothing according to selfish ambition nor according to empty glory, but in lowliness of mind considering one another as surpassing yourselves,
not each looking to the things of themselves, but each also to the things of others.
For think this among you which also in Christ Jesus,
who in form of God existing did not consider the being equal with God a grasping,
but himself he emptied, form of a slave having taken, in likeness of humans having become, and in appearance having been found as a human
he lowered himself, having become obedient until death, and death of a cross;
Therefore also God super-exalted him and graced to him the name, the one above every name,
so that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of heavenly ones and earthly ones and ones under the earth,
and every tongue should confess that Lord is Jesus Christ, to glory of God Father.
So then, my beloved, just as you always obeyed, not as in my arrival only but now much more in my absence, with fear and trembling work out your own salvation;
For God is the one working in you both the willing and the working on behalf of the good pleasure.
Do all things apart from grumblings and disputings,
so that you may become blameless and unmixed, children of God unblemished in the midst of a generation crooked and distorted, among whom you appear as luminaries in a world,
holding forth a word of life, for a boast to me for the day of Christ, that not into emptiness I ran, nor into emptiness I laboured.
But if also I am being poured out upon the sacrifice and priestly service of your trust, I rejoice and rejoice together with all of you;
And the same thing you also rejoice and rejoice together with me.
But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy quickly to you, so that I also may be of good soul having come to know the things about you;
For I have no one equal-souled, who genuinely will be anxious for the things about you;
For they all seek the things of themselves, not the things of Jesus Christ;
But you know his provenness, that as a child to a father, with me he slaved for the good news.
This one therefore I hope to send, as soon as I may see off the things about me, immediately;
But I have been persuaded in the Lord that I myself also will come quickly.
But I considered it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, the brother and co-worker and fellow soldier of mine, but your sent-one and minister of my need;
since he was yearning for all of you and being distressed because you heard that he was sick.
For indeed he was sick, near to death; but God had mercy on him, and not on him only but also on me, so that I might not have grief upon grief.
More eagerly therefore I sent him, so that seeing him again you may rejoice, and I may be less-grieved.
Receive him therefore in the Lord with all joy, and hold such ones as held-in-honour;
because through the work of the Christ he drew near as far as death, having gambled with the soul, so that he might fill up your lack of the service toward me.

philippians_3.t: For the rest, my brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not irksome to me, and for you is safe.
Look at the dogs, look at the evil workers, look at the cutting-apart;
For we are the circumcision, the ones serving by spirit of God and boasting in Christ Jesus and not having confidence in flesh,
although I have confidence also in flesh. If any other seems to have confidence in flesh, I more —
in circumcision an eighth-day one, of the race of Israel, of tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, according to law a Pharisee,
according to zeal persecuting the assembly, according to righteousness the one in law having become blameless.
But whatever things were gains to me, these I have considered because of the Christ a loss;

But rather indeed I also consider all things to be loss because of the surpassing of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, because of whom I was made to lose all things, and I consider them to be dung, so that I may gain Christ,
and be found in him, not having my righteousness the one out of law, but the one through faith in Christ, the righteousness out of God upon the trust,
of the knowing him and the power of his rising and the sharing of his sufferings, being conformed to his death,
if somehow I may attain to the out-resurrection, the one out of dead ones.
Not that I already received or already have been perfected, but I pursue if also I may lay hold, upon which also I was laid hold of by the Christ Jesus.
Brothers and sisters, I do not reckon myself to have laid hold; but one thing — the things behind forgetting, and to the things in front stretching out,
toward the mark I pursue for the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.
As many therefore as are complete, let us think this; and if in anything you think otherwise, this also God will reveal to you;
Only, to what we have arrived, to walk in line by the same rule, to think the same.
Become fellow-imitators of me, brothers and sisters, and watch the ones walking thus, just as you have us as a pattern.
For many walk, of whom I often was telling you, and now weeping I tell, the enemies of the cross of the Christ,
of whom the end is destruction, of whom the god is the belly and the glory in their shame, the ones thinking the earthly things.
For our commonwealth exists in heavens, out of which also we eagerly await a Saviour, Lord Jesus Christ,
who will refashion the body of our lowliness for it to become conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working of his being able also to subject to himself all things.

philippians_4.t: So then, my brothers and sisters beloved and longed-for, my joy and crown, thus stand in the Lord, beloved.
Euodia I urge and Syntyche I urge to think the same in the Lord;

Yes, I ask also you, genuine yokefellow, take hold together with them, who in the good news strove together with me, with also Clement and the rest of my co-workers, of whom the names are in a book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice.
Let your yieldingness be known to all humans. The Lord is near.
Be anxious about nothing, but in everything by the prayer and the petition with thanksgiving let your requests be made known toward God;
and the peace of God, the one surpassing all mind, will garrison your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

For the rest, brothers and sisters, whatever things are true, whatever honourable, whatever just, whatever pure, whatever lovely, whatever well-spoken-of, if any virtue and if any praise — these things reckon.
What things also you learned and received and heard and saw in me, these practise; and the God of the peace will be with you.
But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly that already at length you revived the thinking on my behalf; upon which also you were thinking, but you were lacking opportunity.
Not that I speak according to lack; for I learned, in whatever things I am, to be self-sufficient.
I know also to be lowered, I know also to abound; in everything and in all things I have been initiated both to be filled and to hunger, both to abound and to lack;
I have strength for all things in the one empowering me.
Nevertheless you did well, having shared together with my affliction.
And you also know, Philippians, that in beginning of the good news, when I went out from Macedonia, no assembly shared with me in an account of giving and receiving except you only;
because even in Thessalonica both once and twice you sent to me for the need.
Not that I seek after the gift, but I seek after the fruit increasing to your account;
But I have in full all things and abound; I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you, an odour of sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God.
And my God will fill every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
And to the God and Father of us the glory into the ages of the ages. Amen.
Greet every holy one in Christ Jesus. The brothers with me greet you.
All the holy ones greet you, and especially the ones out of Caesar's household.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ with your spirit. Amen. [To Philippians it was written from Rome through Epaphroditus.]

philemon_1.t: Paul, prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon the beloved and our fellow worker,
and to Apphia the sister and to Archippus our fellow soldier and to the assembly according to your house:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to my God always, making remembrance of you at my prayers,
hearing of your love and the trust which you have toward the Lord Jesus and unto all the holy ones,
so that the sharing of your trust may become effective in full knowledge of every good thing that is in us unto Christ.
For much joy I had and encouragement upon your love, because the inward parts of the holy ones have been rested through you, brother.
Therefore having much boldness in Christ to order you the fitting thing,
on account of the love rather I appeal, being such a one as Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus —
I appeal to you concerning my child, whom I begot in the bonds, Onesimus,
the one once to you useless, but now to you and to me well-useful,
whom I sent back to you — him, that is, my own inward parts.
whom I was wanting to hold to myself, so that on behalf of you he might serve me in the bonds of the good news;
but apart from your opinion I wanted to do nothing, so that your good might not be as according to compulsion but according to willingness.
For perhaps because of this he was separated for an hour, so that eternally you might have him fully —
no longer as a slave but beyond a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you both in flesh and in the Lord?
If therefore you have me a partner, receive him as me.
But if in anything he wronged you or owes, this to me charge.
I Paul wrote with my own hand, I will repay — so that I may not say to you that also your own self you owe me besides.
Yes, brother, may I have use of you in the Lord; rest my inward parts in Christ.
Having been persuaded of your obedience I wrote to you, knowing that also beyond what I say you will do.
But at the same time also prepare for me a lodging; for I hope that through your prayers I will be granted to you.
Greets you Epaphras my fellow captive in Christ Jesus,
Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

revelation_1.t: An unveiling of Jesus Christ, which God gave to him to show to his servants what must happen in quickness, and he signified, having sent through his messenger to his servant John,
who witnessed the word of God and the witness of Jesus Christ, as much as he saw.
Blessed is the one reading and those hearing the words of the prophecy and keeping the things written in it; for the season is near.
John to the seven assemblies in Asia: grace to you and peace from the one who is and the he-was and the one coming, and from the seven spirits which are before his throne,
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn out of the dead ones and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To the one loving us and having released us out of our sins in his blood
and he made us a kingdom, and priests to his God and Father — to him the glory and the might into the ages of the ages, amen.
Behold, he comes with the clouds, and every eye will see him, and whoever pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth will beat themselves over him. Yes, amen.
I am the alpha and the o, beginning and end, says the Lord God, the one who is and the he-was and the one coming, the all-holder.

I John, also your brother and fellow-sharer in the affliction and in the kingdom and endurance in Jesus Christ, came to be on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and because of the witness of Jesus Christ.
I came to be in spirit on the lordly day and I heard behind me a great voice as of a trumpet

saying, I am the A and the O, the first and the last; and what you see write into a book and send to the seven assemblies in Asia: to Ephesus and to Smyrna and to Pergamum and to Thyatira and to Sardis and to Philadelphia and to Laodicea.
And there I turned to see the voice which was speaking with me. And having turned I saw seven golden lampstands
and in the midst of the seven lampstands one like a son of man, having been clothed to the feet and having been girded at the breasts with a golden girdle.
And his head and the hairs white as white wool, as snow, and his eyes as a flame of fire
and his feet like burnished bronze as having been fired in a furnace — feminine, agreeing with nothing — and his voice as a voice of many waters.
and having in his right hand seven stars, and out of his mouth a sharp two-mouthed broadsword going out, and his appearance as the sun shines in its power.
And when I saw him, I fell toward his feet as dead, and he placed his right hand on me saying to me: Do not fear. I am the first and the last
and the living one, and I became dead and behold I am living into the ages of the ages, amen; and I have the keys of death and of Hades.
Write therefore what you saw and what things are and what things are about to happen after these things,

The mystery of the seven stars which you saw upon my right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are angels of the seven assemblies, and the lampstands which you saw, seven, are seven assemblies.

revelation_2.t: To the messenger of the assembly in Ephesus write: These things says the one holding fast the seven stars in his right hand, the one walking in the midst of the seven golden lampstands.
I know your works and your labour and your endurance, and that you are not able to bear evil ones, and you tested those saying themselves to be apostles and they are not, and you found them false.
And you have endurance and you bore up and on account of my name you have laboured and you have not grown weary.
But I have against you that you left your first love.

Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and change your mind and do the first works; and if not, I come to you quickly and I will move your lampstand out of its place, if you do not change your mind.
But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
The one having an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To the one conquering I will give to him to eat out of the wood of life which is in the midst of the paradise of my God.
And to the messenger of the assembly in Smyrna write: These things says the first and the last, who became dead and lived:
I know your works and the affliction and the poverty — but rich you are — and the blasphemy from those saying themselves to be Jews and they are not, but a synagogue of the adversary.

Fear nothing which you are about to suffer. Behold indeed the slanderer is about to throw out of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction of ten days. Become faithful until death, and I will give you the wreath of life.
The one having an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. The one conquering shall never be harmed out of the second death.
And to the messenger of the assembly in Pergamum write: These things says the one having the sharp two-mouthed broadsword:

I know your works, and where you dwell, where the throne of the adversary is, and you hold fast my name and you did not deny my trust, and in the days in which Antipas my witness my faithful one, who was killed beside you, where the adversary dwells.

But I have against you a few things, that you have there ones holding fast the teaching of Balaam, who was teaching Balak to throw a stumbling-block before the sons of Israel, both to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit sexual immorality.
Thus you also have ones holding fast the teaching of the Nicolaitans likewise.
Change your mind therefore; and if not, I come to you quickly and I will war with them by the broadsword of my mouth.

The one having an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To the one conquering I will give to him to eat from the hidden manna, and I will give to him a white pebble, and upon the pebble a new name having been written which no one knows except the one receiving.
And to the messenger of the assembly in Thyatira write: These things says the son of God, the one having his eyes as a flame of fire, and his feet like fine bronze:
I know your works and the love and the trust and the service and your endurance, and your works, and the last ones greater than the first.

But I have against you a few things, that you permit the woman Jezebel, she who says herself to be a prophetess, and she teaches and deceives my servants to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
And I gave to her time so that she might change her mind, and she does not want to change her mind out of her sexual immorality.
Behold I throw her into a bed, and the ones committing adultery with her into great affliction, if they do not change their minds out of her works.
And her children I will kill with death, and all the assemblies will know that I am the one searching kidneys and hearts, and I will give to you, to each, according to your works.

But to you I say, to the rest, the ones in Thyatira, as many as do not have this teaching, and whoever did not know the deep things of the adversary, as they say: I do not throw upon you another burden,
Except what you have, hold fast until whenever I come.
And the one conquering and the one keeping my works until the end, I will give to him authority over the nations,
and he will shepherd them with an iron staff, as the clay vessels are broken in pieces,
as I also have received from my Father; and I will give to him the morning star.
The one having an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.

revelation_3.t: And to the messenger of the assembly in Sardis write: These things says the one having the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you live, and you are dead.
Become watching, and strengthen the remaining things which were about to die; for I have not found your works having been fulfilled before my God.

Remember therefore how you have received and heard, and keep and change your mind. If therefore you do not watch, I will come upon you as a thief, and you shall never know what sort of hour I will come upon you.
But you have a few names in Sardis which did not defile their garments, and they will walk with me in white, because they are worthy.
The one conquering, thus he will be clothed in white garments, and I shall never wipe out his name out of the book of life, and I will confess his name before my Father and before his messengers.
The one having an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.

And to the messenger of the assembly in Philadelphia write: These things says the holy one, the true one, the one having the key of David, the one opening and no one will shut it except the one opening, and shutting and no one opens:
I know your works. Behold I have given before you a door having been opened which no one is able to shut it; because you have a little power and you kept my word and you did not deny my name.

Behold I give out of the synagogue of the adversary, of those saying themselves to be Jews and they are not, but they lie — behold I will make them so that they will come and bow before your feet and know that I loved you.
Because you kept the word of my endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of the testing which is about to come upon the whole inhabited world, to test the ones dwelling upon the earth.
Behold I come quickly; hold fast what you have, so that no one takes your wreath.

The one conquering, I will make him a pillar in the sanctuary of my God, and outside he shall never go out still, and I will write upon him the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem — she who is coming down out of heaven from my God — and my name, the new one.
The one having an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.
And to the messenger of the assembly in Laodicea write: These things says the amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God:
I know your works, that neither cold are you nor hot. Would that cold you were or hot;
Thus because you are lukewarm and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of my mouth,
because you say that rich am I and I have become rich and I have need of nothing, and you do not know that you are the wretched one and the pitiable one and poor and blind and naked,

I counsel you to buy from me gold having been fired out of fire so that you may become rich, and white garments so that you may be clothed and the shame of your nakedness may not be made visible, and eye-salve to anoint your eyes so that you may see.
I, as many as I love, I reprove and discipline; be zealous therefore and change your mind.
Behold I have stood upon the door and I knock; if anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I also will come in toward him and will dine with him and he with me.
